After 2 seconds of sitting still or coming to a full stop and then being tapped, it reverts to its item form which can be picked up and reused.
If the Beach Ball is hit more than ten times without it touching the ground, a status message appears saying "Beach Ball was hit <number of times> times before touching the ground!"
Beam Sword: The Beam Sword is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Armored Skeletons. When swung, it fires a yellow Sword Beam projectile that can pierce one enemy and bounce off blocks three times before dissipating.
Beams: Beams or columns are background furniture items that provide support for Torches and can be used as decoration. They form continuous vertical pillars when stacked. They are found naturally in Underground Cabins, and can be crafted.

Beams and columns can be stacked from the ground, and exist in the background, providing support for suspended Torches that will not inhibit character movement. In this way, beams and columns provide a function similar to trees (which also exist in the background and allow the player to suspend high Torches), but which the player can construct where they like. Where background walls exist, beams and columns can also be placed in "midair", without support from below.

Despite their appearance as background walls, beams and columns instead share a layer with other furniture items (like tables, Torches, statues, Switches, timers, etc.), thus the two cannot share the same tile space. They can also prevent a door from opening.
Beanie: The Beanie is a vanity item purchased from the Clothier for 1 Gold, while living in the Snow biome.
Bedazzled Nectar: The Bedazzled Nectar is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Glittery Butterfly that follows the player. The Bedazzled Nectar has a chance of being sold by the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum.
Beds: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration.
Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it.
There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.
Bee: The Bee is a small pre-Hardmode flying enemy that usually appears in the Underground Jungle. They can be spawned by the Queen Bee, and will also appear when destroying Bee Hives and occasionally when mining Hive blocks (which are mainly found in Bee Hive biomes). They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree. They attack by flying into their target, dealing contact damage. In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Bees will inflict players with the Poisoned debuff for 2–6 / 2.5–7.5 seconds.

On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, Bees can also damage other enemies. Bees can select any enemy (except themselves and the Queen Bee) or the player as their target, and they always attack the nearest target. Bees deal 100% of their contact damage to the target but will also take 100% of contact damage from said target.
Bee Cloak: The Bee Cloak is a Hardmode accessory that combines the effects of the Star Cloak and the Honey Comb. When the player is injured, three stars will fall on the player's current location and bees are released.
Bee Gun: The Bee Gun is a pre-Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee. When used, it fires a burst of Bee projectiles that home in on enemies, can pierce enemies twice or bounce on blocks three times, and have a 1/2 (50%) chance to deal 1 extra damage.
Bee Hive: The Bee Hive is a natural trap which spawns over time under Jungle grass ceilings of the Jungle and Underground Jungle. When a Bee Hive is hit, it falls to the ground and rolls, releasing 2–5 Bees upon breaking. If it falls into any liquid, it will not release any Bees upon breaking, and drop 2–5 Hive blocks instead. It can be crafted and placed manually.
Bee Keeper: The Bee Keeper is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee. When swung, it will inflict the Confused debuff on hit for 2 seconds. It also summons a burst of 1–3 Bee projectiles on hit, which home in on enemies, deal 1/3 (33.33%) of the weapon's damage (10 base damage), can pierce enemies twice and bounce on blocks three times, and have a 1/2 (50%) to deal 1 extra damage.
Bee Wax: Bee Wax is a crafting material dropped by the Queen Bee. It cannot be crafted or placed. It takes 44 to craft a set of Bee armor and the Hornet Staff, which amounts to killing Queen Bee 2–3 times.
Bee armor: Bee armor is a pre-Hardmode summoner armor set consisting of the Bee Headgear, Bee Breastplate, and Bee Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 30 Bee Wax.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Bee set: The Bee set is a vanity set consisting of the Bee Hat, the Bee Shirt, and the Bee Pants. All three pieces are dropped by the Queen Bee, with a 1/9 (11.11%) chance each. In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), each piece instead has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped from her Treasure Bag, and one piece is always dropped.
Beenade: The Beenade is a consumable ranged weapon that acts similarly to a regular Grenade when thrown but releases 15–24 friendly bee projectiles upon detonating after 3 seconds. These bee projectiles deal 100% of the Beenade's damage (12 base damage) per hit and have a 1/2 (50%) chance to deal 1 extra damage, but cannot inflict critical hits. The bee projectiles will home in on nearby enemies before dissipating after a 10-second duration, upon piercing enemies or ricocheting off solid blocks a total of 3 times, or immediately upon contact with water or lava.
Beenades have a 3/4 (75%) / 100% chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee in stacks of 10–30 (10–29), and can also be crafted from Grenades and Bee Wax.
Beetle Husk: The Beetle Husk is a Hardmode, post-Golem crafting material dropped by Golem.

Crafting all Beetle Husk items requires (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 42 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 26 Beetle Husks. Crafting one full set of Beetle armor (without wings) requires 18 Beetle Husks, meaning the player will have to fight Golem 3–5 times / 1 time to guarantee enough Beetle Husks for a full set.
Beetle armor: Beetle armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee armor set consisting of the Beetle Helmet and Beetle Leggings, as well as two different chestpieces: the Beetle Scale Mail and Beetle Shell, providing offensive and defensive bonuses respectively. Crafting the full set with one chestpiece requires a total of 18 Beetle Husks and a full set of Turtle armor (54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore), and 3 Turtle Shells). Crafting all four pieces requires a total of 26 Beetle Husks, 78 Chlorophyte Bars (390 Chlorophyte Ore), and 4 Turtle Shells.
Beguiling Lyre: The Beguiling Lyre is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Faun that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Faun will fly in order to catch up to them. The Beguiling Lyre has a 6/125 (4.8%) of being dropped from Iron and Mythril Crates.
Bejeweled Staff: The Bejeweled Staff is an unobtainable magic weapon. It is seemingly a combination of all the gem staves, combining the effects of all gem types. The projectiles fired has the following stats and abilities:
Projectiles have a damage multiplier of 1, a duration of 1.5 seconds, +2 penetrate count, +4 armor penetration, and a hitbox of 4.375×4.375 tiles.
Each use fires 3 projectiles, which home in onto targets with clear line of sight that are no more than 62.5 tiles tiles away, and attempt to home again at low velocity.

Projectiles can ricochet on solid blocks at the cost of 1 penetrate count and 20% velocity. They will home in onto targets with clear line of sight that are no more than 150 tiles away upon ricocheting.
Projectiles have Topaz's ability of creating 10×10-tile explosions upon dissipating and Emerald's ability of gradually losing speed (See Gem staves § Gem enchantments for details).
Projectiles randomly selects visual of all gem staff projectiles.
Bell: The Bell is a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Wizard for 1 Gold. It is used to the craft the Fairy Bell, a light pet-summoning item.
When used, the Bell creates a sound that changes in pitch depending on the distance between the player and the point clicked.
Benches: Benches are furniture items that fulfill a house's chair requirement.
As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Bench will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5.
Bernie's Button: Bernie's Button is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns Bernie to follow the player. Bernie's Button can be purchased from the Princess for 25 Gold.
Berserker's Glove: The Berserker's Glove is a Hardmode accessory. While equipped, it grants the following effects:
Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips
Betsy: Betsy is a Hardmode, post-Golem mini-boss that spawns once during the seventh and final wave of Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. Like all enemies in the Old One's Army, she will despawn upon completion or failure of the event. Defeating Betsy is the only way to complete the final wave of the event successfully.
Betsy's Egg: Betsy's Egg is a Hardmode, post-Golem pet-summoning item that spawns Itsy Betsy to follow the player. Betsy's Egg has a 1/4 (25%) of being dropped from Betsy in Master Mode.
Betsy's Wrath: Betsy's Wrath is a Hardmode, post-Golem wand that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. When used, it fires three fireballs that travel in arcs. The fireballs explode upon impact with an enemy or a block and inflict the Betsy's Curse debuff, which adds 40 armor penetration against affected entities for 10 seconds.
Bewitching Table: The Bewitching Table is a furniture item found naturally placed in the Dungeon and can be obtained by fishing in the Dungeon. In Hardmode, it is also sold by the Witch Doctor for 10 Gold if the Wizard is present. It emits light when placed. It fulfills a house's table requirement.

Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Bewitching Table grants the Bewitched buff, which increases the player's minion slots by 1. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

Unlike equipment buff items, the Bewitching Table must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 3×3 tiles being available.
Bezoar: The Bezoar is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Poisoned debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Hornets, Moss Hornets, and Toxic Sludges.
Binoculars: The Binoculars are a tool that can be held in order to shift the player's view based on the cursor location. They must be placed in the hotbar and selected. While highlighted in the hotbar, the screen view is scrolled a short distance away from the character, following the mouse pointer. The view becomes centered not on the player, but on a point almost halfway between the player and the cursor. The Binoculars have a 1/40 (2.5%) / 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu.
Biome Keys: Biome Keys are Hardmode items used to open the Biome Chests in the Dungeon. Opening a Chest consumes the key. Though unusable until Plantera is defeated, they can be dropped at any time during Hardmode. Each key has a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping from an enemy in the key's respective biome.

Any enemy in the biome that drops coins, except Meteor Heads, when killed has a chance of dropping a key, not just biome-exclusive enemies. Additionally, enemies in hybrid biomes have a chance to drop any key from their composite biomes. The type of key is determined by which biome the player currently is in, not the enemy killed.

Any Biome Key dropped prior to defeating Plantera will display the tooltip “It has been cursed by a powerful Jungle creature” and will be unable to open its respective chest until Plantera is defeated, although they are usable in other worlds that have Plantera defeated already.
Biome Sight Potion: The Biome Sight Potion is a buff potion which grants the Biome Sight buff when consumed. The buff highlights all tiles that are infected with The Corruption, The Crimson, or The Hallow in purple, red, and pink respectively, while in the dark. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Bird: The Bird, Blue Jay, and Cardinal are flying critters that can spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Much like the Vulture, Birds remain still until approached, whereupon they will fly away. Birds will occasionally chirp when nearby. Birds may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Birds have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Birds can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Bird / Blue Jay / Cardinal Cage). Once crafted, the Birds cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Birds can be spawned by the Bird Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Bird to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Birdie Rattle: The Birdie Rattle is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Lil' Harpy that follows the player. The Lil' Harpy, when summoned, will fly above and behind the player, and will behave similar to the Zephyr Fish, continually flying around and looking side to side. It will never land and can fly through blocks. The Birdie Rattle can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Gold.
Birds: The Bird, Blue Jay, and Cardinal are flying critters that can spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Much like the Vulture, Birds remain still until approached, whereupon they will fly away. Birds will occasionally chirp when nearby. Birds may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Birds have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Birds can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Bird / Blue Jay / Cardinal Cage). Once crafted, the Birds cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Birds can be spawned by the Bird Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Bird to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Black Belt: The Black Belt is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that grants a 1/10 (10%) chance to dodge an attack, including instances of damage taken from hazards such as traps and lava. A cloud of smoke surrounds the player when performing a dodge. The Black Belt has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance of being dropped by Bone Lees in the post-Plantera Dungeon.
Black Fairy Dust: Black Fairy Dust is a crafting material used solely to craft Tattered Fairy Wings. It is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave.
Black Graduation set: The Black Graduation set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Black Graduation Cap and the Black Graduation Gown. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) during a Waxing Gibbous.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Black Ink: Black Ink is a dye material that is dropped by Squids, which only spawn in the Ocean biome. Its sole purpose is to make Black Dye.
Black Lens: The Black Lens is a crafting material dropped by Demon Eyes and Wandering Eyes at a 1/100 (1%) chance.
Black Recluse: The Black Recluse is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in and around Spider Nests in the Cavern layer. It has a 1/10 (10%) chance to inflict the Acid Venom debuff for 4 / 8 / 10 seconds. In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), it gains a special spit attack that inflicts the Webbed debuff for 0.5–2.5 seconds.
Black Scorpion: The Scorpion and Black Scorpion are harmless critters that are most commonly found in a Desert. For detailed spawning conditions, see Notes.
Scorpions have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Scorpions can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scorpion/Black Scorpion Cage). Once crafted, the Scorpions cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Scorpions can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% (regular) / 15% (black) bait power.
Scorpions can be spawned by the Scorpion Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Black Slime: The Black Slime is a variety of slime that only spawns in the Cavern layer. When a Black Slime attacks, it has a chance to inflict the Darkness debuff, which decreases the radius that light sources will illuminate, making it more difficult to see.
Like most other slimes, the Black Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
On Desktop, Console, Mobile, and 3DS, they can rarely be found carrying bonus drops, which the player receives upon the slime's death.
Blackcurrant: The Blackcurrant is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking an Ebonwood or an Ebonwood Palm tree.
Blackened Fish: The Blackened Fish is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Blade Staff: The Blade Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons an Enchanted Dagger minion. It flies towards enemies and slashes through them repeatedly at a fast pace. It also has 25 armor penetration. Enchanted Daggers arrange themselves along a carousel above the player's head, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby. The Blade Staff has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime.

Its best modifier is generally Focused, Ballistic, or Worthy (see below for details), as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it. Although the Eager modifier is recognized in-game as its best modifier, the majority of enemies do not have enough defense for the extra armor penetration to provide a greater benefit, with the exception of high-defense bosses like Duke Fishron or the Empress of Light.
Blade of Grass: The Blade of Grass is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it fires a Leaf Blade projectile that travels upwards in a circle and homes in on enemies. The Leaf Blade projectile can pass through blocks, deals 25% of the weapon's damage (4 base damage), has 20 armor penetration, and can pierce two enemies. The sword and its projectiles both have a 1/4 (25%) chance of inflicting the Poisoned debuff for 7 seconds upon hit.
Bladed Glove: The Bladed Glove is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a roughly 1/2000 (0.05%) chance of being dropped by any weak enemy during the Halloween seasonal event. It has a very short range, but an exceptionally high attack speed.
Bladetongue: The Bladetongue is a Hardmode broadsword that can be obtained extremely rarely by fishing in the Crimson biome in any layer.

On enemy hits, it inflicts the Ichor debuff for 5–9 seconds and fires an ichor stream at a random angle in front of the player. The ichor stream is affected by gravity, deals 50% of the weapon's damage (27 base damage) and 70% of its knockback (base knockback of 4.025 (Average)), pierces 4 enemies before dissipating on the 5th hit, can bounce off blocks, and also inflicts the Ichor debuff for 3–7 seconds.
It is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Toxikarp, the Hallow's Crystal Serpent, and the Jungle's Barnacle Staff.
Blend-O-Matic: The Blend-O-Matic is a crafting station that is purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold. On the Old-gen console and 3DS, it can only be purchased at night. Its sole purpose is to craft Asphalt Blocks which are used to run faster when walked on.
Blessed Apple: The Blessed Apple is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Unicorn Mount, capable of an extra jump as well as the ability to sprint and charge through enemies, damaging them in the process. The Blessed Apple has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Unicorns.

Once a high speed is reached, the Unicorn emits a sparkle effect, and from that point on, it will be able to damage enemies on contact. Dashing through an enemy grants 0.1 seconds of invincibility frames.
Blindfold: The Blindfold is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Darkness debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Corrupt Slimes, Slimelings, Crimslimes, Dark Mummies, and Blood Mummies.
Blinkroot: Blinkroot is a type of herb that appears as stems with glowing dots. It grows naturally on Dirt or Mud Blocks, regardless of lighting or elevation, as long as the blocks bear no grass of any kind. Blinkroot can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Blinkroot Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles.

Blinkroot enters and exits its bloom state randomly. Its blooming is indicated by the yellow dots and pulsating yellow light emitted. Harvesting mature Blinkroot yields 1 Blinkroot item. Harvesting blooming Blinkroot yields 1 Blinkroot item and 1–3 Blinkroot Seeds. Harvesting blooming Blinkroot with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Blinkroots and 1–5 Blinkroot Seeds instead.
Both Blinkroot and Blinkroot Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.
Blinkroot Seeds: Blinkroot Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Blinkroots while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Blinkroots while they are fully grown. A Blinkroot plant switches between its blooming and non-blooming state at random. Its blooming state can be identified by the yellow dots on the ends of its fronds and the blinking light it emits. Each plant will drop 1–3 Blinkroot Seeds when harvested while blooming.

Blinkroot Seeds can be placed on Dirt and Mud Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Blinkroots. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Underground, but will only yield seeds when blooming.
Blizzard Staff: The Blizzard Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that is dropped from the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event with a 5.19%–10.37% (15.56%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave. When used, it causes a wide spread of icicles to rain from the sky, directed towards the cursor. It summons four icicles per use, which do not pierce enemies or pass through blocks.
Its best modifier is Mythical. It also makes the weapon fire six icicles per use instead of four.
Blizzard in a Balloon: The Blizzard in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the effects of the Blizzard in a Bottle and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to ~10½ tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 14½ tiles, for a total height of 25 tiles.

The total jump height of the Blizzard in a Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the total underwater jump height from 19 tiles (8 + 11 from Blizzard jump) to 16 tiles (7 + 9 from Blizzard jump).
Blizzard in a Bottle: The Blizzard in a Bottle is a pre-Hardmode accessory which works similarly to the Cloud in a Bottle, allowing the player to double-jump. Instead of a cloud being produced when the player jumps, a trail of snow is produced at the player's feet. The Blizzard jump goes 8 tiles into the air, totaling 14 tiles when put together with the first jump. The Blizzard in a Bottle has a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Boreal Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can also be crafted at a Crystal Ball.
Block-placing wands: Block-placing wands are special tools that allow the player to place blocks they would normally not be able to place. They do not consume any mana. Each wand consumes a specific material from the player's inventory (details listed below). There are 6 different block-placing wands.
Blood Butcherer: The Blood Butcherer is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it inflicts the Blood Butchered debuff upon enemy hits for 9 seconds and causing enemies to visibly bleed, dealing 4 damage per second (4 damage displayed every 1 second). Repeated attacks will cause the debuff to stack up to 5 times, for a total of 20 damage per second (20 damage displayed every 1 second).
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Light's Bane. The Blood Butcherer has a greater size and base damage than the Light's Bane, but has a slower speed.
Blood Crawler: The Blood Crawler is a pre-Hardmode enemy commonly found in The Crimson. In addition to walking, it can crawl on background walls.
Blood Eel: The Blood Eel is a flying Hardmode enemy that can be spawned by fishing in water during a Blood Moon. When the bobber dips and the player attempts to reel in a fish, a Blood Eel or another enemy has a chance to spawn within a few tiles of the bobber in place of a fish. Its behavior is rather similar to that of the Wyvern with being able to freely fly, though it moves considerably faster.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Blood Eel requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Blood Feeder: The Blood Feeder is a Hardmode enemy that spawn in pools of water in The Crimson during Hardmode. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) They have higher stats than Corrupt and Vicious Goldfish.
Blood Jelly: Jellyfish are enemies found in water. When underwater, they attack by propelling themselves towards the player in short bursts. When outside of water, they will be unable to move or pursue the player in any way. Jellyfish are able to jump out of the water to attack players, often leaving them stranded on land. Most varieties of Jellyfish produce light, making them easy to spot in dark areas. There are 5 Jellyfish variants, 3 of which only appear during Hardmode.

In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a Jellyfish will periodically become "electrified" (except for Fungo Fish). During this electrified state, it is invincible, and will constantly maintain its speed unless it comes into contact with a solid block or the water's surface. Certain attacks to Jellyfish in this state will hurt the player by 1.3× the contact damage of the Jellyfish (see Notes for details). Unlike other damage sources, this damage will not be reduced by banners.
Blood Lust Cluster: The Blood Lust Cluster is a pre-Hardmode axe.
Its Corruption counterpart is the War Axe of the Night.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Blood Mummy: Mummies are Hardmode enemies that spawn in the Desert biome and areas where Sand Blocks are present. They follow the Fighter AI, behaving similarly to Zombies.

There are several different types of Mummies: the standard Mummy, as well as the Dark Mummy, Light Mummy, and Blood Mummy. They spawn in Corrupted Deserts, Hallowed Deserts and Crimson Deserts, respectively.

Dark Mummies and Blood Mummies are 50% faster than other Mummies. All mummies receive a 100% speed increase when their health is reduced below 50%. In addition, Mummies inflict the following debuffs upon hitting the player:
Blood Orange: The Blood Orange is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Shadewood or a Shadewood Palm tree.
Blood Rain Bow: The Blood Rain Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen. When used, it converts any type of arrow into a spread of 1–3 streams of blood (average of 1.83 streams) to rain from the sky, directed towards the cursor. Each use only consumes one arrow. The streams dissipate upon contact with an enemy or a block.
Blood Squid: The Blood Squid is a flying Hardmode enemy summoned by the Dreadnautilus during a Blood Moon. It resembles a regular Squid, but is larger, redder-colored, and has multiple eyes on its body, similar to the Drippler. The Dreadnautilus always summons Blood Squids in groups of three.

The Blood Squid attempts to close in on the player before firing a single red Blood Shot projectile at the player, similar to the Dreadnautilus's own Blood Shots, but with higher damage. Like the Dreadnautilus, it recoils after each shot.
Blood Thorn: The Blood Thorn is a Hardmode magic weapon that summons three penetrating Blood Thorn projectiles upon use, which erupt from solid blocks and platforms to damage enemies near the player's cursor. It has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Hemogoblin Sharks.
Blood Zombie: The Blood Zombie is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a Zombie variant that only spawns during a Blood Moon. It acts mostly the same as normal Zombies, walking towards the player to deal contact damage while attempting to navigate around obstacles, and opening doors if they are in the way. However, it speeds up considerably the closer it gets to the player, and it generally has greater health, damage, and speed than most other Zombies. In Expert Mode, it moves even faster.
It does not have any variants, nor does it have an Armed variation in Expert Mode.
Bloodbath Dye: Bloodbath Dye is a dye purchased from the Dye Trader during a Blood Moon for 7 Gold 50 Silver. When applied, it gives the item an appearance similar to dripping blood.
Bloody Machete: The Bloody Machete is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that has a 1/2000 (0.05%) chance of being dropped by any weak enemy during the Halloween seasonal event. When thrown, it falls downward after reaching a medium range, then returns to the player upon contact with a block or an enemy. It also inflicts the Bleeding debuff on hit.
On the I am error secret world seed, the Bloody Machete has a chance of being obtained from any Chest.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Bloody Moscato: The Bloody Moscato is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It can be considered the Crimson counterpart to the Smoothie of Darkness.
Bloody Spine: The Bloody Spine is a boss-summoning item that summons the Brain of Cthulhu when used. It can only be used in The Crimson or Underground Crimson, at any time.
Bloody Tear: The Bloody Tear is an event-summoning item used to summon a Blood Moon. It can only be used at night, and attempting to use it during the day or while a Blood Moon is already active will not summon a Blood Moon, affect the ongoing Blood Moon, or consume the item.

The Bloody Tear has a 1/100 (1%) chance to be dropped from Blood Zombies and Dripplers, a 1/25 (4%) chance from Blood Eels, Hemogoblin Sharks, Wandering Eye Fish, and Zombie Mermen, a 1/10 (10%) chance from Clowns, and a 1/5 (20%) chance from The Bride and The Groom. The Bloody Tear can only be dropped during a Blood Moon, i.e. enemies killed after the Blood Moon has ended do not drop it. The exception to this are The Groom and The Bride, who can drop it at any time. Statue-spawned Blood Zombies and Dripplers can never drop a Bloody Tear.
Additionally, Dreadnautiluses have a 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%) chance of dropping it at any time.
Blowgun: The Blowgun is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 5 Gold. It is an indirect upgrade to the Blowpipe. When used, it fires Seeds and darts as ammunition. While a Blowgun is in a player's inventory, there is a chance that any vegetation growing on normal grass, in Clay Pots, and in Planter Boxes will drop Seeds. Flowers typically drop 4 Seeds at a time, while tall grass typically drops 1–2 Seeds.
Blowpipe: The Blowpipe is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being obtained from wooden Chests on the Surface or in the Underground layer. When used, it fires Seeds and darts as ammunition. While a Blowpipe is in a player's inventory, there is a chance that any vegetation growing on normal grass, in Clay Pots, and in Planter Boxes will drop Seeds. Flowers typically drop 4 Seeds at a time, while tall grass typically drops 1–2 Seeds.
Blue Acid Dye: Blue Acid Dye is a dye acquired as a random reward from the Dye Trader for giving him a Strange Plant. When equipped in a dye slot, it applies a dark blue rippling effect that pulses outward, similar to Acid Dye and Red Acid Dye. Items dyed by it can be seen in the dark, but do not emit light.
Blue Armored Bones: The Blue Armored Bones is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. Similar to Angry Bones, they come in multiple varieties, follow the Fighter AI, and can open closed doors after two or five hits. They also have a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Broken Armor debuff for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds.
Blue Armored Bones spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by brick walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Blue Berries: Blue Berries are a dye material and type of plant. Placed Blue Berries have the appearance of a blueberry bush. They can grow on regular grass or Jungle grass above surface. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Blue Dye.
Blue Bikini set: The Blue Bikini set is a vanity set consisting of the Blue Bikini Top and the Blue Bikini Bottom. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Blue Chicken Egg: The Blue Chicken Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Blue Chicken that follows the player. The Blue Chicken Egg can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 25 Gold.
Blue Cultist Archer: The Cultists are Hardmode, post-Golem enemies that spawn along with a Mysterious Tablet at the entrance to the Dungeon after Skeletron and Golem have been defeated. Four Cultists will appear there: two Cultist Archers and two Lunatic Devotees. Defeating all four of the Cultists causes the Lunatic Cultist to spawn instantly at their location, destroying the Mysterious Tablet in the process. Defeating the Lunatic Cultist then initiates the Lunar Events.

Until one of the Cultists is attacked, they are passive and deal no contact damage, and players can walk through them freely without activating them. Attacking any of the four will awaken the Archers, who will begin to fire Wooden Arrows using bows and will deal contact damage. Lunatic Devotees are always passive and never deal contact damage.

All four Cultists respawn and reset their location and initial passive state after 12 minutes (12 in-game hours), if the Lunatic Cultist was not summoned, if the player runs away or dies during the fight, when all four Celestial Pillars are destroyed, or when the world is closed and restarted. Restarting the world can be the fastest option to reset them to their original state.
The Lunatic Devotee and Cultist Archer require 25 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entries and corresponding banners, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Blue Fairy: The Pink Fairy, Green Fairy, and Blue Fairy are critters that emit light, which will attempt to lead the player to valuable treasures, such as Life Crystals, Chests, or ore deposits. They spawn in the bottom half of the Underground layer and in the Cavern layer, but only if at least one Fallen Log is present in the world on the surface (see Fallen Log § Notes for the exact area). If all Fallen Logs have been destroyed, they will no longer spawn independently. The three fairy variants all function identically.

Fairies can also spawn at Fallen Logs and from shaken Pearlwood trees on the surface at night. In this case, they will not lead players to treasure; instead, when approached, they try to flee much like Birds or Faelings. Unlike fairies spawned underground, these fairies can be caught with a Bug Net and carried around in the inventory. If released again, they act like the ones spawned underground and will attempt to lead the player to treasure. They can also be crafted into animated decorative furniture (Fairy jars). Once crafted, the fairies cannot be released again unless de-crafted via Shimmer.
They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Blue Graduation set: The Blue Graduation set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Blue Graduation Cap and the Blue Graduation Gown. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) during a Waning Crescent.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Blue Horseshoe Balloon: The Blue Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 75%, grants a double-jump, and grants +0.05 luck (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks, while the double-jump's height is increased from 5 blocks to 9 blocks, reaching a total of 19.5 blocks with both jumps.
Blue Jay: The Bird, Blue Jay, and Cardinal are flying critters that can spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Much like the Vulture, Birds remain still until approached, whereupon they will fly away. Birds will occasionally chirp when nearby. Birds may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Birds have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Birds can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Bird / Blue Jay / Cardinal Cage). Once crafted, the Birds cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Birds can be spawned by the Bird Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Bird to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Blue Jellyfish: Jellyfish are enemies found in water. When underwater, they attack by propelling themselves towards the player in short bursts. When outside of water, they will be unable to move or pursue the player in any way. Jellyfish are able to jump out of the water to attack players, often leaving them stranded on land. Most varieties of Jellyfish produce light, making them easy to spot in dark areas. There are 5 Jellyfish variants, 3 of which only appear during Hardmode.

In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a Jellyfish will periodically become "electrified" (except for Fungo Fish). During this electrified state, it is invincible, and will constantly maintain its speed unless it comes into contact with a solid block or the water's surface. Certain attacks to Jellyfish in this state will hurt the player by 1.3× the contact damage of the Jellyfish (see Notes for details). Unlike other damage sources, this damage will not be reduced by banners.
Blue Macaw: The Scarlet Macaw and Blue Macaw are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. They may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Macaws have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Macaws can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scarlet / Blue Macaw Cage). Once crafted, the Macaws cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Macaws can be spawned by the Macaw Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Blue Moon: The Blue Moon is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron flail that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes.
If the Sunfury is also in the player's inventory, then the Sunfury will be thrown out at the same time as the Blue Moon, but in the mirrored direction.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Blue Slime: The Blue Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that commonly spawns in Forest biomes during the daytime, as well at any time in the Underground layer. Blue Slimes only target the player when damaged, during the night, or at any time when underground.
Like most other slimes, the Blue Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
On Desktop, Console, Mobile, and 3DS, they can rarely be found carrying bonus drops, which the player receives upon the slime's death.
Blue Starry Block: The Blue Starry Block is an animated decorative block that depicts twinkling blue stars on a black background. It is the blue-themed variant of the Gold Starry Block.
Blue Starry Wall: Blue Starry Wall is a decorative wall crafted from Blue Starry Blocks. It is one of only a few animated background walls.
Bomb: The Bomb is an explosive that explodes 3 seconds after being thrown. The explosion breaks nearly all blocks, background walls, and furniture within a 4-tile radius, except explosion-proof objects. The explosion also deals 100 damage to all enemies, critters, and players in the radius, but not NPCs. The Bomb works in liquids. A lit Bomb can be defused by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, canceling the explosion and safely dropping the Bomb as an item for the player to pick it back up.

The Bomb can be purchased from the Demolitionist and Skeleton Merchant for 3 Silver each or obtained from Pots, Chests, by powering Bomb Statues, or as a drop from Undead Miners with a 18/25 (72%) chance. It also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
The Hardmode variant of the Bomb is the Power Bomb. Power Bombs have a greater radius and can explode early Hardmode ores, unlike the Bomb.
Bomb Fish: The Bomb Fish is an explosive that functions identically to the Sticky Bomb, but does not slow down in water. It is obtained through fishing, with the number obtained depending on the player's Fishing Power.
Bone: Bones are crafting materials and consumable ranged weapons. They are dropped by Angry Bones, Dark Casters, Cursed Skulls, and Librarian Skeletons which spawn in the Dungeon.
Bones are greatly affected by gravity, and arc similarly to Throwing Knives and Shurikens. Of these three consumable ranged weapons, Bones have the least range (Throwing Knives having the greatest).
Furthermore, Bones can be placed as blocks using the Bone Wand, upon which they become Bone Blocks.
Bone Arrow: The Bone Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 15 Copper each, during moon phases 1 (full), 2, 5 (new), and 6. Bone Arrows can pierce one enemy.
Bone Biter: Sand Sharks are Hardmode enemies only found in Desert biomes during a Sandstorm. They are able to "swim" through all varieties of Sand, Hardened Sand, and Sandstone Blocks, but will collide normally against any other block. When they draw near a player, they will lunge out of the sand to attack.
The Sand Shark itself only appears in ordinary Deserts. There are other variants for different versions of the Desert:
Bone Biter in the Corrupted Desert
Flesh Reaver in the Crimson Desert
Crystal Thresher in the Hallowed Desert
Bone Block: Bone Blocks are blocks that are placed by the Bone Wand at the cost of 1 Bone per block.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, mining them will drop Bones. There is no way to obtain the block as an item in these versions.

On the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, mining them will drop the Bone Block as an item. There is no way to convert them back into regular Bones. The block item cannot be used to craft Bone Block Walls or Bone furniture, which are instead made from raw Bones themselves, at a Bone Welder.
Bone Block Wall: The Bone Block Wall is a type of wall which is crafted from Bones. Despite the naming similarity to Bone Blocks, it has never been able to craft them, nor been used to craft them.
Bone Feather: The Bone Feather is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting material used solely to craft Bone Wings. It has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of being dropped by any Armored Bones variant (Blue, Rusty, or Hell Armored Bones) in the Dungeon after Plantera has been defeated.
Bone Glove: The Bone Glove is a pre-Hardmode accessory that throws ricocheting crossbones every time a weapon is used, at a maximum of once per second. The crossbones projectiles ricochet off walls three times or pierce two enemies before being destroyed, deal 25 classless damage, and additionally have 25 armor penetration. The Bone Glove is always dropped from Skeletron's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Bone Helm: The Bone Helm is a pre-Hardmode accessory that summons Shadow Hand projectiles to damage enemies. These Shadow Hands spawn a distance from enemies before flying at them, piercing anything in their path including through blocks. Their flight behavior mirrors the Shadow Hands found in the Deerclops fight, either flying straight or swerving harshly in flight. The Bone Helm is always dropped from Deerclops' Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Bone Javelin: The Bone Javelin is a consumable ranged weapon crafted from Sturdy Fossils. Upon hitting an enemy, it will stick to the enemy and inflict the Penetrated debuff for 15 seconds, dealing 3 damage per second (3 damage displayed every 1 second). Up to six Bone Javelins can be stuck onto an enemy, dealing a total of 18 damage per second (18 damage displayed every 1 second).
Bone Key: The Bone Key is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Skeletron Head that follows the player. The Baby Skeletron Head floats around the player and sometimes spins its head, similarly to Skeletron's spinning head attack or the Dungeon Guardians in general. This action may also occur if the player is a bit further away from the Skeletron Head. The Bone Key is always dropped by Dungeon Guardians. Because Dungeon Guardians have extremely high stats intended to instantly kill all players, this can be a difficult item to acquire.
Bone Lee: Bone Lee is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It moves at an extraordinary speed, deals large amounts of damage, and has high knockback resistance. It will also spawn at any time in the Dungeon regardless of the type of Dungeon wall present.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Bone Pickaxe: The Bone Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe that has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Undead Miners. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. Upon hitting an enemy, it releases a non-piercing lobbed bone projectile that is affected by gravity, and deals 75% of the pickaxe's damage (6 base damage) and its full knockback.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Bone Rattle: The Bone Rattle is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Face Monster that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Face Monster will appear to hold onto a flying Crimera-like creature to catch up to them. The Bone Rattle has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by the Brain of Cthulhu.
Bone Serpent: The Bone Serpent is a pre-Hardmode worm enemy that spawns in The Underworld. Due to their large size, speed, and high damage, they can be dangerous enemies to encounter, especially if they attack while the player is exploring a Ruined House.
Bone Sword: The Bone Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons. Upon hitting an enemy, it releases a non-piercing lobbed bone projectile that is affected by gravity, and deals 75% of the weapon's damage (14 base damage) and its full knockback.
Bone Throwing Knife: The Bone Throwing Knife is a consumable ranged weapon similar to Throwing Knives. It can hit up to 6 targets. Combined with fossil armor, it can be an effective weapon against the Eater of Worlds due to its piercing.
Bone Welder: The Bone Welder is a crafting station used to craft Bone furniture out of Bones and Gothic furniture out of Gothic Bricks, and can also craft Dungeon Shelves when combined with Ecto Mist (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Bone Welder can be found in the Dungeon, either inside Locked Gold Chests (1/8 (12.5%) chance for each chest) or placed on the ground. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it is also sold by the Steampunker when in a Graveyard.
Book: The Book is a crafting material used only to craft Bookcases, Pianos, and Librarian Blocks. It can also be placed as decoration on Flat-surface items. Books are found placed on the Dungeon's many shelves, where they can be freed with a pickaxe or drill. They can also be renewably obtained from Dungeon or Stockade Crates, and can be bought from the Wizard for 15 Silver each.
Book of Skulls: The Book of Skulls is a pre-Hardmode spell book that has a 36/343 (10.5%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Skeletron. When used, it fires slow-moving skull projectiles which home in on enemies, can pierce twice before dissipating on the third hit, can pass through blocks, and emit a fair amount of light.
Bookcases: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement.

There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.
Boomstick: The Boomstick is a pre-Hardmode gun. It can be found in Ivy Chests (21.72% chance) in the Underground Jungle, and also in Jungle Crates (19/100 (19%) chance). When used, it fires a spread of 3–4 bullets, consuming one piece of ammunition.
Booster Track: Booster Tracks are placeable furniture-type blocks that can be placed next to Minecart Tracks to automatically boost the speed of a Minecart that rides over it. The direction of the boost is indicated by the animated red arrow it displays, which can be toggled using a Hammer or wire. Each Booster Track increases speed by 20 mph, regardless of the Minecart variant used. The Booster Track can be purchased from the Mechanic for 50 Silver.
Boreal Crate: The Boreal Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Snow and Ice biome. Boreal Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in Frozen Chests. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Frozen Crate.
Boreal Wood: Boreal Wood is a type of wood harvested from Boreal trees found naturally growing in the Snow biome, or from Underground Cabins in the Ice biome. Boreal trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Snow Blocks above surface.
Boreal Wood Bow: The Boreal Wood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Boreal Wood Hammer: The Boreal Wood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Boreal Wood Sword: The Boreal Wood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword.
Boreal Wood Wall: Boreal Wood Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Boreal Wood.
Boreal Wood armor: Boreal Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Boreal Wood Helmet, Boreal Wood Breastplate, and Boreal Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Boreal Wood. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.
Boring Bow: The Boring Bow is an unimplemented item. It has no name set and will thus display as "ItemName.BoringBow". No other stats, behaviors, or associated projectiles exist for this item.
Bottle: A Bottle is a crafting material required to craft most potions. Like the Pink Vase, Mug, and different Cups, placing it (on most "flat-surface items" or a platform) allows it to act as a Placed Bottle where the player can craft potions. Bottles can also be "filled" when standing near water or honey, turning them into Bottled Water or Bottled Honey, respectively.
Bottles can be crafted from Glass and found in chests.
Bottled Honey: Bottled Honey is a pre-Hardmode crafting material and recovery potion. When used, it restores 80 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It also grants the player the Honey buff for 15 seconds. In addition to being crafted, Bottled Honey is also dropped by the Queen Bee, found in Bee Hives in the Underground Jungle.
Bottled Water: Bottled Water is a pre-Hardmode crafting material and recovery potion. It can be crafted at a sink or a body of water. Bottled Water mainly serves as the basis of almost every craftable potion in the game, and is also required for crafting flasks.
When used, it restores 30 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 45 seconds. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.
Bottomless Buckets: Bottomless Buckets are tools that are capable of placing an infinite amount of liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button. There are four different types of Bottomless Buckets, one for each type of liquid: Bottomless Water Bucket, Bottomless Lava Bucket, Bottomless Honey Bucket, and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket.

Bottomless Buckets can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at placing liquids when compared to standard buckets (especially when moving the cursor around while placing).
Boulder: The Boulder is a unique placeable foreground object that is stationary when placed. When unsupported, it falls and begins to roll away, picking up speed and damaging players, enemies, critters, and NPCs along its path. Boulders will also begin to roll if hit with a pickaxe or drill, meaning that they cannot be picked up again once placed.

Boulders will roll across flat surfaces and down slopes, but will break and disappear on contact with an obstacle. They deal 70 / 140 / 280 / 420 damage to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on contact, and can pierce through an unlimited number of entities. Boulders accelerate to a top speed of 27 tiles per second (36 mph) over the course of 2.17 seconds or 32 tiles.

Boulder traps occur naturally in the Underground and Cavern layers, and consist of a single Boulder in the ceiling, supported by six (2×3) Active Stone Blocks wired to an Orange Pressure Plate. Once a player walks onto the Pressure Plate, the Boulder falls down and begins rolling.

In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, Boulders will release 2–4 miniature Boulders when they break. These function identical to the Boulder projectile, but are smaller and deal 75% damage (157 / 210 / 315).

During world generation, a small number of Boulders are designated to drop a Friendly Boulder when they break. Depending on world size, 2 (small worlds), 4 (medium worlds), or 6 (large worlds) Boulders out of all the Boulders in the world are selected for this. This number is doubled in No Traps.
Boulder Block: Boulder Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks crafted from Boulders. Their main use is crafting Boulder furniture and Boulder Walls. They are less efficient to craft than Stone Slab, but are significantly more efficient than Gray Brick as an intermediate crafting step for Stone-based furniture.
Boulder Wall: Boulder Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Boulder Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Bouncy Bomb: The Bouncy Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Bomb, but bounces off blocks more intensely.
Bouncy Boulder: The Bouncy Boulder is a placeable object that begins to roll and bounce when it becomes unsupported. Once it is in motion, it will bounce several times before coming to a stop. Its motion is similar to a Bouncy Bomb but faster, and it does damage like a Boulder. It rarely spawns naturally in most worlds, but is more common in Celebration Mk 10, No Traps, and Zenith worlds.
Bouncy Dynamite: Bouncy Dynamite is an explosive that functions like Dynamite, but bounces off blocks more intensely.
Bouncy Glowstick: The Bouncy Glowstick is a consumable light source that bounces off surfaces while also providing light. Bouncy Glowsticks are the opposite of Sticky Glowsticks, bouncing off of surfaces instead of sticking to them.
Bouncy Grenade: The Bouncy Grenade is an explosive consumable ranged weapon made of Pink Gel and Grenades. Instead of rolling or sticking in place upon contact with tiles, it will bounce and retain much of its momentum.
Like normal Grenades, they will detonate upon touching an enemy, or the player that threw it.
Bouncy Slime: The Bouncy Slime is a Hardmode slime and boss servant that is summoned by Queen Slime alongside Crystal Slimes and Heavenly Slimes. It shoots Bouncy Gel projectiles at the player every 0.67 / 0.5 seconds.
Bowl of Soup: The Bowl of Soup is a food item crafted at the Cooking Pot. When consumed, it grants the Plenty Satisfied buff. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Bowls: Bowls are a type of decorative furniture that can be placed on flat-surface items. Unlike plates, food cannot be placed in bowls. Only the regular Bowl can be used in crafting.
The regular Bowl can also occasionally be found in the Dungeon on top of Tables and Work Benches.
Brain Scrambler: The Brain Scrambler is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that appears during the Martian Madness event. It fires green laser projectiles, at a maximum fire rate of once every 0.67 seconds (40 ticks), which have a chance to inflict the Confused debuff.
Brain Scrambler (item): The Brain Scrambler is a Hardmode, post-Golem mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Scutlix Mount. The Brain Scrambler has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to drop from Scutlix Gunners during the Martian Madness event.
The Scutlix Mount offers increased acceleration and land speed (41 mph top speed), increased jump height (21.88 tiles / 43.76 feet), and cancels fall damage.

Additionally, its eyes automatically fire two damaging red lasers at nearby enemies once every 0.33 seconds. The laser projectiles deal 150 base damage and cannot be boosted by any damage bonuses, cannot critically strike, and inflict no knockback. The Scutlix can only target enemies within 53.125 tiles in its field of vision, which is a roughly 120° cone in front of it, and cannot target enemies behind itself unless the player manually turns it around to face them, which also occurs when the player attacks in that direction.
Brain Suckler: The Brain Suckler is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist flying enemy that spawns in the area of the Nebula Pillar during the Lunar Events. It latches onto the player's head, dealing large amounts of damage at a steady rate, while also inflicting the Obstructed debuff for the remainder of the time it is on the player. The debuff causes the player's screen to darken significantly, except for a small area around the player, similar to the Blackout debuff. It additionally has the effect of Bleeding, preventing natural health regeneration.
Brain in a Jar: The Brain in a Jar is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Spider Brain, a miniature version of the Brain of Cthulhu, that follows the player. The Brain in a Jar has a 1/4 (25%) of being dropped by the Brain of Cthulhu in Master Mode.
Brain of Confusion: The Brain of Confusion is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from the Brain of Cthulhu's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. It grants the following effects while equipped:

Upon taking damage, the player has a 1/6 (16.67%) of dodging an attack, negating damage from that attack. Upon dodging, the player also receives the Cerebral Mindtrick debuff for four seconds. Despite being a debuff, it increases critical strike chance and summon damage by 10%. While the debuff is active, the player cannot dodge another attack.
Upon taking damage, nearby enemies have a 3/5 (60%) chance of receiving the Confused debuff. The chance, duration, and area of effect of the debuff are based on the amount of damage taken.
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Worm Scarf.
Brain of Cthulhu: The Brain of Cthulhu is a pre-Hardmode, Crimson-themed boss. Fighting the boss and its attendant Creepers is the only way to obtain Tissue Samples, and is one of the ways to obtain usable quantities of Crimtane Ore. Defeating the Brain of Cthulhu for the first time also allows the Tavernkeep NPC to spawn as the Unconscious Man, and allows meteorites to land.
The Brain of Cthulhu is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Eater of Worlds. Unlike its Corruption counterpart, however, it does not have a mechanical equivalent in Hardmode.
While the Brain of Cthulhu is alive, the music Boss 3 will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Bramble Crate: The Bramble Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Jungle. Bramble Crates contain items found in standard crates, and they always contain an item normally found in Ivy Chests within Jungle Shrines. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Jungle Crate.
Brand of the Inferno: The Brand of the Inferno is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss broadsword. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance of inflicting the Hellfire debuff for five seconds on hit and also allows the player to parry incoming damage while equipped with a shield.

While holding the Brand of the Inferno with any equipped shield (excluding the Huntress's Buckler), pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button will cause the player to raise the shield. When timed correctly, up to 0.33 seconds before taking a hit, the enemy's attack will be parried, which negates the contact damage being dealt to the player, deals 200% of the contact damage of the attacking enemy, inflicts a knockback value of 5 (Average), and grants the player 30 invincibility frames (60 with the Cross Necklace equipped). Successfully parrying an attack also grants the Striking Moment buff, causing the next melee-based attack to deal 500% or five times its usual base damage for the next five seconds. Alternatively, if the shield is held in place, 20 defense is temporarily gained; this lasts until the shield is lowered.
The Brand of the Inferno is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3.
Breaker Blade: The Breaker Blade is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. It has a larger size than most other swords. It deals 250% damage (175 base damage) to enemies at 90% health or higher.
Breathing Reed: The Breathing Reed is a tool that aids in underwater breathing, and also functions as a broadsword. It has a 9/40 (22.5%) chance of being found in Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates.

When selected, the Breathing Reed is held above the player. This slows down the rate at which their breath meter depletes, and halves the rate at which they lose health while drowning. The reed's tip does not need to be above the surface of the water for this to take effect. The player's breath meter refills as soon as the tip of the reed is outside of water, but not within a block.
Brick Layer: The Brick Layer is a construction accessory that is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. While equipped, it grants +50% placement speed when placing blocks.
Bride of Frankenstein set: The Bride of Frankenstein set is a vanity set that can be obtained from a Goodie Bag with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance. It consists of a Bride of Frankenstein Mask and Bride of Frankenstein Dress.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Broken Bat Wing: The Broken Bat Wing is a rare Hardmode crafting material used solely to craft Bat Wings. It has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped by Vampires during a Solar Eclipse.
Broken Hero Sword: The Broken Hero Sword is a Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting material that has a 1/4 (25%) / 7/16 (43.75%) chance of being dropped by Mothrons.
Bubble: Bubbles are animated background furniture blocks, which have special behavior regarding liquids, interacting as if the Bubble was a solid block. When Bubbles are placed together in groups, they connect to make a larger Bubble or more complex structures.
Bubbles are purchased from the Party Girl for 2 Silver each during Hardmode.
Grates function as the opposite of Bubbles, acting as solid blocks but allowing liquids to flow through.
Bubble Gun: The Bubble Gun is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it rapidly fires a large spread of short-range bubbles, with three bubbles per use. Bubble projectiles gradually slow down and dissipate upon contact with an enemy or block, or after 1.67 seconds.
Bubble Machine: The Bubble Machine is a novelty furniture mechanism purchased from the Party Girl for 4 Gold (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) during the day / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) at any time. When placed, it continuously produces bubbles. These bubbles are purely visual, have no functional effect, and can be produced infinitely at no cost.

Each bubble is of a random size, and a random one of four possible colors: pink, purple, green, or blue. With no obstacles in the way, bubbles last for random durations. They will pop on contact with characters or foreground blocks.
It can be activated and deactivated via wire, but is always on by default when first placed.
Bubble Wand: The Bubble Wand is an auto-swing novelty item that produces rainbow-colored bubbles. The bubbles are purely visual, have no functional effect, and can be produced infinitely at no cost. The Bubble Wand is purchased from the Party Girl for 5 Gold.

Each bubble is of a random size, and a random one of four possible colors: Pink, purple, green, or blue. With no obstacles in the way, bubbles last for random durations. They will pop on contact with characters or foreground blocks.
Bubblegum Block: The Bubblegum Block is a Hardmode building material crafted from Stone Blocks and Orichalcum Ore. When placed, it resembles Stone Blocks coated with bubblegum. It is essentially the Orichalcum Ore's equivalent of a brick.
Bubblegum Block Wall: Bubblegum Block Wall is a background wall crafted from Bubblegum Blocks.
Buccaneer set: The Buccaneer set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Buccaneer Bandana, Buccaneer Tunic, and Buccaneer Pantaloons. Each piece has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Pirate Deckhands, Pirate Corsairs, Pirate Deadeyes, and Pirate Crossbowers during the Pirate Invasion event.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Buckets: Buckets are tools used to carry water, lava, or honey, allowing them to be removed or placed. With an Empty Bucket, pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on any sufficient body of liquid collects it, which replaces the Empty Bucket with the respective Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, or Honey Bucket. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button again will deposit the liquid at the location of the cursor, wherein the filled bucket is again replaced with an Empty Bucket. Each bucket holds one tile of liquid. Shimmer cannot be collected with standard buckets.

When an Empty Bucket is dropped as an item into the world (with the Throw button) while it is raining, and there are no background walls behind the dropped item, it will turn into a Water Bucket after some time has passed. Empty Buckets will not fill under Rain Clouds or Magic Droppers.

The Bottomless Water Bucket, Bottomless Lava Bucket and Bottomless Honey Bucket act as infinite water, lava, and honey placing buckets, whereas the Super Absorbant Sponge, Lava Absorbant Sponge, and Honey Absorbant Sponge are essentially infinite Empty Buckets that accept only water, lava or honey, respectively. They also add and remove liquids at a slightly faster speed than their normal bucket counterparts (especially when moving the cursor around while filling/draining).
Bug Net: The Bug Net is a tool used to capture most critters as inventory items. It is swung like a broadsword, but it deals no damage. The Bug Net is nearly required in order to go fishing, as it is the initial and primary method of obtaining bait. Most critters that are insects, worms, or snails can function as bait once captured.
The Bug Net can be purchased from the Merchant for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 25 Silver / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 1 Gold.

The Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are upgraded versions of the Bug Net that are bigger, swing faster, and can destroy tall grass, vines, and uproot plants just like swords and other weapons do, despite dealing no damage. They are also able to catch Underworld critters (Lavafly (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Hell Butterfly (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Magma Snail (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)), unlike the standard Bug Net; attempting to catch one with a standard Bug Net will deal 1 damage to the player and inflict the On Fire! debuff for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 13 seconds.
Buggy: Buggy is one of three critters that occasionally spawn in the Jungle or Underground Jungle biome when a player breaks a plant, the others being Sluggy (more common) and Grubby (most common). Buggy is the rarest of the three. Buggy has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Buggy can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Buggy Cage). Once crafted, Buggy cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Buggy can be used as bait for fishing, with 40% bait power.
Buggy can be spawned by the Buggy Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Builder Potion: The Builder Potion is a buff potion that grants the Builder buff when consumed. It grants the following effects:
+25% placement speed when placing blocks and walls

This lasts for 45 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Builder Potions can be found in pots and chests.
Bundle of Balloons: The Bundle of Balloons is an accessory that allows the wearer to perform a quadruple jump, as well as increasing the player's jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%. Each of the jumps has an effect from the different combined items: sandstorm jump, then blizzard jump, then cloud jump.
Crafting this item requires three of the variants of Cloud in a Balloon, which in turn requires a total of 3 Shiny Red Balloons. In particular it requires the relatively rare Sandstorm in a Bottle.
Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons: The Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons is an accessory which combines the functionalities of the Bundle of Balloons and the Lucky Horseshoe.

When equipped, it allows the wearer to perform a quadruple jump, as well as increasing the player's jump duration by 33%, jump speed by 30%, and luck by 0.05. Each of the jumps has an effect from the different combined items: sandstorm jump, then blizzard jump, then cloud jump. Having it equipped also prevents the player from taking fall damage.
Bundled Party Balloons: Bundled Party Balloons are a vanity accessory purchased from the Clothier for 2 Gold while a Party is active. When worn, the balloons will be shown being held by the player, bobbing up and down.
The Bundled Party Balloons cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Bunny: The Bunny is a harmless critter that spawns in the Forest biome. They are the most common critters in Terraria, and are usually the first ones a new player will see.
Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Bunny Cage). Once crafted, the Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Bunnies can be spawned by the Bunny Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Bunny to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile Powder/Vicious Powder, Bunnies will turn into Corrupt Bunnies or Vicious Bunnies.
During Halloween, Christmas, or a Party, each Bunny has a 2/3 (66.67%) chance to spawn wearing a Green Slime costume, Santa costume, or Party Hat, respectively, in that order.
Gem Bunnies spawn near towns in the Cavern layer.
Bunny Cannon: The Bunny Cannon is a Hardmode placeable furniture/weapon. It can be purchased from the Pirate for 50 Gold when the Party Girl is present and one of the mechanical bosses has been defeated. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Bunny Cannon fires an arcing Explosive Bunny projectile that bounces off blocks and pierces an infinite amount of targets. The projectile loses 50% of its momentum every time it bounces, and once it has lost most of its momentum, it will (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) transform into an Explosive Bunny critter / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) explode after several seconds. If the projectile lasts for 10 seconds without losing enough momentum, it will explode. The projectile and its explosion deal 350 classless damage and knockback of 8 (Very strong), and do not destroy blocks. The Bunny Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Bunny Cannons in the world.

The angle of a placed Bunny Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Bunny Cannon to rotate it in that direction, or tapping the side of the Bunny Cannon. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, though the arcing trajectory of the Explosive Bunnies can be used to hit targets below the emplacement. Each rotation tilts the Bunny Cannon by one step (22.5°).

(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Bunny Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either shoot an explosive bunny or rotate toward the side the Wire is on. When a Bunny Cannon is fired with this method, there is a cooldown of 1 minute 8 seconds before that specific Bunny Cannon can be fired again by wiring signal, and a cooldown of 7 seconds before any other Bunny Cannon in the world can be fired by wiring signal. Torches can be still used to fire Bunny Cannons during this cooldown.
Explosive Bunny critters spawned by the cannon will disappear in a puff of smoke when attempting to capture it with Bug Net and deal no damage on death.
Bunny Hood: The Bunny Hood is a vanity headgear item. It has a 1/75 (1.33%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Bunnies and Vicious Bunnies (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). On the Nintendo 3DS version, it can also be dropped by Diseaster Bunnies or Lepus.
Bunny License: The Bunny License is a consumable item that can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold after filling out 45% (246 entries) of the Bestiary.
