Upon use, the status message "The license teleports away to the bunny delivery service..." is displayed. Following this status message, a Town Bunny will move into an available house the next morning. Using a second Bunny License when a Town Bunny is already present in the current world displays the status message "Pet Exchange: Successful!" and causes it to be "exchanged": the Town Bunny releases a puff of smoke and has its breed and name rerolled immediately.
Bunny Stew: The Bunny Stew is a food item crafted at the Cooking Pot. When consumed, it grants the Well Fed buff. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Bunny set: The Bunny set is a vanity set composed of the Bunny Tail and Bunny Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a First Quarter or a Waxing Gibbous for 6 Gold (set).
Burger: The Burger is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Burger has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Crimeras and Eaters of Souls. Statue-spawned Eaters of Souls do not drop it, as it is a food item.
Burning Hades Dye: Burning Hades Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When applied, it turns the item orange and adds fire effects.
Butcher: The Butcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. It slowly builds up speed over time, similarly to an Antlion Charger, and wields a bloodied chainsaw that deals heavy damage to players on contact. As the Butcher takes damage, its movement speed will increase.
Butcher's Chainsaw: The Butcher's Chainsaw is a Hardmode, post-Plantera chainsaw that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance to drop from Butchers during the Solar Eclipse event. Upon hitting an enemy, it fires a spread of 2–5 glowing sparks that are lightly affected by gravity, can pierce once before dissipating on the second hit, deal 50% of the weapon's damage (60 base damage), and inflict 20% of its knockback (base knockback of 1.6 (Very weak)). Sparks also have a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Hellfire debuff for 1–4 seconds.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Butcher's set: The Butcher's set is a Hardmode, post-Plantera vanity set consisting of the Butcher Mask, Butcher's Bloodstained Apron, and Butcher's Bloodstained Pants. Each piece has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Butchers during the Solar Eclipse event.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Butterflies: Butterflies are small critters that can naturally spawn on Surface in Forest and the Hallow, and also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. In both cases, they can only spawn during daytime if wind speed is lower than 20 mph, and if it is not currently raining. There are 8 variants of ordinary Butterflies with different appearences, chosen randomly when they spawn. They can be caught with a Bug Net and carried in the inventory.

When an ordinary Butterfly is being spawned, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance (affected by luck) for it to be replaced by a Gold Butterfly, which can be caught with a Bug Net and crafted into Golden Delight.

The Hell Butterfly (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can naturally spawn in the Underworld during daytime. It can also spawn from shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld, or from destroying wild Ash grass plants. It can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Attempting to catch it with a standard Bug Net will not work, and the player will take 1 damage and be inflicted with On Fire! for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 12.5 seconds.
All Butterflies can be crafted into butterfly jars, and can be be used as bait for fishing.
Butterfly: Butterflies are small critters that can naturally spawn on Surface in Forest and the Hallow, and also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. In both cases, they can only spawn during daytime if wind speed is lower than 20 mph, and if it is not currently raining. There are 8 variants of ordinary Butterflies with different appearences, chosen randomly when they spawn. They can be caught with a Bug Net and carried in the inventory.

When an ordinary Butterfly is being spawned, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance (affected by luck) for it to be replaced by a Gold Butterfly, which can be caught with a Bug Net and crafted into Golden Delight.

The Hell Butterfly (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can naturally spawn in the Underworld during daytime. It can also spawn from shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld, or from destroying wild Ash grass plants. It can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Attempting to catch it with a standard Bug Net will not work, and the player will take 1 damage and be inflicted with On Fire! for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 12.5 seconds.
All Butterflies can be crafted into butterfly jars, and can be be used as bait for fishing.
Butterfly Dust: Butterfly Dust is a rare Hardmode crafting material used solely to craft Butterfly Wings. It has a 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped by Moths in the Underground Jungle.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, at least one mechanical boss must be defeated before it will drop.
Butterfly jars: Butterfly jars are pieces of decorative furniture created by combining a butterfly, captured with a Bug Net, with a Bottle. By throwing a butterfly jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the butterfly as an item.
Butterfly jars function the same way as cages for other critters. They have an animated sprite when placed down, and the butterflies will fly around inside the jars.
Cactus: Cactus is a crafting material obtained by harvesting Cactus plants, using an axe or chainsaw just like with trees. In addition to crafting, Cactus can be used as a building material.
Cactus Pickaxe: The Cactus Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks weaker than Meteorite.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Cactus Sword: The Cactus Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword.
Cactus Wall: Cactus Wall is a background wall made from Cactus.
Cactus armor: Cactus armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Cactus Helmet, Cactus Breastplate, and Cactus Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Cactus.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
A Thorns effect, which causes the player to deal 15 / 30 / 45 damage and inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on enemies upon contact.
Cages: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item.
Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages.

Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.
Calming Potion: The Calming Potion is a buff potion which grants the Calm buff when consumed. The buff reduces the enemy spawn rate by 39%, and the maximum number of enemies on-screen is reduced by 40%. This lasts for 12 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Calming Potions can be found in Pots and Crates.
Campfires: Campfires are a type of furniture and crafting station that emit light and grant the Cozy Fire buff to players in their vicinity, which provides 10% increased innate health regeneration and additionally grants 0.5 HP/s constant regeneration.
The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the campfire, similar to Heart Lanterns and Sunflowers.
Campfires are also minor crafting stations, and uniquely, campfires are used to cook Marshmallow on a Stick (see their page for details).

Campfires can be toggled off and on with ⚷ Open / Activate, which extinguishes the flame, light, and disables the Cozy Fire buff. They can also be extinguished and lit with the Water Gun and Slime Gun respectively, and as mechanisms, they can be toggled with wire. Campfires are extinguished by rain in The Constant special world seed.
Can Of Worms: The Can Of Worms is a consumable grab bag item, which when opened with ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory, contains 5–11 different worms. Cans Of Worms can be found in Chests on the surface.
Candelabras: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water.
There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 / 12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.
Candles: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms.

Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.
Candy Cane Blocks: Candy Cane Blocks are blocks that are dropped in stacks of 20–49 from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 16.803% in pre-Hardmode and 15.683% in Hardmode. They have no value other than as building material, and in crafting Candy Cane Wall. Despite them both being Candy Cane Blocks, they do not "merge" when placed next to each other.
Candy Cane Pickaxe: The Candy Cane Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. It is obtained from Presents dropped during the Christmas event, with a chance of 0.634% in pre-Hardmode and 0.592% in Hardmode.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Candy Cane Sword: The Candy Cane Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 0.639% (pre-Hardmode) / 0.596% (Hardmode) chance to be obtained from Presents dropped during the Christmas event.
Candy Cane Walls: Candy Cane Walls are background walls crafted from Candy Cane Blocks. They can only be obtained during Christmas, but will remain in the world after Christmas passes.
Candy Corn Rifle: The Candy Corn Rifle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that consumes Candy Corn as ammunition. When used, it rapidly fires Candy Corn shots that pierce up to two enemies and ricochet up to four times, dissipating on their fifth impact or upon hitting a third enemy. The projectiles are affected by gravity. The Candy Corn Rifle also has a base 10% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%, and has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance not to consume ammunition.

The Candy Corn Rifle is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Candy Corn Rifle is always accompanied by 50 to 100 Candy Corn. Additional Candy Corn can also be bought from the Arms Dealer for 5 Copper each if the Candy Corn Rifle is in the player's inventory.
Cannon: The Cannon is a Hardmode placeable furniture/weapon, purchased from the Pirate for 25 Gold. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Cannon fires an arcing Cannonball that explodes upon contact with a block. The Cannonball can also pierce through three enemies, exploding upon the fourth hit. The Cannonball and its explosion deal 300 classless damage and knockback of 8 (Very strong), and do not destroy blocks. The Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Cannons in the world.

The angle of a placed Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Cannon to rotate it in that direction, or tapping the side of the Cannon. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, though the arcing trajectory of the Cannonballs can be used to hit targets below the emplacement. Each rotation tilts the Cannon by one step (22.5°).

(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the Wire is connected, it will either shoot a Cannonball or rotate toward the side the Wire is on. When a Cannon is fired with this method, there is a cooldown of 10 seconds before that specific Cannon can be fired again by wiring signal, and a cooldown of 2 seconds before any other Cannon in the world can be fired by wiring signal. Torches can be still used to fire Cannons during this cooldown.
Cannonball: The Cannonball is a type of decorative block sold by the Pirate for 2 Silver each.
Capes: Capes are vanity accessories which provide no stats or bonuses. Most are purchased from the Traveling Merchant, though the Hunter Cloak (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be purchased from the Clothier and the Prince Cape (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is exclusively sold by the Princess (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Capricorn set: The Capricorn set is a vanity set consisting of the Capricorn Helmet, the Capricorn Chestplate, the Capricorn Hooves, and the Capricorn Tail. It is one of the six sets that were added as part of the Journey's End Vanity Contest; the original concept was submitted by R-MK.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The leggings of this vanity have the unique feature of being able to switch from tail to legs and vice-versa via the ⚷ Open / Activate key when they are not equipped.
Captain armor: Captain armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Captain Hat, Captain Vest, and Captain Pants.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
−24% enemy spawn rates and −30% maximum enemy count
Captain armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Angler armor, still providing the set bonus. The only difference is the defense.
Cardinal: The Bird, Blue Jay, and Cardinal are flying critters that can spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Much like the Vulture, Birds remain still until approached, whereupon they will fly away. Birds will occasionally chirp when nearby. Birds may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Birds have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Birds can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Bird / Blue Jay / Cardinal Cage). Once crafted, the Birds cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Birds can be spawned by the Bird Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Bird to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Carrot: The Carrot is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Bunny that follows the player. If the player gets too far away from the bunny, it will fly at a fast speed while emitting a trail of smoke to catch up to the player. The color of the bunny's fur is defined by the shirt color chosen for the character, meaning the color can be changed using a Dresser. The Carrot is only available to players in the Terraria Collector's Edition and Terraria 15th Anniversary Collector's Edition, and will automatically appear in the inventory of any newly generated characters.
Carton of Milk: The Carton of Milk is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Carton of Milk has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons. Statue-spawned Skeletons do not drop it, as it is a food item.
Cascade: The Cascade is a pre-Hardmode-exclusive, post-Skeletron yoyo that has a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of being dropped by any enemy in or near The Underworld. Once Hardmode begins, it will no longer drop, being replaced by the Hel-Fire.

On every 2nd yoyo hit, the Cascade shoots a fiery explosion towards the nearest enemy within a 13-tile radius. The fiery explosion deals 200% of the Cascade's damage (54 base damage) and its full knockback, but does not pierce. The Cascade and its explosion both have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 1–4 seconds.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Cat Ears: Cat Ears are a headpiece vanity item that can be obtained from Goodie Bags during Halloween with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance.
Cat License: The Cat License is a consumable item that can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold.

Upon use, the status message "The license teleports away to the cat delivery service..." is displayed. Following this status message, a Town Cat will move into an available house the next morning. Using a second Cat License when a Town Cat is already present in the current world displays the status message "Pet Exchange: Successful!" and causes it to be "exchanged": the Town Cat releases a puff of smoke and has its breed and name rerolled immediately.
Cat set: The Cat set is a vanity set consisting of the Cat Mask, Cat Shirt, and Cat Pants. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to be dropped by Goodie Bags.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Its male and female variants look identical.
Catacomb: The Catacomb is a decorative item that can be placed on background walls in a manner similar to a painting. It resembles a rectangular pit in the wall with a skeleton resting inside. The Catacomb can appear with one of three different frame styles, and one of three different skeleton positions. Catacombs can be found on the walls deep within a Dungeon with tiled walls.
Catalyst Band: The Catalyst Band is a Hardmode accessory item made by combining a Poison Barb and a Philosopher's Stone at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Arrows fired by the player inflict the Poisoned debuff for 1.5 seconds.
All player's attacks inflict the Accelerated Afflictions debuff for 5 seconds, which doubles damage from blood-loss, flame, and toxin debuffs (see Notes for complete list).
Cattiva: Cattiva is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Cattiva minion. It runs and jumps towards enemies, dealing contact damage. When Cattiva is falling and its target is more than 6.25 tiles above it, it can also perform a double jump with visuals similar to the Cloud in a Bottle to reach its target. Unlike the double jumps used by the player, Cattiva does not need to land on the ground to refresh its double jump and can use it endlessly while mid-air.

Cattiva can also mine alongside the player with a pickaxe power equivalent to 41% (approximately that of the Iron Pickaxe) and mining speed of 16. It will continue to mine even after the player stops, as long as the player is still nearby. Cattiva will also cut down trees and cacti alongside the player, either cutting the same tree/cactus or another one nearby. It has an axe power of 171% when cutting trees and an axe power of 57% when cutting cacti, as well as a chopping speed of 16 in both cases. Only one copy of Cattiva can be summoned at a time; additional uses of the summon weapon do not summon additional minions, nor do they improve the existing minion. Like other Pals, Cattiva can be petted using ⚷ Open / Activate.

Cattiva has a rare chance to spawn on Grass, Jungle grass, Snow, or Ice blocks above surface during daytime if the player is not in a Graveyard biome, but it cannot spawn in the center 1/4 of the world. It is initially spawned as the distressed Cattiva, with two Goblin Archers spawned around it. After killing both Goblin Archers (or making them despawn), Cattiva will turn into its item form when the player is within 6.25 tiles from it.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Cave Bat: The Cave Bat is a common pre-Hardmode bat enemy found only in the Cavern layer. It is fairly small and can be difficult to hit with certain weapons. One is to proceed with caution when entering caves early on, as Cave Bats can pose a moderate threat when one is not prepared to deal with them. In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), they can inflict the Feral Bite debuff, making them more dangerous. Like most other bats, they cannot enter water.
Cave Walls: The Cave Dirt Wall, Craggy Stone Wall, Fractured Stone Wall, Mottled Stone Wall, Old Stone Wall, Rocky Dirt Wall, Rough Dirt Wall, Stalactite Stone Wall, and Worn Stone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground and Cavern layers, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on the Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
The Craggy Stone, Fractured Stone, Mottled Stone, and Stalactite Stone Walls are unavailable on the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version.
Celebration: The Celebration is a Hardmode, post-Golem launcher that fires two firework rocket projectiles at once, consuming one rocket. The firework rockets travel for 0.75 seconds before exploding. The Celebration can be purchased from the Party Girl for 80 Gold.
Celebration Mk2: The Celebration Mk2 is a Hardmode launcher that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When used, it consumes rockets and fires one of seven special rocket types, distinguished by color. The rockets are affected by gravity to varying extents and explode upon impact with blocks. Although their base damage, critical strike chance, and knockback are identical, they behave differently:
The Celebration Mk2 also has a 1/2 (50%) chance not to consume ammunition.
Its best modifier is Unreal, Godly or Demonic, as it does not benefit from attack speed and velocity modifiers.
Celestial Cuffs: The Celestial Cuffs are a pre-Hardmode accessory that grant the following effects while equipped:
Increases the pickup range for Stars by 18.75 tiles.
Restores mana when the player takes damage. Mana restored is equal to the damage of the attack before factoring defense and damage reduction.
Celestial Emblem: The Celestial Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that offers 15% increased magic damage and a 18.75-tile increased pickup range for Stars (21.375 tile total range).
Celestial Magnet: The Celestial Magnet is a pre-Hardmode accessory that greatly increases the pickup range for Stars. The increase in pickup range is 18.75 tiles, extending the base range of 2.625 tiles to 21.375 tiles. This effect does not stack with the Celestial Magnet's upgrades.
The Celestial Magnet has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being found inside Skyware Chests on Floating Islands, as well as a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Sky Crates and Azure Crates.
Celestial Shell: The Celestial Shell is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that combines the stat-boosting powers of the Celestial Stone with the transformation powers of the Moon Shell, allowing both of their effects to happen simultaneously while taking only one accessory slot.
Celestial Sigil: The Celestial Sigil is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist boss-summoning item that summons the Moon Lord when used. It can be used in any biome, at any time. Rather than summoning the Moon Lord instantly, it triggers a 12-second countdown before he spawns.
The Celestial Sigil can only be used under the following circumstances:
There is no invasion event active, including the Lunar Events.
The Moon Lord is not already being summoned.
The Mysterious Tablet is not visible to any player.
Celestial Starboard: The Celestial Starboard is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord wing-type accessory. In addition to granting remarkable flight capabilities, it has both hover and upwards boost capability. At its top speed, it travels at 82 mph horizontal, 115 mph vertical, and 51 mph while falling. The Celestial Starboard is always dropped from the Moon Lord's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Celestial Stone: The Celestial Stone is a Hardmode post-Golem accessory crafted from a Moon Stone and a Sun Stone at the Tinkerer's Workshop. It offers the same boosts as its components do, and as such, it is active during both day and night. It can be combined with the Moon Shell to form a Celestial Shell.
Celestial Wand: The Celestial Wand is a pet-summoning item that spawns Estee to follow the player. When the player is far enough away, Estee will emit a bright yellow beam trail while flying at high speed in order to catch up to them, which resembles that of a Fallen Star. The Celestial Wand can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum, and is always sold alongside the Star Princess set.
Cell Phone: The Cell Phone is a post-Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the PDA and the Magic Mirrors, displaying all information and allowing the player to teleport to their spawn point. Unlike most informational items, the Cell Phone does not double as an accessory. It instead functions solely from the player's main inventory.
Cenx's Dress set: Cenx's Dress set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is one of two vanity sets made for Cenx, the Creative Director on Terraria. Equipping the full set produces pink glowing particles when the player is near a light source.
Cenx's Dress equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to her clothing set:

Cenx's set, another vanity set created for Cenx, has the same chance of being dropped by Treasure Bags. One bag will never contain all of Cenx's items. Both do however contain Cenx's Wings and Cenx's Tiara.
Cenx's set: Cenx's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is one of two vanity sets made for Cenx, the Creative Director on Terraria. Equipping the full set produces pink glowing particles when the player is near a light source. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Cenx's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to her clothing set:

Cenx's Dress set, another vanity set created for Cenx, has the same chance of being dropped by Treasure Bags. One bag will never contain all of Cenx's items, due to there being two sets. They will always, however, contain Cenx's Wings and Cenx's Tiara.
Chain: Chains are used both for climbing and as components for various crafting recipes. They are used in crafting items such as the Grappling Hook, Sawmill, all types of watches, and chandeliers. Chains can be placed and used like Rope and offer the same ascent and descent speeds, although they cannot be turned into coils like Rope can. Placed Chains are background objects, and much like furniture, do not count as background walls in a house, are not suitable for NPCs, and cannot be actuated.
Chains are not destroyed when dropped in lava, despite having a rarity of.
Chain Guillotines: The Chain Guillotines are a Hardmode flail that have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Mimics. When used, they fire two blades attached to chains in rapid succession, with a maximum range of 32 tiles. They can pierce enemies that are very close by.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Chain Gun: The Chain Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that is dropped by Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event with a 6.25%–16.67% / 12.5%–50% chance depending on the current wave. When used, it very rapidly fires bullets in a wide spread. It also has a 66% chance not to consume ammunition.
Its best modifier is Rapid. However, Godly may be preferred to save ammo. Due to its low use time, it can only gain modifiers that give a speed boost of 15%, thus it cannot have the Unreal modifier.
Chain Knife: The Chain Knife is a pre-Hardmode flail that has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance of being dropped by Cave Bats. When used, it fires a knife attached to a chain that can extend up to 9.4 tiles.
On the I am error secret world seed, the Chain Knife has a chance of being obtained from any Chest.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Chairs: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too.
As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5.
Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.
Chandeliers: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms.
The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.
Chaos Cylinder: The Chaos Cylinder is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/5 (20%) of dropping from Hallowed Mimics. While equipped, it grants +8% ranged damage and causes all ranged weapons to use ammo in special ways. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Chaos Cylinder in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between its four modes:
Default: Ammo is used in rotating order within the ammo slots.
Full: Ammo is used in rotating order across the entire inventory.
Random: Ammo is used randomly across the entire inventory.
Simple: Effect disabled, ammo is used normally.
Chaos Elemental: The Chaos Elemental is a Hardmode enemy that spawns on Pearlstone, Pearlsand and Pink Ice Blocks in the Cavern layer. It runs around and tries to deal contact damage to the player. Occasionally, it will also teleport to a random location on-screen. Like many Underground Hallow enemies, Chaos Elementals have a glowing pink after-image.
Chaos Fish: Chaos Fish are a type of fish which are found rarely by fishing in the Underground Hallow. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Teleportation Potions.
Charged Blaster Cannon: The Charged Blaster Cannon is a Hardmode, post-Golem magic gun that has a 1/800 (0.13%) chance to drop from all basic enemies during the Martian Madness event. It possesses multiple firing modes with escalating speed, damage, and method of attack depending on how long the ⚒ Use / Attack key is held while firing it.
A single tap of the ⚒ Use / Attack key fires a small energy orb that dissipates after hitting an enemy.
Holding ⚒ Use / Attack rapidly fires small orbs at a rate of once every 0.17 seconds, up to a total of 6 small orbs. Mana is only consumed upon firing the first small orb.

After holding ⚒ Use / Attack for 1.5 seconds (i.e., 0.67 seconds after the 6th small orb has been fired), it will shoot a larger orb with infinite piercing and 250% of the weapon's damage (250 base damage).
Continuing to hold ⚒ Use / Attack fires larger orbs at a rate of once every 0.5 seconds. Mana is only consumed upon firing the first large orb.

Holding ⚒ Use / Attack continuously for an additional 1.5 seconds (i.e., 0.5 seconds after the 3rd large orb has been fired) fires a large, solid blue energy beam that pierces infinitely, travels for a maximum of 150 tiles, and deals 150% of the weapon's damage (150 base damage) to enemies at a rate of every 10 ticks or six times per second. Mana is consumed at the rate of once every 0.33 seconds, i.e. 42 base mana per second.
The attack is immediately canceled when mana is depleted, or when the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released, or after the beam is fired for 5 seconds.
Charm of Myths: The Charm of Myths is a Hardmode accessory which combines the effects of the Band of Regeneration and the Philosopher's Stone. When equipped, it regenerates 1 health every second and decreases the Potion Sickness debuff duration by 25%. This debuff normally imposes a 60-second cooldown after consuming a recovery potion; the Charm of Myths reduces it to 45 seconds.
Chattering Teeth Bomb: The Chattering Teeth Bomb is a Hardmode enemy spawned by Clowns during Blood Moons. It hops about, similarly to the Herpling, making small jumps and then large jumps as it makes its way toward the player. Once it is close enough to the player, it will explode.
Chef set: The Chef set is a set of Vanity items made up of the Chef Hat, the Chef Uniform, and the Chef Pants. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 7 Gold 50 Silver (set).
Cherry: The Cherry is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Boreal tree.
Chest Lock: The Chest Lock is a consumable item. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on certain types of Chests when holding it will turn the Chest into a locked Chest and consume the Chest Lock. The content of the Chest will not be affected by the conversion. Chests locked by this way work the same as the naturally generated locked Chests, requiring another respective key to unlock.
Chests: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of 10×4 / 8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode.

Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again.
There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.
Chicken Bones' set: Chicken Bones' set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Chicken Bones, who is a programmer at Re-Logic and part of the tModLoader development team.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Chicken Bones' equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Chicken Nugget: The Chicken Nugget is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 14 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Chicken Nugget has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Harpies. Statue-spawned Harpies do not drop it, as it is a food item.
Chik: The Chik is a Hardmode yoyo. On every 3rd yoyo hit, the Chik deals 200% damage ((68 base damage) and also shoots a spread of 5 crystal shards in random directions that can pass through blocks and travel for a short distance before disappearing. The crystal shards do not pierce, and each deal 100% of the Chik's damage ((34 base damage) and knockback (base knockback of 3.3 (Weak)).
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Chillet: Chillet and Chillet Ignis are pre-Hardmode mount-summoning items. When used, they summon the Chillet or Chillet Ignis mount, respectively, which increases damage dealt by 10% while mounted and is capable of performing "Rocket Slam", a dash. Dashing into an enemy deals 32 base summon damage, inflicts a knockback of 6 (Average), and grants the player 0.17 seconds of invincibility frames. Chillet and Chillet Ignis are functionally identical, and either variant can be obtained from the Huge Dragon Egg at a 1/2 (50%) chance.

Trusty Chillet and Trusty Chillet Ignis are upgraded, Hardmode-exclusive versions of Chillet and Chillet Ignis obtained via crafting. They have increased maximum speed, jump reach, dash speed, and dash damage (150 base summon damage), but are otherwise identical to their pre-Hardmode counterparts.
Like other Pals, Chillet and its variants can be petted using ⚷ Open / Activate.
Chimney: The Chimney is a decorative structure with a style similar to a Fireplace. It serves no in-game purpose, aside from cosmetics.

It has 3 states that can be toggled via wire. In the first state, it is turned off; in the second, it adds a small smoke animation; and in the third, it adds smoke particles which behave like bubbles from the Bubble Machine.
Chippy's Cloak (Inactive): Chippy's Cloak (Inactive) is a crafting material used solely to craft Chippy's Cloak. It is always dropped by Skeletron's Red Hat variant along with the rest of Chippy's set.
Chippy's Couch: Chippy's Couch is a furniture item that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Skeletron.
Chippy's set: Chippy's set is a set of vanity items consisting of Chippy's Helmet, Chippy's Chestplate, Chippy's Greaves, and Chippy's Headband. It is always dropped by Skeletron's Red Hat variant.
Chippy's equipment also includes the following non-vanity item, which drops with the set:
Chippy's Cloak (Inactive), which can be crafted into Chippy's Cloak
Chlorophyte Arrow: The Chlorophyte Arrow is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses arrow. It can bounce off blocks up to three times, dissipating upon hitting blocks for the fourth time. It bounces towards the direction of the nearest enemy within a 50-tile radius that has an unobstructed line of sight to the arrow. Its damage is decreased by 34% after bouncing for the first time, but further bounces do not incur a damage penalty.
Chlorophyte Bar: The Chlorophyte Bar is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses bar.
Chlorophyte Brick: Chlorophyte Bricks are Hardmode bricks crafted from Chlorophyte Ore and Stone Blocks.
Similarly to Chlorophyte Ore, Chlorophyte Bricks can convert adjacent Mud and Jungle grass into Chlorophyte Ore. Chlorophyte Bricks can also restrict the spread of the evil biomes around them.
See Chlorophyte Ore § Mechanics for further information.
Chlorophyte Brick Wall: Chlorophyte Brick Walls are Walls that can be manually crafted. When placed, it presents a dark shade of green followed by a gemstone-like pattern.
Chlorophyte Bullet: The Chlorophyte Bullet is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses bullet. It strongly homes in on the nearest enemy.
Chlorophyte Chainsaw: The Chlorophyte Chainsaw is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses chainsaw and the alternative to the Chlorophyte Greataxe.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Chlorophyte Claymore: The Chlorophyte Claymore is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses broadsword. When swung, a large green aura with a bright edge follows the swing, extending its reach and also covering behind the player. The sword also releases several short-lived spore clouds as it is swung, which are purely visual and deal no damage.

On every third use, a sparkling glow appears at tip of the sword and the swing becomes empowered, causing it to deal 150% of the weapon's damage (142 base damage) and 125% of its knockback (base knockback of 7.5 (Very strong)). If the empowered swing collides with solid blocks (including platforms and Planter Boxes), it creates a small explosion at the point of impact which deals same damage as the empowered swing, while also launching several lingering spore clouds upwards that pierce infinitely and deal 112.5% of the weapon's damage (106 base damage), but cannot pass through blocks. The explosion and spore clouds do not inflict any knockback.
Its shortsword counterpart is the Chlorophyte Saber.
Chlorophyte Drill: The Chlorophyte Drill is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses drill. It is the alternative to the Chlorophyte Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Chlorophyte Dye: Chlorophyte Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It can only be obtained after defeating any mechanical boss. When equipped, it gives items a black and green color palette which glows in the dark.
Chlorophyte Extractinator: The Chlorophyte Extractinator is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses crafting station and the upgrade to the Extractinator. It has the following upgraded functions:
It converts items 3.33× as fast (every 3 ticks).
In Hardmode, it converts Silt, Slush, and Desert Fossils into early Hardmode ores (those that can generate from destroying altars). Existing conversions and rates are unchanged.
If it is obtained in pre-Hardmode (whether via bringing it from a different world or on I am error worlds), it will not return Hardmode ores.
It converts Glowing Mosses into any kind of moss (except Helium Moss), instead of only regular ones.
It converts the Corruption, Crimson, and Hallow variants of most blocks into their normal variants.
It converts ores and bars into their alternate ore types (such as Copper into Tin).
It converts Dungeon Bricks into their variants.
In worlds with the I am error secret world seed enabled, it can also be found naturally in Underground Desert Cabins.
Chlorophyte Greataxe: The Chlorophyte Greataxe is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses axe and the alternative to the Chlorophyte Chainsaw.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Chlorophyte Jackhammer: The Chlorophyte Jackhammer is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses hammer.

Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. Mechanical tools can only have universal modifiers, because they cannot have their speed modified.
Chlorophyte Ore: Chlorophyte Ore is a Hardmode ore. After Hardmode starts, Mud Blocks located near Jungle grass blocks (naturally in the Underground Jungle) in or below the bottom half of the Underground layer will occasionally be replaced by Chlorophyte Ore. It requires at least a Pickaxe Axe or Drax to be mined, whose materials require defeating all three mechanical bosses.

Chlorophyte Ore is also renewable; it will slowly spread itself by converting adjacent Mud and Jungle grass blocks into more Chlorophyte Ore. It can also convert nearby Dirt Blocks to Mud, convert blocks of Corrupt, Crimson, Hallowed, and regular grass to Jungle grass, as well as convert infected tiles back to its Jungle variant. Chlorophyte Ore can only spread and convert blocks if it is in or below the bottom half of the Underground layer. It can only spread itself to directly adjacent tiles (and only if there is not too much Chlorophyte nearby already) and can only convert tiles up to 6 tiles away.
See Mechanics section for details about generation and spread of Chlorophyte Ore, and the difference of mechanics of Chlorophyte Ore in special world seeds.
Chlorophyte Partisan: The Chlorophyte Partisan is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses spear. When thrust, it fires a Spore Cloud projectile that deals the weapon's damage and knockback, lasts for a short time, can pass through blocks, and pierces an infinite number of enemies.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Chlorophyte Pickaxe: The Chlorophyte Pickaxe is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Chlorophyte Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Chlorophyte Saber: The Chlorophyte Saber is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses shortsword. When used, the sword is thrusted in repeated stabbing motions with slightly varying angles for each thrust, akin to Gladius and Starlight. Each thrust deals 70% of the weapon's damage (56 base damage) and inflicts the Spored debuff on enemies and other players in PvP for 5 seconds, causing enemies to lose 90 health per second (60 damage displayed every 0.67 seconds) and players to lose 15 health per second (1 damage displayed every 0.07 seconds). The damage of Spored can be increased by Accelerated Afflictions.
Its broadsword counterpart is the Chlorophyte Claymore.
Chlorophyte Shotbow: The Chlorophyte Shotbow is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses repeater. When used, it fires 2–3 arrows per shot, consuming one piece of ammunition.
Chlorophyte Warhammer: The Chlorophyte Warhammer is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Chlorophyte armor: Chlorophyte armor is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses armor set consisting of the Chlorophyte Plate Mail and Chlorophyte Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Chlorophyte Mask, Chlorophyte Helmet, Chlorophyte Headgear, and Chlorophyte Visor, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, magic and summon damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all six pieces requires a total of 90 Chlorophyte Bars (450 Chlorophyte Ore).
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:
Summons a Leaf Crystal minion above the player. It periodically fires green, laser-like bolts of energy that instantly hit the target and deals 100 base damage and 10 (Extremely strong) knockback.
Chocolate Chip Cookie: The Chocolate Chip Cookie is a Hardmode food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Chocolate Chip Cookie has a 1/75 (1.33%) chance of being dropped by Gastropods.
Christmas Pudding: Christmas Pudding is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Christmas Pudding can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 3.601% in pre-Hardmode and 3.361% in Hardmode.
Christmas Tree: The Christmas Tree is a decorative Hardmode furniture item purchased from Santa Claus for 25 Silver. It can be decorated with toppers, garlands, bulbs, and lights to alter its appearance.
Christmas Tree Sword: The Christmas Tree Sword is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that is dropped by the Everscream during the Frost Moon event with a 3.46%–10.37% (6.22%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave. When swung, it fires a star ornament that releases a ball ornament every 0.17 seconds while traveling. The stars dissipate after piercing one enemy or after 1.67 seconds. The balls linger for 0.83 seconds before falling. Both types of projectiles cannot pass through blocks or enemies.
Christmas Tree decorations: Christmas Tree decorations are Hardmode furniture items used to decorate Christmas Trees. There are four categories: toppers, bulbs, lights, and garlands. Each tree can only include one of each type. Most decorations can be purchased from Santa Claus for 5 Silver each, except for the Old-gen console-exclusive Star Topper 4, which can be found in Presents.
Decorations can only be removed by replacing specific decorations with another of the same type, or by removing the tree with a pickaxe, drill, or explosives and placing it again.
Christmas lights: Christmas lights are decorative furniture items and light sources that resemble Christmas string lights and emit very dim light. They can be placed on all four sides of blocks and can be toggled with wires. Christmas lights are purchased from Santa Claus for 5 Silver each.
Christmas lights are available in three colors that are each sold separately.
Chromatic Cloak: The Chromatic Cloak is a Hardmode accessory. When equipped, touching Shimmer does not immediately inflict the Shimmering debuff, and the player can instead start Shimmering at any time by holding the ▼ Down key. However, after Shimmering starts, it cannot be interrupted, not even if the Chromatic Cloak is removed and equipped again.

While the Chromatic Cloak is equipped, being submerged in Shimmer is comparable to being submerged in water: the player's horizontal and vertical movement speed are slowed by the same amount, the Shimmer can be swam in using accessories such as Flippers, and the player will transform into Merfolk if wearing the Neptune's Shell or its upgrades. However, the player cannot drown in the Shimmer; the breath meter does not appear.
Chum Bucket: The Chum Bucket is a consumable item that increases Fishing Power when thrown into a liquid. Chum Buckets have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped from Blood Moon enemies: Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen drop it in stacks of 4–6, and Hemogoblin Sharks, Blood Eels, and Dreadnautiluses in stacks of 7–10. All of these enemies have a chance to spawn while fishing during a Blood Moon.

The Fishing Power bonus depends on how many Chum Buckets are present on the liquid's surface. A single bucket used will increase Fishing Power by 11, two for a total of 17, and finally three for a total of 20. This bonus is added after all other fishing factors; therefore, unlike other fishing gear, it is not influenced by time factors. See the relevant section on Fishing for details.

Each bucket present in the pool lasts up to 10 times reeling in the line, even if nothing is on the line or if the line breaks. Reeling in the line reduces the lifetime of all Chum Buckets in the same body of liquid, rather than just one Chum Bucket.
Having any Chum Buckets present on the water's surface will multiply Shark spawn rates by 5× and Orca spawn rates by 2.78×.
Classy Cane: The Classy Cane is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to be dropped by the Tax Collector. Like the Flymeal, it has the special ability to damage town NPCs, but will always only deal 1 damage to them. In addition, hitting an enemy or NPC with the Classy Cane drops 1–49 Copper Coins.
Clay Block: Clay is a block type mainly used as a crafting material. It is found primarily in Surface-level (above 0 elevation) areas, and is more rare at the upper parts of the Underground. Because of this, the largest deposits of Clay can be found simply by exploring the Surface for differently-colored patches in the Dirt.
Clay Bud Staff: The Clay Bud Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Clay Bud minion. The Clay Bud walks and jumps into enemies, dealing contact damage to them when slamming down with its arms. If the Clay Bud strays too far away from the player, it will propel itself up by using the leaves at top of its head and fly to the player. Much like Pals, the Clay Bud minion can be petted by using ⚷ Open / Activate.
Clay Pot: The Clay Pot is a furniture item in which a herb or flower seed can be planted. If left empty, wild grass plants will randomly grow out of it, provided the pot is placed on the surface or in Space. The plant in a Clay Pot cannot be cut in the regular manner, e.g. via nearby swinging tools. Instead, it needs to be removed with a pickaxe, a drill, the Staff of Regrowth, or the Axe of Regrowth (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Clentaminator: The Clentaminator is a Hardmode tool which can be used to create or destroy biomes. It uses Solutions as ammunition, with each Solution spreading a different biome. It has a similar firing pattern to the Flamethrower, but has a much longer range, fires through blocks and works in water. The Clentaminator is generally the fastest means of spreading or removing Hallow, Corruption and Crimson. It can also rapidly convert Jungle to Glowing Mushroom biome and vice versa.
It can be purchased from the Steampunker for 2 Platinum.
After the Moon Lord is defeated, the Clentaminator can be upgraded into the Terraformer by throwing it into Shimmer.
The Clentaminator cannot be purchased in Remix and Zenith worlds.
The Clentaminator cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Climbing Claws: The Climbing Claws are an accessory that lets players partially "stick" to the sides of blocks, slowly sliding down them when moving against them in midair. Jumps can also be performed off the sides of blocks. By repeatedly sticking and jumping, vertical blocks can be scaled. When sliding down, the slide speed can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Climbing Claws have a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found inside surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. They can also be purchased for 2 Gold 50 Silver from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waxing Crescent. Their availability very early in the game makes them a useful accessory for mobility, as they allow the player to slowly but surely climb up some walls without needing ropes.

Climbing Claws function identically to the Shoe Spikes, but are found in different locations. When both Climbing Claws and Shoe Spikes are equipped, the wearer remains completely "stuck" at a fixed point when moving against the sides of blocks, and may slide down with the ▼ Down key. This effect can also be achieved using a single accessory if the Climbing Claws and Shoe Spikes are combined into the Tiger Climbing Gear at a Tinkerer's Workshop.
Clinger: The Clinger is a Hardmode enemy found in the Underground Corruption biome. Clingers spawn anchored to a block, with their head attached to an extendable "stem" that does not damage the player. They attack by launching orbs of Cursed Flames at the player, which can inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff.
Clinger Staff: The Clinger Staff is a Hardmode magic weapon that generates a 15-tile high wall of Cursed Flame, which deals damage and inflicts the Cursed Inferno debuff to enemies that walk through it for a duration of 7 seconds. The point at which the wall is generated must be in a direct line of sight; otherwise, the wall will not generate, though still consume mana. The Clinger Staff's wall lasts for 5 minutes before dissipating, but can be also forced to dissipate instantly by using ⚷ Open / Activate on the wall while the player is within 15 tiles of it. Only one wall may be generated at a time; if another is summoned, the first one will vanish. The Clinger Staff has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Mimics.

Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Clinger Staff's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.
Clockwork Assault Rifle: The Clockwork Assault Rifle is a Hardmode gun that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. When used, it fires in three-shot bursts, with each burst consuming one piece of ammunition.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Clothier: The Clothier is an NPC vendor who mainly sells vanity items. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

He is the same character as the Old Man who guards the Dungeon before Skeletron is defeated. After defeating Skeletron, the Old Man is freed from his curse, and he disappears from the Dungeon's entrance. His clothes are no longer tattered, his eyes have turned from red to blue, and he is wearing a Red Hat and scarf. Equipping the Clothier Voodoo Doll allows the player to attack and kill the Clothier (similar to the Guide Voodoo Doll) with any damage-inflicting item. Doing so at night resummons Skeletron, but killing the Clothier without the Clothier Voodoo Doll equipped (such as by using the Flymeal on its own) will not summon the boss.

The Clothier will defend himself against nearby enemies by firing shadowflame skull projectiles that damage and inflict the Shadowflame debuff on enemies for 5–10 seconds. He deals 16 / 24 / 28 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
Clothier Voodoo Doll: The Clothier Voodoo Doll is a boss-summoning item used to summon Skeletron after it has been defeated. It has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance to drop from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon.

When equipped in an accessory slot (but not social slots), the Clothier Voodoo Doll allows the player, Fallen Stars, and other NPCs to harm and kill the Clothier. As long as the Clothier Voodoo Doll is equipped, the Clothier will summon Skeletron upon dying at night (7:30 PM to 4:30 AM). The Clothier can die by any means to summon Skeletron.
Unlike the Guide Voodoo Doll, the Clothier Voodoo Doll is not destroyed upon use, and has no effect when dropped into lava.
The Clothier Voodoo Doll cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Clothier's set: The Clothier's set is a vanity set consisting of the Red Hat, Clothier's Jacket (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Clothier's Pants (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The Red Hat will always drop from the Clothier NPC. The other parts of the set are sold by the Clothier for 3 Gold each, during Halloween.
Cloud: Cloud is a type of block found beneath Floating Islands, along with Rain Cloud blocks; on the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, they can be found in stacks in Skyware Chests, Sky Crates and Azure Crates as well. Cloud blocks display as solid blocks, but light passes through them as if they were empty space. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, landing on them will not inflict fall damage.
Cloud Wall: The Cloud Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated on Floating Islands. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.
Cloud in a Balloon: The Cloud in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the functionality of the Cloud in a Bottle and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to 10.5 tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 9 tiles, for a total height of 19.5 tiles.

The total jump height of the Cloud in a Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the player's total underwater jump height from 15 tiles (8 + 7 from Cloud jump) to 13 tiles (7 + 6 from Cloud jump).
Cloud in a Bottle: The Cloud in a Bottle is an accessory that can be found in Gold Chests in the Underground and Cavern layers. When equipped, it allows the player an extra jump. The extra jump has a 75% jump duration compared to a normal jump, increasing the maximum height the player can reach without other accessories by 5 tiles, for a total of 11 tiles.
Clown: The Clown is an uncommon Hardmode enemy that only appears during Blood Moons. Although it has a chance to inflict the Confused debuff upon contact with the player, its primary weapons are yellow Happy Bombs, which are thrown in an arc, bounce off surfaces, and explode upon contact with the player or after their 5 seconds fuse timer runs out, dealing high damage but not destroying tiles. Clowns can also throw Chattering Teeth Bombs which chase the player and explode.
Once the player has defeated at least one Clown in a world, the Clothier will start selling the Clown set.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
The Clown requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Clown set: The Clown set is a vanity set which consists of the Clown Hat, the Clown Shirt, and the Clown Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 4 Gold (set), once a Clown has been defeated.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Clumsy Slime: Town Slimes are a type of town pet. There are 8 different Town Slimes and all of them can exist at the same time (unlike the different breeds of the Town Bunny, Town Cat, and Town Dog).

Almost all types of Town Slimes are acquired via some form of transformation, similar to the Tax Collector. Afterwards, the transformed Town Slime will move into a vacant house if one is available. If it is killed, it will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house. The initial transformation does not need to be repeated.

Town Slimes can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). They may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for their home tile (standing point).
Cluster Rocket I: The Cluster Rocket I is a type of rocket ammunition. Unlike the Cluster Rocket II, it does not destroy tiles. Upon exploding, cluster rockets shoot out 6 shrapnels that create secondary explosions upon hitting enemies or after a short time, each of which deals 50% of the rocket's damage.
It can be purchased from the Cyborg for 7 Silver 50 Copper each after completing the Martian Madness event.
Cluster Rocket II: The Cluster Rocket II is a type of rocket ammunition. Unlike the Cluster Rocket I, it destroys tiles. Unique from other rockets, cluster rockets shoot out shrapnel that create several secondary explosions which deal half of the base damage. These secondary explosions will destroy additional tiles.
Cluster Rocket IIs can be purchased from the Cyborg for 15 Silver each during a Blood Moon or Solar Eclipse after the Martian Madness event has been defeated.
Coal: Coal is an item with no use. It can drop from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 1/30 (3.33%) in pre-Hardmode and 7/225 (3.11%) in Hardmode. It also has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped from Jungle Mimics, which only spawn when the Celebration Mk 10 special seed is active.
Cobalt Bar: The Cobalt Bar is a Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Bar.
Cobalt Brick: Cobalt Brick is a сobalt tier brick.
Cobalt Brick Wall: Cobalt Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Cobalt Bricks.
Cobalt Chainsaw: The Cobalt Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Cobalt Waraxe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Chainsaw.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Cobalt Drill: The Cobalt Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Cobalt Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Mythril and Orichalcum Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Drill. The Cobalt Drill has slightly less pickaxe power and damage.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Cobalt Naginata: The Cobalt Naginata is a Hardmode spear.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Pike.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Cobalt Ore: Cobalt Ore belongs to the first tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the first altar broken, either it or Palladium Ore can spawn in the underground and cavern layers. Mining Cobalt Ore requires a Molten Pickaxe or better.

As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
Cobalt Pickaxe: The Cobalt Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Cobalt Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Mythril and Orichalcum Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Pickaxe. The Cobalt Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Cobalt Repeater: The Cobalt Repeater is a Hardmode repeater.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Repeater.
Cobalt Shield: The Cobalt Shield is a pre-Hardmode shield accessory that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). While equipped, it grants 1 defense and immunity to knockback.
Cobalt Sword: The Cobalt Sword is a Hardmode broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Sword.
Cobalt Waraxe: The Cobalt Waraxe is a Hardmode axe and the alternative to the Cobalt Chainsaw.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Waraxe.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Cobalt armor: Cobalt armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Cobalt Breastplate and Cobalt Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Cobalt Helmet, Cobalt Mask, and Cobalt Hat, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 45 Cobalt Bars (135 Cobalt Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 65 Cobalt Bars (195 Cobalt Ore).
Its alternate ore counterpart is Palladium armor.
The player also emits visual afterimages while moving.
Cobweb: Cobwebs are crafting materials used to craft Silk and other items. Cobwebs can also be placed. Placed Cobwebs catch players who fall into them and reset fall damage. They break after a short time when a player is stuck in them, and they can also be harvested instantly with any weapon or swung tool.

Cobwebs are commonly found in underground areas in clusters of 5 or more alongside the edges of walls or ceilings, and are guaranteed to drop a Cobweb item when broken. They are also found in large quantities in Spider Nests, where they regrow over time; however, Cobwebs found there only have a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop when broken.

In Expert Mode worlds with the Remix seed enabled, web spit attack from Black Recluses and Jungle Creepers can randomly place Cobwebs in a 13×13 rectangular area centered on the location where Web Spit projectiles disappear.
Cobwhip: The Cobwhip is a pre-Hardmode whip. It has a 60% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

Releases a small spider that lasts for 3 seconds, which repeatedly deals 2 damage on contact and has 30 armor penetration, but does not inflict knockback. The spider also applies the Cobwhip's tag damage to enemies it hits, like the whip itself. If a spider already exists, Cobwhip hits will refresh its duration instead of releasing a new one.
Cochineal Beetle: The Cochineal Beetle is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Cavern layer. It drops the Red Husk, which can be used to make Red Dye.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Cockatiels: The Yellow Cockatiel and Gray Cockatiel are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. They may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Cockatiels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Cockatiels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Yellow / Gray Cockatiel Cage). Once crafted, the Cockatiels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Cockatiels can be spawned by the Cockatiel Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Coconut: The Coconut is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a regular, Corrupt, Crimson, or Hallowed Palm tree in the Ocean biome.
Code 1: The Code 1 is a pre-Hardmode yoyo that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold once the Eye of Cthulhu has been defeated.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Code 2: The Code 2 is a Hardmode, post one-mechanical boss yoyo that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 25 Gold.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Coffee: Coffee is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Coffee has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Snatchers, Man Eaters, and Angry Trappers, and a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Bone Lees.
Cog: Cogs are Hardmode crafting materials and placeable blocks that are purchased from the Steampunker for 7 Silver each. They are used to make High Velocity Bullets, Liquid Sensors, and Steampunk furniture.

When Cogs are placed together they will display animated machinery. Corners, lines, and junctions will never be animated, though blocks inside the group of Cogs and the left border will always be animated and other borders are sometimes animated with a 2/3 (66.67%) chance.
Crafting all Steampunk furniture will require 159 / 153 / 33 Cogs.
Cog Wall: Cog Walls are a type of background wall made from Cogs. The wall is animated similar to placed cogs.
Coin Gun: The Coin Gun is a Hardmode ranged weapon that uses coins as ammunition, which affects its damage and velocity depending on the type of coin fired. The weapon itself has 0 base damage, with the entirety of its damage value stemming from the coins used to fire it. Coin projectiles dissipate upon hitting an enemy or solid block and cannot be retrieved once fired. The Coin Gun is dropped very rarely (1/4000 (0.025%) chance) by regular Pirate Invasion enemies, excluding the Parrot. The Coin Gun's drop chance from Pirate Captains is quadrupled (1/1000 (0.1%) chance) and increased again from the Flying Dutchman (1/50 (2%) chance).

Its best modifier is Agile, as it can only receive modifiers affecting its speed, velocity, critical strike chance, and knockback. Rapid and Hasty modifiers are recognized in-game as its "best" modifier due to them increasing the item's value by the most.
Coin Ring: The Coin Ring is a Hardmode accessory created by other accessories exclusively dropped from pirate enemies during Pirate Invasion. It combines the effect of Gold Ring and Lucky Coin, which increases the pickup range for coins, and causes enemies to occasionally drop 1 to 10 more coins when hit and grants +0.05 luck.
Coins: Coins are the main unit of currency in Terraria, primarily used for transactions with NPCs. They are obtained by killing enemies, selling items to or interacting with NPCs, or finding them in multiple forms of loot. The currency comprises four different denominations of coins: Copper Coins, Silver Coins, Gold Coins, and Platinum Coins.
The denominations are, ranked from lowest to highest value:
Despite coins appearing as the materials copper, silver, gold, or platinum, they are not related to their respective ores and cannot be crafted from them.
The coin value an enemy drops upon death is calculated from fixed base values with some random variation. See NPC drops § Coin drops for further information.
As a secondary function, coins are used as ammunition for the Coin Gun. They can also be placed to form Coin Piles.
Combat Wrench: The Combat Wrench is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron boomerang that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by the Mechanic. It can pierce multiple targets before returning.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Companion Cube: The Companion Cube is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Companion Cube that follows the player. The Companion Cube can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Platinum.

Normally, the Companion Cube follows the player by hopping towards them. However, when the player and the Companion Cube are in complete darkness (including the absence of light sources), the Cube can occasionally "stab" the player, inflicting 3 damage.

When the Companion Cube falls into lava, it emits the Lunatic Cultist's death sound. When submerged in lava for long enough, there is a chance it may make the Moon Lord's death sound. The Companion Cube will also occasionally emit the flatulence sound normally produced by the Whoopie Cushion.
Compass: The Compass is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the player's horizontal position. Position is shown in the number of feet (1 foot = 1/2 tile) to the east or west of the center of the map. The centerpoint of the map is usually very close to the initial spawn point.

The Compass has a 79/6400 (1.23%) chance of being dropped by Crawdads, Giant Shellies, and Salamanders, a 1/75 (1.33%) chance to be dropped by Piranhas, and a 1/50 (2%) chance to be dropped by Mother Slimes, Snow Flinx, Undead Vikings, and Armored Vikings.
Compass Rose: The Compass Rose is a decorative item that can be placed on background walls. It is randomly awarded by the Angler NPC for completing quests.
On the minimap, it is referred to as a trophy.
Confetti: Confetti is a crafting material used to make several festive items. It is purchased from the Party Girl for 2 Silver each, or dropped by Confetti Slimes.
Confetti Block: The Confetti Block is an animated block type showing falling confetti. It is one of the few items that uses the Crystal Ball as a crafting station. Besides the confetti, it is transparent, like Glass. The Midnight Confetti Block is a dark, non-transparent version of it.
Confetti Cannon: The Confetti Cannon is a Hardmode novelty furniture/mechanism. It is purchased from the Party Girl for 25 Gold, when the Pirate is present. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Confetti Cannon fires a burst of multicolored gravity-affected Confetti that is purely visual, dealing no damage or knockback. The Confetti Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Confetti Cannons in the world.

The angle of a placed Confetti Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Confetti Cannon to rotate it in that direction, or tapping the side of the Confetti Cannon. It has 9 possible orientations and cannot fire downward. Each step tilts the Confetti Cannon by 1/16 of a circle (22.5°).
The Confetti Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either shoot Confetti (with a cooldown of 0.5 seconds) or rotate toward the side the Wire is on.
Confetti Gun: The Confetti Gun is a consumable novelty weapon that fires a cloud of colorful confetti. This effect is purely visual and causes no damage or functional effect. Confetti Guns are consumed upon use; they can only be used once each. They are purchased from the Party Girl for 1 Silver each.
Confetti Wall: Confetti Walls are a type of background wall made from Confetti Blocks. They resemble Glass Walls with falling confetti. They are one of only a few animated background walls. Midnight Confetti Walls are an opaque version of them.
Constellation: The Constellation is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist whip. It has a 10% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
