Marks enemies with cosmic energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Constellation, the cosmic energy fully grows. The next time Constellation hits an enemy marked with grown cosmic energy, it releases 6 non-piercing Shooting Stars that home in on enemies after a short delay, each dealing 39.6% of the whip's damage (51 base damage) and 100% of its knockback, and the cosmic energy is reset to its non-grown state. The Shooting Stars also apply the Constellation's cosmic energy, tag damage, tag critical strike chance to enemies they hit like the whip itself, but cannot trigger the effect of grown cosmic energy and cause more Shooting Stars to spawn. All enemies hit by a swing will be marked by cosmic energy, but effect of cosmic energy can be triggered only once per swing.
Uniquely among whips, the Constellation's tag effect lasts for 8 seconds instead of the usual 4 seconds.
Conveyor Belt: Conveyor Belts (Clockwise and Counter Clockwise) are blocks obtained from Conveyor Slimes or, in Hardmode, purchased from the Steampunker for 5 Silver each. The Conveyor Slime drops only the clockwise variant; however, the two variants are interchangeable via crafting.
They have the unique ability to move certain entities in their respective direction upon contact. The following entities are affected by Conveyor Belts:
Slimes (and Hoppin' Jacks, who use Slime AI)
The following stationary NPCS: Gnomes, non-Biome Mimics, Lost Girls, Bound NPCs, and the distressed forms of Cattiva and Foxparks.
Falling blocks (Sand, Slush, Silt, Shell Piles, Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and Ash on worlds with the For the Worthy seed active) become items when falling onto Conveyor Belts.

Conveyor Belts will remain active from the moment they are placed. Being powered with Wire reverses their direction, toggling between Clockwise and Counter Clockwise. Their direction can also be switched from the crafting menu. Like most other blocks, they can be shaped into half-blocks and angled slopes using a hammer, allowing for diagonal movement. Conveyor Belts can also carry items vertically.
Cooked Fish: The Cooked Fish is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Cooked Marshmallow: The Cooked Marshmallow is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

The Cooked Marshmallow is created by holding a Marshmallow on a Stick over a Campfire for up to 15 seconds. The Marshmallow on a Stick must be held by the player, either by attaching it to the cursor in the inventory or selecting it in the hotbar, for the entire duration over the Campfire in order for it to be cooked. Selecting a different item in the hotbar, moving/turning away from the Campfire, or turning the Campfire off resets the timer.
Cooked Shrimp: The Cooked Shrimp is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Cooking Pots: The Cooking Pot is a crafting station that is solely used to turn various items into food, consumables that induce the Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied and Exquisitely Stuffed buffs. Such food material include the Bowl of Soup, Cooked Fish, Cooked Shrimp, and Grub Soup.

The Cauldron is the Halloween-themed variant of the Cooking Pot that is functionally identical in every way, except for its animated sprite and the small amount of light it emits. Unlike the Cooking Pot, the Cauldron cannot be crafted, and can only be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 1 Gold 50 Silver during Halloween.
Cool Slime: Town Slimes are a type of town pet. There are 8 different Town Slimes and all of them can exist at the same time (unlike the different breeds of the Town Bunny, Town Cat, and Town Dog).

Almost all types of Town Slimes are acquired via some form of transformation, similar to the Tax Collector. Afterwards, the transformed Town Slime will move into a vacant house if one is available. If it is killed, it will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house. The initial transformation does not need to be repeated.

Town Slimes can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). They may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for their home tile (standing point).
Cool Whip: The Cool Whip is a Hardmode whip. It has a 30% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

Grants the A Nice Buff buff, creating a homing snowflake projectile that lasts for 3 seconds, which repeatedly deals 15 damage and has 30 armor penetration. The snowflake also applies the Cool Whip's tag damage to enemies it hits, like the whip itself. If a snowflake already exists, Cool Whip hits will refresh its duration instead of creating a new one.
Inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 4 seconds.
Copper Axe: The Copper Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe. Newly created characters spawn with a Copper Axe (Iron Axe in Journey Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)).
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Axe.
The Copper Axe can also be purchased from the Merchant for 4 Silver.

Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and either Agile or Forceful/Strong for combat purposes, due to its unusually low base damage. Though it can obtain the Ruthless modifier, the reduced knockback may be undesirable for early stages of the game.
Copper Bar: The Copper Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Bar.
Newly created characters outside of Journey Mode will always spawn with the Copper Shortsword, Copper Pickaxe, and Copper Axe, regardless of whether the world generated with Copper or Tin.
Copper Bow: The Copper Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Copper Brick: Copper Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Like the ore used to make it, placed Copper Bricks will sparkle. As copper becomes fairly useless quite early in the game, this is an inexpensive ore brick to build with. Despite being made of Copper, it has no sell value, as with most other bricks. Copper Plating is also available as a decorative block, with the same ingredients and color but a different texture.
Copper Brick Wall: Copper Brick Walls are a type of background wall crafted from Copper Bricks. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.
Copper Broadsword: The Copper Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Copper Shortsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Broadsword.
Copper Hammer: The Copper Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Copper Ore: Copper Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on the surface. Copper Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Tin Ore.
Copper Pickaxe: The Copper Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks weaker than Meteorite. Newly created characters spawn with a Copper Pickaxe (Iron Pickaxe in Journey Mode). It can also be purchased from the Merchant for 5 Silver.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Pickaxe. The Copper Pickaxe has slightly less damage, mining speed, and range.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Copper Plating: Copper Plating is a pre-Hardmode brick. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Plating.
Copper Plating Wall: Copper Plating Wall is a background wall made of Copper Plating.
Copper Shortsword: The Copper Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Copper Broadsword. Newly created characters spawn with a Copper Shortsword (Iron Shortsword in Journey Mode).
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Shortsword.
Copper armor: Copper armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Copper Helmet, Copper Chainmail, and Copper Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 48 Copper Bars (144 Copper Ore). The full set grants 6 defense while equipped.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Tin armor.
Coral: Corals are crafting materials which can be found in the Ocean biomes at the ends of the world. They grow naturally on Sand Blocks underwater, within 380 tiles of the left or right edges of the world, and above the depth of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) −20 feet / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 0 feet, as long as no more than 5 Corals ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Seashells) are within 7 tiles horizontally and vertically.

Corals can be harvested either with a pickaxe/drill/explosives, by mining out the sand underneath them, or by placing a block above them. Afterwards, they can be placed on any type of block and will take on a random appearance out of six possible varieties.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Corals will spawn slower on sand under less than 5 tiles of water. Spawn rates scale with rain, wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Corals will only spawn on sand under at least 5 tiles of water. Rain and wind do not affect spawn rates.
Coralstone Block: Coralstone Blocks are decorative blocks. When placed, they can have one of the many kinds of coral on it. Much like Sunplate Blocks, Coralstone Blocks show a special, non-changing image if a square of nine or more are put next to each other. In this case, the image is a coral that looks much like a sponge.
Corite: The Corite is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events. It is a flying enemy that shrouds itself in fire before charging toward the player at high speeds, all while traveling through blocks.
Corrupt Bunny: The Corrupt Bunny is a pre-Hardmode enemy that results from a Bunny that has been corrupted, either by the player using Vile Powder on it or when a Bunny spawns during a Blood Moon in a Corruption world.
Corrupt Crate: The Corrupt Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in The Corruption. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally dropped by destroying a Shadow Orb. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Defiled Crate.
Corrupt Goldfish: The Corrupt Goldfish is a pre-Hardmode enemy that results from a Goldfish being corrupted, either by the player using Vile Powder on it or when a Goldfish spawns during a Blood Moon in a Corruption world. Corrupt Goldfish can also spawn naturally in the waters of The Corruption.
Corrupt Grass Wall: The Corrupt Grass Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in The Corruption, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, by purchasing it from the Dryad during a Blood Moon for 2 Silver 50 Copper each. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

The Clentaminator/Terraformer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (using Purple Solution) and Unholy Water convert Grass Walls, Flower Walls, and Jungle Walls (both safe and unsafe) to unsafe Corrupt Grass Walls.
Corrupt Grass Walls can spread The Corruption to nearby pure walls. See Biome spread for further information.
Corrupt Mimic: Mimics are rare Hardmode enemies disguised as Chests, appearing as the appropriate chest type for the environment.
Mimics can be spawned by the player using the Chest Statue, even in pre-Hardmode. However, Mimics spawned this way only drop the Mimic Banner.
Rarer Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics can also be spawned manually by players via a Key of Light or Key of Night (see the Biome Mimic section below).

They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics require 25 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Corrupt Penguin: The Corrupt Penguin is a pre-Hardmode enemy that results from a Penguin that has been corrupted, either by the player using Vile Powder on it or when a Penguin spawns during a Blood Moon in a Corruption world.
Corrupt Seeds: Corrupt Seeds are seeds used to plant Corrupt grass on Dirt Blocks, which will then spread The Corruption in all directions. They drop from the Eye of Cthulhu and can be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a world with Corruption. In a world with Crimson, Corrupt Seeds can be purchased from the Dryad if she is spoken to in a Hardmode Graveyard.
Corrupt Seeds can also be planted on Mud Blocks to create Corrupt Jungle grass.
Corrupt Slime: The Corrupt Slime is a Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in The Corruption and Underground Corruption. It splits into two to three Slimelings upon death. Both its original form and the Slimelings have a 1/4 (25%) chance of inflicting the Darkness debuff for 15 / 30 / 37.5 seconds.
Like most other slimes, the Corrupt Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel accessory equipped.
Corrupt Walls: The Corrupt Growth Wall, Corrupt Mass Wall, Corrupt Pustule Wall, and Corrupt Tendril Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Corruption, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on the Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
Corruptor: The Corruptor is a Hardmode enemy that spawns within The Corruption and resembles a larger version of the Eater of Souls. It intermittently fires Vile Spit projectiles that inflict the Weak debuff.
Cosmic Car Key: The Cosmic Car Key is a Hardmode, post-Golem mount-summoning item. When used, it summons a rideable UFO Mount that allows the player to fly and hover indefinitely. The Cosmic Car Key has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event.
Cosmic Ember Brick: Cosmic Ember Brick is a type of decorative brick obtained by throwing Luminite Brick into Shimmer during a Waxing Gibbous.
Cosmic Ember Brick Wall: Cosmic Ember Brick Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Cosmic Ember Bricks.
Cosmic Skateboard: The Cosmic Skateboard is a Hardmode, post-Golem pet-summoning item that spawns an Alien Skater that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Alien Skater turns its skateboard into a rocket-powered hoverboard to catch up to them. The Cosmic Skateboard has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer in Master Mode.
Countercurse Mantra: The Countercurse Mantra is an immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Silenced and Cursed debuffs.
It can be obtained in pre-Hardmode, as the Megaphone can be obtained by throwing the Nazar into Shimmer.
Counterweights: Counterweights are accessories sold by the Traveling Merchant and the Skeleton Merchant. They fire a second yoyo-type projectile after hitting an enemy with a yoyo, which travels towards it, then orbits around the player. Counterweights deal the yoyo's full damage and stay active until the yoyo is retracted towards the player. There are six different color variants with identical functionalities.
Country Club set: The Country Club set is a vanity set. It is purchased from the Golfer for 7 Gold 50 Silver (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Cowboy set: The Cowboy set is a Hardmode vanity set that includes the Cowboy Hat, Cowboy Jacket, and Cowboy Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 15 Gold (set), during the first-quarter moon phase.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Crab: The Crab is a weak pre-Hardmode enemy found in Oceans, walking along the bottom and occasionally jumping. They may also walk on land, and whether or not they are in water has no effect on their behavior.
Cracked Dungeon Bricks: Cracked Dungeon Bricks are bricks which can be found in the Dungeon and appear very similar to ordinary Dungeon Bricks. If jumped on, walked across, grappled to, mined with any pickaxe or drill, or hit by projectiles, several Cracked Dungeon Bricks nearby the targeted block, including the block itself, may fall and be destroyed upon hitting solid ground, dropping no item. Cracked Dungeon Bricks can conceal important pathways to significant portions of the Dungeon, potentially making it seem much smaller than it actually is. Additionally, naturally-generated Cracked Dungeon Bricks often conceal rectangular pits lined with Spikes, which may sometimes be filled with water to make escape more difficult.

Cracked Dungeon Bricks can be crafted with regular Dungeon Bricks at a Heavy Assembler. Crafted Cracked Dungeon Bricks behave the same as naturally generated Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and do not drop an item upon destruction.
Crate Potion: The Crate Potion is a buff potion which grants the Crate buff when consumed. The buff increases the chance of getting a crate from 1/10 (10%) to 1/4 (25%) when fishing. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
The Crate Potion can be obtained both from crafting and as a reward from the Angler for completing fishing quests.
Crawdad: The Crawdad is a pre-Hardmode enemy found in the Cavern layer, and has two color variants that share identical stats and behavior. The Crawdad acts like a Crab, walking along the ground and jumping at the player when in close enough proximity, though it is slightly faster. It is also capable of moving through water unhindered. When a Crawdad is right next to the player, it will attack with its claw, dealing large amounts of damage per hit.

Crawdads are unique in that their ability to spawn is connected to two other enemies: the Giant Shelly and the Salamander. Of these three enemies, a world will choose two types that it can spawn, leaving the third inaccessible. Crawdads will never spawn in a world that features both Giant Shellies and Salamanders together. This is taken into account by the Bestiary progression logic (the missing enemy will register as unlocked when the other two exclusive creatures are unlocked) and the banner acquisition (any two of the trio's banners can be used to craft the banner of the missing member of the trio).
Crawltipede: The Crawltipede is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist, worm enemy that spawns in the area of the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events. Unlike other worm enemies, its head and body segments are invincible and its tail is the only segment that is vulnerable to attacks, which also takes 10× damage from all hits. It flies directly at airborne players and deals high damage while ignoring players on the ground. The Crawltipede's primary role seems to be forcing the player to stay near the ground, opening them up to melee attacks from the other Solar Pillar enemies.
Cream Soda: The Cream Soda is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Cream Soda has a 1/70 (1.43%) chance of being dropped by Cursed Skulls, and a 1/35 (2.86%) chance of being dropped by Giant Cursed Skulls.
Creature from the Deep: The Creature from the Deep is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. It attacks like most other fighter-type enemies on land, but it also has the ability to swim in liquids. While swimming, its speed and maneuverability increase dramatically. It is also capable of jumping out of the water towards the player, doing so with maneuverability similar to a Unicorn.
Creeper: The Creeper is a pre-Hardmode boss servant that is summoned by the Brain of Cthulhu in a group of 20. They follow and orbit the Brain of Cthulhu, acting as a shield for it. Creepers do not respawn once they are killed. All Creepers must be destroyed first before the Brain of Cthulhu becomes vulnerable to attacks. Creepers have a 1/2 (50%) chance to drop a Heart if the player is below full health (as opposed to 1/12 (8.33%) for most enemies).
On For the Worthy worlds, Creepers spawn in groups of 40.
Creeper Egg: The Creeper Egg is a Hardmode light pet-summoning item that spawns a Flickerwick to follow the player around. When active, it is similar to the Wisp in a Bottle, where it provides light wherever the player goes. The summoned Flickerwick has the same movement speed as the player, and cannot be left behind easily. The Creeper Egg is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/5 (20%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/10 (10%) chance during Tier 3. While equipped, light is produced not only around the pet, but also around the player.
Creeper set: The Creeper set is a vanity set consisting of the Creeper Mask, Creeper Shirt, and Creeper Pants. Its male and female variants look identical. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to drop from Goodie Bags during Halloween.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Crescent Wall: Crescent Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Crescent Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Crimera: The Crimera is a common pre-Hardmode flying enemy that spawns predominantly in The Crimson. It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Eater of Souls, and behaves in the same manner, attacking by flying toward the player while circling them at a distance before periodically rushing in.
Similar to Eater of Souls, Crimera can appear in three size variants: Little Crimera, Crimera, and Big Crimera, each with corresponding health, damage, and defense.
The Little Crimera also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Shadewood or Shadewood Palm tree.
Crimslime: The Crimslime is a Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in The Crimson. It spawns with either 85%, 100%, or 115% of its usual size, with the stats altered accordingly. In the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it has a chance to inflict the Darkness debuff on contact.
Like most other slimes, the Crimslime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Crimson Axe: The Crimson Axe is a Hardmode enemy which is found in the Underground Crimson. It hovers and spins before lunging at the player, traveling through any blocks to reach them. Any damage dealt to it stops its attack, forcing it to pause and spin again. It has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Cursed debuff upon contact.
Crimson Crate: The Crimson Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in The Crimson. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally dropped by destroying a Crimson Heart. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Hematic Crate.
Crimson Grass Wall: The Crimson Grass Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in The Crimson, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, by purchasing it from the Dryad during a Blood Moon for 2 Silver 50 Copper each. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

The Clentaminator/Terraformer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (using Red Solution) and Blood Water convert Grass Walls, Flower Walls, and Jungle Walls (both safe and unsafe) to unsafe Crimson Grass Walls.
Crimson Grass Walls can spread The Crimson to nearby pure walls. See Biome spread for further information.
Crimson Heart (item): The Crimson Heart is a light pet-summoning item that spawns a fast-moving bleeding Crimson Heart that emits dim, red light. It follows the player around while affected by gravity, rolling or hopping along the ground. If it falls far behind the player, it will fly through blocks to catch up. The Crimson Heart has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped from destroyed Crimson Hearts, but it also has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being acquired from Crimson and Hematic Crates, which are obtained by fishing in The Crimson.
The Corruption counterpart to the Crimson Heart is the Shadow Orb.
Crimson Mimic: Mimics are rare Hardmode enemies disguised as Chests, appearing as the appropriate chest type for the environment.
Mimics can be spawned by the player using the Chest Statue, even in pre-Hardmode. However, Mimics spawned this way only drop the Mimic Banner.
Rarer Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics can also be spawned manually by players via a Key of Light or Key of Night (see the Biome Mimic section below).

They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics require 25 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Crimson Rod: The Crimson Rod is a pre-Hardmode magic weapon that launches a reddish rain cloud towards the cursor, where it rains damaging blood droplets downward onto enemies below. One cloud projectile can be placed at a time and it does not pass through terrain, instead stopping if it hits a surface before it reaches its target location. Once placed, the cloud will remain for five minutes but can be removed early by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, similarly to the Nimbus Rod's cloud. As well, its coverage area is rather narrow, making it difficult to use in open areas or against agile foes. The droplets can pierce one enemy, dissipating upon hitting a second one or a solid block.

The Crimson Rod has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Crimson Hearts found in The Crimson or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Crimson Crates and Hematic Crates, which are fished in the Crimson.
Its Corruption counterpart is the Vilethorn.
Its best modifier is Demonic because it cannot get modifiers that affect knockback.
Crimson Seeds: Crimson Seeds are seeds used to plant Crimson grass on Dirt Blocks, which will then spread The Crimson in all directions. They drop from the Eye of Cthulhu and can be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a world with Crimson. In a world with Corruption, Crimson Seeds can be purchased from the Dryad if she is spoken to in a Hardmode Graveyard.
Crimson Seeds can be used to farm Vicious Mushrooms and may be used to spread Crimson in Corrupt worlds.
Crimson Seeds can also be planted on Mud Blocks to create Crimson Jungle grass.
Crimson Tigerfish: Crimson Tigerfish are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in The Crimson in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Heartreach Potions.
Crimson Walls: The Crimson Crust Wall, Crimson Scab Wall, Crimson Teeth Wall, and Crimson Blister Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Crimson, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
Crimson armor: Crimson armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Crimson Helmet, Crimson Scalemail, and Crimson Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Crimtane Bars (180 Crimtane Ore) and 45 Tissue Samples.
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Shadow armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

Greatly increased health regeneration rate (+50% natural regeneration, and doubles its ramp-up speed), indicated by faint red pulses around the player: Each pulse represents one health point regenerated. These become more frequent the longer the player avoids damage, and even more frequent while standing still.
The player leaves a visual trail of red bubbles while moving.
Crimstone Block: Crimstone is a block type found in The Crimson. Before Hardmode, it is most prominent in the lining of Chasms. It requires at least 65% pickaxe power (Deathbringer Pickaxe / Nightmare Pickaxe, or better) or explosives to mine. Deathweed can grow on it.

Crimstone is the Crimson version of Stone (similar to Ebonstone in The Corruption, or Pearlstone in The Hallow). As with Ebonstone, Crimstone can be converted into ordinary Stone via Purification Powder or Green Solution used by the Clentaminator.
In Hardmode, the spread of Crimson converts ordinary Stone blocks into Crimstone. Crimstone itself also spreads Crimson to susceptible blocks nearby.
Crimstone Brick: Crimstone Brick is a type of brick. Unlike its raw block counterpart, the Crimstone Block, it does not spread The Crimson, nor does it turn the area into a Crimson biome, thus making it a safe construction material for NPC houses and other structures. Its Corruption counterpart is Ebonstone Brick.
Crimstone Brick Wall: The Crimstone Brick Wall is a placeable item that looks like a blood-stained brick wall.
Crimstone Wall: The Crimstone Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in The Crimson, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
The Clentaminator/Terraformer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (using Red Solution) and Blood Water convert Stone Walls to unsafe Crimstone Walls.
Crimstone Walls can spread The Crimson to nearby pure walls. See Biome spread for further information.
Crimtane Bar: The Crimtane Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Demonite Bar.
Crimtane Brick: Crimtane Brick is a brick made from Crimtane Ore and Crimstone. A box of it appears after the Wall of Flesh has been defeated in a Crimson world. It is red and black in color, it is not resistant to explosions, and it gives off a faint red glow when placed.
Crimtane Brick Wall: The Crimtane Brick Wall is a background wall. It emits faint red light when placed.
Crimtane Ore: Crimtane Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It is primarily dropped from the Brain of Cthulhu, as well as the Eye of Cthulhu in Crimson worlds. Crimtane Ore can also be found rarely in small veins underground. When below 0 ft in elevation, a Gold Pickaxe or better is needed to mine it, otherwise any pickaxe can be used.
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Demonite Ore.
Crispy Honey Block: The Crispy Honey Block is a block formed when honey comes into contact with lava. It can also be crafted.
Crispy Honey Blocks are not destroyed when dropped into lava, despite having a rarity of.
Critter Shampoo: Critter Shampoo is a vanity accessory equipped in a social accessory slot that changes the color of summoned minions when paired with a dye in the corresponding dye slot. It is purchased from the Zoologist for 10 Gold after completing at least 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary.
The Critter Shampoo cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Cross Necklace: The Cross Necklace is a Hardmode accessory that increases the duration of the invincibility frames a player is afforded after taking damage. The Cross Necklace has a (Desktop, Console, Mobile and 3DS versions) 1/6 (16.67%) / (Old-gen console version) 1/7 (14.29%) chance to be dropped by Mimics.
Crossed Heart Necklace: The Crossed Heart Necklace is a Hardmode accessory item made by combining a Panic Necklace and a Cross Necklace at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Player gains the Panic! buff for 8 seconds upon taking damage, increasing their movement speed by 100%
Doubles the length of invincibility frames after taking damage
Crowno's set: Crowno's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Crowno, an artist that develops graphics for Terraria.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Crowno's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Cryocore Brick: Cryocore Brick is a type of decorative brick obtained by throwing Luminite Brick into Shimmer during a First Quarter.
Cryocore Brick Wall: Cryocore Brick Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Cryocore Bricks.
Crystal Assassin armor: Crystal Assassin armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Crystal Assassin Hood, Crystal Assassin Shirt, and Crystal Assassin Pants. Queen Slime always drops one piece / two pieces upon defeat.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
The ability to dash by pressing Dash, or by double-tapping ◀ Left or ▶ Right while the "Double Tap Dashing" setting is enabled.
Crystal Ball: The Crystal Ball is a Hardmode furniture item which functions as a crafting station. It is purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Crystal Ball grants the Clairvoyance buff and opens its crafting menu.
The Clairvoyance buff boosts the following magic-related stats:

The Clairvoyance buff lasts until the player dies or leaves the world. The buff can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

Unlike equipment buff items, the Crystal Ball must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 2×2 tiles being available.
Crystal Block: The Crystal Block is a Hardmode decorative building block crafted from Crystal Shards at an Adamantite or Titanium Forge. It has a luminous shade with colors ranging from magenta to blue. It can be made into Crystal Block Walls and other Crystal furniture.
Crystal Block Wall: The Crystal Block Wall is a type of Wall that can be crafted with Crystal Blocks. It has a purple-blue color, along with a dark tone.
Crystal Bullet: The Crystal Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It shatters upon impact with enemies or solid blocks, splitting into two small shards. The shards have a short range, can pass through blocks, and each deal 50% of the gun and bullet's combined damage.
Crystal Dart: The Crystal Dart is a Hardmode dart. It can bounce between enemies and blocks, automatically targeting nearby enemies. The Crystal Dart can either bounce off blocks or hit enemies for a total of 5 times, reducing its damage by 15% per bounce.
Crystal Serpent: The Crystal Serpent is a Hardmode wand that can be obtained extremely rarely by fishing in The Hallow biome in any layer.

When used, it fires a pink charge that shatters into 3–5 smaller sparks upon impact with an enemy or block, each of which deals 80% of the weapon's damage and knockback (32 base damage and a knockback of 3.52 (Weak)). These sparks are affected by gravity and bounce off blocks, lasting for 0.67 seconds before dissipating.
It is the Hallowed counterpart to the Corruption's Toxikarp, the Crimson's Bladetongue, and the Jungle's Barnacle Staff.
Crystal Shard: Crystal Shards are a common Hardmode crafting material found in the Underground Hallow. They can naturally grow on the left, right, and bottom sides of Pearlstone, Pink Ice, Pearlsand, Hardened Pearlsand, and Pearlsandstone Blocks. Due to their constant regrowth, they can be farmed (see Guide:Farming resources § Crystal Shards for details). Crystal Shards emit a small glow, similar to Demonite Ore and Crimtane Ore. They do not spread the Hallow.
When a Crystal Shard is to be grown, it has a 1/50 (2%) chance to be replaced by a Gelatin Crystal (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) instead.
Crystal Shards furthermore have a 1/2 (50%) chance to be obtained from Divine Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), in stacks of 4–10.

Crystal Shards are also placeable in nearly any position (on walls, floors, and ceilings), though they are often not luminous enough to replace other light sources, and placement has no other functional effect. Although natural Crystal Shards can only grow on blocks related with The Hallow, they can be placed anywhere once harvested.

Crafting all items, including only one color of Phasesaber and excluding consumables and furniture, requires a total of 90 Crystal Shards. The amount required to craft every weapon and every color of Phasesaber is 290 Crystal Shards.
Crystal Slime: The Crystal Slime is a Hardmode slime and boss servant that is summoned by Queen Slime alongside Bouncy Slimes and Heavenly Slimes. It fires a Crystal Spike projectile every 0.83 seconds. In Expert Mode, it fires three projectiles at once every 0.42 seconds, but only if there are fewer than four other Crystal Slimes alive. Otherwise, it behaves like in Classic Mode.
Crystal Storm: The Crystal Storm is a Hardmode spell book that rapidly fires a slight spread of small crystal shards. The shards last for 2.5 seconds each and slow down as they travel. They can bounce off blocks an unlimited amount of times for their duration, and do not pierce.

The Crystal Storm is the Hallow counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Flames and the Crimson's Golden Shower, all of which require a Spell Tome and ingredients exclusive to their underground biome counterparts.
Crystal Thresher: Sand Sharks are Hardmode enemies only found in Desert biomes during a Sandstorm. They are able to "swim" through all varieties of Sand, Hardened Sand, and Sandstone Blocks, but will collide normally against any other block. When they draw near a player, they will lunge out of the sand to attack.
The Sand Shark itself only appears in ordinary Deserts. There are other variants for different versions of the Desert:
Bone Biter in the Corrupted Desert
Flesh Reaver in the Crimson Desert
Crystal Thresher in the Hallowed Desert
Crystal Vile Shard: The Crystal Vile Shard is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Hallowed Mimics. When used, it extends a crystal spike from the player's position, which passes through blocks, pierces infinite enemies, and deals 0.17 s global invincibility.

The crystal spike has 7–8 shaft segments followed by 1 head segment, and each has a length of 2 tiles. The head deals 125% of the weapon's damage and knockback. The spike extends segmentally every 0.05 s, with each individual segment lasting 0.15 s.

The projectiles of Crystal Vile Shard have 10 armor penetration, which stacks with the former segment.Hence the actual armor penetration increases with segments, from the root's 10 to the head's 80 or 90.
Cultist set: The Cultist set is a vanity set purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) after the Lunatic Cultist has been defeated. Its appearance is based on the clothing worn by Cultists, but its design is different from the robes worn either by normal Lunatic Devotees or the Lunatic Cultist itself. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The Solar Cultist set consists of the Solar Cultist Hood and the Solar Cultist Robe, which are sold during the day.
The Lunar Cultist set consists of the Lunar Cultist Hood and the Lunar Cultist Robe, which are sold during the night.
Cups: Cups are a type of decorative furniture that can be placed on a table, Work Bench, or other flat furniture item. Once placed, all cups function as Placed Bottle crafting stations.
There are four cup variants. Three are crafted and one (the Chalice) is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Silver.
Cursed Arrow: The Cursed Arrow is a Hardmode arrow. It inflicts the Cursed Inferno debuff for 7 seconds upon contact with enemies.
Its Crimson counterpart is the Ichor Arrow.
Cursed Bullet: The Cursed Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It inflicts the Cursed Inferno debuff for 7 seconds on hit, causing damage over time that cannot be extinguished by water (unlike the On Fire! debuff).
Its Crimson counterpart is the Ichor Bullet.
Cursed Dart: The Cursed Dart is a Hardmode dart. As it travels, it releases cursed flames that fall and land on blocks, lingering for 3 seconds before dissipating. The Cursed Dart can hit up to 3 targets. The cursed flames cannot pierce enemies and deal 80% of the Cursed Dart's damage and 50% of its knockback. The darts and flames both inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff for 3–6 seconds on hit.
It is the Corruption's counterpart to the Crimson's Ichor Dart.
Cursed Flame: Cursed Flame is a Hardmode crafting material, whose Crimson counterpart is Ichor. It is dropped by World Feeders, Vile Ghouls and Clingers, all of which can be found in The Corruption. It can also be found in Defiled Crates.
Cursed Flames: The Cursed Flames are a Hardmode spell book that fire gravity-affected bouncing green fireballs. The fireballs can bounce off blocks four times and pierce enemies once, and they inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff for 7 seconds on hit, dealing 24 damage per second.

The Cursed Flames are the Corruption counterpart to the Crimson's Golden Shower and the Hallow's Crystal Storm, all of which require a Spell Tome and ingredients exclusive to their underground biome counterparts.
Cursed Hammer: The Cursed Hammer is a Hardmode enemy which spawns in the Underground Corruption. It hovers and spins before lunging at the player, traveling through any blocks to reach them. Any damage dealt to it stops its attack, forcing it to pause and spin again. It has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Cursed debuff upon contact.
Cursed Piper Flute: The Cursed Piper Flute is a transformation mount item that turns the player into a Rat. While in this form, the player has a small hitbox and can fit in 1-tile gaps, but loses their ability to use items; using items will result in the player dismounting and returning to normal. The rat form also grants the player the ability to stick to the sides of blocks by moving in the direction of them, while slowly sliding down. The player can also climb up blocks by holding ▲ Up, and slide down blocks quicker by holding ▼ Down. The rat forms replaces player's hurt sound with a rat's squeak.
The Cursed Piper Flute can be found in Ivy Chests within the Underground Jungle.
Cursed Sapling: The Cursed Sapling is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Cursed Sapling that follows the player. It appears as a small, dark blue tree stump with a jagged head, a jack-o-lantern face, and roots on which it walks. The Cursed Sapling is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave.
Cursed Skull: The Cursed Skull is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy that spawns in the Dungeon. It is similar to the Meteor Head, with high damage, slow speed, and the ability to travel through tiles. It floats slowly towards the player, occasionally stopping to float in a circle around them for a while, before suddenly lunging forward to attack, similar to the Eye of Cthulhu. Upon striking a player, the Cursed Skull has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of inflicting the Cursed debuff for 4 / 8 / 10 seconds. This renders the player unable to use items, including weapons, potions, and hooks, making it very difficult to avoid taking further damage.
Cursed Skulls spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by brick walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Cutlass: The Cutlass is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by regular Pirate Invasion enemies (excluding the Parrot), a 1/50 (2%) chance from Pirate Captains, and a 1/10 (10%) chance from the Flying Dutchman. Striking enemies with the weapon increases its damage by 12% per hit, up to a maximum of 50%. This damage bonus decays at a rate of 0.5% per tick or 30% per second.
Cyan Beetle: The Cyan Beetle is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Ice biome in the Cavern Layer. When killed, it will always drop the Cyan Husk, which can be used to craft Cyan Dye.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Cyan Husk: The Cyan Husk is a dye material that is dropped by Cyan Beetles, which only spawn in the Underground Snow biome. Its sole purpose is to make Cyan Dye.
Cyborg: The Cyborg is a Hardmode, post-Plantera NPC vendor who sells several "high-tech" items, most notably rocket ammunition for launcher weapons. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

The Cyborg will defend himself against nearby enemies with three different kinds of explosives: grenades, rockets, and proximity mines, which are identical in behavior to the Grenade Launcher, Rocket Launcher, and Proximity Mine Launcher respectively. The Cyborg's proximity mines will also deal triple their usual damage when stationary.
Cyborg set: The Cyborg set is a vanity set which consists of the Cyborg Helmet, Cyborg Shirt, and Cyborg Pants, resembling the Cyborg NPC. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
It is purchased from the Cyborg for 9 Gold (set), during Halloween.
D-Town's set: D-Town's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for D-Town, the Business Director at Re-Logic. Equipping the full set produces a pulsating effect similar to Adamantite armor, as well as a glow effect similar to Spooky armor.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
D-Town's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
DPS Meter: The DPS Meter is an informational accessory that displays the DPS of the weapon that last dealt damage to any entity, including enemies, critters, NPCs, Target Dummies, and other players.
The DPS Meter can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold.
Daedalus Stormbow: The Daedalus Stormbow is a Hardmode bow that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Hallowed Mimics. When used, it causes a wide spread of arrows to rain from the sky, directed towards the cursor. It fires two to four arrows per use, while only consuming a single arrow from the player's inventory.
Damselfish: Damselfish are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in pure Space layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Calming Potions.
Dangersense Potion: The Dangersense Potion is a buff potion which grants the Dangersense buff when consumed. The buff reveals hazardous traps, blocks, and objects that can potentially harm or impede the player by highlighting them in red, even in complete darkness. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Dangersense Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.
Dao of Pow: The Dao of Pow is a Hardmode flail. It has a 4/5 (80%) chance of inflicting the Confused debuff for 2–4 seconds upon striking an enemy.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Dark Artist armor: Dark Artist armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem mage/summoner armor set consisting of the Dark Artist's Hat, Dark Artist's Robes, and Dark Artist's Leggings. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 150 Defender Medals.
The Dark Artist armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Apprentice armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

Flameburst sentry summons have 50% increased attack range (84 tiles), 40% increased projectile velocity, a significantly increased field of view, and increased projectile explosion radius (from a 6×6 to 13×13-tile rectangle).
The Phantom Phoenix's Phoenix projectile explosion radius is increased from a 6×6 to 13×13-tile rectangle.
Dark Caster: The Dark Caster is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Dungeon. They follow the Caster AI, firing three Water Sphere projectiles before teleporting to another on-screen location. Water Spheres travel through walls but can be destroyed with a single hit from any weapon.
The Dark Caster has a Red Hat variant summoned by the Red Hat Skeletron, with slightly different behavior (see Red Hat Skeletron for details).
Dark Celestial Brick: Dark Celestial Brick is a type of decorative brick obtained by throwing Luminite Brick into Shimmer during a Waning Crescent.
Dark Celestial Brick Wall: Dark Celestial Brick Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Dark Celestial Bricks.
Dark Harvest: The Dark Harvest is a Hardmode, post-Plantera whip that is dropped by Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. It has a 10% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

Marks enemies with dark energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by the Dark Harvest, it triggers a Reaping effect, causing up to 3 nearby targets to take 15 damage. Reaping is not affected by any damage bonuses and has 50 armor penetration. The dark energy is not consumed upon activating its effect and its duration can be refreshed.
Grants the Harvest Time buff, increasing whip speed by 35% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits.
Dark Lance: The Dark Lance is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron spear that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. The Dark Lance inflicts the Shadowflame debuff for 4–5 seconds and creates a small shockwave at its tip.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Dark Mage: The Dark Mage is a mini-boss that spawns during the Old One's Army event, during wave 5 in Tier 1, and waves 4 and 6 in Tier 3.
Dark Mage's Tome: The Dark Mage's Tome is a mount-summoning item that places the player on a Book Mount which grants limited flight. The Dark Mage's Tome has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Dark Mage in Master Mode.

The mount allows a player to hover and glide at a fixed height of 8 tiles high in mid-air for 5 seconds following a jump or walking off a ledge. It otherwise glides along the ground, and automatically climbs ledges that are no more than 1-tile-high. Whether on the ground or hovering, its top speed is 41 mph. The Book Mount also cancels fall damage.
Extra jump accessories can be used during hover, increasing the max hover height. The height is also adjustable in the down direction by pressing ▼ Down.
Dark Mummy: Mummies are Hardmode enemies that spawn in the Desert biome and areas where Sand Blocks are present. They follow the Fighter AI, behaving similarly to Zombies.

There are several different types of Mummies: the standard Mummy, as well as the Dark Mummy, Light Mummy, and Blood Mummy. They spawn in Corrupted Deserts, Hallowed Deserts and Crimson Deserts, respectively.

Dark Mummies and Blood Mummies are 50% faster than other Mummies. All mummies receive a 100% speed increase when their health is reduced below 50%. In addition, Mummies inflict the following debuffs upon hitting the player:
Dark Shard: The Dark Shard is a Hardmode crafting material used in the crafting of the Dao of Pow, Onyx Blaster and Ruinous Staff. It has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Dark Mummies and Shadow Mummies (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) in Corrupt Deserts, and Blood Mummies (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in Crimson Deserts.

On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, the Dark Shard also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to drop from Tainted/Vile Ghouls which respectively spawn within the Crimson/Corrupted Underground Desert, and a 1/25 (4%) chance of dropping from Bone Biters and Flesh Reavers.
The Hallow counterpart is the Light Shard.
Dart Pistol: The Dart Pistol is a Hardmode ranged weapon that autofires darts as ammunition, and is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Dart Rifle, with a higher rate of fire but lower damage. It has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics.
Dart Rifle: The Dart Rifle is a Hardmode ranged weapon that autofires darts as ammunition, and is the Corruption counterpart to the Crimson's Dart Pistol, with higher damage but a lower rate of fire. It has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Mimics.
Dart Trap: The Dart Trap is a trap that can be found naturally placed in Cavern layer and Dungeon. It fires a dart when triggered via wire which does not consume any ammunition. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 3 1/3 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 3 seconds between firing. The darts deal 40 / 80 / 120 damage and inflict Poisoned for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds to players (20 damage and 10 seconds of Poisoned to NPCs, enemies, and critters).
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Dart Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer.
Daybloom: Daybloom is a type of herb that appears as a small yellow flower with a straight green stem. It grows naturally on regular grass and Hallowed grass. Daybloom can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Daybloom Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles.

Daybloom blooms during daytime (4:30 AM to 7:29 PM). Its blooming is indicated by the yellow sunflower-like head. Harvesting mature Daybloom yields 1 Daybloom item. Harvesting blooming Daybloom yields 1 Daybloom item and 1–3 Daybloom Seeds. Harvesting blooming Daybloom with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Dayblooms and 1–5 Daybloom Seeds instead.
Both Daybloom and Daybloom Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag. Daybloom can also be dropped by Angry Dandelions.
Daybloom Seeds: Daybloom Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Dayblooms while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Dayblooms while they are fully grown. Daybloom will only bloom during daytime, showing off a sunflower-like head. Each plant will drop 1–3 Daybloom Seeds when harvested while blooming.

Daybloom Seeds can be placed on pure and Hallowed grass (including Mowed grass and Mowed Hallowed grass), empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Dayblooms. They will grow anywhere, not just in direct sunlight on the Surface, but will only yield seeds when blooming.
Daybloom Staff: The Daybloom Staff is an early pre-Hardmode wand which fires a short-ranged burst of 4 non-piercing yellow pellets toward the cursor with slight inaccuracy.
Daybreak: The Daybreak is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist melee weapon that fires a gravity-affected sun spear projectile. It sticks onto the targeted enemy upon contact, dealing damage and inflicting the Daybroken debuff, which deals 100 damage per second for a duration of 5 seconds. Up to eight sun spears can be stuck onto a single enemy at one time, resulting in 800 DPS for the debuff.

When more than eight sun spears are attached, the earliest one will dissipate and cause a Solar Explosion. Additionally, a sun spear will dissipate and cause a Solar Explosion whenever it collides with blocks, when the target it is stuck to dies, or when its duration ends. Solar Explosions deal the weapon's damage and inflicts the Daybroken debuff, but cannot deal critical hits.

Its best modifier is Ruthless. Since part of the Daybreak's damage output comes from the Solar Explosions which cannot critically hit, critical hit chance bonuses are less effective than direct increases in damage.
Deactivated Probe: The Deactivated Probe is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Destroyer-Lite, a miniature version of The Destroyer that follows the player. The Deactivated Probe has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by The Destroyer in Master Mode.
Dead Man's Chest: The Dead Man's Chest is a naturally-generated Chest rigged with a large variety of traps in order to kill the player upon opening it. This setup usually includes 3–5 Boulder traps, 2–6 Dart Traps, and 0–3 Explosives, with a possibility of 1–2 Geysers if generated at depths in which lava can spawn naturally. The Boulder traps are set up above the chest, the Dart Traps are set up horizontally, and the Explosives are hidden underneath.
Dead Man's Chests will always generate alone, and never in an Underground Cabin.
The Dead Man's Chest will contain standard Gold Chest loot based on where it is found, as well as having a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to contain the Dead Man's Sweater.
Dead Man's Sweater: The Dead Man's Sweater is an armor item with a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being found inside Dead Man's Chests. It provides 4 defense, and reduces the duration of the debuffs inflicted by trap projectiles and the damage dealt by them by 50%. If the damage dealt by trap projectiles is greater than 300 after the 50% reduction, it is then set to 300. This is applied before the damage is reduced by the player's defense.
Deadly Sphere: The Deadly Sphere is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. Upon spawning, it flies randomly in the direction of the player until it is within close enough proximity while traveling through blocks. Upon noticing the player, the Deadly Sphere grows spikes and begins to spin before rapidly charging toward them indefinitely while attempting to remain directly on top of them. While attacking the player, they are unable to charge through blocks.
Deadly Sphere Staff: The Deadly Sphere Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Deadly Sphere minion. It flies and charges through enemies at a high velocity but cannot move through blocks. Once every three attacks, it briefly stops in place to cycle through one of three forms before continuing to attack. The Deadly Sphere Staff has a 1/30 (3.33%) / 59/900 (6.56%) chance of being dropped by Deadly Spheres.
Death Sickle: The Death Sickle is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance of being dropped by Reapers during the Solar Eclipse event. When swung, it fires a spinning purple sickle that can pass through blocks. The sickles travel slowly for about 12 tiles before stopping in place, can pierce four enemies, or linger for three seconds before dissipating.
Deathbringer Pickaxe: The Deathbringer Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Hellstone, Crimstone Blocks, and Ebonstone Blocks.
Its Corruption counterpart is the Nightmare Pickaxe. The Deathbringer Pickaxe has slightly more pickaxe power and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Deathweed: Deathweed is a type of herb which appears as a short, withered purple stalk. It grows naturally on Ebonstone, Crimstone, Corrupt grass, Crimson grass, Corrupt Jungle grass, and Crimson Jungle grass. Deathweed can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Deathweed Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles.

Deathweed blooms during a Blood Moon or a full moon at nighttime (7:30 PM to 4:29 AM). Its blooming is indicated by purple glowing particles. Harvesting mature Deathweed yields 1 Deathweed item. Harvesting blooming Deathweed yields 1 Deathweed item and 1–3 Deathweed Seeds. Harvesting blooming Deathweed with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Deathweeds and 1–5 Deathweed Seeds instead.
Both Deathweed and Deathweed Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.
Deathweed Seeds: Deathweed Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Deathweeds while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Deathweeds while they are fully grown. A Deathweed plant only blooms during Blood Moons and Full Moons. Its blooming state can be identified by the sickly red pods on its leaves. Each plant will drop 1–3 Deathweed Seeds when harvested while blooming.

Deathweed Seeds can be placed on Corrupt and Crimson grass, Ebonstone and Crimstone Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Deathweeds. They will grow anywhere, not just in the evil biomes, but will only yield seeds when blooming.
Decay Chamber: The Decay Chamber is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Lesion furniture (Corruption-themed furniture) out of Lesion Blocks. The Decay Chamber can be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold but only appears for sale in worlds that are generated with The Corruption. It can also be crafted from the Flesh Cloning Vat, its Crimson counterpart.
Lesion Blocks are crafted using a Meat Grinder, so the Decay Chamber is of little use without one.
Decorative Cobweb: Decorative Cobweb is a building material that is visually identical to Cobwebs, with the exception that it is not destroyed by weapons, projectiles, or contact with entities. Additionally, it does not slow down entities on contact.
Decorative Healing Potion: The Decorative Healing Potion is a furniture item and crafting station that can only be placed on flat-surface items. It generates naturally on Dungeon shelves, and drops a Lesser Healing Potion when mined. It shares recipes with Placed Bottles.
Its thematic counterpart is the Decorative Mana Potion.
Decorative Mana Potion: The Decorative Mana Potion is a furniture item and crafting station that can only be placed on flat-surface items. It generates naturally on Dungeon shelves, and drops a Lesser Mana Potion when mined. It shares recipes with Placed Bottles.
Its thematic counterpart is the Decorative Healing Potion.
Deer Thing: The Deer Thing is a boss-summoning item that summons Deerclops when used. It can only be used in the Snow or Ice biome, at any time.
In addition to being crafted, Deer Things also have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Frozen Chests found in the Ice biome (but not Snow).
Deerclops: Deerclops is a pre-Hardmode boss encountered in the Snow biome. Fighting Deerclops is not required for game progression, but defeating it rewards the player with coins and other useful items.
While Deerclops is alive, its exclusive music Deerclops will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Deerclops Eyeball: The Deerclops Eyeball is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Tiny Deerclops that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, Tiny Deerclops flies while holding onto a bird to catch up with them. The Deerclops Eyeball has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops in Master Mode.
Defender Medal: Defender Medals are a form of currency used to purchase items from the Tavernkeep. They are obtained in the Old One's Army event, being dropped by the Eternia Crystal at the end of each wave, beginning with the third wave. Betsy's Expert Mode Treasure Bag also contains 30–49 Defender Medals. In addition, the player can obtain 10 Defender Medals by talking to the Tavernkeep and selecting the "Eternia Crystal" option, but this can only be done once per character.
Defender's Forge: The Defender's Forge is a portable, personal storage item which is purchased from the Tavernkeep for 50 Defender Medals.
The storage provided by the Defender's Forge is separate from the Piggy Bank, Safe, and Void Vault, so it allows the player to carry significantly more items at any given time.
Defiled Crate: The Defiled Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in The Corruption. Defiled Crates contain items found in standard crates, and additionally always drop an item normally obtained by destroying a Shadow Orb. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Corrupt Crate.
Demolitionist: The Demolitionist is an NPC vendor who sells explosives. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
The player has an explosive in their inventory (items stored in storage items like chests, or portable storage items like the Piggy Bank do not count towards this requirement).
These requirements only apply to the initial spawning. If the Demolitionist is killed, he will automatically respawn after some time.
The Demolitionist will defend himself against nearby enemies by throwing Grenades. He deals 20 / 30 / 35 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
Demon: The Demon is a pre-Hardmode enemy found in The Underworld. It attacks by summoning volleys of four spinning purple blades that gradually accelerate toward the player, which are similar to those fired by the Demon Scythe that it has a chance to drop. These blades deal high damage and have a chance to inflict the Darkness debuff for 15 / 30 / 37.5 seconds and are stopped by any block, but cannot be destroyed with weapons.
Like other Underworld enemies, the Demon is immune to lava. A rarer variation of the Demon is the Voodoo Demon.
Demon Bow: The Demon Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Tendon Bow.
Demon Conch: The Demon Conch is a rare pre-Hardmode tool obtainable by fishing in lava. It teleports the player to the center of the Underworld 0.75 seconds (45 ticks) after being used. Like the Magic Mirror, it can be used infinitely at no cost, making it a viable alternative to using conventional hellevators.
Demon Eye: The Demon Eye is a common pre-Hardmode flying enemy that appears in most surface biomes during nighttime, particularly in Forests. It has a slow turn rate, follows the player, and bounces off blocks. Its trajectory is changed when hit with a weapon that causes knockback.
Demon Heart: The Demon Heart is a Hardmode permanent booster item that permanently grants the player an extra accessory slot, for use only within Expert and Master Mode worlds. This effect does not stack and may only be used once per player. The Demon Heart is always dropped from the Wall of Flesh's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. If a player opens the Wall of Flesh's Treasure Bag after they have already consumed a Demon Heart, another one will not be obtained.

When a player who consumed a Demon Heart is in a Classic Mode world (a non-Expert or Master world), the extra accessory slot is disabled, removing all functional or display effects from any items equipped in the slot, and darkening the slot itself. Players in Classic worlds are also prevented from equipping items in the sixth or seventh slot, though an equipped item in the slot may still be taken out, and placed back into the inventory.
Demon Horns: The Demon Horns are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.
Demon Scythe: The Demon Scythe is a pre-Hardmode spell book that has a 1/35 (2.86%) chance of being dropped by Demons and Voodoo Demons. When used, it fires a sickle projectile that is initially static before gradually accelerating. The sickles can hit up to five times before dissipating, and they cannot pass through blocks.
Demonite Bar: The Demonite Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Crimtane Bar.
Demonite Brick: Demonite Brick is a brick crafted from Demonite Ore and Ebonstone. A box of it also appears after the Wall of Flesh has been defeated on a Corruption world ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) in any type of world). It is not resistant to explosions, and gives off a faint glow when placed.
Demonite Brick Wall: Demonite Brick Wall is a wall crafted from a Demonite Brick. It emits a faint blue glow when placed.
Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.
Demonite Ore: Demonite Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It is primarily dropped from the Eater of Worlds, as well as the Eye of Cthulhu in Corruption worlds. Demonite Ore can also be found rarely in small veins underground. When below 0 ft in elevation, a Gold Pickaxe or better is needed to mine it, otherwise any pickaxe can be used.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Crimtane Ore.
Depth Meter: The Depth Meter is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the player's vertical position, or depth. Depth is relative to the boundary between the Surface and Underground layers, which has a depth of 0 and is displayed as "Level". Depth is shown in the number of feet (1 foot = 1/2 tile) to this boundary, and is measured from the player's feet. The display also shows the name of the current layer.

The Depth Meter has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Cave Bats, Jungle Bats, Ice Bats, Giant Bats, and Spore Bats. Furthermore, it has a 1/80 (1.25%) chance of being dropped from Crawdads (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Giant Shellies (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Salamanders (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Derpling: The Derpling is a Hardmode, insect-like enemy which spawns on the surface Jungle during the day in place of the Giant Flying Foxes which spawn at night. It jumps high, can strafe to the sides in mid-air, and attempts to land on top of the player. Derplings should be defeated quickly, as they spawn fast and can easily overwhelm the player.
Desert Fossil: Desert Fossil is a type of block found in the Underground Desert biome in medium to large veins. Desert Fossils can be used with an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to produce Sturdy Fossils, along with regular Extractinator drops.
Desert Fossil Wall: The Desert Fossil Wall is a type of background wall that can be crafted from Desert Fossils.
Desert Spirit: The Desert Spirit is a Hardmode enemy that can be found in Corrupted or Crimson Underground Desert biomes. The Desert Spirit has an attack pattern that is unique compared to most enemies. Upon appearing near a player, it will begin casting 5 Desert Spirit's Curse projectiles that attempts to home in on the nearest player, phasing through blocks and slowly gaining speed. After 3 seconds, the projectiles will explode. The projectiles themselves do not deal any damage, but their explosions do. Similar to other casters, the Desert Spirit will finally teleport to a different location and repeat the process.
Desert Spirit Lamp: The Desert Spirit Lamp is a decorative Hardmode furniture item and crafting material. It can only be placed on flat-surface furniture. It has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped from Desert Spirits, which can be encountered in the Corrupted or Crimson Underground Desert.
Desert Tiger Staff: The Desert Tiger Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Desert Tiger minion. It runs towards enemies to deal contact damage. Every six seconds, the tiger can perform a pounce attack at nearby enemies, dealing 50% extra damage (+20 base damage) and passing through blocks to reach them.

When the Desert Tiger Staff is used more than once, multiple Desert Tigers do not spawn; instead, the existing Desert Tiger becomes stronger (+16/+17 damage; 40% of the weapon's listed damage, which is additive to pounce's 50%) and faster for each additional summon. The Desert Tiger appears as a cub if summoned 1 to 3 times, an adult if summoned 4 to 6 times, and an armored adult if summoned 7 or more times.
The Desert Tiger Staff is always found in the Dungeon's Desert Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Desert Key after Plantera has been defeated.

Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach a certain threshold (including whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless. The exact threshold varies depending on the number of summons, which is listed in Notes below.
Destroyer Emblem: The Destroyer Emblem is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that gives the player 10% increased damage and 8% increased critical strike chance.
Detonator: Detonators are activation mechanisms that can be found underground as part of traps, wired to Explosives. They are often found planted on top of suspiciously large veins of underground metals (e.g. Silver).

A Detonator be tripped either with ⚷ Open / Activate or when a player falls on the plunger, while it cannot be triggered by enemies or NPCs. Detonators send an activation trigger to other mechanisms connected to it through Wire when tripped.

Unlike pressure plates, a player has to actually fall from above to trigger a Detonator. Even walking off a 1.5 block high column will not work, while walking off a 2 block high column reliably triggers it. This makes explosive traps that use a Detonator instead of a pressure plate slightly less dangerous as they are more difficult to trigger accidentally (as well as much easier to see).

When triggered by player, a Detonator disables itself for one second. When activated by a Wire, it is disabled until it is activated by Wire again. When it is disabled, plunger is stuck down and it cannot be triggered.
Devil Horns: The Devil Horns are a vanity item that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.
Unlike Demon Horns, they do not hide the player's hair.
Devourer: The Devourer is a pre-Hardmode worm enemy that spawns in the Corruption, though it is less common than the abundant Eaters of Souls. Like other worms, it attacks by burrowing through blocks to reach the player.
The Devourer requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Diabolist: The Diabolist is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It attacks by firing Inferno Bolts at the player, which can travel through blocks. In addition to dealing direct damage to the player, the bolts also explode upon reaching where they were aimed at, creating a large flaming sphere that lasts for 9 seconds and deals massive damage on contact. Both the bolts and the spheres inflict the On Fire! debuff for 8–15 / 16–30 / 20–37.5 seconds. Diabolists teleport to a different location on-screen after firing three projectiles or upon being hit.
Diabolists spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by tiled walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Diamond: Diamond is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. Out of all available gems, Diamond is the most valuable gem, being able to craft its corresponding set of standard gem items, and it also has two exclusive recipes: the Magic Mirror and the Diamond Toilet. It can be obtained in the following ways:
Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable white gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form.
Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator.
Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance.
Rarely, Diamond can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well.
Like all other gems, Diamond can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.
Diamond Bunny: Gem Bunnies are harmless critters that can only spawn in the Cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Bunnies, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa.
Gem Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Bunny Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Diamond Ring: The Diamond Ring is a vanity accessory. When worn, it places a blue dot on each of the player's wrists. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Platinum.
The Diamond Ring cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Diamond Robe: The Diamond Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. When worn, the Diamond Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to hit in a larger radius and pierce an additional enemy. The Diamond Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4.

Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Diamond Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.
Diamond Squirrel: Gem Squirrels are harmless critters that can only spawn in the cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Squirrels, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa. Gem Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Gem Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Squirrel Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Diamond Staff: The Diamond Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires a bright white bolt which can pierce once and has a large hitbox, indicated by the faint, extra shine. While wearing a gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details).
Digger: The Digger is a worm enemy that appears in the Underground and Cavern layers in Hardmode. On Old-gen console and 3DS, it completely replaces the pre-Hardmode Giant Worm. On Desktop, Console, and Mobile, Giant Worms still spawn rarely in Hardmode, but share kill count and banner with Diggers.
Digging Molecart: The Digging Molecart is a minecart that automatically digs a tunnel and lays down regular Minecart Tracks. It is sold by the Zoologist for 50 Gold once the Bestiary is 25% completed (137 entries).

Once mounted on existing tracks, the Digging Molecart moves forward with a maximum speed of 31 mph, digging out a tunnel five tiles high and laying track as it goes. The Digging Molecart will only move and place tracks horizontally, even if it is started on a diagonal slope.
