Digtoise: Digtoise is a pre-Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Digtoise that follows the player. While holding the item, pressing ⚒ Use / Attack causes it to roll in the direction of the cursor. Upon contact with a block, it will start mining in that direction (either downwards or horizontally) 3 blocks at a time, with a pickaxe power equivalent to 26% (lower than any pickaxe) and mining speed of 20. When digging horizontally, it can pass over a one-tile gap, but a gap of two or more tiles will cause it to stop. It will also stop when it hits a block that it does not have enough pickaxe power to mine. While holding the item, pressing ⚒ Use / Attack anywhere on the screen besides Digtoise itself causes it to stop mining, while pressing ⚷ Open / Activate anywhere besides Digtoise itself causes it to despawn. While Digtoise is alive, it will appear on the map with its own icon, and an exclamation mark will appear next to Digtoise item in the player's hotbar. Like other Pals, it can be petted by using ⚷ Open / Activate directly on it.

Digtoise is rarely found as "Sleeping Digtoise", a solid object in the Underground Desert. The Sleeping Digtoise has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to replace Antlion Eggs during world generation, and has a 1/100 (1%) chance to replace Antlion Eggs when they regrow.
Dirt Block: The Dirt Block is one of the most common blocks in Terraria, occurring naturally almost everywhere throughout the world. All caves above the elevation of 0 ft are made of Dirt. Below 0 ft, in the underground layer, the caves are made of roughly 50% Dirt. Small patches of Dirt can be found in the cavern layer, though it is mostly made of Stone.

Dirt Blocks may be covered by different types of grass: regular, Corrupt, Crimson, Hallowed, mowed, or mowed Hallowed. Grass spreads onto adjacent Dirt Blocks, and it can be grown manually using seeds or the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth.
In all cases, the grass applies to the block as a whole, and will appear on all exposed surfaces.

If a grass block is covered by blocks on its four sides, the grass will remain and show as markings on the block. However, if the block is completely surrounded with eight blocks, the grass is lost and the block will revert to regular Dirt.
Dirt Bomb: The Dirt Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Bomb, but its explosion will place Dirt Blocks in open spaces, instead of destroying blocks. Existing blocks within the explosion radius will remain unaffected.
Dirt Rod: The Dirt Rod is a unique tool that is used solely to move Dirt Blocks around, and is unlike the use of ordinary mining tools and block placement. When used while the cursor is over a Dirt Block, the block becomes a Dirt Ball projectile that sticks to the cursor as long as the ⚒ Use / Attack key is held down. The Dirt Ball can be carried through blocks and relocated anywhere on the screen. When released, the Dirt Ball is affected by gravity and also continues to carry the speed it was being moved at previously, allowing it to be "thrown". Upon impact with any blocks, a released Dirt Ball turns back into a solid Dirt Block.
The Dirt Rod is purchased from the Dryad for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 Gold / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 20 Gold.
Dirt Wall: The Dirt Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in most caves and under overhangs on the surface, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
The Natural Dirt Wall is an item that places an unsafe Dirt Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Dirt Wall into Shimmer.
Dirt Walls (natural): The Cracked Dirt Wall, Crumbling Dirt Wall, Layered Dirt Wall, and Wavy Dirt Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground layer, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
Disc Wall: The Disc Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated on Floating Islands. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.
Disco Ball: The Disco Ball is a novelty Hardmode light source that can be placed on the underside of blocks, generating short pulses of colored light that cycle through the spectrum (In the Nintendo 3DS version, the Disco Ball will cycle through red, green, and blue only). The light can be toggled with wires. It is purchased from the Merchant in Hardmode for 1 Gold each.
Discount Card: The Discount Card is a Hardmode accessory. When equipped, it reduces NPC shop buy prices, Nurse healing, and reforging prices by 1/5 (20%). The card must be equipped before talking to an NPC to enable discounts.

The Discount Card has a 1/1000 (0.1%) chance to be dropped by pirates (except Parrots) during Pirate Invasions, with a 1/250 (0.4%) chance from the Pirate Captain. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be dropped by the Flying Dutchman.
The Discount Card does not affect the following:
Sell prices (when selling items to NPCs).
Items repurchased after selling them (e.g. selling a Titan Glove for 2 Gold will still cost 2 Gold to take back).
Items sold by the Tavernkeep for Defender Medals, such as his sentry summon weapons.
Diva Slime: Town Slimes are a type of town pet. There are 8 different Town Slimes and all of them can exist at the same time (unlike the different breeds of the Town Bunny, Town Cat, and Town Dog).

Almost all types of Town Slimes are acquired via some form of transformation, similar to the Tax Collector. Afterwards, the transformed Town Slime will move into a vacant house if one is available. If it is killed, it will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house. The initial transformation does not need to be repeated.

Town Slimes can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). They may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for their home tile (standing point).
Divine Crate: The Divine Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in The Hallow. Divine Crates contain items found in standard crates, and additionally have a chance to drop Crystal Shards or Souls of Light. Its pre-Hardmode equivalent is the Hallowed Crate, and its Corruption and Crimson variants are the Defiled Crate and Hematic Crate, respectively.
Diving Gear: The Diving Gear is an accessory that combines the functionality of the Flipper and Diving Helmet:
The player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly.
The player's breath meter will deplete much slower, and the rate at which drowning damage is taken is slowed.
Diving Helmet: The Diving Helmet is an armor piece for the helmet slot. It has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Sharks and Orcas. When equipped, it causes the breath meter to deplete much slower and slows the rate at which drowning damage is taken.
Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester: Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester is a vanity item that has a 1/14 (7.14%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops.
Djinn's Curse: Djinn's Curse is a Hardmode armor item that can be equipped in the "pants" slot. It visually replaces the player's feet with a genie-like effect, similar to the Desert Spirit's appearance.

When equipped in the functional "pants" armor slot, it also provides a slow-fall effect which is exactly identical to the buff of the Featherfall Potion: negates fall damage, and reduces the player's fall speed and gravity by 2/3 (66.67%).

Additionally, holding the ▼ Down key will revert fall speed and gravity back to normal; holding the ▲ Up key will change the fall speed and gravity reduction percentage to 90%. Due to the reduced gravity, the distance players are knocked back when hit by an attack will also be increased.
Djinn's Curse also works with mounts and minecarts (except the Bee Mount, Djinn's Curse has no effect on it), and works during reversed gravity.
Djinn's Curse has a 13/400 (3.25%) chance of being dropped by Desert Spirits.
Doctor Bones: Doctor Bones is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a Zombie variant that rarely appears in the Jungle and Underground Jungle at night. It acts the same as normal zombies, slowly walking towards the player to deal contact damage, while attempting to navigate around obstacles and only being able to open doors during a Blood Moon. It has significantly greater health than all other zombies and deals slightly higher damage. It drops the Archaeologist's Hat when killed.
It does not have any variants, nor does it have an Armed variation in Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. Doctor Bones requires 10 kills to be awarded completion of his Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Dog License: The Dog License is a consumable item that can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold after filling out 25% (137 entries) of the Bestiary.

Upon use, the status message "The license teleports away to the dog delivery service..." is displayed. Following this status message, a Town Dog will move into an available house the next morning. Using a Dog License when a Town Dog is already present in the current world displays the status message "Pet Exchange: Successful!" and causes it to be "exchanged": the Town Dog releases a puff of smoke and has its breed and name rerolled immediately.
Dog Whistle: The Dog Whistle is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Puppy that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Puppy flies by twirling its tail like a propeller to catch up to them. The Dog Whistle can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a 29/12,000 (0.24%) chance in pre-Hardmode and 203/90,000 (0.23%) chance in Hardmode.
Dog set: The Dog set is a vanity set composed of the Dog Tail and Dog Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Full Moon or a Waning Gibbous for 6 Gold (set).
Dolphin: The Dolphin is a critter that spawns and swims in Oceans. Dolphins make typical dolphin sounds and occasionally jump and flip above the Ocean surface. They also sometimes poke their head out of the water in direction of the nearest player.
The Dolphin has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.
Unlike most critters, the Dolphin cannot be caught with a Bug Net, which means there is no craftable cage for it.
Doors: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about.
Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details.

Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door.

The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method.
Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators.
There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 / 19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.
Double Cod: Double Cod are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in the Sky or Surface layers of the Jungle. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Ammo Reservation Potions.
Dr. Man Fly: Dr. Man Fly is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. He mainly attacks by throwing Toxic Flasks at the player, dealing area-of-effect damage. He gives the player a warning about an oncoming Toxic Flask attack by pausing in place. Like the Nailhead and Eyezor, they appear to traverse much slower than many of the other Solar Eclipse enemies, leaving the player enough time to plan a safe attack against them.
Dr. Man Fly set: The Dr. Man Fly set is a Hardmode, post-Plantera vanity set consisting of the Dr. Man Fly Mask and the Dr. Man Fly's Lab Coat. Each piece has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Dr. Man Flies during the Solar Eclipse event.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Dragon Egg: The Dragon Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Hoardagron that follows the player. The Dragon Egg is dropped by Dark Mages during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 1, and a 1/12 (8.33%) chance during Tier 3.
Dragon Fruit: The Dragon Fruit is a Hardmode food and fruit item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Pearlwood tree or Pearlwood Palm tree.
Dragonflies: Dragonflies are small, rare critters which can be found on surface. When approached, they will fly a short distance up and away from the player.
Dragonflies can only spawn during the day when the wind speed is lower than 20 mph, with their weather requirements depending on the number of nearby Town NPCs:
No Town NPCs: They can only spawn when it is not raining.
1 or 2 Town NPCs: They can spawn during both clear weather and rain, though it becomes less likely for them to spawn during clear weather the more NPCs there are.
In Classic Mode or below, they can only spawn during rain.
In Expert Mode or above, they primarily spawn during rain, but have a small chance (1/30 (3.33%) of spawn attempts) to spawn in clear weather.

Furthermore, there must be at least one cattail within a 61×41-tile rectangle area centered on the spawning tile. The dragonfly will spawn on the cattail instead of the original spawning tile. As a result, they are capable of spawning on screen. Black, Orange and Yellow variants can spawn at cattails near Sand Blocks (usually in Desert), whereas Blue, Green and Red variants can spawn at cattails near pure Grass or Mowed grass (usually in Forest). Note that this is determined by the original spawning tile, not the tile the cattail grows, e.g. a Red Dragonfly can spawn on a cattail growing on a Sand Block as long as there is a Grass tile nearby.
Dragonflies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Dragonflies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (dragonfly jars). Once crafted, the Dragonflies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Dragonflies can be spawned by the Dragonfly Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Dragonfly to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Dragonfly to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Dragonfly jars: A dragonfly jar is a piece of decorative furniture created by combining a dragonfly, captured with any Bug Net, with a Bottle. By throwing a dragonfly jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the dragonfly as an item.
Dragonfly jars function the same way as cages for other critters. They have an animated sprite when placed down, and the dragonflies will fly around inside the jars.
Drakanian: The Drakanian is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist ground-based enemy that spawns in the area of the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events. It can originally spawn riding a Drakomire, forming a Drakomire Rider, and each can be separately killed. Killing the Drakomire first will cause the Drakanian to fully heal and attack the player.
Drakin: The Drakin is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Old One's Army event. It spawns during Tier 2 during waves 4–7, and Tier 3 during waves 3–7.

The Drakin has a large amount of health and immunity to knockback and attacks by firing a barrage of six small purple Drakin Shot projectiles every second, making it a rather resilient and difficult enemy.
The Drakin requires 100 kills to be awarded completion of its corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Drakomire: The Drakomire is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist, ground-based enemy that spawns in the area of the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events. It periodically comes to a stop and shoots three Solar Flares at the player. Drakanians will occasionally spawn riding a Drakomire, resulting in a Drakomire Rider.
Drakomire Rider: The Drakomire Rider is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that is a combination of a Drakanian and a Drakomire, and spawns in the area of the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events.
Drax: The Drax is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses drill and axe. It is the alternative to the Pickaxe Axe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Dreadnautilus: The Dreadnautilus is a Hardmode enemy that can be spawned by fishing in water during a Blood Moon. When the bobber dips and the player attempts to reel in a fish, a Dreadnautilus or another enemy (Wandering Eye Fish, Zombie Merman, Blood Eel, or Hemogoblin Shark) has a chance to spawn within a few tiles of the bobber in place of a fish. The Dreadnautilus is rarer than the other four Blood Moon fishing enemies, spawning from only 1/10 (10%) of spawn attempts, on average. It is widely considered the most difficult of these five enemies. If the Dreadnautilus is not defeated by dawn (4:30 AM), it will fly away and despawn.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Dreadnautilus requires 10 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Dreamer Ghoul: Ghouls are Hardmode Underground Desert enemies who follow the Fighter AI (behaving similarly to Zombies). Ordinary Ghouls spawn inside the normal Underground Desert, the Vile Ghoul inside Corrupt parts of the Underground Desert, the Tainted Ghoul inside Crimson parts of the Underground Desert, and the Dreamer Ghoul inside Hallowed parts of the Underground Desert.
Dressers: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement.

There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.
Drill Containment Unit: The Drill Containment Unit (sometimes abbreviated to DCU) is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord mount-summoning item that summons a Drill Mount, a rideable, flying vehicle that mines tiles extremely quickly via a stream of blue lasers. It can fly and hover indefinitely and has a mining range of 15 tiles.
The Drill Mount is one of the fastest controllable ways to mine in Terraria, but it has a number of special characteristics:
Unlike other mounts, players cannot use any tools or weapons while riding the Drill Mount.
Unlike most other mounts, players can fly through liquids while riding the Drill Mount, though they can still drown.

Unlike other mining tools, the Drill Mount does not inflict damage on enemies. It also cannot mine blocks behind other blocks, rather always drilling tunnels through all blocks directly ahead of the player.
Mining speed bonuses do not affect Drill Mount's mining speed.

The Drill Mount flies at 41 mph vertically, 31 mph horizontally, and 51 mph diagonally. Pressing ⚒ Use / Attack makes the Drill Mount mine all mineable blocks, including furniture, objects, trees, Lihzahrd Bricks, Altars (during Hardmode), and Shadow Orbs / Crimson Hearts, among others. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate makes the Drill Mount mine background walls. Holding ⚷ Open / Activate and ⚒ Use / Attack simultaneously will mine both blocks and walls.

Crafting the Drill Containment Unit requires a total of 160 Luminite (thus requiring defeating the Moon Lord at least twice), 600 Chlorophyte Ore, 600 Glowing Mushrooms, 20 Ectoplasm, 120 each of Hellstone and Meteorite ores, and 40 Obsidian. This also requires four different crafting stations: a Hardmode Forge for the Chlorophyte and Spectre Bars, an Autohammer for the Shroomite Bars, an Ancient Manipulator for the Luminite Bars, and a Hardmode Anvil for the Drill Containment Unit itself.
Drippler: The Drippler is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy that spawns during a Blood Moon. It hovers above the ground and floats slowly towards the player, but can be easily knocked back with most weapons.
Drippler Crippler: The Drippler Crippler is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Blood Eels. When thrown, it fires a thorny ball from the flail's head, which deals 50% of the weapon's damage (55 base damage). Thorny balls are affected by gravity, can bounce off blocks twice, and pierce two enemies; dissipating upon hitting a block or enemy a third time, or when it stops rolling.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Druidic Serpent Cloak: The Druidic Serpent Cloak is a Hardmode accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:

Attacking with a whip 3 times in a row or after a 2 seconds delay causes the player to automatically perform an extra whip swing, dealing 30% of the whip's damage (minimum of 3 damage) and 25% of its knockback. If the player has more than one tag effect slot, the extra whip swing will be instead performed by the next whip in the player's inventory, or the same whip they are currently using if they have no other whips.

Causes three stars to fall around the player upon taking damage, with each star dealing 75 / 150 / 225 damage, having 25 armor penetration, and piercing once. The stars pass through blocks until they reach the player's altitude, at which point they dissipate upon impact with blocks.
Drum Set: The Drum Set is a novelty furniture item used in conjunction with the Drumstick to produce drum sounds. The Drum Set and Drumstick can be purchased from the Merchant for 10 Gold and 50 Silver respectively after either the Eater of Worlds, the Brain of Cthulhu, Skeletron, or the Wall of Flesh has been defeated.

To play drum sounds, the player holding the Drumstick must be standing directly over the Drum Set and press ⚒ Use / Attack. The particular drum sound played is determined by the distance from the character to the cursor. From closest to farthest, by distance from the player (approximate percentage of the screen away from the character):
Dryad: The Dryad is an NPC vendor who sells various nature-themed items, including seeds, powders, and Planter Boxes. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
The Eye of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds, Brain of Cthulhu, or Skeletron has been defeated.

In addition to selling items, the Dryad can also report the percentages of Corruption/Crimson and Hallow that exist in the current world, which is based on the total number of blocks of each corresponding biome.

The Dryad will defend herself against nearby enemies by casting the Dryad's Ward, which summons two rotating circles of leaves around her, with the outer circle indicating the range of the attack. The attack lasts 10 seconds in total, however, if the Dryad takes damage when casting, the attack immediately ends. Counting from when the circles of leaves are summoned (and assuming the Dryad is uninterrupted), within the first 1.67 seconds, the radius of the Dryad's Ward is 18.75 tiles (300 pixels). The radius then generally increases to 37.5 tiles (600 pixels) over the course of 3.33 seconds, remains unchanged for another 3.33 seconds, after which the radius generally increases to 75 tiles (1200 pixels) over the course of 1.17 seconds before finally dissipating. 0.5 seconds after the circles of leaves are summoned, the Dryad's Blessing buff is granted to players and other town NPCs within its radius, while Dryad's Bane is inflicted on enemies with a clear line of sight inside its radius. Dryad's Blessing provides defense, health regeneration, and a thorns effect (similar to the Thorns Potion), while Dryad's Bane deals damage over time. See Dryad's Blessing page for details about the buff and debuff.
Dryad set: The Dryad set is a vanity set which is purchased from the Dryad for 6 Gold (set), during Halloween. It resembles the clothing that the Dryad wears regularly. It consists of the Dryad Coverings and Dryad Loincloth.
Dual Hook: The Dual Hook is a Hardmode grappling hook that reaches 27.5 tiles and has two hooks which can be launched simultaneously; however, only one hook can be attached to a block at any time. Launching a second hook will not release the player from the first hook unless the new hook successfully attaches to a block. The Dual Hook has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by Mimics.
Duck: The Duck and Mallard Duck are critters. They can usually only spawn in the middle third of the above-ground world, or in areas near an NPC's house if water is present. They only appear in pools of water, regardless of their size or if they are naturally generated. They quite frequently make a "quack" sound when nearby. Ducks may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.

Ducks will passively wander the surface until they fall a certain distance or are submerged, at which point they will switch to their alternate flying form, where they will fly in a given direction for a certain amount of time before landing and switching back to their passive form. Despite their spawn conditions, they do not prioritize water whenever landing.
Ducks have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Ducks can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Duck / Mallard Duck Cage). Once crafted, the Ducks cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Ducks can be spawned by the Duck Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Ducks: The Duck and Mallard Duck are critters. They can usually only spawn in the middle third of the above-ground world, or in areas near an NPC's house if water is present. They only appear in pools of water, regardless of their size or if they are naturally generated. They quite frequently make a "quack" sound when nearby. Ducks may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.

Ducks will passively wander the surface until they fall a certain distance or are submerged, at which point they will switch to their alternate flying form, where they will fly in a given direction for a certain amount of time before landing and switching back to their passive form. Despite their spawn conditions, they do not prioritize water whenever landing.
Ducks have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Ducks can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Duck / Mallard Duck Cage). Once crafted, the Ducks cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Ducks can be spawned by the Duck Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Duke Fishron: Duke Fishron is a Hardmode boss. While he can be summoned as soon as Hardmode is initiated, his difficulty is on par with that of a post-Golem boss, making him a serious threat to unprepared players. Fighting Duke Fishron is not required for game progression, but his defeat rewards the player with powerful weapons and equipment.
While Duke Fishron is alive, his exclusive music Duke Fishron will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Dune Splicer: The Dune Splicer is a worm-type Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Underground Desert, or much more commonly on the surface of the Desert during a Sandstorm. It is the Hardmode counterpart of the Tomb Crawler.
Dunerider Boots: The Dunerider Boots are an accessory that can be found in Sandstone Chests in the top 4/7ths of the Underground Desert, and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis.
They grant the following effects while equipped:
The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of sand clouds as they sprint.
Increased maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second).
While moving on Sand, Sandstone, or Hardened Sand:
+75% acceleration and deceleration (from 0.3 tiles/second² to 0.525 tiles/second² and from 0.75 tiles/second² to 1.3125 tiles/second², respectively)
Dungeon Brick Walls: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon, considered unsafe. They drop as items when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting on Desktop, Console, and Mobile. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.

There are a total of nine different variants (three variants in three colors), but each Dungeon can include only the three wall types matching that Dungeon's color. A single Dungeon will usually contain all three types in different areas; in each area, the faction flags found will correspond to the wall variant.

Cursed Dungeon Brick Walls (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are items that place unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls. They are visually identical to their counterparts and are obtained via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Dungeon Bricks: Dungeon Bricks are a type of brick from which the Dungeon is constructed. On world generation, one of three colors of Dungeon Brick is chosen to create the entirety of the Dungeon. Dungeon Brick is one of very few block types that is impervious to explosions. 100% pickaxe power (a Molten Pickaxe or better) is required to mine Dungeon Bricks in the Underground-level Dungeon, although any pickaxe can mine Dungeon Bricks at or above the Surface layer, and any Dungeon Bricks placed within the center third of the world. They can also be obtained from Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates.
Dungeon Crate: The Dungeon Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Dungeon after Skeletron has been defeated. Opening Dungeon or Stockade Crates is the only way to obtain the Golden Lock Box, and therefore any Dungeon-exclusive items normally found in Locked Gold Chests, once the Dungeon has been fully looted. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Stockade Crate.
Dungeon Guardian: The Dungeon Guardian is an extremely dangerous and resilient enemy resembling Skeletron's head. If a player enters the Dungeon in a world where Skeletron has not been defeated and travels below zero depth (the border between the surface and underground layers), one or more Dungeon Guardians will spawn and quickly fly toward the player, dealing 9,999 damage each, which will instantly kill most players if they are unprepared. Dungeon Guardians are large, very fast (traveling at around 41 mph in all directions), and travel through all blocks.

Because of the Dungeon Guardian's high defense (9,999), any player who attacks it, regardless of the weapon or other equipment (with very few exceptions), will deal only 1 damage, or 2 for critical hits. This means that the Dungeon Guardian will normally take an average of 1.04 damage. While killing a Dungeon Guardian is possible (and will award the Bone Key pet summon), it requires careful preparation. See the Tips section for setups.
The Dungeon Guardian's damage ignores dodge effects. The Dungeon Guardian's Bestiary entry will automatically fill itself out once Skeletron is defeated.
Dungeon Slime: The Dungeon Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Dungeon. It is an indigo-colored slime that contains a Golden Key inside, and always drops it when defeated. Unlike most other slimes, it does not drop Gel. It can spawn anywhere in the Dungeon, but appears less frequently than other Dungeon enemies.
Like most other slimes, the Dungeon Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Dungeon Spirit: The Dungeon Spirit is a flying Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It can only spawn when another enemy is defeated, having a 1/13 (7.69%) / 1/9 (11.11%) chance to rise from the enemy's remains. It can travel through blocks and drops Ectoplasm, which can be used to craft many Spectre-related items, as well as the Pumpkin Moon Medallion and Naughty Present.
Durendal: The Durendal is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss whip. It has a 20% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

Marks enemies with enchanted energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Durendal, the hit deals 30 extra damage and a visual bright flash appears. The mark expires after its effect is triggered once, meaning the enemy must be tagged again to reapply it, but the tag damage will still last for its usual duration.
Grants the Durendal's Blessing buff, increasing whip speed by 25% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits.
Dye Trader: The Dye Trader is an NPC vendor who sells the Dye Vat and other dye-related items. He will move in when the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

The player has a dye, dye plant, Strange Plant, or Dye Vat in their inventory, and at least four other town NPCs are in the world. Note that while the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, and town pets count towards this total, the Skeleton Merchant does not.
These requirements only apply to the initial spawning. If the Dye Trader is killed, he will automatically respawn after some time.

Once Hardmode has been reached, players may trade Strange Plants with the Dye Trader for uncraftable and unpurchasable animated dyes. These dyes are given at random in sets of 6 for each exchanged Strange Plant.

The Dye Trader will defend himself against nearby enemies with his Exotic Scimitar. He deals 11 / 16 / 19 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Dye Trader also has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping the Exotic Scimitar upon death.
Dye Trader's set: The Dye Trader's set is a vanity set consisting up of the Dye Trader's Turban (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the Dye Trader Robe. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The items are purchased from the Dye Trader NPC for 6 Gold (set) during Halloween.
Dye Vat: The Dye Vat is a crafting station used to craft dyes, paints, and colored string and Golf Balls. It is purchased from the Dye Trader for 5 Gold.
Dyes: Dyes are items that can be placed in the "dye slots" of a player's inventory to alter the colors and/or textures of equipped armor, vanity items, and accessories. The Dye Trader NPC sells two dyes (Silver Dye and Brown Dye) as well as the Dye Vat (5 Gold). The other dyes must be crafted using the Dye Vat or obtained through trading in Strange Plants to the Dye Trader. Primary crafted dyes can be further combined to craft Bright, Gradient, and Compound dyes. There are 119 different dyes in the game (118 on single-player worlds, as Team Dye is not available in single-player worlds). Some dyes will make sprites visible in complete darkness, most of which are Strange Dyes.
If the Critter Shampoo is dyed (by placing a dye in the respective accessory dye slot), the dye will be applied to all of the player's minions.
Dynamite: Dynamite is an explosive that explodes 5 seconds after being thrown. The explosion breaks nearly all blocks, background walls, and furniture within a radius of 7 tiles, except explosion-proof objects. The explosion also deals 250 damage to all enemies, critters, and players (but not NPCs) within 7.8 tiles horizontally and vertically of the Dynamite. Dynamite works in liquids. Lit Dynamite can be defused by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, canceling the explosion and safely dropping the Dynamite as an item for the player to pick it back up.
Dynamite can be found in Chests or purchased from the Demolitionist for 20 Silver each.
Dynasty Shingles: Dynasty Shingles are blocks purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Copper each, and are only sold when the Traveling Merchant is also selling Dynasty Wood. They cannot be crafted into any background walls.
Dynasty Walls: White Dynasty Wall and Blue Dynasty Wall are background walls crafted from Dynasty Wood, which is sold by the Traveling Merchant.
Dynasty Wood: Dynasty Wood is a type of wood purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Copper per block. When placed, it forms continuous structures with automatic frames.
Easter Block: Easter Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks purchased from the Dye Trader for 2 Silver each. Their main use is crafting Easter furniture and Easter Walls.
Easter Wall: Easter Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Easter Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Eater of Souls: The Eater of Souls is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy that spawns predominantly in The Corruption. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Crimera. Eaters of Souls spawn from both Ebonstone and Corrupt grass, with large groups coming from chasms. They circle the player at a distance before periodically rushing in to deal contact damage. There are three size variants, each with corresponding amounts of health, defense, and damage.
The Little Eater also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking an Ebonwood or Ebonwood Palm tree.
Eater of Worlds: The Eater of Worlds is a pre-Hardmode Corruption-themed worm boss. It is not a single target, but a string of segments with individual health. When any inner body segment is destroyed, it splits into multiple smaller worms, each with their own head and tail. Each section of the Eater of Worlds must be killed in order to defeat the entire boss. The Eater of Worlds is immune to lava, like all enemies that pass through blocks.

Fighting the Eater of Worlds is the only way to obtain Shadow Scales, and it is one of the only ways to obtain usable quantities of Demonite Ore. Individual segments drop some of these when killed, with a larger amount of them being dropped upon defeating the entire boss.
The Eater of Worlds is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Brain of Cthulhu. The Hardmode mechanical boss equivalent to the Eater of Worlds is The Destroyer.
While the Eater of Worlds is alive, its exclusive music Eater of Worlds will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Eater's Bone: The Eater's Bone is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Eater that follows the player. The Baby Eater will not teleport to the player when it is far away, unlike most other pets. The Eater's Bone has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by the Eater of Worlds.
Ebonkoi: Ebonkoi are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in The Corruption in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Wrath Potions.
Ebonstone Block: Ebonstone is a block type found in The Corruption. Before Hardmode, it is most prominent in the lining of Chasms. It requires at least 65% pickaxe power (Nightmare Pickaxe / Deathbringer Pickaxe, or better) or explosives to mine. Deathweed can grow on it.

Ebonstone is the Corruption version of Stone (similar to Crimstone in The Crimson, or Pearlstone in The Hallow). As with Crimstone, Ebonstone can be converted into ordinary Stone via Purification Powder or Green Solution used by the Clentaminator.
In Hardmode, the spread of Corruption converts ordinary Stone blocks into Ebonstone. Ebonstone itself also spreads Corruption to susceptible blocks nearby.
Ebonstone Brick: Ebonstone Brick is a type of brick. Unlike its raw block counterpart, the Ebonstone Block, it does not spread The Corruption, nor does it turn the area into a Corruption biome, thus making it a safe construction material for NPC houses and other structures. Its Crimson counterpart is Crimstone Brick.
Ebonstone Brick Wall: Ebonstone Brick Wall is a wall crafted from Ebonstone Brick. Like the brick, Ebonstone Brick Walls do not spread The Corruption.
Ebonstone Wall: The Ebonstone Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in The Corruption, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
The Clentaminator/Terraformer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (using Purple Solution) and Unholy Water convert Stone Walls to unsafe Ebonstone Walls.
Ebonstone Walls can spread The Corruption to nearby pure walls. See Biome spread for further information.
Ebonwood: Ebonwood is a type of wood harvested from Ebonwood trees and Ebonwood Palm trees found naturally growing in Corruption biomes. Ebonwood trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Corrupt grass or Corrupt Jungle grass above surface, and Ebonwood Palm trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Ebonsand Blocks above surface.
Ebonwood Bow: The Ebonwood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Shadewood Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Ebonwood Hammer: The Ebonwood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its Crimson counterpart is the Shadewood Hammer.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Ebonwood Sword: The Ebonwood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword.
Its Crimson counterpart is the Shadewood Sword.
Ebonwood Wall: Ebonwood Wall is a type of wall made from Ebonwood.
Ebonwood armor: Ebonwood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ebonwood Helmet, Ebonwood Breastplate, and Ebonwood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Ebonwood. The full set grants 5 defense while equipped.
Its Crimson counterpart is Shadewood armor, which has identical stats.
Echo Block: The Echo Block is a type of block which turns completely invisible once placed. It is sold by the Cyborg NPC for 10 Silver when he is spoken to in a Graveyard. Once placed, the Echo Block cannot be seen by the player unless they have the Spectre Goggles equipped or are near an Echo Chamber.

Despite their invisibility, Echo Blocks retain the properties of normal blocks and can thus be hammered, actuated with an Actuator, stood and grappled on, used to hoik, and mined with any pickaxe or drill.
Echo Chamber: The Echo Chamber is a furniture item. It can be activated and deactivated similarly to a monolith. When active, it grants the ability to see Echo Blocks, Echo Platforms, Echo Walls, Ghostly Stinkbug Blockers, and tiles painted with Echo Coating. It can also be equipped as a vanity accessory, which enables its effect globally for the player, similar to the Radio Thing.
Echo Wall: The Echo Wall is a type of background wall made from Echo Blocks. It appears completely invisible once placed and cannot be seen by the player unless they have the Spectre Goggles equipped or are near an Echo Chamber. Like other walls, it stops enemies from spawning when it is placed and can be used for houses.
Ectoplasm: Ectoplasm is a Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting material dropped from Dungeon Spirits in the Dungeon. Dungeon Spirits drop 1–2 Ectoplasm upon death.
Eggnog: Eggnog is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 8.101% in pre-Hardmode and 7.561% in Hardmode. When used, it restores 80 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 40 seconds. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.
Elder Slime: Town Slimes are a type of town pet. There are 8 different Town Slimes and all of them can exist at the same time (unlike the different breeds of the Town Bunny, Town Cat, and Town Dog).

Almost all types of Town Slimes are acquired via some form of transformation, similar to the Tax Collector. Afterwards, the transformed Town Slime will move into a vacant house if one is available. If it is killed, it will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house. The initial transformation does not need to be repeated.

Town Slimes can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). They may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for their home tile (standing point).
Elderberry: The Elderberry is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking an Ebonwood or an Ebonwood Palm tree.
Electric Eel: The Electric Eel is a Hardmode whip that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. It has a 5% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
Inflicts its own unique debuff for 4 seconds to enemies, causing them to take 50 damage per second (50 damage displayed every 1 second).

Marks enemies with electric energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Electric Eel, the hit deals 50 extra damage, plus an additional 50 damage for each enemy within a 28.125-tile radius of the marked target. The maximum damage increase is 300 with 5 or more enemies near the marked target. Additionally, when the electric energy is triggered, resonating lightning will jump from the marked target towards up to 5 nearby enemies within a 28.125-tile radius, dealing 20 damage to them. The electric energy expires after its effect is triggered once, meaning the enemy must be tagged again to reapply it, but the other tag effects still last for their duration.
Electrosphere Launcher: The Electrosphere Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Golem launcher that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. When used, it consumes rockets and fires blue missiles that form an Electrosphere upon impact with blocks, enemies, or reaching the cursor's position when fired. Electrospheres deal damage repeatedly and last for 5 seconds, but do not inflict any knockback. Multiple Electrospheres cannot overlap, with newly summoned ones replacing older ones.
Elf Archer: The Elf Archer is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during wave 2 of the Frost Moon event. She is very similar to the Pirate Crossbower, Goblin Archer, and Skeleton Archer, shooting Flaming Arrows which inflict the On Fire! debuff for 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds.
Defeating an Elf Archer during the Frost Moon event will add 3 / 6 / 7.5 points to the final score.
Elf Copter: The Elf Copter is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during wave 6 of the Frost Moon event. It travels through blocks, firing bullets rapidly at players within its line of sight.
Defeating an Elf Copter during the Frost Moon event will add 8 / 16 / 20 points to the final score.
Elf Melter: The Elf Melter is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged weapon that uses Gel for ammunition. It is an indirect upgrade to the Flamethrower. When used, it consumes one Gel and releases five bursts of fire in quick succession. The fire expands as it travels, creating a cone-like area of effect, before dissipating shortly after. The fire has 15 armor penetration, inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 20 seconds, and can pierce through three enemies. The fire's damage decreases by 15% per enemy pierced.
The Elf Melter is dropped by Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event with a 6.25%–16.67% / 12.5%–50% chance depending on the current wave.

Its best modifier is Unreal. A modifier granting +10% speed will increase the number of flame streams per use from five to six while still consuming 1 Gel. A modifier with added velocity will increase the range of each stream, i.e. by about 5 tiles for +15% and about 3 tiles for +10%.
Elf set: The Elf set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Elf Hat, the Elf Shirt, and the Elf Pants. Each piece has a 1/600 (0.17%) chance of being dropped by a Zombie Elf.
Emerald: Emerald is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It can craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and has no exclusive recipes. It can be obtained in the following ways:
Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable green gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form.
Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator.
Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance.
Rarely, Emerald can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well.
Like all other gems, Emerald can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.
Emerald Bunny: Gem Bunnies are harmless critters that can only spawn in the Cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Bunnies, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa.
Gem Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Bunny Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Emerald Robe: The Emerald Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. The Emerald Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to stick to blocks, as well as increasing their pierce by 1. It also causes projectiles to be shot out much faster and then decelerate over time, eventually lingering in mid-air if they have not hit any blocks. The Emerald Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4.

Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Emerald Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.
Emerald Squirrel: Gem Squirrels are harmless critters that can only spawn in the cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Squirrels, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa. Gem Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Gem Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Squirrel Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Emerald Staff: The Emerald Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires a high-velocity green bolt which gradually slows down and then lingers in place. The green bolt can pierce once, and can stick to blocks and deal damage to enemies that walk into it. While moving, the green bolt also has a damaging trail that follows it, extending its hitbox. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details).
Empress of Light: The Empress of Light is a Hardmode, post-Plantera boss. She is generally fought at night, and becomes "enraged" with greatly increased damage during the day. Fighting the Empress of Light is not required for game progression, but her defeat rewards the player with powerful weapons and equipment.

While she can be summoned as soon as Plantera is defeated, her difficulty is on par with that of a post-Golem boss, making her a serious threat to unprepared players. Taking her on early poses a significant challenge that typically requires practicing to dodge her telegraphed attacks.
While the Empress of Light is alive, her exclusive music Empress of Light will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Empty Bullet: Empty Bullets are a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Arms Dealer for 5 Copper (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) / 3 Copper (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) each. While they have no function as ammunition on their own, Empty Bullets are used to craft Hardmode bullets with special effects.
Empty Dropper: The Empty Dropper is a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Wizard for 1 Silver. It is used in the crafting of Magic Droppers. The Crystal Ball must be near water, lava, or honey, to craft the respective liquid's dropper.
Enchanted Boomerang: The Enchanted Boomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang. It is a direct upgrade to the Wooden Boomerang.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Enchanted Moondial: The Enchanted Moondial is a Hardmode furniture item. It can be triggered by the ⚷ Open / Activate key or wires, doing so will advance time to dusk (7:30 PM) on the current or following day (depending on whether it is activated during day or night). It has a 7-day cooldown period, so once used, it will not be usable again until 7 in-game days have passed (see Notes for details). When the Enchanted Moondial is ready to be used, the dial at the top of its sprite and the moon in the middle will both glow bright blue, and the shape of the glowing moon in the middle corresponds to the current moon phase. The Enchanted Moondial is obtained by throwing an Enchanted Sundial into Shimmer.

The Enchanted Moondial does not turn the time to dusk immediately. It instead "fast-forwards" time, causing it to pass 60 times faster than usual (1 hour of in-game time, which would usually take 1 minute of real-life time, takes only 1 second while the Enchanted Moondial is active). When the Enchanted Moondial is taking effect, the effect of other time-accelerating methods (beds and the Journey Mode Time Menu) will be ignored. However, unlike these methods, the Enchanted Moondial does not increase the tile update rate in the world, meaning that things like plant growth and biome spread are unaffected when it is active.
Enchanted Nightcrawler: The Enchanted Nightcrawler is a critter that appears as a glowing pink and sparkly Worm. Enchanted Nightcrawlers can spawn naturally during a Starfall when few clouds are in the sky (such as during a Lantern Night), can be obtained by crafting, and also have a 3/10 (30%) chance of being obtained from a Can Of Worms. The Enchanted Nightcrawler has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Enchanted Nightcrawler can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Enchanted Nightcrawler Cage). Once crafted, the Enchanted Nightcrawler cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Enchanted Nightcrawler can be used as bait for fishing, with 35% bait power.
Enchanted Pixie Dust: The Enchanted Pixie Dust is a Hardmode transformation mount item that turns the player into a Pixie. While in this form, the player will emit a dim light in a 15-block radius and gain infinite flight. Additionally, the player will be able to fit through 1-tile gaps and their hurt sound is replaced with a twinkling sound. If the player has any dashes equipped, they can also perform a dash by pressing Dash, or by double-tapping ◀ Left or ▶ Right while the "Double Tap Dashing" setting is enabled. The player loses their ability to use other items, and doing so will result in the player dismounting and returning to normal. It is dropped by Pixies with a 1/200 (0.5%) chance after defeating any mechanical boss.
Enchanted Sundial: The Enchanted Sundial is a Hardmode furniture item. It can be triggered by the ⚷ Open / Activate key or wires, doing so will advance time to sunrise (4:30 AM) the following day. It has a 7-day cooldown period, so once used, it will not be usable again until 7 in-game days have passed (see Notes for details). When the Enchanted Sundial is ready to be used, the dial at the top of its sprite and the sun in the middle will both glow bright yellow.
The Enchanted Sundial is obtained from fished Pearlwood Crates (1/200 (0.5%) chance), Mythril Crates (1/60 (1.67%) chance), and Titanium Crates (1/20 (5%) chance).

The Enchanted Sundial does not turn the time to the next day immediately. It instead "fast-forwards" time, causing it to pass 60 times faster than usual (1 hour of in-game time, which would usually take 1 minute of real-life time, takes only 1 second while the Enchanted Sundial is active). When the Enchanted Sundial is taking effect, the effect of other time-accelerating methods (bed and Journey Mode Time Menu) will be ignored. However, unlike these methods, the Enchanted Sundial does not increase tile update rate in world, meaning that things like plant growth and biome spread is unaffected when it is active.
The Enchanted Moondial is its night counterpart, allowing the player to advance time to dusk (7:30 PM) of the current or following day.
Enchanted Sword: The Enchanted Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it occasionally fires an Enchanted Beam projectile that cannot pierce enemies or pass through blocks. Both the sword and its projectile produce lingering particles that emit large amounts of light.

The Enchanted Sword can be obtained by destroying an "enchanted sword in stone" background object, which can be found in random locations underground and in Enchanted Sword Shrines. Destroying this background object has a 29/30 (96.67%) chance to drop an Enchanted Sword, with the other 1/30 (3.33%) times instead dropping a Terragrim. The Enchanted Sword also has a 1/30 (3.33%) and 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be found in Golden and Titanium Crates respectively.
Enchanted Sword (NPC): The Enchanted Sword is a Hardmode enemy which spawns in the Underground Hallow. It hovers and spins before lunging at the player, traveling through any blocks to reach them. Any damage dealt to it stops its attack, forcing it to pause and spin again. It has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Cursed debuff upon contact.
Enchanted Timer: The Enchanted Timer is an unobtainable accessory that periodically guarantees critical hits.

While equipped, it is automatically charged up over the course of 1.85 seconds, provided the player is standing still and is not using any items. The charge rate is halved while moving or while using an item, and doing both at once reduces the charge rate to 1/3 (33.33%). Once fully charged, the player's next attack opens a 0.25-second window during which all of their attacks are guaranteed to critically strike. Afterwards, the Enchanted Timer is reset and begins charging up anew.
Encumbering Stone: The Encumbering Stone is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents item pickup while inside the player's inventory. While in the inventory, the Encumbering Stone will prevent the pickup of any items, even if the player already has a stackable item in their inventory. The Encumbering Stone will also prevent items from being added to the Void Bag.
Items reeled in from fishing are still placed in the player's inventory. Hearts and Stars will also be picked up even with the Encumbering Stone in the inventory.

Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Encumbering Stone in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Encumbering Stone and Uncumbering Stone. Toggling it to the Uncumbering Stone disables its functions, allowing the player to pick up items again.
The Encumbering Stone has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being found in Sandstone Chests in the Underground Desert.
Endless Musket Pouch: The Endless Musket Pouch is a Hardmode ammunition item. While in the inventory, it acts as an infinite source of Musket Balls.
Endless Quiver: The Endless Quiver is a Hardmode ammunition item. While in the user's inventory, it acts as a Wooden Arrow that cannot be depleted. It is also compatible with bows that convert Wooden Arrows into a special type (e.g. The Bee's Knees).
Endurance Potion: The Endurance Potion is a buff potion that grants the Endurance buff when consumed, which provides +10% damage reduction. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Engineering Helmet: The Engineering Helmet is a vanity item equipped on the Social Helmet Slot. It is purchased from the Mechanic for 1 Gold.
Escargot: Escargot is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Eternia Crystal: The Eternia Crystal is an event-summoning item. When used on the Eternia Crystal Stand while under the correct terrain requirements, the Old One's Army event begins. The Eternia Crystal can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for 25 Silver (pre-mechanical bosses), 1 Gold (post-one mechanical boss), or 4 Gold (post-Golem).
Eternia Crystal Stand: The Eternia Crystal Stand is a furniture item that initiates the Old One's Army event when an Eternia Crystal is placed on it with ⚷ Open / Activate. The Eternia Crystal Stand can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for 1 Gold.
Etherian Goblin: The Etherian Goblin is an enemy that spawns during the Old One's Army event. It is by far the event's most common enemy, spawning during every wave regardless of the current tier.

The Etherian Goblin attacks by slowly approaching its target, hacking away with its weapon when it is close to the player or the Eternia Crystal, similar to Armed Zombies in Expert Mode. Like many other enemies from the event, its appearance and stats change depending on what point in the game the player has reached. Like most other ground-based enemies of the Old One's Army, if an Etherian Goblin's target is too far away or obstructed, it will enter an ethereal state, allowing it to pass through tiles. It is also unaffected by Teleporters or Lava.
The Etherian Goblin requires 1,000 kills to be awarded completion of its corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Etherian Goblin Bomber: The Etherian Goblin Bomber is an enemy that spawns during the Old One's Army event. It spawns during Tier 1 during waves 2–5, Tier 2 during waves 3 and 5–7, and Tier 3 during waves 1–2 and 5–7.

As its name implies, it attacks by hurling bouncy Goblin Bomb projectiles at its target, similar to Clowns. While they might not pose the biggest threat to players with decent equipment, they can easily gain the upper hand against an early-game defender, especially if the Tavernkeep was discovered directly after defeating the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu. Like many other enemies from the event, its appearance and stats change, depending on what point in the game the player has reached.
The Etherian Goblin Bomber requires 500 kills to be awarded completion of its corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Etherian Javelin: The Etherian Javelin is an unobtainable item resembling the weapons used by Etherian Javelin Throwers. It only exists as an ID and an image in the game's files. Attempting to use third-party tools to obtain it will result in it instantly disappearing.
Etherian Javelin Thrower: The Etherian Javelin Thrower is an enemy that spawns during the Old One's Army event. It spawns during Tier 1 during waves 3–5, Tier 2 during waves 1–4 and 6–7, and Tier 3 during waves 1–4 and 6.
As its name implies, the Etherian Javelin Thrower attacks by throwing javelins approximately every two seconds if it is within 37 tiles of the player or the Eternia Crystal.
The Etherian Javelin Thrower requires 200 kills to be awarded completion of its corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Etherian Lightning Bug: The Etherian Lightning Bug is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that spawns during Old One's Army event. It spawns during Tier 3 in waves 2 and 6.

Upon gaining line of sight with the player, an Etherian Lightning Bug flies towards them and attempts to position itself slightly beyond the melee reach of the player (or a distance less than 10 tiles away from the player). Afterward, it fires short-ranged Withering Bolts approximately once every half second which deal high damage and inflict the Withered Weapon debuff, which halves player-inflicted damage for 5 seconds.
It is one of only two enemies from the Old One's Army that requires the usual 50 kills to obtain its corresponding banner, the other being the Wither Beast.
Etherian Mana: Etherian Mana is used to summon Tavernkeep's sentries during the Old One's Army event, and is dropped by all of the event's enemies. Each wave has a designated amount of mana to be dropped over its course (see wave chart), and it will be dropped in stacks of 1 by the respective number of enemies during the wave. When collected in the player's inventory, the amount of Etherian Mana they have will appear in the bottom right corner of any Tavernkeep's sentry summon weapons in the hotbar, similar to the way ammo is displayed for ranged weapons.

Activating the Eternia Crystal gives the player a starting amount of 10 Etherian Mana, and each wave will produce between exactly 20, 30, or 40 Etherian Mana. Each Tavernkeep's sentry costs 10 Etherian Mana to summon, so conserving Etherian Mana and developing a strategy is key to the event.
Once the Old One's Army event ends, all Etherian Mana dropped in the world and inside the player's inventory will despawn.
Etherian Wyvern: The Etherian Wyvern is a flying enemy that spawns during the Old One's Army event. It spawns during Tier 1 during waves 4–5, Tier 2 during waves 3–7, and Tier 3 during waves 3–4.

The Etherian Wyvern passes through all solid blocks and flies fairly high above the player or the Eternia Crystal before diving towards its closest target. This causes it to dip below the surface of blocks, making it somewhat difficult to hit without weapons that can attack through blocks. The Etherian Wyvern can attack approximately once every 1.5 seconds, and periodically lets out a screech as it is diving at a target. Additionally, Betsy can also summon a maximum of nine Tier 3 Etherian Wyverns during her roar attack.
The Etherian Wyvern requires 200 kills to be awarded completion of its corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Eucalyptus Sap: The Eucalyptus Sap is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Sugar Glider that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Sugar Glider flies while extending its gliding membranes to catch up to them. The Eucalyptus Sap has a small chance of dropping when the player shakes a Forest tree.
Eventide: The Eventide is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bow that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light. When used, it fires a burst of four arrows and one Twilight Lance projectile, with the Twilight Lance dealing 200% of the weapon's damage (110 base damage when using Wooden Arrows). It can also convert Wooden Arrows into Twilight Lances, which only deal 100% of the weapon's damage. The Twilight Lances are unaffected by gravity and can pierce four time, dissipating on the fifth hit.
Everscream: The Everscream is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Frost Moon event. It is the Frost Moon equivalent of the Mourning Wood, which behaves in an almost identical way to the Everscream.
Defeating the Everscream during the Frost Moon event will add 50 / 100 / 125 points to the final score.
Evolution Beast: The Evolution Beast is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Nebula Pillar during the Lunar Events. It attacks by shooting a slow, homing Nebula Sphere and attempting to ram the player.
Excalibur: The Excalibur is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss broadsword. When swung, a large yellow aura follows the swing, reaching about twice the distance of the sword itself. The aura can hit up to three enemies.
Exotic Chew Toy: The Exotic Chew Toy is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Fennec Fox that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Fennec Fox pet will fly by flapping its ears like wings to catch up to them. The Exotic Chew Toy can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum.
Exotic Scimitar: The Exotic Scimitar is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped from the Dye Trader. Striking enemies with the weapon increases its damage by 12% per hit, up to a maximum of 50%. This damage bonus decays at a rate of 0.5% per tick or 30% per second.
Exploding Bullet: The Exploding Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It explodes on impact with enemies or blocks, dealing damage and knockback to a single other enemy within an area.

Exploding Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Exploding Bullets is 14 Silver 50 Copper, which is 29 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Exploding Bullets is 29 Gold.
Explosive Bunny: The Explosive Bunny is a critter that explodes upon death. Crafting it requires a Bunny, which must be caught with any Bug Net. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Explosive Bunnies can be released as a critter, though it will always be placed at the player's feet instead of at the cursor like with most other critters. Projectiles launched by the Bunny Cannon will also release an Explosive Bunny at the projectiles position after a short period, though they cannot be caught and their explosion deals no damage to enemies or the player.
The Explosive Bunny's explosion deals 350 / 700 / 1050 damage to the player (175 damage to friendly NPCs, critters, and enemies) within a 8×8-tile area centered on it, but does not destroy tiles.
Explosive Powder: Explosive Powder is a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Demolitionist for 12 Silver each, once the Wall of Flesh has been defeated. It is solely used to make Exploding Bullets, an ammo type with strong knockback.
Explosive Trap sentry summons: The Explosive Trap Rod, Cane, and Staff are special sentry summon weapons that summon their respective sentries. Each Explosive Trap sentry causes an explosion when enemies are nearby. Explosive Traps do not disappear when exploding, and will remain until its duration has expired or when the Old One's Army event ends. The higher the tier, the more damage the Explosive Traps deal.
The Rod is sold by the Tavernkeep for 5 Defender Medals. The Cane is sold for 15 Defender Medals after defeating one mechanical boss. The Staff is sold for 60 Defender Medals after defeating Golem.

During the Old One's Army event, Etherian Mana can be collected, which allows the placement of multiple Explosive Traps that remain permanently until the event is over. Etherian Mana cannot be used outside the event. These weapons cannot be used outside of the Old One's Army event until the event has been successfully completed.

Explosive Trap sentries are boosted by the Huntress armor and Red Riding armor set bonuses, which increase their fire rates and cause them to inflict the Oiled debuff on struck enemies for 4–8.5 seconds.

Their best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 95% (including whip bonuses) or 20.5% (excluding whip bonuses), the Explosive Trap Staff's best modifier becomes Ruthless.
Explosives: Explosives are a placeable, consumable mechanism that can be triggered using wiring. Pressing ▲ Up and ▼ Down keys when placing Explosives rotates the placed visual.

Triggering Explosives cause a large explosion. The explosion destroys most placed blocks and items (except for explosion-proof items) within a radius of 10 tiles, and deals damage within a 16.25×16.25-tile area. The explosion deals 500 damage and inflicts a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) to all entities.

Explosives can spawn naturally as traps wired to Pressure Plates, or wired to Detonators (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) next to a vein of ores can be found in the Underground and Cavern layer.
Extendo Grip: The Extendo Grip is a construction accessory that is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. While equipped, it increases placement range and tool range by 2 tiles vertically and 3 tiles horizontally.
Extractinator: The Extractinator (or Silt Extractinator) is a special crafting station that converts Silt, Slush, and Desert Fossils into various resources such as ores, coins, and gems. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can also convert Glowing Mosses into any other regular moss, fishing trash into low level bait, and other miscellaneous materials.

After being placed, suitable blocks must be consumed using the ⚷ Open / Activate key directly on the Extractinator, and the converted items will be dropped. Extractable blocks are selected automatically from the player's inventory while Auto Select is activated.
When an Extractinator receives a Wire signal, it will attempt to process an extractable block from a Chest placed directly next to the Extractinator. It can perform this up to once per second.

It can be obtained from multiple sources, with a 4.9% chance of spawning in Frozen Chests, a 5% to 6.67% chance of spawning in Gold Chests in the Underground and Cavern layers, and a 1.86% chance of being dropped by opening Wooden Crates. Underground Cabins in the Underground Desert (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) also have a chance to contain an Extractinator as part of the random decor.
Feeding blocks to the Extractinator is the only way to obtain Amber Mosquitoes, and, along with opening crates, the only reliable way to obtain a world's alternative pre-Hardmode ores.
Eye Bone: The Eye Bone is a pet-summoning item that spawns Chester, a mobile Piggy Bank, to follow the player. Chester, being a pet, is essentially an upgrade to the Money Trough as it follows the player and does not require repeated summons. The Eye Bone has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops.
Eye Patch: The Eye Patch is a Hardmode vanity item. It has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Pirate Deckhands, Pirate Corsairs, Pirate Deadeyes, and Pirate Crossbowers during the Pirate Invasion event.
Eye Spring: The Eye Spring is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns an Eyeball Spring that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Eyeball Spring spins its tentacles to catch up to the player. The Eye Spring has a 1/15 (6.67%) / 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Eyezors.
Eye of Cthulhu: The Eye of Cthulhu is a pre-Hardmode boss. It is typically one of the first bosses a player may encounter, as it spawns automatically when a relatively early level of game advancement is achieved. It can also be summoned manually with the Suspicious Looking Eye at night (see Summoning and spawning below).
While the Eye of Cthulhu is alive, its exclusive music Boss 1 will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Eye of the Golem: The Eye of the Golem is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that grants +10% critical strike chance. It has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem.
Eyebrella: The Eyebrella is a vanity item that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. When equipped, it summons a raincloud that constantly produces raindrops above the player's head. This effect is purely visual; it does not deal any damage.
Eyezor: The Eyezor is an uncommon Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event, and primarily attacks by advancing toward the player while firing high-velocity purple laser beams at them. It also travels faster than normal Zombies and is highly resistant to knockback. As the Eyezor takes damage, its movement speed and the rate at which it fires lasers will increase.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
FPV Goggles: The FPV Goggles are a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory purchased from the Cyborg for 10 Gold. It centers the screen on the Kwad Racer Drone or Wall Racer Car while one is active, allowing the player to fly the drone or drive the car without having to keep it within the screen, or to use it to scout out areas that are difficult to reach.
Face Monster: The Face Monster is a pre-Hardmode enemy that can be found in The Crimson. It follows the Fighter AI, being able to open doors at any time. Like other Crimson enemies, it drops Vertebra fairly often.
Faecorn: The Faecorn is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Cenaxe pet, which passively harvests items from trees. The Faecorn has a small chance of dropping when the player shakes a Forest tree.
