The Cenaxe pet appears to swing an axe, but it does not destroy tree tiles. It passively generates:
Acorns and the appropriate wood from most trees
Cenaxe needs to hit a tree tile with leaves (a branch with leaves, or the top tile of a tree) to be able to drop Acorns.
Gems, Stone Blocks and Gemcorns from gem trees
Cenaxe needs to hit a gem tree tile with leaves to be able to drop Gemcorns.
Glowing Mushrooms from Giant Glowing Mushrooms
Faeling: The Faeling is a flying critter that emits light, which naturally spawns in the Aether. Most critters that come into contact with Shimmer will also transform into Faelings. Faelings can pass through blocks and try to fly away from the player if they get too close.
The Faeling has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Faeling can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Faeling in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Faeling cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Fairies: The Pink Fairy, Green Fairy, and Blue Fairy are critters that emit light, which will attempt to lead the player to valuable treasures, such as Life Crystals, Chests, or ore deposits. They spawn in the bottom half of the Underground layer and in the Cavern layer, but only if at least one Fallen Log is present in the world on the surface (see Fallen Log § Notes for the exact area). If all Fallen Logs have been destroyed, they will no longer spawn independently. The three fairy variants all function identically.

Fairies can also spawn at Fallen Logs and from shaken Pearlwood trees on the surface at night. In this case, they will not lead players to treasure; instead, when approached, they try to flee much like Birds or Faelings. Unlike fairies spawned underground, these fairies can be caught with a Bug Net and carried around in the inventory. If released again, they act like the ones spawned underground and will attempt to lead the player to treasure. They can also be crafted into animated decorative furniture (Fairy jars). Once crafted, the fairies cannot be released again unless de-crafted via Shimmer.
They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Fairy Bell: The Fairy Bell is a Hardmode light pet-summoning item that spawns a Fairy, a glowing creature resembling a Pixie, which follows the player and produces light for an unlimited duration. The summoned Fairy will be either pink, green, or blue, the color of which changes randomly each time the Fairy is summoned. The Fairy is faster and brighter than the Shadow Orb and Crimson Heart, but not as fast or bright as the Wisp in a Bottle.
Fairy Boots: Fairy Boots are an accessory that are made from the Spectre Boots and Flower Boots at a Tinkerer's Workshop. They combine both effects into one pair of boots.
Fairy Glowstick: The Fairy Glowstick is a consumable light source sold by the Zoologist for 75 Copper when all three fairies have been recorded in the Bestiary. The Fairy Glowstick functions like a regular Glowstick when thrown. However, upon colliding with solid blocks, it will hover to a maximum of approximately 7 tiles above where it had landed.
The Fairy Glowstick provides more illumination compared to a regular Glowstick while in liquids.
Fairy jars: Fairy jars are animated decorative furniture items, crafted using a Bottle and their respective fairy. By throwing a fairy jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the fairy as an item.

Fairy jars can be placed on top of solid blocks and platforms, and give off a faint light. They function as light sources (but will not function as a valid one for housing) and illuminate underwater, but are not controllable mechanisms like some other light sources.
Fake Unicorn Horn: The Fake Unicorn Horn is a vanity accessory purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.
Falcon Blade: The Falcon Blade is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 38/625 (6.08%) chance of being obtained from Iron Crates and a 299/5000 (5.98%) chance from Mythril Crates. Striking enemies with the weapon increases its damage by 12% per hit, up to a maximum of 50%. This damage bonus decays at a rate of 0.5% per tick or 30% per second.
Fallen Star: The Fallen Star is an item that randomly falls from the sky at night and disappears at dawn (4:30 AM). They can be used to craft Mana Crystals, which permanently increase a player's mana capacity by 20 points each. They are used in a variety of crafting recipes and as ammunition for the Star Cannon and Super Star Shooter. Fallen Stars can be stored in ammo slots.
Fallen Stars will spawn randomly throughout nighttime and their spawn rate is determined by two factors: the world size and a multiplier randomly set at nightfall (see Notes for details).

Fallen Stars emit light, making them easy to spot at night. They cannot be placed by the player as permanent light sources, but can be combined with a Bottle to craft the Star in a Bottle. They disappear at dawn if outside of the player's inventory or a storage item, even if dropped by the player.

If a Fallen Star strikes an enemy or critter while falling, it will deal 1,000 base damage to the struck entity. Fallen Stars cannot damage players or NPCs unless playing in a world with the Remix special world seed enabled. On these worlds, Fallen Stars that fall from the sky do not drop as an item on impact, and can only be obtained from pots or slimes as their bonus drop. Fallen Stars will deal 2,000 / 4,000 / 6,000 to players on these worlds.
Fallen Star Block: Fallen Star Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks crafted from Fallen Stars and Stone Blocks. Their main use is crafting Fallen Star furniture and Fallen Star Walls.
Fallen Star Wall: Fallen Star Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Fallen Star Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Fallen Tuxedo set: The Fallen Tuxedo set is a set of vanity items consisting of the Fallen Tuxedo Shirt and the Fallen Tuxedo Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
They are purchased from the Clothier for 50 Gold (set), during a Blood Moon.
Familiar set: The Familiar set is a vanity set that displays the player's default clothes. It consists of the Familiar Wig, the Familiar Shirt, and the Familiar Pants, and can be purchased from the Clothier for 3 Gold (set).

When a piece of the Familiar set is equipped in the vanity armor slot, it will disable the graphics of any item worn in the corresponding armor slot. As such, the Familiar Wig will show the character's hairstyle whereas the Familiar Shirt and Familiar Pants will show the character's default shirt and pants, respectively.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Fancy Dishes: The Fancy Dishes are a furniture item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 20 Silver.
Fart in a Balloon: The Fart in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the effects of the Fart in a Jar and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to ~10.5 tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 18.5 tiles, for a total of 29 tiles.

Unlike most other double-jump balloons, the Fart in a Balloon's full jump is high enough for the player to take minor fall damage, unless the player has fall damage immunity accessories like the Lucky Horseshoe.
Fart in a Jar: The Fart in a Jar is an accessory that allows the player to perform a double jump, accompanied by a farting sound effect. The Fart jump goes 10.5 tiles into the air, totalling 16.5 tiles when put together with the first jump.
Fast Clock: The Fast Clock is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Slow debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Pixies, regular Mummies, and Wraiths.
Feather: The Feather is a common crafting material dropped frequently by Harpies. It is used in crafting the Featherfall and Gravitation Potions and once again becomes important in Hardmode for crafting the first tier of wings – Angel and Demon Wings.
Featherfall Potion: The Featherfall Potion is a buff potion which grants the Featherfall buff when consumed. The buff negates fall damage, and reduces the player's fall speed and gravity to 1/3 (33.33%) of normal, allowing them to jump higher and fall slower. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

While the buff is active, the player can also control their falling speed more precisely depending on the Hover Controls option in gameplay settings. The three available speeds are normal gravity, the default of 1/3rd normal gravity, and 10% of normal gravity. With the default hold control scheme, the player will experience normal gravity while the ▼ Down key is held, 10% gravity while the ▲ Up key is held, and 1/3rd gravity otherwise. With the click control scheme, their gravity will be set to 1/3rd upon touching and leaving the ground, and can be increased by one stage by pressing ▼ Down or decreased by one stage by pressing ▲ Up.

The Featherfall buff also works with mounts and minecarts (except for the Bee Mount), and works during reversed gravity. Fall damage will be negated even if the player is falling at normal speed or is under the effects of the Stoned debuff.
In addition to being crafted, Featherfall Potions can be found in pots and chests.
Fedora: The Fedora is a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.
Fences: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.
Feral Claws: Feral Claws are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be found in Jungle Crates, Bramble Crates, and Ivy Chests located in Jungle Shrines and at the base of a Living Mahogany Tree in the Underground Jungle. While equipped, it grants the following effects:
Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips
Fertilizer: The Fertilizer is a consumable item which immediately grows a sapling or gemcorn into the corresponding tree.

Each use causes the player character to throw out Fertilizer in a small area in front of them. If a sapling meeting the required growing conditions is present in the area of effect, it will immediately sprout into a tree of the corresponding biome, but saplings that do not meet the conditions will not sprout into trees. The Fertilizer allows saplings to grow in front of any background walls and removes the restrictions related to them, but the other growing conditions still remain. The Fertilizer will be consumed on use regardless of whether saplings grow or not.
Fetid Baghnakhs: The Fetid Baghnakhs are a Hardmode broadsword that have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics. They have a very short range, but an exceptionally high attack speed.
Feywood: Feywood is a type of wood used to craft the Feywood furniture set.
Feywood Wall: Feywood Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Feywood Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Fez: The Fez is a head piece vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 Gold 50 Silver.
Finch Staff: The Finch Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Baby Finch minion. It flies towards enemies to deal contact damage. The Finch Staff has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being found in Living Wood Chests within Living Trees. Newly created Journey Mode characters spawn with a Finch Staff.
Fire Feather: The Fire Feather is a Hardmode crafting material used solely to craft the Flame Wings. It has a (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1/50 (2%) / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 1/75 (1.33%) chance of being dropped by Red Devils in The Underworld after defeating any mechanical boss.
Fire Gauntlet: The Fire Gauntlet is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses accessory. While equipped, it grants the following effects:
Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips
Causes melee weapons to inflict the Hellfire debuff on hit
Fire Imp: The Fire Imp is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Underworld. It fires Burning Spheres, which travel through blocks and have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds. The Burning Spheres can easily be destroyed by hitting them with any weapon, minion, or damage-dealing tool or pet.
Like all casters, the Fire Imp will follow the pattern of firing three times, pausing for several seconds, and teleporting to another location on the screen.
Fireblossom: Fireblossom is a type of herb which appears as a small, magma-colored flower. It grows naturally on Ash Blocks and Ash grass. Fireblossom can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Fireblossom Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles.

Fireblossom blooms at sunset, from 3:45 PM to 7:30 PM, unless it is raining. Its blooming is indicated by the fiery flower and fire particles emitted. Harvesting mature Fireblossom yields 1 Fireblossom item. Harvesting blooming Fireblossom yields 1 Fireblossom item and 1–3 Fireblossom Seeds. Harvesting blooming Fireblossom with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Fireblossoms and 1–5 Fireblossom Seeds instead.
Both Fireblossom and Fireblossom Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.
Fireblossom Seeds: Fireblossom Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Fireblossoms while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Fireblossoms while they are fully grown. А Fireblossom will bloom when the sun is setting if it is not raining, from 3:45 PM to 7:30 PM. Each plant will drop 1–3 Fireblossom Seeds when harvested while blooming.

Fireblossom Seeds can be placed on Ash Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, even inside lava, and will grow into harvestable Fireblossoms. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Underworld, but will only yield seeds when blooming.
Like the Fireblossom, this item is not destroyed when coming into contact with lava, despite having a rarity of.
Firecracker: The Firecracker is a Hardmode whip that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. It has a 34% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

Marks enemies with blazing energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by the Firecracker, a small explosion occurs and multiplies damage of the minion or sentry's attack by 2.75×. The explosion also hits other nearby enemies for 2.75× of the attack's damage. The mark is only applied to one enemy per strike, and the explosion effect only triggers once per mark.
Inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 4 seconds to all hit targets.
Its best modifier is Legendary. Light is also an option if enemies marked by the Firecracker can be attacked rapidly enough by minions or sentries.
Firecracker (mobile): The Firecracker was an unobtainable thrown consumable weapon. It was intended to be dropped from the Red Envelope, another removed unimplemented item related to the removed unimplemented Chinese New Year seasonal event.
Firefly: The Firefly is a harmless critter that gives off a tiny amount of light. Fireflies will spawn near grass on the surface at night, except inside houses. Their spawn rate will be randomly set everyday, making their spawn amount varying greatly each night.
The Firefly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Firefly can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Firefly in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Firefly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Firefly can be used as bait for fishing, with 20% bait power.
The Firefly can be spawned by the Firefly Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Its Hallow counterpart is the Lightning Bug.
Fireplace: The Fireplace is a decorative furniture item with a style similar to that of the Chimney. A Fireplace operates similarly to a Campfire, having the same dimensions, emitting light, and granting nearby players the Cozy Fire regeneration buff. The buff is applied to all players who are within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Fireplace.
A Fireplace differs from a Campfire in the following ways:
A Fireplace has a flat surface on which other items can be placed, and will function as a valid surface for a Placed Bottle crafting station.
A Fireplace functions as a valid light source for NPC housing, while the Campfire does not.
A Fireplace cannot be toggled manually via the ⚷ Open / Activate button, while the Campfire can be. However, both can be toggled via Wire.
A Fireplace cannot be used to produce a Cooked Marshmallow, while a Campfire can.
A Fireplace will function within water, while most Campfires (those other than the Coral Campfire, Cursed Campfire, and Ichor Campfire) will not.
A Fireplace is not a crafting station.
Firestarter's set: The Firestarter's set is a vanity set consisting of the Firestarter's Sweater and the Firestarter's Skirt. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Firework Fountain: The Firework Fountain is a placed novelty mechanism that is purchased from the Party Girl for 3 Gold. Once placed, it can be activated via Wire, or by interacting with the Fountain directly via ⚷ Open / Activate. Each activation causes the Fountain to randomly fire one of four colorful sparkle fountain effects, which lasts for 10 seconds. Its effect is purely visual, causes no damage, and can be used infinitely at no cost.
Firework Rockets: Firework Rockets are consumable Hardmode mechanisms that produce colorful effects. Once placed, a Firework Rocket can be activated via wire or by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it directly, which causes it to launch upwards and explode into a colorful effect. Each rocket can only be used once. Firework Rockets are purchased from the Party Girl during Hardmode for 15 Silver each.

Aside from their visual effects, Firework Rockets also deal 150 ranged damage and inflict a knockback of 7 (Strong). Their critical strike chance is based on ranged critical strike chance of the player who activated it.Verify
Fireworks Box: The Fireworks Box is a placed novelty mechanism that is purchased from the Party Girl for 5 Gold. Once placed, it can be activated via Wire (with a 0.5 second cooldown) or by interacting with the Box directly via ⚷ Open / Activate (no cooldown). Each activation causes the Box to randomly fire one of the four possible firework rockets that cause no damage. The firework rockets explode upon colliding with solid blocks or after traveling for 0.75 seconds (22.5 tiles of distance), creating a visual firework effect. It can be used infinitely at no cost.
First Fractal: The First Fractal is an unobtainable melee weapon that was originally supposed to be the new endgame sword for 1.4.0.1, but the concept was discarded during development. Its place is now taken by Zenith, though this item is still in Terraria's code. It strongly resembles the Terra Blade.

Using the weapon summons projectiles that resemble copies of the player (with all dyes removed) holding one of 15 different sprite variations of the sword in a flying barrage of attacks that follow the cursor. When there are enemies nearby, the weapon automatically targets them instead, ignoring the cursor position.
Fish (item): The Fish is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Penguin that follows the player. When the player is flying or is far enough away, the Baby Penguin will use a jetpack to catch up. The Fish has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being obtained from Frozen Chests and a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped from Frozen and Boreal Crates.
Fish Bowls: The Fish Bowl, Gold Fish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Pupfish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Lava Serpent Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are decorative furniture items. The Fish Bowl and Gold Fish Bowl also double as wearable items that can be equipped in the player's helmet slot.

Fish Bowls cause only visual effects when placed in the helmet vanity slot. When instead placed in the functional head armor slot, the breath meter appears as if the player were underwater, and if worn long enough the player will drown and die. Breathing aids like the Breathing Reed or Gills Potion will allow for normal breathing when wearing the bowl.

The Fish, Gold Fish and Pupfish Bowls are crafted, while the Lava Serpent Bowl has a 39/200 (19.5%) chance of being found inside Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. Crafted Fish Bowls can be converted back into their ingredients by throwing them into Shimmer, gaining back the fish as an item.
Fish Costume set: The Fish Costume set is a vanity set composed of the Fish Costume Mask, Fish Costume Shirt, and Fish Costume Finskirt. The complete set can be acquired randomly as a reward for completing a Fishing quest from the Angler NPC. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Fish Finder: The Fish Finder is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the weather, wind speed, moon phase, and the player's Fishing Power.
Fisherman's Pocket Guide: The Fisherman's Pocket Guide is an informational accessory that displays the player's current Fishing Power.

The Fisherman's Pocket Guide can be received as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a Fisherman's Pocket Guide as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.
Fishing Bobbers: Fishing Bobbers are accessories that change the appearance of a fishing pole's bobber and increase the player's Fishing Power by 10.

The Fishing Bobber is acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details), while the rest are crafted.

The Angler will not give the player a Fishing Bobber as a reward if they already have one in their inventory, in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.
Fishing Potion: The Fishing Potion is a buff potion which grants the Fishing buff when consumed. The buff increases Fishing Power by 15. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
The Fishing Potion can be obtained both from crafting and as a reward from the Angler for completing fishing quests.
Fishing poles: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.
Flairon: The Flairon is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it swings like a thrown flail and releases non-piercing, homing bubbles.

Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the item switches it into the Flairoon. When used, it is launched like a launched flail that also releases homing bubbles while traveling. The flail retracts after contact with enemies or blocks, or after extending for more than 25 tiles.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Flamarang: The Flamarang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang and an upgrade to the Enchanted Boomerang. It has a 1/2 (50%) chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff to enemies for 3 seconds on hit.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Flame Trap: The Flame Trap is a trap found naturally in the Jungle Temple. When activated, it fires a jet of fire, which has a maximum range of 20 (47) tiles, and can pierce an infinite number of targets. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 3.33 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 3 seconds between firings. The fire deals 80 / 160 / 240 damage to players (40 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), and inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 20 / 40 / 50 seconds on players (20 seconds on NPCs, enemies, and critters).
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Flame Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer.
Flame Waker Boots: The Flame Waker Boots are a vanity accessory obtained by opening Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates, found by fishing in Lava. They cause the player’s feet to leave trails of fire while moving on blocks. They are entirely cosmetic and provide no functional benefit of their own.
Flameburst sentry summons: The Flameburst Rod, Cane, and Staff are special sentry summon weapons that summon their respective sentries. Each Flameburst Tower shoots fireballs towards enemies, which explode on contact and have a chance to inflict the On Fire! or Hellfire debuff. Unlike other projectile sentries, the Flameburst Tower is unable to fire upward at an angle greater than 45°; thus it often ignores flying enemies. The higher the tier, the more damage the Flameburst Towers deal.
The Rod is sold by the Tavernkeep for 5 Defender Medals. The Cane is sold for 15 Defender Medals after defeating one mechanical boss. The Staff is sold for 60 Defender Medals after defeating Golem.

During the Old One's Army event, Etherian Mana can be collected, which allows the placement of multiple Flameburst Towers that remain permanently until the event is over. Etherian Mana cannot be used outside the event. These weapons cannot be used outside of the Old One's Army event until the event has been successfully completed.

Flameburst Tower sentries are boosted by the Apprentice armor and Dark Artist armor set bonuses, which dramatically increase their range, field of view, and projectile velocity. The Dark Artist armor will also boost the explosion radius of the sentries' projectiles.

Their best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 162% (including whip bonuses) or 62% (excluding whip bonuses), the Flameburst Staff's best modifier becomes Ruthless.
Flamelash: The Flamelash is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron wand. When used, it fires a fireball that follows the cursor when ⚒ Use / Attack key is held. If the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released mid-drag, the fireball will be fired in that direction. If the cursor is stationary on release, it is fired directly away from the player. Once it is released, the fireball homes in on nearby enemies and can pierce once, creating a small explosion upon contact with a block or second enemy. It also has a 1/2 (50%) chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff for 4–8 seconds. The Flamelash has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxs obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.
Flamethrower: The Flamethrower is a Hardmode, post-Skeletron Prime ranged weapon that uses Gel for ammunition. When used, it consumes one Gel and releases five bursts of fire in quick succession. The fire expands as it travels, creating a cone-like area of effect, before dissipating shortly after. The fire has 15 armor penetration, inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 20 seconds, and can pierce through three enemies. The fire's damage decreases by 15% per enemy pierced.

Its best modifier is Unreal. A modifier granting +10% speed will increase the number of flame streams per use from five to six while still consuming 1 Gel. A modifier with added velocity will increase the range of each stream, i.e. by about 5 tiles for +15% and about 3 tiles for +10%.
Flaming Arrow: The Flaming Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3 seconds on enemies.
Flaming Mace: The Flaming Mace is a pre-Hardmode flail. It has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff on hit. While the player is in water or the flail's head is submerged, the fire is extinguished and the weapon effectively becomes a regular Mace.
Its best modifier is Ruthless. Godly and Demonic may give higher crit chance, but rounding causes Ruthless to have much higher damage for this weapon.
Flare Gun: The Flare Gun is a weapon that is found randomly in Gold Chests underground. When used, it fires Flares, which provide light and stick to the blocks they hit.
The Flare Gun cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Flarefin Koi: Flarefin Koi are a type of pre-Hardmode ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) / Hardmode ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions)) fish which are found very rarely by fishing in any biome in any layer, but only in lava. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Inferno Potions.
Flares: Flares are a type of ammunition used solely by the Flare Gun. When fired, they travel in a slight arc and stick to blocks, similar to Sticky Glowsticks, but have greater velocity and range. They emit low-level tinted light for 10 minutes, but can be removed early by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Flares disappear when burnt out and cannot be recovered once fired. They work in liquids, although they bounce off Shimmer.
All types of Flares (except the Cursed Flare) inflict the On Fire! debuff. There is a 2/3 (66.67%) chance that the debuff will last 5 seconds, and a 1/3 (33.33%) chance that it will last 10 seconds.
Flask of Cursed Flames: The Flask of Cursed Flames is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff on hit for 3–6 seconds, which deals 24 damage per second and increases knockback on targets. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles.

The Flask of Cursed Flames cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.
Flask of Fire: The Flask of Fire is a flask that causes melee weapons and whips (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3–6 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles.
The Flask of Fire cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.
Flask of Gold: The Flask of Gold is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Midas debuff for 2 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles.
The Flask of Gold cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.
Flask of Ichor: The Flask of Ichor is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips to inflict the Ichor debuff for 10–19 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles.
The Flask of Ichor cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.
Flask of Nanites: The Flask of Nanites is a Hardmode, post-Plantera flask that causes melee weapons and whips (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Confused debuff for 1–3 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles. It also grants a 1.05× damage multiplier to melee and whip attacks, which is applied after other damage bonuses, but before damage of the hit is reduced by enemies' defense.
The Flask of Nanites cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.
Flask of Party: The Flask of Party is a flask that causes melee weapons and whips (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to create bursts of confetti when hitting enemies. The confetti is purely cosmetic and does not provide damage bonuses. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also create confetti when the projectiles hit enemies.
The Flask of Party cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.
Flask of Poison: The Flask of Poison is a flask that causes melee weapons and whips (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Poisoned debuff for 5–9 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles.
The Flask of Poison cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.
Flask of Venom: The Flask of Venom is a Hardmode, post-Plantera flask that causes melee weapons and whips to inflict the Acid Venom debuff on hit for 5–9 seconds, as well as the Potent Acid debuff for 1 second. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuffs on enemies hit by the projectiles.
The Flask of Venom cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.
Fledgling Wings: The Fledgling Wings are the only pre-Hardmode wings. Like all wings, they grant the player the ability to fly and glide when equipped, as well as not take fall damage. At top speed, they allow traveling at 15 mph horizontally and 22 mph vertically. They have a flight time of 0.42 seconds and a vertical speed multiplier of 150%.
The Fledgling Wings have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being obtained from Skyware Chests, Sky Crates, and Azure Crates. Journey Mode characters always spawn with a pair of Fledgling Wings.
Flesh Block: The Flesh Block is a Hardmode block. They are used to craft Flesh furniture and Flesh Block Walls. When placed, eyeballs and intestines can be seen bulging out of the block. Flesh Blocks will not spread The Crimson.
Flesh Block Wall: The Flesh Block Wall is a type of background wall. As with most placed walls, it is compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Flesh Cloning Vat: The Flesh Cloning Vat is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Flesh furniture (Crimson-themed furniture) out of Flesh Blocks. The Flesh Cloning Vat can be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold, but only appears for sale in worlds that are generated with The Crimson. It can also be crafted from the Decay Chamber, its Corruption counterpart.
Flesh Blocks are crafted using a Meat Grinder, so the Flesh Cloning Vat is of little use without one.
Flesh Grinder: The Flesh Grinder is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its Corruption counterpart is The Breaker.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Flesh Knuckles: The Flesh Knuckles are a Hardmode accessory that have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics. While equipped, they increase the player's defense by 8 and aggro by 400.
They are the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Putrid Scent; both can be exchanged via Shimmer.
Flesh Reaver: Sand Sharks are Hardmode enemies only found in Desert biomes during a Sandstorm. They are able to "swim" through all varieties of Sand, Hardened Sand, and Sandstone Blocks, but will collide normally against any other block. When they draw near a player, they will lunge out of the sand to attack.
The Sand Shark itself only appears in ordinary Deserts. There are other variants for different versions of the Desert:
Bone Biter in the Corrupted Desert
Flesh Reaver in the Crimson Desert
Crystal Thresher in the Hallowed Desert
Flint: The Flint is a Hardmode melee weapon. The weapon builds up charge while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held down, and releasing the button swings it in an arc around the player, accompanied by a yellow aura that reaches further than the weapon itself and also covers behind the player. If the weapon builds up charge for at least 0.5 seconds, it begins to glow brighter and produces a charging sound, signifying that it is fully powered. Swinging the weapon in this state releases a damaging wave of fire in front of the player that quickly travels forward across the terrain. The swing deals 178% of the weapon's damage (124 base damage) regardless of its charge, while the wave of fire deals same damage as the weapon.
Flintlock Pistol: The Flintlock Pistol is a pre-Hardmode gun that can be bought from the Arms Dealer for 5 Gold.
Flinx Fur: Flinx Fur is a crafting material dropped by Snow Flinx, an enemy found in the Ice biome. They drop 1–2 / 1–3 Flinx Fur.
Flinx Fur Block: Flinx Fur Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks crafted from Flinx Fur. Their main use is crafting Flinx Fur furniture and Flinx Fur Walls.
Flinx Fur Coat: The Flinx Fur Coat is a pre-Hardmode armor piece. When equipped, it gives the player an additional minion slot, and increases summon damage by 5%.
Flinx Fur Wall: Flinx Fur Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Flinx Fur Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Flinx Staff: The Flinx Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Flinx minion. It runs towards enemies, bouncing upwards upon contact before attempting to hit its target again. Its rapid attack rate also allows its bouncing to keep it airborne atop slow flying enemies.
Flipper: The Flipper is an accessory that allows a player to swim in liquids. When equipped, the player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly – essentially allowing unlimited multi-jumps while within liquid. It can be found in Water Chests and Ocean/Seaside Crates.
Flipper Potion: The Flipper Potion is a buff potion which grants the Flipper buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to move horizontally and vertically through water, lava, and honey without slowing down, and also allows the player to swim without equipping any swimming accessories, such as the Flipper. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Flipper Potions can be found in Pots and crates.
Floaty Gross: The Floaty Gross is a floating Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Underground Crimson. It can float through blocks in a manner similar to Wraiths and has a 1/25 (4%) to inflict the Weak debuff for 2 / 4 / 5 minutes upon contact with the player. Because of its low knockback resistance and ability to pass through walls, weapons with high knockback will be more effective against it in the narrow crevices of the Underground Crimson.
Flocko: The Flocko is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during wave 11 of the Frost Moon event. Flockos tend to spawn along with the Ice Queen and attack by flying toward the player while spinning at high speed.
Defeating a Flocko during the Frost Moon event will add 5 / 10 / 12.5 points to the current score.
Floret Protector set: The Floret Protector set is a vanity set consisting of the Floret Protector Helmet, the Floret Protector Shirt, and the Floret Protector Pants. It is one of the six sets that were added as part of the Journey's End Vanity Contest; the original concept was submitted by yikescloud. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Flounder: Flounders are a type of fish which are found plentifully by fishing in the Desert biome.
Flow Invader: The Flow Invader is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist flying enemy that spawns in the area of the Stardust Pillar during the Lunar Events. When it spawns, three smaller minions will appear one at a time and begin orbiting it. The Flow Invader uses these as attacks, launching them as high-speed projectiles towards the player. The orbiting minions will reappear over time. The Flow Invader will launch all of its remaining minions at the player upon death.
Flower Boots: Flower Boots are a rare accessory which cause flowers to grow when the player walks on regular, Jungle, Hallowed, and Ash grass. These flowers are functionally the same as the wild grass plants that grow naturally on grass, and drop Seeds and Hay normally.
Wearing Flower Boots drastically decreases the chance of critters spawning from destroyed flowers.
Flower Boots can occasionally be found in Ivy Chests, Jungle Crates, and Bramble Crates.
Flower Pow: The Flower Pow is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When thrown, it rapidly fires pink flower petals at nearby enemies, which deal 33.33% of the weapon's damage (43 base damage) and inflict 50% of its knockback (base knockback of 3.25 (Weak)).
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Flower Seeds: Flower Seeds are seeds used to plant a random flower. They can all be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Silver each. Flower Seeds can only be planted on pure grass and mowed grass blocks (not on any other type of grass), in Clay Pots, in Planter Boxes, and in Rock Golem Heads.

When used on a grass or mowed grass block, Flower Seeds cannot be planted if there is a background wall behind the block or on the tile above the block (with a few exceptions). However, it is possible to plant the seed and then place a wall behind it without breaking the plant.
Flower Wall: The Flower Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Forest and in Enchanted Sword Shrines, considered unsafe. It does drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be obtained by purchasing it from the Dryad for 10 Copper each. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Flower of Fire: The Flower of Fire is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron wand that fires a slow, non-piercing fireball that can bounce off blocks up to five times. The fireball dissipates upon contact with an enemy, with a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for a duration of 5 seconds. The Flower of Fire has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from Shadow Chests in The Underworld, and has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian and Hellstone Crates.
Flower of Frost: The Flower of Frost is a Hardmode wand that has a 19/80 (23.75%) chance of being dropped by Ice Mimics. When used, it fires a non-piercing ball of frost that can bounce off blocks up to seven times, dissipating on its eighth impact. The ball of frost inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 8 seconds on hit.
Flurry Boots: The Flurry Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be found in Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as in Frozen (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Boreal Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). While equipped, they grant the ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster, and they increase the player's maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second). The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint.
The Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots, and Sailfish Boots (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) have the same functionality, and their effects do not stack with each other.
Flying Carpet: The Flying Carpet is a flight accessory that allows the player to float for 5 seconds, similar to the Hoverboard. It can be found inside Chests located within Pyramids in the Desert. It can also be obtained by throwing a Pharaoh's Robe into Shimmer.

The Flying Carpet is activated by holding ↷ Jump in mid-air, after all jumps from extra jump accessories are used. Once it is activated, the player is put on an imaginary horizontal rail. Releasing the key deactivates the carpet, but it may be reactivated at a lower height if there is still flight time left.
Flying Dragon: The Flying Dragon is a Hardmode, post-Golem broadsword that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. When swung, it fires red crescent-shaped projectiles every 20 ticks, which pierce four enemies, pass through blocks, and dissipate after one second.
Flying Dutchman: The Flying Dutchman is a Hardmode mini-boss that spawns during the Pirate Invasion event. The Flying Dutchman emits golden particles while hovering approximately 26 tiles above the player, and is armed with four cannons that fire explosive cannonballs toward the nearest player while occasionally spawning standard Pirate Invasion enemies that fall from the deck and onto solid ground. The boss will be defeated and drop loot upon depleting the health of all four cannons.

The Flying Dutchman does not disappear after the Pirate Invasion is over (though it will explode if it has not been engaged before the invasion ends), and defeating the Flying Dutchman will not end the invasion. Several Flying Dutchmen can appear during a single Pirate Invasion, or none at all. They only appear when the event progress has passed 50%, and where there is at least 40×30 tiles space.
Flying Fish: The Flying Fish is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy that spawns when the weather is rainy in any surface biome. It follows a path much like the Eater of Souls, but has relatively low movement speed. Unlike most other flying enemies, it is able to freely enter water. Flying Fish will ignore players not in their line of sight, e.g. behind a wall or under a roof.
Flying Knife: The Flying Knife is a Hardmode melee weapon that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Hallowed Mimics. When used, it fires a controllable knife. Holding the ⚒ Use / Attack button directs the projectile's general path, although it also continuously moves on its own and ricochets off blocks. When the ⚒ Use / Attack button is released or after one minute of continuous use, the knife returns to the player.

Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. However, the bonus knockback granted by the Godly modifier is not always beneficial and makes it tricky to damage the same targets. For example, the knife will not necessarily be knocking enemies away from the player. Alternatively, modifiers that reduce knockback (the best being Ruthless) can be beneficial, reducing the distance enemies are knocked away from the cursor.
Flying Snake: The Flying Snake is a flying enemy that spawns in the Jungle Temple. Its only spawning requirement is that the player stands in front of unsafe Lihzahrd Brick Walls. The Flying Snake flies directly towards nearby players and deals contact damage, identically to a Bat.
Flymeal: The Flymeal is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. Like the Classy Cane, it has the special ability to attack town NPCs. Flymeal completely ignores the defense of NPCs, and does 2× damage to them (30 base damage; 4× damage or 60 base damage to the Nurse instead). It also inflicts the Stinky debuff for 5 seconds.
Fog Machine: The Fog Machine is a placed novelty mechanism that is purchased from the Party Girl for 4 Gold at night. When placed, it produces fog cloud effects around itself. It can be toggled on and off via Wire. The fog is purely visual, has no functional effect, and can be produced infinitely at no cost.
Fogbound Dye: Fogbound Dye is a dye purchased from the Dye Trader while in a Graveyard for 7 Gold 50 Silver. When equipped, it reduces the color saturation of the item and gives it a grayer tone, with a fog-like effect overlaying on top of the item.
FoodBarbarian's set: FoodBarbarian's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for FoodBarbarian, one of the production assistants at Re-Logic.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
FoodBarbarian's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Football: The Football is a novelty item that players can throw to each other, or to themselves. It is sold by the Party Girl for 20 Copper, after the player has accumulated a golf score of at least 501.
Holding the Football and pressing ⚒ Use / Attack throws the Football. It can then be "caught" and picked up again, even while in flight, by another player, or by the same player.

A player who takes any damage while a Football is anywhere in their inventory will automatically fumble (drop) the Football, and it can again be picked up by another player, or by the same player. If multiple Footballs are in the player's inventory at the time, they all drop.
Forbidden Block: Forbidden Blocks are Hardmode blocks crafted from Stone Blocks and Forbidden Fragments. Their main use is crafting Forbidden furniture and Forbidden Walls.
Forbidden Fragment: The Forbidden Fragment is a Hardmode crafting material which is always dropped by Sand Elementals, which spawn during Sandstorms in the Desert. To craft all items that require this material, 9 Forbidden Fragments are required.
Forbidden Wall: Forbidden Wall is a Hardmode wall. As with most crafted walls, Forbidden Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Forbidden armor: Forbidden armor is a Hardmode mage/summoner armor set consisting of the Forbidden Mask, Forbidden Robes, and Forbidden Treads. Crafting the full set requires a total of 3 Forbidden Fragments and 46 Adamantite or Titanium Bars (184 ore).
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

Summons a Forbidden Sign minion that floats behind the player. Double-tapping either ▼ Down or ▲ Up (depending on the "Activate Set Bonuses" setting) will consume 20 mana and send dust particles at the nearest solid block beneath the cursor's location, summoning an Ancient Storm. The storm rapidly deals 20 contact damage. The dust particles cannot pass through solid objects, so if they hit one before reaching the cursor, the Ancient Storm will not be summoned.
Format:C: The Format:C is a Hardmode yoyo. It has a base 24% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%, and deals 250% damage on critical hits, as opposed to the usual 200%.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Fossil Pickaxe: The Fossil Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. It is slightly faster than both the Gold Pickaxe and Platinum Pickaxe in terms of mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Fossil armor: Fossil armor is a pre-Hardmode ranged armor set consisting of the Fossil Helmet, Fossil Plate, and Fossil Greaves. Crafting the full set requires a total of 60 Sturdy Fossils.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Fox set: The Fox set is a vanity set. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to drop from Goodie Bags during Halloween. The set consists of the Fox Mask, Fox Shirt, and Fox Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Its male and female variants look identical.
Fox set (Zoologist): The Fox set is a vanity set composed of the Fox Tail and Fox Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Third Quarter or a Waning Crescent for 6 Gold (set).
Foxparks: Foxparks is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Foxparks minion. It does not deal contact damage, but runs and shoots fireballs towards enemies that inflict the On Fire! debuff for 5–10 seconds. When the weapon is held down using ⚒ Use / Attack, Foxparks will teleport to the player and be held while using a special flamethrower attack that does not consume any ammunition. The flamethrower attack rapidly shoots flames that inflict the On Fire! debuff for 5 seconds, can pierce through enemies, and lose 15% damage per hit. Both attacks deal 100% of the weapon's damage and knockback. Only one copy of Foxparks can be summoned at a time; additional uses of the summon weapon do not summon additional minions, nor do they improve the existing minion. Like other Pals, Foxparks can be petted using ⚷ Open / Activate.

Foxparks has a rare chance to spawn on Grass, Jungle grass, Snow, or Ice blocks above surface during daytime if the player is not in a Graveyard biome, but it cannot spawn in the central lateral 1/4 of the world. It is initially spawned as the distressed Foxparks, with two Goblin Archers spawned around it. After killing both Goblin Archers (or making them despawn), Foxparks will turn into its item form when the player is within 6.25 tiles from it.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Frankenstein: Frankenstein is a Hardmode enemy that commonly spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. Frankensteins behave similarly to Zombies, but have increased stats.
Freeze Bomb: The Freeze Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Bomb, but its explosion will convert water to Ice Blocks, instead of destroying blocks. The Freeze Bomb has a fuse timer of 3 seconds and its explosion deals only 1 damage to the player who threw it, but no damage to enemies, critters and NPCs.
The Freeze Bomb can be purchased from the Demolitionist for 10 Silver at night after the Eye of Cthulhu or King Slime has been defeated.
Fried Egg: The Fried Egg is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 14 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Fried Egg has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Wall Creepers, Black Recluses, and Sand Poachers. Statue-spawned Wall Creepers do not drop it, as it is a food item.
Friendly Boulder: The Friendly Boulder is a pet-summoning item that spawns a harmless Friendly Boulder that rolls around to follow the player. When the player is flying or far enough away, the Friendly Boulder will roll through the air toward the player. The Friendly Boulder can be obtained as a rare drop from naturally generated Boulders.
Friendly Rainbow Boulder: The Friendly Rainbow Boulder is a pet-summoning item obtained by throwing a Friendly Boulder into Shimmer, which summons a Rainbow Boulder pet to follow the player.

When far from the player, the boulder will bounce around, leaving a rainbow trail and explosion of sparkles every bounce. This behavior appears to mimic the real Rainbow Boulder, but it will not attack enemies or locate treasure.
Friendly Rainbow Boulder produces light when it bounces, meaning it is one of the only non-light pets that produces light.
Fries: Fries are a food item that grant the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Fries have a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Flying Fish.
Fritz: Fritz is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. It moves very quickly on the ground and leaps into players to attack.
Frog: The Frog is a harmless critter that spawns in the Jungle at any time. When in water, Frogs will swim along the water's surface. Frogs will occasionally croak during nighttime, or if they are below the surface.
The Frog has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Frog can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Frog Cage). Once crafted, the Frog cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Frog can be spawned by the Frog Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Frog to spawn in place of an ordinary one. There is also a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to spawn a Mystic Frog (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in place of an ordinary one.
Frog Flipper: The Frog Flipper is an accessory crafted from a Frog Leg and a Flipper. It combines the abilities of these two items, increasing the player's jump speed and safe falling distance, allowing auto-jump, and giving the player the ability to swim.
Frog Gear: The Frog Gear is an accessory that combines the effects of the Frog Leg, Flipper, and Tiger Climbing Gear.
Frog Leg: The Frog Leg is an accessory that can be fished in any viable body of water. It aids jumping in the following ways:
Increases the player's jump speed by 1.6.
The player automatically jumps while the ↷ Jump key is held.
Increases the maximum safe falling distance by 10 tiles.
These effects also apply with wings equipped.
Frog Webbing: The Frog Webbing is an accessory crafted from a Frog Leg and a Tiger Climbing Gear. It combines the abilities of these two items, increasing the player's jump speed and safe falling distance, allowing auto-jump, and granting enhanced mobility on walls.
Froggle Bunwich: The Froggle Bunwich is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 6 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Frost Core: The Frost Core is a Hardmode crafting material that is always dropped from Ice Golems, which spawn during Blizzards in the Snow biome. To craft all items that require this material, 5 Frost Cores are required.
Frost Daggerfish: The Frost Daggerfish is a consumable ranged weapon. It can hit up to 3 targets. Depending to player's final Fishing Power, from 7 to 137 Frost Daggerfish can be fished from lakes in Snow biomes at a time. When thrown, the Frost Daggerfish acts similarly to Shurikens or Throwing Knives, flying in an arc and then spinning to the ground, where they break upon impact.
The Angler uses Frost Daggerfish to defend himself against nearby enemies.
Frost Minnow: Frost Minnows are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in a Snow biome in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Warmth Potions.
Frost Staff: The Frost Staff is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Icy Mermen and Ice Elementals. When used, it fires a frost bolt that pierces one enemy and does not pass through blocks. The Frost Staff also inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 7 seconds on hit.
Frost armor: Frost armor is a Hardmode melee/ranged armor set consisting of the Frost Helmet, Frost Breastplate, and Frost Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 3 Frost Cores and 46 Adamantite or Titanium Bars (184 ore).
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
+11% melee and ranged critical strike chance
Melee and ranged weapons give off blue light and particles, and inflict the Frostbite debuff for 5–14 seconds upon enemy hits.
The player also leaves behind a visual snow trail while walking, and their hurt sound will be set to that of Thin Ice shattering.
Frostbrand: The Frostbrand is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 19/80 (23.75%) chance of being dropped by Ice Mimics. When swung, it fires a Frost Bolt projectile that pierces two enemies before dissipating on the third hit, cannot pass through blocks, and inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 4 seconds on hit.
Frostburn Arrow: The Frostburn Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Frostburn debuff for 3 seconds on enemies.
Frostspark Boots: The Frostspark Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory crafted from Lightning Boots and Ice Skates, and combines their functionality. They grant the following effects while equipped:
The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of snow clouds as they sprint.
Increased maximum movement speed to 35 mph (25.67 tiles/second).
The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual cloud trail.
When paired with wings, this flight is disabled to give the wings an additional 0.7 seconds of flight time.
Increased acceleration and deceleration on all Ice Blocks, Thin Ice, Frozen Slime Blocks, and Aetherium Blocks. The player will no longer cause Thin Ice to break upon landing.
Frozen Banana Daiquiri: The Frozen Banana Daiquiri is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 15 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Frozen Chest: The Frozen Chest is a Chest storage item found only in the Ice biome, spawning as frequently as Chests do in other biomes.
Frozen Crate: The Frozen Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Snow and Ice biome. Frozen Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in Frozen Chests. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Boreal Crate.
Frozen Crown: The Frozen Crown is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a miniature Ice Queen that follows the player. The Frozen Crown is dropped by the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event in Master Mode with a 12.5–25% chance depending on the current wave.
Frozen Shield: The Frozen Shield is a Hardmode, post-Plantera shield that combines the functionalities of the Paladin's Shield and the Frozen Turtle Shell. While equipped, it grants the following effects:

While the wearer's health is above 25%, it grants all nearby players on their team (excluding themselves) the Paladin's Shield buff, which provides 25% damage reduction and redirects that damage to the wearer.
While the wearer's health is at or below 50%, it grants the wearer +25% damage reduction.
Frozen Slime Block: Frozen Slime Blocks are blocks without any friction, making them more slippery than their constituent block, the Ice Block.

When a character moves atop Frozen Slime Blocks, their movement speed is maintained when direction keys are released, sliding at full speed until the Frozen Slime Blocks end or an obstacle is reached. Speed is maintained even when auto-stepping up single-block steps.
Frozen Turtle Shell: The Frozen Turtle Shell is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Ice Tortoises. While equipped, it grants the Ice Barrier buff, which provides +25% damage reduction while the player's health is at or below 50%. While the effect is active, it displays as a blue circle spinning around the player.
Frozen Zombie: The Frozen Zombie is a Zombie variant that only appears on the Surface Snow biome at night. It acts the same as normal Zombies, slowly walking towards the player to deal contact damage, while attempting to navigate around obstacles and only being able to open doors during a Blood Moon. It is differentiated from other Zombies in that it is dressed in a light blue snow suit, which it can drop as armor pieces in the form of the Snow Hood, Snow Coat, and Snow Pants.
Like normal Zombies, it has an armed variation in Expert Mode, which can perform a "slashing" attack when close to the player to deal extra damage with increased range.
Fruit Juice: Fruit Juice is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 15 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Fruit Juice can be crafted from any variety of fruit, making it a viable source of food early on.
Fruit Salad: The Fruit Salad is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 25 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Fruitcake Chakram: The Fruitcake Chakram is a pre-Hardmode boomerang dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 0.626% in pre-Hardmode and 0.584% in Hardmode.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Full Moon Squeaky Toy: The Full Moon Squeaky Toy is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Werewolf that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Werewolf flies after them by flapping its arms, mimicking a bird-like creature. The Full Moon Squeaky Toy can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Hardmode Blood Moon for 30 Gold.
Funeral set: The Funeral set is a vanity set consisting of the Funeral Hat, Funeral Coat, and Funeral Pants.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 30 Gold (set) when he is spoken to in the Graveyard biome.
Fungi Bulb: The Fungi Bulb is an uncommon enemy found in Glowing Mushroom biomes above the surface. During Hardmode, they can also appear in Underground Glowing Mushroom biomes. The Fungi Bulb follows the plant behavior akin to the Man Eater, but is less aggressive. Unlike its tougher Hardmode variant, the Giant Fungi Bulb, it does not fire spore projectiles.
Fungo Fish: Jellyfish are enemies found in water. When underwater, they attack by propelling themselves towards the player in short bursts. When outside of water, they will be unable to move or pursue the player in any way. Jellyfish are able to jump out of the water to attack players, often leaving them stranded on land. Most varieties of Jellyfish produce light, making them easy to spot in dark areas. There are 5 Jellyfish variants, 3 of which only appear during Hardmode.

In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a Jellyfish will periodically become "electrified" (except for Fungo Fish). During this electrified state, it is invincible, and will constantly maintain its speed unless it comes into contact with a solid block or the water's surface. Certain attacks to Jellyfish in this state will hurt the player by 1.3× the contact damage of the Jellyfish (see Notes for details). Unlike other damage sources, this damage will not be reduced by banners.
Furnace: The Furnace is a crafting station used mainly to smelt ores into bars and create various pieces of furniture. It is also a light source, but it is not valid for housing. The Furnace smelts all pre-Hardmode ores besides Hellstone, which must be smelted in a Hellforge. The Glass Kiln, Hellforge, and Hardmode Forges are upgraded versions of the Furnace, each with additional crafting recipes.
The Furnace can also be purchased from the Merchant when he is in the Jungle biome for 3 Silver.
Fuzzy Carrot: The Fuzzy Carrot is a mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Bunny Mount. It has a top speed of 40 mph. The Fuzzy Carrot is obtained from the Angler as a reward for completing his 5th fishing quest.
GPS: The GPS is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the in-game time, the player's horizontal position, and their depth.
Galaxy Pearl: The Galaxy Pearl is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's luck by 0.03. It can only be used once per player and is obtained by throwing a Pink Pearl into Shimmer.
Gangsta Hat: The Gangsta Hat is a vanity item purchased from the Clothier after the Frost Legion has been defeated.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can only be purchased at night, for 1 Gold.
On the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, it can be obtained for free at any time.
Garden Gnome: The Garden Gnome is a small furniture item formed when a Gnome touches sunlight. A placed Garden Gnome positively influences the player's Luck stat by 0.2. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Garden Gnome, similar to the Heart Lantern. Additional Garden Gnomes do not increase luck further.
Garden Gnomes have five different sprites when placed (which are functionally identical):
Facing a direction with their arms akimbo.
Facing a direction with their arms on their side.
Mooning their bottom toward the screen.
The ▲ Up and ▼ Down buttons cycle which sprite will be placed.
Garland: The Garland is a vanity item for the Social Helmet slot.
Gas Trap: The Gas Trap is a trap item obtained by throwing a Whoopie Cushion into Shimmer. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to appear in any chest when the No Traps special seed is active.

After being placed in a stationary storage item, the Gas Trap will activate the next time that storage item is opened, inflicting the Poisoned debuff to all entities within a small radius, with a duration of 49 seconds / 1 minute 38 seconds / 2 minutes 3 seconds for players and 49 seconds for NPCs, enemies and critters. The Gas Trap then becomes a Used Gas Trap and can only be "refilled" by throwing it into Shimmer, producing a new Gas Trap. Only one Gas Trap will be used at a time whenever a player opens a storage item if multiple are inside. A Gas Trap will not activate if the storage item it was placed in is opened in a singleplayer world while autopause is enabled.
Gastropod: The Gastropod is a flying Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns frequently on the surface of The Hallow at night. If the player is within its line of sight, it will open its shell and fire high-velocity Pink Lasers which emit faint pink light.
Like most other slimes, the Gastropod will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel accessory equipped.
Gatligator: The Gatligator is a Hardmode gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 35 Gold. When used, it rapidly fires bullets in a roughly 30° spread, at a varying velocity. It also has a 50% chance not to consume ammunition.
Gato Egg: The Gato Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Propeller Gato that follows the player. The Gato Egg is dropped by Dark Mages during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 1, and a 1/12 (8.33%) chance during Tier 3.
Gel: Gel is a common crafting material dropped by most slimes and Slimed Zombies. Gel is vital due to it being an ingredient in Torches, and is used regularly from the beginning stages all the way through to endgame scenarios. It is also used as ammunition for the Flamethrower and the Elf Melter, and can therefore be stored in the player's ammo slots.
Gel Dye: Gel Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It is received as a random reward. When equipped, the Gel Dye produces an effect similar to that of the Slime debuff caused by the Slime Gun.
Gelatin Crystal: The Gelatin Crystal is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Queen Slime when used. It can only be used in The Hallow or Underground Hallow, at any time.
Crystal Shards have a 1/50 (2%) chance to be replaced by a Gelatin Crystal upon generation. A Shard will drop a Crystal when broken.
Gelatinous Pillion: The Gelatinous Pillion is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a friendly Winged Slime Mount. Similar to the pre-Hardmode Slime Mount, the Winged Slime offers increased jump height, provides boosted movement speed, negates fall damage, and allows continuous auto-jump by holding the ↷ Jump key. It also shares the Slime Mount's abilities to deal 40 summon damage to enemies when jumping on them from above, and floating when entering liquids.

The Winged Slime Mount grants 2.66 seconds of flight time, similar to low-tier wings, allowing the player to fly up to a height of 73 tiles, as well as gliding while holding the ↷ Jump key after flight time has been exhausted. It can also hover by holding ▼ Down, similar to the Hoverboard.
The Gelatinous Pillion has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime in Classic Mode, or a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Queen Slime's Treasure Bag.
Gem Bunnies: Gem Bunnies are harmless critters that can only spawn in the Cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Bunnies, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa.
Gem Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Bunny Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Gem Locks: Gem Locks are activation mechanisms that can be placed on background walls. They trigger when a Large Gem of the corresponding type is inserted or removed with ⚷ Open / Activate.
Gem Squirrels: Gem Squirrels are harmless critters that can only spawn in the cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Squirrels, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa. Gem Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Gem Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Squirrel Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Gemcorns: Gemcorns are seeds crafted from an Acorn and any gem. When placed, they create saplings that can grow into gem trees. Natural gem trees occasionally generate within the Underground and Cavern layers. Destroying a gem tree generally yields 7–48 Stone Blocks, 0–11 Gemcorns of the tree's type, and 0–24 gems of the tree's type (each tile of the tree has a 1/10 (10%) chance of dropping a gem, otherwise dropping 1–2 Stone Blocks, and every non-barren leaf/branch tile additionally has a 1/2 (50%) chance to drop another Gemcorn. See Growing conditions section for detailed info).
Gemcorns cannot be retrieved after being placed. Destroying the sapling will not yield any items.
Gemspark Blocks: Gemspark Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks. They glow when placed or dropped as an item, with the color of the glow depending on the gem used to craft the block. They are also considered mechanisms, as their glow can be toggled by wiring them to a trigger.

If a waterfall passes through a Gemspark Block, it will also color and add a glowing effect to it. When the Gemspark Block is in its active state, the resulting waterfall will take on the color of the Gemspark Block, and will glow for its entire length. Glowing waterfalls emit a very faint light onto other objects. Gemspark Blocks will not change the color of lavafalls, honeyfalls, or Shimmerfalls (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Gemspark Walls: Gemspark Walls are the wall equivalent of Gemspark Blocks, and come in Online and Offline variants. Like Gemspark Blocks, Online Gemspark Walls emit light when placed or dropped as an item, but do not count as a light source for NPC housing. Unlike Gemspark Blocks, Gemspark Walls do not act as Mechanisms and their online and offline states cannot be switched after being placed. Online Gemspark Walls placed behind blocks will cause the blocks to appear fully lit, similar to the effect of Illuminant Coating.
Gemstone Walls: The Gemstone Walls are types of background walls. Except for the Amber Stone Wall, they can be found naturally generated in Gemstone Caves, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on the Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
Gender Change Potion: The Gender Change Potion is a pre-Hardmode potion that allows the player to swap their character style between male and female. Hurt sounds and equipment sprites change accordingly. The effect lasts until another Gender Change Potion is used.
Gentleman's set: The Gentleman's set is a vanity set consisting of the Gentleman's Beard, the Gentleman's Long Beard, the Gentleman's Magnificent Beard, the Gentleman's Vest, and the Gentleman's Trousers. The Vest and Trousers can be crafted, while the Gentleman's Beard can be bought from the Stylist for 5 Gold.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

When equipped in an accessory slot, the Gentleman's Beard will grow longer over time. After 12 minutes of being equipped, the beard has a 1/9 (11.11%) chance every second to grow to the next stage. This growth is not affected by speeding up time, and will not occur when the beard is equipped in a vanity slot. The beard also changes colors based on the player's hair color. The longer versions of the beard can be crafted back into the shorter versions.
Geode: The Geode is a consumable that has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Granite Elementals and Granite Golems. When used, it is thrown and drops gems upon impact with blocks. Each Geode drops 2 types of gems with 3–6 gems of each type.
Geyser: The Geyser is a trap that spews a vertical stream of fire which deals a base damage of 40 / 80 / 120 and a knockback of 2 (Very weak) emitting large amount of light. It will activate when a player touches it or when it is triggered via wire.
