Geysers are found naturally-placed in random areas that are deep enough to generate lava, including the Underworld and deeper Cavern areas. They are generated without Pressure Plates or wires attached to them.
Geysers can be placed on the top or bottom of blocks, facing upward or downward respectively, but not sideways.

Geysers consume no ammunition, and their output is limited only by a cooldown period of 3.33 seconds. Geyser fire streams extend up to 20 tiles up or down (which can be blocked by solid blocks) and last for 1 second. The stream also has the ability to move through solid blocks and liquids before creating the fire stream (see Notes for details).
Ghastly Glaive: The Ghastly Glaive is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss spear that is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) chance / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. Unlike any other spear, it is thrust in a curved motion. Upon striking an enemy, a yellow ghast projectile appears next to a random nearby enemy and flies in a straight line through it for 1 second before dissipating. The ghast projectile pierces enemies infinitely and deals the weapon's full damage, but does not inflict knockback.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Ghost (enemy): The Ghost is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Cavern layer during the Halloween seasonal event.

On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, Ghosts will also spawn in the Graveyard mini-biome in Surface and cavern layers, regardless of time, and have a chance to spawn when breaking Tombstones.

Ghosts behave like Wraiths, hovering above the ground and passing through solid tiles to reach the player. In order for Ghosts to travel up to players, they must have a solid block to pass through, or else they will stay hovering just above the ground.
Ghost set: The Ghost set is a vanity set. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to drop from Goodie Bags during Halloween. It consists of a Ghost Mask and Ghost Shirt. When a player wearing it is killed, the set parts float down into the ground and the player's severed remains do not appear. The set also becomes transparent, possibly meaning the player becomes a ghost, however the set parts are still separated.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Ghostar's set: Ghostar's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Ghostar, a former production assistant at Re-Logic.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Ghostar's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to her clothing set:
Ghoul: Ghouls are Hardmode Underground Desert enemies who follow the Fighter AI (behaving similarly to Zombies). Ordinary Ghouls spawn inside the normal Underground Desert, the Vile Ghoul inside Corrupt parts of the Underground Desert, the Tainted Ghoul inside Crimson parts of the Underground Desert, and the Dreamer Ghoul inside Hallowed parts of the Underground Desert.
Ghoulder: The Ghoulder is a special type of Boulder that generates instead of normal Boulders near the Dungeon (see Boulder generation). It initially behaves similar to a normal Boulder, but gains new behavior upon hitting the ground when falling faster than 26 mph, or upon colliding with left or right side of blocks. This new behavior causes it to enter a ghost form and chase the closest player while freely flying and passing through blocks, but only when the player is facing away from it. When the player faces towards the Ghoulder, it will regain its normal appearance and drop down to the ground, and stay motionless afterwards until the player faces away from it again. The Ghoulder deals 140 / 280 / 420 damage to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), and inflicts a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on contact.
Gi: The Gi is an armor item that can be equipped in the shirt slot. It provides 4 defense along with a 5% damage and critical strike chance boost to weapons. It also provides a 10% melee and movement speed increase. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold. The Gi will visually cover up what is equipped in the pants slot.
Giant Antlion Charger: The Antlion Charger is an enemy similar in appearance to the Antlion, and is found in the Underground Desert or on surface Deserts during pre-Hardmode Sandstorms. Unlike the Antlion, the Antlion Charger will, as its name suggests, charge at the player instead of remaining stationary. It can jump over blocks and will gradually build up speed while moving before charging the player. It can rarely drop the Mandible Blade.
Giant Antlion Swarmer: The Antlion Swarmer is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy found in the Underground Desert or on surface Deserts during Sandstorms. It is a large dragonfly-like creature that looks similar to the Antlion and Antlion Charger.
Giant Bat: The Giant Bat is a Hardmode bat enemy that spawns in the Cavern layer. It can inflict the Confused debuff for 5 / 10 / 12.5 seconds, and also has a 1/10 (10%) chance to inflict the Feral Bite debuff in Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) for 30–90 seconds. It appears much larger than a normal Cave Bat.
Giant Bow: The Giant Bow is a festive vanity item that has a 1/20 (5%) chance to drop during Christmas by Present Slimes, which visually have a large bow on. The Bow itself is red, but it can drop from any of the four colors of Present Slime.
When worn in the helmet slot, a bow appears on top of the player's head.
Giant Cursed Skull: The Giant Cursed Skull is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It acts similarly to the Cursed Skull in flight pattern, except it is much larger and will occasionally shoot "Shadowflames", high-velocity white blasts that pass through tiles. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it has a chance to inflict the Cursed debuff upon contact, while its projectiles always inflict the debuff, which lasts for 4 / 8 / 10 seconds.
Giant Cursed Skulls spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by slab or tiled walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Giant Flying Fox: The Giant Flying Fox is a Hardmode bat enemy that spawns only on the surface of the Jungle at night. In Expert Mode, it can inflict the Feral Bite debuff.
Giant Fungi Bulb: The Giant Fungi Bulb is a Hardmode enemy found in Glowing Mushroom biomes both above and below the surface. They act similar to Man Eaters and Snatchers, but have a longer reach and launch Fungi Spores towards the player, dealing high damage. Fungi Spores fly towards their target, breaking upon contact with blocks, and glide downward in a serpentine pattern. They can be destroyed by one hit with any weapon or damage-inflicting tool.
Giant Harpy Feather: The Giant Harpy Feather is a rare crafting material used solely to craft Harpy Wings. It has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Harpies.
Giant Shelly: The Giant Shelly is a pre-Hardmode enemy found in the Cavern layer, and has two color variants that share identical stats and behavior. The Giant Shelly walks around slowly and occasionally curls into its shell. It then starts spinning and hurls itself at the player, gaining increased defense and dealing high contact damage. Giant Shellies attack very quickly and deal high damage compared to other enemies for the stage in the game where they are found.

Giant Shellies are unique in that their ability to spawn is connected to two other enemies: the Crawdad and the Salamander. Of these three enemies, a world will choose two types that it can spawn, leaving the third inaccessible. Giant Shellies will never spawn in a world that features both Crawdads and Salamanders together. This is taken into account by the Bestiary progression logic (the missing enemy will register as unlocked when the other two exclusive creatures are unlocked) and the banner acquisition (any two of the trio's banners can be used to craft the banner of the missing member of the trio).
Giant Tiki: The Giant Tiki is a furniture item that is sold by the Witch Doctor when in the Jungle for 25 Silver. It has three different sprites which can be cycled through with the ▲ Up and ▼ Down keys before placing.
Giant Tortoise: The Giant Tortoise is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Jungle and Underground Jungle. It walks around slowly, and occasionally retracts into its shell. It then starts spinning and hurls itself at the player, gaining increased defense and dealing high contact damage. It drops Turtle Shells, which are vital for crafting Turtle armor.
A functionally identical variant of the Giant Tortoise, the Ice Tortoise, can be encountered in the Ice biome.
Giant Worm: The Giant Worm is a pre-Hardmode worm enemy that spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and tunnels through blocks to attack the player. It makes a distinctive shuffling sound that grows louder and more rapid as it approaches the player, providing an indicator of its presence and proximity. It also leaves behind a subtle particle effect in its trail.
On Old-gen console and 3DS versions, it only spawns in pre-Hardmode and is replaced by the Digger in Hardmode.
Gigazapper: The Gigazapper is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that appears during the Martian Madness event. It uses a short-ranged electrical spear weapon unavailable to players, with a maximum fire rate of once every half of a second. Its projectiles shock the player, inflicting the Electrified debuff for 4–8 seconds, causing the player to lose health rapidly.
Gills Potion: The Gills Potion is a buff potion which grants the Gills buff when consumed. The buff prevents the player's breath meter from depleting and thus prevents drowning. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Gills Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.
Ginger Beard: The Ginger Beard is a vanity accessory found in Iron and Mythril Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height.
The Ginger Beard cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Gingerbread Cookie: The Gingerbread Cookie is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Gingerbread Cookie can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 3.601% in pre-Hardmode and 3.361% in Hardmode.
Gingerbread Man: The Gingerbread Man is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Frost Moon event. He is much like the Splinterling but drops no items.
Defeating a Gingerbread Man during the Frost Moon event will add 2 / 4 / 5 points to the current score.
Glacier Fang: The Glacier Fang is a pre-Hardmode wand that fires chargeable icicles toward the cursor, affected by gravity. It can be found in Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, Frozen Crates, and Boreal Crates.

The weapon builds up charge when the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held, gradually increasing the icicle's damage, knockback, velocity, size, and amount of enemies it can pierce (see Notes for details). If the weapon builds up charge for 1 second, the icicle reaches full power and will be automatically launched. The icicle can be also launched early by releasing ⚒ Use / Attack before it is fully charged. In addition to consuming mana on the initial use, the weapon also consumes mana for a second time when it has built up charge for 0.33 seconds, and a for a third time when it has built up charge for 0.67 seconds. Each time the weapon consumes mana when building up charge, the icicle held by the player also visually grows larger and makes a charging sound. The icicle loses 34% of its damage for each enemy it pierces. The Glacier Fang also has a base 15% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Gladiator armor: Gladiator armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Gladiator Helmet, Gladiator Breastplate, and Gladiator Leggings. Each piece has a 1/21 (4.76%) chance of being dropped by Hoplites.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Gladius: The Gladius is a pre-Hardmode shortsword that is dropped by Hoplites with a 1/20 (5%) chance. It attacks three times in quick succession per use, with slightly varying angles with each stab.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Glass: Glass is crafted from different types of sand at a Furnace. Glass can be placed as a block and is an ingredient in producing various items.
Glass Kiln: The Glass Kiln is a crafting station used to craft Glass furniture out of Glass. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it also has the ability to produce all normal Furnace recipes. Like the Furnace, it emits light when placed.
Glass Slipper: The Glass Slipper is a vanity accessory sold by the Princess for 1 Platinum. It will leave sparkling particles when the player walks around.
The Glass Slipper cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Glass Wall: Glass Walls are transparent walls that can be used to make windows that let in natural light, while preventing monster spawns. They are crafted from Glass and also spawn naturally in houses on Floating Islands. They can be crafted into Stained Glass.
Glommer's Flower: Glommer's Flower is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns Glommer to follow the player. Glommer's Flower is dropped from Derplings with a 1/100 (1%) chance and increased to 1/40 (2.5%) in The Constant secret seed.
Glow Tulip: The Glow Tulip is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Caveling Gardener that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, it flies through solid tiles while holding onto a Snare Plant in order to catch up to them. The Glow Tulip can be found rarely near the left and right edges of the world below the Surface as a plant. Depending on world size, a set amount of Glow Tulips will spawn during world generation: 2 in small worlds, 4 in medium worlds, and 6 in large worlds. Half of them are usually generated on the left side and the other half on the right side of the world.
It can also be detected by the Metal Detector.
Glowing Mushroom: The Glowing Mushroom is a plant, crafting material, and block that can be found on Mushroom grass in the Glowing Mushroom biome. Glowing Mushroom plants emit blue light.

Instead of being placed as a plant, Glowing Mushroom items are placed as solid blocks. Glowing Mushroom items can be obtained by destroying Glowing Mushroom plants, cutting down Giant Glowing Mushrooms, and destroying Mushroom vines and cattails. Doing so will also yield Mushroom Grass Seeds.
Glowing Mushroom Dye: Glowing Mushroom Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it gives items a blue and black color palette which glows in the dark.
Glowing Snail: The Glowing Snail is an uncommon critter that only spawns in either surface or underground Glowing Mushroom biomes. It emits light and is quite large compared to its normal counterpart. The Glowing Snail has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Glowing Snail can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Glowing Snail Cage). Once crafted, the Glowing Snail cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Glowing Snail can be used as bait for fishing, with 15% bait power.
The Glowing Snail can be spawned by the Snail Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Glowstick: The Glowstick is a consumable light source that can be held or tossed a fair distance. It works underwater but cannot be placed on a wall or floor like Torches can. After being thrown, a Glowstick will emit light for 5 minutes before expiring. Afterward, it disappears and cannot be retrieved. Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it before it expires, however, causes the Glowstick to drop as an item for the player to pick it back up.

Glowsticks can be purchased for 10 Copper each, either from the Merchant during the night (any moon phase) or from the Skeleton Merchant during the day (except for Full Moons). Glowsticks are always dropped from Blue, Pink, and Green Jellyfish, as well as from Flying Fish and Raincoat Zombies. They are also commonly found in Pots and Chests.
Gnome: The Gnome is an uncommon pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns around the surface, and spawns more commonly in Living Trees. When it is not behind a background wall on the surface during the daytime, it will turn into a Garden Gnome which increases the luck of nearby players.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Gnome requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Goat Skull: The Goat Skull is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Goat Mount which allows the mounted player to perform a double jump, similar to the Cloud in a Bottle. The Goat Skull has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh in Master Mode.

Once a high enough speed is reached, the Goat Mount leaves a trail of fire on solid blocks behind itself, similar to Flame Waker Boots, and from that point on, it will be able to damage enemies on contact. The invulnerability is granted for 1/10th of a second when the player and the Goat Mount dash through an enemy, much like the brief invulnerability after taking damage.
Goblin Archer: The Goblin Archer is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Goblin Army event. It fires Wooden Arrows at players within its line of sight while stationary. Its attacks can be interrupted by knocking it back.
Goblin Archers will also spawn alongside the distressed Cattiva and Foxparks, and must be defeated before the Pals turn into their item forms.
Goblin Battle Standard: The Goblin Battle Standard is an event-summoning item that initiates the Goblin Army event when used. The Goblin Battle Standard is consumed when used, so one must be crafted for each invasion the player wishes to summon. In order for it to be used, at least one player in the current world must also have 200 health or more.
The Tattered Cloth required for crafting the Goblin Battle Standard is obtained by killing Goblin Scouts, which spawn occasionally in the East and West sixths of the world.
Goblin Bomber Cap: The Goblin Bomber Cap is an unobtainable item resembling the cap worn by Etherian Goblin Bombers. It only exists as an ID and image file in the game's code. Attempting to use third-party tools to obtain it will result in it instantly disappearing.
Goblin Mask: The Goblin Mask is an unimplemented item resembling an Etherian Goblin mask. It only exists as an ID and image file in the game's code. It presumably would be available as part of the Dungeon Defenders 2 crossover. Attempting to use third-party tools to obtain it will result in it instantly disappearing.
Goblin Peon: The Goblin Peon is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Goblin Army event. It is the event's most basic enemy and follows the Fighter AI. Approximately one out of every five goblins will be a Peon (17.8% chance to spawn). It has the unique ability to destroy doors that are in its way (destroyed doors drop as collectible items).
The Goblin Peon is only two tiles tall (instead of the 3-tile player height) and can fit through smaller gaps in the player's walls.
Goblin Scout: The Goblin Scout is an uncommon pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns on the surface in the farthest edges of the player's world. It appears to be an enemy from the Goblin Army event, but it spawns during ordinary gameplay. The Tattered Cloth it drops is a component for the Goblin Battle Standard, which summons a Goblin Army.

Goblin Scouts can only be found in the furthest east and furthest west sixths of the world. They will not spawn on Sand Blocks or on blocks infected by The Corruption, The Crimson or The Hallow and will only spawn during the day.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Goblin Sorcerer: The Goblin Sorcerer is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Goblin Army event. Approximately one out of every nine goblins will be a Sorcerer (11.11% chance to spawn). The Goblin Sorcerer fires three Chaos Balls in succession that travel through blocks before it teleports. The Sorcerer cannot fire and will not teleport when taking damage.
Goblin Tech: The Goblin Tech is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the most valuable block nearby, the player's current DPS, and their current movement speed.
Goblin Thief: The Goblin Thief is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Goblin Army event. It follows the typical Fighter AI but moves at a higher speed than similar enemies. Goblin Thieves can jump high and open Tall Gates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) faster than other fighters. Approximately one out of every six goblins will be a Thief (15.8% chance to spawn).
Goblin Tinkerer: The Goblin Tinkerer is an NPC vendor who sells several unique items and also provides the reforge function. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

Rescuing him as the Bound Goblin, who can be rarely encountered in the Cavern layer (or the Underground layer if playing on the Remix special world seed), after a Goblin Army has been defeated. Interacting with him in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will free him. If the Bound Goblin is killed, he will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Goblin Tinkerer NPC is killed, he will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.

The Goblin Tinkerer's reforge option allows the player to randomize the modifier of a weapon or accessory, which makes the resulting item's stats better or worse than they were originally. Reforging costs one-third of the item's current value, which can also be affected by its current modifier. The reforge cost is also affected by the Goblin Tinkerer's happiness, and therefore can be decreased by equipping a Discount Card or Greedy Ring.
The Goblin Tinkerer will defend himself against nearby enemies by throwing Spiky Balls. He deals 15 / 22 / 26 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
The Bound Goblin is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Goblin Warlock: The Goblin Warlock is a Hardmode enemy that rarely spawns during the Goblin Army event. Because of her high stats and relatively high difficulty compared to other goblins, she will present a challenge for new Hardmode players. Defeating her, however, rewards the player with weapons that are themed after Shadowflame, all of which accordingly inflict the Shadowflame debuff.

The Goblin Warlock initially seems to behave like a typical Fighter AI enemy, though once she is close enough to the player, she will summon a Shadowflame Apparition above herself before flying directly upwards. She will not stop her ascent until she is above the player, at which point she will then dash over towards the player's current position before slowly gliding towards the ground in a somewhat rectangular flight pattern. The Goblin Warlock also flies towards the player if they move too far away from her and passes through any solid blocks in her path. If she is hovering at any time, she will fire Chaos Balls approximately once every half-second, which can be destroyed by any weapon or projectile.

She is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Goblin Warlock requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of her Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Goblin Warrior: The Goblin Warrior is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Goblin Army event. It follows the Fighter AI and is the most commonly encountered enemy in the event. Approximately one out of every three goblins will be a Warrior (31.6% chance to spawn).
Like many other enemies that follow the Fighter AI, Goblin Warriors can open doors and Tall Gates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Goblorc Ears: The Goblorc Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.
Goggles: Goggles are a piece of armor placed in the helmet slot. Unlike most helmets, Goggles do not cover the player's hair. Due to their low defense, they are often used as vanity items.
Gold Axe: The Gold Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Axe.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Gold Bar: The Gold Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Bar.
Gold Bird: The Gold Bird is a harmless critter. It may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Bird, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Bird has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Bird can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Bird Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Bird cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Bird itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Bow: The Gold Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Gold Brick: Gold Bricks are a type of brick crafted from Gold Ore. In some worlds, they are found as part of Jungle Shrines in the Underground Jungle. Like the ore they are made of, placed Gold Bricks will sparkle.
Gold Brick Wall: The Gold Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.
Gold Broadsword: The Gold Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Gold Shortsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Broadsword.
Gold Bunny: The Gold Bunny is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Bunny, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Bunny has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Bunny can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Bunny Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Bunny cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Bunny itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Butterfly: The Gold Butterfly is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Butterfly, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Butterfly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Butterfly can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Butterfly Jar). Once crafted, the Gold Butterfly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Butterfly itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
The Gold Butterfly can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Chest: The Gold Chest is a naturally-generated chest, with various loot as its contents. Each chest includes one special item, as well as some coins and other more common items. Gold Chests are found in Underground Cabins or randomly in the Underground and Cavern layers, as well as in the Pyramids.

Apart from the initial items, Gold Chests function identically to other chests. Removing all items from a Gold Chest will allow it to be freed or broken with a pickaxe or drill. It can then be picked up, placed, and used just like any other chest, with 40 slots of storage space. There are only three minor differences to other chests: Gold Chests cannot be crafted and are only generated on world creation at the random locations; they can also be sold to an NPC at 10 Silver, which is more than the standard chest, which only sells for 1 Silver. Gold Chests have a sparkle effect when exposed to a light source, similar to coins.
Gold Crown: The Gold Crown is a craftable vanity item that can be worn in the Social Helmet inventory slot. It is also one of the crafting materials for the Slime Crown, which is used to spawn King Slime.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Crown.
Gold Dragonfly: The Gold Dragonfly is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Dragonfly, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Dragonfly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Dragonfly can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Dragonfly Jar). Once crafted, the Gold Dragonfly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Dragonfly itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
The Gold Dragonfly can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Dust: Gold Dust is a Hardmode crafting material that is purchased from the Merchant for 17 Silver each. Its sole purpose is to craft the Flask of Gold and Golden Bullets, which both allow the player to inflict the Midas debuff.
Gold Frog: The Gold Frog is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Frog, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Frog has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Frog can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Frog Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Frog cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Frog itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Goldfish: The Gold Goldfish is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Goldfish, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Goldfish has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Goldfish can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Fish Bowl). Once crafted, the Gold Goldfish cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Goldfish itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Grasshopper: The Gold Grasshopper is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Grasshopper, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Grasshopper has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Grasshopper can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Grasshopper Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Grasshopper cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Grasshopper itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
The Gold Grasshopper can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Hammer: The Gold Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Gold Ladybug: The Gold Ladybug is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Ladybug, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Ladybug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Ladybug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Ladybug Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Ladybug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Ladybug itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
The Gold Ladybug can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power.

Touching naturally spawned Gold Ladybugs will temporarily increase the player's luck, while killing natural or player-released Gold Ladybugs or consuming them as bait will temporarily decrease the player's luck and boost the chance of rain. However, using them for crafting does not affect luck, allowing the following recipes to be made consequence-free.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Mouse: The Gold Mouse is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Mouse, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Mouse has only 5 health and no defense, and can only be damaged by players.

The Gold Mouse can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Mouse Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Mouse cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Mouse itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Ore: Gold Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on Floating Islands. Gold Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Platinum Ore.
Gold Pickaxe: The Gold Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. It can also mine Meteorite.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Pickaxe. The Gold Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Gold Ring: The Gold Ring is a Hardmode accessory that greatly increases the pickup range for coins. It has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance to be dropped by pirates (except Parrots) during Pirate Invasions, with a 1/125 (0.8%) chance from the Pirate Captain. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be dropped by the Flying Dutchman (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The increase in pickup range is 21.875 tiles, extending the base range of 2.625 tiles to 24.5 tiles. This effect does not stack with that of any of the Gold Ring's upgrades.
Gold Seahorse: The Gold Seahorse is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Seahorse, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Seahorse has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Seahorse can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Seahorse Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Seahorse cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Seahorse itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Shortsword: The Gold Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Gold Broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Shortsword.
Gold Squirrel: The Gold Squirrel is a harmless critter. Gold Squirrel may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Squirrel, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Squirrel has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Squirrel can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Squirrel Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Squirrel cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Squirrel itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Starry Block: The Gold Starry Block is an animated decorative block. When placed it shows twinkling, gold stars on a black background. It is the gold-themed variant of the Blue Starry Block.
Gold Starry Wall: Gold Starry Wall is a background wall made from Gold Starry Blocks. It is one of only a few animated background walls.
Gold Water Strider: The Gold Water Strider is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Water Strider, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Water Strider has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Water Strider can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Water Strider Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Water Strider cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Water Strider itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
The Gold Water Strider can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold Worm: The Gold Worm is a critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Worm, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version.
The Gold Worm has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Gold Worm can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Worm Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Worm cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Worm itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold.
The Gold Worm can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power.
Gold Worms have a 1/20 (5%) chance of being obtained from opening a Can Of Worms.
Uniquely, the Gold Worm has an exceptionally low chance of being consumed as bait of 1/20 (5%).
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Gold armor: Gold armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Gold Helmet, Gold Chainmail, and Gold Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Gold Bars (300 Gold Ore). The full set grants 16 defense while equipped.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Platinum armor.

The Ancient Gold Helmet is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Gold Helmet. The Ancient Gold Helmet has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons, and can also be obtained by dropping a Gold Helmet into Shimmer. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Gold Helmet prior to 1.0.3.
Golden Bug Net: The Golden Bug Net is an upgraded version of the Bug Net and Lavaproof Bug Net. It functions similarly, being a swung tool that captures critters, but is larger, faster, and can destroy any tiles that weapons can destroy (like tall grass, vines, or fully grown Pumpkins), and also allows the player to catch Underworld critters (Lavaflies, Hell Butterflies, and Magma Snails). The Golden Bug Net has a base 1/80 (1.25%) chance of being obtained from the Angler as a reward for completing fishing quests.
Golden Bullet: The Golden Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It inflicts the Midas debuff on hit for 2 seconds, causing enemies to drop 10%-50% more coins when killed.

Golden Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Golden Bullets is 19 Silver 50 Copper, which is 39 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Golden Bullets is 39 Gold.
Golden Carp: Golden Carp are a type of fish which are found extremely rarely by fishing in any biome in the Underground, Cavern and Underworld layers, with the exception of the Desert. They have an extraordinarily high sell value of 10 Gold.
Golden Crate: The Golden Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any layer. It is the highest tier of standard crate, having the greatest value if sold directly. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Titanium Crate.
Golden Delight: The Golden Delight is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 48 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. It is crafted at the Cooking Pot with any gold critter or Golden Carp.
Golden Key: Golden Keys are required to unlock the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon and Golden Lock Boxes (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) obtained by fishing in the Dungeon, as well as to free the Elder Slime (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) from an Old Shaking Chest (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). A Golden Key is consumed upon use, so each unlock will require an additional key.
Golden Keys can be acquired by:
Finding one in an unlocked normal Chest in the Dungeon.
Killing any other Dungeon enemy, excluding post-Plantera enemies (1.52% chance).
Breaking a Pot in the Dungeon (1/35 (2.86%) chance ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) / 1/40 (2.5%) chance ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions)).
Golden Lock Box: The Golden Lock Box is a grab bag item that is always obtained from Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates. It always contains one rare item normally found in locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon. It requires one Golden Key to open, which can be obtained from any Dungeon enemy, generally a Dungeon Slime.
Golden Seaweed: The Golden Seaweed was used to summon a pet Golden Turtle. It lasted until the player manually canceled the buff by using the Golden Seaweed again. It was obtained from Chests, but only on the Amazon Fire TV. It was obtainable on other mobile devices via trading.
This item was removed alongside all other mobile exclusive content in the Mobile 1.3.0.7 update.
Players on Windows Phone who acquired the Golden Seaweed via trading continue to have access to it.
Golden Shower: The Golden Shower is a Hardmode spell book that fires arcing golden ichor streams in quick succession. Each stream can hit up to 5 targets. The streams inflict the Ichor debuff for 10 seconds (15 seconds in PvP), which adds 15 armor penetration.

The Golden Shower is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Flames and the Hallow's Crystal Storm, all of which require a Spell Tome and ingredients exclusive to their underground biome counterparts.
Goldfish: The Goldfish is a critter that swims in water and walks on land during rain. It flops in place when out of water and rain; it does not take damage while doing so. The Goldfish has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Goldfish can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Fish Bowl). Once crafted, the Goldfish cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Goldfish can be spawned by the Fish Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Goldfish to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile Powder/Vicious Powder (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Goldfish will turn into Corrupt Goldfish or Vicious Goldfish (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Golem: Golem is a Hardmode, post-Plantera boss fought in the Jungle Temple. It attacks the player by stomping on them, launching its fists, and firing barrages of projectiles. Defeating Golem is a prerequisite for unlocking the Lunar Events, the Martian Madness, and Tier 3 of the Old One's Army.
While Golem is alive, its exclusive music Boss 4 will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Golem Fist: The Golem Fist is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When used, it fires a large, high-velocity fist attached to a chain that retracts on impact with enemies or blocks, or after traveling for more than 31.25 tiles away from the player.. Upon hitting enemies or blocks, it creates a shockwave that deals 100% of the weapon's damage and knockback to nearby enemies if extended by more than 9.375 tiles. Both the Golem Fist and its shockwave have a 1/3 (33.33%) to inflict the Confused debuff for 1-2 seconds on hit.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Golf Balls: Golf Balls are accessories that are used in golf and come in a variety of colors. The plain, white Golf Ball can be purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold and can be used for crafting the colored variants.
The Golf Ball items are not required to play golf, as pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on an empty Golf Tee will always create a Golf Ball projectile. Their main purposes are:
Changing the color of this projectile, which is a purely visual effect. The Golf Ball item does not need to be equipped for this, having it in the inventory is sufficient.

Manually placing Golf Ball projectiles anywhere in the world, even outside of Golf Tees. This is done by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button while the Golf Ball item is selected. The item will not be consumed, it can be reused to place an unlimited number of Golf Ball projectiles.
Golf Ball projectiles can be hit with a Golf Club and despawn when entering a Golf Cup or when the player presses the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them.
Golf Cart Keys: The Golf Cart Keys are a post-Skeletron mount-summoning item that places the player in a rideable Golf Cart. The Golf Cart emits light from its front that reaches about 40 tiles, with the brightest point being at about 15 tiles. The Golf Cart Keys can be purchased from the Golfer for 50 Gold after Skeletron has been defeated, and a golf score greater than 2000 is earned by the player.
Golf Clubs: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. There are four types of Golf Clubs, the Driver, Iron, Wedge, and Putter, which are each used to hit the Golf Ball a different horizontal and vertical distance.
Special variants of Golf Clubs can be unlocked by achieving different golf scores. All upgrades are purely aesthetic, despite being more expensive as the tier increases.
They do not harm enemies or critters.
Golf Cup: The Golf Cup is a block and activation mechanism used in Golf. It can be purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold. When a Golf Ball enters the cup, the Golf Ball projectile is removed from the world, the cup emits a wire signal, and a status message will share how many strokes the player took between placing the ball, hitting it and reaching the cup.
Golf Tee: The Golf Tee is a furniture item used in golfing purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold. It assists in placement of Golf Balls, and balls struck from a Golf Tee will travel further.
Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on a Golf Tee places a Golf Ball on top of it.
Golf Whistle: The Golf Whistle is a tool used in golf that allows a player to recover Golf Balls, returning it to the previous position before it was hit when used. Using the Golf Whistle adds one stroke to the player's golf score for the shot as a penalty. The Golf Whistle can be purchased from the Golfer for 10 Gold.
Golf trophies: Golf trophies are decorative furniture items that can be purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold each once the player has reached a certain golf score.
Golfer: The Golfer is an NPC vendor who sells golfing-related items. More items will be unlocked as the player's golf score increases, including clubs, trophies, and paintings. He will move in once the following criteria are met:
There is an available vacant house.

Rescuing him as the Golfer Rescue, who can be rarely encountered in the Underground Desert. Interacting with him in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will free him. If the stationary Golfer is killed, he will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Golfer NPC is killed, he will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.
The Golfer will attack nearby enemies with his golf balls to defend himself.
He is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Goodie Bag: The Goodie Bag is a grab bag item available during the Halloween seasonal event. Each contains one random reward from the list below. Goodie Bags are opened by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory, similar to all other grab bags. They can be opened anytime, even outside the Halloween season.

Goodie Bags are dropped with a 1/80 (1.25%) chance by any enemy that has more than 1 maximum health, deals more than 0 damage, and drops coins, during Halloween only. Therefore, enemies spawned by statues, enemies from the Old One's Army and Lunar Events, etc. can never drop Goodie Bags (see Coin drops for the full list). Moreover, Meteor Heads cannot drop Goodie Bags either.
Gothic Brick: Gothic Bricks are pre-Hardmode bricks crafted from Stone Blocks, Cobwebs, and Bones at a Bone Welder. Their main use is crafting Gothic furniture and Gothic Brick Walls.
Gothic Brick Wall: Gothic Brick Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Gothic Brick Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Gradient: The Gradient is a Hardmode yoyo that can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 20 Gold. It leaves behind a visual gradient trail when used.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Grandfather Clocks: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner.

There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 / 5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.
Granite Block: Granite is a block found underground in Granite Caves. In addition to being found in placed form, it can also drop from Granite Elementals and Granite Golems.
Granite Chest: The Granite Chest is a chest storage item found only in Underground Cabins within Granite Caves. Like Marble Chests and Rich Mahogany Chests, Granite Chests have exactly the same loot as Gold Chests.
Granite Elemental: The Granite Elemental is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in Granite Caves and floats towards the player. In Expert Mode, Granite Elementals have a 1/6 (16.67%) chance to shield themselves and drop to the ground defensively when attacked, making them immune to all damage for 2 seconds before they begin hovering again.
Granite Elementals always drop Granite Blocks upon death, like Granite Golems. They can also rarely drop the Night Vision Helmet.
Granite Golem: The Granite Golem is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in Granite Caves. Every 5 seconds, it will stand still and shield itself from all attacks for 2 seconds, making it completely invulnerable. It can still deal damage to players during this invulnerable state should they walk into it.
Like the Granite Elemental, it will always drop a small amount of Granite Blocks. It can also rarely drop the Night Vision Helmet.
Granite Wall: The Granite Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Granite Caves, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be generated as part of an Underground Cabin in a Granite Cave, considered safe. It is also considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Grape Juice: Grape Juice is a Hardmode food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Grapefruit: The Grapefruit is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Forest tree.
Grapes: Grapes are a Hardmode food item that grant the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Grapes have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped by Derplings and Giant Flying Foxes.
Grass Seeds: Grass Seeds are seeds used to plant regular grass on Dirt Blocks. They are purchased from the Dryad for 20 Copper each, while a Blood Moon is not occurring. They can also be obtained from putting Poo into an Extractinator, with a 0.67% chance per item.
Grass Wall: The Grass Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in above-ground tunnels and grottoes on the surface, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained by purchasing it from the Dryad for 10 Copper each, while a Blood Moon is not occurring. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Grasshopper: The Grasshopper is a type of critter that can be found when destroying grass plants and moves by hopping along the ground identically to slimes. The Grasshopper has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Grasshopper can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Grasshopper Cage). Once crafted, the Grasshopper cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Grasshopper can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% bait power.
The Grasshopper can be spawned by the Grasshopper Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Grasshopper to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Grate: The Grate is a foreground block which allows liquids to fall through while remaining solid for everything else, acting like a drainage system.

Grates can be toggled open and closed when triggered via wire. An open Grate is transparent, allowing light and liquid through, while a closed Grate is opaque and acts as a solid block. If a Grate is triggered while liquid is passing through it, the Grate holds the liquid until it is opened again or the liquid is removed by a player, e.g. via the use of an Empty Bucket, Super Absorbant Sponge, or Dry Bomb.
Bubbles function as the opposite of Grates, acting as background objects which prevent the flow of liquids through them but allow through other things like players.
Grates are not destroyed when dropped in lava, despite having a rarity of.
Gravedigger set: The Gravedigger set is a vanity set consisting of the Gravedigger Hat and Gravedigger Coat.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) when he is in the Graveyard biome.
Gravedigger's Shovel: The Gravedigger's Shovel is a tool that can be used to dig up "soft" blocks (see below) more efficiently than a pickaxe or drill, in a 3×3-tile rectangle centered on the cursor.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Gravitation Potion: The Gravitation Potion is a buff potion which grants the Gravitation buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to invert gravity with ▲ Up, making the screen appear upside-down and causing the player to fall upwards and walk on top of ceilings. The effect can be toggled while in midair. This lasts for 3 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Gravitation Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.
Gravity Globe: The Gravity Globe is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord accessory that allows the holder to flip gravity, so that the player falls up instead of down, and toggle gravity back to normal afterward. Once equipped, pressing the ▲ Up key toggles the gravity direction. This only affects the player with the item equipped. The Gravity Globe is always dropped from the Moon Lord's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Gray Brick: The Gray Brick is a pre-Hardmode brick.
Gray Brick Wall: Gray Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Gray Bricks. They can only be painted white, black or brown.
Gray Cockatiel: The Yellow Cockatiel and Gray Cockatiel are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. They may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Cockatiels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Cockatiels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Yellow / Gray Cockatiel Cage). Once crafted, the Cockatiels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Cockatiels can be spawned by the Cockatiel Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Gray Grunt: The Gray Grunt is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that spawns during the Martian Madness event. While outwardly similar to most Martian enemies, it is unique in that it is completely invulnerable to knockback.
Gray Swimshorts: The Gray Swimshorts are a craftable vanity item.
Gray Zapinator: The Gray Zapinator is a pre-Hardmode-exclusive magic gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 17 Gold. It is only available once King Slime, the Eye of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds, Brain of Cthulhu, Queen Bee, Deerclops, or Skeletron has been defeated. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Orange Zapinator.

The weapon fires a blue laser beam that behaves very erratically. Upon striking an enemy, the projectile slows down by 40%, decreases its current damage and knockback by 10%, and can choose from an assortment of special effects as described below. The laser beam will disappear after hitting eight enemies or after 60 seconds. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, it costs no mana to use.
Greater Healing Potion: The Greater Healing Potion is a Hardmode recovery potion that restores 150 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.
Greater Healing Potions can be crafted using materials found in The Hallow or obtained from most Hardmode bosses as well as from Biome Mimics and Martian Saucers.
It is the third tier of healing potion, succeeding the Lesser Healing Potion and Healing Potion, and preceding the Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion.
Greater Mana Potion: The Greater Mana Potion is a Hardmode recovery potion that restores 200 mana and inflicts the Mana Sickness debuff upon use. Unlike most potions, Greater Mana Potions cannot be crafted, and are instead purchased from the Wizard for 5 Silver, or dropped from all Biome Mimics except the Jungle Mimic.
It is the third tier of mana potion, succeeding the Lesser Mana Potion and Mana Potion, and preceding the Super Mana Potion.
Grebe: The Grebe is a critter that spawns in bodies of water in the Desert biome that are directly above Sand Blocks. It may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. The Grebe has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Grebe can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Grebe Cage). Once crafted, the Grebe cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Greedy Ring: The Greedy Ring is a Hardmode accessory that combines the Discount Card's 20% discount off at any NPC shop, the Lucky Coin's 20% chance of spawning 1–10 extra coins whenever an enemy is hit and +0.05 luck, and the Gold Ring's increased coin pickup range.
Green Cap: The Green Cap is a piece of armor. It will always drop from the Guide, but only when his name is Andrew.
Green Fairy: The Pink Fairy, Green Fairy, and Blue Fairy are critters that emit light, which will attempt to lead the player to valuable treasures, such as Life Crystals, Chests, or ore deposits. They spawn in the bottom half of the Underground layer and in the Cavern layer, but only if at least one Fallen Log is present in the world on the surface (see Fallen Log § Notes for the exact area). If all Fallen Logs have been destroyed, they will no longer spawn independently. The three fairy variants all function identically.

Fairies can also spawn at Fallen Logs and from shaken Pearlwood trees on the surface at night. In this case, they will not lead players to treasure; instead, when approached, they try to flee much like Birds or Faelings. Unlike fairies spawned underground, these fairies can be caught with a Bug Net and carried around in the inventory. If released again, they act like the ones spawned underground and will attempt to lead the player to treasure. They can also be crafted into animated decorative furniture (Fairy jars). Once crafted, the fairies cannot be released again unless de-crafted via Shimmer.
They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Green Horseshoe Balloon: The Green Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 33%, jump speed by 30%, grants a double jump, and grants +0.05 luck. The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks (~75% increase), while the double jump's height is increased from 10.5 blocks to 18.5 blocks, reaching a total of 29 blocks with both jumps. The double jump also makes a fart sound.
Jump height is oddly reduced when underwater, to 18 blocks (7 blocks + ~11 blocks from Fart jump).
Green Jellyfish: Jellyfish are enemies found in water. When underwater, they attack by propelling themselves towards the player in short bursts. When outside of water, they will be unable to move or pursue the player in any way. Jellyfish are able to jump out of the water to attack players, often leaving them stranded on land. Most varieties of Jellyfish produce light, making them easy to spot in dark areas. There are 5 Jellyfish variants, 3 of which only appear during Hardmode.

In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a Jellyfish will periodically become "electrified" (except for Fungo Fish). During this electrified state, it is invincible, and will constantly maintain its speed unless it comes into contact with a solid block or the water's surface. Certain attacks to Jellyfish in this state will hurt the player by 1.3× the contact damage of the Jellyfish (see Notes for details). Unlike other damage sources, this damage will not be reduced by banners.
Green Mushroom: The Green Mushroom is a type of mushroom. It grows on Dirt, Stone, Mud, or regular Jungle grass in the Underground and Cavern layers. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Green Dye.
Green Slime: The Green Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that commonly spawns in Forest biomes during the daytime. It is the weakest slime and also one of the most common ones to encounter, likely making it the first enemy a player will come across in a new world. Green Slimes will not target the player under usual circumstances, but will become aggressive when damaged, during the night, or if brought underground.
Like most other slimes, the Green Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
On Desktop, Console, Mobile, and 3DS, they can rarely be found carrying bonus drops, which the player receives upon the slime's death.
Green Swimshorts: The Green Swimshorts are a craftable vanity item.
Grenade: The Grenade is an explosive consumable ranged weapon which can be purchased from the Demolitionist for 75 Copper each, or found rarely in natural Chests and, once Hardmode is activated, in Pots (replacing Shurikens).
A thrown Grenade will bounce slightly and roll until it either hits a valid target or 3 seconds have elapsed, after which it will explode.
Grenade Launcher: The Grenade Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher. When used, it consumes rockets and launches grenades that explode after three seconds have passed or upon contact with enemies. The grenades are strongly affected by gravity and can damage the player for a flat 60 damage.

The Grenade Launcher has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to be dropped from Plantera, and it is guaranteed to drop the first time Plantera is defeated (unless in Expert Mode, where she drops her Treasure Bag instead). In addition, 50–149 Rocket Is will be dropped alongside the Grenade Launcher.
Its best modifier is Unreal for combat purposes and Rapid for mining and usage of liquid rockets.
Grilled Squirrel: The Grilled Squirrel is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Grim Dye: Grim Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it turns the color of the armor or vanity currently selected into a blood red type color, while emitting a dark effect around the player, similar to Loki's Dye.
Grox The Great's set: Grox The Great's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Grox The Great, one of the programmers who develops Terraria.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Grox The Great's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Grub Soup: Grub Soup is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 14 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Grubby: Grubby is one of three critters that occasionally spawn in the Jungle or Underground Jungle biome when a player breaks a plant, the others being Sluggy (rarer) and Buggy (rarest). Grubby is the most common of the three. Grubby has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Grubby can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Grubby Cage). Once crafted, Grubby cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Grubby can be used as bait for fishing, with 15% bait power.
Grubby can be spawned by the Buggy Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Guardian Golem: The Guardian Golem is a Hardmode, post-Golem light pet-summoning item that spawns a Toy Golem light pet upon being used or equipped. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Toy Golem emits a rocket exhaust to catch up to them. The Guardian Golem has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Golem in Master Mode.
Guide: The Guide is usually the first NPC a player encounters. He spawns near the player when the world is created. He provides tips mainly aimed at new players via the “Help” option and displays crafting recipes (including the crafting station required) of items shown to him via the “Crafting” option.

Unlike most other NPCs, the Guide spawns upon world creation, before a house is available. He will, however, move into the first house built. If he is killed, a proper house will need to be built before he can respawn, but he has no additional requirements.

The Guide will defend himself against nearby enemies using a Wooden Bow, firing Wooden Arrows initially and then upgrading to Flaming Arrows during Hardmode. He deals 8 / 12 / 14 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
Guide Voodoo Doll: The Guide Voodoo Doll is a boss-summoning item used to summon the Wall of Flesh. It is a guaranteed drop from Voodoo Demons, a fairly rare enemy in the Underworld.

If the item is dropped and destroyed by lava in the Underworld, the Guide will instantly die and the Wall of Flesh will be summoned. The Guide must be alive for this process to occur. If the item is destroyed by lava elsewhere, the Guide will die as normal but the boss will not be summoned; if the item is destroyed by lava when the Guide is not alive, the item will be wasted without summoning the boss.

On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, if more than one Guide Voodoo Doll is in a stack upon being destroyed by lava, other NPCs will be killed alongside the Guide depending on the amount within the stack. However, the Wall of Flesh will only be summoned once.
When the Guide Voodoo Doll is equipped as an accessory, it becomes possible for the player and other NPCs to kill the Guide with direct attacks from weapons (which normally would not damage him).
The Guide Voodoo Doll cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Guide to Critter Companionship: The Guide to Critter Companionship is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from harming critters while inside their inventory or opened Void Bag. It can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold.

Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Critter Companionship in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Critter Companionship and the Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive), disabling its functions.
Guide to Environmental Preservation: The Guide to Environmental Preservation is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from breaking plants while inside their inventory or opened Void Bag. It can be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Gold.

Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Environmental Preservation in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Environmental Preservation and the Guide to Environmental Preservation (Inactive), disabling its functions.
Guide to Old World Parkour: The Guide to Old World Parkour is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord tool that slightly modifies the player's movement capabilities while inside their inventory or opened Void Bag.
When jumping from a grapple, the player jumps at half height rather than full height.
The strength of the speed-reducing debuffs Chilled, Burning, and Slow is affected in some way.
The behavior of the Shield of Cthulhu when dashing into multiple targets at once is affected in some way.

Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Old World Parkour in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Old World Parkour and the Guide to Old World Parkour (Inactive), disabling its functions.
Guide to Peaceful Coexistence: The Guide to Peaceful Coexistence is a pre-Hardmode tool that combines the effects of the Guide to Critter Companionship and the Guide to Environmental Preservation, preventing player attacks from harming critters and breaking plants when placed within the player's inventory or opened Void Bag.

Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence and the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive), disabling its functions.
Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage: The Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage is an accessory that, when equipped, causes destroyed vines to drop Vine Ropes. It has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found in surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. It can also be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver during First Quarter moons.
Gummy Worm: The Gummy Worm is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's Fishing Power by 3. It can only be used once per player and is obtained when a Gold Worm comes into contact with Shimmer, either as a critter or in dropped item form.
Gungnir: The Gungnir is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss spear. When thrust, it creates a small shockwave at its tip.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Guy Fawkes Mask: The Guy Fawkes Mask is a head piece vanity item. It is purchased from the Clothier during Halloween for 3 Gold.
Hades Dye: Hades Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it turns the dyed armor, accessory, or equipment blue, also adding a blue flames effect.
Haemorrhaxe: The Haemorrhaxe is a Hardmode hamaxe that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Hemogoblin Sharks and Blood Eels.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Hair Dyes: Hair Dyes are consumable items sold by the Stylist NPC. When used, they replace a player's hair color with a dynamic effect.
Hallowed Bar: The Hallowed Bar is a Hardmode bar. It is dropped by all three mechanical bosses: The Twins, The Destroyer, and Skeletron Prime.
Hallowed Brick: The Hallowed Brick is a Hardmode brick that is crafted from Pearlstone Blocks and Hallowed Bars.
Hallowed Brick Wall: Hallowed Brick Wall is a Hardmode wall. As with most crafted walls, Hallowed Brick Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Hallowed Crate: The Hallowed Crate is a crate that can only be fished in The Hallow. It contains items found in standard crates.

The Hallowed Crate can be obtained by throwing a Divine Crate into Shimmer. It can also be obtained by building an artificial Hallowed biome in a pre-Hardmode world and fishing for it there. When fishing in the Hallow in Hardmode, only Divine Crates will be caught, the Hallowed Crate's Hardmode counterpart.
Hallowed Crown: The Hallowed Crown is a craftable vanity item that can be worn in the Social Helmet inventory slot. Unlike other Hallowed head pieces, it is not armor, provides no bonuses to the player, and does not count towards the Hallowed armor set bonus.
Hallowed Grass Wall: The Hallowed Grass Wall is a type of background wall which can be found in The Hallow, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, by purchasing it from the Dryad in Hardmode for 2 Silver 50 Copper each. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

The Clentaminator/Terraformer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (using Blue Solution) and Holy Water convert Grass Walls, Flower Walls, and Jungle Walls (both safe and unsafe) to unsafe Hallowed Grass Walls.
Hallowed Grass Walls can spread The Hallow to nearby pure walls. See Biome spread for further information.
Hallowed Jousting Lance: The Hallowed Jousting Lance is a Hardmode melee weapon. When attacking using ⚒ Use / Attack, the lance will extend, and holding ⚒ Use / Attack will keep it extended at a fixed angle. The damage and knockback will increase depending on the player's movement speed, making mounts, sprinting accessories, or dash abilities (such as those granted by Shield of Cthulhu, Tabi/Master Ninja Gear, or Solar Flare armor) useful for maximizing damage. When the player takes damage, the Hallowed Jousting Lance will stop being active.
It is the upgrade of the Jousting Lance and the precursor to the Shadow Jousting Lance.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Hallowed Mimic: Mimics are rare Hardmode enemies disguised as Chests, appearing as the appropriate chest type for the environment.
Mimics can be spawned by the player using the Chest Statue, even in pre-Hardmode. However, Mimics spawned this way only drop the Mimic Banner.
