Rarer Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics can also be spawned manually by players via a Key of Light or Key of Night (see the Biome Mimic section below).

They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics require 25 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Hallowed Repeater: The Hallowed Repeater is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss repeater.
Hallowed Seeds: Hallowed Seeds are Hardmode seeds used to plant Hallowed grass on Dirt Blocks, which will then spread The Hallow. Hallowed Seeds are purchased from the Dryad in Hardmode for 20 Silver each.
Hallowed Walls: The Hallowed Prism Wall, Hallowed Cavern Wall, Hallowed Shard Wall, and Hallowed Crystalline Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Hallow, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on the Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
Hallowed armor: Hallowed armor is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss armor set consisting of the Hallowed Plate Mail and Hallowed Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Hallowed Mask, Hallowed Helmet, Hallowed Headgear, and Hallowed Hood, providing bonuses for melee, ranged, magic, and summon damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Hallowed Bars. Crafting all six pieces requires a total of 90 Hallowed Bars.
Hallowed armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Hallowed armor pieces, still providing the set bonus.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:

Upon enemy hits, the player receives the Holy Protection buff, which grants the ability to dodge the next attack dealt by an enemy or other damage source. It has a 30-second cooldown after the dodge has been activated.
The player also emits visual pulses and afterimages while moving.
Ham Bat: The Ham Bat is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Pigrons. It gains slightly increased damage if a food buff is active. Killing an enemy with the Ham Bat grants the Hearty Meal buff, which increases the player's health regeneration by 3 per second. This lasts for 7 seconds, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The buff will not stack upon killing another enemy; the duration instead resets.
In a The Constant world, the drop chance is increased to 1/10 (10%).
Hammush: The Hammush is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss hammer that is purchased from the Truffle for 40 Gold. When used, the Hammush releases 5 lingering Mushroom projectiles from its tip and along its swing arc. The Mushroom projectiles deal 50% of the Hammush's damage (13 base damage), but do not inflict knockback and cannot pierce. Like the Pwnhammer, it can destroy altars.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Hand Of Creation: The Hand Of Creation is a post-Skeletron construction accessory. It grants the following effects while equipped:
+50% placement speed when placing blocks and walls
Increased placement range and tool range by 2 tiles vertically and 3 tiles horizontally
Automatically applies paint or coating to placed objects
Increased pickup range of items from 2.625 tiles to 12 tiles
Hand Warmer: The Hand Warmer is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Chilled and Frozen debuffs. It is obtained from Presents, with a chance of about 0.622% in pre-Hardmode and about 0.580% in Hardmode.
Handgun: The Handgun is a pre-Hardmode gun that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon, and from Golden Lock Boxes found in Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates.
Hanging Brazier: The Hanging Brazier is a placeable decorative furniture item. It can only be placed on the ceiling, and breaking one of the blocks above it will drop the item. The Hanging Brazier is a valid light source for NPC housing.
Hanging Pot: The Hanging Pot is a placeable decorative furniture item obtained by opening Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.
Hanging Skeleton: The Hanging Skeleton is a decorative furniture item that can be placed on background walls. It can be found in the Dungeon, where they only appear in areas backed by Slab or Tile Walls.
Hanging herbs: Hanging herbs are placeable decorative furniture items craftable with one Hanging Pot and one herb. They can only be placed on the ceiling and breaking one of the blocks above a hanging herb will drop the item.
Happy Grenade: The Happy Grenade is an explosive consumable ranged weapon that inflicts half the damage of an ordinary Grenade and displays a confetti effect. They must be acquired initially from being dropped by the Party Girl when she is killed, although she only has 1/4 (25%) chance of dropping them each time she is killed. Once the Party Girl respawns again, they can be purchased from her for 2 Silver 50 Copper each, while the player has them in their inventory.
Hardened Sand Blocks: The Hardened Sand Block is a type of block, along with Sandstone Blocks, that make up the Underground Desert biome. It looks similar to Sand Blocks, with an altered texture and slightly different color. Unlike sand, it is not affected by gravity. Like all sand-based blocks, it has Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Hardened Ebonsand, Hardened Crimsand, and Hardened Pearlsand respectively.
Hardened Sand Walls: The Hardened Sand Wall, Hardened Ebonsand Wall, Hardened Crimsand Wall, and Hardened Pearlsand Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert, considered unsafe. Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Hardened Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow. Converted Hardened Sand Walls may further spread conversion; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Hardened Sand Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
The Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall is an item that places an unsafe Hardened Sand Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Hardened Sand Wall into Shimmer.
Hardmode Anvils: The Mythril Anvil and Orichalcum Anvil are Hardmode crafting stations that serve and extend the function of a pre-Hardmode Anvil. These are very crucial to game advancement, as they account for making nearly every Hardmode recipe before the Ancient Manipulator. In addition to acting as a direct replacement to Lead and Iron Anvils and inheriting all of their crafting recipes, they further serve the similar function of crafting bars forged of Hardmode ores into weapons, armor and tools, as well as several other items, such as wings.
Hardmode Forges: The Adamantite Forge and Titanium Forge are Hardmode crafting stations that incorporate the same functions as a regular Furnace and Hellforge, with the additional bonus of being able to smelt Adamantite, Titanium and Chlorophyte ores into their respective bars. They emit light and give off fire particles when placed, like the Furnace and Hellforge.
The Adamantite Forge and Titanium Forge are functionally identical.
Hardy Saddle: The Hardy Saddle is a mount-summoning item that summons a Turtle Mount that can swim and has increased movement speed in liquids (51 mph maximum), but reduced movement speed (26 mph maximum) and jump reach (3.53 tiles maximum) on land. It also allows the player to breathe underwater.
The Hardy Saddle has a 7/80 (8.75%) chance of being obtained from Golden Crates and a 133/1600 (8.31%) chance of being obtained from Titanium Crates.
Harp: The Harp is a Hardmode crafting material, used only to craft the Magical Harp. While the Harp can be used itself, it has no functional use, and only makes sounds. It is sold by the Wizard for 1 Gold each.

When used, the Harp generates harp sounds. The sound's pitch is determined by the distance between the center of the character and the point clicked. Clicking the center of the character plays middle C, while clicking at a distance of at least that of the top or bottom of the screen plays C6 (two octaves above middle C). The smallest interval between notes the harp can play is a whole tone, or two semitones. A difference of 1/24 of the screen height equals an interval of a whole tone.
Harpoon: The Harpoon is a unique pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that auto-fires an arcing spear projectile connected to the player via a chain that pierces through enemies and inflicts the Bleeding debuff for 8–12 seconds on hit. It retracts if it hits a third enemy, collides with solid blocks, has traveled for more than 62.5 tiles away from the player, or if the player lets go of the ⚒ Use / Attack button. Its physics are similar to launched flails, though it is highly affected by gravity. The Harpoon has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by most enemies during a Goblin Army.

The Harpoon only has an attack cooldown of 0.08 seconds after its spear is fully retracted; meaning its fire rate is mostly dependent only on how long it takes for it to retract. The projectile also pierces infinitely and goes through blocks on its return trip, similar to a flail or boomerang, making it effective for crowd control.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Harpy: The Harpy is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy that spawns in Space and at high altitudes, typically around Floating Islands. They move following the Bat AI, and fire slow-moving blue feather projectiles in inaccurate bursts of three.
Prior to Hardmode, they cannot spawn in the central vertical section of the map, which is one-tenth the width of the entire map. This restriction is removed in Hardmode.
Up to seven Harpies can exist on-screen during the day, ten at night, and fifteen during a Blood Moon.
Harpy Block: Harpy Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks crafted from Feathers. Their main use is crafting Harpy furniture and Harpy Walls.
Harpy Charm: The Harpy Charm is a pre-Hardmode combat accessory that grants +5% ranged critical strike chance and redirects arrows fired by the player towards the closest enemy. Arrows must be at least 25 tiles away from the player in order to be redirected. After the Harpy Charm redirects an arrow, it goes on cooldown for 1.5 seconds, during which the effect will not occur.
Harpy Wall: Harpy Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Harpy Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Hat Rack: The Hat Rack is a decorative furniture item that can be used to display up to two helmet-slot armor and vanity items, as well as dyes.

Items can be placed on a Hat Rack by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, which opens a small set of inventory-like slots beneath the player's main inventory. There are two slots for two helmets, in addition to an associated dye slot underneath each one. Placing items in these slots immediately displays them on the Hat Rack. Items placed in the left slot are displayed on the upper part of the Hat Rack, while items placed in the right slot are displayed on the lower part. Items cannot be displayed on the middle, top part.
Hay: Hay is a type of block that is harvested from wild grass plants and sea oats by using a Sickle. It can be used to make Target Dummies.
Hay Wall: The Hay Wall is a type of wall made from Hay.
Headless Horseman: The Headless Horseman is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) wave 5 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) wave 9 of the Pumpkin Moon event. He is an exceptionally dangerous enemy due to his speed, high contact damage, and immunity to knockback. The Headless Horseman attacks by charging forward and doing a low, quick jump to reach the player. Additionally, on the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, the Headless Horseman can also throw a Pumpkin Head projectile, which moves in a wavelike manner and homes into the player for an extended period of time.
Defeating a Headless Horseman during the Pumpkin Moon event will add (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 50 / 100 / 125 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 25 points to the final score.
Healing Potion: The Healing Potion is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that restores 100 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It is the second tier of healing potion, succeeding the Lesser Healing Potion and preceding the Greater Healing Potion, Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion.

In addition to being crafted, Healing Potions can be found naturally in pots during Hardmode and pots in the Underworld in pre-Hardmode. Healing Potions are also dropped by Deerclops, Skeletron, and the Wall of Flesh, and are sold by the Merchant and the Skeleton Merchant in Hardmode for 10 Silver.
Heart Hairpin: The Heart Hairpin is a vanity item that is sold by the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold. It is worn in the helmet slot.
Heart Lantern: The Heart Lantern is a functional lantern that grants the Heart Lamp buff, providing a health regeneration of 1 HP per second to all players within a rectangular area of 170×125 / 100×84 tiles.
Like other lanterns, the Heart Lantern is a mechanism that can be toggled on or off if wired, though this does not affect the buff.
Heartreach Potion: The Heartreach Potion is a buff potion which grants the Heartreach buff when consumed. The buff increases the pickup range of life recovery Hearts by 15.625 tiles, from 2.625 tiles to a total of 18.25 tiles. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Heartreach Potions can be found in Pots and crates.
Heat Ray: The Heat Ray is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When used, it fires yellow lasers that instantly travel their maximum distance. The lasers do not pierce enemies.
Heavenforge Brick: Heavenforge Brick is a type of decorative brick obtained by throwing Luminite Brick into Shimmer during a Full Moon.
Heavenforge Brick Wall: Heavenforge Brick Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Heavenforge Bricks.
Heavenly Slime: The Heavenly Slime is a Hardmode slime and boss servant that is summoned by Queen Slime alongside Crystal Slimes and Bouncy Slimes. It flies around trying to ram into the player.
Heavy Assembler: The Heavy Assembler is a crafting station used to make various building materials, decorative items, and mechanisms.
Heavy Sling: The Heavy Sling is a Hardmode accessory that has a 19/80 (23.75%) chance of dropping from Ice Mimics. While equipped, it allows the player to pick up a sentry when coming in contact with it, causing the sentry to attach itself to the player and move with them while still performing its usual attacks. The player cannot drop a sentry after picking it up, but can despawn it by using ⚷ Open / Activate on the sentry, by unequipping the Heavy Sling, or by summoning another sentry when not having enough sentry slots. The picked up sentry also still despawns 10 minutes after it has been summoned. The player can only pick up 1 sentry at a time.
Hel-Fire: The Hel-Fire is a Hardmode yoyo that has a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of being dropped by any enemy in or near The Underworld. It inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 3–8 seconds upon hit.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Helium Moss Brick: Helium Moss Brick is a type of brick made from Helium Moss that glows in the dark when placed, and cycles through the colors of the rainbow.
Helium Moss Brick Wall: Helium Moss Brick Wall is a brick background wall that glows in the dark when placed. Just like Helium Moss Bricks and Helium Moss, its glow cycles through the colors of rainbow.
Hell Armored Bones: The Hell Armored Bones is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawn in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. Similar to Angry Bones, they come in multiple varieties and follow the Fighter AI. Hell Armored Bones are visible in darkness but do not actually emit light, except for a faint glow when immersed in water. They also inflict the On Fire! debuff for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds.
Hell Armored Bones spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by tiled walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Hell Butterfly: Butterflies are small critters that can naturally spawn on Surface in Forest and the Hallow, and also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. In both cases, they can only spawn during daytime if wind speed is lower than 20 mph, and if it is not currently raining. There are 8 variants of ordinary Butterflies with different appearences, chosen randomly when they spawn. They can be caught with a Bug Net and carried in the inventory.

When an ordinary Butterfly is being spawned, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance (affected by luck) for it to be replaced by a Gold Butterfly, which can be caught with a Bug Net and crafted into Golden Delight.

The Hell Butterfly (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can naturally spawn in the Underworld during daytime. It can also spawn from shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld, or from destroying wild Ash grass plants. It can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Golden Bug Net (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Attempting to catch it with a standard Bug Net will not work, and the player will take 1 damage and be inflicted with On Fire! for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 12.5 seconds.
All Butterflies can be crafted into butterfly jars, and can be be used as bait for fishing.
Hellbat: The Hellbat is a pre-Hardmode bat enemy that spawns in The Underworld. Although they cannot fly underwater or through lava, they take no damage from making contact with either.
In worlds with Remix active, it drops lava upon death.
Hellfire Arrow: The Hellfire Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow that explodes upon impact, damaging all enemies in a small area.
Hellfire Arrows can be found in Shadow Chests and Pots in The Underworld, crafted at an anvil, or purchased from the Demolitionist for 1 Silver each in Hardmode.
Hellfire Treads: The Hellfire Treads are a pre-Hardmode accessory that combines the effects of the Spectre and Flame Waker Boots. It grants the player the ability to fly and to gain increased movement speed when running continuously, and causes the player's feet to leave trails of fire while moving on blocks, which is a purely visual effect.
Hellforge: The Hellforge is a crafting station that functions as a regular Furnace, with the additional ability of smelting Hellstone into Hellstone Bars. It is also used to craft the essential Adamantite/Titanium Forge in Hardmode. Like its predecessor, it emits light when placed and is not a valid light source for housing.

The Hellforge cannot be crafted, and is instead found in Ruined Houses in the Underworld or obtained from Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates. It can only be collected from the Underworld with tools with at least 65% pickaxe power, i.e. a Deathbringer/Nightmare Pickaxe or better is required. It cannot be broken by explosives during pre-Hardmode.
Hellhound: The Hellhound is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during wave 3 of the Pumpkin Moon event. Hellhounds follow the Unicorn AI and run and leap towards the player to deal contact damage; the player will be barely able to outrun them with boots or similar movement accessories, thus attacking them while out of their reach is important while fighting them.
Defeating a Hellhound during the Pumpkin Moon event will add (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / 10 / 15 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 4 points to the final score.
The Hellhound requires 100 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Hellstone: Hellstone is a pre-Hardmode ore that can be found in The Underworld. Mining it requires at least a Nightmare/Deathbringer Pickaxe, and it cannot be mined with explosives in pre-Hardmode. Hellstone releases a half-tile of lava when mined in The Underworld.
Hellstone inflicts the Burning debuff on players who touch it, which can be negated through items such as the Obsidian Skull and Obsidian Skin Potion.
Hellstone Bar: The Hellstone Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. It is used to craft some of the most powerful equipment available pre-Hardmode, and remains useful, if not necessary, in dealing with the shift in difficulty upon entering Hardmode. Notably, the Molten Pickaxe is the only pre-Hardmode pickaxe capable of mining the first tier of Hardmode ores, Cobalt and Palladium.
Hellstone Brick: Hellstone Bricks are placeable blocks that occur naturally in unique Ruined Houses, though they can also be crafted.

Like plain Hellstone, players without an Obsidian Skull or one of its upgrades in their accessory slot will receive the Burning debuff from making contact with the brick. Mining the block or carrying it in one's inventory incurs no negative effect, however. As with most damaging blocks, NPCs and enemies are immune to this damage.
Unlike Hellstone itself, Hellstone Bricks are always vulnerable to explosions.
Hellstone Brick Wall: The Hellstone Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Ruined Houses in the Underworld, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Hellstone Crate: The Hellstone Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in lava. Opening Hellstone and Obsidian Crates is the only way to obtain the Obsidian Lock Box, and therefore any Underworld-exclusive items normally found in locked Shadow Chests, once the Underworld has been fully looted. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Obsidian Crate.
Hellwing Bow: The Hellwing Bow is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron bow that fires arrows inaccurately. When used, it converts Wooden Arrows into flaming bat projectiles that are unaffected by gravity, can pierce infinitely, and cannot pass through blocks. The Hellwing Bow has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.
Hematic Crate: The Hematic Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be obtained by fishing in The Crimson. Hematic Crates contain items found in standard crates, and additionally always drop an item normally obtained by breaking a Crimson Heart. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Crimson Crate.
Hemogoblin Shark: The Hemogoblin Shark is a Hardmode enemy that can be spawned by fishing in water during a Blood Moon. When the bobber dips and the player attempts to reel in a fish, a Hemogoblin Shark or another enemy has a chance to spawn within a few tiles of the bobber in place of a fish. The Hemogoblin Shark can move extraordinarily fast on land, swim quickly in liquids, jump very high, and fire a barrage of Blood Shot projectiles.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Hemogoblin Shark requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Hemopiranha: Hemopiranha are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in The Crimson in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Rage Potions.
Herb Bag: The Herb Bag is a consumable grab bag item, which when opened with ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory, contains 2–40 herbs and/or herb seeds. Herb Bags can be found in Chests on the surface.

A Herb Bag contains 2–5 stacks of 2–8 items each, determined randomly when opened (see Notes for details). It is possible that some or all stacks are of the same item, in which case the stacks are merged. Therefore, Herb Bags always contain at least one and at most five different items.
Hercules Beetle: The Hercules Beetle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that increases the damage of summon weapons by 15% and increases their knockback by 2. The Hercules Beetle can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 40 Gold if he is spoken to in the Jungle after Plantera has been defeated.
Hermes Boots: The Hermes Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be found in Chests in the Underground and Cavern layers. While equipped, they grant the ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster, and they increase the player's maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second). The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint.
The Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots, and Sailfish Boots (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) have the same functionality, and their effects do not stack with each other.
Hero Shield: The Hero Shield is a Hardmode post-Plantera shield accessory that redirects 25% of damage from players on the same team while above 25% health, similar to the effect of the Paladin's Shield. Furthermore, it increases defense by 10, increases aggro by 400, and grants immunity to knockback.
Hero's set: The Hero's set is a vanity set composed of the Hero's Hat, the Hero's Shirt, and the Hero's Pants. Crafting the entire set requires 420 Cobwebs and 27 Jungle Grass Seeds as base ingredients.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Heroicis' Wings (Inactive): Heroicis' Wings (Inactive) are a crafting material used solely to craft Heroicis' Wings. They can be obtained along with the rest of Heroicis' set by throwing a Platinum Coin into water in an Oasis.
Heroicis' set: Heroicis' set is a set of vanity items consisting of Heroicis' Hat, Heroicis' Coat, and Heroicis' Pants. It is obtained by throwing a Platinum Coin into a pool of water, lava, or honey in a Desert. The coin is destroyed as soon as it is submerged and the set items appear at its location. They float upwards to linger in midair above the surface of the liquid, until a player picks them up.
Heroicis' equipment also includes the following non-vanity item and monolith, which appear with the set:
Heroicis' Wings (Inactive), which can be crafted into Heroicis' Wings
Herpling: The Herpling is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Crimson. It attacks the player by quickly jumping across the ground. While it cannot jump very high, it can cover horizontal distance very quickly, making it a potent threat.
Hexxed Branch: The Hexxed Branch is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Tree Mount, a ground-based mount that is unable to fly. Upon reaching 90% of its full speed, the Tree Mount briefly emits an orange ring and gains a flaming trail, and becomes able to deal 120 base summon damage and knockback of 12 (Insane) to enemies upon contact, which also grants the player 0.1 seconds of Invincibility frames. The Hexxed Branch is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event in Master Mode with a 6.25–25% chance depending on the current wave.
HiTek Sunglasses: The HiTek Sunglasses are a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity item for the social helmet slot. They are similar to the Sunglasses and Goggles, in that they provide eye graphics without concealing the player's hair. HiTek Sunglasses are purchased from the Cyborg for 5 Gold, after the Martian Madness event has been defeated.
High Test Fishing Line: The High Test Fishing Line is an accessory that prevents fishing line from breaking while fishing when equipped. Without the High Test Fishing Line equipped, there is a 1/7 (14.29%) chance that the line will break on any reel-in that was supposed to yield a catch. The High Test Fishing Line can be acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details).

The Angler will not give the player a High Test Fishing Line as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.
High Velocity Bullet: The High Velocity Bullet is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss bullet. It is the bullet with the highest velocity. The High Velocity Bullet can hit up to 3 targets. The damage of the High Velocity Bullet decreases by 15% each time it hits a target.

High Velocity Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 High Velocity Bullets is 9 Silver 50 Copper, which is 19 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 High Velocity Bullets is 19 Gold.
Hive: Hive is a block type that Bee Hives are made from. Upon mining it may either turn into liquid honey, spawn in a Bee, or simply drop like a regular item. Hive blocks can also be acquired by dropping Honey Blocks or Crispy Honey Blocks into Shimmer.
Hive blocks can only be placed using a Hive Wand, consuming Hive blocks from the player's inventory.

While using the Hive block directly, there is a 1/30 (3.33%) chance per tick (average of once every 0.5 seconds) to release a bee projectile that chases enemies, without consuming the item. The bee projectile deals 5 base damage and is considered a melee projectile, meaning it can critically strike using the player's melee critical strike chance, and benefit from melee effects such as Flasks, Magma Stone, Frost armor's set bonus, and Sharpening Station, but does not have its damage boosted by the player's melee damage bonuses.
Hive blocks can be converted into Honey Blocks when used on an Extractinator.
Hive Pack: The Hive Pack is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from the Queen Bee's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While equipped, it grants a 1/2 (50%) chance of replacing friendly Bee projectiles with stronger Giant Bees.
Hive Wall: The Hive Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Bee Hives, considered unsafe. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player. Unlike Hive blocks, it does not need a Hive Wand to be placed.
Hive-Five: The Hive-Five is a pre-Hardmode yoyo. Upon enemy hits, it has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of summoning a homing Bee projectile. The Bee projectile deals 50% of the weapon's damage (12 base damage), has a 1/2 (50%) chance to deal 1 extra damage, can pierce enemies or bounce off blocks up to 3 times, and lasts for 10 seconds.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Holly: The Holly is a decorative item resembling an Advent wreath, a typical Christmas ornament. It can be placed on a background wall, similar to paintings. It is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 9.001% in pre-Hardmode and 8.401% in Hardmode.
Holy Arrow: The Holy Arrow is a Hardmode arrow. Upon contact with enemies or blocks, two Hallow Star projectiles will fall from the sky to the impact location. The stars deal 1/3 (33.33%) of the combined damage of the arrow and weapon, and do not pierce.
Honey Balloon: The Honey Balloon is an accessory that combines the functions of a Shiny Red Balloon and a Honey Comb. It boosts jump height by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's jump height to ~10½ blocks (~75% increase), while oddly reducing it when underwater, from 8 blocks-to 7 blocks, and releases a small swarm of angry bees when the player is hurt, which seek out and deal small amounts of damage to enemies. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it also grants the Honey buff after being damaged.
Honey Block: Honey Blocks are blocks formed when water comes into contact with honey. When placed, they slow the movement of any player walking on them. Vertically, a player can slowly slide down them (even without having the Climbing Claws or Shoe Spikes equipped). They also greatly reduce jump height to one tile, or 3 tiles with the Shiny Red Balloon equipped. NPCs, critters, and enemies are not affected.
Honey Comb: The Honey Comb is a pre-Hardmode accessory which has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by the Queen Bee. When equipped, it spawns 1–4 Bee projectiles which attack nearby enemies each time the player takes damage, and grants the Honey buff for 5 seconds after being damaged.
Honey Dispenser: The Honey Dispenser is a crafting station used to craft Honey furniture out of Honey Blocks. The Honey Dispenser has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Ivy Chests in the Underground Jungle. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can also be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold in the Jungle.
Honeyed Goggles: The Honeyed Goggles is a pre-Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Bee Mount which grants limited flight. The Honeyed Goggles have a 1/20 (5%) / 11/100 (11%) chance of being dropped from the Queen Bee.

While the Bee Mount is slow on the ground, it is capable of flying and will greatly increase in speed while doing so. While flying, the player's vertical speed is kept constant. The Bee Mount can fly in the air for 10.66 seconds before it enters a "tired" state, during which it slows and glides down. The glide can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Afterwards, it requires a 3-second rest period on the ground in order to begin flying at full speed again. If the player takes off again immediately after landing an exhausted bee, it will fly, but much slower than usual. Its rest period is indicated by a "heavy breathing" animation that stops when the Bee Mount has fully recovered.
Honeyfall Block: The Honeyfall Block is a block which shows an animated texture of flowing honey.
Honeyfall Wall: The Honeyfall Wall is one of only a few animated background wall types. It depicts flowing honey.
Honeyfin: The Honeyfin is a pre-Hardmode fish and recovery potion that restores 120 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. It can also be used to craft Seafood Dinner.
Honeyfin can only be caught from honey, e.g. in Bee Hives within the Underground Jungle. They are the only non-quest fish that can be caught in honey.
Hook: The Hook is a crafting material used solely to craft the Grappling Hook. It has a 1/25 (4%) chance to drop from Skeletons, Undead Miners, Hoplites, and Undead Vikings in the Marble Caves, Ice biome, and Cavern layer. It also has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to drop from Piranhas in the Jungle, Underground Jungle, Cavern, and Underground layer.
Hook of Dissonance: The Hook of Dissonance is a Hardmode grappling hook that fires a single hook that reaches 30 tiles; when the hook attaches to a block, it will instantly teleport the user to the hook's position if the path to the hook is wide enough to fit a player. The Hook of Dissonance has a 1/3 (33.33%) / 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime.
Hooks: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below).

The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify

Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite.
All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.
Hoplite: The Hoplite is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in Marble Caves. It throws piercing Javelins at the player, which deals immense damage, especially in Expert Mode or Master Mode. The Javelins they throw are also fairly accurate and are more likely to hit the player than most other enemy-fired projectiles. This makes the Hoplite an enemy to avoid early on in the game until players are properly equipped and ready to face them.
Hoppin' Jack: The Hoppin' Jack is a Hardmode enemy that will only appear at night during the Halloween seasonal event, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or in Graveyards (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) at any time of year. He attacks by hopping towards the player in a manner identical to most slimes. The Hoppin' Jack becomes significantly quicker after he loses any health.

Notably, despite using the Slime AI, he is not treated as a slime for most other purposes. Hoppin' Jack drops no Gel on death, will still attack the player even if they have the Royal Gel equipped, and killing one is not necessary to earn the Gelatin World Tour ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) or Slimer/King of Slimes achievements.
Hornet: The Hornet is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy found in the Underground Jungle. They follow the Flying AI, floating just out of reach and then charging the player, while also firing stinger projectiles (at an increased rate in Expert Mode). The stingers cannot be destroyed with weapons and travel at about the same speed as the darts from a Dart Trap. Stingers have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff on the player for 10 seconds. In Expert Mode, the chance is 1/3 (33.33%) for 20 seconds and 2/3 (66.67%) for 2–10 seconds.
Hornet Staff: The Hornet Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Hornet minion. It hovers above enemies, firing stingers that inflict the Poisoned debuff for 4–7 seconds and do not pierce.
Hotdog: The Hotdog is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 12 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Hotdog has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Bone Serpents and Red Devils.
Houndius Shootius: The Houndius Shootius is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons the Houndius Shootius sentry. It shoots fireballs towards enemies, which dissipate upon contact with enemies or blocks. The Houndius Shootius has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops.
Hoverboard: The Hoverboard is a Hardmode wing-type accessory. It functions like a regular pair of wings, but with the added ability to hover by holding ↷ Jump and ▼ Down.
The Hoverboard has a flight height of 94 tiles, and a hover speed of 52 mph.
Huge Dragon Egg: The Huge Dragon Egg is a consumable grab bag item, which can be opened with ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory and contains either a Chillet or Chillet Ignis. It is rarely found placed in the Cavern layer.
Hunter Cloak: The Hunter Cloak is a vanity item sold by the Clothier for 15 Gold when the player has an accumulated golf score of 2000 or more. It is also occasionally sold by the Traveling Merchant, regardless of golf scores.
The Hunter Cloak cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Hunter Potion: The Hunter Potion is a buff potion which grants the Hunter buff when consumed. The buff shows the location of enemies, critters, and NPCs on the screen by highlighting them in red (enemies) or green (critters and NPCs). Although these affected entities glow, they do not emit any light to the surrounding area. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Hunter Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and Crates.
Huntress armor: Huntress armor is a Hardmode ranged/summoner armor set consisting of the Huntress's Wig, Huntress's Jerkin, and Huntress's Pants. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 45 Defender Medals after defeating any mechanical boss.
The Red Riding armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Huntress armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Explosive Trap sentry summons have increased fire rate and inflict the Oiled debuff, which causes enemies to take extra damage while afflicted with a fire debuff.
Huntress's Buckler: The Huntress's Buckler is a Hardmode shield accessory that increases the player's sentry slots by one and increases summon damage by 10%. The Huntress's Buckler is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event with a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/12 (8.33%) chance during Tier 3.
Ice Bat: The Ice Bat is a pre-Hardmode bat enemy that spawns in the Ice biome. It inflicts the Chilled debuff and, more rarely, the Frozen debuff. Additionally, it emits a very faint glow.
Ice Blade: The Ice Blade is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that is found in Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, Frozen Crates, and Boreal Crates. When swung, it occasionally fires an Ice Bolt projectile that deals the weapon's damage and does not pass through blocks or pierce enemies. The Ice Blade also has a base 6% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.
Ice Blocks: Ice Blocks are a common block type found alongside Snow Blocks in the Snow and Ice biomes. They can be mined with a pickaxe or drill. Ice Blocks have low friction, causing a player walking over them to slide when stopping or changing directions. This effect can be mitigated by equipping Ice Skates or other accessories crafted from them.
Ice Blocks can be converted into three other variants via the spread of biomes:
Corruption spreads onto Ice to create Purple Ice Blocks
Crimson spreads onto Ice to create Red Ice Blocks
Hallow spreads onto Ice to create Pink Ice Blocks
These will also spread their respective biomes.
Ice Boomerang: The Ice Boomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that has a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen and Boreal Crates. It can also inflict the Frostburn debuff for 3 seconds, and also has a base 6% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Ice Bow: The Ice Bow is a Hardmode bow that has a 19/80 (23.75%) chance of being dropped by Ice Mimics. When used, it converts any type of arrow into high-velocity Frost Arrows. Unlike the Frostburn Arrow item, they do not inflict the Frostburn debuff.
Ice Brick: The Ice Brick is a brick type made from Ice Blocks. It does not have the sliding properties of ice, nor does it cause snow to fall like Snow Bricks.
Ice Brick Wall: Ice Brick Wall is a type of Wall that is made using Ice Bricks.
Ice Cream: Ice Cream is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 14 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Ice Cream has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Ice Bats, Ice Slimes, and Spiked Ice Slimes.
Ice Elemental: The Ice Elemental is a Hardmode enemy that appears in the Snow biome at night and in the Ice biome at any time. The Ice Elemental slowly hovers towards the player and shoots Frost Blasts which, on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Frostburn debuff for 6 / 12 / 15 seconds.
Ice Feather: The Ice Feather is a Hardmode crafting material used solely to craft Frozen Wings. The Ice Feather has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Ice Golems during a Blizzard in the Snow biome.
Ice Golem: The Ice Golem is a rare Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Snow biome during Blizzards. The Ice Golem walks slowly, and, when it has a clear line of sight with the player, fires high-velocity Frost Beam projectiles that chill and occasionally freeze them in place. Its movement speed and the rate at which it fires beams increase exponentially the further its health is depleted. It has a guaranteed chance to drop a Frost Core, the main ingredient for the Frost armor, Cool Whip, and Blizzard in a Bottle.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Ice Golem requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Ice Machine: The Ice Machine is a crafting station used to craft Frozen furniture out of Ice Blocks and Snow furniture out of Snow Blocks. The Ice Machine has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Frozen Chests in the Ice biome. On Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can also be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold while in the Snow biome.
Ice Mimic: Mimics are rare Hardmode enemies disguised as Chests, appearing as the appropriate chest type for the environment.
Mimics can be spawned by the player using the Chest Statue, even in pre-Hardmode. However, Mimics spawned this way only drop the Mimic Banner.
Rarer Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics can also be spawned manually by players via a Key of Light or Key of Night (see the Biome Mimic section below).

They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics require 25 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Ice Queen: The Ice Queen is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Frost Moon event. She is the event's final enemy and can move freely through blocks. She is the equivalent to the Pumpking from the Pumpkin Moon, being the Frost Moon's most powerful enemy, coming in at the last waves of the event, and being the event's only flying boss.
Defeating the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event will add 150 / 300 / 375 points to the final score, giving the most number of points for any enemy in the event.
Ice Rod: The Ice Rod is a Hardmode magic weapon that autofires blocks of ice, which have the unique ability of placing solid, temporary Ice Blocks at the location of the cursor and which last for 15 seconds before shattering. These Ice Blocks are translucent, cast a dim, flickering blue light, and are slippery like normal Ice Blocks. The Ice Rod can be purchased from the Wizard for 50 Gold.

The location of the cursor must be unoccupied in order to form an Ice Block. If the tile is occupied either by blocks or background objects, the fired Ice Block acts as an ordinary projectile, flying in a straight line and unaffected by gravity, and shatters when it hits an enemy or other foreground objects. If the cursor is on an existing Ice Block from a previous casting, it will cause the next projectile to pass through the existing Ice Block.
Ice Sickle: The Ice Sickle is a Hardmode broadsword that can be dropped with a 1/100 (1%) chance by Armored Vikings, Ice Elementals, Ice Tortoises, and Icy Mermen. When swung, it fires a spinning blue sickle projectile that deals 67% of the weapon's damage (33 base damage) and can pierce up to 4 enemies. The sickle gradually slows down after being fired, dissipating after traveling for 3 seconds.
Ice Skates: Ice Skates are a pre-Hardmode accessory that improves a player's movement control on Thin Ice, all Ice Blocks, Ice Rod blocks, Frozen Slime Blocks and Aetherium Blocks. The player accelerates faster, slides shorter distances, and will no longer cause Thin Ice to break when landing from falls or jumps. Ice Skates have a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Boreal Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Ice Slime: The Ice Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Snow biome during the daytime. Upon contact with the player, it has a chance to inflict the Chilled debuff, if the player is not already inflicted with the Frozen debuff.
Like most other slimes, the Ice Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Ice Tortoise: The Ice Tortoise is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Ice biome. It walks around slowly, and occasionally retracts into its shell. It then starts spinning and hurls itself at the player, gaining increased defense and dealing high contact damage.
A functionally identical variant of the Ice Tortoise, the Giant Tortoise, can be encountered in the Jungle and Underground Jungle.
Ice Wall: The Ice Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Ice biome, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Ichor: Ichor is a Hardmode crafting material dropped by Ichor Stickers in the Underground Crimson and the Tainted Ghoul in the Crimson Underground Desert. It is also obtained from Hematic Crates. It is used to craft many Ichor-related items. It is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Flame.
Ichor Arrow: The Ichor Arrow is a Hardmode arrow. It inflicts the Ichor debuff for 10 seconds upon contact with enemies.
Its Corruption counterpart is the Cursed Arrow.
Ichor Bullet: The Ichor Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It inflicts the Ichor debuff on hit for 10 seconds (15 seconds in PvP), decreasing the enemy's defense by 15. Combined with the bullet's base damage, it effectively deals a total of 21 damage.
Its Corruption counterpart is the Cursed Bullet.
Ichor Dart: The Ichor Dart is a Hardmode dart. It can pierce infinitely when initially fired. After traveling for a random duration between 0.1 seconds to 0.5 seconds, the Ichor Dart splits into 3–5 non-piercing darts (average of 3.75 darts). Ichor Darts inflict the Ichor debuff for 7–14 seconds.
They are the Crimson's counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Darts.
Ichor Sticker: The Ichor Sticker is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Underground Crimson and floats around in the air. When tracking the player, it spits a stream of Ichor at them, similar to that of the Golden Shower. The stream inflicts the Ichor debuff for 15 / 30 / 37.5 seconds, lowering the player's defense by (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 15 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 20. Upon death, Ichor Stickers will also drop Ichor.
Icy Merman: The Icy Merman is a Hardmode enemy found in the Ice biome. Upon gaining line of sight of the player, it will stop in place and begin firing Icewater Spit projectiles similar to those fired by the Frost Staff, but with less frequency. Its projectiles also behave similarly to those of the Ice Elemental, but deal less damage and are fired more rapidly. The Icewater Spit attack always inflicts the Chilled debuff, and has a 1/10 (10%) chance to inflict Frozen.
Illegal Gun Parts: Illegal Gun Parts are a crafting material used to craft the Sandgun, the Megashark, and the Flamethrower. They are sold by the Arms Dealer for 20 Gold at night.
Illuminant Bat: The Illuminant Bat is a Hardmode bat enemy that only spawns in the Underground Hallow. It is the Hallowed version of the Giant Bat, but is much stronger and emits a blurred, after-image effect.
Illuminant Slime: The Illuminant Slime is a Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Underground Hallow, replacing normal cave slimes (Black and Mother Slimes) in most cases. Compared to its pre-Hardmode counterparts, it deals much more damage and has more health. The Illuminant Slime gives off a small amount of light and leaves an after-image (like the Chaos Elemental and Illuminant Bat), which appears as a long, pink trail.
Like most other slimes, the Illuminant Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Imbuing Station: The Imbuing Station is a crafting station used to craft flasks. It is purchased from the Witch Doctor for 7 Gold.
Imp Staff: The Imp Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Flying Imp minion. It hovers near enemies, shooting fireballs that inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3–6 seconds and can pierce up to 4 times, dissipating on the 5th hit.
Infernal Wisp Dye: Infernal Wisp Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye obtained by turning in Strange Plants to the Dye Trader. Any equipment it is applied to is colored bright orange, while also emitting an orange glow.
Inferno Fork: The Inferno Fork is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that has a 1/20 (5%) / 39/400 (9.75%) chance of being dropped by Diabolists in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires a fireball that causes a lingering explosion upon contact with an enemy or a block. The explosion hits repeatedly, dealing 75% of the weapon's damage (52 base damage). The fireball and the explosion also inflict the Hellfire debuff for 8–15 seconds.
Inferno Potion: The Inferno Potion is a buff potion that grants the Inferno buff when consumed. The buff casts a spinning ring of fire around the player that deals 20 damage per second and inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 2 seconds to all enemies inside of it while also giving off light. Critters and other passive NPCs are unaffected. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Inferno Potions can be found in Shadow Chests.
Influx Waver: The Influx Waver is a Hardmode, post-Golem broadsword that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. When swung, it fires a blue sword projectile. Upon contact with enemies, the sword projectile will teleport onto nearby enemies two times, hitting three times in total.
Infused Fertilizer: The Infused Fertilizer is a consumable item which immediately grows a sapling or gemcorn into extra-tall versions of their respective trees, similar to the Fertilizer. It is obtained by throwing Fertilizer into Shimmer.

Similar to Fertilizer, for Infused Fertilizer to work, the sapling must fulfill the growing requirements (besides the restrictions related to background walls behind the sapling, which will be ignored), but needs higher vertical clearance, unlike Fertilizer: 29–40 tiles for Mahogany trees, 35–39 tiles for Palm trees, 26–31 tiles for gem trees, and 24–35 tiles for all other types of trees. Saplings that do not fulfill the growing requirements will not sprout into trees but still consume the Infused Fertilizer.
Inner Tube: The Inner Tube is an accessory that has a 9/40 (22.5%) chance of being found in Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates. When equipped, it causes the player to float on the surface of liquids instead of sinking to the bottom and gives +5 Fishing Power. This effect can be temporarily negated by holding ▼ Down. Additionally, when the player is in any liquid, the Inner Tube also grants the player the Flipper's effect (press ↷ Jump to swim upwards).
Invisibility Potion: The Invisibility Potion is a buff potion that grants the Invisibility buff when consumed. This lasts for 3 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The buff is furthermore immediately canceled if the player takes damage of any kind.
The buff provides the following effects:
The player becomes invisible, including their armor, vanity items, and mount.
−17% enemy spawn rates and −20% maximum enemy spawn count.

−750 aggro, meaning enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details). This does not prevent enemies from firing projectiles at the player.
Attacking or using any item will cause the player to reappear temporarily and reduce the aggro reduction bonus to –250.
In addition to being crafted, Invisibility Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.
Iridescent Brick: Iridescent Brick is a cheap brick. It can be mined with any pickaxe or drill. It and its walls can either be crafted, or collected from Jungle Shrines in the Underground Jungle.
Iridescent Brick Wall: The Iridescent Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.
Iridescent Brick Walls reflect the color of the light that they are lit with.
Iron Axe: The Iron Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe. In Journey Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the Iron Axe replaces the Copper Axe for newly created characters.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Axe.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Iron Bar: The Iron Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Bar.
Newly created characters in Journey Mode will always spawn with the Iron Shortsword, Iron Pickaxe, and Iron Axe, regardless of whether the world generated with Iron or Lead.
Iron Bow: The Iron Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Iron Brick: Iron Brick is a type of Brick crafted from Iron Ore.
Iron Brick Wall: Iron Brick Wall is a type of background wall.
Iron Broadsword: The Iron Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Iron Shortsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Broadsword.
Iron Crate: The Iron Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. It is the middle tier of standard crate. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Mythril Crate.
Iron Hammer: The Iron Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Newly created characters spawn with an Iron Hammer in Journey Mode.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Hammer.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Iron Ore: Iron Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on the surface. Iron Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes. It can be obtained from all types of crates.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Lead Ore.
Iron Pickaxe: The Iron Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks weaker than Meteorite. In Journey Mode, the Iron Pickaxe replaces the Copper Pickaxe for newly created characters.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Pickaxe. The Iron Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Iron Shortsword: The Iron Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Iron Broadsword. In Journey Mode, the Iron Shortsword replaces the Copper Shortsword for newly created characters.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Shortsword.
Iron armor: Iron armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Iron Helmet, Iron Chainmail, and Iron Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Iron Bars (180 Iron Ore). The full set grants 9 defense while equipped.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Lead armor.

The Ancient Iron Helmet is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Iron Helmet. The Ancient Iron Helmet has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons, and can also be obtained by dropping an Iron Helmet into Shimmer. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Iron Helmet prior to 1.0.3.
Ironskin Potion: The Ironskin Potion is a buff potion that grants the Ironskin buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's defense by 8, thus reducing damage by 4 / 6 / 8. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Ironskin Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Item Flask: The Item Flask is a furniture item that can be hung from the underside of blocks or placed on platforms. It has three different sprites which can be cycled through with the ▲ Up and ▼ Down keys before placing it. Once placed, pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on it while holding any item places and displays that item in the Item Flask. Hitting the Item Flask with a pickaxe or drill, or pressing ⚷ Open / Activate again will retrieve the item.
The color of the liquid of the Item Flask corresponds to the rarity color (e.g. or) of the item placed in the Item Flask.
Item Frame: The Item Frame is a furniture item that can be placed on a 2×2 area of background wall, placed on or hung from blocks, or placed on top of platforms. Once an Item Frame is placed, pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on it while holding any item places and displays that item in the Item Frame. Hitting the Item Frame with a pickaxe or drill, or pressing ⚷ Open / Activate again will retrieve the item.
Ivy: The Ivy is a novelty instrument. It will always drop from the Steampunker, but only when her name is Whitney. When used, the player strums a chord depending on how far the cursor is from the player.
Ivy Chest: The Ivy Chest is a chest storage item found only in Jungle Shrines and Living Mahogany Trees in the Underground Jungle.
Jack 'O Lantern: The Jack 'O Lantern is a placeable furniture item that gives off light. It can have different faces when placed.
Jack 'O Lantern Launcher: The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that consumes Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns as ammunition. Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns bounce off blocks before exploding upon contact with an enemy or after 5 seconds. The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher has a base 10% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.

The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is always accompanied by 25 to 50 Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns. Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns can also be bought from the Arms Dealer for 15 Copper each if the Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is in the player's inventory.
Jack 'O Lantern Mask: The Jack 'O Lantern Mask is a vanity item for the helmet slot. It is dropped by Headless Horsemen during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 0.71%–5% (1.25%–5%) chance depending on the current wave.
Javelin: The Javelin is a consumable ranged weapon that are dropped by Hoplites, which have a 1/2 (50%) chance to drop 40–80 Javelins. When used, it flies straight for approximately 36 tiles before dropping abruptly. It can hit up to 3 targets.
Jellyfish (bait): Jellyfish are a type of bait which are found rarely by fishing. Each has a bait power of 20%.
The Blue Jellyfish bait item is caught by fishing in Underground or Cavern water bodies.

The Green Jellyfish bait item is caught under the same conditions as Blue Jellyfish, but requires Hardmode. Once Hardmode is activated, there is a 1/2 (50%) chance that a Jellyfish bait item caught in the Underground or below will be Green (likewise for Blue).
The Pink Jellyfish bait item is caught by fishing in an Ocean biome.
Unlike critter bait items, Jellyfish bait items are not caught using the Bug Net. Jellyfish bait items are separate and unrelated to Jellyfish enemies.
Jellyfish Block: Jellyfish Blocks are Hardmode blocks purchased from the Pirate in a Graveyard for 2 Silver each. Their main use is crafting Jellyfish furniture and Jellyfish Walls. They glow in the dark when placed.
Jellyfish Diving Gear: Jellyfish Diving Gear is an accessory crafted by combining Jellyfish Necklace and Diving Gear at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It combines the functionalities of its ingredients:
The player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly.
The player's breath meter will deplete much slower, and the rate at which drowning damage is taken is slowed.
The player emit light when submerged in water and honey, and emits very faint light out of water and honey.
Jellyfish Necklace: The Jellyfish Necklace is an accessory which has a 1/100 (1%) chance to drop from Pink, Blue, or Green Jellyfish in the Ocean and Underground or Cavern layer. In the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, the Jellyfish Necklace provides a faint pink glow when the player is submerged in water or honey. In the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, this glow is also provided out of liquids and its brightness is significantly increased when submerged.
Jellyfish Wall: Jellyfish Wall is a Hardmode wall. As with most crafted walls, Jellyfish Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning. They glow in the dark when placed like the Jellyfish Blocks that it is made from.
Jellyfish jars: Jellyfish jars are animated decorative furniture items. The Jellyfish needed to craft these decorations are bait items obtained by fishing, not by killing the actual Jellyfish enemies. By throwing a jellyfish jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the jellyfish as an item.

Jellyfish jars can be placed on top of solid blocks and platforms, and give off a faint light. They function as valid light sources for houses and illuminate underwater, but are not controllable mechanisms like some other light sources.
Jester's Arrow: The Jester's Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It is unaffected by gravity and can pierce an infinite number of enemies, and its damage decreases by 10% per each enemy pierced.
In addition to being crafted, Jester's Arrows can be found in Gold Chests in the Cavern layer.
Jetpack: The Jetpack is a Hardmode wing-type accessory obtainable after defeating any mechanical boss. Like all wings, it grants the player the ability to fly and glide when equipped, as well as not take fall damage. At top speed, it allows traveling at 33 mph horizontally and 38 mph vertically. It has a flight time of 2.5 seconds and a vertical speed multiplier of 150%.

Additionally, the Jetpack have a unique ability to upwards boost by holding the ▲ Up key when flying, increasing the top vertical speed to 77 mph. However, the flight time is consumed at double the normal rate when the boost is activated.
Jewel of Light: The Jewel of Light is a Hardmode, post-Plantera light pet-summoning item that spawns a Fairy Princess that provides pink-colored light. It is fast and will always position itself slightly elevated behind the player. The Jewel of Light has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light in Master Mode. While equipped, not only does the pet produce light, but the player as well.
Jim's Cap: Jim's Cap is an vanity item. It will always drop from the Painter, but only when his name is Jim.
Jim's set: Jim's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Jimmarn, an artist who develops graphics for Terraria. Equipping the full set produces a glow effect similar to Spooky armor and grants an after-image movement effect similar to Ninja armor.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Jimmarn's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Joja Cola: The Joja Cola is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 2 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. It has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being fished up instead of a junk item when fishing.

When talking to the Dryad and holding a Joja Cola, the Dryad's “Status” option will be replaced by “Purify”. Upon selecting this option, the Dryad will summon a star-shaped portal with a Junimo pet jumping out of it after a brief delay. The pet will pull a Stardrop from the ground and then vanish, dropping the item for the player to collect. This process can be repeated an unlimited number of times.
Jousting Lance: The Jousting Lance is a Hardmode melee weapon purchased from the Zoologist for 6 Gold after filling out 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary. When attacking using ⚒ Use / Attack, the lance will extend, and holding ⚒ Use / Attack will keep it extended at a fixed angle. The damage and knockback will increase depending on the player's movement speed, making mounts, sprinting accessories, or dash abilities (such as those granted by Shield of Cthulhu, Tabi/Master Ninja Gear, or Solar Flare armor) useful for maximizing damage. When the player takes damage, the Jousting Lance will stop being active.
It is the precursor to the Hallowed and Shadow Jousting Lances.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Junction Box: The Junction Box is a mechanism that allows wires of the same color to cross without connecting. It is purchased from the Mechanic for 2 Silver. The Junction Box can be placed in midair, without the need for support. Hammering the Junction Box changes the directions that the different colored wires enter and exit the Junction Box.
Jungle Bat: The Jungle Bat is a common pre-Hardmode bat enemy that spawns in the Jungle and less commonly in the Underground Jungle. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree at night. In Expert Mode, it can inflict the Feral Bite debuff. Like most other bats, it cannot enter water.
Jungle Crate: The Jungle Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Jungle. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally found in Ivy Chests within Jungle Shrines or Living Mahogany Trees. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Bramble Crate.
Jungle Creeper: The Jungle Creeper is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Underground Jungle. Like other spiders, it can climb on background walls.

On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it has a 1/10 (10%) chance to inflict the Acid Venom debuff for 4 / 8 / 10 seconds. Additionally in Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), it gains a special spit attack that inflicts the Webbed debuff for 0.5–2.5 seconds.
Jungle Grass Seeds: Jungle Grass Seeds are seeds used to plant Jungle grass in Mud Blocks, which can potentially create an artificial Jungle or Underground Jungle (depending on depth) if enough Jungle grass and plants are created. Jungle Grass Seeds can be found by cutting down plants growing on Jungle grass using virtually any tool or weapon. They can also be obtained from putting Poo into an Extractinator, with an 0.67% chance per item.
Jungle Juice: Jungle Juice is a Hardmode recovery potion that restores 180 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced by the Philosopher's Stone or its upgrades.
It is the fourth tier of healing potion, succeeding the Greater Healing Potion and preceding the Super Healing Potion.
Jungle Rose: The Jungle Rose is a vanity accessory which can be harvested from the floor of the Jungle and Underground Jungle. Certain small red flowers growing on Jungle grass have a 1/20 (5%) chance to drop the item when cut.
The Jungle Rose cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Jungle Slime: The Jungle Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that only spawns in the Jungle during the daytime. They have relatively high damage and health compared to most other slimes in the early game.
Notably, Jungle Slimes drop a much larger amount of coins than any common slime prior to Hardmode.
Like most other slimes, the Jungle Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
On Desktop, Console, Mobile, and 3DS, they can rarely be found carrying bonus drops, which the player receives upon the slime's death.
Jungle Spores: Jungle Spores are crafting materials acquired by destroying green glowing orbs that grow randomly on Jungle grass in the Underground Jungle, in or below the Cavern layer. Each orb drops 2–3 Jungle Spores. Harvested Jungle Spores cannot be replanted.
Crafting all items requires a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 122 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 62 Jungle Spores.
Jungle Turtle: The Jungle Turtle is a harmless critter that spawns in or near a body of water on the surface Jungle at any time. Like its Forest counterpart, it moves slowly on land and swims at the surface of water. The Jungle Turtle has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Jungle Turtle can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Jungle Turtle Cage). Once crafted, the Jungle Turtle cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Jungle Turtle can be spawned by the Turtle Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Jungle Wall: The Jungle Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Jungle, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained by purchasing it from the Dryad for 10 Copper each, in Hardmode. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Jungle Walls (natural): The Lichen Stone Wall, Leafy Jungle Wall, Ivy Stone Wall, and Jungle Vine Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Jungle, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on the Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
Jungle armor: Jungle armor is a pre-Hardmode mage armor set consisting of the Jungle Shirt, Jungle Hat, and Jungle Pants. Crafting a full set requires a total of 32 Jungle Spores, 2 Vines, and 10 Stingers.
Jungle armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Cobalt armor pieces, still providing the set bonus but not the grass particle effect.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
The player also emits visual grass particles while moving.
Junk: Junk items are fished instead of regular fishing catches when the player's fishing conditions are particularly unfavorable. Their only use is being converted by the Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to obtain low-level bait. There are three different junk items, all of which are functionally identical: Old Shoe, Seaweed, and Tin Can.
Junk items can only be caught if both of the following conditions are met:
The lake is smaller than 300 tiles (water) or 200 tiles (honey).
This requirement decreases at higher altitudes, reaching a minimum of 75 tiles (50 for honey)
The player's Fishing Power is lower than 50.

If either condition is not met (i.e., the lake size or the player's Fishing Power is high enough), then regular fishing catches are caught instead of junk items. If both conditions are met, the chances to fish a junk item are very high (except during a Blood Moon, during which enemies will commonly be caught instead of other drops).
There is a 1/8 (12.5%) chance for a Joja Cola to be fished up in place of a junk item.
KO Cannon: The KO Cannon is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Clowns. When used, it fires a boxing glove attached to the player via a chain. The glove retracts on contact with blocks or enemies, or after traveling 12 tiles.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Kaleidoscope: The Kaleidoscope is a Hardmode, post-Plantera whip that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light. It has a 20% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
Karate Tortoise set: The Karate Tortoise set is a vanity set that can be obtained from Goodie Bags during Halloween, with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance. It consists of a Karate Tortoise Mask, Karate Tortoise Shirt and Karate Tortoise Pants. Its male and female variants look identical.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Katana: The Katana is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold. The Katana has a base 19% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Kazzymodus' set: Kazzymodus' set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Kazzymodus, who is in charge of quality assurance at Re-Logic.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Kazzymodus' equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Keg: The Keg is a crafting station used solely to brew Ale. In addition to being crafted, it can sometimes be found in Underground Cabins.
Key of Light: The Key of Light is a craftable item which spawns a Hallowed Mimic when placed in any slot of any empty Chest. The world must be in Hardmode and the only item inside the Chest must be a single Key of Light.
The Hallowed Mimic is spawned as soon as the Chest is closed, consuming both the Key of Light and the Chest.
Key of Night: The Key of Night is a craftable item that spawns a Corrupt Mimic or a Crimson Mimic when placed in any slot of any empty Chest, depending on whether the world generated with The Corruption or The Crimson, respectively. The world must be in Hardmode and the only item inside the Chest must be a single Key of Night.
The Corrupt/Crimson Mimic is spawned as soon as the Chest is closed, consuming both the Key of Night and the Chest.
