Keybrand: The Keybrand is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that has a 1/200 (0.5%) / 399/40,000 (0.9975%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Hell Armored Bones, and Rusty Armored Bones in the Hardmode Dungeon. It deals increased damage against enemies depending on their missing health, up to a maximum of 200% damage against enemies that have less than 10% health remaining. The Keybrand also has a 20% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapon, causing it to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds, or touching any solid block, then embed itself in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches it. It can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. It can also be recalled mid-throw.
Killing Deck: The Killing Deck is a Hardmode magic weapon that can be purchased from the Wizard for 20 Gold during a Blood Moon. It launches Killing Card projectiles that fly for 0.5 seconds in a serpentine pattern before abruptly falling. They stick to any block or enemy they hit, but stop dealing damage after becoming stuck, and return to the player 5 seconds after the impact. While returning, the cards fly in a straight line and can travel through blocks, deal 150% of the weapon's damage (33 base damage), and pierce infinitely.
The Killing Deck cycles through four attacks, advancing to the next one on each use of the weapon:
Launches a single Killing Card projectile in the direction of the cursor.
Launches one Killing Card in the direction of the cursor and another one in the opposite direction.
Launches a spread of six Killing Cards.
Recalls all Killing Cards immediately, causing them to return to the player early. If no cards are out anymore when this attack is used, then it is skipped and the first attack is used again instead.
Kimono: The Kimono is a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Gold.
King Slime: King Slime is a pre-Hardmode boss. Fighting King Slime is not required for game progression, but his defeat may reward the player with useful items. Defeating him for the first time also causes the Nerdy Slime town pet to spawn from the boss.
While King Slime is alive, his exclusive music King Slime will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Kinship Peach: The Kinship Peach is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss crafting material, which is notably crafted using Life Fruit. It is used to upgrade Cattiva and Foxparks to their "trusty" variants.
Kites: Kites are miscellaneous items that can be held by the player. A kite can be flown during Windy Days or if the player runs fast enough while holding it. It can be raised higher with ⚒ Use / Attack and lowered with ⚷ Open / Activate. Lowering a kite back to the player will make them put it away. As long as the kite is above the player's head, the player will get the High Spirits buff which will increase in duration until it maxes out at 12 minutes and 1 second. The buff has the following effects:
+15% placement speed when placing blocks and walls
Up to +0.1 luck, depending on the remaining buff duration:
+0.067 with less than 9 minutes but at least 6 minutes remaining
+0.033 with less than 6 minutes but at least 3 minutes remaining

A kite can be placed on the ground from the hotbar with ⚷ Open / Activate if the player is not currently flying the kite. The kite initially has some upwards momentum that carries it several blocks above the stake into the air, even on a calm day.
Kobold: The Kobold is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Old One's Army event. It spawns during Tier 2 during waves 2–7, and Tier 3 during waves 2–5.

When it is near the player or the Eternia Crystal, it will emote a speech bubble with an exclamation mark, light its fuse, and begin screaming while dashing towards the nearest target. When it reaches a target, it kills itself and creates an explosion with a radius similar to that of a Grenade. The detonation will not destroy tiles, also similar to a Grenade.

Like other members of the Old One's Army, if a Kobold's target is too far away or obstructed, it will enter an ethereal state, allowing it to float upwards and pass through tiles. Kobolds are also unaffected by Teleporters or Lava, and will take half damage from Traps.
The Kobold requires 200 kills to be awarded completion of its corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Kobold Dynamite Backpack: The Kobold Dynamite Backpack is an unimplemented item that resembles the dynamite backpack worn by Kobolds and Kobold Gliders. It only exists as an ID and image file in the game's code. Attempting to use third-party tools to obtain it will result in it instantly disappearing.
Kobold Glider: The Kobold Glider is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Old One's Army event. It spawns during Tier 2 during waves 5–7, and Tier 3 during waves 4–5.

When it is close to or below the player or the Eternia Crystal, it will briefly spin upwards before lighting its fuse and diving towards its closest target, effectively turning itself into a homing missile. Upon contact with the player, Eternia Crystal, or solid blocks, it will detonate with a radius similar to that of a Grenade. The explosion cannot destroy tiles.
The Kobold Glider requires 100 kills to be awarded completion of its corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Kraken: The Kraken is a Hardmode yoyo that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop from Duke Fishron. It has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.

While in use, it constantly emits a whirlpool loop around the yoyo, which increases its hit detection range significantly. On every 4th yoyo hit, it fires a spread of three wave projectiles towards its target, which can pass through blocks and disappear after traveling a short distance. The waves pierce infinitely and each deal 50% of the Kraken's damage ((60 base damage) and 100% of its knockback.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Krampus: The Krampus is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during wave 8 of the Frost Moon event.
Defeating a Krampus during the Frost Moon event will add 10 / 20 / 25 points to the final score.
Krypton Moss Brick: Krypton Moss Brick is a type of brick made from Krypton Moss that glows in the dark when placed.
Krypton Moss Brick Wall: Krypton Moss Brick Wall is a brick background wall that glows in the dark when placed, like Krypton Moss and the Krypton Moss Brick it is made from.
Kwad Racer Drone: The Kwad Racer Drone is a Hardmode, post-Plantera novelty item purchased from the Cyborg for 10 Gold. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button while selected in the hotbar summons a harmless drone that can be controlled by the ▲ Up, ◀ Left, and ▶ Right buttons. Pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again or switching to another item instantly destroys the drone. The player appears to wield a remote control when the drone is in use.
The player is locked in place while the drone is active. Equipping the FPV Goggles will center the camera on the drone.
Lac Beetle: The Lac Beetle is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Underground Jungle on Jungle Grass. When killed, it will drop the Violet Husk, which can be used to make Violet Dye.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Ladybug: The Ladybug is a small uncommon critter that can be found in Forests at daytime if the wind speed is greater than or equal to 20 mph. Ladybugs spawn much more frequently if the player is also in a town.
The Ladybug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Ladybug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Ladybug Cage). Once crafted, the Ladybug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Ladybug can be used as bait for fishing, with 17% bait power.
There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Ladybug to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

Touching naturally spawned Ladybugs will temporarily increase the player's luck, while killing natural or player-released Ladybugs or consuming them as bait will temporarily decrease the player's luck and boost the chance of rain. However, using them for crafting does not affect luck, allowing the following recipes to be made consequence-free. See Ladybug luck for more details.
Lamia: The Lamia is a Hardmode enemy that can only be found in the Underground Desert biome. When found in regular or Hallowed Underground Deserts, it has pale blonde hair and has a chance to drop the Sun Mask. Corruption/Crimson Underground Deserts will spawn an alternate variant having much darker hair than its normal counterpart. The "corrupted" version has a chance to drop the Moon Mask.
Both variants have a rare chance to drop a piece of the Lamia set.
Lamia set: The Lamia set is a Hardmode vanity set which consists of the Lamia Mask, Lamia Wraps and the Lamia Tail. It is rarely dropped by Lamias, with a 1/120 (0.83%) chance per piece for both types of Lamia.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Lamp Post: The Lamp Post is a piece of furniture that emits light. It can be placed underwater and can be toggled with wires. It counts as a light source for housing.
Lamps: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp).
Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava.
The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps.
Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)
Land Mine: The Land Mine is a unique Hardmode, post-Plantera placeable item. They remain dormant once placed, until an entity touches them or they are activated by Wire, at which point they explode, dealing 250 base damage to all entities within a 8×8-tile area. The only tile destroyed by the explosion is the activated landmine itself.
Land Mines can be purchased from the Demolitionist for 5 Gold each after Plantera and at least one Pirate Invasion have been defeated.
Lanterns: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire.

There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff.

The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.
Large Bamboo: Large Bamboo is a block created from Bamboo that visually appears to be one large stalk as opposed to several bundled together.
Large Bamboo Wall: Large Bamboo Wall is a wall created from Large Bamboo that visually appears to be made of larger stalks than Bamboo Wall.
Large Gems: Large Gems are items designed for the PvP game Capture the Gem, and are dropped when the player dies, even if they are in Classic or Softcore mode. With each different Large Gem that is held or carried in the player's inventory, a hologram of it appears above the player's head. If two or more different Large Gems are carried, their holograms will revolve in a circular pattern above the player's head. They are immediately deleted if placed in a player's trash slot.
Large Gems can be placed into a Gem Lock to function as a key. This is primarily used in making adventure maps.

Each Large Gem can also be combined with a Minecart at any Anvil to produce a Gem Minecart. The Gem Minecarts are mechanically identical to the regular Minecart, but are aesthetically representative of their Gem type, and sparkle.
Large Volcano: The Large Volcano is a decorative animated furniture item that emits light when placed. Its animation can be toggled on and off with wires.
Laser Drill: The Laser Drill is a Hardmode, post-Golem drill that has a 1/800 (0.13%) chance of being dropped from all basic enemies during the Martian Madness event. It produces a green glowing drill-like beam that extends up to a base distance of 16 tiles. It can mine all blocks.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Laser Machinegun: The Laser Machinegun is a Hardmode, post-Golem magic gun that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. When used, it fires two inaccurate blue lasers that do not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. The weapon accelerates while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held down, reaching its maximum fire rate after nearly two seconds of continuous usage.
Its best modifier is Mythical. Since it does not benefit from speed modifiers, Godly and Demonic provide the same DPS bonus as Mythical.
Laser Rifle: The Laser Rifle is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. When used, it fires fast-moving purple lasers that can hit up to three enemies. The lasers will increase in damage, pierce, knockback, and size (only visually) as they travel. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, the Laser Rifle costs no mana to use.
Last Prism: The Last Prism is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord magic weapon that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When used, it projects six rainbow-colored beams each dealing the weapon's listed damage, which immediately begin to rotate and converge into one concentrated beam over a duration of 3 seconds. The fully-converged beam instead deals 300% of the weapon's damage (300 base damage) per hit. While held, the Last Prism's aim works in a sweeping motion, meaning the turn rate is reduced.
In addition to consuming mana on the initial use, the weapon will also consume mana while firing the beams, with the mana usage increasing exponentially as the beams converge:
During the first 1.5 seconds of use, mana is consumed at a rate of once every 0.5 seconds, for up to 3 times.
During the next 0.5 seconds of use, mana is consumed at a rate of once every 0.25 seconds, for up to 2 times.
Afterwards, mana is consumed at a rate of once every 0.08 seconds, or 12 times per second.

Its best modifier is Mythical or Masterful. The Last Prism is unaffected by attack speed bonuses, meaning that Mythical provides +5% critical strike chance while Masterful lowers the weapon's mana cost.
Lava Bat: The Lava Bat is a Hardmode bat enemy that appears in the Underworld after one of the mechanical bosses has been defeated. It is a stronger version of the Hellbat.
In the Zenith (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) special world seed, it drops lava upon death.
Lava Boulder: The Lava Boulder is a special type of Boulder. It deals 140 / 280 / 420 damage to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters) and inflicts On Fire! for 5 / 10 / 12.5 seconds to players (5 seconds to NPCs, enemies, and critters). It can be encountered within 60 tiles of Lava.
Upon breaking, it releases lava in connected open space within a 4-tile radius.
Lava Charm: The Lava Charm is an accessory that grants immunity to lava for 7 seconds. It is found in Chests located in the cavern layer as well as obtained from Hellstone Crates and Obsidian Crates with a 1/20 (5%) chance. It can only be found in Chests in the lower portion of the Caverns where lava pools can naturally spawn, as opposed to Chests throughout the entirety of the Caverns.

When the Lava Charm is equipped and the player comes into contact with lava, a 7-second countdown begins, signified by a lava meter that displays over the player's head. It operates similarly to the breath meter, but displays flame icons instead of bubbles. Lava immunity time is recharged gradually by exiting lava, the same way breathing time is recharged by exiting water (albeit much more slowly).
Lava Cloud: The Lava Cloud is a block that glows in the dark when placed. It replaces Rain Clouds in Skyblock islands that spawn in the Underworld, which most prominently occurs when combined with the Remix special seed. Like Rain Cloud, Lava Clouds cause purely decorative lava drops to appear beneath them to fall for about 18 tiles before fading away for 5 or more.
Lava Lamp: The Lava Lamp is a furniture item purchased from the Party Girl for 2 Gold, that emits a small amount of light and has an animated texture. It is not a mechanism but can be placed on tables. It is not considered a suitable light source for an NPC house. It is used purely as a decorative light source.
Lava Moss Brick: Lava Moss Brick is a type of brick made from Lava Moss that glows in the dark when placed. It will always glow with the same coloration regardless of the paint that is applied to it.
Lava Moss Brick Wall: Lava Moss Brick Wall is a brick background wall that glows in the dark when placed, like Lava Moss and the Lava Moss Brick it is made from.
Lava Slime: The Lava Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in The Underworld. It gives off an orange glow with fire particles.

Lava Slimes take no damage from lava and float on it like regular slimes do on water, except they rebound very high into the air when they come up, instead of gently bouncing up and down like normal slimes. Lava Slimes also have increased mobility compared to most slimes. Unlike most slimes, the Lava Slime does not drop Gel upon death but still drops coins.

In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Lava Slimes leave behind a small amount of lava when killed. The amount of lava produced by each slime randomly varies from 19.6% to 58.8% of a full tile. Since the minimum amount of fluid required to fill a bucket is 39.2% of a full tile, this means the lava dropped from one slime is bucketable around half the time. When the Skyblock tile threshold is reached and Remix seed is inactive, Lava Slimes create either 4, 6 or 9 full tiles of lava upon death depending on their position, meaning the lava is always bucketable. This happens regardless of difficulty, even in Classic Mode.
Like most other slimes, the Lava Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Lava Waders: The Lava Waders are a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory. They grant the following effects while equipped:
The ability to stand and walk on the surface of all liquids.
When walking on liquid, press the ▼ Down key allows submerging into the liquid.
Prevents fall damage when landing on the surface of any liquid.
Decreases the damage taken from lava from 80 to 35, and reduces the duration of On Fire! debuff inflicted by lava from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds.
Equipping the Ash Wood armor at the same time provides immunity to lava damage and debuff.
Lava Walls: The Obsidian Wall, Ember Wall, Cinder Wall, Magma Wall, and Smouldering Stone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the lower Cavern layer, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on the Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
The Ember, Cinder, Magma, and Smouldering Stone Walls are unavailable on the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version.
Lavafall Block: The Lavafall Block is an animated block type that shows flowing lava, which glows when placed. It does not satisfy the need for a light source in an NPC house.
Lavafall Wall: Lavafall Wall is one of few animated background wall types. It depicts flowing lava, and in a similar manner to lava also emits light when placed. Despite it being made from lava, it will still burn in lava.
Lavafly: The Lavafly is a critter that spawns occasionally in the Underworld at night. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld at any time. Also from destroyed wild Ash grass plants at any time and even outside of the Underworld. It gives off a tiny amount of light, similarly to the Firefly. The Lavafly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Lavafly can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net or the Golden Bug Net. Trying to catch it with a standard Bug Net will only set the player on fire. After being caught, it can be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Lavafly in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Lavafly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Lavafly can be used as bait for fishing, with 25% bait power. Using it as bait also allows fishing in lava.
Lavaproof Bug Net: The Lavaproof Bug Net is an upgraded version of the Bug Net. It allows the player to successfully catch the Lavafly, Magma Snail, and Hell Butterfly that can be used to fish in lava. It swings faster than the Bug Net and can destroy tall grass and vines.
Its upgraded version is the Golden Bug Net which is faster and bigger.
Lavaproof Fishing Hook: The Lavaproof Fishing Hook is an accessory that allows the player to fish in lava with any bait and any fishing pole. It has a 19/100 (19%) chance of being obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates, both of which can be obtained from fishing in lava.
Lavaproof Tackle Bag: The Lavaproof Tackle Bag is an accessory that combines the functionalities of its components: the Angler Earring's 10% boost to Fishing Power, the Tackle Box's chance not to consume bait, the unbreakable quality of the High Test Fishing Line, and the ability to fish in lava from the Lavaproof Fishing Hook.

The Lavaproof Tackle Bag's increase in Fishing Power stacks with that of the Angler Earring and the Angler Tackle Bag, granting a total boost of 30% if all three are equipped. The decreased chance to consume bait does not stack with that of the Tackle Box or the Angler Tackle Bag.
Lawn Flamingo: The Lawn Flamingo is a decorative furniture item that can be placed and serves no purpose other than as decoration. It can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold.
Lawn Mower: The Lawn Mower is a tool that can be purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold and mows normal and Hallowed grass. Mowed grass has a different texture, reduces enemy spawn chance by 10%, prevents grass plants (and dye plants) from growing, and allows Golf Balls to travel on top of it with unhindered movement while golfing. The Lawn Mower deals a fixed 8 classless damage to entities only while the player is moving forwards, is not in the air, and is not grappled. When it is used on grass other than normal and hallowed, it only removes weeds and flowers.
Lazure's set: Lazure's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Lazure, a former artist at Re-Logic.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Lazure's equipment also includes these non-vanity items, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Lead Axe: The Lead Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Iron Axe.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Lead Bar: The Lead Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Iron Bar.
Newly created characters in Journey Mode will always spawn with the Iron Shortsword, Iron Pickaxe, and Iron Axe, regardless of whether the world generated with Iron or Lead.
Lead Bow: The Lead Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Iron Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Lead Brick: Lead Brick is a type of Brick crafted from Lead Ore.
Lead Brick Wall: Lead Brick Wall is a type of background wall.
Lead Broadsword: The Lead Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Lead Shortsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Iron Broadsword.
Lead Hammer: The Lead Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Iron Hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, and Quick provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Lead Ore: Lead Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on the surface. Lead Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Iron Ore.
Lead Pickaxe: The Lead Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks weaker than Meteorite.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Iron Pickaxe. The Lead Pickaxe has slightly more pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Lead Shortsword: The Lead Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Lead Broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Iron Shortsword.
Lead armor: Lead armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Lead Helmet, Lead Chainmail, and Lead Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Lead Bars (180 Lead Ore). The full set grants 11 defense while equipped.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Iron armor.
Leaf Blower: The Leaf Blower is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When used, it rapidly fires a spread of leaf projectiles that begin swirling after traveling for about 15 tiles, and move in a spiral circle pattern while gradually fading away. The leaves cannot pass through blocks or pierce enemies.
Leather: Leather is a crafting material that is used to create the Archaeologist's Jacket and the Archaeologist's Pants. It is made using Rotten Chunks, a material only obtainable in Corruption worlds.

It cannot be obtained in a Crimson world unless the player makes an artificial Corruption biome (e.g. using Corrupt Seeds, purchased from the Dryad in a Graveyard (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) or uses a Corrupt Statue.
Leather Whip: The Leather Whip is a pre-Hardmode whip that is virtually always available to be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold (save for certain scenarios). It has a 50% multihit penalty, and inflicts 4 tag damage on enemies.
Leech: The Leech is a pre-Hardmode worm enemy and boss servant that is summoned by the Wall of Flesh. Multiple Leeches are released from the Wall's mouth, first in groups of 3-4. The groups grow larger and more frequent as the boss takes damage. The Wall of Flesh will eventually release them in a continuous stream.
Leinfors' set: Leinfors' set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Leinfors, a former production assistant at Re-Logic.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The Leinfors' Luxury Shampoo accessory will add a sparkle effect to the character's hair.
Leinfors' equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Lemon: The Lemon is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Forest tree.
Lemonade: Lemonade is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Lens: A Lens is a common crafting material that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Demon Eyes and Wandering Eyes.
Leprechaun set: The Leprechaun set is a vanity set. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to be obtained by opening a Goodie Bag from the Halloween event. It consists of a Leprechaun Hat, Leprechaun Shirt and Leprechaun Pants.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Lesion Block: The Lesion Block is a Hardmode block. It is used to craft Lesion furniture and Lesion Block Walls. Lesion Blocks will not spread the Corruption.
Lesion Block Wall: The Lesion Block Wall is a type of background walls. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.
Lesser Healing Potion: The Lesser Healing Potion is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that restores 50 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It is the first tier of healing potion, preceding the Healing Potion, Greater Healing Potion, Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion.

In addition to being crafted, Lesser Healing Potions can also be found naturally in pots (only in pre-Hardmode), generated chests, Wooden and Pearlwood Crates, or dropped from most early pre-Hardmode bosses. They can also be purchased for 3 Silver from the Merchant, or from the Skeleton Merchant during moon phases 2, 4, 6, and 8:. Naturally-placed Lesser Healing Potions appear frequently on platforms in the Dungeon (along with Lesser Mana Potions). When encountered in placed form, they function as Placed Bottle crafting stations. They also show the "bottle" tooltip on the map. They can be freed with a pickaxe or ⚷ Open / Activate and retrieved, and can be placed by the player by crafting them into Decorative Healing Potions.
Lesser Mana Potion: The Lesser Mana Potion is a recovery potion that restores 50 mana when used and inflicts the Mana Sickness debuff upon use. It can be purchased from the Merchant for 1 Silver each, and can also be found in Wooden and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing.

Naturally-placed Lesser Mana Potions appear frequently on platforms in the Dungeon (along with Lesser Healing Potions). When encountered in placed form, they function as Placed Bottle crafting stations. They also show the "bottle" tooltip on the map. They can be freed with a pickaxe or ⚷ Open / Activate and retrieved, and can be placed by the player by crafting them into Decorative Mana Potions.
It is the first tier of mana potion, preceding the Mana Potion, Greater Mana Potion, and Super Mana Potion.
Lever: The Lever is a 2×2 activation mechanism purchased from the Mechanic for 30 Silver. It can activate Statues, lights, etc. via ⚷ Open / Activate.
The Lever can be placed on any flat surface, the same as furniture, including on platforms. It can also be placed on background walls.

Despite its depiction as a switch with two positions, the Lever does not need to act as an on/off mechanism. When wired to Dart Traps, for example, activating the Lever will always cause the trap to shoot, the same as a Pressure Plate would, no matter which position the Lever happens to be in.
Librarian Block: Librarian Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks that are used to craft Librarian Platforms, Librarian Walls, and Librarian furniture.
Librarian Skeleton: The Librarian Skeleton is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in front of placed Books in the Dungeon. It teleports around the player, preferably near books, and attacks by throwing nearby books at the player, which go through blocks. A bright sigil shows behind the enemy as it attacks.
Librarian Wall: Librarian Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Librarian Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Life Crystal: The Life Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's health capacity by 20, adding a red heart to the player's health bar, while also restoring 20 health.

Life Crystals can be found naturally placed in any area in the Underground layer and below, though they are fairly uncommon. They cannot be found in the Underworld or the Dungeon. Life Crystals also have a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to drop from a Golden Crate, or 19/160 (11.88%) chance from a Titanium Crate.

Up to 15 Life Crystals can be used per player, increasing health capacity by 300 health (15 hearts). Added to the 100 health (5 hearts) new players begin with, a total of 400 health (20 hearts) can be achieved. Additional Life Crystals can no longer be used at that point, and attempting to do so will not consume the item.

After a world converts to Hardmode, and after the 400 health maximum is reached from consuming Life Crystals, Life Fruits can then be used to increase health capacity further, to a maximum of 500 health (20 Life Fruits).
Life Crystal Boulder: The Life Crystal Boulder is a furniture item. It spawns naturally in the Celebration Mk 10, No Traps, and the Zenith special world seeds.

It appears to be an ordinary Life Crystal and is generated in a similar manner upon world creation, but acts identically to a Boulder if hit with a pickaxe or drill, or otherwise unsupported by solid blocks. The Life Crystal Boulder falls directly downwards until it collides with a solid block, at which point it begins rolling, accelerating and dealing damage to the player, enemies, critters, and NPCs. Life Crystal Boulders pierce through an unlimited number of entities and accelerate to a top speed of 36 mph over the course of 2.17 seconds.

Life Crystal Boulders roll across flat surfaces and down slopes but break and disappear upon colliding with an obstacle, such as a wall of solid tiles. They deal 140 / 280 / 420 to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters) and inflict a knockback value of 10 (Extremely strong) on contact. However, when the Life Crystal Boulder breaks after colliding with solid blocks or after rolling for one minute (like all other projectiles), it drops a Life Crystal item.
Life Drain: The Life Drain is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics. When used, it creates an invisible aura that deals continuous damage to all enemies near the cursor's position, as long as the line of sight between the player and the cursor is unobstructed. A stream of red particles flows toward the player from each targeted enemy. While the aura is hitting enemies, the user receives the Life Drain buff, which adds 1.5 health per second to existing health regeneration, plus 0.5 health per second for every two extra enemies hit, while also increasing the ramp-up speed of natural regeneration greatly. Enemies that are being damaged by the Life Drain's aura are additionally inflicted with a unique debuff that deals 25 damage per second (5 damage displayed every 0.2 seconds).
Its best modifier is Mythical for damage output, or Celestial for mana conservation.
Life Fruit: The Life Fruit is a Hardmode plant and permanent booster item that grows on Jungle grass in any area within the Underground layer or below, and only after any mechanical boss has been defeated. Life Fruit grow 25% faster on average in Expert Mode.

When used, a Life Fruit permanently increases the player's health capacity by 5 and restores the player's health by 5, turning one unit in the player's health bar golden. Life Fruit can only be used once a player has reached the 400 health cap from consuming Life Crystals. A total of 20 Life Fruit is required to reach the maximum 500 health capacity. Once this is reached, the player's health cannot be increased beyond 500, with the exception of the Lifeforce buff.
Life Preserver: The Life Preserver is a wall decoration acquired by finishing Angler quests. It is rewarded with a 1/70 (1.43%) chance.
Lifeforce Potion: The Lifeforce Potion is a buff potion that grants the Lifeforce buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's health capacity by up to 20% (see below for details). This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

Maximum health granted by the Lifeforce buff will not be counted by health conditions of certain game mechanics (e.g. the spawning of Nurse, Eye of Cthulhu, and Goblin Army, etc.). The player have to increase their permanent maximum health (with permanent boosters) to fulfill these conditions.
Lifeform Analyzer: The Lifeform Analyzer is an informational accessory that displays the name of rare enemies, critters, and undiscovered NPCs (see list below) within 81.25 tiles around the player.
The Lifeform Analyzer can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold.
Light Disc: The Light Disc is a Hardmode, post-The Destroyer boomerang. It does not necessarily return immediately upon contact with objects, but instead can bounce off blocks before returning. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not have to return to the player before being fired, with a maximum of six Light Discs that can be thrown out at one time.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Light Mummy: Mummies are Hardmode enemies that spawn in the Desert biome and areas where Sand Blocks are present. They follow the Fighter AI, behaving similarly to Zombies.

There are several different types of Mummies: the standard Mummy, as well as the Dark Mummy, Light Mummy, and Blood Mummy. They spawn in Corrupted Deserts, Hallowed Deserts and Crimson Deserts, respectively.

Dark Mummies and Blood Mummies are 50% faster than other Mummies. All mummies receive a 100% speed increase when their health is reduced below 50%. In addition, Mummies inflict the following debuffs upon hitting the player:
Light Shard: The Light Shard is a Hardmode crafting material used in the crafting of the Dao of Pow, Sky Fracture and Ruinous Staff. It has a 1/10 (10%) chance to drop from Light Mummies and Spectral Mummies (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which spawn in Hallowed deserts.

On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, the Light Shard also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to drop from Dreamer Ghouls in The Hallowed Underground Desert, and a 1/25 (4%) chance of dropping from Crystal Threshers.
Its Corruption/Crimson counterpart is the Dark Shard.
Light's Bane: The Light's Bane is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it creates a dark slash near the tip of the sword. The slashes deal 50% of the weapon's damage (8 base damage) and its full knockback, have 5 armor penetration, pierce once, and will automatically target enemies within a radius of 3.125 tiles. The weapon also has a chance to create a big slash that is twice as large and deals 100% of the weapon's damage. The chance of big slashes occurring is equal to the player's melee critical strike chance.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Blood Butcherer. The Light's Bane is faster than the Blood Butcherer, but has a lower size and base damage.
Lightning Aura sentry summons: The Lightning Aura Rod, Cane, and Staff are special sentry summon weapons that summon their respective sentries. Each Lightning Aura sentry consists of an aura with a radius of 9 tiles, which damages enemies repeatedly while within. For enemies with less than 999 defense, Lightning Aura sentries have armor penetration equal to their defense, completely bypassing it. The higher the tier, the more damage the Lightning Auras deal.
The Rod is sold by the Tavernkeep for 5 Defender Medals. The Cane is sold for 15 Defender Medals after defeating one mechanical boss. The Staff is sold for 60 Defender Medals after defeating Golem.

During the Old One's Army event, Etherian Mana can be collected, which allows the placement of multiple Lightning Auras that remain permanently until the event is over. Etherian Mana cannot be used outside the event. These weapons cannot be used outside of the Old One's Army event until the event has been successfully completed.

Lightning Aura sentries are boosted by the Monk armor and Shinobi Infiltrator armor set bonuses, which increase their attack rate and allow them to deal critical hits. These weapons will have a fixed 1/6 (16.67%) (Monk armor) or 1/4 (25%) (Shinobi Infiltrator armor) chance to deal critical strike. This critical strike is determined separately from the summon tag critical chance (from whips), meaning that these two critical strike chances are two independent events instead of additive values (see Notes for exact numbers). The Shinobi Infiltrator armor also increases the size of the Lightning Aura's circle.
Their best modifier is generally Fabled. However, if using whips, the Rod's best modifier is Ballistic if the player's summon damage bonuses do not reach 110%.
Lightning Boots: The Lightning Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory and the direct upgrade to the Spectre Boots. They grant the following effects while equipped:
The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint.
Increased maximum movement speed to 35 mph (25.67 tiles/second).
The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual cloud trail.
When paired with wings, this flight is disabled to give the wings an additional 0.7 seconds of flight time.
Lightning Bug: The Lightning Bug is a harmless Hardmode critter that gives off a tiny amount of light, similarly to the Firefly. It spawns on Hallowed grass blocks during the night. The Lightning Bug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Lightning Bug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Lightning Bug in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Lightning Bug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Lightning Bug can be used as bait for fishing, with 35% bait power.
The Lightning Bug can be spawned by the Firefly Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Lightning Carrot: The Lightning Carrot is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Volt Bunny that follows the player. While flying to keep pace with the player, the Volt Bunny dashes and releases a series of spherical blue sparks, which emit a decent amount of light while moving erratically and can spread light over an area. If there are no available tiles for the pet to "sit" on, like when climbing walls or flying, the Volt Bunny will constantly jump around. The Lightning Carrot can be purchased from the Zoologist for 50 Gold after completing 50% (273 entries) of the Bestiary.
Lightning Strike: The Lightning Strike is a Hardmode wand that calls down lightning bolts from the sky. When used, it creates a blue spark at the cursor's location which is initially harmless. If the player's line of sight to the cursor is obstructed by blocks, the spark will be instead created at the closest block in the direction of the cursor. The spark then attempts to follow the cursor, but cannot pass through blocks. If any enemies come within 0.75 tiles of the spark, it will attach itself to them and follow their movement instead of the cursor, similar to a natural lightning strike during Thunderstorm.

The spark detonates 0.5 seconds after it is created, causing a lightning bolt to strike at its location from above, damaging any enemies in its path and inflicting the Hellfire and Zapped debuffs for 4–7 seconds. The lightning bolt can pass through blocks until it reaches the spark's location, at which point it explodes, dealing damage to other nearby enemies within an area. If the spark is inside liquids while it detonates, the lightning bolt will also electrify a large circular area in the liquid, dealing damage to enemies within it. However, this also causes the lightning bolt and the electrified liquid to deal 120 base damage to the player upon contact, and inflict them with the Zapped debuff for 4–7 seconds, but not the Hellfire debuff. The lightning bolt loses 20% of its damage for each enemy struck. The Lightning Strike also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Lihzahrd: The Lihzahrd is an enemy that spawns in the Jungle Temple and initially behaves like an ordinary walking fighter. However, as soon as its health is reduced to below 55% (220 / 440 / 660), it enters its second, crawling form, causing it appear like a more lizard-like quadrupedal creature. In this form, the Lihzahrd is much faster, gains additional damage and defense, and becomes immune to knockback, but has reduced jump height.
Lihzahrd Altar: The Lihzahrd Altar is a furniture item used for summoning Golem with Lihzahrd Power Cells. Upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it, one Lihzahrd Power Cell is consumed from the player's inventory and Golem is instantly summoned. The Lihzahrd Altar is always found naturally placed in the final chamber of the Jungle Temple.

Like Lihzahrd Bricks, the Lihzahrd Altar is impervious to explosions and can only be removed with the Picksaw, Laser Drill, or Luminite Pickaxes. Once picked up, it can be placed anywhere and can be used to summon Golem in any area at any time, as long as the world is in Hardmode with Plantera defeated.
Lihzahrd Brick: Lihzahrd Bricks are blocks that make up the structure of the Jungle Temple. They are the toughest block in the game, being impervious to explosives and only breakable using the Picksaw or a better pickaxe or drill. They also cannot be made inactive using Actuators until Plantera has been defeated, unless they are above the surface layer.
Like Jungle grass, placing 140 (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) / 80 (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Lihzahrd Bricks in one area creates a Jungle biome.
Lihzahrd Brick Wall: The Lihzahrd Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Jungle Temple, considered unsafe. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

The Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall is an item that places an unsafe Lihzahrd Brick Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Lihzahrd Brick Wall into Shimmer after Golem has been defeated.
Lihzahrd Chest: Lihzahrd Chests are chests found in the Jungle Temple. Each contains one Lihzahrd Power Cell, and may contain a Lihzahrd Furnace, some Solar Tablet Fragments, and sometimes, a Solar Tablet. They also contain other typical Gold Chest loot.
Lihzahrd Furnace: The Lihzahrd Furnace is a Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting station used to craft Lihzahrd furniture out of Lihzahrd Bricks. It is always found in every Lihzahrd Chest in the Jungle Temple. Once Golem has been defeated, it can also be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold when she is spoken to in the Jungle.
Lihzahrd Power Cell: The Lihzahrd Power Cell is a boss-summoning item used to summon Golem. It can only be used at the Lihzahrd Altar (located in the final chamber of the Jungle Temple), at any time, as long as the world is in Hardmode and Plantera has been defeated. Upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Lihzahrd Altar, one Lihzahrd Power Cell is consumed from the player's inventory and Golem is summoned.

One Lihzahrd Power Cell is guaranteed to be found within each Lihzahrd Chest, and they additionally have a 1/50 (2%) chance of dropping from Lihzahrds and Flying Snakes, both of which spawn exclusively within the Jungle Temple.
Lilac Dusk set: The Lilac Dusk set is a vanity set consisting of the Lilac Dusk Hairclip, the Lilac Dusk Dress, and the Lilac Dusk Skirt. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 7 Gold 50 Silver (set).
Lilith's Necklace: Lilith's Necklace is a Hardmode transformation mount item that turns the player into a Wolf. Some vanity items are visible when transformed, but certain accessories cannot be used, such as wings. The player can still swing weapons, drink potions, and use items as normal, with unique visual animations for each action. The player's hurt sound is also replaced with a wolf's bark. Lilith's Necklace has a 1/30 (3.33%) / 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Wolves.
Newly created Journey Mode characters named Wolfpet or Wolf Pet (case-insensitive) will have Lilith's Necklace equipped in the mount slot.
Lime Kelp: The Lime Kelp is a dye material and type of plant. It grows on any tiles submerged in at least 2 tiles of any liquid in the Underground and Cavern layers. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Lime Dye.
Liquid bombs: Liquid bombs are explosive items that function like the Bomb, but their explosion will either place or remove liquids, instead of destroying blocks. There are four different types of liquid bombs: Dry Bomb, Wet Bomb, Lava Bomb, and Honey Bomb.
The Dry Bomb deletes all liquids in a small area when it explodes.
The Wet Bomb places water in a small area when it explodes.
The Lava Bomb places lava in a small area when it explodes.
The Honey Bomb places honey in a small area when it explodes.

If a liquid bomb touches either of these three liquids, it will immediately explode and apply its effects. However, all liquid bombs will bounce off Shimmer. Shimmer does not restrict their effects in any other way.

Wet Bombs are obtainable by opening Obsidian or Hellstone Crates found by fishing in lava. If the player is carrying a Wet Bomb, the Demolitionist will sell Wet Bombs for 25 Silver each. Purchasing more Wet Bombs will allow the player to craft the other variants (see below). The Demolitionist will also sell the three other types of bombs for the same price while the player is carrying them.
Liquid rockets: Liquid rockets are rocket ammunition items which place or remove liquids in addition to dealing damage. There are four different types of liquid rockets: Dry Rocket, Wet Rocket, Lava Rocket, and Honey Rocket.

When a liquid rocket is fired, it will explode upon contact with enemies or blocks similarly to normal rockets, and additionally apply its special effect (see below). If, however, the rocket touches any liquid while in flight, it will immediately explode and apply its effects. All liquid rockets deal damage to nearby players, enemies, and critters.
Dry Rockets are purchasable from the Cyborg for 50 Silver each at any time. They can be used to craft the other three rockets, and those can be crafted back into Dry Rockets (see below).
Little Kinship Peach: The Little Kinship Peach is a Hardmode crafting material. It is used to upgrade Chillet into Trusty Chillet, Chillet Ignis into Trusty Chillet Ignis, and Digtoise into Trusty Digtoise.
Living Fire Blocks: Living Fire Blocks are Hardmode animated background furniture blocks that, when placed, resemble small animated flames and emit faint orange light. They deal no damage on contact and can be freed with any pickaxe or drill. Living Fire Blocks have a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by any enemy killed in the Underworld during Hardmode, including the Wall of Flesh, and drop in stacks of 20–50 at a time.

While Living Fire Blocks can be placed in a manner similar to traditional, foreground blocks, they are actually in the background, similar to furniture, allowing the player to walk directly through them. They can attach to each other horizontally as well as vertically, but other traditional, foreground block types will not attach to them.
There are five color variations of the base Living Fire Block, all of which are crafted from it. They are functionally identical.
Living Flame Dye: Living Flame Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It can only be obtained after defeating a mechanical boss. Upon application, the dye will cause all items in the slot equipped to change colors to a fiery red, with a yellow-to-red rippling effect. Additionally, any items affected by this dye will flash upon taking damage.
Living Leaf Wall: Living Leaf Wall is a type of wall. Like other player-crafted walls, it can be used for valid housing.
They naturally generate in the treetops of the living Trees in the save the rainforest seed.
Living Loom: The Living Loom is a crafting station used to craft Living Wood furniture out of any kind of Wood as well as Feywood furniture out of Feywood. It can also be used as a Loom. Living Looms can be found inside Living Trees placed near Living Wood Chests, but not all worlds are guaranteed to contain a Living Loom. They can also be obtained by throwing a Loom into Shimmer.
Living Ocean Dye: Living Ocean Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It is only obtainable after defeating any mechanical boss.
Living Rainbow Dye: Living Rainbow Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It is only obtainable after defeating a mechanical boss.
Living Wood Chest: A Living Wood Chest is a Chest storage item that can be found inside rooms within hollow Living Trees. It can also be crafted at a Living Loom, which is generated alongside a Living Wood Chest in the treasure room of Living Trees.
Living Wood Wall: The Living Wood Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Living Trees, considered unsafe, where it does not drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be found naturally generated in Living Mahogany Trees, considered safe, where it does drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Under normal circumstances, unsafe Living Wood Walls only allow Goldfish, Snails, Mice, Worms, Squirrels, Bunnies, and Gnomes to spawn in front of them. Notably, Gnomes only spawn on the surface, meaning unsafe Living Wood Walls underground will spawn exclusively critters. This effect is not applied in Remix and Zenith worlds.
The Overgrown Living Wood Wall is an item that places an unsafe Living Wood Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Living Wood Wall into Shimmer.
Lizard Egg: The Lizard Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Lizard that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Pet Lizard will sprout wings like those of a Flying Snake to catch up with the player. The Lizard Egg has a 1/1000 (0.1%) chance of being dropped by Flying Snakes and Lihzahrds in the Jungle Temple.
Lizard set: The Lizard set is a vanity set composed of the Lizard Tail and the Lizard Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a New Moon or a Waxing Crescent for 6 Gold (set).
Lobster Tail: The Lobster Tail is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Logic Gate Lamps: A Logic Gate Lamp is a mechanism that is placed atop a Logic Gate or another Logic Gate Lamp. The Logic Gate is activated based on its type and the states of the Logic Gate Lamps atop it. The state of a Logic Gate Lamp is toggled via wire. The Logic Gate Lamps, along with the Logic Gates, are purchased from the Steampunker.
Logic Gates: A Logic Gate is a mechanism used to provide logic to wiring setups. Input is provided using a stack of Logic Gate Lamps placed on top of it. The logic gate turns on and off depending on its inputs, and emits a signal every time its state changes.
The logic gates, along with the Logic Gate Lamps, are purchased from the Steampunker for 2 Gold each.
Loki's Dye: Loki's Dye is a Hardmode dye that can be obtained from Hardmode bosses' Treasure Bags (except Queen Slime's), as part of Loki's set. It does not change the color of the armor, but rather adds a dark gray flames effect, similar to four other dyes which are obtained by trading Strange Plants with the Dye Trader in Hardmode. Equipping Loki's Dye in all 3 dye slots intensifies the effect. It also makes the item in whatever slot it’s in glow in the dark.
Loki's set: Loki's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Loki, the Chief Strategy Officer at Re-Logic. Equipping the full set produces a pulsating effect similar to Adamantite armor, a glow similar to Spooky armor, and causes the armor to appear darker.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Loki's equipment also includes these non-vanity items, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Loom: The Loom is a crafting station used to craft Silk, as well as some items that require Silk as an ingredient. It can sometimes be found in Underground Cabins.
Lost Girl: The Nymph is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Cavern layer of any biome. When encountered, she appears as the Lost Girl, who seems to be a helpless, stationary NPC in need of rescue. However, when a player gets close or attacks the Lost Girl, she transforms into the Nymph and starts attacking the player by running towards them. For a pre-Hardmode enemy, she deals comparatively high damage.
The Lost Girl will only transform into a Nymph if any of the following conditions are met:
The Lost Girl does not have full health.
The distance between the player and the Lost Girl is less than 12.5 tiles, and she has a direct line of sight to the player.
The Lost Girl is moving in any direction (e.g. caused by falling or knockback).
The Lost Girl is immune to the Confused debuff, but the transformed Nymph is not.

She is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. The Nymph requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of her Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Love Potion: The Love Potion is a Hardmode thrown potion that functions similarly to Thrown Water. Upon colliding with solid blocks, it inflicts the Lovestruck debuff on players (including the user), enemies, critters, and NPCs within a radius of 9 tiles, causing them to emit red hearts for 30 seconds. It also increases affected NPCs' happiness by 10% for the duration of the effect.
Its counterpart is the Stink Potion.
Luck Potions: The Luck Potions are three types of buff potions which grant the Lucky buff, increasing the player's luck. This lasts for 5–15 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

Consuming a Lesser, regular, or Greater Luck Potion grants 5, 10, or 15 minutes of the Lucky buff, respectively. The buff is unique in that its effectiveness depends on the remaining duration, which is shown below:
The values do not stack, and the only difference between the Luck Potions is the duration of the effect:
Consuming a Lesser Luck Potion (5 minutes of Lucky) gives +0.1 luck for 5 minutes.
Consuming a regular Luck Potion (10 minutes of Lucky) gives +0.2 luck for 5 minutes, then +0.1 luck for 5 minutes.
Consuming a Greater Luck Potion (15 minutes of Lucky) gives +0.3 luck for 5 minutes, then +0.2 luck for 5 minutes, and then +0.1 luck for 5 minutes.
Lucky Clover: The Lucky Clover is an item rarely obtained from cutting tall grass. It increases the player's luck by 0.03 while it is in their inventory or opened Void Bag. Having more than one Lucky Clover does not increase luck any further.
Lucky Coin: The Lucky Coin is a Hardmode accessory. While equipped, it causes enemies to drop extra coins when damaged and grants the player +0.05 luck.

It has a 1/2000 (0.05%) chance to be dropped by pirates (except Parrots) during Pirate Invasions, with a 1/500 (0.2%) chance from the Pirate Captain. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be dropped by the Flying Dutchman.

With the Lucky Coin equipped, there is a 1/5 (20%) chance that 1 to 10 extra coins of the same type will drop each time the player damages an enemy. Each time extra coins drop, the following probabilities determine the coin type:
Lucky Horseshoe: The Lucky Horseshoe is an accessory that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being found inside Skyware Chests on Floating Islands, as well as a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Sky Crates and Azure Crates. While equipped, it negates fall damage and grants +0.05 luck. This bonus does not stack with any of its upgrades.
Lucy the Axe: Lucy the Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. She occasionally displays a line of dialogue depending on certain player actions. Lucy the Axe also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Her best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Luminite: Luminite is a Hardmode ore dropped by the Moon Lord in stacks of 70–90 (90–110). It does not naturally generate in the world, and can be mined using any pickaxe.

Crafting all items (excluding ammunition, dye, and bricks) requires a total of 362 Luminite Bars and 25 Luminite (1,473 Luminite; requires defeating the Moon Lord 17–22 / 14–17 times). Crafting all items pertaining to one type of Lunar Fragment (i.e., armor, wings, pickaxe/drill, and hamaxe) requires 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite) in addition to 85 of the Lunar Fragment; this requires defeating the Moon Lord only 4 / 3–4 times.
Luminite Arrow: The Luminite Arrow is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord arrow. When a Luminite Arrow dissipates, a Luminite Arrow Trail projectile will be fired after a short delay which copies the arrow's flying trail and deals the same base damage as the arrow. The Luminite Arrow and its trail can pierce 3 enemies, and their damage decreases by 4% per enemy pierced. Both the arrow and its trail also dissipate upon contact with blocks or after 0.75 seconds.
Luminite Axes: Luminite Axes are unobtainable tools. The four types are the Solar Flare Axe, Vortex Axe, Nebula Axe, and the Stardust Axe, each themed after a different Celestial Tower. They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes. Even with Terrasavr and some other inventory editors, they seem to disappear, leaving an empty slot.
Their best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Luminite Bar: The Luminite Bar is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord bar.

Crafting all items pertaining to one type of Lunar Fragment (i.e., armor, wings, pickaxe, and hamaxe) requires 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite) in addition to 85 of the Lunar Fragment; this requires defeating the Moon Lord 4 / 3–4 times.
Luminite Brick: Luminite Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Despite being made of Luminite, the highest tier of ore, it has no sell value. It can be used to craft Luminite Brick Walls.
Luminite Brick Wall: Luminite Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Luminite Bricks. It stops enemies from spawning on the tile where it's placed. It can be used to make houses for NPCs.
Luminite Bullet: The Luminite Bullet is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord bullet. The Luminite Bullet can hit an infinite number of targets. The damage of the Luminite Bullet decreases by 4% each time it hits a target. This can reduce its damage down to 0, but it will continue to travel. It will disappear after 1.67 seconds or upon hitting a block.
Luminite Chainsaws: Luminite Chainsaws are unobtainable tools. All of the chainsaws share the same stats. The four types are the Solar Flare Chainsaw, Vortex Chainsaw, Nebula Chainsaw, and the Stardust Chainsaw, each themed after different Celestial Pillars. They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes.
Like all axes and chainsaws, they are used to cut down Trees, Cacti, and Giant Glowing Mushrooms, so the best possible modifier is Godly.

With current methods, it is impossible to hack these items into a character's inventory using external editors, as they will disappear from that character's inventory as soon as they load into a world.
Luminite Drills: The Luminite Drills are Hardmode, post-Moon Lord drills. The four types are the Vortex Drill, Nebula Drill, Solar Flare Drill, and Stardust Drill. They are the alternative versions of the Luminite Pickaxes, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. All four drills have identical stats and can mine all blocks.
Their best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Luminite Hamaxes: The Luminite Hamaxes are post-Moon Lord hamaxes. The four types are the Solar Flare Hamaxe, the Vortex Hamaxe, the Nebula Hamaxe, and the Stardust Hamaxe. All share the same stats.
They have the highest hammer power in the game, along with The Axe. They are beaten only by The Axe in axe power, making them the second-strongest axes.
Their best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for these tools.
Luminite Hammers: Luminite Hammers are unobtainable tools. The four types are the Solar Flare Hammer, Vortex Hammer, Nebula Hammer, and the Stardust Hammer, each themed after a different Celestial Tower. They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes.
Luminite Pickaxes: Luminite Pickaxes are Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pickaxes. The four types are the Solar Flare Pickaxe, Vortex Pickaxe, Nebula Pickaxe, and Stardust Pickaxe. They are the alternate versions of the Luminite Drills, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. All four pickaxes have identical stats and can mine all blocks.
Their best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for these tools.
Luna's set: Luna's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Luna ("RunicPixels"), who is an artist at Re-Logic.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Luna's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to her clothing set:
Lunar Flare: The Lunar Flare is a Hardmode spell book that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When used, it summons a spread of three lunar flares that rain down towards the cursor. The flares explode upon impact with enemies and blocks, but can pass through blocks until they have reached the cursor's location, then exploding.
Lunar Hook: The Lunar Hook is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist grappling hook crafted from Lunar Fragments. It has four glowing hooks which can be launched simultaneously and reach up to 34.375 tiles. Each hook is themed after one of the four Celestial Pillars.
Lunar Portal Staff: The Lunar Portal Staff is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord summon weapon that summons a Lunar Portal sentry. It continuously fires beams that sweep across enemies, which pierce infinite enemies but cannot pass through blocks. Unlike most sentries, the Lunar Portal floats midair. The Lunar Portal Staff has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord.
Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 164% (including whip bonuses) or 64% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.
Lunar Rust Brick: Lunar Rust Brick is a type of decorative brick obtained by throwing Luminite Brick into Shimmer during a Waning Gibbous.
Lunar Rust Brick Wall: Lunar Rust Brick Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Lunar Rust Bricks.
Lunatic Cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is a Hardmode, post-Golem boss. Defeating it initiates the Lunar Events, and also causes the Clothier to begin selling the Solar and Lunar Cultist sets depending on the time of day.

Unlike most bosses, the Lunatic Cultist does not drop any weapons, accessories, or materials. However, it does drop the Ancient Manipulator, a placeable crafting station used to craft many endgame items.
While the Lunatic Cultist is alive, its exclusive music Lunatic Cultist will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Lunatic Devotee: The Cultists are Hardmode, post-Golem enemies that spawn along with a Mysterious Tablet at the entrance to the Dungeon after Skeletron and Golem have been defeated. Four Cultists will appear there: two Cultist Archers and two Lunatic Devotees. Defeating all four of the Cultists causes the Lunatic Cultist to spawn instantly at their location, destroying the Mysterious Tablet in the process. Defeating the Lunatic Cultist then initiates the Lunar Events.

Until one of the Cultists is attacked, they are passive and deal no contact damage, and players can walk through them freely without activating them. Attacking any of the four will awaken the Archers, who will begin to fire Wooden Arrows using bows and will deal contact damage. Lunatic Devotees are always passive and never deal contact damage.

All four Cultists respawn and reset their location and initial passive state after 12 minutes (12 in-game hours), if the Lunatic Cultist was not summoned, if the player runs away or dies during the fight, when all four Celestial Pillars are destroyed, or when the world is closed and restarted. Restarting the world can be the fastest option to reset them to their original state.
The Lunatic Devotee and Cultist Archer require 25 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entries and corresponding banners, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Macaws: The Scarlet Macaw and Blue Macaw are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. They may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Macaws have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Macaws can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scarlet / Blue Macaw Cage). Once crafted, the Macaws cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Macaws can be spawned by the Macaw Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Mace: The Mace is a pre-Hardmode flail found in Gold Chests located in the underground or cavern layer.
Its best modifier is Ruthless. Godly and Demonic modifiers may give higher crit chance, but rounding causes Ruthless to have much higher damage for this weapon.
Maggot: The Maggot is a critter that replaces Worms in the Graveyard biome, and can also be spawned from Maggot Zombies when they are killed. The Maggot has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Maggot can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Maggot Cage). Once crafted, the Maggot cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Maggot can be used as bait for fishing, with 22% bait power.
Maggot Zombie: The Maggot Zombie is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a Zombie variant that spawns in the Graveyard mini-biome. When a Maggot Zombie is killed, up to three Maggots will be spawned. Maggot Zombies have a more dreadful and rotten appearance than other Zombies, and is implied that it is missing an eye, due to its sprite depicting a Maggot crawling through it.
Magic Conch: The Magic Conch is a tool that teleports the player to the Ocean that is furthest away from them, 0.75 seconds (45 ticks) after being used. Like the Magic Mirror and Demon Conch, it can be used an unlimited amount of times. The Magic Conch can be found in Sandstone Chests in the top 4/7ths of the Underground Desert and Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis.
Magic Cuffs: The Magic Cuffs are a pre-Hardmode accessory that grant the following effects while equipped:
Restores mana when the player takes damage. Mana restored is equal to the damage of the attack before factoring defense and damage reduction.
Magic Dagger: The Magic Dagger is a Hardmode magic weapon that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by Mimics. When used, it rapidly fires Magic Dagger projectiles that travel in a straight line in the direction of the cursor for 24 tiles, then suddenly become affected by gravity. The projectiles can hit up to 3 enemies and cannot pass through blocks.
Magic Droppers: Magic Droppers are Hardmode items used to place "droplets" — dripping liquid effects on ceilings. Once placed, they permanently display an intermittent dripping effect. The effect is purely visual, and has no functional use. Magic Droppers are crafted with an Empty Dropper at Water, Lava, Honey, or with any Sand, with the Crystal Ball nearby. The Magic Shimmer Dropper is an exception, crafted by throwing an Empty Dropper into the Shimmer.
Magic Droppers can be placed at the bottom side of a block, consuming the item in the process. Droplets can be removed by mining them with a pickaxe, but doing so will not drop any item.

Droplets are also naturally generated in random areas on world generation. They spawn below ceilings that have their corresponding liquid above them, as though that liquid were "leaking through". Natural droplets can be mined just like the player-placed version, and similarly drip indefinitely until removed by a player.
Magic Hat: The Magic Hat is a pre-Hardmode armor piece that can be equipped in the helmet slot. While equipped, it grants +2 defense and increases the player's magic damage and magic critical strike chance by 6% each. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 Gold.

The Magic Hat is part of the Wizard set, which further consists of a Mystic Robe or any gem-augmented Robe. The Wizard set provides a Set Bonus of +60 maximum mana with the Magic Hat equipped. The Magic Hat's alternative is the Wizard Hat.
Magic Lantern: The Magic Lantern is a light pet-summoning item that spawns a small glowing Magic Lantern which hovers above the player, emitting dim yellow light. The lantern will also highlight all treasure within up to 15 tiles from the lantern's location, overlaying small yellow sparkles over nearby valuable treasure, which is similar to the sparkling effect produced by a Spelunker Potion. The Magic Lantern can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 10 Gold during the night of a full moon.

The lantern will always try to maintain a position just forward of and above the player, passing through blocks as needed. If the player is far enough away or in midair, the lantern will propel itself with a rocket exhaust in order to catch up to them. The lantern's position can block objects of interest at ceiling height, but if the player just turns around, the lantern will move to their other side.
Magic Mirrors: The Magic Mirror is a pre-Hardmode tool. When used, it plays an animation before teleporting the player to their spawn point. Compared to the Recall Potion, the Magic Mirror has unlimited uses, but a delay of 0.75 seconds (45 ticks), which is longer than the Recall Potion's 0.167 seconds (10 ticks) before teleporting.
The Ice Mirror (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a functionally identical alternative to the Magic Mirror.

Magic Mirrors can be found in Chests generated in the Underground and Cavern layers. Ice Mirrors can be found in Frozen Chests generated in the Ice biome. Newly created characters in Journey Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) spawn with a Magic Mirror.
Magic Missile: The Magic Missile is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron wand. When used, it fires a magic missile that follows the cursor when ⚒ Use / Attack key is held. If the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released mid-drag, the missile will be fired in that direction. If the cursor is stationary on release, it is fired directly away from the player. Once it is released, the missile homes in on nearby enemies, creating a small explosion upon contact with an enemy or block. The Magic Missile has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes.
Magic Power Potion: The Magic Power Potion is a buff potion which grants the Magic Power buff when consumed. The buff increases magic damage by 20%. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Magic Power Potions can be found in Pots and Shadow Chests in The Underworld.
Magic Quiver: The Magic Quiver is a Hardmode accessory that boosts arrow- and Stake-firing weapons. It has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped from Skeleton Archers.
When equipped, it grants the following bonuses to arrows, Stakes, and the weapons that fire them:
+10% damage, to both the ammo and the weapon
+120% velocity in total (does not fully affect certain projectiles; see Notes for details)
Magic String: The Magic String is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss accessory that can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 1 Platinum. While equipped, all yoyos and counterweights are thrown when ⚒ Use / Attack is released, instead of being retracted. The released projectiles deal 75% of their initial damage and knockback, and can bounce and roll on blocks and platforms.
Magic Yoyo Bag: The Magic Yoyo Bag is a Hardmode accessory that combines the effects of Magic String and the Yoyo Bag. It grants the following effects while equipped:
+25% yoyo range, with an additional +2 tiles
Creates a duplicate yoyo upon the first enemy hit with a yoyo
Creates a counterweight upon the second enemy hit with a yoyo, and a duplicate counterweight upon the third enemy hit

When yoyos run out of spin duration or when ⚒ Use / Attack is released, all active yoyos and counterweights will be thrown instead of being retracted, dealing 75% of their initial damage and knockback, and bouncing and rolling on blocks and platforms
Magical Harp: The Magical Harp is a Hardmode magic weapon that autofires ricocheting, piercing projectiles that graphically resemble purple musical notes. Each projectile lasts for 3 seconds before dissipating and will both ricochet infinitely and pierce enemies up to 5 times.
