The Magical Harp's musical notes gain a 5% damage penalty for each enemy hit. Notes produce a reasonable amount of purple light and are not affected by gravity.

Notes are initially at a high speed until they go a variable distance, equivalent to the distance between the player and the cursor, where they slow down. Additionally, initial note velocity is set so the amount of time until the note reaches the cursor is constant. The Magical Harp also plays sound while firing that resembles plucked strings, with a pitch that correlates to the distance of the cursor.
Magical Pumpkin Seed: The Magical Pumpkin Seed is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Squashling that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Squashling will twirl and fly after the player to catch up to them. The Magical Pumpkin Seed has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being obtained from harvesting fully-grown Pumpkins during the Halloween seasonal event.
Magiluminescence: The Magiluminescence is a pre-Hardmode accessory that increases the player's maximum movement speed by 15% and their acceleration and deceleration by 75%. This increase stacks with the bonus of the Hermes Boots and their variants. It also creates an aura of light around the player, which can be useful when exploring underground. The Magiluminescence's movement speed buffs are disabled when the player is not grounded.
Magma Skull: The Magma Skull is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Burning debuff. It also grants immunity to lava for 7 seconds.
Magma Snail: The Magma Snail is a critter that spawns in The Underworld. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld. The Magma Snail emits light. The Magma Snail has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Magma Snail can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net or the Golden Bug Net. Trying to catch it with a standard Bug Net will only set the player on fire. After being caught, it can be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Magma Snail Cage). Once crafted, the Magma Snail cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Magma Snail can be used as bait for fishing, with 35% bait power. Using it as bait also allows fishing in lava.
Magma Stone: The Magma Stone is an accessory that causes the wearer's melee attacks to inflict the Hellfire debuff for up to 6 seconds on enemies. In PvP, only direct hits from melee weapons can inflict the Hellfire debuff, while melee projectiles instead inflict the On Fire! debuff; both debuffs last up to 6 seconds against other players. The Magma Stone also adds orange flame particle effects on the sprites of both the weapon and its projectiles, giving off light. It has a 1/50 (2%) chance to be dropped by Lava Bats and a 1/150 (0.67%) chance to be dropped by Hellbats in The Underworld.
Magnet Flower: The Magnet Flower is a pre-Hardmode accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:
Automatically consumes mana potions in the player's inventory or opened Void Bag when mana is depleted.
Increases the pickup range for Stars by 18.75 tiles.
Magnet Sphere: The Magnet Sphere is a Hardmode, post-Plantera spell book that has a 1/300 (0.33%) / 599/90,000 (0.6656%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Rusty Armored Bones, and Hell Armored Bones in the post-Plantera Dungeon. When used, it fires a slow-moving cyan sphere that rapidly fires instantaneous, non-piercing beams at the closest enemy as it travels. It passes through all enemies and bounces off solid blocks. The sphere dissipates after 15 seconds have passed, it has traveled 52 tiles, or when another sphere is fired.

Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Magnet Sphere's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.
Maid set: The Maid set is a vanity set consisting of the Maid Bonnet, Maid Dress and Maid Shoes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Malaise: The Malaise is a pre-Hardmode yoyo.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Artery. The Malaise has slightly higher knockback and spin duration than the Artery, but slightly lower damage and reach.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Mallard Duck: The Duck and Mallard Duck are critters. They can usually only spawn in the middle third of the above-ground world, or in areas near an NPC's house if water is present. They only appear in pools of water, regardless of their size or if they are naturally generated. They quite frequently make a "quack" sound when nearby. Ducks may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.

Ducks will passively wander the surface until they fall a certain distance or are submerged, at which point they will switch to their alternate flying form, where they will fly in a given direction for a certain amount of time before landing and switching back to their passive form. Despite their spawn conditions, they do not prioritize water whenever landing.
Ducks have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Ducks can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Duck / Mallard Duck Cage). Once crafted, the Ducks cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Ducks can be spawned by the Duck Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Man Eater: The Man Eater is a pre-Hardmode enemy found in the Underground Jungle, and is nearly identical in appearance and behavior to the above-ground Snatcher. Man Eaters spawn anchored to blocks, with an extendable stem topped by a pincher. The stem itself is a passive component and can be walked through safely without incurring damage; only the pincher inflicts or takes damage.
Mana Cloak: The Mana Cloak is a Hardmode accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:
Automatically consume mana potions from the player's inventory or open Void Bag when mana is depleted.
Causes three stars to fall around the player upon taking damage. (See #Taking damage.)
Causes one star to fall near enemies struck with a magic weapon, which then transform into a Mana Cloak Star power-up that is similar to Stars. (See #Dealing damage.)
Mana Crystal: The Mana Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's maximum mana by 20, up to a maximum of 200 total. It takes 9 Mana Crystals to reach this maximum. It also restores 20 mana when used, but only as long as the character's maximum mana is below 200. Mana Crystals are created by combining 5 Fallen Stars. It takes 45 Fallen Stars to maximize the player's mana.
Mana Flower: The Mana Flower is a pre-Hardmode accessory that reduces mana cost by 8%, and automatically consumes mana potions in the player's inventory or opened Void Bag when mana is depleted.
Mana Potion: The Mana Potion is a recovery potion that restores 100 mana and inflicts the Mana Sickness debuff upon use. It can be crafted or occasionally obtained from any Crates except for Wooden and Pearlwood Crates. They are also sold by the Merchant in Hardmode for 2 Silver 50 Copper.
It is the second tier of mana potion, succeeding the Lesser Mana Potion, and preceding the Greater Mana Potion and Super Mana Potion.
Mana Regeneration Band: The Mana Regeneration Band is an accessory item made by combining a Band of Starpower and a Band of Regeneration at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Mana Regeneration Potion: The Mana Regeneration Potion is a buff potion which grants the Mana Regeneration buff when consumed. The buff increases the rate at which the player's mana regenerates. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Mana Regeneration Potions can be found in Pots and Shadow Chests in The Underworld.
Mandible Blade: The Mandible Blade is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Antlion Chargers and Antlion Swarmers. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapon in direction of the cursor, which can travel forward for 0.25 seconds before sharply dropping down. The Mandible Blade has a base 11% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Mango: The Mango is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Mahogany tree.
Mannequin: The Mannequin is a furniture item that can be used to display armor, weapons, and vanity items, as well as accessories and dyes.

Items can be placed on a Mannequin by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, which opens a small set of inventory-like slots beneath the player's main inventory. There are three slots for helmet, shirt, and pants, five slots for accessories, and one slot for weapons. In addition, each slot besides the weapons slot has an associated dye slot underneath it. Placing items in these slots immediately displays them on the Mannequin.
Mannequins can only be removed if no items are placed on them.
The Mannequin always displays armor and clothing in their male sprite forms. The Womannequin can be used to display them in their female counterparts.
The pose of a Mannequin can be changed by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on it whilst holding any hammer. This changes its appearance, as well as the position of the weapon that it is holding.
Marble Block: The Marble Block is a natural block found in Marble Caves. It can be crafted into Smooth Marble Blocks in order to craft the Marble-themed furniture set.
Marble Chest: The Marble Chest is a chest storage item found only in Underground Cabins within Marble Caves. Like Granite Chests and Rich Mahogany Chests, Marble Chests have exactly the same loot as Gold Chests.
Marble Wall: The Marble Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Marble Caves, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be generated as part of an Underground Cabin in a Marble Cave, considered safe. It is also considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Maroon Graduation set: The Maroon Graduation set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Maroon Graduation Cap and the Maroon Graduation Gown. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) during a Waxing Crescent.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Marrow: The Marrow is a Hardmode bow that has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance to be dropped by Skeleton Archers. When used, it converts any type of arrow into high-velocity Bone Arrows that shatter into 2 bone shards upon hitting enemies or blocks, each of which deals 25% of the weapon's damage (11 base damage when using Wooden Arrows) but does not inflict knockback. The bone shards do not pierce and are launched away from the struck enemy or block, in addition to being heavily affected by gravity. The Marrow has a base 9% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.
Marshmallow: The Marshmallow is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 1 minute, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Marshmallows can be purchased from the Merchant for 1 Silver each when he is spoken to in a Snow biome.
The Marshmallow is also a crafting material used to craft the Marshmallow on a Stick, which can be turned into a Cooked Marshmallow at a Campfire, greatly extending its buff duration.
Marshmallow on a Stick: The Marshmallow on a Stick is an item that is used to create a Cooked Marshmallow by holding it over any lit Campfire, i.e. the Marshmallow must overlap with the 2×3-tile rectangle of the Campfire. It must be held for up to 15 seconds. The Marshmallow on a Stick must be held by the player, either by attaching it to the cursor in the inventory or selecting it in the hotbar, for the entire duration over the Campfire in order for it to be cooked. Selecting a different item in the hotbar, moving/turning away from the Campfire, or turning the Campfire off resets the timer.
The exact cooking duration is randomized and can last between 7.5 seconds and 15 seconds. The average cooking duration is 12.5 seconds.
Martian Conduit Plating: Martian Conduit Plating is a post-Golem block dropped by most enemies during the Martian Madness event, and is used to create a variety of space- or Martian-themed furniture.
Like Spooky Wood, it can only be obtained during its respective event; it can only be crafted by uncrafting its platforms and wall.
When placed in dark areas, the block has a notable pulsating light effect.
Crafting all pieces of furniture requires 161 Martian Conduit Plating blocks.
Martian Conduit Wall: Martian Conduit Wall is a background wall type crafted from Martian Conduit Plating. It emits a faint glow when placed.
Martian Costume set: The Martian Costume set is a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity set consisting of the Martian Costume Mask, Martian Costume Shirt, and Martian Costume Pants. Each piece has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Gray Grunts, Ray Gunners, Scutlix Gunners, and Brain Scramblers during the Martian Madness event.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Martian Drone: The Martian Drone is a Hardmode, post-Golem flying enemy that spawns during the Martian Madness event. It can move through solid blocks, and when it is positioned lower than the player, flies directly towards a point just above the player. After reaching this point, or the player is positioned lower than the Martian Drone, it will dive down towards the player. Once it gets close enough to the player, it self-destructs, dealing area-of-effect damage. Martian Drones do not contribute progress towards the Martian Madness event if they self-destruct.
Martian Dye: Martian Dye is a Hardmode, post-Golem dye that is sometimes acquired from the Dye Trader after completing a Strange Plant quest. It is only obtainable after completing a Martian Madness event. When equipped, it gives items a cyan and white color palette which glows in the dark.
The brightness of the glow depends on how close each color in the color palette is to cyan. Pure cyan glows at full brightness, while pure white does not glow at all.
Martian Engineer: The Martian Engineer is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that appears during the Martian Madness event. Martian Engineers have the ability to build Tesla Turrets around them.
Martian Officer: The Martian Officer is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that spawns during the Martian Madness event. It will always initially spawn with a protective Bubble Shield, which provides the Officer significantly added defense and hit points, as well as immunity to lava and knockback, until it is depleted. After the Bubble Shield is destroyed, the Officer can now actually be harmed. If the Martian Officer is not killed within three seconds after the Bubble Shield is depleted, the Bubble Shield will reactivate with full strength. The Officer's health will not be restored.
Martian Probe: The Martian Probe is a rare Hardmode, post-Golem flying enemy that can spawn above the surface in the outer two thirds of the world, most commonly in the Space layers. The Martian Probe initially appears with a green light. When it detects the player, the light turns red, it gains the ability to pass through blocks, and attempts to escape. If allowed to, it initiates the Martian Madness event.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Martian Saucer: The Martian Saucer is a Hardmode, post-Golem mini-boss that spawns during the Martian Madness event after it is at least 30% completed. The Martian Saucer hovers in the air and can pass through blocks. It has four turrets that must be destroyed individually: two rocket launchers and two laser machine guns. In addition, the Martian Saucer itself fires a “Martian Deathray”, a large yellow beam that can only be fired directly downwards and cannot be destroyed independently.
Martian Uniform set: The Martian Uniform set is a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity set consisting of the Martian Uniform Helmet, Martian Uniform Torso, and Martian Uniform Pants. Each piece has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Gigazappers, Martian Engineers, and Martian Officers during the Martian Madness event.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Martian Walker: The Martian Walker is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that spawns during the Martian Madness event. It appears as a large tripod enemy that moves at a very fast pace and fires rapid barrages of blue Laser Rays at the player.
Masks: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot.
Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions:
The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag.
The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage.
The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.
Master Gamer's set: The Master Gamer's set is a vanity set consisting of the Master Gamer's Jacket and the Master Gamer's Pants. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold (set).
Master Ninja Gear: The Master Ninja Gear is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that combines the abilities of the Black Belt, the Tabi, and the Tiger Climbing Gear. It allows the player to cling to and slide down vertical walls, quickly dash short distances by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right key, or the Dash button once, and offers a 1/10 (10%) chance to automatically dodge enemy attacks. There is a one-second cooldown period between dashes.
Meat Grinder: The Meat Grinder is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Flesh Blocks and Lesion Blocks. It has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by several Crimson and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Corruption enemies.

Flesh and Lesion Blocks can be used as building materials, and crafted into flesh-/lesion-themed walls and furniture via the Decay Chamber/Flesh Cloning Vat. As a result, the Meat Grinder is of little use without them.
Mechanic: The Mechanic is an NPC vendor who sells wire, actuators, and various mechanisms, as well as Wire Cutters and Wrenches, allowing the player to construct and activate wired devices like traps and critter engines. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

Rescuing her as the Bound Mechanic, who can be rarely encountered in the Dungeon in the Cavern layer and below after Skeletron has been defeated. Interacting with her in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will free her. If the Bound Mechanic is killed, she will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Mechanic NPC is killed, she will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.

The Mechanic will defend herself against nearby enemies with her Combat Wrench. She deals 11 / 16 / 19 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Mechanic also has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping the Combat Wrench upon death.
The Bound Mechanic is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Mechanical Battery Piece: The Mechanical Battery Piece is one of three parts needed to craft the Minecart Upgrade Kit. It is always dropped from Skeletron Prime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Mechanical Eye: The Mechanical Eye is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons The Twins when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night.
If the Twins have not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Eye.
Mechanical Glove: The Mechanical Glove is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses accessory. While equipped, it grants the following effects:
Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips
Mechanical Lens: The Mechanical Lens is an informational accessory which reveals placed Wire and Actuators. Each color of Wire can be shown at maximum brightness, regular, or faded, which is configurable via toggles. The Mechanical Lens is purchased from the Mechanic for 1 Gold.
Mechanical Ruler: The Mechanical Ruler is an informational accessory that, when equipped, draws a cyan, semi-transparent grid overlay on the screen, making individual block distances much clearer. This grid fades out when the player begins moving and returns once movement stops. The row and column of the block the mouse is hovering over are also highlighted in red, drawing a cross on the screen with the cursor at its center. The Mechanical Ruler can be purchased from the Mechanic for 1 Gold.
When the Mechanical Ruler is in the inventory or equipped, a toggle for controlling its function appears to the left of the main inventory / in the tools menu below the inventory.
Mechanical Skull: The Mechanical Skull is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Skeletron Prime when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night.
If Skeletron Prime has not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Skull.
Mechanical Wagon Piece: The Mechanical Wagon Piece is one of three parts needed to craft the Minecart Upgrade Kit. It is always dropped from The Destroyer's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Mechanical Wheel Piece: The Mechanical Wheel Piece is one of three parts needed to craft the Minecart Upgrade Kit. It is always dropped from The Twins' Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Mechanical Worm: The Mechanical Worm is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons The Destroyer when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night.
If the Destroyer has not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Worm.
Medicated Bandage: The Medicated Bandage is an immunity accessory that combines the functions of the Adhesive Bandage and the Bezoar. This item grants immunity to any Bleeding and Poison debuffs.
It is one of the ingredients required to make the Ankh Charm, which is further required to make the Ankh Shield.

While the Medicated Bandage is exclusive to Hardmode on the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, it can be obtained in pre-Hardmode on the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, as it is possible to obtain the Adhesive Bandage by throwing the Bezoar into Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Medusa: Medusa is a Hardmode enemy found near Marble Caves, and is a relatively fast-moving melee attacker who has the unique ability to inflict the Stoned debuff through her gaze. This debuff deals 20 / 40 / 60 damage to the player and petrifies them, turning them into stone.
The player will be unable to move or use items for the duration of the debuff, similar to the Frozen debuff.
Fall damage-negating accessories are disabled, fall damage is increased, and the minimum distance for fall damage to occur is reduced.

The debuff's onset is marked by Medusa's snake hair (as well as Medusa herself) lashing out red tongues, accompanied by a unique noise and a yellow particle effect, giving players notice before they are petrified. Players can avoid getting Stoned by facing the other direction when the animation completes, or by having Medusa's line of sight blocked by solid blocks.
The less health Medusa has, the faster she will move, similar to Mummies. Her speed increases linearly from 8 mph at full health to 18 mph just before dying.
She is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Medusa Head: The Medusa Head is a Hardmode magic weapon that continuously fires close-range yellow beams up to four times per second, hitting up to three enemies per attack within a 20-tile radius of the player. 15 mana is consumed per each attack, regardless of the number of enemies struck. No mana is consumed if the Medusa Head is used while no enemies are within range. The Medusa Head has a 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Medusa.
Megaphone: The Megaphone is an immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Silenced debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Pixies, Green Jellyfish, Dark Mummies, and Blood Mummies. While these are all Hardmode-exclusive enemies, the Megaphone can already be obtained in pre-Hardmode via Shimmer.
Megashark: The Megashark is a Hardmode, post-The Destroyer gun and the direct upgrade to the Minishark. When used, it fires bullets very rapidly in a small spread. It also has a 50% chance not to consume ammunition.
Meowmere: The Meowmere is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When swung, it fires a cat head projectile with a visual rainbow trail every 0.23 seconds. The cat head deals 125% of the weapon's damage (250 base damage), is affected by gravity, and can pierce enemies or bounce off blocks up to four times. Upon bouncing off a block, the cat head makes a "meow" sound and emits damaging rainbow explosions that grow in size with each bounce.
Merchant: The Merchant is an NPC vendor who will move in once the following conditions have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

All players in the current world have more than 50 Silver total between them in their inventories. Coins stored in chests and portable storage items like the Piggy Bank do not count toward this requirement.
These requirements only apply to the initial spawning. If the Merchant is killed, he will automatically respawn after some time.
The Merchant will defend himself against nearby enemies by lobbing Throwing Knives. He deals 12 / 18 / 21 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
Mercury Brick: Mercury Brick is a type of decorative brick obtained by throwing Luminite Brick into Shimmer during a New Moon.
Mercury Brick Wall: Mercury Brick Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Mercury Bricks.
Mermaid set: The Mermaid set is a vanity set composed of the Seashell Hairpin, Mermaid Adornment, and Mermaid Tail. The complete set is awarded randomly for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Metal Detector: The Metal Detector is an informational accessory that detects valuable objects, including ores, chests, Life Crystals, and Life Fruit, within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the player. The Metal Detector displays the specific type of what was detected, for instance, "Chlorophyte detected nearby!" When multiple valuables are detected, only the one with the highest value is noted.
The Metal Detector has a 1/2 (50%) / 100% chance of being dropped by Nymphs, a rare cavern enemy.
Meteor Hamaxe: The Meteor Hamaxe is a pre-Hardmode hamaxe. It combines the functionality of a hammer and an axe.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Meteor Head: The Meteor Head is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy that only spawns in a Meteorite biome. They override all other enemy spawns in the biome, except the Ocean biome. Once only 74 blocks of Meteorite remain, the area is no longer considered a Meteorite biome. Therefore, Meteor Heads will no longer spawn.

Meteor Heads follow the Flying AI, and slowly float towards the player while passing through solid blocks. They inflict large amounts of damage upon contact with the player, and have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff for 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds.
Meteor Shot: The Meteor Shot is a pre-Hardmode bullet. When fired, it can either bounce from a solid block once or pierce through one enemy, but not both.
Meteor Staff: The Meteor Staff is a Hardmode wand. When used, it rapidly summons meteors from the sky which fall in the direction of the cursor and explode upon impact with an enemy or block.
Meteor armor: Meteor armor is a pre-Hardmode mage armor set consisting of the Meteor Helmet, Meteor Suit, and Meteor Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 45 Meteorite Bars (135 Meteorite).
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Reduces the mana cost of the Space Gun, Laser Rifle, Gray Zapinator, and Orange Zapinator to 0
Immunity to meteorite projectiles during the Meteor Shower event
The player also leaves behind a visual trail of flames.
Meteorite: Meteorite is a pre-Hardmode ore typically mined from Meteorite crash sites. It also spawns in high numbers during a Meteor Shower and rarely drops from Meteor Heads. A Meteorite crash site is a mini-biome guaranteed to spawn after the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu is defeated for the first time. If the boss is defeated between midnight and dawn (12:00 AM – 4:30 AM), then the meteor crashes immediately. Otherwise, it will crash at the next midnight (12:00 AM). Meteorite can be mined using a Tungsten Pickaxe or better (its counterpart, the Silver Pickaxe, does not have enough pickaxe power).

Contact with Meteorite blocks causes the player to be inflicted with the Burning debuff, unless the player has the Obsidian Skull accessory (or its upgrades) equipped, or is using an Obsidian Skin Potion.
Meteorite Bar: The Meteorite Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. In addition to being crafted, Meteorite Bars can also be found as common items in Shadow Chests, or more rarely in Gold Chests in the Cavern layer that generate close to the Underworld.
Meteorite Brick: Meteorite Brick is a type of decorative brick crafted with Meteorite. It emits a small amount of light when placed.
Unlike plain Meteorite, Meteorite Bricks do not inflict the Burning debuff or deal damage to players on contact. They are vulnerable to explosions.
Meteorite Brick Wall: Meteorite Brick Wall is a wall made from crafting Meteorite Bricks at a Work Bench. It emits light when placed.
Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.
Midnight Confetti Block: The Midnight Confetti Block is an animated block type showing falling confetti. It is one of the few items that uses the Crystal Ball as a crafting station. It is a dark, non-transparent version of the Confetti Block.
Midnight Confetti Wall: Midnight Confetti Walls are a type of background wall made from Midnight Confetti Blocks. They depict falling confetti.They are one of only a few animated background walls. Confetti Walls are a transparent version of them.
Midnight Rainbow Dye: Midnight Rainbow Dye is a dye that creates a "reverse" rainbow effect that waves throughout the colors of the spectrum. This dye can be earned by trading a Strange Plant with the Dye Trader after defeating the Martian Madness event.
Milkshake: The Milkshake is a Hardmode food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Milkshake has a 1/75 (1.33%) chance of being dropped by Ice Tortoises and Icy Mermen.
Milkyway Weaver: The Milkyway Weaver is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist, worm enemy that spawns in the area of the Stardust Pillar during the Lunar Events. It is similar to the Solar Pillar's Crawltipede, in that it is completely unaffected by gravity and floats freely through the air. However, it is much smaller than the Crawltipede, targets players anywhere instead of only in the air, and rather than its tail, its head is its only vulnerable part.

While the Milkyway Weaver attacks primarily by trying to charge towards the player to inflict contact damage, it slows down after chasing the player for 5.42 seconds. During this time, it charges up for 4.58 seconds while emitting an increasingly bright blue glimmer before summoning certain Stardust Pillar enemies in a constellation pattern, similar to the Stardust Pillar's own summoning attack. It resumes chasing the player after summoning an enemy and repeats its attack cycle.
Mime Mask: The Mime Mask is a vanity item equipped in the Social Helmet slot. It is purchased from the Clothier during a Blood Moon for 2 Gold.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) The game does not display the Mime Mask as a vanity item.
Mimic: Mimics are rare Hardmode enemies disguised as Chests, appearing as the appropriate chest type for the environment.
Mimics can be spawned by the player using the Chest Statue, even in pre-Hardmode. However, Mimics spawned this way only drop the Mimic Banner.
Rarer Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics can also be spawned manually by players via a Key of Light or Key of Night (see the Biome Mimic section below).

They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed Mimics require 25 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Minecart Track: Minecart Tracks are placeable furniture-type blocks that allow for rapid transportation over long distances. They form a continuous track when placed next to each other, and form slopes when placed diagonally. Although they cannot be walked on, they can be grappled using a hook.
Minecart Tracks generate in large quantities in Abandoned Minecart Tracks (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), but can also be obtained via crafting.

When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key.

To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff (right-clicking the icon, selecting the icon and canceling it in the equipment menu, double-tapping the icon, or canceling the buff from the buffs screen). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways.
Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart.
The player can alternatively move on top of Minecart Tracks using Roller Skates.
Minecart Upgrade Kit: The Minecart Upgrade Kit is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses permanent booster item that permanently unlocks a boost for all Minecarts, including a speed increase, extra defense when moving, and a laser attack. It also drops a Mechanical Cart when used. The Minecart Upgrade Kit can only be obtained by combining the Mechanical Wheel Piece, Wagon Piece, and Battery Piece, which are dropped from the Treasure Bags of the mechanical bosses in Expert Mode.
The Minecart boost can be toggled via a toggle on the Minecart slot in the equipment menu.
Minecarts: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key.

Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details).

To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways.

By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart.

Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.
Mini Nuke I: The Mini Nuke I is a type of rocket ammunition. Unlike the Mini Nuke II, it does not destroy tiles. It is a direct upgrade to the Rocket III, dealing more damage over a larger blast radius, but with lower knockback.
Mini Nuke II: The Mini Nuke II is a type of rocket ammunition. Unlike the Mini Nuke I, it destroys tiles. It is a direct upgrade to the Rocket IV, dealing more damage over a larger blast radius, but with lower knockback.
Mini Star Cell: The Star Cell is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Stardust Pillar during the Lunar Events. It floats slowly towards the player but can move at a faster rate if the player begins moving away from it.

Upon death, it splits into multiple Mini Star Cells. If these Mini Star Cells are not dealt with, they will grow into a full-sized Star Cell, that can also split into more Mini Star Cells. Mini Star Cells do not contribute to the kill count required to break the Stardust Pillar's shield, though after growing back, they do.
Mini Volcano: The Mini Volcano is a decorative animated furniture item that emits light when placed. Its animation can be toggled on and off with wires. It has a 19/100 (19%) chance of being dropped when opening Obsidian and Hellstone Crates.
Mining Potion: The Mining Potion is a buff potion which grants the Mining buff when consumed. The buff increases mining speed by 25%. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Mining Potions can be found in pots, chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Mining armor: Mining armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Mining Helmet, Mining Shirt, and Mining Pants. The Mining Helmet can be purchased from the Merchant for 4 Gold and can also be dropped by Undead Miners with a 1/20 (5%) chance. The Mining Shirt and Mining Pants are dropped from Undead Miners with a 3/25 (12%) chance.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
The player emits a small amount of light.
All Mining armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Prospector armor and the Ultrabright Helmet, still providing the set bonus. The only difference is the defense.
Minishark: The Minishark is a pre-Hardmode gun that can be purchased from the Arms Dealer for 35 Gold. When used, it rapidly fires bullets at a slight spread, with each shot having a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of not consuming any ammunition.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Mirage Crate: The Mirage Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Desert biome. Mirage Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in a Sandstone Chest in the Underground Desert. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Oasis Crate.
Mirage Dye: Mirage Dye is a Hardmode dye obtained by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. Unlike other dyes, it does not change the color of objects, but instead applies a multicolored Shimmering effect.
Mister Stabby: Mister Stabby is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Frost Legion event. It chases the player and occasionally stops in place to do a considerably long stabbing animation with its knife. When attacking the player, it will dash and bounce around the terrain, making it difficult to hit.
Mitey-Titey: The Mitey-Titey is a tool used to place stalagmites and stalactites using items from the player's inventory. It is sold by the Demolitionist for 25 Gold.
The Mitey-Titey can use various blocks to place down stalagmites and stalactites from different biomes. These stalagmites and stalactites drop the block used to place them when destroyed.
The placement style of the stalagmites or stalactites can be cycled through by pressing the ▲ Up and ▼ Down button.
Mobius Strip: The Mobius Strip is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance to drop from Golem. While equipped, it grants the following effects:
Mollusk Whistle: The Mollusk Whistle is a mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Flamingo. The Flamingo mount allows players to float in all liquids, similar to using an Inner Tube, and dive by holding ▼ Down. The mount bobs to the surface when the ▼ Down key is released, and if deep enough, the player will launch out of the water into the air. The Mollusk Whistle can be purchased from the Zoologist for 20 Gold after filling out 25% (137 entries) of the Bestiary.
Molotov Cocktail: The Molotov Cocktail is a consumable ranged weapon with a relatively short throwing arc. Upon hitting a solid object or enemy, it will explode and release 6 Molotov Fire light emitting projectiles, which can hit up to 3 targets. These smaller projectiles deal 50% damage (11 base damage), apply no knockback and inflict the On Fire! debuff on enemies for 3–6 seconds. Its high damage and ability to inflict fire damage make it a powerful early- to mid-pre-Hardmode weapon.
Molten Charm: The Molten Charm is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that combines the effects of the Lava Charm and Obsidian Skull.

When the Molten Charm is equipped and the player comes into contact with lava, a 7-second countdown begins, signified by a lava meter that displays over the player's head. It operates similarly to the Breath meter, but displays flame icons instead of bubbles. Lava immunity time is recharged gradually by exiting lava, the same way breathing time is recharged by exiting water (albeit much more slowly).
The Molten Charm also grants immunity to the Burning debuff inflicted by contact with Meteorite, Hellstone, and Hellstone Brick. It does not grant immunity to other fire-based damage.
Molten Fury: The Molten Fury is a pre-Hardmode bow. When used, it converts Wooden Arrows into Flaming Arrows, causing them to inflict the On Fire! debuff on hit.
Molten Hamaxe: The Molten Hamaxe is a pre-Hardmode hamaxe. It has a chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff on enemy hits.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Molten Pickaxe: The Molten Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Dungeon Bricks, Cobalt Ore, and Palladium Ore. The Molten Pickaxe occasionally inflicts the On Fire! debuff on hit enemies.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Molten Quiver: The Molten Quiver is a Hardmode accessory that converts Wooden Arrows fired by the player into Flaming Arrows. In addition, it has the same effects as the Magic Quiver.
Molten Skull Rose: The Molten Skull Rose is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory. It grants 7 seconds of immunity to lava, immunity to the Burning debuff, and reduces damage taken from lava.
Molten armor: Molten armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Molten Helmet, Molten Breastplate, and Molten Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 45 Hellstone Bars (135 Hellstone and 45 Obsidian).
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Immunity to the On Fire! and Burning debuffs
The player also leaves behind a visual trail of flames.
Money Trough: The Money Trough is a portable storage item that temporarily summons a flying pet-like version of the Piggy Bank. The Money Trough enables players to access the contents of their Piggy Bank without having to manually place the Piggy Bank or any furniture for it to rest on. The floating Piggy Bank despawns after 3 minutes, but can be resummoned repeatedly at no cost. The Flying Piggy Bank does not follow the player like pets or minions would, instead it hovers stationarily at the point summoned. Once summoned, other players may use it as well to access their own Piggy Bank.

The Money Trough has a 1/200 (0.5%) / 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Blood Zombies and Dripplers during a Blood Moon, or with a much lower (1/4000 (0.025%) / 1/2000 (0.05%)) chance from their statue-spawned versions (regardless of whether a Blood Moon is occurring). It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being dropped by Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen, which can be fished up during a Blood Moon.
Monk armor: Monk armor is a Hardmode melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Monk's Bushy Brow Bald Cap, Monk's Shirt, and Monk's Pants. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 45 Defender Medals after defeating any mechanical boss.
The Shinobi Infiltrator armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Monk armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Lightning Aura sentry summons have increased attack rate and can deal critical hits with a fixed 1/6 (16.67%) chance.
Monk's Belt: The Monk's Belt is a Hardmode accessory that increases the player's sentry slots by one and increases summon damage by 10%. The Monk's Belt is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event with a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/12 (8.33%) chance during Tier 3.
Monoliths: Monoliths are furniture items that activate backgrounds and other screen effects normally seen during events or under other special circumstances. When placed, they can be toggled with the ⚷ Open / Activate button or via wire, like other mechanisms, providing their effects in a small area around them. Monoliths only cause modified visuals; they do not spawn any event enemies or bosses, and they do not change the music. They can also be equipped as vanity accessories, which enables their effect globally for the player.

There are 11 different monoliths: the Vortex, Nebula, Stardust, Solar, and Void Monoliths can be crafted at an Ancient Manipulator, the Blood Moon Monolith has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses, the Radio Thing has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by Deerclops, the Aether Monolith can be obtained via dropping an Angel Statue into Shimmer, the CRT and Retro Monoliths are sold by the Cyborg for 25 Gold, and the Film Projector can be obtained as part of Heroicis' set by dropping a Platinum Coin into the Water of an Oasis.
The Nebula, Solar, Stardust, and Vortex Monoliths mimic effects that normally surround the corresponding Celestial Pillar during the Lunar Events.
The Blood Moon Monolith mimics the effects seen during a Blood Moon.
The Void Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Moon Lord boss fight.
The Radio Thing activates the same sepia filter of The Constant world seed.
In The Constant seed, however, it instead deactivates the filter.
The Aether Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Aether mini-biome.

Unlike the other monoliths, the Aether Monolith has three states: One off state (which disables the Aether effect entirely in its area, even if it would normally be present due to Shimmer) and two on states – low, which acts as if the monolith were not present (allowing the Aether effect if enough Shimmer is nearby but not forcing it on), and high, which forces the Aether effect on.
The CRT Monolith mimics the effect of an old-fashioned CRT TV.
The Retro Monolith mimics the effect of an old two-color green and black monitor, like the original Gameboy.
The Film Projector adds a black-and-white effect to the screen.
Monster Lasagna: The Monster Lasagna is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Monster Meat: The Monster Meat is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pig Man that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Pig Man flies while carrying an Umbrella from Don't Starve in order to catch up. The Monster Meat can be dropped from most Corruption or Crimson enemies with a 1/1500 (0.07%) chance. On The Constant seed, the drop rate is increased to a 1/500 (0.2%) chance.
Moon Charm: The Moon Charm is a Hardmode accessory that, when equipped during nighttime, transforms the player into a werewolf and applies the Werewolf buff, which provides several stat bonuses. Additionally, the Moon Charm replaces the sound the player makes when damaged with the hurt sound that regular Werewolf enemies also have. The Werewolf buff does not pacify Werewolf enemies or make the player immune to damage from them. Although the regular Werewolf enemy is colored blue, the player Werewolf will be colored brown. The Moon Charm has a 1/60 (1.67%) chance of being dropped by Werewolves.
The Werewolf buff provides the player with these bonuses:
Slightly increased jump height and jump speed
+0.5 health regeneration per second (similar to the Band of Regeneration, but with half the speed)
Moon Globe: The Moon Globe is a thrown consumable item purchased from the Zoologist for 3 Gold after the Bestiary is 50% complete (273 entries). When a Moon Globe is thrown and shatters on a surface, the world's moon style will be randomized to one of 9 options.
Moon Lord: The Moon Lord is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist boss. He is the final boss of the Desktop, Console, and Mobile versions of Terraria.
While the Moon Lord is alive, his exclusive music Moon Lord will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Lunar Boss (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Moon Lord Legs: The Moon Lord Legs are an armor item for the legs slot. They are exclusively found in worlds created with the Drunk seed active, where they have a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to generate as secondary loot in all naturally generated Chests.
They grant the following effects while equipped:
Increases the maximum safe falling distance by 10 tiles, jump speed by 1.8, and jump duration by 1
The player's legs are replaced with Moon Lord-themed tentacles with a unique walking animation.
Moon Lord Torso: The Moon Lord Torso is a vanity item equipped in the body slot. It is exclusive to For the Worthy and Zenith worlds, where it has a 1/5 (20%) to be found as secondary loot in Locked Gold Chests and Biome Chests (except desert chest) in the Dungeon, and the same chance to drop from Golden Lock Boxes obtained from fishing in the Dungeon.
Moon Mask: The Moon Mask is a vanity headpiece dropped by Lamias in Underground Deserts tainted with The Corruption or The Crimson.
Moon Shell: The Moon Shell is a Hardmode accessory that can be crafted at the Tinkerer's Workshop. It combines the effects of the Moon Charm and the Neptune's Shell: Equipping it will turn the player into a Merfolk when entering water or honey (at any time), or into a Werewolf at night. The Merfolk form replaces the Werewolf form if entering water at night.
The buffs from the Moon Charm:
Slightly increased jump height and jump speed
+0.5 health regeneration per second (similar to the Band of Regeneration, but with half the speed)
The buff from the Neptune's Shell:

Entering applicable liquids with this accessory equipped transforms the player into a merperson and grants the Merfolk buff. While in this form, the breath meter will refill as if the player is in open air, therefore effectively preventing drowning. The player will be able to move freely in water.
Moon Stone: The Moon Stone is a Hardmode accessory which has a 1/35 (2.86%) / 69/1225 (5.63%) chance to drop from Vampires during the Solar Eclipse event. It grants the same stat bonuses as the Sun Stone, but these bonuses will only activate during the night or during a Solar Eclipse.
Moonglow: Moonglow is a type of herb which appears as a bent stalk with a drooping blue-white flower. It grows naturally on regular Jungle grass. Moonglow can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Moonglow Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles.

Moonglow blooms during nighttime (7:30 PM to 4:29 AM). Its blooming is indicated by the blue flower and blue-white light particles emitted. Harvesting mature Moonglow yields 1 Moonglow item. Harvesting blooming Moonglow yields 1 Moonglow item and 1–3 Moonglow Seeds. Harvesting blooming Moonglow with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Moonglows and 1–5 Moonglow Seeds instead.
Both Moonglow and Moonglow Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.
Moonglow Seeds: Moonglow Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Moonglows while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Moonglows while they are fully grown. Moonglow will only bloom at night, and will glow and give off blue orbs of light. Each plant drops 1–3 Moonglow Seeds when harvested while blooming.

Moonglow Seeds can be placed on Jungle grass, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Moonglows. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Jungle, but will only yield seeds when blooming.
Moonplate Block: Moonplate Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks obtained from throwing Sunplate Blocks into Shimmer. Their main use is crafting Duskware furniture and Crescent Walls.
Morning Star: The Morning Star is a Hardmode, post-Plantera whip that has a 1/200 (0.5%) / 399/40,000 (0.9975%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Rusty Armored Bones, and Hell Armored Bones in the Hardmode Dungeon. It has a 5% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
Moss: Moss is a grass-like plant that grows on Stone Blocks. It comes in 11 different variants. Mossy stone requires one more hit to break than clean stone. Moss will be destroyed if the Stone Block it is on converts to Ebonstone, Crimstone, or Pearlstone.

Moss sprouts fuzz that can be cut like wild grass plants. Using a Paint Scraper or Spectre Paint Scraper to harvest moss fuzz has a 1/9 (11.11%) chance of dropping moss as a plantable item. Collected moss can be placed on Stone Blocks and Gray Bricks, or used to craft Mossy Walls.

There are 5 types of regular moss: Green Moss, Brown Moss, Red Moss, Blue Moss, and Purple Moss. One of each regular moss can be found throughout each third of a given map (three variants per world). They can be found either randomly on cave surfaces or in moss chambers with a matching Mossy Wall.

Glowing mosses are special variants of moss that glow in vibrant colors. These include the Lava Moss, Krypton Moss, Xenon Moss, Argon Moss, Neon Moss, and Helium Moss. Lava Moss can be found in patches around the lava layer of the Caverns. Krypton, Xenon, Argon, and Neon Moss grow in glowing moss biomes and in much larger areas than other mosses, and only one type among these can be found in each world. Up to two (small world) / three (medium world) / four (large world) glowing moss biomes will be generated in the Cavern layer, mostly above the lava layers, but not near the horizontal center of the world. Helium Moss does not spawn naturally and can instead be obtained by throwing any other glowing moss into Shimmer.

Mosses that did not naturally spawn in a world can be obtained by putting any glowing moss in an Extractinator, which produces regular mosses, or a Chlorophyte Extractinator, which produces all variants of mosses. Moss Zombies spawned in surface Graveyards can also drop all variants of mosses.
Moss Hornet: The Moss Hornet is a Hardmode flying enemy similar to the pre-Hardmode Hornet, being encountered in the Underground Jungle biome and requiring blocks of Jungle grass in order to spawn. Compared to the more random flying patterns of pre-Hardmode Hornets, Moss Hornets act more aggressively, hovering closer to the player's position and shooting their stingers in rapid bursts. The stingers have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff to the player for 10 seconds. In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the chance is 1/3 (33.33%) for 20 seconds and 2/3 (66.67%) for 2–10 seconds. They cannot be destroyed with weapons and travel at about the same speed as the darts from a Dart Trap.

Moss Hornets have a (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1/100 (1%) / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 1/150 (0.67%) chance to drop the Tattered Bee Wing. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, the Tattered Bee Wing will only drop once any mechanical boss has been defeated in the current world.
Moss Zombie: The Moss Zombie is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a Zombie variant that spawns in a surface Graveyard mini-biome if the player has negative luck.
Mossy Walls: The Green Mossy Wall, Brown Mossy Wall, Red Mossy Wall, Blue Mossy Wall, and Purple Mossy Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground and Cavern layers in moss chambers, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
Moth: The Moth is a rare Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Underground Jungle on Jungle Grass. It flies around very slowly, and upon seeing the player, will direct its attention towards them and attempt to deal contact damage. Upon killing a Moth, there is a chance that it will drop Butterfly Dust, which is solely used to craft Butterfly Wings. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, the Butterfly Dust can only drop once any mechanical boss has been defeated in the current world.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. The Moth requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Mother Slime: The Mother Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Cavern layer. Upon death, it spawns 1-3 Baby Slimes, and like all slimes, drops Gel. It is one of the largest ordinary slimes in the game, only topped by King Slime, Queen Slime, and the Rainbow Slime.
Like most other slimes, the Mother Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel accessory equipped.
Mothron: Mothron is a rare, powerful, Hardmode, post-Plantera, flying enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. Mothron can pass through all blocks and attacks by chasing after the player or aligning itself horizontally with them before lunging towards them at varying speeds, inflicting heavy contact damage depending on its velocity. Occasionally, it lands on blocks to lay several Mothron Eggs that spawn Baby Mothrons if they are not destroyed in time, much like Lepus (3DS version).

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. Mothron requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Mourning Wood: The Mourning Wood is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Pumpkin Moon event. It is the Pumpkin Moon equivalent of the Everscream, which behaves in an almost identical way to the Mourning Wood.
Defeating the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event will add 75 / 150 / 187.5 points to the final score.
Mouse: The Mouse is a critter that spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, but not in Ice, Crimson, Corruption, Jungle or Hallow biomes. It can also spawn in front of unsafe Living Wood Walls below the surface at a much higher rate. Its small size and speed can make it difficult to spot even in well-lit conditions, although it occasionally squeaks. The Mouse has only 5 health and no defense, and can only be damaged by players.

The Mouse can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Mouse Cage). Once crafted, the Mouse cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Mouse can be spawned by the Mouse Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Mouse to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Mrs. Claus set: The Mrs. Claus set is a vanity set. It is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode. It consists of a Mrs. Claus Hat, Mrs. Claus Shirt and Mrs. Claus Heels. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Mud Ball: The Mud Ball is a consumable weapon. When used, it throws a Mud Ball projectile that is affected by gravity, pierces enemies infinitely, and places a Mud Block upon hitting the ground. If the hit location is occupied by other foreground objects, the Mud Block will be broken into item form.
Mud Block: Mud Blocks are a very common block type that comprises the majority of the Jungle, Underground Jungle, and Glowing Mushroom biome. It also generates in irregular patches in the Cavern layer. Mud Blocks may be covered by Jungle grass, Mushroom grass, Corrupt grass, or Crimson grass on any side, which can be planted with Jungle Grass Seeds, Mushroom Grass Seeds, Corrupt Seeds, and Crimson Seeds. Only Jungle grass and Mushroom grass are incapable of growing on Dirt Blocks.
Mud Bud: The Mud Bud is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns Plantero, a miniature version of Plantera, that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, Plantero flies towards them in a manner similar to Plantera's second form while emitting a trail of falling leaves that are affected by wind. The Mud Bud can be purchased from the Zoologist for 50 Gold after defeating Plantera.
Mud Wall: The Mud Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Jungle and occasionally the Underground Jungle, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

If Mud Walls are sprayed with Dark Blue Solution they will turn into unsafe Mushroom Walls. If these Mushroom Walls are sprayed with Green Solution they will revert back into unsafe Mud Walls or unsafe Jungle Walls, this seemingly being determined by layer level.
Mudstone Brick: The Mudstone Brick is a type of brick made from Stone Blocks and Mud Blocks. It can also be obtained from Jungle Shrines. It is brown in color with a Stone-like texture.
Mudstone Brick Wall: The Mudstone Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.
Mug: The Mug is a cup made of Glass. It can be used to craft Ale. It can be placed on a flat furniture item, where it functions as a Placed Bottle crafting station.
Multicolor Wrench: The Multicolor Wrench is a tool that can place down any combination of Wire color, and also remove it. It can be used at any part of the screen, regardless of block placement range. When used with ⚷ Open / Activate, a menu with five different buttons will be displayed: four for selecting the four colors of Wire, and one for toggling between placing or harvesting selected colors of Wire.
The menu will pop up at the cursor's position, with buttons in a radial pattern.
The menu will pop up above the ⚷ Open / Activate button, with buttons listed in two rows.
Mummy: Mummies are Hardmode enemies that spawn in the Desert biome and areas where Sand Blocks are present. They follow the Fighter AI, behaving similarly to Zombies.

There are several different types of Mummies: the standard Mummy, as well as the Dark Mummy, Light Mummy, and Blood Mummy. They spawn in Corrupted Deserts, Hallowed Deserts and Crimson Deserts, respectively.

Dark Mummies and Blood Mummies are 50% faster than other Mummies. All mummies receive a 100% speed increase when their health is reduced below 50%. In addition, Mummies inflict the following debuffs upon hitting the player:
Mummy set: The Mummy set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Mummy Mask, the Mummy Shirt, and the Mummy Pants. Each piece is dropped by Mummies with a 1/75 (1.33%) chance.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Muramasa: The Muramasa is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron broadsword that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes. When swung, it creates a blue slash upon enemy hits. The slashes deal 50% of the weapon's damage (12 base damage), inflict no knockback, do not pierce, and have 5 armor penetration.
Mushi Ladybug: The Mushi Ladybug is an enemy that spawns in Glowing Mushroom biomes, both on the surface and below-ground in Hardmode, but only on the surface in pre-Hardmode. The Mushi Ladybug's high health and damage, quick movement, and ability to fly short distances place them among the more dangerous enemies that can spawn before Hardmode.
Mushroom: The Mushroom is a pre-Hardmode crafting material and recovery potion that spawns randomly on grass or Hallowed grass on the surface layer. It can be harvested with any tool or weapon.
When used, the Mushroom restores 15 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 30 seconds. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.
In The Constant worlds, eating a Mushroom also resets Hunger to 5 minutes of Peckish, if the player is hungry.
Mushroom Cap: The Mushroom Cap is a vanity hat purchased from the Truffle for 2 Gold. It greatly resembles a Glowing Mushroom without the stalk.
Mushroom Chest: Mushroom Chests are chests that can be found inside Underground Cabins in Glowing Mushroom biomes.
Mushroom Grass Seeds: Mushroom Grass Seeds are seeds that have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to drop from harvesting Glowing Mushrooms. The seeds can also be purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver 50 Copper each if she is spoken to in a Glowing Mushroom biome. Shaking a Giant Glowing Mushroom occasionally yields Mushroom Grass Seeds as well. They can also be obtained by using Poo on an Extractinator.

Mushroom Grass Seeds must be planted on Mud Blocks and can be grown both above and under ground. Once planted, Mushroom grass will begin to spread to adjacent Mud Blocks and grow Glowing Mushrooms, as well as Giant Glowing Mushrooms when enough space is available.

Mushroom grass spreads much slower than ordinary or Corrupt grass, at a speed comparable to Jungle grass – 3–5 tiles per day for each continuous section of Mud Blocks. Mushroom grass, as well as the mushrooms that grow on it, emit moderate light.
Mushroom Spear: The Mushroom Spear is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss spear that can be purchased from the Truffle for 70 Gold. When thrust, it summons seven spinning mushrooms that linger in midair and deal 33.33% of the weapon's damage (20 base damage) but do not inflict knockback.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Mushroom Staff: The Mushroom Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Mushroom Boi minion. It runs and jumps towards enemies, dealing contact damage. If the nearest target is too far away, the Mushroom Boi will dive towards it, creating a red explosion on impact that deals 133% of the weapon's damage (10 base damage) and 300% of its knockback (base knockback of 6 (Average)), and then teleport back to the player.
Mushroom Wall: The Mushroom Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Underground Cabins in the Glowing Mushroom biome, considered safe. It is also considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Spraying Mud Walls or Jungle Walls with Dark Blue Solution creates unsafe Mushroom Walls. These do not drop as an item when destroyed.
Mushroom set: The Mushroom set is a vanity set consisting of the Mushroom Hat, Mushroom Vest, and Mushroom Pants. All three pieces have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Mushroom Chests in underground Glowing Mushroom biomes.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Music Boxes: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord.
A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways:
Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires.
Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation.
There are 101 different Music Boxes available.
Musket: The Musket is a pre-Hardmode gun. It will always drop from the first Shadow Orb destroyed in a Corruption world (along with 100 Musket Balls) and has a 1/5 (20%) chance of dropping from destroyed Shadow Orbs afterward. It also has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from Corrupt (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Defiled Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) fished in the Corruption. The Musket has a base 12% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Its Crimson counterpart is The Undertaker. The Musket deals a much higher damage per shot at a slower fire rate.
Musket Ball: The Musket Ball is a pre-Hardmode bullet. It has no special properties and is used for crafting a variety of more advanced ammunition. When either Musket Balls or Tungsten Bullets are fired with certain guns, they will be converted into a special projectile (e.g. the Uzi converting them into High Velocity Bullets). Some other guns, such as the Pew-matic Horn, can convert any type of bullet.

Musket Balls can be bought from the Arms Dealer for 7 Copper each, or 70 Silver for 1000 rounds. They can also be obtained from Shadow Orbs and Crimson Hearts (along with a Musket or The Undertaker), or from a Present (along with a Red Ryder) during Christmas.
The Endless Musket Pouch serves as an infinite amount of Musket Balls.
Mysterious Package: The Mysterious Package was an unobtainable pet-summoning item, which was supposed to summon a Pet Drone that would drop a box every few minutes. It was likely intended to be available to those who bought Terraria on Amazon. It was only obtainable through third party softwares and was removed entirely shortly after its introduction.
Mystic Arts Sash: The Mystic Arts Sash is a Hardmode accessory item made by combining a Mana Regeneration Band and a Black Belt at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Mystic Bloom: The Mystic Bloom is a pre-Hardmode magic weapon that fires three non-piercing petals which slowly home in on nearby enemies within a 25-tile radius and can bounce off blocks, each dealing 100% of the weapon's damage and knockback. If no enemies are within range, the petals instead linger in place after traveling a short distance.
Mystic Frog: The Mystic Frog is a critter that has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of spawning in place of an ordinary Frog in the Jungle. The Mystic Frog has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.
Unlike most critters, the Mystic Frog cannot be caught with a Bug Net, which means there is no craftable cage for it.

If the player throws Purification Powder on it, it will transform into the Mystic Slime town pet. Afterwards, the Mystic Frog will no longer spawn. If the Mystic Slime is killed, it will respawn naturally without the need to purify another Mystic Frog. Only one Mystic Frog can be alive at a time.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Mystic Robe: The Mystic Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It provides minimal defense (2) but a 6% damage and critical strike boost to magic weapons, along with a 10% reduction in mana use. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 Gold 50 Silver.

Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, while wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 Mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses intact.
Mystic Slime: Town Slimes are a type of town pet. There are 8 different Town Slimes and all of them can exist at the same time (unlike the different breeds of the Town Bunny, Town Cat, and Town Dog).

Almost all types of Town Slimes are acquired via some form of transformation, similar to the Tax Collector. Afterwards, the transformed Town Slime will move into a vacant house if one is available. If it is killed, it will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house. The initial transformation does not need to be repeated.

Town Slimes can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). They may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for their home tile (standing point).
Mythical set: The Mythical set is a removed unimplemented vanity set that was intended to be dropped by the Mythical Wyvern during the Chinese New Year seasonal event.

As the Mythical Wyvern was unimplemented, the Mythical set was unobtainable. The Mythical Wyvern had an ID and was fully coded, but was never able to spawn naturally nor be summoned with an item. It was the only set of which only one of the pieces had a sell value.
Mythril Bar: The Mythril Bar is a Hardmode bar. It is one of the two ores able to create a Hardmode Anvil, which is used to craft most Hardmode equipment.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Bar.
Mythril Brick: Mythril Brick is a mythril tier brick.
Mythril Brick Wall: Mythril Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Mythril Bricks.
Mythril Chainsaw: The Mythril Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Mythril Waraxe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Chainsaw.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Mythril Crate: The Mythril Crate is a Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. It is the middle tier of standard crate. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Iron Crate.
Mythril Drill: The Mythril Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Mythril Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Drill. The Mythril Drill has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Mythril Halberd: The Mythril Halberd is a Hardmode spear.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Halberd.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Mythril Ore: Mythril Ore belongs to the second tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the second altar broken, either it or Orichalcum Ore can spawn in the cavern layer. Mining Mythril Ore requires a Cobalt/Palladium Pickaxe or better.

As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
Mythril Pickaxe: The Mythril Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Mythril Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Pickaxe. The Mythril Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Mythril Repeater: The Mythril Repeater is a Hardmode repeater.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Repeater.
Mythril Sword: The Mythril Sword is a Hardmode broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Sword.
Mythril Waraxe: The Mythril Waraxe is a Hardmode axe and the alternative to the Mythril Chainsaw.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Waraxe.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Mythril armor: Mythril armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Mythril Chainmail and Mythril Greaves, as well as three different headpieces: the Mythril Helmet, Mythril Hat, and Mythril Hood, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively.
