Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 45 Mythril Bars (180 Mythril Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 65 Mythril Bars (260 Mythril Ore).
Its alternate ore counterpart is Orichalcum armor.
Nachos: Nachos are a food item that grant the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Nachos have a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Angry Tumblers and all Sand Shark variants.
Nail Gun: The Nail Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that consumes Nails as ammunition. When used, it fires a Nail that deals 15% of the weapon's damage (17 base damage) and sticks to enemies or blocks before exploding after 1.5 seconds, dealing 135% damage (155 base damage). Nails are unaffected by gravity until they have traveled roughly 30 tiles, after which they move with an arc similar to that of arrows.

The Nail Gun has a 1/25 (4%) / 49/625 (7.84%) chance of being dropped by Nailheads during the Solar Eclipse event. The Nail Gun is always dropped alongside 100–200 Nails. Additional Nails are also sold by both the Merchant and the Arms Dealer for 1 Silver each when the player has the Nail Gun in their inventory.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Nailhead: The Nailhead is an uncommon Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. In addition to dealing high contact damage, the Nailhead has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to fire three to five Nail projectiles in a wide spread when attacked. He has significantly more health than most other Solar Eclipse enemies and has a high resistance to knockback.
The Nailhead requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of his Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Nanites: Nanites are a Hardmode crafting material used solely for crafting items that inflict the Confused debuff. Nanites are purchased from the Cyborg for 15 Silver each.
Nano Bullet: The Nano Bullet is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bullet. It inflicts the Confused debuff on hit for 1–3 seconds, reversing enemy movement to make them run away from the player rather than towards them. The fired Nano Bullets receive a 1.25× damage multiplier, which is applied to the total damage of gun and bullet, and after other damage bonuses. Nano Bullets can also bounce off blocks once, disippating upon hitting blocks for the second time. They bounce towards the direction of the nearest enemy within a 50-tile radius that has an unobstructed line of sight of to the bullet, but will only deal 66% damage after bouncing.

Nano Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Nano Bullets is 17 Silver 50 Copper, which is 35 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Nano Bullets is 35 Gold.
Nature's Gift: Nature's Gift is an accessory that reduces the mana cost of using magic weapons and other mana-consuming items by 6%. It is acquired by harvesting a rare flower that grows on Jungle grass in the Underground Jungle, using any weapon or tool. The flower appears as a blue version of the Jungle Rose.
Naughty Present: The Naughty Present is a Hardmode, post-Plantera event-summoning item used to summon the Frost Moon event. It can only be used at night. Attempting to use it during the day will not begin the event, and the item will not be consumed from the player's inventory.
Nazar: The Nazar is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Cursed debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Cursed Skulls, Giant Cursed Skulls, Cursed Hammers, Crimson Axes, and Enchanted Swords.
Nebula Arcanum: The Nebula Arcanum is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist magic weapon that fires a swirling purple orb when used. The orb will slowly home in on enemies within a 50-tile range and bounce off blocks, hitting three times before exploding into 10–16 smaller shard projectiles that each deal 65% of the weapon's listed damage (45 base damage), inflict 80% of its knockback (base knockback of 4 (Weak)), and do not pierce. All three hits do not have to be on the same target, as it will continue to home in on other enemies in range if its target dies before the third hit. If the projectile does not hit enemies three times, it will explode after 11 seconds.

As the main orb remains active, it also produces additional, smaller orb projectiles that orbit around it, each of which deals 50% of the weapon's listed damage (35 base damage), passes through blocks, inflicts no knockback, and pierces an unlimited number of enemies. A maximum of eight of these projectiles can be summoned per orb. Two to three of these projectiles appear per second for the first half of the projectile's lifetime and disappear at the same rate as it approaches its detonation.
Nebula Blaze: The Nebula Blaze is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist magic weapon that inaccurately fires pink, high-velocity projectiles which home in on nearby enemies, with a 1/5 (20%) chance to fire a larger blue Nebula Blaze Ex projectile that deals 300% of the weapon's damage (390 base damage) and moves 60% faster.
When held, it appears as a pink glow covering the player's hand, which gives off a small amount of light and leaves behind a pink particle trail as the player moves.
Nebula Brick: The Nebula Brick is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist brick that is crafted from Nebula Fragments. It is one of the four Fragment Bricks, bricks which are crafted with Lunar Fragments. It glows when placed and can be used to craft Nebula furniture.
Nebula Brick Wall: Nebula Brick Wall is a background wall made from Nebula Bricks.
Nebula Dye: Nebula Dye is a Hardmode, endgame dye crafted using Nebula Fragments dropped by the Nebula Pillar in the Lunar Events. The dye gives the player a pink/purple shiny look on armor, equipment or accessories and looks like stars are moving rapidly upward on anything with the dye. As with the other lunar dyes, the Nebula Dye can not be combined with any other dyes.
Nebula Floater: The Nebula Floater is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist flying enemy that spawns in the area of the Nebula Pillar during the Lunar Events. The Nebula Floater periodically spawns up to three Nebula Eyes that float around it. If it has a clear line of sight to the player, it will hover in place and start firing pink Nebula Lasers from one of the Nebula Eyes at the player, otherwise, it will move towards the player through all tiles. It can also do random teleports around the player periodically, and will also attempt to do so with a small chance if it is hit.
Nebula Fragment: The Nebula Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist crafting material. It is one of the four Lunar Fragments, dropped from the Nebula Pillar during the Lunar Events in stacks of 12–60 / 24–100. Nebula Fragments can be used to craft Nebula armor, an end-game armor set that benefits all types of magic weapons, as well as Nebula-themed tools, weapons, wings, etc.

Crafting all items requires 121 Nebula Fragments and 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite), which necessitates defeating the Nebula Pillar at least 3–11 / 2–8 times (note that the Nebula Fragment can also be crafted from the other fragments) and fighting the Moon Lord at least 4 / 3–4 times.
Nebula Fragment Block: Nebula Fragment Blocks are blocks made from Nebula Fragments which are dropped by the Nebula Pillar. The blocks have a crystal-like appearance with intense shades of pink and purple. They can be crafted with the Ancient Manipulator. Walls cannot be crafted with them.
Nebula Pillar: The Celestial Pillars (also known as the Lunar Pillars, Lunar Towers, or Celestial Towers) are four late-Hardmode, stationary bosses that appear during the Lunar Events after the Lunatic Cultist has been defeated. To break their protective shields, 100 of the unique enemies that spawn in a large surrounding area must be defeated. Pillars drop Lunar Fragments when destroyed, and destroying all four of them results in the spawn of the Moon Lord.

The four Celestial Pillars are the Solar Pillar, the Vortex Pillar, the Nebula Pillar, and the Stardust Pillar. They represent the four damage types in Terraria: Solar for melee, Vortex for ranged, Nebula for magic, and Stardust for summon. After the defeat of the Lunatic Cultist, they appear at four locations equally spaced across the map (see pillar spawning mechanics below), and do not move apart from slowly bobbing up and down in place. Each pillar takes control of the world in a circular area around it with a radius of 250 tiles (500 feet). When the player is in that affected area, the background will change to a pillar-specific one, and only pillar-specific enemies will spawn in large numbers.

Initially, each Celestial Pillar has a large shield around it which prevents it from taking any damage. In order to remove the shield, the player must kill 100 enemies corresponding to that specific pillar, which are the major threat of the Lunar Events; they can deal high amounts of damage, inflict debuffs, and easily swarm the player if not dealt with quickly. The enemy kill count does not reset if the player dies, but leaving the world does reset it.

Defeating pillar-specific enemies releases small red energy particles that travel to the pillar shield to indicate the progress. Once the kill count of a pillar is reached, its shield is lowered and it becomes vulnerable to damage. The pillars themselves are fairly easy to defeat, being extremely large and immobile, and having only 20,000 health each and only fairly weak or no attacks. However, enemies continue to spawn even after the shield is lowered, until the pillar is defeated.
There is no set order in which the Celestial Pillars must be defeated. The following status messages will appear from whichever pillars are taken down first, second, third, and fourth:
First pillar defeated: "Your mind goes numb..."
Second pillar defeated: "You are overwhelmed with pain..."
Third pillar defeated: "Otherworldly voices linger around you..."
After defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar, the screen starts to vibrate and the music volume lowers before eventually going completely silent. After 60 seconds, the Moon Lord will spawn.
After defeating the Moon Lord, each pillar will only require 50 of their respective enemies killed to lower their shields instead of 100.
Nebula armor: Nebula armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord mage armor set consisting of the Nebula Helmet, Nebula Breastplate, and Nebula Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Nebula Fragments.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

Grants a chance for special booster items to spawn upon striking enemies with magic weapons. Each booster provides a buff, indicated by the booster orbiting the player. Boosters of the same type can stack with each other up to 3 times. Boosters expire after 8 seconds and the buff decreases by one level. Boosters can float in the air and have a greater pickup range than normal.
The boosters are not tied to the armor, so any player can pick up the booster items, even if they are not wearing the armor set.
In multiplayer, picking up a booster item will also grant nearby teammates (within a 43.75-tile radius) the buff. Players without a team will give the buff to all nearby players.
Necro armor: Necro armor is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron ranged armor set consisting of the Necro Helmet, Necro Breastplate, and Necro Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 135 Cobwebs and 150 Bones.

The Ancient Necro Helmet is dropped from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon, at a 1/450 (0.22%) chance. It is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Necro Helmet. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Necro Helmet prior to 1.0.3.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
The player also emits a visual afterimage while moving, and their hurt sound will be set to that of a Skeleton.
Necromancer: The Necromancer is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It attacks by rapidly firing Shadow Beams at the player, thin rays of purple light that reflect off walls multiple times. These rays are instantaneous and inflict the Slow debuff for 5–15 / 10–30 / 12.5–37.5 seconds. Necromancers teleport to a different location on-screen after firing projectiles five times or with a 1/2 (50%) chance upon being hit.
Necromancers spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by brick walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Necromantic Scroll: The Necromantic Scroll is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that increases the player's minion slots by one and increases the damage of all summon weapons by 10%. It is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave.
Nectar: The Nectar is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Hornet that follows the player. This pet will not teleport to the player when it is far away. The Nectar has a 1/15 (6.67%) / 1/9 (11.11%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee.
Negative Dye: Negative Dye is a type of dye bought from the Dye Trader during a full moon, or given as a possible reward for turning in a Strange Plant in Hardmode. When applied, it will completely invert the color of dyed armor or accessories. It is not combinable with other dyes.
Neon Moss Brick: Neon Moss Brick is a type of brick made from Neon Moss that glows in the dark when placed.
Neon Moss Brick Wall: Neon Moss Brick Wall is a brick background wall that glows in the dark when placed, like Neon Moss and the Neon Moss Brick it is made from.
Neon Tetra: Neon Tetras are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in the Jungle in any layer. They sell for twice what other fish in their catch quality do, and on the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version they have no use except for this sell price.
Neptune's Shell: Neptune's Shell is a Hardmode accessory that aids maneuverability in water, honey, and Shimmer by granting indefinite breathing time while submerged, swimming via the ↷ Jump key, and eliminating the slow movement speed usually caused by submerging underwater. Entering applicable liquids with this accessory equipped transforms the player into a merperson and grants the Merfolk buff. While in this form, the breath meter will refill as if the player is in open air, therefore effectively preventing drowning.
Neptune's Shell has a 1/50 (2%) / 99/2500 (3.96%) chance of being dropped by Creatures from the Deep.

Neptune's Shell can be considered an upgrade from the Diving Gear in most respects, but it lacks the extra mobility on Ice Blocks from the Arctic Diving Gear and the extra lighting underwater of the Jellyfish Necklace.
Nerdy Slime: Town Slimes are a type of town pet. There are 8 different Town Slimes and all of them can exist at the same time (unlike the different breeds of the Town Bunny, Town Cat, and Town Dog).

Almost all types of Town Slimes are acquired via some form of transformation, similar to the Tax Collector. Afterwards, the transformed Town Slime will move into a vacant house if one is available. If it is killed, it will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house. The initial transformation does not need to be repeated.

Town Slimes can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). They may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for their home tile (standing point).
Nettle Burst: The Nettle Burst is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When used, it extends a snaking vine from the player's position, which passes through blocks, pierces infinite enemies, and deals 0.17 s global invincibility.
The snaking vine has 11–12 segments, and each has a length of 2 tiles. The vine extends segmentally every 0.07 s, with each individual segment lasting 1.48 s.
The projectiles of Nettle Burst have 10 armor penetration, which stacks with the former segment.Hence the actual armor penetration increases with segments, from the root's 10 to the end's 110 or 120.
Night Owl Potion: The Night Owl Potion is a buff potion that grants the Night Owl buff when consumed. The buff improves the player's night vision, and sharply increases the radius of any available light source. The buff itself has no effect in total darkness. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Night Owl Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and Crates.
Night Vision Helmet: The Night Vision Helmet is an armor piece for the helmet slot. For the player wearing it, it increases the apparent light level provided by all light sources on the screen, similarly to the Night Owl buff. The Night Vision Helmet has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to be dropped by Granite Elementals and Granite Golems. It can also be purchased from the Cyborg for 5 Gold, after the Martian Madness event has been completed in the current world.
Night's Edge: The Night's Edge is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron broadsword. When swung, a circular purple aura follows the swing, reaching slightly farther than the sword itself. Another aura swings towards the cursor, further increasing range. The auras can hit up to two enemies each, but the same enemy cannot be hit by both auras.
Nightglow: The Nightglow is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic weapon that fires four rainbow-colored projectiles which emerge from the player and home in on nearby enemies. Each projectile ricochets off solid blocks and can pierce twice before dissipating on the third hit, but loses 20% of its damage for each enemy struck. The Nightglow has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light.
Nightmare Pickaxe: The Nightmare Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Hellstone, Crimstone Blocks, and Ebonstone Blocks.
Its Crimson counterpart is the Deathbringer Pickaxe. The Nightmare Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Nimbus Rod: The Nimbus Rod is a Hardmode magic weapon that creates storm clouds that drop damaging "rain" projectiles directly below themselves. When cast, a cloud projectile is fired from the Nimbus Rod and travels towards the cursor. Upon reaching its destination or colliding with a solid block, the cloud stops and starts sending damaging raindrop particles downward, each dealing the weapon's stated damage. The raindrop can hit up to 5 targets. Each cloud lasts for five minutes and up to two clouds can be spawned at once. Using the Nimbus Rod when there are already two active clouds will cause the oldest cloud to disappear. Clouds can also be removed manually by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. The Nimbus Rod has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being dropped by Angry Nimbuses.
Its best modifier is Demonic because it cannot get modifiers that affect knockback.
Ninja armor: Ninja armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ninja Hood, Ninja Shirt and Ninja Pants. King Slime drops each piece separately (1 per kill with a 1/3 (33.33%) chance each), or two pieces from the Treasure Bag it drops in Expert Mode.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
North Pole: The North Pole is a Hardmode, post-Plantera spear that is dropped by the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event with a 5.19%–10.37% (15.56%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave. When thrust, it fires an icy spear projectile that is unaffected by gravity until after traveling for 0.5 seconds. It can pierce enemies twice and cannot pass through blocks. The spear also releases a trail of damaging snowflakes that rain down, dissipating upon contact with an enemy or block.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Nurse: The Nurse is an NPC who will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
The player's maximum health is greater than 100.
The Nurse will fully restore the player's health and cure them of any active debuffs at the cost of coins (there are exceptions, see Notes and History).

Healing costs are 1 Copper per health restored, plus an additional 1 Silver per active debuff on the player, all multiplied by the Nurse's current Happiness price adjustment, and then doubled if playing on Expert Mode. Also, the Nurse charges increasing amounts of money for healing as the game progresses; these specific increases are listed below. Thus, at the start of the game, the cost of restoring 100 health can range from 75 Copper / 1 Silver 50 Copper (with maximum happiness) to 1 Silver 50 Copper / 3 Silver (with maximum unhappiness), while by endgame it can range from 1 Gold 50 Silver / 3 Gold up to 3 Gold / 6 Gold.

The Nurse will defend herself against nearby enemies by throwing green syringes that damage and poison enemies for 3–5 seconds. She can also throw red syringes to heal herself and other nearby NPCs for 20 health, which can also home in on targets. She deals 8 / 12 / 14 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
Nurse set: The Nurse set is a vanity set that resembles the Nurse's clothes. It is sold by the Arms Dealer during Halloween for 9 Gold (set). It consists of the Nurse Hat, Nurse Shirt, and Nurse Pants.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Nutcracker: The Nutcracker is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during wave 3 of the Frost Moon event. There are two Nutcracker variants, each with slightly differing damage and defense. The first variant will transform into the more powerful second variant when its health is reduced to below 55% (990 / 1,485 / 2,227). The Nutcracker's spinning second form gains a higher resistance to knockback and significantly increased movement speed.
Defeating a Nutcracker during the Frost Moon event will add 4 / 8 / 10 points to the final score.
Nymph: The Nymph is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Cavern layer of any biome. When encountered, she appears as the Lost Girl, who seems to be a helpless, stationary NPC in need of rescue. However, when a player gets close or attacks the Lost Girl, she transforms into the Nymph and starts attacking the player by running towards them. For a pre-Hardmode enemy, she deals comparatively high damage.
The Lost Girl will only transform into a Nymph if any of the following conditions are met:
The Lost Girl does not have full health.
The distance between the player and the Lost Girl is less than 12.5 tiles, and she has a direct line of sight to the player.
The Lost Girl is moving in any direction (e.g. caused by falling or knockback).
The Lost Girl is immune to the Confused debuff, but the transformed Nymph is not.

She is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. The Nymph requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of her Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Oasis Crate: The Oasis Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Desert biome. Oasis Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in a Sandstone Chest in the Underground Desert. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Mirage Crate.
Obsidian: Obsidian is a pre-Hardmode ore that is created when water and lava collide. Mining Obsidian requires a Gold/Platinum Pickaxe or better. Explosives can also destroy Obsidian.
Uniquely, Obsidian has no bar form of its own. It is used to craft Hellstone Bars instead.
Obsidian can be converted into Sand Blocks when used on an Extractinator.
Obsidian Brick: The Obsidian Brick is a brick-block mainly used for building. It can be crafted at a Furnace or mined by any tier of pickaxe. It is commonly found in the Underworld's Ruined Houses.
Obsidian Brick Wall: The Obsidian Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Ruined Houses in the Underworld, considered unsafe. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Obsidian Crate: The Obsidian Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in lava. Opening Obsidian and Hellstone Crates is the only way to obtain the Obsidian Lock Box, and therefore any Underworld-exclusive items normally found in locked Shadow Chests, once the Underworld has been fully looted. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Hellstone Crate.
Obsidian Horseshoe: The Obsidian Horseshoe is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:
Immunity to the Burning debuff inflicted by Meteorite, Hellstone, and Hellstone Bricks
Obsidian Lock Box: The Obsidian Lock Box is a grab bag item which is always obtained from Obsidian and Hellstone Crates. It always contains one rare item normally found in locked Shadow Chests in the Underworld. It requires a Shadow Key to be in the player's inventory to open the box, which can be found in locked Gold Chests or Golden Lock Boxes in the Dungeon.
Obsidian Rose: The Obsidian Rose is an accessory that reduces the base damage taken from lava from 80 to 35 and halves the duration of the On Fire! debuff inflicted by it from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds.
Additionally, equipping both Ash Wood armor and the Obsidian Rose (or its upgrades) provides immunity to lava damage and debuff.
The Obsidian Rose has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Fire Imps, an enemy found in The Underworld.
Obsidian Shield: The Obsidian Shield is a pre-Hardmode shield and immunity accessory that grants +2 defense, immunity to knockback, and immunity to the Burning debuff.
Obsidian Skin Potion: The Obsidian Skin Potion is a buff potion which grants the Obsidian Skin buff when consumed. The buff makes the player immune to lava and the On Fire! debuff. It also grants immunity to the Burning debuff from touching Meteorite, Hellstone, Hellstone Bricks, and Ancient Hellstone Bricks for its duration. This lasts for 6 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Obsidian Skin Potions can be found in pots and Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as in crates.
Obsidian Skull: The Obsidian Skull is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants +1 defense and immunity to the Burning debuff inflicted upon contact with Meteorite, Hellstone, Hellstone Bricks, or Ancient Hellstone Bricks. It does not grant immunity to lava or fire-based attacks.

In For the Worthy (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Zenith (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) worlds, the Obsidian Skull also protects against the Burning debuff inflicted by contact with Crispy Honey Blocks.
Obsidian Skull Rose: The Obsidian Skull Rose is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants immunity to the Burning debuff and reduced damage from lava.
Obsidian Swordfish: The Obsidian Swordfish is a Hardmode spear that is obtained via fishing in lava, by using any lava fishing method (including lava bait or Lavaproof Fishing Hook). When thrust, it fires 1–3 piercing gravity-affected embers that each deal 50% of the weapon's damage (35 base damage) and inflict the Hellfire debuff for 3-6 seconds. The embers can hit a total of 3 enemies and do not inflict any knockback. The Obsidian Swordfish also has a 24% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Obsidian Water Walking Boots: Obsidian Water Walking Boots are a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grant the ability to walk on water, honey, and Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), while also giving immunity to the Burning debuff. They do not allow walking on lava.
Obsidian armor: Obsidian armor is a pre-Hardmode summoner armor set consisting of the Obsidian Outlaw Hat, Obsidian Longcoat, and Obsidian Pants. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Obsidian, 30 Silk, and 20 Shadow Scales or Tissue Samples.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Unlike any other whip speed bonus, this stacks multiplicatively with melee speed bonuses.
Obsidifish: Obsidifish are a type of pre-Hardmode ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) / Hardmode ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions)) fish which are found rarely by fishing in any biome in any layer, but only in lava. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners, Inferno Potions, and Potions of Return.
Ocean Crate: The Ocean Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Ocean. Ocean Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in Water Chests. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Seaside Crate.
Ocram's Razor: Ocram's Razor is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Mechdusa when used. It can only be used in worlds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix seeds. It is crafted with the Mechanical Eye, Mechanical Worm, and Mechanical Skull and can be used in any biome, at any time.
This item has no function when brought to other worlds, and its tooltip will display 'It has no effect in this world' instead.
Office Block: Office Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks. Their main use is crafting Office furniture and Office Walls.
Office Wall: Office Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Office Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Offline Gemspark Walls: Offline Gemspark Walls are a group of walls made from Gemspark Blocks. Unlike Gemspark Blocks, they produce no light, and have no mechanical function. Gemspark Walls are the illuminant variant.
Ogre: The Ogre is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss mini-boss that spawns in the Old One's Army event during wave 7 in Tier 2, and waves 5 and 6 in Tier 3.
Ogre Mask (unobtainable): The Ogre Mask is an unobtainable item. It is extremely similar in both name and appearance to the obtainable Ogre Mask. It only exists as an ID and image file in the game's code and therefore does nothing. Attempting to use third-party tools to obtain it will result in it instantly disappearing.
Ogre's Club: The Ogre's Club is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Ogre that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Ogre will hold onto an Etherian Wyvern by its tail in order to catch up to them. The Ogre's Club has a 1/4 (25%) chance of dropping from the Ogre in Master Mode.
Old Man: The Old Man is an NPC whose primary function is to summon Skeletron, and can be found at the Dungeon's entrance. When spoken to at night, the Old Man will give the player the option to “Curse”, which summons Skeletron. When spoken to during the day, the Old Man will tell the player to return at night. He will also judge players with 300 maximum health (15 hearts) or less, or 10 defense or less as unworthy, but still allows them to summon Skeletron.

The Dungeon can be entered without defeating Skeletron, but traveling deeper than ground level within it (below zero depth) will spawn Dungeon Guardians that will most likely kill the player on contact (see Guide:Dungeon Guardian strategies).
When Skeletron is defeated, the Old Man is freed from his curse and will arrive as the Clothier (as long as a vacant house is available), in addition to allowing access to the Dungeon.
Old One's Skeleton: The Old One's Skeleton is a pre-Hardmode boss servant that is summoned by the Dark Mage during the Old One's Army event.
The Old One's Skeleton requires 150 kills to be awarded completion of its corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Onyx Blaster: The Onyx Blaster is a Hardmode gun and the direct upgrade to the Shotgun. When used, it fires a spread of 4 bullets, consuming one piece of ammunition. It also fires an onyx crystal that explodes upon impact with an enemy or a block, or after traveling for 0.33 seconds. The projectile deals 200% of the weapon's damage, e.g. 62 damage when using Musket Ball.
Optic Staff: The Optic Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a miniature version of The Twins as minions. The pair of minions, named Spazmamini and Retanimini, fly towards enemies to dash through them and fire lasers at them, respectively. Each pair of Twins counts as a single minion towards the minion slot cap.
Orange Bloodroot: The Orange Bloodroot is a type of plant. It can grow below Dirt Blocks in the Underground and Cavern layers. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Orange Dye.
Orange Zapinator: The Orange Zapinator is a Hardmode magic gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Gold.

The weapon fires a blue laser beam that behaves very erratically. Upon striking an enemy, the projectile slows down by 40%, decreases its current damage and knockback by 10%, and can choose from an assortment of special effects as described below. The laser beam will disappear after hitting eight enemies or after 60 seconds. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, it costs no mana to use.
Orca: The Orca is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Ocean. It is a stronger version of the Shark, acting similarly but with higher stats.

Throwing a Chum Bucket into Ocean water will multiply the spawn chance of Orcas by 2.78×. Unlike Chum Buckets' effect on Fishing Power, only one use is required to boost the spawn chance of Orcas to maximum possible value.
Orichalcum Bar: The Orichalcum Bar is a Hardmode bar. It is one of the two ores able to create a Hardmode Anvil, which is used to craft most Hardmode equipment.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Bar.
Orichalcum Chainsaw: The Orichalcum Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Orichalcum Waraxe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Chainsaw.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Orichalcum Drill: The Orichalcum Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Orichalcum Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Drill. The Orichalcum Drill has slightly more pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Orichalcum Halberd: The Orichalcum Halberd is a Hardmode spear.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Halberd.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Orichalcum Ore: Orichalcum Ore belongs to the second tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the second altar broken, either it or Mythril Ore can spawn in the cavern layer. Mining Orichalcum Ore requires a Cobalt/Palladium Pickaxe or better.

As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
Orichalcum Pickaxe: The Orichalcum Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Orichalcum Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Pickaxe. The Orichalcum Pickaxe has slightly more pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Orichalcum Repeater: The Orichalcum Repeater is a Hardmode repeater.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Repeater.
Orichalcum Sword: The Orichalcum Sword is a Hardmode broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Sword.
Orichalcum Waraxe: The Orichalcum Waraxe is a Hardmode axe and the alternative to the Orichalcum Chainsaw.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Waraxe.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Orichalcum armor: Orichalcum armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Orichalcum Breastplate and Orichalcum Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Orichalcum Mask, Orichalcum Helmet, and Orichalcum Headgear, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Orichalcum Bars (216 Orichalcum Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Orichalcum Bars (312 Orichalcum Ore).
Its alternate ore counterpart is Mythril armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:

Upon enemy hits, a flower petal is summoned at the edge of the screen and is shot towards the target, moving to the other end of the screen and damaging every enemy along the way. The petal deals 36 classless damage. Petals travel very fast (123 mph) and can pass through blocks and liquids. There is a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before another flower petal can be summoned, meaning that this set bonus adds roughly 100 DPS.
Ornate Shadow Key: The Ornate Shadow Key is a pet-summoning item that spawns a pet Shadow Mimic to follow the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Shadow Mimic propels itself by spinning towards them while emitting a trail of purple flames. It will also occasionally spit out non-collectible cosmetic coins. The Ornate Shadow Key has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being obtained from Shadow Chests and a 1/20 (5%) chance of being obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.
Ouroboros Ring: The Ouroboros Ring is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:

Attacking with a whip 3 times in a row or after a 2 seconds delay causes the player to automatically perform an extra whip swing, dealing 30% of the whip's damage (minimum of 3 damage) and 25% of its knockback. The extra whip swing will be performed by the next whip in the player's inventory, or the same whip they are currently using if they have no other whips.
Owl: The Owl is a critter that spawns near Towns on the surface Forest and Hallow during the night, when it is not raining. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest tree at night. The Owl has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Owl can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Owl Cage). Once crafted, the Owl cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Owl can be spawned by the Owl Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Oyster: The Oyster is a consumable grab bag item, which when opened with ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory, contains a Shucked Oyster, and has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop (in order of increasing rarity) a White, Black, or Pink Pearl. Oysters can be acquired by fishing in the Desert biome.
PDA: The PDA is a post-Skeletron informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the in-game time, the weather, wind speed, moon phase, the player's Fishing Power, the most valuable block nearby, nearby rare creatures, the number of nearby enemies, the player's enemy kill count, the player's current DPS, the player's current movement speed, the player's horizontal position, and the player's depth.
Pad Thai: Pad Thai is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Pad Thai can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 55 Silver.
Paint Roller: The Paint Roller is a tool which is used to paint walls. It is purchased from the Painter for 1 Gold. Its upgrade, the Spectre Paint Roller, grants a bonus to range. Using a roller requires paint to be in the player's inventory.
The Paint Roller cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Paint Scraper: The Paint Scraper is a tool which is used to remove paint off tiles and walls, eliminating the need of breaking and re-placing a tile to remove its paint. The Paint Scraper is purchased for 1 Gold from the Painter. Its upgrade, the Spectre Paint Scraper, grants a bonus to range. Paint removed by a scraper can never be recovered.
The Paint Scraper can be used to obtain moss by removing it from tiles.
The Paint Scraper cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Paint Sprayer: The Paint Sprayer is a construction accessory that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. While equipped, or (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) when held in the inventory, it automatically applies paint or coating to any object when placing it. Like the Paintbrush and the Paint Roller, it will use the paint that is first in order in the inventory.
Paintball Gun: The Paintball Gun is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that fires a three-shot burst of slow-moving, arcing multicolored Paintball projectiles which consume no mana or ammunition, dissipating upon contact with an enemy or surface. The Paintball Gun has a 11% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%. It has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by the Painter.

The Paintball projectiles cause certain slimes (see Notes for the full list) to change color on hit, according to the color of the Paintball. This is a purely visual change – it does not change the slime's type, AI, or stats. It lasts until the slime is hit by another Paintball, comes into contact with a painted block, or dies.
Paintbrush: The Paintbrush is a tool which is used to apply paint to tiles. It is purchased from the Painter for 1 Gold. Its upgrade, the Spectre Paintbrush, grants a bonus to range.
The Paintbrush cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Painter: The Painter is an NPC vendor who sells paint and painting tools, as well as paintings and wallpapers. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
8 other town NPCs are in the world. Note that while the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, and town pets count towards this total, the Skeleton Merchant does not.
The Painter's shop inventory changes based on external factors. The biome in which he is talked to, the moon phase, and seasonal events all determine which paintings and wallpapers are available.

He has two shop menus: one is the default “Shop”, where paint and painting tools are sold; the other is “Decor”, where paintings and wallpapers are sold. If any pylon is available, it is sold in both shop menus.

The Painter will defend himself against nearby enemies with his Paintball Gun. He deals 8 / 12 / 14 damage during pre-Hardmode, which increases to 10 / 15 / 17 damage during Hardmode, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Painter also has a 1/10 (10%) chance of dropping the Paintball Gun upon death.
Paintings: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares.

There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.
Paints: Paint is used to modify the color of objects. Nearly anything can be painted, including blocks, background walls, and furniture, along with non-collectable environment objects like trees, tall grass, flowers, and other ambient growth. Basic paint is purchased from the Painter NPC. Two of the same color can be combined at a Dye Vat to create "deep" color versions, which apply their color more vividly and are required in order to paint certain objects.
Coating (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is used to apply a special effect over a block and can be applied in tandem with paint and other coatings. It is purchased from the Painter NPC.

Paint and coatings are applied to blocks and furniture with the Paintbrush, and to walls with the Paint Roller, with each tile consuming one item of paint/coating. The Paint Sprayer will automatically paint items when placing them. Paint and coatings can be removed with the Paint Scraper, although they will never be retrieved upon doing so. Destroying a painted block will not drop the paint item either.

Paint can be placed in ammo slots. If more than one type of paint or coating is present in the player's inventory, the paint or coating in the earliest inventory slot is used first (starting from the top-left slot).
Pair of Eyeballs: The Pair of Eyeballs is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns Rez and Spaz, miniature versions of The Twins in their first form. The Pair of Eyeballs has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by The Twins in Master Mode.
Pal Metal set: The Pal Metal set is a vanity set consisting of the Pal Metal Chestplate and Pal Metal Leggings.

These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold (set) if the player has Cattiva, Foxparks, Chillet, Chillet Ignis, Digtoise, or their "Trusty" variants in their inventory or in any portable storage item upon speaking to the NPC.
Paladin: The Paladin is a rare, resilient Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It is immune to knockback and attacks by rapidly throwing hammer projectiles which can pass through blocks and inflict extreme damage.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. The Paladin requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Paladins spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by brick walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Paladin's Hammer: The Paladin's Hammer is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that has a 1/15 (6.67%) / 29/225 (12.89%) chance of being dropped by Paladins in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it swings once before being thrown at a high velocity, piercing an infinite number of enemies, and returning to the player after traveling a certain distance or upon hitting solid blocks.

Upon colliding with blocks after being thrown, it creates a huge shockwave that inflicts 175% of the weapon's knockback (base knockback of 15.75 (Insane)) to nearby enemies. Both the hammer and its shockwave inflict the Broken Armor debuff for 1.5 seconds to enemies and for 10–20 seconds to other players on PvP, which adds 20 armor penetration against enemies and halves the defense of players.

The thrown hammer deals 133.3% of the weapon's damage (133 base damage) on its first hit. Afterwards, it deals 90% of the weapon's damage to the second enemy hit and then loses 10% damage on each subsequent hit, dealing 81% damage to the third enemy, 72.9% damage to the fourth enemy, and so on.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Paladin's Shield: The Paladin's Shield is a Hardmode, post-Plantera shield that has a 1/10 (10%) / 19/100 (19%) chance of being dropped by Paladins in the Hardmode Dungeon. While equipped, it grants the following effects:

While the wearer's health is above 25%, it grants all nearby players on their team (excluding themselves) the Paladin's Shield buff, which provides 25% damage reduction and redirects that damage to the wearer.
Palladium Bar: The Palladium Bar is a Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Bar.
Palladium Chainsaw: The Palladium Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Palladium Waraxe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Chainsaw.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Palladium Column: The Palladium Column is a building material crafted from Stone Blocks and Palladium Ore. It is essentially the Palladium Ore's equivalent of a brick.
Palladium Column Wall: Palladium Column Wall is a wall crafted from Palladium Columns.
Palladium Drill: The Palladium Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Palladium Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Mythril and Orichalcum Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Drill. The Palladium Drill has slightly more pickaxe power and damage.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Palladium Ore: Palladium Ore belongs to the first tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the first altar broken, either it or Cobalt Ore will spawn in the underground and cavern layers. Mining Palladium Ore requires a Molten Pickaxe or better.

As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
Palladium Pickaxe: The Palladium Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Palladium Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Mythril and Orichalcum Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Pickaxe. The Palladium Pickaxe has slightly more pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Palladium Pike: The Palladium Pike is a Hardmode spear.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Naginata.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Palladium Repeater: The Palladium Repeater is a Hardmode repeater.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Repeater.
Palladium Sword: The Palladium Sword is a Hardmode broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Sword. The Palladium Sword has slightly higher damage and knockback, but a slower attack speed.
Palladium Waraxe: The Palladium Waraxe is a Hardmode axe and the alternative to the Palladium Chainsaw.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Waraxe.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Palladium armor: Palladium armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Palladium Breastplate and Palladium Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Palladium Mask, Palladium Helmet, and Palladium Headgear, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Palladium Bars (162 Palladium Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Palladium Bars (234 Palladium Ore).
Its alternate ore counterpart is Cobalt armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:
Hitting an enemy grants the Rapid Healing buff for 5 seconds, providing a flat health regeneration of 2 HP per second.
Further hits will refresh the duration. The buff is not canceled when the armor is removed.
Being flat health regeneration, it applies separately from the normal type. This also causes this regeneration to bypass the Bleeding debuff.
While this buff is applied, the player emits visual orange heart particles.
Palm Wood: Palm Wood is a type of wood harvested from Palm trees found naturally growing in the Ocean biome and Oasis biome. Palm trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of regular Sand Blocks above surface.
Only regular Palm trees growing on regular Sand will drop Palm Wood. Palm trees that are growing on Ebonsand, Crimsand, or Pearlsand will instead drop Ebonwood, Shadewood or Pearlwood, respectively.
Palm Wood Bow: The Palm Wood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Palm Wood Hammer: The Palm Wood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Palm Wood Sword: The Palm Wood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword.
Palm Wood Wall: Palm Wood Wall is a background wall made from Palm Wood.
Palm Wood armor: Palm Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Palm Wood Helmet, Palm Wood Breastplate, and Palm Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Palm Wood. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.
Panda Ears: Panda Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.
Panic Necklace: The Panic Necklace is an accessory, that, when equipped, grants the player the Panic! buff for 8 seconds when harmed by any source of damage besides fire blocks, increasing movement speed by 100%. The Panic Necklace has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Crimson Hearts found in The Crimson or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Crimson Crates and Hematic Crates, which are fished in the Crimson. It can furthermore be crafted.
Paper Airplanes: The Paper Airplane and White Paper Airplane are consumable ranged weapons. When thrown, they will travel in a different path each time, as they are affected by wind speed and direction, which is especially apparent on a Windy Day. The two variants are functionally identical. They are sometimes dropped by slimes that are carried by Windy Balloons, which can spawn during a Windy Day.
Unlike other consumable ranged weapons, Paper Airplanes always drop as an item after flying for too long, hitting a block, or hitting an enemy.
Papyrus Scarab: The Papyrus Scarab is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that combines the bonuses of the Necromantic Scroll and the Hercules Beetle. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Parka set: The Parka set is a vanity set which consists of Parka Hood, Parka Coat, and Parka Pants. It is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in Pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Parrot: The Parrot is a Hardmode flying enemy that spawns during the Pirate Invasion. It flies towards the player in an attempt to deal contact damage. It will occasionally roost on any block if not pursuing the player, similarly to Ravens and Vultures.
Parrot Cracker: The Parrot Cracker is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Parrot that follows the player. If the player stays still for long enough, it will perch on a nearby solid block, staying still until the player moves away from it. The Parrot Cracker can be purchased from the Pirate for 3 Platinum 75 Gold if he is spoken to in an Ocean biome.
Party Bullet: The Party Bullet is a bullet that releases a visual cloud of confetti upon contact with enemies or blocks.

Party Bullets are craftable with a Hardmode ingredient (see Crafting section below). Party Bullets can also be dropped from a Pigronata with a 1/9 (11.11%) chance; this is the only way to obtain Party Bullets pre-Hardmode.

Party Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Party Bullets is 4 Silver 50 Copper, which is 9 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Party Bullets is 9 Gold.
Party Center: The Party Center is an animated novelty mechanism furniture item bought from the Party Girl NPC for 20 Gold. Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on a Party Center toggles the Party event.
Party Girl: The Party Girl is an NPC vendor who sells festive novelty items and furniture.

Unlike other town NPCs, the Party Girl only has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to be eligible for spawning every 2-minute interval, during which she is subject to regular NPC spawn rate, once the criteria below are met. In other words, she will take on average 40 times longer to spawn than regular NPCs. Along with this percentage chance, she will move in once the following criteria are met:
There is an available vacant house.
20 other town NPCs are in the world. Note that while the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, and town pets count towards this total, the Skeleton Merchant does not.
If the Party Girl is killed, she will respawn with normal spawn chances instead of being rarer.

The Party Girl will defend herself against nearby enemies by throwing Happy Grenades. She deals 30 / 45 / 52 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Party Girl also has a 1/4 (25%) chance of dropping 30–60 Happy Grenades upon death.
During a natural Party, she will give a Slice of Cake to the first player that talks to her.
Party Hat: The Party Hat is a Vanity item sold by the Party Girl NPC for 1 Gold.
Party Present: The Party Present is a decorative furniture item that can be purchased from the Party Girl during a Party for 20 Silver. It has one of several different appearances when placed, similar to Books.
Peace Candle: The Peace Candle is a furniture item that emits a low amount of light and can be placed only on flat-surface items. While placed nearby or while held, it grants the Peace Candle buff to the player.

The Peace Candle buff decreases spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%. The buff is applied to any players holding a Peace Candle or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Peace Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice. Multiple Candles will not stack with each other, even if one is placed and the other held. Peace Candles can only be placed on platforms and flat furniture items like Work Benches and Tables.
The Peace Candle can be made from a Pink Torch and either Gold Bars or Platinum Bars, meaning that the player needs to have defeated Pinky at least once to craft this item.
Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on Peace Candles shuts them off, and they will toggle when activated via wiring. Peace Candles that are turned off will not activate the Peace Candle buff.

The Peace Candle's effect is the opposite of the Water Candle, which increases enemy spawn rate. If a Peace Candle and a Water Candle are active at the same time, they will cancel each other's effects out, resulting in no difference in spawn rate.
Peach: The Peach is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Forest tree.
Peach Sangria: The Peach Sangria is a food item that grants Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Pearls: Pearls are crafting materials obtained from opening Oysters, and are used to craft Luck Potions. Each of the three pearls have different rarities, with the rarer ones being crafted into stronger potions. Additionally, when the Pink Pearl is thrown into Shimmer, it turns into a Galaxy Pearl. The player can only receive one pearl from each Oyster, with a 1/4 (25%) chance in total.
Pearlstone Block: The Pearlstone Block is a Hardmode block type found in The Hallow. It requires at least a Nightmare Pickaxe, Deathbringer Pickaxe, or explosives to mine.

Pearlstone is the Hallow version of Stone (similar to Ebonstone in The Corruption, or Crimstone in The Crimson). In a way similar to Ebonstone and Crimstone, Pearlstone can be converted into ordinary Stone via Vile Powder, Vicious Powder, or the Clentaminator with the Green Solution.

During the initial creation of the Hallow biome upon the defeat of the Wall of Flesh, Stone blocks in the conversion path become Pearlstone blocks (see Hardmode). Pearlstone itself also continues to spread Hallow to all Stone, Sand, Ice, and Grass covered dirt within a three tile radius. Over time, it will grow Crystal Shards if it is in the Cavern layer or below.
Pearlstone Brick: Pearlstone Brick is a brick made from Pearlstone. It does not spread The Hallow when placed, therefore making it a safer construction material than its raw ingredients.
Pearlstone Brick Wall: Pearlstone Brick Walls are a type of wall crafted from Pearlstone Bricks. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.
Pearlstone Wall: The Pearlstone Wall is a type of background wall which can be found in Corruption/Crimson chasms that have been taken over by the Hallow, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
The Clentaminator/Terraformer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) (using Blue Solution) and Holy Water convert Stone Walls to unsafe Pearlstone Walls.
Pearlstone Walls can spread The Hallow to nearby pure walls. See Biome spread for further information.
Pearlwood: Pearlwood is a Hardmode-exclusive type of wood harvested from Pearlwood trees and Pearlwood Palm trees found naturally growing in Hallow biomes. Pearlwood trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Hallowed grass or Mowed Hallowed grass above surface, and Pearlwood Palm trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Pearlsand Blocks above surface.
Pearlwood Bow: The Pearlwood Bow is a Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Pearlwood Crate: The Pearlwood Crate is a Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. It is the lowest tier of standard crate, having the least value if sold directly. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Wooden Crate.
Pearlwood Hammer: The Pearlwood Hammer is a Hardmode hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Pearlwood Sword: The Pearlwood Sword is a Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword.
Pearlwood Wall: Pearlwood Wall is a type of wall made from Pearlwood.
Pearlwood armor: Pearlwood armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pearlwood Helmet, Pearlwood Breastplate, and Pearlwood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Pearlwood. The full set grants 8 defense while equipped.
Peddler's Hat: The Peddler's Hat is a vanity item that always drops from the Traveling Merchant if he is killed. It appears identical to the hat that the Traveling Merchant wears.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) When dropped into Shimmer, it turns into a Peddler's Satchel.
Peddler's Satchel: The Peddler's Satchel is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the number of items sold by the Traveling Merchant by 1. It can only be used once in the world and is obtained by throwing a Peddler's Hat into Shimmer.
Consuming the item displays the status message "The Traveling Merchant's satchel deepens!".
Pedguin's set: Pedguin's set is a vanity set. Each piece has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt and Vicious Penguins.
Penguin: The Penguin is a harmless critter that only spawns in the Snow biome and may spawn with different colors. The Penguin has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Penguin can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Penguin Cage). Once crafted, the Penguin cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Penguin can be spawned by the Penguin Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile/Vicious Powder, Penguins will turn into Corrupt Penguins or Vicious Penguins.
Pew-matic Horn: The Pew-matic Horn is a pre-Hardmode gun that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. When used, it converts any bullet into a randomized item fired as a projectile. The projectiles travel in an arc and dissipate upon contact with an enemy or block. The projectile's damage varies depending on its appearance.
Phantasm: The Phantasm is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist bow. When used, it fires a burst of four arrows that are loosely grouped together, while only consuming one arrow per use. Its fire rate will gradually increase while in use. Upon enemy hits, the Phantasm fires an additional burst of three Phantasm Arrow projectiles. Phantasm Arrows home in on the hit target, move through blocks, deal 30% of the original projectile's damage, and inflict no knockback. The Phantasm has a 2/3 (66.67%) chance of not consuming ammunition.
Its best modifier is Unreal, Godly or Demonic, as it does not benefit from attack speed and velocity modifiers.
Phantasm Dragon: The Phantasm Dragon is a Hardmode boss servant that is summoned by the Lunatic Cultist. Its behavior is nearly identical to the Wyvern's. The Lunatic Cultist summons a Phantasm Dragon when the player attacks one of the Lunatic's duplicates or takes too long to hit the real one during its ritual attack. If the player does the above action again while a Phantasm Dragon is still alive, the Lunatic Cultist will summon an Ancient Vision instead.
Phantom Phoenix: The Phantom Phoenix is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss bow. When used, it fires a slight spread of two arrows, alongside a large Phoenix projectile on every third use. The weapon only consumes 1 arrow per use, and its use time is increased by 50% after firing a Phoenix projectile (base use time of 27 (Average)) but returns to normal after firing arrows. The Phoenix projectile deals 200% of the weapon's damage (74 base damage when using Wooden Arrows) and 100% of its knockback (base knockback of 4 (Weak) when using Wooden Arrows), inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 8 seconds and pierces infinitely, but loses 5% of its damage per hit. The Phoenix explodes after traveling for 2 seconds or upon colliding with blocks and liquids, dealing damage within a 6×6-tile rectangular area centered around the point of impact. The Phantom Phoenix also converts Wooden Arrows into Flaming Arrows, without increasing their damage.
The Phantom Phoenix is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3.
Pharaoh's set: The Pharaoh's set is a vanity set consisting of the Pharaoh's Mask and the Pharaoh's Robe. A full set can be found in a Gold Chest within a Pyramid, at a 1/9 (11.11%) chance. On Celebration Mk 10 worlds, this chance is guaranteed.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can also be obtained by throwing a Sandstorm in a Bottle and a Flying Carpet into Shimmer to get each respective vanity piece.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Phase Dye: Phase Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It seems to invert the colors of the object it is attached to as well as giving a strange purple aura.
When the user is damaged, the dye flashes very quickly.
Phaseblades: Phaseblades are a group of pre-Hardmode broadswords. There are nine different color variations with identical statistics. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapons, causing them to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds or upon contact with blocks, then embed themselves in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches them. They can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. They can also be recalled mid-throw. All phaseblades emit a small amount of light corresponding to their color when swung, thrown, or embedded in the ground.
Phasesabers are the Hardmode upgrades of the phaseblades.
Phasesabers: Phasesabers are a group of Hardmode broadswords, direct upgrades to the phaseblades with much more damage and slightly faster use time. There are nine different color variations with identical statistics. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapons, causing them to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds or upon contact with blocks, then embed themselves in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches them. They can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. They can also be recalled mid-throw. All phasesabers emit a small amount of light corresponding to their color when swung, thrown, or embedded in the ground.
Phasic Warp Ejector: The Phasic Warp Ejector is an unimplemented and incomplete item. Its only remains in the game files are an item ID and an image, containing no stats or behavior.
The Phasic Warp Ejector has an associated projectile named the "Phasic Warp Disc", although its intended function is unknown.
Philosopher's Stone: The Philosopher's Stone is a Hardmode accessory which decreases the Potion Sickness debuff duration by 25%. This debuff normally imposes a 60-second cooldown after consuming a recovery potion; the Philosopher's Stone reduces it to 45 seconds. It has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance to be dropped by Mimics.
Pho: Pho is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Pho can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 75 Silver.
Phoenix Blaster: The Phoenix Blaster is a pre-Hardmode gun and the direct upgrade to the Handgun, with increased damage and velocity but slightly less knockback.
Phoenix Quiver: The Phoenix Quiver is a Hardmode accessory made by combining a Harpy Charm and a Molten Quiver at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Arrows are periodically redirected towards enemies; redirected arrows inflict the Hellfire debuff on hit for 5 seconds
Grants the following boosts to weapons that fire arrows or Stakes:
Wooden Arrows and Endless Quiver are converted into Flaming Arrows when fired
Pianos: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement.

There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 / 10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.
Pickaxe Axe: The Pickaxe Axe is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses pickaxe and axe. It is the alternative to the Drax, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Picksaw: The Picksaw is a Hardmode pickaxe and axe that has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Golem. It can mine all blocks.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Piece of Moon Squid: The Piece of Moon Squid is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pet-summoning item that spawns a Moonling, which resembles the Moon Lord's head, that follows the player. The Piece of Moon Squid has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord in Master Mode.
Piggy Bank: The Piggy Bank is a portable storage item which can be purchased from the Merchant for 1 Gold. It requires a flat-surface item for placement. It has 40 slots like other storage items. The Piggy Bank inventory can also be accessed via the Money Trough (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Eye Bone (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Unlike normal Chests, the Piggy bank (along with the Safe, Defender's Forge, and Void Vault) is considered "personal storage". Items contained in a Piggy Bank are attached to the character rather than to a container in the world: The bank can be picked up and moved regardless of the items within. Coins and items stored within it are safe from other players, and will not be dropped on death. They will even travel with a character who goes to a different world. However, if a Hardcore character dies, all items in their personal storage will be deleted with the character and permanently lost.
Pigron: The Pigron is a Hardmode enemy found in the Ice biome when it is overlapped with the Underground Corruption, Underground Crimson, or Underground Hallow. It has multiple color variants, depending on which overlapping biome it spawns in, but all share identical stats and behavior.

Pigrons have a special ability to become transparent and nearly invisible, allowing them to fly through solid blocks. As a transparent Pigron starts to attack, it will become visible again. When it starts moving towards the player, it occasionally makes an audible growl. If it is in its solid, visible state and is blocked by solid blocks on its path to the player, it will become transparent again to pass through them.
Pigronata: The Pigronata is a placeable furniture item hung by the player from the underside of blocks, similar to banners. When hit with weapons or projectiles, it is destroyed in a shower of confetti, and drops coins and/or other loot. Pigronatas can be purchased from the Party Girl during a Party for 1 Gold each.
Pin Flags: Pin Flags are furniture items used in golfing. They are purely decorative and come in multiple colors. They can be purchased from the Golfer for 20 Silver each.
Pin Wheel: The Pin Wheel is a novelty furniture. When placed, the wheel spins if it is windy, with its spin speed depending on the current wind speed in the area. It is purchased from the Merchant for 20 Silver during the Windy Day event.
Pine Tree Block: Pine Tree Blocks are blocks that are dropped in stacks of 20–49 from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event (December 15–December 31), with a chance of 16.803% in pre-Hardmode and 15.683% in Hardmode. When placed, a Pine Tree Block appears to be a small sapling, but will become bigger as more are added. If one or more are stacked on a single block, it will appear as a trunk.
Pine Tree Blocks can be used to craft the alternative Pine Wood block, and they both can be used to craft Pine furniture.
Pine Tree Wall: Pine Tree Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Pine Tree Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Pine Wood: Pine Wood is a type of wood crafted from Pine Tree Blocks.
Pine Wood Wall: Pine Wood Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Pine Wood Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Pineapple: The Pineapple is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Mahogany tree.
Pink Fairy: The Pink Fairy, Green Fairy, and Blue Fairy are critters that emit light, which will attempt to lead the player to valuable treasures, such as Life Crystals, Chests, or ore deposits. They spawn in the bottom half of the Underground layer and in the Cavern layer, but only if at least one Fallen Log is present in the world on the surface (see Fallen Log § Notes for the exact area). If all Fallen Logs have been destroyed, they will no longer spawn independently. The three fairy variants all function identically.

Fairies can also spawn at Fallen Logs and from shaken Pearlwood trees on the surface at night. In this case, they will not lead players to treasure; instead, when approached, they try to flee much like Birds or Faelings. Unlike fairies spawned underground, these fairies can be caught with a Bug Net and carried around in the inventory. If released again, they act like the ones spawned underground and will attempt to lead the player to treasure. They can also be crafted into animated decorative furniture (Fairy jars). Once crafted, the fairies cannot be released again unless de-crafted via Shimmer.
They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Pink Gel: Pink Gel is a rare crafting material dropped by Pinky in stacks of 25–50. It is primarily used to craft "bouncy" versions of certain consumable items, as well as Restoration Potions. "Bouncy" items act like their normal variants, but bounce more times and more vigorously before losing momentum.
Crafting one of each item requires 22 Pink Gel, meaning that killing a single Pinky is sufficient to craft all items at least once.
