Pink Gel Dye: Pink Gel Dye is a dye that is crafted from Gel Dye. The Gel Dye can be acquired from the Dye Trader, and can be combined with Pink Gel, a crafting material dropped by Pinky, at a Dye Vat. Just like the Gel Dye, the Pink Gel Dye will produce an effect similar to the Slime debuff caused by the Slime Gun, though it will be displayed in a color that's more pink than blue.
Pink Horseshoe Balloon: The Pink Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 33% and jump speed by 30%, grants a double jump, and grants +0.05 luck. The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks (~75% increase), while the double jump's height is increased from 7 blocks to 13 blocks, reaching a total of 23.5 blocks with both jumps.
Jump height is oddly reduced when underwater, reducing total underwater jump height from 17.5 blocks (8 blocks + 9½ blocks from Tsunami jump) to 15 blocks (7 blocks + 8 blocks from Tsunami jump).
Pink Jellyfish: Jellyfish are enemies found in water. When underwater, they attack by propelling themselves towards the player in short bursts. When outside of water, they will be unable to move or pursue the player in any way. Jellyfish are able to jump out of the water to attack players, often leaving them stranded on land. Most varieties of Jellyfish produce light, making them easy to spot in dark areas. There are 5 Jellyfish variants, 3 of which only appear during Hardmode.

In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a Jellyfish will periodically become "electrified" (except for Fungo Fish). During this electrified state, it is invincible, and will constantly maintain its speed unless it comes into contact with a solid block or the water's surface. Certain attacks to Jellyfish in this state will hurt the player by 1.3× the contact damage of the Jellyfish (see Notes for details). Unlike other damage sources, this damage will not be reduced by banners.
Pink Maid set: The Pink Maid set is a vanity set consisting of the Pink Maid Bonnet, Pink Maid Dress and Pink Maid Shoes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Pink Prickly Pear: The Pink Prickly Pear is a dye material. It grows on top of regular or Hallowed Cacti above surface, but can also be seen on top of Corrupt or Crimson Cacti (see Notes for details). Unlike many plants, instead of being broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to craft Pink Dye.
Pink Slime Block: The Pink Slime Block can be created with Pink Gel if the player is near a Solidifier. In a similar way to Silly Balloons, landing on Pink Slime Blocks negates fall damage and causes the player to bounce. Like with Slime Blocks, running over Pink Slime Blocks produces droplet particles.

The height of the bounce is dependent on the player's speed, not on the distance they've fallen. Holding a Portal Gun or riding the Slime Mount can allow for higher bounce due to the higher speed limit.
Pink Snow armor: Pink Snow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pink Snow Hood, Pink Snow Coat, and Pink Snow Pants.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Immunity to the Chilled and Frozen debuffs
Pink Snow armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Snow armor, still providing the set bonus.
Pink Vase: The Pink Vase is a decorative furniture item. A placed Pink Vase also serves as a Placed Bottle for potion crafting.
Pinky: Pinky is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in place of certain types of other slimes (see Notes section for details). Despite its small size, Pinky has more health and defense than nearly all other pre-Hardmode slimes, though it has one of the lowest values of damage and knockback resistance in the game. It is also the only source of Pink Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Like most other slimes, the Pinky will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
On Desktop, Console, Mobile, and 3DS, they can rarely be found carrying bonus drops, which the player receives upon the slime's death.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. Pinky requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Piranha: The Piranha is a pre-Hardmode enemy that can be found in water pools in the Jungle and Underground Jungle biomes, as well as in the Cavern layer. It is twice as common in the Jungle biomes.

Piranhas swim in a straight line left or right until hitting a wall, where they flip directions. They will swim towards the player if they are submerged in water; otherwise, they pay no attention to them. They move their tail back and forth and swim in a slight zig-zag. If a Piranha is outside of water, it will flop around wildly, making it dangerous to approach.
Piranha Gun: The Piranha Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged weapon that costs no ammunition. It fires a spread of three returning Mechanical Piranha projectiles that inflict the Hemorrhage debuff for 4–6 seconds on hit. The Mechanical Piranha initially moves in a straight path until it collides with an enemy, at which point it latches into the target, follows its movement and deals continuous damage while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held. If the initial target is killed and the button is still held, the projectiles will home in towards other nearby enemies. The Piranhas return to the gun when the button is released or once no other enemies are in the vicinity, and despawn after one minute of continuous use. Any Piranhas that return to the gun while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held will be automatically relaunched towards the cursor. Each Piranha can target different enemies, or the same one if there are too few nearby. The Piranha Gun is always found in the Dungeon's Jungle Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Jungle Key after Plantera has been defeated.
Its best modifier is Unreal. Because its attack speed is unaffected by modifiers, Godly and Demonic can also be considered the best modifiers for the Piranha Gun.
Pirate: The Pirate is a Hardmode NPC vendor who sells cannons and other pirate-related items, with a nearly identical appearance to the Pirate Captain enemy. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
The Pirate Invasion event has been completed at least once.
He will defend himself using his Pirate Cannon, which fires both bullets and cannonballs.
Pirate Captain: The Pirate Captain is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Pirate Invasion event. Upon being within line of sight of the player, he attacks using an assault rifle-like gun that shoots at a speed comparable to the Minishark, then stops to fire a single cannonball from its underbarrel mounted cannon while stationary. The cannonball has a short range and detonates upon impact with blocks, much like those fired from the Flying Dutchman, and deals immense amounts of damage.

A Pirate's Curse will be spawned when a Pirate Captain is killed. It will slowly drift towards the player through walls much like Wraiths, but it can freely fly through the air and does not need to hover on blocks.

He is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Pirate Captain requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of his Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Pirate Corsair: The Pirate Corsair is a Hardmode enemy that spawns commonly during the Pirate Invasion. It moves towards the player by running and jumping, similar to the Pirate Deckhand, but has slightly higher stats.
Pirate Crossbower: The Pirate Crossbower is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Pirate Invasion event. She fires Flaming Arrows every few seconds, which deal high damage and have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff for 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds.
Pirate Deadeye: The Pirate Deadeye is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Pirate Invasion event. It appears similar to the Pirate Deckhand but comes armed with a blunderbuss that can fire bullets at the player, an eye patch, and slightly modified stats.
Pirate Deckhand: The Pirate Deckhand is a Hardmode enemy which appears during a Pirate Invasion. It moves towards the player by running and jumping, similar to the Pirate Corsair.
Pirate Map: The Pirate Map is a Hardmode event-summoning item used to summon a Pirate Invasion. The Pirate Map has a 1/100 (1%) chance of dropping from most enemies killed in the surface Ocean biome during Hardmode (see Notes for more details).
In order for it to be used, at least one player must have 200 health or more.
Pirate Staff: The Pirate Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Pirate minion. It runs and jumps towards enemies, attacking with a sword up close. When trying to reach an enemy that is too high above it, the Pirate minion can also double jump or use a grappling hook while mid-air to reach it.

The Pirate Staff has a 1/1000 (0.1%) chance to be dropped by regular pirates (except Parrots) during the Pirate Invasion event. The Pirate Staff has an increased 1/250 (0.4%) chance to be dropped from Pirate Captains, and a higher 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be dropped by the Flying Dutchman.
Pirate set: The Pirate set is a vanity set which consists of the Pirate Hat, Pirate Shirt and Pirate Pants. They are purchased from the Pirate for 15 Gold (set).
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Pixel Box: The Pixel Box is a mechanism that can be bought from the Mechanic for 2 Silver. When activated, it looks fully illuminated but does not emit light.

Pixel Boxes can be placed anywhere, even if a wall is not present, similarly to Logic Gates. They are always placed in the deactivated state. If a wire below or above the Pixel Box is turned on at the same time as a wire to the left or right of the Pixel Box, it will turn on. Turning on the wire only below or above or only to the left or right will have no effect. Wires must be placed on the Pixel Box in order for them to function.
Pixie: The Pixie is a Hardmode enemy that spawns frequently in The Hallow at the surface layer. Pixies hover a limited height aboveground, emitting a fair amount of flickering light, and can inflict the Slow or Silenced debuffs upon contact. They always drop Pixie Dust, a common Hardmode crafting material.
Pixie Dust: Pixie Dust is a common Hardmode crafting material that always drops from Pixies.
Pixie Dye: Pixie Dye is a Hardmode dye sometimes acquired from the Dye Trader as a reward for completing a Strange Plant quest. It can only be obtained after defeating Plantera. When equipped, it turns the player yellow-orange, mimicking the slight glow that Pixies give off.
Pixie set: The Pixie set is a vanity set that can be obtained from Goodie Bags with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance. It consists of a Pixie Shirt and Pixie Pants.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Pizza: Pizza is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Pizza has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Hoplites and Medusas. Statue-spawned Hoplites and Medusas do not drop it, as it is a food item.
Piña Colada: The Piña Colada is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Plaguebringer's set: The Plaguebringer set is a vanity set consisting of the Plaguebringer's Skull, the Plaguebringer's Cloak, and the Plaguebringer's Treads. It is one of the six sets that were added as part of the Journey's End Vanity Contest; the original concept was submitted by SodaHunter.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Crafting the set requires materials that can only be found in the Crimson. Its Corruption counterpart is the Timeless Traveler's set.

It is possible for the player to create an artificial Crimson biome in a Corrupt world by purchasing Crimson Seeds from the Dryad in a Graveyard during Hardmode to get the materials necessary to make this set.
When the full set is worn, it displays a special set animation of Cursed Flames emitting from it. The color of the flames will change according to the dye applied to the cloak.
Planked Wall: Planked Wall is a background wall that naturally spawns in Underground Cabins. It can also be crafted.
Planter Boxes: Planter Boxes are flat-surface items of furniture purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver each in which herb or flower seeds can be planted. If left empty, wild grass plants will randomly grow out of them, provided the box is placed on the surface or in Space. The plant in a Planter Box cannot be cut in the regular manner, e.g. via nearby swinging tools. Instead, it needs to be removed with a pickaxe or drill, or the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth.
Planter Boxes are placed and act like platforms: They do not require support beneath them and they can be walked on, but pressing ▼ Down will let a player fall through them.

Although the various Planter Boxes have different seed names and appearances, the differences are purely cosmetic: Any herb seeds can grow in any Planter Box, and planting seeds in their respective Planter Boxes will not provide any extra benefit. Depending on the evil biome of the world, the Dryad will sell a Deathweed Planter Box showing either Corrupt grass or Crimson grass.
Plantera: Plantera is a Hardmode boss that can be fought in the Underground Jungle after all three mechanical bosses (The Twins, The Destroyer, and Skeletron Prime) have been defeated. Plantera drops a Temple Key upon being defeated, allowing access to the Jungle Temple.
While Plantera is alive, her exclusive music Plantera will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Plantera (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Plantera Seedling: The Plantera Seedling is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Plantera Seedling that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Plantera Seedling flies by twirling its petals like a propeller to catch up to them. The Plantera Seedling has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Plantera in Master Mode.
Plasma Lamp: The Plasma Lamp is a mechanism item that emits a faint blue light and has an animated texture. It is not considered a suitable light source for an NPC house. It is used purely as a decorative light source. The Plasma Lamp can be purchased from the Party Girl for 2 Gold.
Plate: The Plate is a decorative furniture item that can be placed. Once placed, food can be placed onto or removed from the Plate by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate.
Platforms: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above.
Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.
Platinum Axe: The Platinum Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Axe.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Platinum Bar: The Platinum Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Bar.
Platinum Bow: The Platinum Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Platinum Brick: Platinum Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Like the ore it's made of, placed Platinum Bricks will sparkle. Despite being made of Platinum, it has no sell value. It can be crafted into Platinum Brick Walls.
Platinum Brick Wall: Platinum Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Platinum Bricks. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.
Platinum Broadsword: The Platinum Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Platinum Shortsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Broadsword.
Platinum Crown: The Platinum Crown is a craftable vanity item that can be worn in the Social Helmet inventory slot. It is also one of the crafting materials for the Slime Crown, which is used to spawn the King Slime.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Crown.
Platinum Hammer: The Platinum Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Platinum Ore: Platinum Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on Floating Islands. Platinum Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Gold Ore.
Platinum Pickaxe: The Platinum Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. It can also mine Meteorite.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Pickaxe. The Platinum Pickaxe has slightly more pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Platinum Shortsword: The Platinum Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Platinum Broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Shortsword.

Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. Due to invincibility frames, modifiers with speed boosts reduce the hit rate of the Platinum Shortsword to enemies.
Platinum armor: Platinum armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Platinum Helmet, Platinum Chainmail, and Platinum Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Platinum Bars (300 Platinum Ore). The full set grants 20 defense while equipped.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Gold armor.
Plum: The Plum is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Boreal tree.
Plumber's set: The Plumber's set is a vanity set made up of the Plumber's Hat, the Plumber's Shirt, and the Plumber's Pants. The hat has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance to be dropped by Fire Imps, while the shirt and pants are purchased from the Clothier for 25 Gold each, during a full moon.
These items are purely vanity items and provide no increase in defense or other bonuses.
Pocket Mirror: The Pocket Mirror is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Stoned debuff. It has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by naturally spawned Medusas.
Pogo Stick: The Pogo Stick is a mount-summoning item that summons a Pogo Stick Mount. Jumping again while in the air causes the player to do a front flip. The Pogo Stick Mount doubles the speed at which the player falls, allowing a top falling speed of 102 mph. It also increases the maximum safe falling distance by 20 tiles, reduces fall damage by 75%, has a max horizontal speed of 26 mph, and keeps a certain amount of momentum while airborne, meaning it continues traveling in the last horizontal direction the player inputted while in the air, rather than slowing. The Pogo Stick can be purchased from the Party Girl for 25 Gold.
Poison Barb: The Poison Barb is a pre-Hardmode combat accessory that causes arrows fired by the player to inflict the Poisoned debuff for 1.5 seconds. The Poison Barb has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found inside surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing.
Poison Dart: The Poison Dart is a pre-Hardmode dart. It inflicts the Poisoned debuff on hit, which has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to last for 60 seconds, and a 2/3 (66.67%) chance to last for 30 seconds.
Poison Staff: The Poison Staff is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped by Black Recluses. When used, it fires a burst of 3–4 Poison Fangs in a roughly 30° spread. Each projectile pierces two enemies and inflicts the Poisoned debuff for 30 seconds.
Poisoned Knife: The Poisoned Knife is a consumable ranged weapon that has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff. It otherwise behaves exactly like the Throwing Knife, except for having slightly better stats overall and auto-use. It can hit up to 2 targets.
Poltergeist: The Poltergeist is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) wave 4 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) wave 5 of the Pumpkin Moon event. It behaves similarly to a Wraith, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) except it can fly freely through the air without needing solid ground to hover on.
Defeating a Poltergeist during the Pumpkin Moon event will add (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10 / 20 / 25 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 8 points to the final score.
The Poltergeist requires 100 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Pomegranate: The Pomegranate is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking an Ash tree.
Poo: Poo is a type of decorative block obtained by sitting on a toilet while any tier of the Well Fed buff is active. The time until Poo is produced is random, though it averages to 10 seconds. Having the Tipsy debuff will reduce this time by 66.67%. Producing Poo will remove the food buff, and the number of blocks dropped increases with the type of the buff and its remaining duration. The maximum number of Poo blocks acquirable at once is 169, from a Golden Delight with 47 minutes of buff time remaining while the player has negative luck.

When Poo is placed down, small flies will continuously fade in and out around it as a visual effect. The quantity of flies scales with the amount of Poo blocks placed in one area. Additionally, Poo blocks apply 3 seconds of the Stinky debuff to all players standing on them. Poo blocks create a squelchy sound when stepped on, and landing on top of them will also not inflict fall damage.
Poo can also generate naturally in Truck stop worlds or drop from the Jungle Mimic in Celebration Mk 10 worlds.
Poo can be used on an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to obtain Dirt, Grass Seeds, Jungle Grass Seeds, and Mushroom Grass Seeds.
Poo Boulder: The Poo Boulder is a special type of Boulder. It acts identically to the Boulder, with the exception of lasting longer and placing Poo when it breaks. A rolling Poo Boulder always inflicts the Poisoned and Stinky debuffs on players for 10 seconds on contact, whereas players standing on top of a stationary Poo Boulder are only inflicted with Stinky for 3 seconds. It can be encountered naturally in Not the Bees, Truck stop, or No Traps worlds.
Poo Wall: Poo Wall is a type of background wall crafted using Poo.
Pork of the Sea: The Pork of the Sea is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Tiny Fishron that follows the player. The Pork of the Sea has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron in Master Mode.
Portable Cement Mixer: The Portable Cement Mixer is a construction accessory that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. While equipped, it grants +50% placement speed when placing walls.
Portable Kiln: The Portable Kiln is a tool used to place decorative pots using items from the player's inventory. It is sold by the Demolitionist for 25 Gold.
The Portable Kiln can use various blocks to place down decorative pots which resemble pots from different biomes. These decorative pots only drop the block used to place them when destroyed.
The placement style of the pots can be cycled through by pressing the ▲ Up and ▼ Down button.
Portal Gun: The Portal Gun is a Hardmode tool that is always dropped from the Moon Lord. It launches projectiles that create up to two different portals upon contact with blocks: one fired using ⚒ Use / Attack, the other using ⚷ Open / Activate. Any player or NPC that touches one portal will be instantly transported to the other one, without losing momentum. Enemies, critters, projectiles, items, or liquids cannot be teleported.

While selected, the Portal Gun will also alter the player's physics: their maximum fall speed is multiplied by 3.5 (from 51 mph to 179 mph) and horizontal momentum/inertia is kept while in the air. This effect is also applied if the last entity that affected the player's fall was a portal.
The Cyborg sells the Portal Gun Station if the player has a Portal Gun in their inventory when speaking to him.
On the We don't even test for that secret world seed, the Portal Gun has a 1/7 (14.29%) of being obtained from any Chest.
Portal Gun Station: The Portal Gun Station is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord furniture item and mechanism that can fire portals, similar to the Portal Gun. The Portal Gun Station can be purchased from the Cyborg for 10 Gold if the player has a Portal Gun or another Portal Gun Station in their inventory.

Once placed, pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on different spots on the Portal Gun Station triggers different effects: pressing at the top toggles between orange and blue portal colors; pressing at the base fires a portal; pressing at the left or right side rotates its shooting direction. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, each rotation tilts it by one step (22.5°).

The Portal Gun Station can also be triggered by wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either change portal color, shoot portal (with a cooldown of 0.5 seconds), or rotate toward the side the wire is on.
Only a pair of portals can exist at a time for each player that has the Portal Gun or Portal Gun Station, whether created by the former or the latter.
Possessed Armor: The Possessed Armor is a Hardmode enemy which spawns on the surface at night, and underground at any time. It walks quickly and casts a motion blur similar to that of the Shadow armor. It can always open doors, regardless of whether or not there is a blood moon.
Possessed Hatchet: The Possessed Hatchet is a Hardmode, post-Golem boomerang that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped from Golem. When thrown, it homes in on enemies within 50 tiles and inflicts the Hemorrhage debuff on hit. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not have to return to the player before being fired, with no limit to the number that can be thrown out at one time.

With no enemies nearby, it returns to the player after traveling 25 tiles. The Possessed Hatchet can hit up to 10 targets. This is different from most boomerangs, which can hit infinite enemies while returning.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Possessed Skull: The Possessed Skull is a pet-summoning item that spawns Skeletron Jr. to follow the player. When the player is too far away or in midair, Skeletron Jr. will start spinning its head in order to catch up to them. The Possessed Skull has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Skeletron in Master Mode.
Possession: Possession is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord whip that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. It has a 5% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

Marks enemies with prophetic energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by Possession, it spawns a vision near the enemy, which fires a beam towards the target that deals 20 damage and has 50 armor penetration, but does not inflict knockback.
Uniquely among whips, it swings four times per use.
Potato Chips: The Potato Chips are a food item that grant the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 25 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Potato Chips have a 1/75 (1.33%) chance of being dropped by Crawdads, Giant Shellies, and Salamanders.
Potion of Return: The Potion of Return is a potion that teleports the player back to their spawn point, similar to the Recall Potion, and additionally creates a portal exit at the location where the potion was consumed. A portal entrance will be created at the spawn point, which can be used to teleport back to where the player consumed the potion. The portal can only be used once and will disappear afterwards. In addition to being crafted, the Potion of Return can be found in Pots in the Cavern layer and the Underworld, as well as in Shadow Chests.
Potted Crystal Plants: Potted Crystal Plants are placeable furniture items. They are purchased from the Princess for 10 Gold each.
Potted Lava Plants: Potted Lava Plants are placeable furniture items. They have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped when opening an Obsidian Crate or Hellstone Crate.
They give off a considerable amount of light when placed but do not count as light sources for NPC housing. They cannot be switched on or off using wiring.
Potted Trees: Potted Trees are decorative items purchased from the Dryad for 3 Gold each.
Power Bomb: The Power Bomb is a Hardmode explosive that is a direct upgrade to the Bomb. It explodes 5 seconds after being thrown, and breaks nearly all blocks, background walls, and furniture within a radius of 9 tiles. Unlike other explosives, it can additionally destroy the early Hardmode ores, although it still cannot destroy other explosion-proof objects. The explosion also deals 200 classless damage to all enemies, critters, and players (but not NPCs) within 8.75 tiles horizontally and vertically of the Power Bomb.
If the player is within 15 tiles of a thrown Power Bomb, they can use ⚷ Open / Activate on it to turn it back into item form and cancel the explosion, and then pick it up.
Power Glove: The Power Glove is a Hardmode accessory. While equipped, it grants the following effects:
Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips
Pre-Hardmode Anvils: The Iron Anvil and Lead Anvil are pre-Hardmode crafting stations used mainly to craft weapons and armor. Both anvils can craft the same items. Most of their recipes require metal bars, although they are also used to make other items, such as the Jungle tier of equipment. An anvil is a vital crafting station for most of the game, as it is used to make items from every tier up to Cobalt and Palladium, after which it must be replaced by a Mythril or Orichalcum Anvil.
Both anvils are craftable, but can sometimes also be found in Underground Cabins. The Iron Anvil can furthermore be purchased from the Merchant.
Predictor: The Predictor is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Nebula Pillar during the Lunar Events. It walks slowly until it is within the line-of-sight of the player, at which point it stops in place and releases four Nebula Piercer projectiles which rise up around it for 1.5 seconds, and then launches them towards the player in a tight spread.
Present: The Present is a grab bag item available during the Christmas seasonal event which contains a random Christmas-themed reward. It can be opened by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it in the player's inventory, similar to all other grab bags. Presents can be opened anytime, even outside the Christmas season.

Presents are dropped with a 1/13 (7.69%) chance by any enemy that has more than 1 maximum health, deals more than 0 damage, and drops coins, during Christmas only. Therefore, enemies spawned by statues, enemies from the Old One's Army and Lunar Events, etc. can never drop Presents (see Coin drops for the full list). Moreover, Meteor Heads cannot drop Presents either.
Presents can be placed down as furniture, and one of eight possible appearances can be cycled through by pressing ▲ Up and ▼ Down.
Present Mimic: The Present Mimic is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Frost Moon event. It acts like normal Mimics do, but passes itself off as a present instead of a Chest. Present Mimics may spawn at any wave, instead of wave-appropriate enemies, if there are currently less than four Present Mimics around.
Defeating a Present Mimic during the Frost Moon event will add 20 / 40 / 50 points to the final score.
Presserator: The Presserator is a construction accessory that is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. It automatically places Actuators to objects when placing them. It requires Actuators to be in the player's inventory in order to function.

The Presserator can be used as long as it is in the player's inventory or equipped. When held or equipped, a toggle for controlling the function of this item appears to the left of the main inventory / in the tools menu below the inventory.
Pressure Plate Track: Pressure Plate Tracks are activation mechanisms that work similarly to Pressure Plates and are activated while riding over with a Minecart. They can be crafted using any type of Pressure Plate.
Pressure Plates: Pressure Plates are activation mechanisms that trigger wired mechanisms when stepped on. A pressure plate's color determines which characters can trigger it.

Red, Brown, Gray, Orange, and Lihzahrd Pressure Plates are randomly generated on the map during world creation as the trigger for traps. They only take up a very small space on top of blocks, so they may be difficult to spot. The color of naturally spawned pressure plates is dependent on the color of the block they are generated on top of. Except for Lihzahrd Pressure Plates, they can also be purchased from the Mechanic.

Weighted Pressure Plates activate once on being depressed, and again on being released. All Weighted Pressure Plates of the same color share a single state. As long as one Weighted Pressure Plate of a given color is already pressed down within a circuit, stepping on another identical plate will not send a new signal. They can be crafted from regular pressure plates.

The Teal Pressure Pad is a special kind of pressure plate that responds to projectiles impacting it, which includes pets that touch it. Unlike regular pressure plates, the Teal Pressure Pad can be placed on all four sides of a block, e.g. on the ceiling or sidewall. It can be purchased from the Mechanic.
Pretty Mirror: The Pretty Mirror is a consumable weapon that can be thrown at targets. The damage it deals is not classified as any of the four damage types and therefore cannot be modified by any buffs or equipment. The Pretty Mirror can be purchased from the Stylist while in a Graveyard for 1 Gold. Upon breaking, the Pretty Mirror decreases luck by 0.25 for 7 minutes to all players within a 19.875×19.875-tile rectangular area centered on the point of impact.
Pretty Pink set: The Pretty Pink set is a vanity set consisting of the Pretty Pink Ribbon, Pretty Pink Dress, and Pretty Pink Stockings. The set is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 55 Gold (set).
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Prince set: The Prince set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Prince Uniform, Prince Cape, and the Prince Pants. It is purchased from the Princess for 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Princess: The Princess is a Hardmode, post-Plantera NPC vendor who sells royal-themed vanity items and furniture, and is typically the final town NPC that the player encounters. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.Verify

All other town NPCs (not including Santa Claus or town pets) are present, meaning that she can only move in after defeating Plantera (as the Cyborg, the second-to-last NPC unlocked by game progression, can only spawn after defeating her).
These requirements only apply to the initial spawning. If the Princess is killed, she will automatically respawn after some time.
The Princess will attack nearby enemies with the Resonance Scepter, for which she has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping upon death if the current world is in Hardmode.
Princess Fish: Princess Fish are a type of Hardmode fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in The Hallow in any layer. They are used to craft Love Potions and Seafood Dinners (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Princess set: The Princess set is a vanity set that can be obtained from Goodie Bags with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance. It consists of a Princess Hat and Princess Dress.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Princess set (Clothier): The Princess set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Tiara and the Princess Dress. It is purchased from the Clothier for 35 Gold (set), during a New Moon.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Prismatic Dye: Prismatic Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye dropped by the Empress of Light with a 1/4 (25%) chance. The dye creates a prism-esque effect, making the equipped item seem transparent and glow in a cycling rainbow.
Prismatic Lacewing: The Prismatic Lacewing is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera flying critter and boss-summoning item that spawns on the surface Hallow after Plantera has been defeated. Prismatic Lacewings disappear almost instantaneously when spawned in any other biome, and only spawn in the Hallow between dusk (7:30 PM) and midnight (12:00 AM). When killed by a player, it summons the Empress of Light; death from non-player sources will generally not result in summoning. Only one Prismatic Lacewing can be naturally spawned at a time.
The Prismatic Lacewing can be caught with Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, and Golden Bug Net. Releasing it from the inventory (with ⚒ Use / Attack) and killing it will still summon the Empress of Light.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Prismatic Lacewing Jar: The Prismatic Lacewing Jar is a placeable furniture item which displays the Prismatic Lacewing, normally a critter which summons the Empress of Light boss if killed. This item is a safe method of displaying captured Prismatic Lacewings. Similarly to the critter it emits light when placed. By throwing a Prismatic Lacewing Jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the Prismatic Lacewing as an item.
The item cannot be used to summon the Empress of Light, and is purely decorative. A Prismatic Lacewing must be killed to summon the boss.
Prismatic Punch: The Prismatic Punch is a Hardmode food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Prismite: Prismites are a type of Hardmode fish which are found rarely by fishing in The Hallow in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Lifeforce Potions.
Probe: The Probe is a Hardmode boss servant that is summoned by The Destroyer. When one of its red-lit segments is damaged, there is a 1/25 (4%) chance that a Probe is spawned from it. Probes can move through blocks and attack by firing Pink Lasers.
Probes make fighting The Destroyer an easier and harder task at the same time – the Hearts they drop will keep the player alive, but they are a major source of damage during the boss fight.
Prospector armor: Prospector armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Prospector Helmet, Prospector Shirt, and Prospector Pants.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
The player emits a small amount of light.
All Prospector armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Mining armor and the Ultrabright Helmet, still providing the set bonus. The only difference is the defense.
Proximity Mine Launcher: The Proximity Mine Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that can be purchased from the Cyborg for 35 Gold. When used, it consumes a rocket and fires a mine that travels in a short arc before becoming stationary and semi-transparent until an enemy approaches or until a minute passes, at which point it explodes. The player will not activate the mine, but will be damaged by an exploding mine. Stationary mines deal 300% of the weapon's damage (240 base damage) to enemies, but not to players, who only take a flat 60 damage instead.
Its best modifier is Unreal for combat purposes and Rapid for mining and usage of liquid rockets.
Psycho: The Psycho is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. He will initially spawn in a nearly invisible, stealthed state, waiting for the player to damage him or get closer than 10.625 tiles before he fully reveals himself, and starts attacking with a knife that deals heavy damage on contact.
Psycho Knife: The Psycho Knife is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance of being dropped by Psychos during the Solar Eclipse event. When holding the Psycho Knife and standing still, the player will quickly enter stealth, causing them to turn almost invisible, move much more slowly, and no longer be targeted by certain enemies' projectile attacks.
Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 0.83 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:
+300% melee damage (increases the weapon's damage to 340 without additional melee bonuses)
+30% melee critical strike chance (34% base chance)
−50% movement speed; then sets sprint speed equal to move speed

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details). Stealth mode additionally prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using items.

Stealth mode is deactivated upon hitting an target, switching to a different item, riding a mount, or taking damage. Swinging the weapon alone does not cancel stealth, nor does moving. However, moving or swinging the weapon before stealth mode is fully engaged will quickly deactivate stealth.
Its best modifier is Legendary. Due to rounding, the Light modifier gives the same speed bonus as Legendary, with fewer other bonuses.
Puffer Shrimp: The Puffer Shrimp is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pufferfish that follows the player in a bubble.
Pufferfish: The Pufferfish is a rare Critter that spawns in the Ocean. Upon getting hit or leaving water, it will puff up. The Pufferfish will float to the surface of water when puffed up.
Pulse Bow: The Pulse Bow is a Hardmode bow that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 45 Gold after defeating all three mechanical bosses. When used, it converts any type of arrow into a high-velocity Pulse Bolt. The Pulse Bolt is unaffected by gravity, can either pierce enemies or bounce off blocks up to five times, and travels for 3.33 seconds before dissipating. The Pulse Bow also has a base 11% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Pumpkin: Pumpkin is a crafting material obtained by harvesting Pumpkin plants using any weapon or tool.
Pumpkin Moon Medallion: The Pumpkin Moon Medallion is a Hardmode, post-Plantera event-summoning item used to summon the Pumpkin Moon event. It can only be used at night. Attempting to use it during the day will not begin the event, and the item will not be consumed from the player's inventory.
Pumpkin Pie: Pumpkin Pie is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Pumpkin Scented Candle: The Pumpkin Scented Candle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera light pet-summoning item that spawns a miniature Pumpking named Jack 'O Lantern to follow the player around. The Pumpkin Scented Candle is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event in Master Mode with a 12.5–25% chance depending on the current wave. While equipped, not only does the pet produce light, but the player as well.
Pumpkin Seed: The Pumpkin Seed is a seed which is used to plant Pumpkins. They may be planted on normal green grass or Hallowed grass (including their mowed versions), and will eventually grow into Pumpkins. They need 2 blocks width and 2 blocks height of clear space to grow, and can grow anywhere grass will grow.
Pumpkin Seeds are purchased from the Dryad for 2 Silver 50 Copper each.
Pumpkin Wall: Pumpkin Wall is a background wall made from Pumpkins.
Pumpkin armor: Pumpkin armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pumpkin Helmet, Pumpkin Breastplate, and Pumpkin Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Pumpkins. The full set grants 7 defense and increases all damage dealt by the player by 10% while equipped.
Pumpkin set: The Pumpkin set is a vanity set which consists of the Pumpkin Mask, Pumpkin Shirt, and Pumpkin Pants. Its male and female variants look identical. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to drop from Goodie Bags during Halloween. Unlike Pumpkin armor, the Pumpkin set cannot be crafted.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Pumpking: The Pumpking is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Pumpkin Moon event. He is the event's final enemy and can move freely through blocks. He is the equivalent to the Ice Queen from the Frost Moon, being the Pumpkin Moon's most powerful enemy, coming in at the last waves of the event, and being the event's only flying boss.
Defeating the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event will add 150 / 300 / 375 points to the final score, giving the most number of points for any enemy in the event.

Like the Mourning Wood, the later the Pumpkin Moon wave in which the Pumpking is killed in, the more likely he is to drop items. A Pumpking defeated during wave 15 has a guaranteed chance to drop at least one item from his standard drop table.
Pumps: Inlet and Outlet Pumps are mechanisms used to transport liquids (water, lava, honey, and Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)), without having to construct pathways through blocks or rely on gravity. Instead, an Inlet and Outlet Pump need only be connected to each other with Wires and activated, which transfers fluid from the Inlet Pump to the Outlet Pump. Each activation transfers up to four tiles of liquid. For continuous automated pumping, a timer can be used.

Despite its appearance as a pipe that takes in liquid from beside it, an Inlet Pump must be submerged in liquid, as it removes liquid that lies directly over its graphic, and does so equally from all of its 2×2 tile space. Similarly, an Outlet Pump spawns liquid directly over its graphic, and does so equally over all of its 2×2 tile space.
Pupfish: The Pupfish is a critter that spawns infrequently in bodies of water in the Desert biome that are directly above Sand Blocks. Unlike many critters, Pupfish are capable of spawning on-screen. The Pupfish has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Pupfish can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Pupfish Bowl). Once crafted, the Pupfish cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Purple Clubberfish: The Purple Clubberfish is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that can be obtained by fishing in The Corruption with a 1/10 (10%) chance with 100 Fishing Power, up to a maximum 1/4 (25%) chance with 300 Fishing Power. It has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Confused debuff for 1–3 seconds on hit.
Purple Mucus: The Purple Mucus is a dye material that is dropped by Sea Snails, which only spawn in the Ocean biome. Its sole purpose is to make Purple Dye.
Purple Ooze Dye: Purple Ooze Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it gives the player a purple tone, with parts of the dye distorting and varying in different shades of purple.
Purple Slime: The Purple Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that commonly spawns in Forest biomes during the daytime. It is a larger and stronger variant of the Blue Slime. Purple Slimes will not usually target the player but will become aggressive when damaged, during the night, or if brought underground.
Like most other slimes, the Purple Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
On Desktop, Console, Mobile, and 3DS, they can rarely be found carrying bonus drops, which the player receives upon the slime's death.
Putrid Scent: The Putrid Scent is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/5 (20%) chance to be dropped by Corrupt Mimics. While equipped, it increases the player's damage and critical strike chance by 5% and decreases aggro by 400.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Flesh Knuckles; both can be exchanged via Shimmer.
Pwnhammer: The Pwnhammer is a Hardmode hammer that is always dropped by the Wall of Flesh. It is able to destroy Demon Altars and Crimson Altars, causing one type of Hardmode ore to appear in the world.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Pygmy Necklace: The Pygmy Necklace is a pre-Hardmode accessory that provides the player with one additional minion slot. It is purchased from the Witch Doctor for 20 Gold at night.
Pygmy Staff: The Pygmy Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Pygmy minion. It fires a spear towards nearby enemies that inflicts the Acid Venom debuff for 5–10 seconds, but does not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. The Pygmy Staff has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped by Plantera.
Pylons: Pylons are placeable furniture items that appear as a large crystal hovering and rotating above a biome-themed stand. With two or more pylons placed in the world, the player can teleport from one pylon to another one. The system they form is referred to as the Pylon Network.
When the player is near a pylon, they can teleport to another pylon by doing any of the following:
Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the pylon, which opens the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map.
Pressing Toggle Full Map to open the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map.
Selecting another pylon on the overlay-mode or portrait-mode minimap.
The following conditions must be met by both the pylon near the player and the target pylon (with the exception of the Universal Pylon):
There must be two or more housed NPCs (including the Old Man and town pets) within a rectangular area of 169×124 tiles centered on each of the two pylons.
More precisely, the home tile of the NPC (Dungeon point in the case of the Old Man) must be within this rectangle, and the NPC must be less than 100 tiles away from their home tile.
The pylons must be placed in their respective biome.
Moreover, the following restrictions apply to all pylons (including the Universal Pylon):
Only one of each type of pylon may be placed in a world.
Pylons can only function when the minimap is enabled in the settings.
The player must be within a rectangular area of 61×62 tiles centered on the pylon.
Pyroclastic Stone: The Pyroclastic Stone is a pre-Hardmode accessory that combines and improves the effects of the Magma Stone and Snapping Stone. It grants the following effects when equipped:
Melee attacks inflict the Hellfire debuff for 2–6 seconds on hit.
Melee and ranged hits are periodically boosted to discharge explosive slashes on hit.
This effect has a cooldown of 6 seconds, indicated by faint orange light.
Boosted hits deal up to 90 additional base damage.
Explosive slashes hit up to 2 additional targets nearby, dealing 45 base damage and a knockback of 5 (Average), and inflicting the Hellfire debuff for 3 seconds to each target.
Quad-Barrel Shotgun: The Quad-Barrel Shotgun is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron gun that can be purchased for 35 Gold from the Arms Dealer when he is spoken to in a Graveyard. When used, it fires eight bullets at a 45° spread, consuming one piece of ammunition.
Queen Bee: The Queen Bee is a pre-Hardmode boss. Fighting her is not required for game progression, but defeating her rewards the player with useful items and weapons and allows the Witch Doctor to move into an available vacant house.
While the Queen Bee is alive, her exclusive music Queen Bee will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Queen Slime: Queen Slime is an early-Hardmode, Hallow-themed boss. Fighting Queen Slime is not required for game progression – much like her pre-Hardmode counterpart, King Slime – but her defeat may reward the player with useful items.
While Queen Slime is alive, her exclusive music Queen Slime will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Queen Spider Staff: The Queen Spider Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons the Spider Turret sentry. It fires Spider Eggs towards enemies once per second, which can bounce and roll on blocks, and are heavily affected by gravity. The Spider Eggs deal no damage themselves, and upon colliding with enemies or after 1 second, they will break and spawn 2–4 Baby Spiders that attack enemies. The Baby Spiders will disappear upon contact with an enemy, dealing damage and inflicting the Acid Venom debuff for 2–4 seconds. If there are no enemies within range, the Baby Spiders will persist for 5 seconds before dissipating.
R.E.K. 3000: The R.E.K. 3000 is a post-Skeletron informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of nearby rare creatures, the number of nearby enemies, and the player's enemy kill count.
Rabbit Perch: The Rabbit Perch is a vanity item purchased from the Zoologist for 15 Gold after filling out 40% (219 entries) of the Bestiary.
Although the item appears to be a hat with rabbit ears, equipping it will show an animated rabbit on the player's head.
Racks: Racks are decorative items that are placed on walls. They have no functional effect. Unlike the Weapon Rack, these racks cannot be used to display other items.
Radar: The Radar is an informational accessory that displays the number of nearby enemies in a 125-tile radius around the player.

The Radar has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found inside surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. The Radar can also be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waxing Gibbous for 2 Gold 50 Silver.
Rage Potion: The Rage Potion is a buff potion which grants the Rage buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's critical strike chance by 10%. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Ragged Caster: The Ragged Caster is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It attacks by firing volleys of three homing Lost Soul projectiles at the player which travel through blocks, decelerate as they approach the player, and inflict the Blackout debuff for 2–6 / 4–12 / 5–15 seconds on hit. Ragged Casters teleport to a different location on-screen after firing nine projectiles.
Ragged Casters spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by slab walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Rain Cloud: Rain Cloud is a type of block found beneath Floating Islands, along with Cloud blocks. Rain Cloud blocks cause purely decorative raindrops to appear beneath them that fall for about 18 tiles before fading away for 5 more. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, landing on Rain Clouds will not inflict fall damage.
Rain Song: The Rain Song is a novelty instrument that has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Flying Fish, which spawn during rain. When used, the player strums a chord depending on how far the cursor is from the player.
Rain armor: Rain armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Rain Hat and Rain Coat. Each piece has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to be dropped by Raincoat Zombies. The full set grants 3 defense while equipped.
Rainbow Boulder: The Rainbow Boulder is a rare object that can be encountered in Boulder traps, where it occasionally replaces the regular Boulder. It can be found more commonly in Celebration Mk 10 worlds. It looks like a light gray bumpy stone with a rainbow glow behind it, and is accompanied with colored sparkles in front of it, although they do not illuminate light.

Like normal Boulders, the Rainbow Boulder starts to move when it is unsupported (e.g. when the pressure plate wired to the trap is activated) or when it is struck with a pickaxe or drill. It does not drop and roll sideways, however. Instead, it starts flying across the screen, emitting light as it does this, traversing through blocks, and attacking nearby enemies, dealing high damage. It also targets treasures, similar to fairies, and leaves sparkles at its location. It moves around for approximately one minute. During this time, a unique music track also plays.
The Rainbow Boulder can be crafted and placed by the player. Player-placed Rainbow Boulders have the same behavior as naturally generated ones when activated.
Rainbow Brick: Rainbow Brick is a Hardmode brick that can be obtained as a drop from the Rainbow Slime. It glows in the dark when placed, and cycles through the colors of the rainbow. The cycling colors of Rainbow Bricks, Rainbow Brick Walls, Helium Moss, Helium Moss Brick, Helium Moss Brick Walls, Rainbow Torches, the Disco Ball, and Rainbow Hair Dye are synchronized with each other.

If a waterfall passes through a Rainbow Brick, it will also cycle through the colors. Rainbow Bricks will not change the color of lavafalls, honeyfalls, or Shimmerfalls (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Rainbow Brick Wall: Rainbow Brick Walls are Hardmode background walls crafted from Rainbow Bricks. Like Rainbow Bricks, they glow when placed and continuously change color.
Rainbow Cloud: The Rainbow Cloud is a rainbow variant of the Cloud, crafted from Rainbow Bricks and Cloud blocks. They glow in the dark and give off a small amount of light while cycling through multiple colors when placed.
Rainbow Crystal Staff: The Rainbow Crystal Staff is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord summon weapon that summons a Rainbow Crystal sentry. It fires spreads of three multicolored light beams towards enemies, but cannot target through blocks. Each beam releases a star that explodes shortly after. Unlike most sentries, the Rainbow Crystal floats midair. The Rainbow Crystal Staff has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord.
Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 98.5% (including whip bonuses) or 24% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.
Rainbow Cursor: The Rainbow Cursor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera vanity accessory that causes the player's cursor to cycle through the colors of the rainbow continuously. It has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped from the Empress of Light.
The Rainbow Cursor cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Rainbow Glowstick: The Rainbow Glowstick is a consumable light source. It behaves similarly to the regular Bouncy Glowstick when thrown, but cycles its light through the rainbow, as well as leaving behind a trail. It can be purchased from the Merchant during a Party for 20 Copper each and can also be obtained from Chests in Celebration Mk 10 or Rainbow road worlds. In those worlds, Rainbow Glowsticks replace Glowsticks in Chests, in the same quantity.
Rainbow Gun: The Rainbow Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic gun that fires a curving rainbow which persists for 40 seconds or until another rainbow is fired, and repeatedly deals damage to enemies that touch it. The rainbow can be also forced to dissipate instantly by using ⚷ Open / Activate on it while the player is within 15 tiles of it. The Rainbow Gun is always found in the Dungeon's Hallowed Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Hallowed Key after Plantera has been defeated.

Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Rainbow Gun's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.
Rainbow Piece: The Rainbow Piece was a crafting material used solely to craft the Pot o' Gold. Rainbow Pieces used to fall from the sky, much like Fallen Stars, except that they fell during the day, disappeared at night, and only fell during the St. Patrick's Day season. They were slightly transparent.
Rainbow Rod: The Rainbow Rod is a Hardmode, post-The Twins wand. When used, it fires a rainbow missile that follows the cursor when ⚒ Use / Attack key is held. If the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released mid-drag, the missile will be fired in that direction. If the cursor is stationary on release, it is fired directly away from the player. Once it is released, the missile homes in on nearby enemies and can pierce twice, creating a small explosion upon contact with a block or third enemy. The missile does not dissipate when touching a block while being controlled, and is not affected by liquids (unlike the Flamelash).
Rainbow Slime: The Rainbow Slime is a rare Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns on Hallowed blocks ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) in The Hallow on non-Hallowed blocks) while it is raining. It constantly changes color, as do the Rainbow Bricks it drops.
Like most other slimes, the Rainbow Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Raincoat Zombie: The Raincoat Zombie is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a Zombie variant that spawns during rain on the surface at night. It acts the same as normal zombies, slowly walking towards the player to deal contact damage, while attempting to navigate around obstacles and only being able to open doors during a Blood Moon. It is differentiated from other zombies in that it is dressed in traditional yellow raincoat attire, which it can also drop in the form of the Rain Hat and Rain Coat armor pieces.
Raincoat Zombies can appear in three different size variations with slightly different stats. Unlike normal zombies, it does not have an Armed variation in Expert Mode.
Rally: The Rally is a pre-Hardmode yoyo that has a 6.5% chance of being dropped by Crawdads, Giant Shellies, and Salamanders in the Cavern layer.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Ram Rune: The Ram Rune is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron accessory that can be obtained as secondary loot from Locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon, and from Golden Lock Boxes found in Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates. When equipped, it allows the player to do a "ground pound" by holding ▼ Down and pressing ↷ Jump while in midair.

Pounding the ground creates a shockwave that deals 30 damage and knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) to all enemies within 8 tiles of the player. If the player does the ground pound from a height of 10 tiles or more, the shockwave becomes empowered and instead deals a critical strike that inflicts 60 damage and knockback of 24 (Insane) to all enemies within 11 tiles of the player. Additionally, if the player makes direct contact with an enemy during the ground pound, the enemy will take an extra 40 damage as well as knockback of 5 (Average), and the player is granted 0.1 seconds of invincibility frames. This direct hit cannot critically strike.
Rambutan: The Rambutan is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Shadewood or a Shadewood Palm tree.
Ranger Emblem: The Ranger Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that increases ranged damage by 15%. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop from the Wall of Flesh.
Rat: The Rat is a harmless critter that spawns in the Graveyard biome. The Rat has only 5 health and no defense, and can only be damaged by players.

The Rat can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Rat Cage). Once crafted, the Rat cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Raven: The Raven is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy that appears in Graveyards (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and can be found in the Forest at night during the Halloween seasonal event. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest tree during this time at night.
Similarly to Vultures, Ravens will first be encountered roosting and will take flight when approached or attacked. It will hover over the player, waiting a few moments before swooping down to attack.
Raven Feather: The Raven Feather is an item that has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Ravens. It decreases the player's luck by 0.1 while it is in their inventory or opened Void Bag. Multiple Raven Feathers do not stack with each other, but the Raven Feather does stack with other items that increase or decrease luck.
Raven Staff: The Raven Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Raven minion. It flies and charges through enemies. The Raven Staff is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave.
Ray Gunner: The Ray Gunner is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that spawns during the Martian Madness event. It fires red laser projectiles, at a maximum fire rate of once every 0.67 seconds (40 ticks).
Raynbro's set: Raynbro's set is a vanity set consisting of Raynbro's Hood, Raynbro's Hoodie, and Raynbro's Pants. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 Gold (set).
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Razorblade Typhoon: The Razorblade Typhoon is a Hardmode spell book that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it fires a high-velocity homing typhoon. The typhoon can pierce enemies and bounce off blocks infinitely, and it lasts for 1.67 seconds.
Razorpine: The Razorpine is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that is dropped by the Everscream during the Frost Moon event with a 3.46%–10.37% (6.22%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave. When used, it rapidly fires 2–4 high-velocity pine needles in a spread, which do not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. The needles become affected by gravity after traveling a medium distance.
Razortip: The Razortip is an unobtainable accessory. When equipped, it grants +8% ranged critical strike chance and +1 damage to all arrows.
Reaper: The Reaper is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it will only spawn after all mechanical bosses have been defeated.

Reapers behave in a similar manner to Wraiths, and have the same AI, but they have higher stats. They also move significantly faster than Wraiths, and with the higher spawn rate of the Solar Eclipse, they often attack from multiple directions at once.

They are fairly vulnerable to knockback. Like many creatures that pass through blocks, they do not take damage from lava. Furthermore, weapons whose animations do not stop upon hitting blocks, like most melee weapons, will damage them despite not normally being able to attack through blocks.
Reaper set: The Reaper set is a vanity set which consists of the Reaper Hood and Reaper Robe. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to be obtained from Goodie Bags during Halloween. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Its male and female variants look identical.
Reaver Shark: The Reaver Shark is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe obtained by fishing in the Ocean. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Recall Potion: The Recall Potion is a potion that will teleport the player to their spawn point 0.167 seconds (10 ticks) after being used. It is identical in function to a Magic Mirror or Ice Mirror, but significantly faster in use time.
In addition to being crafted, Recall Potions can be found in Pots and Chests, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Recon Scope: The Recon Scope is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory. It grants the following effects while equipped:
The ability to "zoom", increasing view range while holding a bullet-firing gun by pressing and holding ⚷ Open / Activate and moving the cursor.
Red Acid Dye: Red Acid Dye is a dye acquired as a random reward from the Dye Trader for giving him a Strange Plant. When equipped in a dye slot, it applies a dark red rippling effect that pulses outward, similar to Acid Dye and Blue Acid Dye. Items dyed by it can be seen in the dark but do not emit light.
Red Brick: Red Bricks are bricks crafted from Clay Block.
Red Brick Wall: Red Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Red Bricks. It stops enemies from spawning where it is placed and, if covering an entire room, can be used to make NPC houses. These can be painted with any available paint color, except Red which will yield no change in the sprite.
Red Devil: The Red Devil is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in The Underworld after any mechanical boss has been defeated. While flying toward the player in a similar manner to that of the Demon, it fires five purple trident projectiles that deal extremely large amounts of damage upon contact. It is considered a more difficult version of the Demon, having more health and dealing much more damage. Similar to the Demon, it drops a magic weapon resembling its means of attack, the Unholy Trident.

While the contact damage of a Red Devil is comparably low, its trident attack is capable of dealing large amounts of damage even to players wearing endgame armor. The tridents are fired in the same burst-like pattern that Demons fire scythes in, although they are slower and move at a constant velocity.
Red Envelope: The Red Envelope is a removed unimplemented item that was intended to drop from all enemies during the Chinese New Year event.
It was a grab bag item, meaning that it would have given the player various items upon opening it.
Red Husk: The Red Husk is a dye material that is dropped by Cochineal Beetles. Its sole purpose is to make Red Dye.
Red Potion: The Red Potion is a potion which can be found in chests within worlds generated with the Drunk seed enabled (1/30 (3.33%) chance), or the For the Worthy seed enabled (1/10 (10%) chance), or both Drunk and For the Worthy enabled (13/100 (13%) chance). It can also be dropped by Jungle Mimics, which spawn in Underground Jungle during Hardmode when Celebration Mk 10 is enabled.
It inflicts a very large number of debuffs for 1 hour / 2 hours / 2.5 hours on players who consume it. If For the worthy is enabled, it instead grants up to three random buffs for 30 minutes.
Red Riding armor: Red Riding armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem ranged/summoner armor set consisting of the Red Riding Hood, Red Riding Dress, and Red Riding Leggings. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 150 Defender Medals.
The Red Riding armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Huntress armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Explosive Trap sentry summons have greatly increased fire rate and inflict the Oiled debuff, which causes enemies to take extra damage while afflicted with a fire debuff.
Red Ryder: The Red Ryder is a pre-Hardmode gun dropped from Presents obtained during Christmas, with a 0.643% chance in pre-Hardmode and 0.6% chance in Hardmode.
Red Slime: The Red Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Underground layer, alongside Yellow Slimes. They are slightly stronger than Blue and Green Slimes.
Like most other slimes, the Red Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
On Desktop, Console, Mobile, and 3DS, they can rarely be found carrying bonus drops, which the player receives upon the slime's death.
Red Snapper: Red Snappers are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in the Ocean in the Sky or Surface layers.
Red Squirrel: The Squirrel and Red Squirrel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are critters that spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Squirrel / Red Squirrel Cage). Once crafted, the Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Squirrels can be spawned by the Squirrel Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Squirrel to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Red Swimsuit: The Red Swimsuit is a craftable vanity item.
Red's Throw: Red's Throw is a Hardmode, Expert Mode-exclusive yoyo that can be obtained from any Hardmode boss's Treasure Bag (except Queen Slime's) as part of Red's set.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Red's set: Red's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Redigit, lead developer of Terraria.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Redigit's equipment also includes these non-vanity items, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Reef Block: Reef Blocks are a type of decorative block. They can be used to craft Reef furniture.
Reef Wall: Reef Walls are a type of background wall. They are crafted with Reef Blocks at a Work Bench.
Reflective Copper Dye: Reflective Copper Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a copper-plated, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over.

As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.
Reflective Dye: Reflective Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over.

As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.
Reflective Gold Dye: Reflective Gold Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a gold-plated, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over.

As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.
Reflective Metal Dye: Reflective Metal Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a black, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over.

As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.
Reflective Obsidian Dye: Reflective Obsidian Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the respective equipment an obsidian-plated, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside.
