From some perspectives, the player may look three-dimensional when this dye is equipped in all slots.

As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.
Unlike the other reflective dyes, this dye is rather dark which results in dark highlights.
Reflective Shades: The Reflective Shades are a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Darkness and Stoned debuffs.
Reflective Silver Dye: Reflective Silver Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a silver-plated, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over.

As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.
Regal Delicacy: The Regal Delicacy is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Slime Princess that follows the player. The pet resembles a miniature Queen Slime with blush, small dotted eyes, and a tiny mouth. The Regal Delicacy has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime in Master Mode.
Regeneration Potion: The Regeneration Potion is a buff potion which grants the Regeneration buff when consumed. The buff provides health regeneration by restoring an additional 2 health per second, for a total of 960 health. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Regeneration Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.
Reindeer Antlers: The Reindeer Antlers are a vanity item that is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 2.308% in pre-Hardmode and 2.154% in Hardmode. When worn in the helmet slot, they place antlers on the player's head.
Reindeer Bells: The Reindeer Bells are a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons the rideable Rudolph mount, which greatly speeds a player's movement and adds the ability to fly. The Reindeer Bells are dropped by the Ice Queen during or after wave 15 of the Frost Moon event with a 1.33%–2.22% / 6.67% chance depending on the current wave.
Similar to the Hoverboard, flight height can be constrained by holding the ▼ Down key in addition to the ↷ Jump key, so movement will be horizontal only.
Release Doves: The Release Doves are a consumable item sold by the Party Girl for 1 Silver when in a Graveyard. Using the item releases three Doves, which fly around and disappear after 5 seconds.
Release Lantern: The Release Lantern is a consumable light source sold by the Party Girl for 1 Silver each during a Lantern Night. When used, it releases a lantern that will float up into the air before disappearing after 16 seconds. It closely resembles the lanterns seen in the background of Lantern Nights and also travels in the direction of the wind.
Relics: Relics are furniture items dropped by bosses and mini-bosses in Master Mode. They are golden depictions of their respective boss that hover above a pedestal, have a golden particle effect, and emit light when placed close to a light source.
There are 28 different relics available in Terraria.
Repaired Life Crystal: The Repaired Life Crystal is a furniture item that places down a decorative Life Crystal. It drops a Life Crystal when destroyed.
Repaired Mana Crystal: The Repaired Mana Crystal is a furniture item that places down a decorative Mana Crystal. It drops a Mana Crystal when destroyed.
Replica Altars: Replica Altars are decorative altar variants. They cannot function as crafting stations, nor do they have any effect (except dropping as items) when destroyed. They can only be broken with a hammer or explosives.
Replica Crimson Heart: The Replica Crimson Heart is a decorative piece of furniture that looks like a Crimson Heart when placed. It can be placed without any blocks or walls supporting it, and it can only be broken with a hammer or explosives.
Replica Shadow Orb: The Replica Shadow Orb is a decorative piece of furniture that looks like a Shadow Orb when placed. It can be placed without any blocks or walls supporting it, and it can only be broken with a hammer or explosives.
Resonance Scepter: The Resonance Scepter is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by the Princess. When used, it creates pink circular auras at the cursor's location, which expand and then collapse into sparkles over the course of 1 second. The auras deal rapid damage and knockback.

Although the projectile appears to instantly travel to its target, there must be a clear line of sight between the player and the cursor's location; the projectile will be summoned at the location of impact with the first block.
Resplendent Dessert: The Resplendent Dessert is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that is a combination of the Royal Delight from King Slime and the Regal Delicacy from Queen Slime, allowing the player to summon both the Slime Prince and Slime Princess at the same time.
Restoration Potion: The Restoration Potion is a recovery potion that can be found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld. When used, it restores 90 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for only 45 seconds (rather than the usual 60 of health-restoring potions). The duration of Potion Sickness can be reduced to 33.75 seconds via the Philosopher's Stone, Charm of Myths or Catalyst Band.
Despite its appearance, the Restoration Potion is not created by upgrading a Lesser Restoration Potion.
Restoration Shield: The Restoration Shield is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron shield accessory item made by combining a Cobalt Shield and a Mana Regeneration Band at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Retinazer: The Twins are a Hardmode mechanical boss which are essentially a more difficult version of the Eye of Cthulhu. The Twins are two separate flying entities, Retinazer and Spazmatism, connected by a tendril, each with its own attack pattern and health. Both must be killed in order to defeat the boss.
While The Twins are alive, their exclusive music The Twins will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Revolver: The Revolver is a pre-Hardmode gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 15 Gold after a Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart has been smashed. Firing the Revolver just as it comes off cooldown will gradually increase its attack speed (up to 100%) and critical strike chance (up to 20%). This effect will not be triggered if the player is autofiring the weapon.
Rich Mahogany: Rich Mahogany is a type of wood harvested from Mahogany trees found naturally growing in the Jungle and Underground Jungle, or from Living Mahogany Trees, Underground Cabins in the Underground Jungle, and Jungle Shrines. Mahogany trees can naturally grow from Jungle grass above surface, or they can also be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Jungle grass above surface.
Rich Mahogany Bow: The Rich Mahogany Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Rich Mahogany Chest: The Rich Mahogany Chest is a chest found only in Underground Cabins within the Jungle and Underground Jungle biomes. Like Granite Chests and Marble Chests, Rich Mahogany Chests have exactly the same loot as Gold Chests.
Rich Mahogany Hammer: The Rich Mahogany Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Rich Mahogany Sword: The Rich Mahogany Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword.
Rich Mahogany Wall: The Rich Mahogany Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Underground Cabins in the Underground Jungle, as well as in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.
Rich Mahogany armor: Rich Mahogany armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Rich Mahogany Helmet, Rich Mahogany Breastplate, and Rich Mahogany Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Rich Mahogany. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.
Rifle Scope: The Rifle Scope is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory. It grants the ability to increase view range while holding a gun by pressing and holding ⚷ Open / Activate and moving the cursor.
The Rifle Scope has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance of being dropped by Skeleton Snipers in the post-Plantera Dungeon.
Roasted Bird: The Roasted Bird is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Roasted Duck: The Roasted Duck is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Robes: Robes are equipable items, most of which provide magic damage bonuses and are a part of the Wizard set. All gem robes are adapted from the Robe, a vanity item equipped in the shirt slot. They resemble the robes worn by Dark Casters and Tim.
Gem staves and Gem robes have a unique mechanic called Gem enchantment, which modifies the projectile fired from gem staves by the ability of the corresponding gem type.
Robot Hat: The Robot Hat is a vanity item equipped in the Social Helmet Slot. It has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance to drop from Piranhas and Angler Fish.
Robot set: The Robot set is a vanity set consisting of the Robot Mask, Robot Shirt, and Robot Pants. Its male and female variants are identical. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to be obtained by opening a Goodie Bag from the Halloween event. When the Robot Shirt is equipped, the player will appear to have their arms facing forward when walking.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Robotic Skull: The Robotic Skull is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns Mini Prime, a miniature version of Skeletron Prime that follows the player. The Robotic Skull has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Skeletron Prime in Master Mode.
Rock Candy: Rock Candy is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Rock Golem: The Rock Golem is a powerful Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Cavern layer. It throws rocks at players that are within its line of sight but out of its contact range. When being attacked, it continues to attack, making stun-lock options unusable.
In For the Worthy and Zenith worlds, Rock Golems release a Boulder projectile on death.
Rock Golem Head: The Rock Golem Head is a dual-purpose vanity and furniture item dropped by Rock Golems at a 1/3 (33.33%) chance. It can be worn or placed.

Flower Seeds can be planted in a placed Rock Golem Head. If left empty, wild grass plants will randomly grow out of it, provided the item is placed on the surface or in Space. The plant in a Rock Golem Head cannot be cut in the regular manner, e.g. via nearby swinging tools. Instead, it needs to be removed with a pickaxe or drill, or the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth.
Rock Lobster: Rock Lobsters are a type of fishing catch which are found plentifully by fishing in the Desert biome.
Rocket Boots: Rocket Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 5 Gold. While equipped, they allow the player to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit visual flame particles that give off a large amount of light.

The flight time of the Rocket Boots is divided into 7 "charges" that each last 0.17 seconds, and releasing ↷ Jump during flight immediately consumes all remaining flight time in a charge. All charges are reset immediately when the player lands on any solid object, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or latches onto a tile with a hook.
Rocket Launcher: The Rocket Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that has a 1/18 (5.56%) / 35/324 (10.8%) chance of being dropped by Skeleton Commandos in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires rockets as ammunition, which can damage the player for a flat 60 damage. Enemies that are directly hit by rockets take double damage (110 base damage).
Its best modifier is Unreal for combat purposes and Rapid for mining and usage of liquid rockets.
Rockets: Rockets are a Hardmode, post-Plantera type of ammunition which are mainly sold by the Cyborg. The Rocket I variant is also dropped by Plantera when it drops the Grenade Launcher. Most launchers use Rockets as ammunition.

All rocket types have two significant defining traits: area of effect, and the ability to destroy tiles. Rockets I and II have a small area of effect, closest to that of a Bomb or Grenade, while Rockets III and IV have an area similar to the blast radius of Dynamite. Rockets I and III will leave tiles unaffected, while II and IV will break blocks and furniture in their blast radius (except for explosion-proof objects).

In most cases, a rocket's splash damage will harm the player who fired it if they are caught in the blast radius, dealing a flat 60 damage. These explosions will not affect other players unless they have PvP enabled, however.
Rockfish: The Rockfish is a pre-Hardmode hammer. It can be fished from the Underground layer within any biome. Its hammer power and tool speed are equal to that of the Molten Hamaxe.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Rod of Discord: The Rod of Discord is a Hardmode tool that has a 1/500 (0.2%) / 1/400 (0.25%) chance of being dropped by Chaos Elementals. When used, it instantly teleports the player to the location of the cursor and inflicts the Chaos State debuff on the player for 6 seconds. Using the Rod of Discord while this debuff is active causes the player to lose health equal to 1/7 (14.29%) of their maximum health.
It can be upgraded into the Rod of Harmony by throwing it into Shimmer after the Moon Lord has been defeated.
Rod of Harmony: The Rod of Harmony is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord tool. It is the direct upgrade to the Rod of Discord, instantly teleporting the player to the location of the cursor when used, but without inflicting the Chaos State debuff.
It is obtained by throwing the Rod of Discord into Shimmer after the Moon Lord has been defeated.
Roller Skates: Roller Skates are pre-Hardmode mount-summoning items that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant or Skeleton Merchant. There are four different color variants with identical functionalities. Unlike other mounts that override the player's movement stats with their own stats, Roller Skates only increase the player's movement stats by a flat amount, meaning the player will still benefit from various movement speed boosts when mounting Roller Skates. These stat increases are detailed below:
Increased maximum movement speed by 5 mph.
These bonuses are applied after most movement speed calculations, therefore they are not affected by most movement speed multipliers.
The only exception to this is the additional movement speed multiplier gained from running on Asphalt Blocks, see Notes for details.

These bonuses are applied after all positive jump height calculations, but before all of the negative, therefore they are not affected by positive multipliers (e.g. Frog Leg), but are affected by negative multipliers (e.g. Oozed).
Additionally, they also grant the following effects:
Velocity is not lost when moving.
Allows the player to move on Minecart Tracks.

Their minimum speed (or coasting speed) matches the player's current block placement speed. By default, this is 8 mph. Because tile placement speed is capped to 300%, the theoretical maximum coasting speed is 27 mph.
Rolling Cactus: The Rolling Cactus is a placeable object that behaves similarly to the Boulder. Rolling Cacti are naturally generated all throughout the Underground Desert but do not respawn once they have been activated. It is stationary when placed, and begins to move when hit by projectiles, pickaxes, or drills, or when the blocks under it are mined or hammered. Its roll direction is determined by whether its horizontal position in the world is an odd or even number, regardless of the slope of the surface it is on (unless it is blocked on one side by blocks, in which case it rolls in the other direction).
When both blocks under a Rolling Cactus are removed or hammered into a half-block, it will drop vertically until it hits a surface, then bounce and roll.

A Rolling Cactus projectile pierces an unlimited number of entities. When a Rolling Cactus that has already started rolling falls onto a lower surface, it maintains its forward momentum while bouncing back up, releasing 3–5 Rolling Cactus Spikes that travel in random directions. Hitting a vertical obstacle also releases Spikes, but destroys the Rolling Cactus. A Rolling Cactus' movement is affected by liquids, and it can roll uphill.

A stationary Rolling Cactus deals 25 damage when a player touches it. A Rolling Cactus projectile deals 70 / 140 / 210 damage to players (35 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters) and inflicts a knockback value of 10 (Extremely strong) upon contact. Rolling Cactus Spikes deal 60 / 120 / 180 damage to players (30 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), inflict a knockback value of 2 (Very weak), pierce entities, and break upon contact with solid tiles.
Rope Coils: Rope Coils are consumable mobility items that, when thrown by the player, travel in an arc affected by gravity until striking a block. On making contact, a vertical string of ten pieces of the respective Rope type will be placed, starting from the point of contact and descending until the Rope runs out or makes contact with another block below. Once in place, the Ropes created by a Rope Coil are ordinary Rope items that can be climbed, expanded with other placed Ropes, and collected with a pickaxe or drill.

If a thrown Rope Coil strikes the top of an already placed Rope, it will automatically extend the existing Rope. If the coil cannot extend lower than ten tiles because of an obstacle, the excess Rope pieces will drop as items. If the coil cannot extend at all, the excess Rope will drop as the coil item.
There are no rope coil analogues for chains nor streamers.
Ropes: Ropes are placeable items that primarily provide quick vertical mobility. They can be placed adjacent to blocks in any direction, or in midair where background walls are present. Ropes can also be placed atop any existing placed Rope, which extends the total length of the Rope downward without the player having to be at the bottom of the Rope column. Once placed, Ropes are used by pressing ▲ Up or ▼ Down while moving over them.
There are four different types of Rope, which are acquired in different ways:
Rope can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, or purchased from the Merchant and Skeleton Merchant for 10 Copper each.
Vine Rope is acquired by destroying vines while the Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage is equipped.
Silk Rope is crafted from Silk at a Loom.
Web Rope is crafted By Hand from Cobwebs.

All Rope variants operate identically, but Silk and Web Ropes are immune to falling lava, as opposed to normal and Vine Ropes, which will be dislodged similarly to Torches. All types can be crafted into their respective Rope Coils, consumable items useful for placing Ropes in inaccessible locations.

Vertical movement speed on a Rope equals that of a free fall, though moving down via the Rope and hitting the ground does not cause fall damage. Horizontal movement is also possible by placing adjacent Rope horizontally, but is much slower.

Visually, the player appears to move along a Rope using a mechanical tool with wheels, as though they were riding a rail. This tool appears automatically when using Rope, does not exist as a separate item, and is available from the beginning of the game.
Rotten Chunk: The Rotten Chunk is a crafting material that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped from Eaters of Souls, Devourers, Corruptors, and on the Nintendo 3DS version, the Eater of Worlds.
Rotten Egg: The Rotten Egg is a consumable ranged weapon obtained commonly from Goodie Bags, which are dropped during the Halloween season, and from shaking trees during that time. They explode on impact.

Rotten Eggs are unique in that they are one of the two player-wielded weapons that can damage friendly entities (including NPCs) by default, the other being the Flymeal (the Clothier and Guide Voodoo Dolls allow killing their respective NPCs, but are not wielded as weapons). They are a slow but effective way of killing NPCs.
Royal Delight: The Royal Delight is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Slime Prince that follows the player. The pet resembles a miniature King Slime with blush, small dotted eyes, and a tiny mouth. The Royal Delight has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by King Slime in Master Mode.
Royal Gel: The Royal Gel is a pre-Hardmode accessory that pacifies most slimes when equipped, causing them to no longer pursue the player, and will deal no contact damage or fire projectiles, even if the player deals damage to them. The Royal Gel is always dropped from King Slime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
This does not apply to the following slimes:
King Slime and his Spiked Slimes, though the normal Blue Slimes that King Slime spawns remain docile.
Queen Slime and her Bouncy Slimes, Crystal Slimes, and Heavenly Slimes.
Royal Guard's Harness: The Royal Guard's Harness is a Hardmode shield accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:
Allows the player to walk past a sentry to carry it
Royal Scepter: The Royal Scepter is a vanity accessory sold by the Princess for 1 Platinum.
The Royal Scepter cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Royal set: The Royal set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Royal Tiara, Royal Blouse, and the Royal Dress. It is purchased from the Princess for 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).
Rubblemaker: The Rubblemaker is a tool used to place ambient objects ("rubble") using items from the player's inventory. It is sold by the Goblin Tinkerer for 25 Gold.
The Rubblemaker can use various blocks to place down decorative backgrounds from different biomes. These background objects drop the block used to place them when destroyed.

By pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button, the Rubblemaker can toggle between three placement sizes: Small, Medium, and Large. The Small setting corresponds to one tile-wide rubble, the Medium setting to two tile-wide rubble, and the Large setting to three tile-wide rubble. Rubble within each setting can be cycled through using the ▲ Up and ▼ Down buttons. The material which is highest and furthest to the left in the player's inventory will be prioritized, and only that material's rubble will be placeable until another supersedes it.
Ruby: Ruby is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It can craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and it also has two exclusive recipes: the Gold Crown and the Platinum Crown. It can be obtained in the following ways:
Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable red gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form.
Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator.
Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance.
Rarely, Ruby can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well.
Like all other gems, Ruby can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.
Ruby Bunny: Gem Bunnies are harmless critters that can only spawn in the Cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Bunnies, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa.
Gem Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Bunny Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Ruby Robe: The Ruby Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. When worn, the Ruby Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to spawn an additional projectile after a short delay at a cost of 50% less damage, leading to a net-neutral effect on damage per second. It also adds 4 Armor penetration to the attacks. The Ruby Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4, applied after the 50% damage multiplier.

Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Ruby Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.
Ruby Squirrel: Gem Squirrels are harmless critters that can only spawn in the cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Squirrels, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa. Gem Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Gem Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Squirrel Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Ruby Staff: The Ruby Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that quickly fires a red bolt, which deals 50% of the weapon's damage (9 base damage) and 100% of its knockback, and has 4 armor penetration, but does not pierce. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details).
Ruinous Staff: The Ruinous Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon crafted using desert and light/dark materials. It summons a Forbidden Ruin minion that hovers above the player. Upon finding a target, the Forbidden Ruin aggressively chases it and tries to stay at a short fixed distance to its target, while firing high-velocity Forbidden Bolt projectiles towards it which gradually slow down. The Forbidden Bolts do not pierce and explode upon dissipating, dealing their full damage and knockback to other nearby enemies, but not to the enemy directly hit by them. When multiple Forbidden Ruins are summoned, they form a spinning orbital formation while firing in rapid succession.
Ruler: The Ruler is a pre-Hardmode shortsword purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 10 Silver. It swings four times in quick succession per use, with slightly varying angles with each stab.
Rune Wizard: The Rune Wizard is a rare Hardmode caster enemy that is found in the lower Cavern layer. He appears to be engulfed in flames, and attacks by firing magical, bright green Rune Blasts at the player that can pass through blocks, similar to other caster enemies such as Fire Imps and Dark Casters. However, unlike Burning Spheres, the Rune Wizard's projectiles cannot be destroyed in any way. He also deals extremely large amounts of contact damage and teleports to a new location after firing six projectiles. The Rune Wizard always drops the Rune Hat and Rune Robe upon death.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. The Rune Wizard requires 10 kills to be awarded completion of his Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Rune set: The Rune set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Rune Hat and Rune Robe. Both pieces are always dropped by the Rune Wizard, a rare Underground enemy. Wearing the full set causes the player to emit a pulse effect, as well as a bright orange and green particle effect from their feet when walking. The particles are visible in darkness but do not emit light onto other objects.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Rusty Armored Bones: The Rusty Armored Bones is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. Similar to Angry Bones, they come in multiple varieties and follow the Fighter AI. They have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Bleeding debuff for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds and a 2/9 (22.22%) chance to inflict the Slow debuff for 5 / 10 / 12.5 seconds. Only one of the debuffs can be inflicted at a time.
Rusty Armored Bones spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by slab walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
The S.D.M.G. (Space Dolphin Machine Gun) is a Hardmode gun that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When used, it very rapidly fires bullets in a small spread. It also has a 66% chance not to consume ammunition. The S.D.M.G. has a base 14% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.
SWAT Helmet: The SWAT Helmet is a vanity item that has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance to drop from Tactical Skeletons in the post-Plantera Dungeon.
Saddles: The Dusty Rawhide Saddle, Royal Gilded Saddle, and Black Studded Saddle are mount-summoning items that summon the rideable Painted Horse Mount, Majestic Horse Mount, and Dark Horse Mount, respectively. All three horse mounts are functionally identical. Once they reach a high speed, they will deal damage to enemies they come into contact with. Saddles are sold by the Zoologist for 25 Gold each, after completing at least 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary.
Safe: The Safe is a portable storage item with 40 slots to store other items. The Safe, Piggy Bank, Defender's Forge (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Void Vault (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) have the unique ability to be carried while they contain items. The Safe can be purchased from the Merchant for 20 Gold after Skeletron has been defeated.

The Safe functions identically to the Piggy Bank. However, it can also be placed on blocks in addition to platforms or on other flat furniture pieces. Additionally, the Safe and Piggy Bank do not share storage space.
Safeman's set: Safeman's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Safeman, the Community Manager at Re-Logic.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Safeman's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to her clothing set:
Sail: The Sail is a type of background wall purchased from the Pirate for 50 Copper each. It is considered a valid wall for housing.
Sailfish Boots: The Sailfish Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be found in Wooden Crates and Iron Crates. While equipped, they grant the ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster, and they increase the player's maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second). The player will leave behind a visual trail of water particles as they sprint.
The Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots, and Sailfish Boots have the same functionality, and their effects do not stack with each other.
Sailor set: The Sailor set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Sailor Hat, Sailor Shirt, and Sailor Pants. Each piece has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Pirate Deckhands, Pirate Corsairs, Pirate Deadeyes, and Pirate Crossbowers during the Pirate Invasion event.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Sake: Sake is a potion that grants the Tipsy debuff when consumed, which increases many of the player's stats but lowers the player's defense for 4 minutes, twice the duration of Ale. Sake can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Silver.
The Tipsy debuff has the following effects:
Reduces the time to produce Poo by 66.67%
Sakura Sapling: The Sakura Sapling is a type of seed that grows into a Sakura tree, which is a tree that can also spawn naturally in Forest biomes, when planted. Its appearance is purely decorative and it functions identically to regular forest trees. Sakura Saplings can be purchased from the Zoologist for 1 Gold once the Bestiary is 30% completed (164 entries).
Salamander: The Salamander is a pre-Hardmode enemy found in the Cavern layer, and has nine color variants that all share identical stats and behavior. When a player is within its line of sight, the Salamander stays rooted in place and fires green spit projectiles that have a 2/3 (66.67%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff for 2–4 / 4–8 / 5–10 seconds.

Salamanders are unique in that their ability to spawn is connected to two other enemies: the Crawdad and the Giant Shelly. Of these three enemies, a world will choose two types that it can spawn, leaving the third inaccessible. Salamanders will never spawn in a world that features both Crawdads and Giant Shellies together. This is taken into account by the Bestiary progression logic (the missing enemy will register as unlocked when the other two exclusive creatures are unlocked) and the banner acquisition (any two of the trio's banners can be used to craft the banner of the missing member of the trio).
Salmon: Salmon are a type of fish which are found plentifully by fishing in a Forest in the Sky or Surface layers. They can only be caught in lakes with more than 1,000 tiles of water.
Sand Blocks: Sand Blocks are soil blocks found in vast quantities in Desert biomes, at shore and bottom of Ocean biomes, and can be found as microbiomes in patches in the Underground layer. They are also shot as projectiles by Antlions. Sand can spread and be converted by the evil biomes and The Hallow (see below).

Sand is subject to gravity, a unique quality only shared by Slush, Silt, Shell Piles, Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and Ash on For the Worthy and Zenith worlds. Sand Blocks will deal damage to any player or enemy they fall on. If the amount of Sand falling on the player is significant, the Suffocation debuff will be inflicted until the player manages to escape. Sand is used to craft a small number of building blocks and other items directly, but it is also the raw material for Glass, which is used for a full furniture set and a variety of other items.

All forms of Sand are also ammunition for the Sandgun, but they cannot be stored in the ammo slots of the inventory. Similar to the Sand Ball projectiles shot by Antlions, shot Sand Blocks will be placed on the ground as blocks if there are space available.
Sand Elemental: The Sand Elemental is a rare Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Desert during Sandstorms. She attacks by summoning three Ancient Storms randomly around the general location of the player, which each lasts 5 seconds. The distance between them varies, and they remain stationary for their lifespan. The Sand Elemental cannot travel through blocks and flies in a non-linear pattern. She attempts to move toward the player and travels faster as her health is depleted. She has a guaranteed chance to drop a Forbidden Fragment, the main ingredient for the Forbidden armor, Spirit Flame, Ruinous Staff, and Sandstorm in a Bottle.

She is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Sand Elemental requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of her Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Sand Poacher: The Sand Poacher is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Underground Desert biome. Following the Spider AI, it will follow and attempt to deal contact damage to the player while also being capable of climbing onto background walls. If the Sand Poacher is climbing on a wall and detects the player within its line of sight, its movement speed increases drastically, making escape more difficult for the player. Upon contact, the Sand Poacher also inflicts the Acid Venom debuff for 4 / 8 / 10 seconds.
Sand Shark: Sand Sharks are Hardmode enemies only found in Desert biomes during a Sandstorm. They are able to "swim" through all varieties of Sand, Hardened Sand, and Sandstone Blocks, but will collide normally against any other block. When they draw near a player, they will lunge out of the sand to attack.
The Sand Shark itself only appears in ordinary Deserts. There are other variants for different versions of the Desert:
Bone Biter in the Corrupted Desert
Flesh Reaver in the Crimson Desert
Crystal Thresher in the Hallowed Desert
Sand Slime: The Sand Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Underground Desert. It can be recognized by its sandy color and texture.
Sand Slimes can drop a Slime Staff at slightly higher odds than nearly all other slimes, excluding Pinky.
Like most other slimes, the Sand Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel accessory equipped.
Sandcastle Bucket: The Sandcastle Bucket is a tool that places a decorative sandcastle and consumes one Sand Block upon use. It can be used on all variants of Sand Blocks and platforms, in any biome. Sandcastles are background furniture objects, but they cannot be picked up; using a pickaxe or drill on them destroys them immediately.
The Sandcastle Bucket can be found randomly in Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates.

When the cursor is moved over a valid block, one out of four sandcastle styles will be selected randomly, they can also be cycled through using the ▲ Up and ▼ Down buttons. Moving the cursor over a different block will produce a different sandcastle preview.
Sandfall Block: The Sandfall Block is an animated block type showing falling sand. It is one of the few items that uses the Crystal Ball as a crafting station.
Sandfall Wall: Sandfall Wall is one of only a few animated background walls. It depicts falling sand.
Sandgun: The Sandgun is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that fires sand ball projectiles that are affected by gravity. Upon contact with an enemy or block, the sand ball turns into its respective form of block (if the space is not occupied). Its sand balls have varying effects depending on which sand block is used for ammunition:
Sandstone Blocks: Sandstone Blocks are blocks found naturally placed in the Underground Desert biome. Like Sand and Hardened Sand, they are corruptable blocks in Hardmode, and have Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Ebonsandstone, Crimsandstone, and Pearlsandstone respectively.
Sandstone Brick: Sandstone Bricks are brick-type blocks that spawn naturally in Pyramids and can also be crafted manually.
Sandstone Brick Wall: The Sandstone Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Pyramids. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.
Sandstone Chest: The Sandstone Chest is a storage item found in the Underground Desert. They are usually found in Underground Cabins but may also uncommonly generate by themselves. Sandstone Chests can also be crafted.
Sandstone Slab: Sandstone Slab is a building material which is similar in appearance to Sandstone Bricks, but darker and larger. Unlike most other building blocks (Stone Slabs in particular), the Sandstone Slab does not have a wall counterpart.
As Sand is affected by gravity, Sandstone Slabs can be used instead of sand when building sand-related structures, as they look almost identical.
Sandstone Walls: The Sandstone Wall, Ebonsandstone Wall, Crimsandstone Wall, and Pearlsandstone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert, considered unsafe. Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Sandstone Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow. Converted Sandstone Walls may further spread conversion to other walls; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Sandstone Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.
The Treacherous Sandstone Wall is an item that places an unsafe Sandstone Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Sandstone Wall into Shimmer.
Sandstorm in a Balloon: The Sandstorm in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the functions of the Sandstorm in a Bottle and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to 10.5 tiles, and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 26.5 tiles, for a total height of 37 tiles.
The total jump height of the Sandstorm in a Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the total underwater jump height from 27 tiles to 22 tiles.

Unlike most other double-jump balloons, the Sandstorm in a Balloon's full jump is high enough for the player to take minor fall damage, unless the player has fall damage immunity accessories like the Lucky Horseshoe.
Sandstorm in a Bottle: The Sandstorm in a Bottle is an accessory found inside Gold Chests within Pyramids. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can also be obtained by throwing a Pharaoh's Mask into Shimmer, opening Oasis/Mirage Crates, and via crafting in Hardmode.

It is similar to the Cloud in a Bottle, providing a double-jump that allows for some extra height, but instead of a cloud beneath the feet, a sand jet appears and the character visually spins as they ascend on that jet.
The Sandstorm jump goes 15 tiles into the air, totalling 21 tiles when put together with the first jump. This is nearly twice as high as the height achievable with the Cloud in a Bottle.
Sanguine Staff: The Sanguine Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Sanguine Bat minion. It flies in an elliptical loop between the player and the target enemy. Sanguine Bats arrange themselves along a semicircle around the player's head, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby. The Sanguine Staff has a 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%) chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses.
Santa Claus: Santa Claus is a unique Hardmode NPC vendor who sells various decorative Christmas-themed items. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
The Frost Legion event has been completed at least once.

Santa Claus will only spawn during the Christmas seasonal event (December 15 – December 31, or unlocked for one in-game day outside of those dates by reaching the Frost Moon event's 15th wave), after which he dies.
Santa Claus will defend himself against nearby enemies by throwing baubles.
Santa set: The Santa set is a vanity set which consists of the Santa Hat, the Santa Shirt, and the Santa Pants. It is purchased from Santa Claus for 45 Gold (set) after the Frost Legion has been defeated.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Santa-NK1: Santa-NK1 is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mini-boss that spawns during the Frost Moon event. When below half health, the face and beard of the Santa mask are torn apart to reveal a rather morbid mechanical skull underneath.
Defeating Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event will add 100 / 200 / 250 points to the final score.
Sapphire: Sapphire is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It can craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and has no exclusive recipes. It can be obtained in the following ways:
Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable blue gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form.
Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator.
Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance.
Rarely, Sapphire can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well.
Like all other gems, Sapphire can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.
Sapphire Bunny: Gem Bunnies are harmless critters that can only spawn in the Cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Bunnies, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa.
Gem Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Bunny Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Sapphire Robe: The Sapphire Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. The Sapphire Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to create two projectiles which move in a double-helix pattern, each dealing 60% damage. The Sapphire Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4, applied after the 60% damage multiplier.

Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Sapphire Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.
Sapphire Squirrel: Gem Squirrels are harmless critters that can only spawn in the cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Squirrels, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa. Gem Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Gem Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Squirrel Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Sapphire Staff: The Sapphire Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires 2 blue bolts which move in a helix pattern and do not pierce, and each deal 60% of the weapon's damage (10 base damage) and 100% of its knockback. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolts will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting them additional effects (see Notes for details).
Sashimi: Sashimi is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Sauteed Frog Legs: Sauteed Frog Legs are a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Sawmill: The Sawmill is a crafting station for advanced Wood and Furniture crafting. It is 3 blocks wide, 3 blocks high, and must be placed on top of solid blocks or platforms.
Sawtooth Shark: The Sawtooth Shark is a pre-Hardmode chainsaw that can be fished from an Ocean biome. It can be caught at a rate of 1/100 (1%) with 50% Fishing Power and 1/50 (2%) with 100% Fishing Power. In terms of axe power, it is equal to the Cobalt Chainsaw.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Scaly Truffle: The Scaly Truffle is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a Pigron Mount that allows the player to fly for a limited time and run faster on land. The Scaly Truffle is obtained by fishing in the cavern layer of an Ice biome overlapping a Hallow, Corruption, or Crimson biome in Hardmode.
Scarab Bomb: The Scarab Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Sticky Bomb, but instead creates a 21-tile long and 3-tile wide shaft. The explosion will always aim away from the player's position, even after being thrown.
It can be crafted, found in Oasis Crates, Mirage Crates, Sandstone Chests, or Pots in the Underground Desert.
Scarecrow: The Scarecrow is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Pumpkin Moon event. There are ten varieties of Scarecrow, five of which lack legs and can only move by jumping, while the other five follow the normal Fighter AI. Scarecrows have a 1/10 (10%) chance to inflict the Weak debuff for 1 minute / 2 minutes / 2 minutes and 30 seconds.
Defeating a Scarecrow during the Pumpkin Moon event will add 1 / 2 / 2.5 points to the final score.
All Scarecrow varieties require 150 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Scarecrow set: The Scarecrow set is a vanity set which consists of the Scarecrow Hat, the Scarecrow Shirt and the Scarecrow Pants. All three parts of the set are dropped by Scarecrows during the Pumpkin Moon event, each with a 0.37%–3.33% (0.56%–3.33%) chance depending on the current wave.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Scarlet Macaw: The Scarlet Macaw and Blue Macaw are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. They may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Macaws have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Macaws can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scarlet / Blue Macaw Cage). Once crafted, the Macaws cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Macaws can be spawned by the Macaw Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Scorpion: The Scorpion and Black Scorpion are harmless critters that are most commonly found in a Desert. For detailed spawning conditions, see Notes.
Scorpions have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Scorpions can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scorpion/Black Scorpion Cage). Once crafted, the Scorpions cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Scorpions can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% (regular) / 15% (black) bait power.
Scorpions can be spawned by the Scorpion Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Scorpions: The Scorpion and Black Scorpion are harmless critters that are most commonly found in a Desert. For detailed spawning conditions, see Notes.
Scorpions have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Scorpions can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scorpion/Black Scorpion Cage). Once crafted, the Scorpions cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Scorpions can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% (regular) / 15% (black) bait power.
Scorpions can be spawned by the Scorpion Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Scourge of the Corruptor: The Scourge of the Corruptor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera melee weapon. When used, it fires an Eater's Bite, a fast javelin-like projectile, that splits into weaker Tiny Eater projectiles upon contact with enemies or blocks. Tiny Eaters home in on enemies and bounce up to five times before dissipating.
The Scourge of the Corruptor is always found in the Dungeon's Corruption Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Corruption Key after Plantera has been defeated.
Its Crimson counterpart are the Vampire Knives.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Scout's Sling: The Scout's Sling is a Hardmode accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:
Allows the player to walk past a sentry to carry it
Scrying Orb: The Scrying Orb is a tool that allows spectating another player in multiplayer. When used, it shifts the camera to the perspective of the next player.
Scutlix: The Scutlix is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that spawns during the Martian Madness event. It consists of the Scutlix creature, ridden by a Scutlix Gunner enemy, both of which have individual health meters and can be killed independently. When one is killed, the other will continue to attack.
Scutlix Gunner: The Scutlix is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that spawns during the Martian Madness event. It consists of the Scutlix creature, ridden by a Scutlix Gunner enemy, both of which have individual health meters and can be killed independently. When one is killed, the other will continue to attack.
Sea Snail: The Sea Snail is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Ocean. The Sea Snail's spawn rate is the lowest of all enemies in the Ocean, one-third that of Squids. It slowly crawls along the seafloor while attempting to deal contact damage. When killed, it drops Purple Mucus, which is used solely to craft Purple Dye at a Dye Vat.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Sea Turtle: The Sea Turtle is a critter that appears in the Ocean biome, swimming in the water and crawling slowly on land.
The Sea Turtle has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.
Unlike most critters, the Sea Turtle cannot be caught with a Bug Net, which means there is no craftable cage for it.
Seafood Dinner: The Seafood Dinner is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 14 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Seagull: The Seagull is a critter that spawns in the Ocean. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Palm tree or its Corrupt, Crimson, or Hallowed variant in the Ocean biome. Unlike Birds, it will not fly away when a player approaches. It will occasionally make typical seagull sounds, walk passively on land, and swim on the water's surface until they fall a certain distance or are approached while swimming, at which point they will switch to their alternative flying form. In their flying form, they will fly in a given direction for a certain amount of time before landing and switching back to their passive form. Despite their spawn conditions, they do not prioritize water whenever landing.
The Seagull may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
The Seagull has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Seagull can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Seagull Cage). Once crafted, the Seagull cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Seagull can be spawned by the Seagull Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Seahorse: The Seahorse is a critter that spawns in the Ocean. They occasionally move in water by swimming in bursts at random directions. The Seahorse has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Seahorse can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Seahorse Cage). Once crafted, the Seahorse cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Seahorse to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Seashells: Seashells are decorative items that can be found in the Ocean biomes. They can spawn on Sand Blocks within the biome, both on the beach and underwater. When placed, they can appear as one of three variants.

Seashells can appear back on beaches and underwater, as long as no more than 3 Corals or Seashells are within an 8-tile range. Spawn rates scale with Rain, Wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block. When a Seashell spawns, there is a 79.4% chance for either a regular Seashell or a Starfish, 9.8% chance for a Tulip Shell, 8.8% chance for a Lightning Whelk Shell, and 2% chance for a Junonia Shell.
Seaside Crate: The Seaside Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Ocean. Seaside Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in Water Chests. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Ocean Crate.
Seaweed: Seaweed is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Turtle to follow the player around. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Turtle will fly with a propeller to catch up to the player. Seaweed has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being found in Ivy Chests, located in the Underground Jungle's Jungle Shrines or Living Mahogany Trees. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it also has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being obtained from Jungle Crates and Bramble Crates.
Seaweed Planter: The Seaweed Planter is a decorative furniture item acquired as a random reward for completing quests from the Angler NPC with a 1/30 (3.33%) chance.
Seed: The Seed is a pre-Hardmode dart. While a Blowpipe or Blowgun is in a player's inventory, there is a chance that any vegetation growing on normal grass, in Clay Pots, and in Planter Boxes will drop Seeds. Flowers typically drop 4 Seeds at a time, while tall grass typically drops 1–2 Seeds.
Seedler: The Seedler is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When swung, it fires Seedler Nut projectiles that travel in a downwards arc before exploding into 4–7 Seedler Thorns upon hitting an enemy or after 0.33–2.15 seconds. Seedler Thorns deal 70% of the weapon's damage (35 base damage) and knockback (base knockback of 4.2 (Average)), are unaffected by gravity, and target nearby enemies when fired.
Seedling: The Seedling is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Sapling to follow the player around. When the player is far enough away or in midair, it will sprout leaflets from its arms and use them as makeshift wings to fly towards them. The Seedling has a 1/20 (5%) / 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being dropped by Plantera.
Selenian: The Selenian is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events. It is a ground-based enemy that wields two flaming swords and possesses a spinning attack that causes it to quickly lunge forward while reflecting the player's projectiles. It takes triple the damage from other player-inflicted sources while spinning. Selenians can reflect bullets, arrows, and darts, but not rockets, and the projectiles of numerous other weapons. For the complete list, see the list of reflected projectiles.
Sensors: Sensors are Hardmode mechanisms that emit a signal under specific circumstances. They can be placed in midair without the support of background walls. There are 7 different types of sensors, split into 2 sub-categories: Logic Sensors and Liquid Sensors.
Seraph Necklace: The Seraph Necklace is a Hardmode accessory made by combining a Harpy Charm and a Cross Necklace at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It combines the effects of the two accessories, periodically redirecting arrows towards enemies and doubling the length of invincibility after taking damage. In addition, the cooldown of the Seraph Necklace's arrow-redirecting effect is 20% lower than the Harpy Charm's, at 1.2 seconds.
Sergeant United Shield: The Sergeant United Shield is a Hardmode boomerang that is rarely sold by the Traveling Merchant for 35 Gold. When thrown, it homes in on enemies within 50 tiles and will attempt to hit up to five enemies before returning to the player, but loses 20% of its damage for each enemy struck.

While holding this weapon and equipping a shield (including the Sergeant United Shield itself, while it is not being thrown), the player is granted the ability to parry incoming damage. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate will cause the player to raise the shield and brace for the next attack. When timed correctly, up to 0.33 seconds before taking a hit, the enemy's attack will be parried, which negates the contact damage being dealt to the player, deals 200% of the contact damage of the attacking enemy, inflicts a knockback value of 5 (Average), and grants the player 30 invincibility frames (60 with the Cross Necklace equipped). Successfully parrying an attack also grants the Striking Moment buff, causing the next melee attack to deal 500% or five times its usual base damage for the next five seconds.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Servant of Cthulhu: The Servant of Cthulhu is a pre-Hardmode boss servant that is summoned by the Eye of Cthulhu during its first stage.
Sextant: The Sextant is an informational accessory that displays the current moon phase.

The Sextant can be received as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a Sextant as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.
Shackle: The Shackle is an accessory that grants 1 point of defense. It is dropped by most kinds of Zombies with a 1/50 (2%) chance. Shackles may be useful early in the game when only few accessories are available. Typically, they should be replaced with more valuable accessories once out of free slots.
Shadewood: Shadewood is a type of wood harvested from Shadewood trees and Shadewood Palm trees found naturally growing in Crimson biomes. Shadewood trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Crimson grass or Crimson Jungle grass above surface, and Shadewood Palm trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Crimsand Blocks above surface.
Shadewood Bow: The Shadewood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow.
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Ebonwood Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Shadewood Hammer: The Shadewood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its Corruption counterpart is the Ebonwood Hammer.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Shadewood Sword: The Shadewood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword.
Its Corruption counterpart is the Ebonwood Sword.
Shadewood Wall: Shadewood Walls are a type of Wall made from Shadewood.
Shadewood armor: Shadewood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Shadewood Helmet, Shadewood Breastplate, and Shadewood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Shadewood. The full set grants 5 defense while equipped.
Its Corruption counterpart is Ebonwood armor, which has identical stats.
Shadow Candle: The Shadow Candle is a furniture item that emits a low amount of light, and can be placed only on flat-surface items. While placed nearby or while held, it grants Shadow Candle debuff to the player.

The Shadow Candle debuff nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns. The debuff is applied to any players holding or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Shadow Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice.
Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Shadow Candle will turn it off. Shadow Candles that are turned off will not activate the Shadow Candle debuff.
Shadow Chest: The Shadow Chest is a storage item which is found only in The Underworld, generally on top of or within Ruined Houses, and contains rare items.

All Shadow Chests are initially locked, requiring a Shadow Key to open. The key is not consumed when used. Each Shadow Chest contains one high-tier item of rarity, along with other standard Underground loot.
Like all other naturally-occurring Chests, Shadow Chests can be freed with a pickaxe or drill after being emptied, and picked up by the player for placement and use elsewhere.
Shadow Dye: Shadow Dye is a type of dye bought from the Dye Trader during a full moon, or given as a possible reward for turning in a Strange Plant in Hardmode. When applied, it will darken the color of an item to almost pure black. Shadow Dye also leaves black colored particles while moving.
Shadow Jousting Lance: The Shadow Jousting Lance is a Hardmode, post-Plantera melee weapon. When attacking using ⚒ Use / Attack, the lance will extend, and holding ⚒ Use / Attack will keep it extended at a fixed angle. The damage and knockback will increase depending on the player's movement speed, making mounts, sprinting accessories, or dash abilities (such as those granted by Shield of Cthulhu, Tabi/Master Ninja Gear, or Solar Flare armor) useful for maximizing damage. When the player takes damage, the Shadow Jousting Lance will stop being active. The Shadow Jousting Lance has a 1/25 (4%) / 49/625 (7.84%) chance of being dropped by Giant Cursed Skulls in the post-Plantera Dungeon.
It is the upgrade of the Jousting Lance and Hallowed Jousting Lance.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Shadow Key: The Shadow Key is an item used solely to open Shadow Chests found scattered in the Underworld and Obsidian Lock Boxes found from Obsidian and Hellstone Crates. It is not consumed upon use; one Shadow Key can be used to open unlimited Shadow Chests. It can be found as secondary loot in Locked Gold Chests and Water Chests within the Dungeon, or from Golden Lock Boxes found in Dungeon and Stockade Crates.
Shadow Orb (item): The Shadow Orb is a light pet-summoning item that spawns a slow-moving Shadow Orb which follows the player around and emits dim, purple light. The orb can move through solid objects and liquids unhindered, but moves very slowly, causing it to fall behind when the player is moving quickly. If it falls far enough behind, it will teleport to the player's location. The Shadow Orb has a 1/5 (20%) chance of dropping from destroyed Shadow Orbs, but it also has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being acquired from Corrupt Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Defiled Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which are obtained by fishing in The Corruption.
The Crimson counterpart to the Shadow Orb is the Crimson Heart.
Shadow Scale: The Shadow Scale is a pre-Hardmode crafting material dropped from the Eater of Worlds (and its Treasure Bag in Expert Mode).
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Tissue Sample.
Shadow armor: Shadow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Shadow Helmet, Shadow Scalemail, and Shadow Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Demonite Bars (180 Demonite Ore) and 45 Shadow Scales.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Crimson armor.
Shadow armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Shadow armor pieces, still providing the set bonus but not the afterimage effect.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
+75% acceleration and deceleration speed and ×1.15 maximum movement speed
The player also emits visual afterimages and shadow particles while moving, and equipped Rocket Boots will emit purple flames.
Shadowbeam Staff: The Shadowbeam Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that has a 1/20 (5%) / 39/400 (9.75%) chance of being dropped by Necromancers in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires a purple beam that travels almost instantly to its maximum distance (112.5 tiles), bouncing off blocks on impact. The beam can pierce infinite enemies, but for each enemy hit, its damage is reduced by 10%. Each enemy can only be hit once.
Shadowflame Apparition: The Shadowflame Apparition is a Hardmode enemy summoned by the Goblin Warlock during the Goblin Army event. Summoned in swarms as projectiles, they pass through blocks while attempting to ram into the player. They are immune to knockback, and both they and their caster move very quickly, allowing them to easily overwhelm the player.
Shadowflame Bow: The Shadowflame Bow is a Hardmode bow that has a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Goblin Warlocks during a Hardmode Goblin Army. When used, it converts any type of arrow into Shadowflame Arrows. Shadowflame Arrows can pierce two enemies and inflict the Shadowflame debuff for 2–5 seconds. Shadowflame Arrows have a medium velocity but a significantly longer arc. The Shadowflame Bow also has a base 7% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Shadowflame Hades Dye: Shadowflame Hades Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When applied, it turns the item violet and adds fire effects that trail behind the player.
Shadowflame Hex Doll: The Shadowflame Hex Doll is a Hardmode magic weapon that fires a spread of three curving purple tentacle projectiles per use at a medium range, inflicting the Shadowflame debuff onto enemies for 4–8 seconds, and piercing 2 targets before dissipating on the 3rd hit. The third tentacle fired in each use is always aimed directly towards the cursor, but the first two keep their random spread. The Shadowflame Hex Doll also has a base 7% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
The Shadowflame Hex Doll has a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Goblin Warlocks during a Hardmode Goblin Army.
Shadowflame Knife: The Shadowflame Knife is a Hardmode melee weapon that has a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Goblin Warlocks during the Goblin Army event. When used, it fires a small gravity-affected knife projectile that can bounce off enemies up to two times, but dissipates upon contact with blocks. It inflicts the Shadowflame debuff for 1–3 seconds on hit. The Shadowflame Knife also has a base 7% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Shark: The Shark is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Ocean. Sharks are rarer than other Ocean enemies like Crabs or Pink Jellyfish, though they are still relatively common.

Throwing a Chum Bucket into Ocean water will multiply the spawn chance of Sharks by 5×. Unlike Chum Buckets' effect on Fishing Power, only one use is required to boost the spawn chance of Sharks to the maximum possible value.
Shark Bait: The Shark Bait is a pet-summoning item that summons a pet Shark Pup. When underwater, the Shark Pup swims around freely. When out of water, it is encased in a bubble. When the player is too far away, the Shark Pup will move swiftly toward them. The Shark Bait has a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Water Chests and a 1/10 (10%) chance of being found in Ocean and Seaside Crates.
Shark Fin: The Shark Fin is a crafting material that has a 19/20 (95%) chance of being dropped by Sharks and Orcas found in the Ocean biome, and a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Sand Sharks during a Sandstorm.
Shark Tooth Necklace: The Shark Tooth Necklace is an accessory which has a 1/150 (0.67%) / 1/75 (1.33%) chance to drop from Blood Zombies and Dripplers found during a Blood Moon. It increases the player's armor penetration by 5 when equipped.
Sharkron: The Sharkron is a Hardmode boss servant fired by Duke Fishron's Sharknado and Cthulhunado attacks. They will first spawn from within the Sharknado or Cthulhunado, staying inside it for some time before being launched directly at the player. They travel in an arc, descending at a slower speed after reaching maximum height. They are killed instantly upon impact with blocks.
Despite being shark-related, Sharkrons do not move faster in water.
Sharkron Balloon: The Sharkron Balloon is an accessory that combines the effects of the Tsunami in a Bottle and the Balloon Pufferfish. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30% increasing the player's first jump's height to ~10½ tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 13 tiles, for a total height of 23½ tiles.

The total jump height of the Sharkron Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the total underwater jump height from 17½ tiles (8 tiles + 9½ tiles from Tsunami jump) to 15 tiles (7 tiles + 8 tiles from Tsunami jump).
It can be combined with a Lucky Horseshoe at a Tinkerer's Workshop to craft a Pink Horseshoe Balloon.
Sharp Spike Block: The Sharp Spike Block is a pre-Hardmode block crafted from Spike Blocks. Upon contact, it deals 70 damage to the player and inflicts the Bleeding debuff for 10–20 / 20–40 / 25–50 seconds.
Sharpening Station: The Sharpening Station is a furniture item found naturally generated in Underground Cabins in the Underground Jungle. In Hardmode, it is also sold by the Merchant for 10 Gold.

Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Sharpening Station grants the Sharpened buff, which increases armor penetration of melee weapons and melee projectiles by 12. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

Unlike equipment buff items, the Sharpening Station must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 3×2 tiles being available.
Shell Pile: Shell Piles are a decorative block found naturally in the Ocean biome in large clumps. They are affected by gravity and will fall if supporting blocks are removed, dealing damage to any player or enemy they land on. They can also be found in Ocean Crates or in Seaside Crates.
Shell Piles can be converted into Sand Blocks when used on an Extractinator.
Shellphone: The Shellphone is a post-Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone, Magic Conch, and Demon Conch. The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point, the Ocean, the Underworld, and the player's spawn point set via a Bed.
Shield of Cthulhu: The Shield of Cthulhu is a pre-Hardmode shield accessory that is always dropped from the Eye of Cthulhu's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While equipped, it grants 2 defense and allows the player to perform a dash attack by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right button, or the Dash button once. Dashing into an enemy deals damage to it, causes the player to bounce backward, and grants 0.07 seconds of invincibility frames and 0.17 seconds of immunity to contact damage from the hit enemy. The cooldown between dashes is 0.5 seconds.
Shifting Pearlsands Dye: Shifting Pearlsands Dye is a Hardmode dye which is very similar to the Shifting Sands Dye, but more pink. It can only be crafted, and cannot be obtained any other way.
Shifting Sands Dye: Shifting Sands Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When applied, it gives the item an appearance similar to falling sand. It can be used to craft Shifting Pearlsands Dye when one acquires Crystal Shards.
Shimmer Arrow: The Shimmer Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow that is obtained by throwing a Wooden or Hellfire Arrow into Shimmer. It experiences reversed gravity when fired. Upon contact with enemies or blocks, it creates a visual rainbow explosion.
Shimmer Gun: The Shimmer Gun is a tool that is obtained by throwing a Slime Gun into Shimmer. When used, it sprays a stream of Shimmer that inflicts the Shimmering debuff on enemies and NPCs. Its stream has similar properties to actual Shimmer, with the exception that it does not affect items and other players:
Town NPCs are transformed into their alternate Shimmered appearance.
Certain enemies are transformed into other enemies.
Most critters are transformed into Faelings.
Most slimes are transformed into Shimmer Slimes.
The Shimmer Gun has an additional effect of converting any Torch shot with it into one matching the biome it is in, similarly to the Torch God's Favor.
It can be used limitlessly and does not consume any ammunition or mana.
The Shimmer Gun cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Shimmer Slime: The Shimmer Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that cannot be found naturally, and is instead created when most varieties of slimes come into contact with Shimmer or upon being sprayed by the Shimmer Gun (with exceptions below). Shimmer Slimes have the ability to reflect projectiles, similarly to Shimmer itself. For the complete list, see the list of reflected projectiles.
