Like most other slimes, the Shimmer Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel accessory equipped.
Shimmerfall Block: The Shimmerfall Block is an animated block type which shows flowing Shimmer. It glows when placed.
Shimmerfall Wall: Shimmerfall Wall is a type of wall. It depicts flowing Shimmer. It glows when placed like Shimmerfall Blocks that it is made from. As with most crafted walls, Shimmerfall Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Shine Potion: The Shine Potion is a buff potion which grants the Shine buff when consumed. The buff makes the player glow brightly, which is useful for exploring caves or while exploring underwater. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Shine Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and Crates.
Shinobi Infiltrator armor: Shinobi Infiltrator armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Shinobi Infiltrator's Helmet, Shinobi Infiltrator's Torso, and Shinobi Infiltrator's Pants. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 150 Defender Medals.
The Shinobi Infiltrator armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Monk armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Lightning Aura sentry summons have increased attack rate, can deal critical hits with a fixed 1/4 (25%) chance, and their radius is increased by 4 tiles.
Shiny Black Slab: The Shiny Black Slab was a pet-summoning item that spawned an Android. It was obtainable from Chests in the surface layer, but only on the Google Play version. It was obtainable on other mobile devices via trading.
This item was removed alongside all other mobile-exclusive content in the Mobile 1.3.0.7 update.
Players on Windows Phone who acquired the Shiny Black Slab via trading continue to have access to it.
Shiny Red Balloon: The Shiny Red Balloon is an accessory that increases the player's jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the height that the player can jump from 6 tiles to ~10½ tiles, effectively a ~75% boost. However, it reduces jump height when underwater, from 8 tiles to ~7 tiles. The Shiny Red Balloon has a 1/4 (25%) of being found inside Skyware Chests on Floating Islands, as well as a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Sky Crates and Azure Crates.
Shiny Stone: The Shiny Stone is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that is always dropped from Golem's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While the player is not moving, not using any items, and not being damaged, the Shiny Stone greatly boosts the player's base health regeneration (i.e., the natural health regeneration without any buffs or debuffs) by accelerating its buildup and increasing the maximum rate, as well as providing +10% base health regeneration. Additionally, the Shiny Stone reduces the damage taken from debuffs by half and gives +2HP/s flat health regeneration, increased to +2.5HP/s if the player has a positive health regeneration stat.
Ship in a Bottle: The Ship in a Bottle is a decorative furniture item acquired by completing Angler NPC quests.
Ship's Wheel: The Ship's Wheel is a wall decoration acquired by completing Angler quests.
Shiverthorn: Shiverthorn is a type of herb which appears as an icy-blue flower. It grows naturally on Snow and Ice Blocks of any type. Shiverthorn can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Shiverthorn Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles.

Shiverthorn blooms randomly, and unlike other herbs, remains bloomed permanently thereafter. Its blooming is indicated by the blue flower and blue-green light emitted. Harvesting mature Shiverthorn yields 1 Shiverthorn item. Harvesting blooming Shiverthorn yields 1 Shiverthorn item and 1–3 Shiverthorn Seeds. Harvesting blooming Shiverthorn with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Shiverthorns and 1–5 Shiverthorn Seeds instead.
Both Shiverthorn and Shiverthorn Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.
Shiverthorn Seeds: Shiverthorn Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Shiverthorns while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on a naturally grown Shiverthorns while they are fully grown. Shiverthorn will always bloom after a period of growth, and unlike other herbs, remains in-bloom permanently thereafter. Blooming Shiverthorn emits a glowing particle effect. Each plant drops 1–3 Shiverthorn Seeds when harvested while blooming.

Shiverthorn Seeds can be placed on Snow Blocks and any type of Ice Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Shiverthorns. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Snow biome, but will only yield seeds when blooming.
Shoe Spikes: The Shoe Spikes are an accessory that lets players partially "stick" to the sides of blocks, slowly sliding down them when moving against them in midair. Jumps can also be performed off the sides of blocks. By repeatedly sticking and jumping, vertical blocks can be scaled. When sliding down, the slide speed can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Shoe Spikes can be found in Gold Chests found in Underground and Cavern layers, and in Rich Mahogany Chests found in the Underground Jungle.

Shoe Spikes function identically to the Climbing Claws, but are found in different locations, Climbing Claws only appearing in surface chests. When both Shoe Spikes and Climbing Claws are equipped simultaneously, the wearer remains completely "stuck" at a fixed point when moving against the sides of blocks, and may slide down with the ▼ Down key. This effect can be achieved using a single accessory if the Shoe Spikes and Climbing Claws are combined into the Tiger Climbing Gear at a Tinkerer's Workshop.
Shotgun: The Shotgun is a Hardmode gun that can be purchased from the Arms Dealer for 25 Gold. When used, it fires a spread of 4–5 bullets, consuming one piece of ammunition.
Shrimp: Shrimp are a type of fishing catch which are found uncommonly by fishing in the Ocean in the Sky or Surface layers.
Shrimp Po' Boy: The Shrimp Po' Boy is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 18 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Shrimp Po' Boy has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Sharks, Orcas, and Crabs. Statue-spawned Sharks, Orcas and Crabs do not drop it, as it is a food item.
Shrimpy Truffle: The Shrimpy Truffle is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that spawns Cute Fishron, a miniature rideable Duke Fishron-style mount that can fly and hover indefinitely. The Shrimpy Truffle is always dropped from Duke Fishron's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Cute Fishron has a base flight speed of 40 mph. Moving through liquids causes Cute Fishron to gain a drastic movement speed bonus of about +105% (to 82 mph, the fastest of any mount), as well as providing the rider with a +15% damage bonus, indicated by Cute Fishron's eyes glowing. These boosts continue for 6 seconds after it leaves liquid, though during this time, its speed boost drops to +100% (to 80 mph). Liquid boosts also take effect when Cute Fishron gets "wet" by flying in the rain, flying through Bubbles filled with liquids, being submerged in liquid from a filled Bucket, or being hit by a Water Gun. The +100% movement speed boost (80 mph) and +15% damage boost also take effect when the rider's health falls below half.

Upon contact with any blocks, Cute Fishron's movement speed is drastically lowered to a very slow crawl (5 mph, or 10 mph if boosted). This speed penalty is removed as soon as it loses contact with blocks.
Shroomerang: The Shroomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that is dropped by Spore Bats with a 1/40 (2.5%) chance.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Shroomite Bar: The Shroomite Bar is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bar.
Shroomite Digging Claw: The Shroomite Digging Claw is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pickaxe and axe. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore. It is the pickaxe with the fastest mining speed.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Shroomite Plating: Shroomite Plating is a building material crafted from Stone Blocks and Shroomite Bars. It produces a small amount of light when placed but it does not count as a light source for housing. It is essentially the Shroomite equivalent of a brick.
Shroomite Plating Wall: The Shroomite Plating Wall is a type of wall made from Shroomite Plating. It glows when placed like the block it is made from.
Shroomite armor: Shroomite armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear, Shroomite Mask, and Shroomite Helmet, providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition. Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:
The player leaves dark blue afterimages when moving

While the player is standing still or is moving slower than their maximum running speed, they quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is gradually built up over the course of 1.12 seconds.

During the first 0.28 seconds of building up stealth, the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following maximum values, and keep these maximum values if the player builds up further stealth beyond that point:
The player also gains the following stat boost, which linearly increases to its maximum value over the full 1.12 seconds duration of building up stealth:
Stealth mode is deactivated upon riding a mount or taking damage. Stealth mode will also fade once the player starts moving (see Notes for details).

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).
Shrub Star: The Shrub Star is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns an Everscream Sapling to follow the player around. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Everscream Sapling flies toward them, tucking its legs together and emitting fire from its legs like a rocket. The Shrub Star is dropped by the Everscream during the Frost Moon event in Master Mode with a 5–25% chance depending on the current wave.
Shucked Oyster: The Shucked Oyster is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It is guaranteed to be obtained when opening an Oyster.
Shuriken: The Shuriken is a consumable ranged weapon. It can hit up to 4 targets. Shurikens can be found in Pots and Chests around the world, and can be purchased from the Merchant for 15 Copper each.
Sickle: The Sickle is a tool that produces Hay blocks when used to cut wild grass plants and sea oats. The collected Hay can be used for building purposes and crafted into Target Dummies and Hay Walls.
The Sickle is purchased from the Merchant for 60 Silver.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Sign: The Sign is a decorative furniture item that can store a player-written message. A Sign must be placed and then the ⚷ Open / Activate button must be pressed on it to edit or display its message. A Sign can be placed on top of blocks, beside them, or hanging from their underside, or be placed on walls. A Sign's message can be up to 10 lines long, at 48 characters max per line, for a total of 480 characters maximum per sign. Signs can be used for decoration, labeling areas, adventure text, etc.

There is a maximum limit of 32,000 placed Signs that can be written on in each world. If more than 32,000 are put down, only the first 32,000 Signs that are interacted with can be edited; the rest do not open a menu upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate (until one of the first 32,000 Signs is removed).
Silk: Silk is an item used to craft the Bed, as well as several placeable decorative items and vanity clothing items.
Silly Balloon Machine: The Silly Balloon Machine is a novelty furniture item that can be purchased from the Party Girl for 5 Gold. Once placed, it continuously produces decorative pink, purple, and green balloons at short random intervals and at no cost. It can be deactivated and reactivated via Wire.
Silly Balloon Walls: Silly Balloon Walls are background Walls crafted from Silly Balloons, which are purchased from the Party Girl during a party.
Silly Balloons: Silly Balloons are blocks that can be purchased during a Party from the Party Girl for 1 Silver each or obtained from killing Balloon Slimes. When a single one is placed, it has a round appearance, just like Bubbles and Smoke Blocks. When balloons of the same color are placed together in groups, they connect to make a seemingly single larger balloon block. If placed adjacent to balloon blocks of other colors, they do not connect, and each will remain a single round balloon.
In a similar way to Pink Slime Blocks, landing on any silly balloon block negates fall damage and causes the player to bounce. Silly Balloons can also be used to craft balloon furniture.
Silly Sunflower set: The Silly Sunflower set is a vanity set which consists of the Silly Sunflower Petals, Silly Sunflower Tops and Silly Sunflower Bottoms. They are purchased from the Clothier for 9 Gold (set) while a Party is active.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Silly Tied Balloons: Silly Tied Balloons are animated novelty furniture items that can be purchased during a Party from the Party Girl for 10 Silver each.
Silly Tied Bundle of Balloons: The Silly Tied Bundle of Balloons is an animated novelty furniture item crafted from green, purple, and pink Silly Tied Balloons, which can be purchased during a Party from the Party Girl.
Silt Block: Silt Blocks are a type of soil blocks that generates in the Underground and Cavern layers, appearing more frequently at lower depths. Silt is affected by gravity and will deal damage to any player or enemy it falls on. Unlike Sand Blocks, silt can stop The Hallow, The Crimson, and The Corruption from spreading. Silt looks similar to Ash Blocks, but is a lighter color.

Silt can be placed in an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to be converted into various valuable materials, including gems, coins, ores, and very rarely, the Amber Mosquito pet summoning item.
Silver Axe: The Silver Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Axe.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Silver Bar: The Silver Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Bar.
Silver Bow: The Silver Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Silver Bracer: The Silver Bracer is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron accessory that can be obtained as secondary loot from Locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon, and from Golden Lock Boxes found in Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Silver Brick: Silver Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Like the ore it is made of, placed Silver Bricks will sparkle. It is not recommended that it be used for building unless the player has silver ore to spare. It can be crafted into Silver Brick Walls.
Silver Brick Wall: Silver Brick Walls are a type of background wall crafted from Silver Bricks. Enemies will not spawn where they are placed, and they can be used for NPC houses.
Silver Broadsword: The Silver Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Silver Shortsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Broadsword.
Silver Bullet: The Silver Bullet is a pre-Hardmode bullet. It deals 2 more damage and is slightly faster than Musket Balls. It also deals 300% damage to Werewolves.

Silver Bullets can be bought from the Arms Dealer in worlds with Silver for 15 Copper each, or 1 Gold 50 Silver for 1000 rounds. During pre-Hardmode, they are only sold during Blood Moons. Once Hardmode begins, they are always available. Silver Bullets can also be found replacing Wooden Arrows in Pots during Hardmode, obtained from Shadow Chests, or crafted.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Bullet.
Silver Hammer: The Silver Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, and Quick provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Silver Ore: Silver Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on Floating Islands. Silver Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Tungsten Ore.
Silver Pickaxe: The Silver Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks weaker than Meteorite.

Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Pickaxe. The Silver Pickaxe has a significantly faster mining speed, but significantly less pickaxe power; it takes more hits to destroy blocks, and cannot mine Meteorite.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Silver Shield: The Silver Shield is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron shield accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:
Silver Shortsword: The Silver Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Silver Broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Shortsword.
Silver armor: Silver armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Silver Helmet, Silver Chainmail, and Silver Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Silver Bars (240 Silver Ore). The full set grants 13 defense while equipped.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Tungsten armor.
Sinks: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station.
There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.
Skeleton: The Skeleton is a pre-Hardmode enemy that frequently spawns in the Cavern layer as one of many variants. Regular Skeletons can be spawned by the Skeleton Statue.
Like many other enemies that follow the Fighter AI, Skeletons can open doors and Tall Gate, albeit only during Blood Moons or rarely in Graveyards.
In Expert Mode, certain Skeletons are able to throw bones when they are close to the player. Regular bone-throwing Skeletons can be spawned by the Bone Skeleton Statue in any difficulty.
Skeleton Archer: The Skeleton Archer is a Hardmode enemy that sometimes spawns in the Cavern layer. They move fairly slow compared to other cave enemies. When the player is in their line of sight, they will stop moving and shoot Flaming Arrows at the player, which have a chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff.
Skeleton Commando: The Skeleton Commando is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It slowly approaches the player, and upon getting within their line of sight, stops in place before firing Rockets that explode upon contact with solid blocks.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Skeleton Commandos spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by brick walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Skeleton Merchant: The Skeleton Merchant is a unique NPC vendor who randomly appears in the Cavern layer. He is not a town NPC and will despawn when off-screen, although enemies will not spawn near him.

The Skeleton Merchant's stock changes at dawn (4:30 AM) daily, and he does not need to respawn for it to do so. The majority of the items in his inventory will vary, depending on the current moon phase.
The Skeleton Merchant will defend himself against nearby non-skeletal enemies by throwing Bones, while ignoring most other skeletons.
Unlike other NPCs, the Skeleton Merchant does not have a map icon.
He is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. His current name will be displayed (e.g. Rattles Magoo) rather than it displaying as Skeleton Merchant.
Skeleton Sniper: The Skeleton Sniper is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. It attacks from long range, slowly approaching the player. As soon as it has a clear line of sight, it pauses briefly before firing a single shot. This shot can be fired from offscreen, travels at an extremely high velocity, and deals enough damage to kill a player with 500 health in three / two / one hit(s).
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Skeleton Snipers spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by slab walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Skeletron: Skeletron is a pre-Hardmode boss. Defeating Skeletron for the first time grants unlimited access to all Dungeon areas for players within the current world and allows the Clothier NPC to move into an available vacant house.

If attempting to enter the Dungeon before killing Skeletron, Dungeon Guardians spawn once a player reaches 0 depth. These enemies deal 9,999 damage and generally kill any player in a single hit. Managing to defeat a Dungeon Guardian does not grant access to the Dungeon, thus defeating Skeletron is mandatory for accessing the Dungeon safely.
While Skeletron is alive, its exclusive music Skeletron will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 1 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Skeletron Prime: Skeletron Prime is a Hardmode mechanical boss which is essentially a more difficult version of Skeletron. It consists of a head and four limbs, but, similarly to Skeletron, only the head needs to be defeated to defeat the boss.
While Skeletron Prime is alive, its exclusive music Skeletron Prime will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Skiphs' Blood: Skiphs' Blood is a Hardmode dye obtained from Hardmode bosses' Treasure Bags (except Queen Slime's) along with Skiphs' set. It can also be a random reward from the Dye Trader for completing a Strange Plant quest after the Moon Lord has been defeated. When equipped, it gives the player a dark purple tone, also adding a Shimmering purple effect to the player's body.
Skiphs' set: Skiphs' set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Skiphs, one of the programmers who develops Terraria and its official website.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Skiphs' equipment also includes these non-vanity items, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Skull: The Skull is a rare vanity item that has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which are found in the Cavern layer, or a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance by those spawned from a Skeleton Statue or a Bone Skeleton Statue (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Skull Bow: The Skull Bow is an unobtainable bow. Apart from standard bow behavior, it can convert Bone Arrows (ID 474) into Bone Arrows from the Marrow (ID 117).
Skull Lantern: The Skull Lantern is a decorative piece of furniture that provides light. They always face left, and cannot be turned off via Wire.
Sky Blue Flower: The Sky Blue Flower is a type of plant. It grows on Jungle grass in any layer except the Underworld, or on regular Sand Blocks submerged in at least 2 tiles of any liquid above surface. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Sky Blue Dye.
Sky Crate: The Sky Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in Space, e.g. in Floating Lakes. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally found in Skyware Chests (with the exception of the Sky Mill). Its Hardmode counterpart is the Azure Crate.
Sky Dragon's Fury: The Sky Dragon's Fury is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee weapon that possesses two different modes of attack.
When pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button while held, the Sky Dragon's Fury spins in a 360° radius around the player, dealing damage and emitting visual trails of blue energy.

When pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button while held, the Sky Dragon's Fury performs an alternate attack: it swings once towards the cursor, firing three blue energy orbs at a spreading 45° angle during the swing. The energy orbs burst into damaging Electrospheres after traveling for 0.25 seconds or upon contact with enemies or blocks. The Electrospheres continuously damage entities within radius, and last for a random duration between 1 second and 2.5 seconds before dissipating. The Sky Dragon's Fury itself during this attack, the energy orbs, and the Electrospheres all deal 50% of the weapon's damage (70 base damage).
The Sky Dragon's Fury has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Sky Fracture: The Sky Fracture is a Hardmode wand. When used, it summons three energy swords in quick succession around the player, aiming at the cursor's location. The swords do not pierce enemies and cannot pass through blocks. The Sky Fracture also has a base 24% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Sky Mill: The Sky Mill is a crafting station used to craft the Cloud, Duskware, Harpy, and Skyware furniture sets; Rain, Rainbow, Snow, Star, and Lava Cloud blocks; and Sunplate Blocks, and Harpy Blocks.

The Sky Mill has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being obtained from Skyware Chests on Floating Islands. It can also be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold if she is spoken to in Space (above 65% altitude of the surface).
The Sky Mill also has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being obtained from Sky or Azure Crates if the Skyblock special world seed is active and the tile threshold is not exceeded.
Skyware Chest: The Skyware Chest is a storage item found only on Floating Islands.
Slap Hand: The Slap Hand is a Hardmode broadsword that can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 25 Gold during a Blood Moon. It is notable for having extremely high base knockback – a rating of 20, one of the highest values among all player-caused sources of knockback. The Slap Hand also has a 19% base critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.
Slasher's Mysterious Skull: Slasher's Mysterious Skull is a transformation mount item that transforms the user into a Velociraptor. While in this form, wings can be used, which differs from other mounts. It will show a Pterosaur carrying the Velociraptor (the player) when flying. However, the player cannot dash while using the mount. The player can still swing weapons, drink potions, and use Hooks and items as normal, with unique visual animations for each action. The player's hurt sound is also replaced with a growl.
Sleepy Octopod: The Sleepy Octopod is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss melee weapon that is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. When used, it is swung continuously in a 360° radius around the player. After swinging for 0.7 seconds, a large shockwave occurs, dealing 300% of the weapon's damage (150 base damage) with an additional 25% critical hit chance. However, the explosion does not infict knockback.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Slice of Cake: The Slice of Cake is a furniture item acquired by being the first player to talk to the Party Girl during a randomly occurring Party. Player-initiated Parties (caused by a Party Center), or the Party initiated at the creation of Celebration Mk 10 or Zenith worlds will not cause her to give players the Slice of Cake.

Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Slice of Cake grants the Sugar Rush buff, which grants +20% movement speed and +20% mining speed. This lasts for 2 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

Unlike equipment buff items, the Slice of Cake must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 2×2 tiles being available.
Slice of Hell Cake: The Slice of Hell Cake is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Imp to follow the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Imp will spread its arms and fly to catch up to them. The Slice of Hell Cake has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests and a 1/20 (5%) chance of being found in Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.
Slime: Slimes are the most common enemy type. They are almost always the first enemy the player encounters in a new world. They come in multiple sizes and colors, each with different health, defense, and damage. Slimes generally follow the basic Slime AI: They hop in the direction of the player and rest a short amount of time afterwards. When a slime is preparing to hop, it bobs up and down rapidly. Slimes can float in water and move significantly faster while doing so, but only the Lava Slime can float in lava.

Slimes spawned on or near the surface are usually neutral and do not chase the player during the day, unless they take damage. All slimes become hostile at night and slimes spawned underground are always hostile. Green, Blue, Red, Purple, and Yellow Slimes usually spawn on or near the surface, while Mother Slime, Baby Slime, and Black Slime can only be found underground. Pinky may appear anywhere, yet rarely. Similar to Pinky, the Golden Slime may appear anywhere rarely, but only when the Celebration Mk 10 special world seed is active. On Windy Days, certain slimes can spawn attached to Windy Balloons.
Most slime types drop 1–2 Gel, with exceptions noted in the table below, and also have a very small chance of dropping a Slime Staff.
Slime Block: The Slime Block is a type of block crafted using the Solidifier. Walking or landing on Slime Blocks produces droplet particles.
Slime Block Wall: The Slime Block Wall is a type of Wall made from a Slime Block.
Slime Crown: The Slime Crown is a boss-summoning item that summons King Slime when used. It can be used in any biome at any time.

When thrown into Shimmer, the Slime Crown is consumed and the Slime Rain event begins immediately. If the event is already in progress, then the item merely sinks to the bottom of the Shimmer like all other non-decraftable items. If the Remix seed is active in the current world, the item will still be consumed, but the Slime Rain will not start.
Slime Gun: The Slime Gun is a tool that has a 2/3 (66.67%) chance of being dropped by King Slime. When used, it sprays an arc of slime which inflicts the Slime debuff on players, enemies, and NPCs for 3 seconds. Additionally, the slime turns on most light sources, as opposed to the stream of the Water Gun, which turns them off. The Slime Gun can be used limitlessly and does not consume any ammunition or mana.
The Slime Gun cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Slime Spear: The Slime Spear is a pre-Hardmode spear that inflicts the Slime debuff for 3 seconds on hit.
On Skyblock worlds, the Slime Spear deals only 9 base damage.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Slime Staff: The Slime Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Baby Slime minion. It bounces towards enemies, dealing contact damage.

The Slime Staff's drop rate from most slimes and Slimed Zombies is 1/10000 (0.01%) / 1/7000 (0.0143%). Pinky has a greatly increased drop rate of 1/100 (1%) / 1/70 (1.4286%), and King Slime holds the greatest drop rate of 1/30 (3.3333%). Additionally, Sand Slimes have a drop rate of 1/8000 (0.0125%) / 1/5600 (0.0179%). The slimes which cannot drop the Slime Staff are: Shimmer, Golden, Lava, Dungeon, Umbrella, Hoppin' Jack, Corrupt, Queen Slime, Crimslime, Gastropod and Rainbow.
Slime Whip: The Slime Whip is a pre-Hardmode whip. It has a 60% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
The whole whip inflicts the Slime debuff for 3 seconds, and the tip of the whip additionally inflicts the On Fire! debuff for 3–5 seconds.
On Skyblock worlds, the Slime Whip deals only 12 base damage.
Slimeling: The Slimeling is a Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in groups of two to three upon the death of a Corrupt Slime. Like its parent, it has a 1/4 (25%) chance of inflicting the Darkness debuff for 15 / 30 / 37.5 seconds.
Like most other slimes, the Slimeling will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Slimer: The Slimer is a Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in The Corruption and Underground Corruption. It spawns as a winged slime, attacking the player using the Bat AI pattern. Once "killed" for the first time, the slime body drops to the ground, continuing to fight using the Slime AI pattern.
Like most other slimes, the Slimer's both forms will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Slimy Saddle: The Slimy Saddle is a pre-Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a friendly Slime Mount. The Slime Mount offers increased jump height (21 tiles) and movement speed (20 mph), increases the maximum safe falling distance by 10 tiles, reduces fall damage by 50%, and enables floating on surfaces of all liquids and continuous auto-jump by holding the ↷ Jump key. Landing on an enemy while riding this mount will deal 40 summon damage and a knockback of 5 (Average), and causes the player to bounce off them. The Slime Mount is affected by summon damage bonuses.
The Slimy Saddle has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by King Slime and a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in King Slime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Sluggy: Sluggy is one of three critters that occasionally spawn in the Jungle or Underground Jungle biome when a player breaks a plant, the others being Grubby (more common) and Buggy (rarest). Sluggy has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Sluggy can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Sluggy Cage). Once crafted, Sluggy cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Sluggy can be used as bait for fishing, with 25% bait power.
Sluggy can be spawned by the Buggy Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Slush Block: Slush Blocks are blocks that appear naturally in Ice biomes. They are subject to gravity and will fall if the blocks supporting them are removed, dealing damage to any player or enemy they fall on (similar to Sand and Silt).

Slush can be placed in an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to be converted into various valuable materials, including gems, coins, ores, and very rarely, the Amber Mosquito pet summoning item.
Smoke Block: Smoke Blocks are animated background furniture blocks that can be purchased from the Party Girl for 1 Silver in Hardmode. When placed together, they will connect in a way that each block on the outer left and right sides visually take up half of a block. For example, if a player were to make a 3×3 arrangement of Smoke Blocks, the entire left and right columns of smoke will appear to be halved, resulting in a slimmer appearance.
Smoke Bomb: The Smoke Bomb is a consumable novelty item. When thrown, it continuously emits thick gray smoke and bounces or rolls until coming to a complete stop. It disappears 1 minute after being thrown, but can be removed early by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it. Smoke Bombs can be purchased from the Party Girl for 20 Copper each.
Smooth Granite Block: Smooth Granite Blocks are blocks with a dark blue appearance. The block can be crafted or found as walls in underground houses in Granite Caves. They can be used to craft the Granite furniture set.
Smooth Granite Wall: Smooth Granite Wall is a type of Wall that can be crafted with Smooth Granite Blocks.
Smooth Marble Block: The Smooth Marble Block is a smoother version of the Marble Block. It can be used to craft the Marble furniture set.
Smooth Marble Wall: Smooth Marble Walls are background walls made from Smooth Marble Blocks.
Smooth Sandstone: Smooth Sandstone is a type of block crafted from Sandstone Blocks. It can be used to craft the Sandstone furniture set.
Smooth Sandstone Wall: The Smooth Sandstone Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Smooth Sandstone Blocks. It is the only Sandstone Wall type not to generate naturally.
Smoothie of Darkness: The Smoothie of Darkness is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It can be considered the Corruption counterpart to the Bloody Moscato.
Snail: The Snail is a rather rare critter that spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, but not in Ice, Crimson, Corruption, or Hallow biomes. It can also spawn in front of unsafe Living Wood Walls below the surface at a much higher rate. The Snail has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Snail can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Snail Cage). Once crafted, the Snail cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Snail can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% bait power.
The Snail can be spawned by the Snail Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Snake Band: The Snake Band is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of dropping from Lamias in the Underground Desert. When equipped, every third attack with a whip causes the player to automatically perform an extra whip swing at the same time. If 2 seconds have passed since the last time the player used a whip, their next whip attack will also trigger the extra whip swing, and afterwards it will be triggered again on every third whip attack. If the player has only one tag effect slot, the extra swing will be performed with the same whip they are currently using. If the player has more than one tag effect slot, the extra swing will be performed with the next whip in the player's inventory (see Notes for more details). The extra whip swing only deals 30% of the whip's damage and 25% of its knockback, although its damage cannot be less than 3.
Snake Charmer's Flute: The Snake Charmer's Flute is a pre-Hardmode tool that places a pot from which a snake rises. Once the snake reaches its full height of 100 tiles or touches a block, it stops rising and becomes climbable like a rope. Blocks can also be placed next to the snake once it has fully extended. The snake and the pot disappear after 30 seconds, and also produce a small amount of light. The Snake Charmer's Flute can be found in Sandstone Chests in the top 4/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis.
Snapping Stone: The Snapping Stone is a pre-Hardmode accessory that has a 1/80 (1.25%) chance of dropping from Granite Golems and Granite Elementals.
When equipped, ranged hits are periodically boosted, and discharge damaging pulses on hit.
This effect has a cooldown of 6 seconds, indicated by faint blue light.
Boosted hits deal up to 60 additional base damage.
Pulses hit up to 2 additional targets nearby, dealing 30 base damage and a knockback of 5 (Average) to each target.
Snapthorn: The Snapthorn is a pre-Hardmode whip. It has a 40% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
Grants the Jungle's Fury buff, increasing whip speed by 12% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits.
Has a 1/5 (20%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff.
Snatcher: The Snatcher is a pre-Hardmode enemy found in the surface Jungle, and is nearly identical in appearance and behavior to the Underground Jungle's Man Eater. Snatchers spawn anchored to blocks, with an extendable stem topped by a pincher. The stem itself is a passive component and can be walked through safely without incurring damage; only the pincher inflicts or takes damage.
Sniper Rifle: The Sniper Rifle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance of being dropped by Skeleton Snipers in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires bullets at an extremely high damage and velocity, with a slow fire rate. It also converts Musket Balls and Tungsten Bullets into High Velocity Bullets, giving them the special effects but not affecting their damage. The Sniper Rifle has a base 29% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.

The Sniper Rifle also has a "zoom" ability activated by holding the ⚷ Open / Activate key (identical to that of the Binoculars and the Rifle Scope), allowing the screen to extend in the direction of the cursor.
Sniper Scope: The Sniper Scope is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory. It grants the following effects while equipped:
The ability to "zoom", increasing view range while holding a bullet-firing gun by pressing and holding ⚷ Open / Activate and moving the cursor.
Snow Balla: The Snow Balla is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Frost Legion event. It moves by hopping towards the player and throws snowballs at them which form Snow Blocks on impact with other blocks, similar to the attack of an Antlion. The Snow Blocks can also spawn in the air if the Snow Balla throws it into the sky.
Snow Block: Snow Blocks are blocks found naturally-placed in the Snow biome. Snow Blocks placed in the Surface layer, either naturally or by a player, will cause a snowfall effect. This is purely visual, and has no functional effects. Snow Blocks cannot be infected by The Hallow or evil biomes. Snow in any form cannot be melted into water, nor produced from water or Ice Blocks.
Snow blocks are also dropped by the Hardmode Frost Legion enemies, and its Snow Balla throws Snowballs that create further Snow blocks when impacting.
Snow Brick: Snow Bricks are bricks crafted from Snow Blocks. Placing snow bricks will cause snow to fall in the background and they count toward the qualifications for a Snow biome.
Snow Brick Wall: The Snow Brick Wall is a pre-Hardmode background wall.
Snow Cloud: Snow Cloud is a type of block that can be crafted at a Sky Mill from Cloud blocks in the Snow biome. Snow Cloud blocks cause purely decorative snowflakes to appear beneath them, continuing for about 8 tiles and then fading away for 5 more. Landing on Snow Clouds will not inflict fall damage.
In Drunk worlds, Snow Clouds are generated naturally as part of snow-themed Floating Islands.
Snow Flinx: The Snow Flinx is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Ice biome (another name for the Cavern layer Snow biome). It is susceptible to knockback, and when hit, will tumble over and fly backwards.
Snow Globe: The Snow Globe is a Hardmode event-summoning item used to summon the Frost Legion event. The player also must have at least 200 maximum health to initiate the event, but can then be used in any world at any time afterward. The Snow Globe has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being obtained from Presents (dropped during the Christmas event) opened specifically in Hardmode worlds.
Snow Hat: The Snow Hat is a vanity item dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode.
Snow Wall: The Snow Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Snow biome, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.
Snow armor: Snow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Snow Hood, Snow Coat, and Snow Pants. Each piece has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to be dropped by Frozen Zombies.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Immunity to the Chilled and Frozen debuffs
Snow armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Pink Snow armor, still providing the set bonus.
Snowball: The Snowball is a consumable ranged weapon that can be crafted from Snow Blocks. Snowballs can also be used as ammunition for the Snowball Cannon.
Snowball Cannon: The Snowball Cannon is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon which uses Snowballs as ammunition. The Snowball Cannon has a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen and Boreal Crates.
Snowball Launcher: The Snowball Launcher is a pre-Hardmode furniture item and placeable weapon that has a 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Snow Flinx. Once placed, interacting with it using the ⚒ Use / Attack button causes it to fire a Snowball that damages enemies, and holding the button will cause it to release a rapid fire of Snowballs with a spread of roughly 30°. The Snowball Launcher has a firing cooldown of 0.12 seconds, giving it a maximum fire rate of 8.57 Snowballs per second. Snowballs have a base damage of 35 and knockback of 3.5 (Weak). This is not affected by the default base damage (−1) or knockback (0) of the Snowball Launcher item.

The Snowball Launcher can also be triggered by wire. Depending on the lateral position of the connected wire within the sprite of the Snowball Launcher, it will either shoot a Snowball (with a cooldown of 0.17 seconds) or turn to the side the wire is on.
Snowfall Block: The Snowfall Block is an animated block type which shows falling snow. Like related blocks such as the Waterfall Block or Lavafall Block, it is one of the few items that uses the Crystal Ball as a crafting station.
Snowfall Wall: Snowfall Wall is one of only a few animated background walls. It depicts falling snow.
Snowman Cannon: The Snowman Cannon is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that is dropped from the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event with a 5.19%–10.37% (15.56%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave.. When used, it consumes rockets and fires homing snowman-shaped rockets that explode on impact with enemies.

For combat purposes, its best modifier is Unreal. For mining and usage of liquid rockets, its best modifier is Unreal on Desktop and Rapid elsewhere. This is due to differences in how use time is rounded between versions, with Unreal Snowman Cannon having a use time of 13 on vanilla desktop versions and 14 elsewhere.Verify
Snowman Gangsta: The Snowman Gangsta is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Frost Legion event. It moves by hopping toward the player while occasionally firing bullets at them at a slow rate, and can only shoot left or right.
Soaring Insignia: The Soaring Insignia is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that boosts the player's flight and movement abilities. It has the following effects:
Increases acceleration by 75%, from 0.3 tiles/second² to 0.525 tiles/second², grants infinite flight time, and increases jump speed by 1.8

Additionally, it increases flight ascent speed with wings or Rocket Boots. With the Soaring Insignia equipped, the player will reach maximum movement speed much quicker and will be able to stop, change directions, and go from flying upwards to falling or vice versa very quickly. The Soaring Insignia is always dropped from the Empress of Light's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
Sofas: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds.
As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5.

There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.
Solar Brick: The Solar Brick is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist brick that is crafted from Solar Fragments. It is one of the four Fragment Bricks, bricks which are crafted with Lunar Fragments. It glows when placed and can be used to craft Solar furniture.
Solar Brick Wall: Solar Brick Wall is a background wall made from Solar Bricks.
Solar Dye: Solar Dye is a Hardmode, endgame dye crafted from Solar Fragments dropped by the Solar Pillar from the Lunar Events. The dye gives a golden, metallic hue and a slight pulsating effect to anything used with it, similar to the Reflective Dyes obtainable from the Dye Trader's Strange Plants quest. Unlike the Metallic dyes, however, items dyed with Solar Dye do not appear to dynamically reflect light, and have the same appearance regardless of the player's proximity to light sources. Also unlike the metallic dyes, dyed items periodically glow (without casting light).
Solar Eruption: The Solar Eruption is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist melee weapon that swings a long whipsword from the player's position towards the cursor. The whipsword sweeps in a narrow arc of varying length before quickly retracting. It can pass through blocks and pierce infinitely. The whipsword creates a Solar Explosion upon hit, dealing damage and inflicting the Daybroken debuff for 5 seconds, which deals 100 damage per second.

Its best modifier is Ruthless. Since part of the Solar Eruption's damage output comes from the Solar Explosions which cannot critically hit, critical hit chance bonuses are less effective than direct increase in damage.
Solar Flare armor: Solar Flare armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord melee armor set consisting of the Solar Flare Helmet, Solar Flare Breastplate, and Solar Flare Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Solar Fragments.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

Grants the Solar Blaze buff, which builds the longer the player avoids taking damage, gaining up to a maximum of three charges. Each charge takes 3 seconds to build. The number of charges built is indicated by a shield that appears in front of the player, with two and three spikes appearing on the shield, corresponding with the charge count.
Taking damage depletes one charge and creates an explosion called Solar Radiance around the player.

While there is at least one charge built, the player can activate a special dash attack by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right key. Striking an enemy with the dash damages it and causes a damaging Solar Radiance explosion, so enemies always take damage twice. A Solar Blaze charge is consumed if at least one enemy was hit. The dash has a 1-second cooldown.

Furthermore, the Solar Blaze buff provides +20% damage reduction, regardless of the number of charges. Combined with the base damage reduction from the armor's set bonus, it grants a total of 29.6% damage reduction.

Each piece equipped (even if hidden by vanity items) causes the player to emit light, with a higher light level for each additional piece equipped. Additionally, equipping the full set causes the player to emit pulses and afterimages while moving.
Solar Fragment: The Solar Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist crafting material. It is one of the four Lunar Fragments, dropped from the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events in stacks of 12–60 / 24–100. Solar Fragments can be used to craft Solar Flare armor, an end-game armor set that benefits all types of melee weapons, as well as Solar-themed tools, weapons, wings, etc.

Crafting all items requires 121 Solar Fragments and 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite), which necessitates defeating the Solar Pillar at least 3–11 / 2–8 times (note that the Solar Fragment can also be crafted from the other fragments) and fighting the Moon Lord at least 4 / 3–4 times.
Solar Fragment Block: Solar Fragment Blocks are blocks made from Solar Fragments which are dropped by the Solar Pillar. The blocks have a crystal-like appearance with intense shades of yellow, red, and orange. They can be crafted with the Ancient Manipulator. Walls cannot be crafted with them.
Solar Pillar: The Celestial Pillars (also known as the Lunar Pillars, Lunar Towers, or Celestial Towers) are four late-Hardmode, stationary bosses that appear during the Lunar Events after the Lunatic Cultist has been defeated. To break their protective shields, 100 of the unique enemies that spawn in a large surrounding area must be defeated. Pillars drop Lunar Fragments when destroyed, and destroying all four of them results in the spawn of the Moon Lord.

The four Celestial Pillars are the Solar Pillar, the Vortex Pillar, the Nebula Pillar, and the Stardust Pillar. They represent the four damage types in Terraria: Solar for melee, Vortex for ranged, Nebula for magic, and Stardust for summon. After the defeat of the Lunatic Cultist, they appear at four locations equally spaced across the map (see pillar spawning mechanics below), and do not move apart from slowly bobbing up and down in place. Each pillar takes control of the world in a circular area around it with a radius of 250 tiles (500 feet). When the player is in that affected area, the background will change to a pillar-specific one, and only pillar-specific enemies will spawn in large numbers.

Initially, each Celestial Pillar has a large shield around it which prevents it from taking any damage. In order to remove the shield, the player must kill 100 enemies corresponding to that specific pillar, which are the major threat of the Lunar Events; they can deal high amounts of damage, inflict debuffs, and easily swarm the player if not dealt with quickly. The enemy kill count does not reset if the player dies, but leaving the world does reset it.

Defeating pillar-specific enemies releases small red energy particles that travel to the pillar shield to indicate the progress. Once the kill count of a pillar is reached, its shield is lowered and it becomes vulnerable to damage. The pillars themselves are fairly easy to defeat, being extremely large and immobile, and having only 20,000 health each and only fairly weak or no attacks. However, enemies continue to spawn even after the shield is lowered, until the pillar is defeated.
There is no set order in which the Celestial Pillars must be defeated. The following status messages will appear from whichever pillars are taken down first, second, third, and fourth:
First pillar defeated: "Your mind goes numb..."
Second pillar defeated: "You are overwhelmed with pain..."
Third pillar defeated: "Otherworldly voices linger around you..."
After defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar, the screen starts to vibrate and the music volume lowers before eventually going completely silent. After 60 seconds, the Moon Lord will spawn.
After defeating the Moon Lord, each pillar will only require 50 of their respective enemies killed to lower their shields instead of 100.
Solar Tablet: The Solar Tablet is a Hardmode event-summoning item used to summon a Solar Eclipse. It may only be used during the day (from 4:30 AM to 7:29 PM), causing the eclipse to begin immediately, regardless of the time. The eclipse lasts until 7:30 PM of the current day.

Solar Tablets have a 1/5 (20%) chance to be found in Lihzahrd Chests in the Jungle Temple. Additionally, Lihzahrds and Flying Snakes have a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of dropping 1–2 Solar Tablet Fragments, which can be used to craft a Solar Tablet.
Solar Tablet Fragment: The Solar Tablet Fragment is a post-Plantera Hardmode crafting material solely used to craft the Solar Tablet, which summons the Solar Eclipse event. Solar Tablet Fragments have a 4/5 (80%) chance of being found in Lihzahrd Chests, and also have a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Lihzahrds and Flying Snakes in the Jungle Temple.
Solidifier: The Solidifier is a crafting station used to craft Slime furniture, some miscellaneous blocks, and two weapons: the Slime Spear and Slime Whip. The Solidifier is always dropped by King Slime, and is also always placed on the starting island of a newly generated Skyblock world.
Solutions: Solutions are a type of ammunition used solely by the Clentaminator and Terraformer. Each solution will convert certain blocks and walls to other blocks and walls, creating and/or destroying different biomes in the process. There are 8 different solutions. 7 of them are sold by the Steampunker, who sells different solutions based on certain conditions, and one is sold by the Truffle, who always sells it.
Solutions cannot be purchased in worlds with the Remix special world seed active.
Sonar Potion: The Sonar Potion is a buff potion which grants the Sonar buff when consumed. The buff displays the name of a fishing catch above a fishing pole's bobber when it receives a bite while fishing, along with a sound effect. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
The Sonar Potion can be obtained both from crafting and as a reward from the Angler for completing fishing quests.
Sorcerer Emblem: The Sorcerer Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that increases magic damage by 15%. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop from the Wall of Flesh.
Soul of Flight: The Soul of Flight is a Hardmode crafting material used to craft several different types of wings and the Soul of Flight in a Bottle (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Souls of Flight are dropped by Wyverns and are the most common soul aside from the Souls of Light and Night.

Souls of Flight are dropped at the position of the Wyvern's head upon death, and like all other souls, float in midair at the drop point, rather than falling to the ground. This can make Souls of Flight more difficult to spot, e.g. if the Wyvern's head was off-screen or within blocks at the time of death.
Soul of Fright: The Soul of Fright is one of the six souls. It is a crafting material dropped by Skeletron Prime.
Soul of Light: Soul of Light is a Hardmode crafting material dropped by most enemies killed in the Underground Hallow (in the Cavern layer) with a 1/5 (20%) chance. This also includes enemies not native to the biome, such as Granite Elementals. See Notes for details.
Soul of Might: The Soul of Might is one of the six souls. It is a crafting material dropped by The Destroyer.
Soul of Night: Soul of Night is a Hardmode crafting material dropped by most enemies killed in the Cavern layer of an Underground Corruption or Underground Crimson biome with a 1/5 (20%) chance. This also includes enemies not native to the biome, such as normal cavern enemies, Underworld enemies, but not enemies spawned from statues. See Notes for details.
Soul of Sight: The Soul of Sight is one of the six souls that can be obtained in Hardmode. It is a crafting material dropped by The Twins.
Soulscourge: The Soulscourge is a pre-Hardmode whip. It has a 40% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Vasculash. Compared to Vasculash, the Soulscourge has 2 less base damage, slightly higher knockback, and 1 more tile of range.
Space Creature set: The Space Creature set is a vanity set consisting of the Space Creature Mask, Space Creature Shirt, and Space Creature Pants. Its male and female variants look identical. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to drop from Goodie Bags during Halloween.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Space Gun: The Space Gun is a pre-Hardmode magic gun. When used, it fires fast green lasers that can hit up to three enemies. The lasers will increase in damage, pierce, knockback and size (only visually) as they travel. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, the Space Gun costs no mana to use.
Spaghetti: The Spaghetti is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. Spaghetti has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Granite Elementals and Granite Golems. Statue-spawned Granite Golems do not drop it, as it is a food item.
Sparkle Slime Balloon: The Sparkle Slime Balloon is a Hardmode novelty consumable item. Upon colliding with solid blocks, it inflicts the Sparkle Slime debuff on players (including the user), enemies, critters, and NPCs within a radius of 9 tiles, causing them to become tinted purple and drip with pink and purple slime for 30 seconds. This debuff is only cosmetic and deals no damage.
The Diva Slime spawns and moves in after throwing or discarding a Sparkle Slime Balloon into Shimmer.
Queen Slime always drops 25–75 / 25–74 Sparkle Slime Balloons upon her defeat, and they are also dropped by Jungle Mimics, which spawn in Celebration Mk 10 and Zenith worlds.
Sparkling Honey: The Sparkling Honey is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Honey Bee pet, a large bee which follows the player around. The Sparkling Honey has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee in Master Mode.
Spazmatism: The Twins are a Hardmode mechanical boss which are essentially a more difficult version of the Eye of Cthulhu. The Twins are two separate flying entities, Retinazer and Spazmatism, connected by a tendril, each with its own attack pattern and health. Both must be killed in order to defeat the boss.
While The Twins are alive, their exclusive music The Twins will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Spear: The Spear is a pre-Hardmode spear that has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found in Wooden Chests that are located on the surface as well as in the underground layer.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Spear Trap: The Spear Trap is a trap found naturally in the Jungle Temple and, rarely, outside the Temple's door. When activated, it launches a spear in a straight line that can pierce an infinite number of targets and retracts upon hitting a solid block or reaching its maximum range of 19.5 tiles. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1.5 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 2 seconds between firings. The spear deals 120 / 240 / 360 damage to players (60 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters).
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Spear Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Unlike Lihzahrd Bricks, breaking Spear Traps does not require the Picksaw.
Spectre Bar: The Spectre Bar is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bar.
Spectre Boots: The Spectre Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory crafted from Rocket Boots and either Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots, Sailfish Boots (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), or Dunerider Boots (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and combines their functionality (except the faster speed on sand from Dunerider Boots).
They grant the following effects while equipped:
The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint.
Increased maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second).
The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual cloud trail.
Spectre Goggles: The Spectre Goggles are a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron accessory which allows the player to see Echo Blocks, Echo Platforms, Echo Walls, Ghostly Stinkbug Blockers, and tiles painted with Echo Coating while equipped. They are sold by the Cyborg and Mechanic for 10 Gold when they are spoken to in a Graveyard.
On the Invisible plane secret world seed, Spectre Goggles have a 1/25 (4%) of being obtained from any Chest.
Spectre Hamaxe: The Spectre Hamaxe is a Hardmode, post-Plantera hamaxe.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Spectre Paint Roller: The Spectre Paint Roller is a Hardmode tool which is used to paint walls, much like the regular Paint Roller sold by the Painter. The advantage over its predecessor is the Spectre Paint Roller's increased range of +3 tiles.
The Spectre Paint Roller cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Spectre Paint Scraper: The Spectre Paint Scraper is a Hardmode tool which is used to remove paint off tiles and walls, much like the regular Paint Scraper sold by the Painter. The advantage over its predecessor is the Spectre Paint Scraper's increased range of +3 tiles. Paint removed by a scraper can never be recovered.
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Like the Paint Scraper, the Spectre Paint Scraper can also collect moss.
The Spectre Paint Scraper cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Spectre Paintbrush: The Spectre Paintbrush is a Hardmode tool which is used to apply paint to tiles, much like the regular Paintbrush sold by the Painter. The advantage over its predecessor is the Spectre Paintbrush's increased range of +3 tiles.
The Spectre Paintbrush cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Spectre Pickaxe: The Spectre Pickaxe is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore. It also has a notably high range bonus of 3 blocks.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Spectre Staff: The Spectre Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that has a 1/20 (5%) / 39/400 (9.75%) chance of being dropped by Ragged Casters in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires a homing orb that pierces two enemies but cannot pass through blocks.
Spectre armor: Spectre armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic armor set consisting of the Spectre Robe and Spectre Pants, as well as two different headpieces: the Spectre Hood and Spectre Mask, providing offensive and defensive bonuses respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Spectre Bars (27 Ectoplasm and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all four pieces requires a total of 66 Spectre Bars (33 Ectoplasm and 330 Chlorophyte Ore).
Specular Fish: Specular Fish are a type of fish that are commonly found by fishing in a Forest or Snow biome in the Underground, Cavern, and Underworld layers. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners, Recall Potions, and Wormhole Potions.
Spell Tome: The Spell Tome is a Hardmode crafting material that is purchased from the Wizard for 5 Gold.
Spelunker Glowstick: The Spelunker Glowstick is a consumable light source that can be held or tossed a fair distance, similar to the regular Glowstick. In addition, it highlights the location of nearby treasures in a 30-tile radius around the Glowstick with a slight yellowish glimmer. It has a shorter lifetime, expiring after only 2 minutes. Spelunker Glowsticks can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 1 Silver 50 Copper each at nighttime. During a full moon, they can also be purchased at daytime.
Spelunker Potion: The Spelunker Potion is a buff potion which grants the Spelunker buff when consumed. The buff illuminates valuable nearby objects and highlights them with a yellow tint. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
The Spelunker buff highlights the following:
In addition to being crafted, Spelunker Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Spicy Pepper: The Spicy Pepper is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking an Ash tree.
Spider Boulder: The Spider Boulder is a special type of Boulder. It acts identically to the Boulder, with the exception of placing Cobwebs while moving and spawning Wall Creepers upon breaking. It generates near Spider Nests.
Spider Egg: The Spider Egg is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Spider to follow the player around. The Pet Spider climbs on background walls and has similar behavior to the Spider AI. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Pet Spider rides on a white spiderweb, as if it were standing on a wall, to keep up with the player. The Spider Egg is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave.
Spider Fang: The Spider Fang is a Hardmode crafting material dropped by Black Recluses in Spider Nests with a 1/2 (50%) / 9/10 (90%) chance. It can be used to craft several minion-related items and armor.
Spider Nest Block: Spider Nest Blocks are Hardmode blocks crafted from one Spider Fang and 10 Cobwebs at a Work Bench. They are used to craft Spider furniture and Spider Nest Walls.
Crafting all items requires 153 Spider Nest Blocks.
Spider Nest Wall: Spider Nest Walls are a type of wall. As with most placed walls, they are compatible with NPC housing and will prevent enemies from spawning.
Spider Staff: The Spider Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Spider minion. It runs towards enemies and latches onto them, repeatedly dealing damage while latched and inflicting the Acid Venom debuff for 2–4 seconds. It can climb background walls and jump high.
Spider Wall: The Spider Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Spider Nests, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed and can only be obtained on Desktop, Console, and Mobile, via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

The Infested Spider Wall (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is an item that places an unsafe Spider Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Spider Wall into Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Unsafe Spider Walls will create Cobwebs in front of them over time, serving as a renewable source for the item. These Cobwebs only have a 1/4 (25%) chance to yield a Cobweb item when destroyed.
Spider armor: Spider armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Spider Mask, Spider Breastplate, and Spider Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 36 Spider Fangs.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Spiffo Plush: The Spiffo Plush is a pet-summoning item that spawns Spiffo to follow the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, Spiffo twirls its tail like a propeller to fly towards them. The Spiffo Plush has a 1/1500 (0.07%) chance of being dropped by Zombies, Frozen Zombies, and Raincoat Zombies.
Spike: The Spike is a trap that can be found in the Dungeon. Upon contact, it deals 60 damage to the player, on all difficulties, and inflicts the Bleeding debuff for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds. It can be broken with a pickaxe, drill, or explosives.
Spikes cannot be destroyed by explosives when the For the Worthy seed is active.
Spike Block: Spike Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks crafted from Stone Blocks and Spikes at a Work Bench. Their main use is crafting Spike furniture, Sharp Spike Blocks and Spike Walls. With the exception of Sharp Spike Blocks, these do not damage the player.
Spike Wall: Spike Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Spike Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.
Spiked Ice Slime: The Spiked Ice Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Ice biome. The Spiked Ice Slime fires Ice Spikes at the player, and the Ice Spikes and the slime itself always inflict the Chilled debuff, and also have a smaller chance to inflict the Frozen debuff.

In Classic Mode, the Spiked Ice Slime only fires one Ice Spike at a time, approximately every 1.5 seconds. In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), however, it shoots 6–8 Ice Spikes around itself in a short range.
Like most other slimes, the Spiked Ice Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Spiked Jungle Slime: The Spiked Jungle Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Underground Jungle. It fires Jungle Spikes at the player which have a chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff. In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), it can also fire five Jungle Spikes at once around itself in a short range.
Like most other slimes, the Spiked Jungle Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Spiky Ball: The Spiky Ball is a consumable ranged weapon that is primarily used as a passive trap by tossing it to the ground, where enemies who pass over it will take damage up to 7 times (after which the Spiky Balls vanish). If not destroyed, it will automatically vanish after 1 minute 20 seconds but can be removed early by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it. It can also be directly thrown at enemies, but it has a very short arc and quickly falls to the ground. Spiky Balls have a 199/400 (49.75%) chance of being dropped by all goblins during the Goblin Army event (except for the Goblin Warlock), and can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 80 Copper each.
The Goblin Tinkerer uses Spiky Balls to defend himself against nearby enemies.
Spiky Ball Trap: The Spiky Ball Trap is a type of trap that can be found naturally in the Jungle Temple and, rarely, outside the Temple's door. When activated, it dispenses orange spiky balls that bounce several times. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 4 seconds between activations. The spiky balls deal 80 / 160 / 240 damage to players (40 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters).
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Spiky Ball Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer. The total number of spiky balls spawned at once is limited. See below for details.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Unlike Lihzahrd Bricks, breaking Spiky Ball Traps does not require the Picksaw.
Spinal Tap: The Spinal Tap is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron whip. It has a 10% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
Spirit Flame: The Spirit Flame is a Hardmode magic weapon that causes a small purple flame to appear in a random location around the player and hovers in midair when used. When an enemy comes within 25 tiles and has a clear line of sight to the flame, it will home in on that enemy. Upon impact with any enemy or block, it will cause a small explosion, dealing splash damage. The Spirit Flame can be used repeatedly to summon multiple flames, and the flames dissipate if no target is acquired within 4 seconds of casting.
Splinterling: The Splinterling is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during wave 2 of the Pumpkin Moon event. It is one of the only sources of Spooky Wood, the other being the Mourning Wood.
Defeating a Splinterling during the Pumpkin Moon event will add 2 / 4 / 5 points to the final score.
The Splinterling requires 150 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Sponges: Sponges are tools used to erase liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on them. This causes the liquid to disappear from the environment without storing it. There are four different types of sponges:
Super Absorbant Sponge for absorbing water and Shimmer
Lava Absorbant Sponge for absorbing lava
Honey Absorbant Sponge for absorbing honey
Ultra Absorbant Sponge for absorbing all kinds of liquid
Attempting to use a sponge on a different type of liquid has no effect.

Sponges can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at draining liquids when compared to using a standard Empty Bucket (especially when moving the cursor around while draining).
Spooky Twig: The Spooky Twig is a Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting material used solely for crafting Spooky Wings. It is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave.
Spooky Wood: Spooky Wood is a type of wood dropped by Splinterlings and Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event. It is used to craft Halloween-themed furniture and Spooky armor.
Spooky Wood Wall: Spooky Wood Wall is a type of background Wall that resembles Wood Wall in texture, but tinted purple. It can be crafted from Spooky Wood.
Spooky armor: Spooky armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summoner armor set consisting of the Spooky Helmet, Spooky Breastplate, and Spooky Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 750 Spooky Wood.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
A visual glowing effect around the player.
Spore Bat: The Spore Bat is a pre-Hardmode bat enemy that spawns in underground Glowing Mushroom biomes. It has the same stats as a Cave Bat. However, Spore Bats have a chance to drop a Shroomerang. In Expert Mode, it can inflict the Feral Bite debuff for 30–90 seconds.
Spore Sac: The Spore Sac is a Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from Plantera's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.
