While equipped, it continuously spawns multiple floating Spore Traps around the player, which will slowly home in on enemies. The Spore Traps can pass through blocks and deal 70 classless damage and a knockback of 1.5 (Extremely weak) upon hitting enemies, and inflict the Poisoned debuff for 5–10 seconds. After hitting a target, each Spore Trap turns into a Spore Gas cloud, which lingers for a short duration and repeatdely deals 70 classless damage, but does not inflict knockback or the Poisoned debuff.
Spore Traps can only spawn near blocks or on background walls, up to 25 tiles away from the player. Without background walls to spawn on, Spore Traps can spawn up to about 3 tiles away from blocks.
Spore Skeleton: The Spore Skeleton is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in Underground Glowing Mushroom biomes, specficially within the Cavern layer. Its behavior, drops, and statistics are all equivalent to normal Skeletons.
Spore Zombie: The Spore Zombie is a zombie variant that only appears on Mushroom Grass above the Surface at any point in the game. It acts the same as normal zombies, slowly walking towards the player to deal contact damage, while attempting to navigate around obstacles. However, it is differentiable by normal zombies due to its mushroom-covered appearance, spawning at any time of day, and generally more powerful stats. Unlike normal zombies, it is always able to open doors regardless of whether or not it is a Blood Moon.
Spore Zombies can appear in two different variations with slightly different stats. Unlike normal zombies, it does not have an armed variation in Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Squid: The Squid is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Ocean. When underwater, it attacks by propelling itself towards the player in short bursts. If led out of the water, it will be unable to move or pursue the player in any way. When killed, it always drops Black Ink, which is used solely to craft Black Dye at a Dye Vat.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Squire Slime: Town Slimes are a type of town pet. There are 8 different Town Slimes and all of them can exist at the same time (unlike the different breeds of the Town Bunny, Town Cat, and Town Dog).

Almost all types of Town Slimes are acquired via some form of transformation, similar to the Tax Collector. Afterwards, the transformed Town Slime will move into a vacant house if one is available. If it is killed, it will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house. The initial transformation does not need to be repeated.

Town Slimes can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). They may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for their home tile (standing point).
Squire armor: Squire armor is a Hardmode melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Squire's Great Helm, Squire's Plating, and Squire's Greaves. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 45 Defender Medals after defeating any mechanical boss.
The Valhalla Knight armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Squire armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Ballista sentry summons have increased projectile velocity and increased pierce (3 to 6)
Upon taking damage, grants the Ballista Panic! buff for 5 seconds, increasing the fire rate (from 3.1 seconds to 1.43 seconds) of all Ballista sentries summoned by the player.
Squire's Shield: The Squire's Shield is a shield accessory that increases the player's sentry slots by one and increases summon damage by 10%. It is dropped by the Dark Mage with a 1/4 (25%) / 1/2 (50%) chance.
Squirrel: The Squirrel and Red Squirrel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are critters that spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Squirrel / Red Squirrel Cage). Once crafted, the Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Squirrels can be spawned by the Squirrel Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Squirrel to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Squirrel Hook: The Squirrel Hook is a pre-Hardmode grappling hook that fires a single hook that reaches 19 tiles, and functions similarly to other hooks with the unique ability to grapple and attach to the trunks of trees and Giant Glowing Mushrooms.

The Squirrel Hook can be purchased from the Zoologist for 2 Gold after filling out at least 10% (55 entries) of the Bestiary. Therefore, it is normally always available for purchase, since the Zoologist does not appear before the Bestiary has been filled to at least 10%. The only exception is the secret world seed Vampirism, where she is the starting NPC.
Squirrels: The Squirrel and Red Squirrel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are critters that spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Squirrel / Red Squirrel Cage). Once crafted, the Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Squirrels can be spawned by the Squirrel Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Squirrel to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Sroller: The Sroller is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events. It can curl into a ball, start spinning and hurls itself at the player, gaining increased defense and dealing high contact damage, similarly to a Giant Tortoise or Ice Tortoise. The Sroller can also create explosions on impact with blocks, dealing even higher area of effect damage.
Staff of Earth: The Staff of Earth is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When used, it fires a Boulder that is affected by gravity, bounces off blocks and rolls on the ground, and can pierce enemies five times, before dissipating on the sixth hit. The Boulder's base damage and knockback depend on its velocity. The Staff of Earth also has a base 24% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.
Staff of Regrowth: The Staff of Regrowth is a multi-function tool that can be found in Ivy Chests, Jungle Crates, and Bramble Crates. It has the following functions:
It grows Grass on Dirt Blocks, without consuming Grass Seeds.
When swung, it breaks directly-targeted vegetation only.
It only harvests blooming herbs, and Smart Cursor only targets blooming herbs. Even when they are directly targeted, it will not break immature herbs, nor harvest non-blooming mature herbs.
It increases the yield of harvested herbs and seeds.
It automatically replants herbs harvested from Planter Boxes and Clay Pots, without consuming seeds.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Staff of the Frost Hydra: The Staff of the Frost Hydra is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons the Frost Hydra sentry. It fires Frost Blasts towards enemies, which pierce twice and inflict the Frostbite debuff.
The Staff of the Frost Hydra is always found in the Dungeon's Ice Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Frozen Key after Plantera has been defeated.
Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 164% (including whip bonuses) or 64% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.
Stained Glass: Stained Glass are a group of walls made from combining gems with Glass Walls. They work like the normal Glass Wall besides changing the color of the sunlight to match that of the stained glass. Multicolored Stained Glass causes sunlight to shift through the color spectrum in a similar manner to Rainbow Brick, although dimmer.
Stake Launcher: The Stake Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera repeater that consumes Stakes as ammunition. When used, it fires Stakes that pierce nine enemies, are unaffected by gravity, and have a higher velocity than most arrows. The Stake Launcher applies a 10% damage penalty to the next hit for each enemy pierced. The Stake Launcher has a base 14% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.

The Stake Launcher is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Stake Launcher is always accompanied by 30 to 60 Stakes. Additional Stakes are sold by the Witch Doctor and Arms Dealer for 15 Copper each while the Stake Launcher is in the player's inventory.
Stalker's Quiver: The Stalker's Quiver is a Hardmode accessory that combines the effects of the Magic Quiver with the aggro-reducing effect of the Putrid Scent.
Star Anise: The Star Anise is a consumable ranged weapon, similar to Shurikens although slightly stronger. It can hit up to 6 targets. 20–40 can drop from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a 6.301% chance in pre-Hardmode and a 5.881% chance in Hardmode.
Star Cannon: The Star Cannon is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that consumes and fires Fallen Stars. The projectiles are not affected by gravity, pierce an infinite amount of enemies, and dissipate after 1 minute or upon impact with a block.
Star Cell: The Star Cell is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Stardust Pillar during the Lunar Events. It floats slowly towards the player but can move at a faster rate if the player begins moving away from it.

Upon death, it splits into multiple Mini Star Cells. If these Mini Star Cells are not dealt with, they will grow into a full-sized Star Cell, that can also split into more Mini Star Cells. Mini Star Cells do not contribute to the kill count required to break the Stardust Pillar's shield, though after growing back, they do.
Star Cloak: The Star Cloak is a Hardmode accessory that causes three stars to fall around the player whenever the player takes damage. It consumes no mana. The stars pass through blocks until reaching the player's altitude, at which point they continue falling until hitting blocks. They can pierce once, dissipating on the second hit.

The stars deal 75 / 150 / 225 damage which is not classified as any of the four damage types and therefore cannot be modified by any buffs or equipment. Furthermore, the stars have 25 armor penetration.
Star Cloud: Star Cloud is a block that functions like the Cloud. It can be crafted or found as the base of Floating Islands on specific secret world seeds. At night, Star Cloud blocks cause purely decorative star particles to shoot off above them. It glows in the dark when placed. Its particles also emit light.
Star Fruit: The Star Fruit is a Hardmode food and fruit item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Pearlwood tree or Pearlwood Palm tree.
Star Hairpin: The Star Hairpin is a vanity item that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold. It is worn in the helmet slot.
Star Princess set: The Star Princess set is a vanity set consisting of the Star Princess Crown and Star Princess Dress.

These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum (set), and is always sold along with the Celestial Wand.
Star Royale Brick: Star Royale Brick is a type of decorative brick obtained by throwing Luminite Brick into Shimmer during a Waxing Crescent.
Star Royale Brick Wall: Star Royale Brick Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Star Royale Bricks.
Star Veil: The Star Veil is a Hardmode accessory that combines the functions of the Star Cloak and the Cross Necklace, spawning falling star projectiles and increasing the length of the invincibility frames granted when the player is hurt.
Star Wrath: The Star Wrath is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When swung, it causes three pink stars to fall toward the cursor. The stars can pierce one enemy and pass through blocks until they are at the cursor's altitude or less than 12.5 tiles above the player's center, after which they will dissipate upon contact with a block.
Star in a Bottle: The Star in a Bottle is a functional lantern that grants the Star in a Bottle buff, providing mana regeneration of 5 mana per second to all players within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles.
Like other lanterns, the Star in a Bottle is a mechanism that can be toggled on or off if wired, though this does not affect the buff.
Starcrash: The Starcrash is a pre-Hardmode whip. It has a 30% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

Marks enemies with primed energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by the Starcrash, a meteor is summoned above the enemy and falls upon it, dealing 1.33× the damage from the minion or sentry's attack to enemies within a 4×4-tile area. The mark is only applied to the first enemy hit by each swing, and the meteor effect only triggers once per mark (the regular tag damage is not limited by this effect).
Stardrop: The Stardrop is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Junimo that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Junimo twirls the leaf on its head like a propeller to fly after them. The Stardrop can be obtained by holding a Joja Cola, talking to the Dryad, and selecting her “Purify” option. After a short animation sequence, the Stardrop is dropped on the ground.
Stardust Brick: The Stardust Brick is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist brick that is crafted from Stardust Fragments. It is one of the four Fragment Bricks, bricks which are crafted with Lunar Fragments. It glows when placed and can be used to craft Stardust furniture.
Stardust Brick Wall: Stardust Brick Wall is a background wall made from Stardust Bricks.
Stardust Cell Staff: The Stardust Cell Staff is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist summon weapon that summons a Stardust Cell minion. It hovers near enemies, firing a homing mini-cell that attaches itself to the target, inflicting the Celled debuff to deal 20 damage per second (20 damage displayed every 1 second). A maximum of 10 mini-cells can be attached to one target at a time, for a total of 200 damage per second (200 damage displayed every 1 second). The Stardust Cell will teleport to enemies out of range.
Stardust Dragon Staff: The Stardust Dragon Staff is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist summon weapon that summons a Stardust Dragon minion. It flies towards enemies, dealing contact damage and dashing to catch up with its target. It can move through and target enemies through blocks.

When the Stardust Dragon Staff is used more than once, multiple Stardust Dragons do not spawn; instead, the existing Stardust Dragon becomes longer and stronger for each additional summon. This damage scaling mechanic also affects the inital summon, causing it to have 69% more damage than what is listed in the tooltip. Each summon after the first provides an additional 46% of the tooltip's damage. At base values this means it would deal 67 damage with +18/+19 per extra summon.

Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach a certain threshold (including whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless. The exact threshold varies depending on the number of summons, which is listed in Notes below.
Stardust Dye: Stardust Dye is a Hardmode, endgame dye crafted using Stardust Fragments obtained from the Stardust Pillar from the Lunar Events. It gives a fade bluish-white color, and it gives a white sparkling effect on the dyed armor pieces and accessories.
Stardust Fragment: The Stardust Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist crafting material. It is one of the four Lunar Fragments, dropped from the Stardust Pillar during the Lunar Events in stacks of 12–60 / 24–100. Stardust Fragments can be used to craft Stardust armor, an end-game armor set that benefits all types of summon weapons, as well as Stardust-themed tools, weapons, wings, etc.

Crafting all items requires 139 Stardust Fragments and 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite), which necessitates defeating the Stardust Pillar at least 3–11 / 2–8 times (note that the Stardust Fragment can also be crafted from the other fragments) and fighting the Moon Lord at least 4 / 3–4 times.
Stardust Fragment Block: Stardust Fragment Blocks are blocks made from Stardust Fragments which are dropped by the Stardust Pillar. The blocks have a crystal-like appearance with intense shades of blue and yellow. They can be crafted at the Ancient Manipulator. Walls cannot be crafted with them.
Stardust Pillar: The Celestial Pillars (also known as the Lunar Pillars, Lunar Towers, or Celestial Towers) are four late-Hardmode, stationary bosses that appear during the Lunar Events after the Lunatic Cultist has been defeated. To break their protective shields, 100 of the unique enemies that spawn in a large surrounding area must be defeated. Pillars drop Lunar Fragments when destroyed, and destroying all four of them results in the spawn of the Moon Lord.

The four Celestial Pillars are the Solar Pillar, the Vortex Pillar, the Nebula Pillar, and the Stardust Pillar. They represent the four damage types in Terraria: Solar for melee, Vortex for ranged, Nebula for magic, and Stardust for summon. After the defeat of the Lunatic Cultist, they appear at four locations equally spaced across the map (see pillar spawning mechanics below), and do not move apart from slowly bobbing up and down in place. Each pillar takes control of the world in a circular area around it with a radius of 250 tiles (500 feet). When the player is in that affected area, the background will change to a pillar-specific one, and only pillar-specific enemies will spawn in large numbers.

Initially, each Celestial Pillar has a large shield around it which prevents it from taking any damage. In order to remove the shield, the player must kill 100 enemies corresponding to that specific pillar, which are the major threat of the Lunar Events; they can deal high amounts of damage, inflict debuffs, and easily swarm the player if not dealt with quickly. The enemy kill count does not reset if the player dies, but leaving the world does reset it.

Defeating pillar-specific enemies releases small red energy particles that travel to the pillar shield to indicate the progress. Once the kill count of a pillar is reached, its shield is lowered and it becomes vulnerable to damage. The pillars themselves are fairly easy to defeat, being extremely large and immobile, and having only 20,000 health each and only fairly weak or no attacks. However, enemies continue to spawn even after the shield is lowered, until the pillar is defeated.
There is no set order in which the Celestial Pillars must be defeated. The following status messages will appear from whichever pillars are taken down first, second, third, and fourth:
First pillar defeated: "Your mind goes numb..."
Second pillar defeated: "You are overwhelmed with pain..."
Third pillar defeated: "Otherworldly voices linger around you..."
After defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar, the screen starts to vibrate and the music volume lowers before eventually going completely silent. After 60 seconds, the Moon Lord will spawn.
After defeating the Moon Lord, each pillar will only require 50 of their respective enemies killed to lower their shields instead of 100.
Stardust armor: Stardust armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord armor set consisting of the Stardust Helmet, Stardust Plate, and Stardust Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Stardust Fragments.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

Summons a Stardust Guardian minion that floats behind the player. It is passive until an enemy is within a 30-tile radius from the player. It will then quickly charge through blocks towards the enemy, striking rapidly with punches that each deal 50 base summon damage. The Stardust Guardian will return behind the player once no enemies are within range.
The Stardust Guardian is affected by summon damage bonuses, including those from whips.
Starfury: The Starfury is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being found inside Skyware Chests on Floating Islands, as well as a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Sky Crates and Azure Crates. When swung, it occasionally summons a star projectile that falls from the sky to the cursor. The star deals 150% of the weapon's damage (37 base damage) and pierces once before dissipating on the second hit, but inflicts no knockback. The star will pass through all blocks until it reaches the lowest empty space at or above the cursor, after which it will break on the next block it hits.
Stargazer: The Stargazer is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Stardust Pillar during the Lunar Events. It walks slowly until it is within the line-of-sight of the player, at which point it stops in place, and fires a large Stardust Laser from its chest towards the player that lingers for a short while. The laser momentarily appears as a harmless thin beam, before quickly widening and damaging the player.
Starlight: The Starlight is a Hardmode, post-Plantera shortsword that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light. When used, it rapidly emits short-range light beams that pierce infinitely. It also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Static Hook: The Static Hook is a Hardmode grappling hook that fires up to two hooks which can be launched simultaneously, reaching up to 37.5 tiles (the longest reach of any hook). The Static Hook can be purchased from the Steampunker for 50 Gold.

When a hook latches onto a block, the player will be immediately suspended at their current location, unaffected by gravity, momentum, or knockback. If a second hook is fired while in this state, the player will stay attached to the first until the second hook attaches, and will not move or fall by any means. Players can use the movement keys to retract or extend the hook manually, up to its full range. Movement keys correspond with direction, so pressing ▲ Up while directly under the grappling hook will move the player upwards, whereas pressing ◀ Left or ▶ Right will not move the player at all in this case.
Statue (enemy): The Statue is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron enemy that spawns in Graveyard biomes. It is more likely to spawn around players with negative luck. It will spawn and act as a random Statue until approached, where it will shriek and start to pursue the player by aggressively stomping towards them, even going through blocks to reach them if needed. It will drop the statue it appears as on death.
If its current targeting player is dead, the Statue will laugh.
The Statue requires 10 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry, as opposed to the usual 50 kills. Unlike most enemies, it does not have a corresponding banner.
Statues: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them.
There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.
Steak: The Steak is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Steak has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by The Possessed, and a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Undead Miners.
Steampunk Boiler: The Steampunk Boiler is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Steampunk furniture out of Cogs. The Steampunk Boiler can be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold, once the Eye of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu and Skeletron have been defeated.
Steampunk Goggles: The Steampunk Goggles are a vanity item sold from the Steampunker for 3 Gold during the Halloween seasonal event.
Steampunk set: The Steampunk set is a Hardmode vanity set which consists of the Steampunk Hat, Steampunk Shirt, and Steampunk Pants. It is purchased from the Steampunker for 4 Gold 50 Silver (set), during the full and waning moon phases.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Steampunker: The Steampunker is a Hardmode NPC vendor who sells the Clentaminator, various furniture crafting stations, and other steampunk-themed items. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
One of the mechanical bosses (The Twins, The Destroyer, or Skeletron Prime) have been defeated.
The Steampunker will attack nearby enemies using a Clockwork Assault Rifle and High Velocity Bullets for defense.
Stellar Tune: The Stellar Tune is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic weapon that fires pairs of star-shaped projectiles that travel in a wave-like pattern toward the cursor and home in on enemies, travel through solid blocks, and explode in a small radius upon impact. Star projectiles will have their damage reduced by 25% (down to 63 base damage) when the line of sight between the player and the projectiles' point of impact is obstructed. It also plays an acoustic guitar chord when fired based on the distance between the player and the cursor (in a similar fashion to the Magical Harp). There are a total of six chords, and each one spans about a four-block distance from the player, except for the last one, which is played at a distance of 21 blocks or more.

The distance from the player to the cursor also controls the speed at which projectiles are fired. However, if the star projectiles are seeking an enemy, they will instead determine their speed based on the distance between them and their target. The Stellar Tune also has a base 24% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. The Stellar Tune has a 1/50 (2%) / 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light.
Step Stool: The Step Stool is a pre-Hardmode accessory. While equipped, holding ▲ Up while stationary extends the Step Stool, granting the following effects:
+2 upwards placement range (does not affect downwards range at all)
Increased hitbox, meaning anything that deals damage that touches the Step Stool will damage the player.

The Step Stool has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found inside surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. It can also be purchased for 2 Gold 50 Silver from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waning Crescent.
Sticky Bomb: The Sticky Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Bomb, but sticks onto any block on contact. If the block it sticks to is removed by some means, it will fall until it hits another.
Sticky Dirt Bomb: The Sticky Dirt Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Dirt Bomb, but sticks onto any block on contact. If the block it sticks to is removed by some means, it will fall until it hits another.
Sticky Dynamite: Sticky Dynamite is an explosive that functions like Dynamite, but sticks onto any block on contact. If the block it sticks to is removed by some means, it will fall until it hits another.
Sticky Glowstick: The Sticky Glowstick is a consumable light source that behaves identically to the standard Glowstick, but sticks to any surface on contact, rather than ricocheting or rolling. After being thrown, a Sticky Glowstick will emit light for 5 minutes and expire afterward. Sticky Glowsticks can be crafted, and are sometimes dropped by Pots in the Underground Snow biome.
Sticky Grenade: The Sticky Grenade is an explosive consumable ranged weapon. It can be made by combining Grenades with Gel. Like the Sticky Bomb, it will not roll, and will instead stick to the first block it touches until it explodes.
Like normal Grenades, they will detonate upon touching an enemy, or the player that threw it.
Sticky Power Bomb: The Sticky Power Bomb is a Hardmode explosive that functions like the Power Bomb, but sticks onto any block on contact. If the block it sticks to is removed by some means, it will fall until it hits another.
Stinger: The Stinger is a crafting material used in various Jungle-themed crafting recipes. It is obtained from Spiked Jungle Slimes, Hornets, and Moss Hornets found in the Underground Jungle biome.
Excluding the consumable items, crafting all items requires 58 Stingers.
Stinger Necklace: The Stinger Necklace is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is obtainable after defeating the Queen Bee. This item combines the Shark Tooth Necklace and the Honey Comb accessories, giving the player 5 armor penetration as well as releasing 1–3 / 1–4 bees when the wearer takes damage and granting the Honey buff for 5 seconds.
Stink Potion: The Stink Potion is a thrown potion that functions similarly to Thrown Waters. Upon colliding with solid blocks, it inflicts the Stinky debuff on players (including the user), enemies, critters, and NPCs within a radius of 9 tiles.
Its counterpart is the Love Potion.
Stinkbug: The Stinkbug is a harmless critter which spawns on the surface. The Stinkbug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Stinkbug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Stinkbug Cage). Once crafted, the Stinkbug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Stinkbug can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% bait power.
Stinkbugs can also be used to craft the Flymeal and Stinkbug Blockers.
Stinkbug Blockers: The Stinkbug Blocker and Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker are furniture items. When placed in a valid house, they will prevent NPCs from moving in.

The Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker is completely invisible when placed and can only been seen if the player has the Spectre Goggles equipped or if they are near an activated Echo Chamber, similar to Echo Blocks.
Stinkfish: Stinkfish are a type of fish which are found rarely by fishing in any biome in the Underground layer or below, with the exception of The Corruption, The Hallow and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) the Desert. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Stink Potions.
Stockade Crate: The Stockade Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Dungeon after Skeletron has been defeated. Opening Stockade or Dungeon Crates is the only way to obtain the Golden Lock Box, and therefore any Dungeon-exclusive items normally found in Locked Gold Chests, once the Dungeon has been fully looted. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Dungeon Crate.
Stone Accent Slab: The Stone Accent Slab is a block which is visually identical to the Stone Slab, except that it does not blend with any blocks other than itself and Smooth Marble Blocks.
Stone Block: The Stone Block is a type of block that is generated naturally in very large parts of the world. The majority of the Underground and Cavern layers is comprised of Stone Blocks. As a crafting ingredient, they are vital early in the game to craft the Furnace and Wooden Arrows.

After Hardmode is activated in a world, nearby Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed blocks can spread through Stone Blocks, changing them into Ebonstone, Crimstone, or Pearlstone, respectively. All three types can also be transformed back into ordinary Stone via Purification Powder or Green Solution used by the Clentaminator.
Stone Blocks can be found with moss growing on them, and it can be placed on them manually. Gemcorns can only be planted on Stone Blocks.
Rock Golems and gem trees drop Stone Blocks, making them a renewable source of Stone Blocks.
Stone Slab: The Stone Slab is a block similar in appearance to regular stone, but smoother, and the texture is made up of much larger bricks. It is extremely easy to produce, although it requires a Heavy Assembler which cannot easily be obtained very early on. Stone Slabs are more efficient to build with than Gray Bricks due to their recipe.
Stone Slab Wall: Stone Slab Wall is a background wall that can be used for housings.
Stone Wall: Stone Wall is a background wall made from Stone Blocks. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player, meaning it can stop enemies from spawning and is suitable for NPC housing.
Stopwatch: The Stopwatch is an informational accessory that displays the player's current movement speed in miles per hour, e.g. "34 mph".
The Stopwatch can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold.
Storm Diver: The Storm Diver is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Vortex Pillar during the Lunar Events. Storm Divers wield a type of ranged weapon that is able to fire tight spreads of projectiles, similar to the Tactical Shotgun. Storm Divers are also able to glide and hover with what appear to be jetpacks. They appear to have mud-colored skin, a green glass helmet, cyan-colored claws, cyan lights, and an alien-like shotgun.
Storm Spear: The Storm Spear is a pre-Hardmode spear that can be found in Sandstone Chests in the lower 3/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis. When thrust, it fires an electric bolt that deals 160% of the weapon's damage (21 base damage) and inflicts 50% its knockback (base knockback of 3 (Very weak)). The bolt does not pierce enemies and cannot pass through blocks.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Strange Brew: The Strange Brew is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant during certain moon phases for 5 Silver. When used, it restores 70–120 health, inflicts 40–70 seconds of Potion Sickness, and has a 3/5 (60%) chance to grant up to 4 seconds of invincibility. The duration of Potion Sickness can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.
Strange Glowing Mushroom: The Strange Glowing Mushroom is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Truffle that follows the player. The Baby Truffle emits a small amount of blue light similar to Glowing Mushrooms. The Strange Glowing Mushroom can be purchased from the Truffle for 45 Gold.
Strange Plant: Strange Plants are Hardmode quest plant items that can be turned in to the Dye Trader by selecting the “Strange Plants” option in his dialogue window. In return, he rewards the player with six vials of one random special exclusive dye per plant. Up to 33 different types of dyes can be acquired this way, with more of them becoming available as the game progresses.
Strange Plants are found at any altitude and can grow in most biomes, though with some restrictions (see below).
Streamers: Streamers are placeable items that can be climbed on for mobility. They are available in three different colors: Blue Streamer, Green Streamer, and Pink Streamer. These are all functionally identical and can be purchased for 50 Copper each from the Party Girl during a Party.

Despite their unique appearance, streamers are functionally the same as Rope. Their ascent speed is 41 mph, the descent speed is 51 mph, and the horizontal speed is 5 mph (although it is listed as 0 mph in the game, it is 7.55 feet per second), though they cannot be crafted into Rope Coils like other Rope variants can. When multiple streamers of the same color are hung in a single horizontal row, they will appear as a banner-style ribbon.
Stress Ball: The Stress Ball is an accessory that has a 1/100 (1%) chance to be dropped by Hoplites. When equipped, while not moving and with the inventory closed, the player will automatically and continuously use the weapon or tool that they are holding. Not all items can be used this way (see below).
Extractinable items can also be used, with the exception of glowing moss and Desert Fossils.
Strings: A string is an offensive accessory that boosts all yoyos. While equipped, the spin duration of all yoyos is increased by 50% and their maximum range is extended by 25%, plus an additional 1.9 tiles, and the maximum range of counterweights is increased from 7.8 tiles to 10.4 tiles. White String is first crafted by the player with 30 Cobwebs at a Loom, and can be combined with certain dyes to form colored variants. These colored strings will be displayed as the color of the string attached to yoyos and counterweights when they are thrown, in addition to providing the duration and range bonuses. They also change the color of the fishing line. They will apply their color changes even when equipped in a social slot.
Strung Counterweight: The Strung Counterweight is an accessory which combines the functionalities of a counterweight and a string. It grants the following effects while equipped:
+25% yoyo range, with an additional +2 tiles
Creates a counterweight upon hitting an enemy with a yoyo
Stucco: Stucco blocks are decorative building materials that are available in four different colors.
Stucco Walls: Stucco Walls are background Walls crafted from Stucco.
Sturdy Fossil: The Sturdy Fossil is a block and crafting material used to make bone- and fossil-themed gear. Sturdy Fossils are obtained by consuming Desert Fossils at an Extractinator, with a 10% chance of acquiring a Sturdy Fossil from each Desert Fossil. They can also be obtained from Tomb Crawlers, Basilisks, Oasis Crates, and Mirage Crates.
Not counting the javelins or the throwing knives, crafting all of the fossil equipment requires 107 Sturdy Fossils.
Stylish Scissors: The Stylish Scissors are a pre-Hardmode broadsword that have a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by the Stylist. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging the weapon will throw the scissors in the direction of the cursor. The thrown scissors travel forward for 0.25 seconds before sharply dropping down, and can pierce through one enemy before dissipating on the second hit. The weapon and its projectiles both inflict the Bleeding debuff for 4–6 seconds on hit.
Stylist: The Stylist is an NPC vendor who can change the player's hairstyle and hair color. She also sells a variety of Hair Dyes, which apply dynamic effects to the player's hair. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

Rescuing her as the Webbed Stylist, who can be encountered randomly in Spider Nests in the Cavern layer. Interacting with her in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will free her. If the Webbed Stylist is killed, she will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Stylist NPC is killed, she will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.

Selecting the “Hair Style” option in the Stylist's dialog opens a window where the player can choose a new hairstyle and color. The changes are immediately visible on the character for preview. Permanently applying the changes incurs a fee: switching to a different hairstyle costs 10 Gold; changing hair color costs 2 Gold. Hairstyle and color can be changed repeatedly and at any time.

Like with all other vendors, the Stylist's prices can vary depending on her happiness; this also affects her prices for hairstyle and color changes, as follows: The combined cost of changing hairstyle and color is multiplied by her happiness-based price multiplier, and then rounded to the nearest multiple of 1 Gold. Thus, the cost of changing hairstyles can be 8–15 Gold Coin, changing hair colors can cost 2–3 Gold Coin, and changing both hairstyle and hair color at once can range from 10 Gold to 18 Gold.

The Stylist will defend herself against nearby enemies with her Stylish Scissors. She deals 10 / 15 / 17 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Stylist also has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping the Stylish Scissors upon death.
The Webbed Stylist is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Stynger: The Stynger is a Hardmode, post-Golem launcher that consumes Stynger Bolts as ammunition. When used, it fires high-velocity Stynger Bolts that explode upon contact with enemies or blocks. The explosion additionally releases 2–5 shrapnel fragments that spread out in random directions and can also explode, each dealing the weapon's full damage and knockback. The main Stynger Bolt deals double damage (124 base damage), but not its explosion.

The Stynger has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When dropped, the Stynger is always accompanied by 60 to 99 Stynger Bolts. Additional Stynger Bolts can be purchased from the Witch Doctor and Arms Dealer (75 Copper per bolt), if the Stynger is in the player's inventory.
Sugar Cookie: The Sugar Cookie is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon. The Sugar Cookie can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 3.601% in pre-Hardmode and 3.361% in Hardmode.
Summer Hat: The Summer Hat is a vanity item equipped in the Social Helmet Slot. It is purchased from the Clothier for 1 Gold, when he is spoken to during the day outside of a Graveyard.
Summoner Emblem: The Summoner Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that increases summon damage by 15%. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop from the Wall of Flesh.
Summoning Potion: The Summoning Potion is a buff potion which grants the Summoning buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's minion slots by 1. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Sun Mask: The Sun Mask is a vanity helmet dropped by Lamias in normal Underground Deserts with a 1/25 (4%) chance.
Sun Stone: The Sun Stone is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory which has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. It grants the same stat bonuses as the Moon Stone; however, these bonuses only activate during the day.
Sunflower: The Sunflower is a large, tall plant which can be found growing naturally on grass, and can be broken with a pickaxe or drill, or by coming into contact with water. It cannot be grown from seeds like most other plants, but is instead placed fully-grown, either naturally upon world generation or by the player. It can also be purchased from the Dryad for 50 Silver each, while a Blood Moon is not occurring.

Sunflowers can only be placed on regular, Hallowed, Jungle, or Ash grass, at any height. They cannot be placed on Corrupt grass, Crimson grass, Mushroom grass, bare Dirt Blocks, nor in Clay Pots or Planter Boxes.

Sunflowers grant the Happy! buff to players in their vicinity, increasing their movement speed and reducing enemy spawns. Furthermore, they serve as a small barrier against the spread of the Corruption/Crimson and Hallow, negate some of the effects of the evil biomes, and help preventing Graveyard biomes from forming.
Sunfury: The Sunfury is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron flail that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3 seconds on hit. The Sunfury also has a base 11% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
If the Blue Moon is also in the player's inventory, then the Blue Moon will be thrown out at the same time as the Sunfury, but in the mirrored direction.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Sunglasses: The Sunglasses are a vanity item equipped in the social helmet slot. While equipped, the sun in the background will change to its pre-1.2 variant wearing sunglasses as well. Cattiva will also appear wearing sunglasses when equipped.
Sunplate Block: Sunplate Block is a block that is found on Floating Islands or can be crafted with Fallen Stars and Stone Blocks in the with a Sky Mill. When a square of four or more Sunplate Blocks are put next to each other, they make a pattern that resembles a starry night sky.
Super Dart Trap: The Super Dart Trap is a trap found inside the Jungle Temple and, rarely, outside the Temple's door. It fires a dart when activated via Wire, which costs no ammunition, but has a cooldown period of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 3.33 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 3 seconds between firings. The darts deal 80 / 160 / 240 damage and inflict Poisoned for 15 / 30 / 37.5 seconds to players (40 damage and 15 seconds of Poisoned to NPCs, enemies, and critters).
(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Super Dart Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer.
(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Unlike Lihzahrd Bricks, breaking Super Dart Traps does not require the Picksaw.
Super Healing Potion: The Super Healing Potion is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist recovery potion that heals 200 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.
Though their crafting cost is fairly significant, they are the highest tier of healing potion in the game. They are also always dropped by the Moon Lord.
It is the fifth and final tier of healing potion, succeeding the Lesser Healing Potion, Healing Potion, Greater Healing Potion, and Jungle Juice.
Super Mana Potion: The Super Mana Potion is a Hardmode, post-Plantera recovery potion that restores 400 mana and inflicts the Mana Sickness debuff upon use. It is the most potent of all mana restoration items.
It is the fourth and final tier of mana potion, succeeding the Lesser Mana Potion, Mana Potion, and Greater Mana Potion.
Super Star Shooter: The Super Star Shooter is a Hardmode ranged weapon that, as a direct upgrade to the Star Cannon, consumes and fires Fallen Stars. The projectiles are not affected by gravity, pierce an infinite amount of enemies, and dissipate into visual light-emitting particles after 1 minute or upon impact with a block. Unlike the Star Cannon, each projectile releases light slashes onto damaged enemies, which deal 75% of the weapon's damage (45 base damage) and pierce infinitely over a small area, but do not inflict any knockback.
Superheated Blood: The Superheated Blood is a mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Lava Shark Mount. The Superheated Blood has a 19/100 (19%) chance of being obtained from Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates found by fishing in lava.

Riding the mount will allow the player to swim very quickly in lava without taking damage. The player will also be immune to all Burning damage. It can also swim in water and honey, but will not protect the player from drowning. It has a maximum speed of 73 mph in liquids and 11 mph on land.
The mount maintains its velocity in the air, allowing for jumps similar to while riding a Minecart. When moving upwards or downwards, it tilts towards that direction.
When submerged in lava, this mount enables 'lava vision' which renders all lava more transparent.
Superhero set: The Superhero set is a vanity set which consists of the Superhero Mask, the Superhero Costume, and the Superhero Tights.
Surly Slime: Town Slimes are a type of town pet. There are 8 different Town Slimes and all of them can exist at the same time (unlike the different breeds of the Town Bunny, Town Cat, and Town Dog).

Almost all types of Town Slimes are acquired via some form of transformation, similar to the Tax Collector. Afterwards, the transformed Town Slime will move into a vacant house if one is available. If it is killed, it will move in again after some time as long as there is a vacant house. The initial transformation does not need to be repeated.

Town Slimes can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). They may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for their home tile (standing point).
Suspicious Grinning Eye: The Suspicious Grinning Eye is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Suspicious Eye, a miniature version of the Eye of Cthulhu, that follows the player. It normally shows a blue iris and pupil, but when moving faster than 31 mph the pupil slides up and reveals a mouth, similar to the Eye of Cthulhu's second form. The Suspicious Grinning Eye has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu in Master Mode.
Suspicious Looking Eye: The Suspicious Looking Eye is a boss-summoning item that summons the Eye of Cthulhu when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night.

In addition to being crafted, Suspicious Looking Eyes also have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Ivy Chests and Gold Chests found in the Cavern layer, including locked ones found inside the Dungeon.
Suspicious Looking Tentacle: The Suspicious Looking Tentacle is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord light pet-summoning item that spawns the Suspicious Looking Eye, a small tentacled floating eye that provides cyan light and follows the player. The Suspicious Looking Tentacle is always dropped from the Moon Lord's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

The pet emits light from both itself and the player. In addition to providing light, the Suspicious Looking Tentacle senses nearby NPCs, enemies, treasure (Pots, Chests, etc.), and ores within a 17-tile radius. This is shown via its pupil and iris pointing in the direction of the entity sensed, as well as expanding for treasure and contracting for enemies. The eye will also sparkle when nearby ores and treasures are detected.
Swamp Thing: The Swamp Thing is a Hardmode enemy that commonly spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. He moves very fast and occasionally stops in place.
Swarm Grenade: The Swarm Grenade is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Swarm Biter that follows the player. When the player moves too far away, the Swarm Biter will disappear and emits a small puff of pink smoke. When the player lands on any other surface that can be stood on, the Swarm Biter will reappear, emitting the same pink smoke. The Swarm Grenade can be purchased from the Zoologist for 10 Gold during a Party.
Sweet Barb: The Sweet Barb is a pre-Hardmode accessory. When equipped, it releases 1–3 homing Bee projectiles that attack nearby enemies each time the player takes damage, and grants the Honey buff for 5 seconds after being damaged. In addition, arrows fired by the player inflict the Poisoned debuff for 1.5 seconds and have a maximum chance of 1/5 (20%) to summon 3–6 homing Bee projectiles on hit.
Sweetheart Necklace: The Sweetheart Necklace is an accessory which releases a concentrated burst of bees and grants the player the Panic! and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Honey buffs when damaged, increasing movement speed by 100% for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 8 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 5 seconds and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) health regeneration for 5 seconds.
Swiftness Potion: The Swiftness Potion is a buff potion which grants the Swiftness buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's maximum movement speed by 25%, but does not stack with sprinting accessories (such as Hermes Boots), nor does it affect the speed of mounts. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Swiftness Potions can be found in pots, chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Switch: The Switch is an activation mechanism purchased from the Mechanic for 20 Silver. It can also be found in the Dungeon connected to Chain Lanterns, where it can be harvested with a Pickaxe or Drill.
The Switch can be placed on top or on the sides of blocks, or on the sides of Wooden Beams or trees. Switches can also be placed on background walls. It is activated by right-clicking on it.

Despite its name, the Switch does not need to act as an on/off mechanism. When wired to Dart Traps, for example, right-clicking the Switch will always cause the Trap to shoot, the same as a Pressure Plate would, no matter which position the switch happens to be in.
Swordfish: The Swordfish is a pre-Hardmode spear obtainable through fishing in the Ocean biome.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
TNT Barrel: The TNT Barrel is a trap which explodes immediately when destroyed, or hit by virtually any weapon or tool. The explosion does not destroy any tiles, deals 400 base damage to players (200 base damage to non-player entities), and inflicts a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) to all entities within a 16.25×16.25-tile area. The TNT Barrel is not a mechanism and cannot be triggered directly by Wire.
TNT Barrels can naturally generate (and generate in particularly large numbers in the Jungle Temple) when the No Traps special seed is active.
TV Head set: The TV Head set is a vanity set consisting of the Video Visage, the Lazer Blazer, and the Pinstripe Pants. It is one of the six sets that were added as part of the Journey's End Vanity Contest; the original concept was submitted by Dr.Zootsuit.
The Video Visage has the unique ability to change colors depending on where the player is and what they are doing.
Tabi: The Tabi is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory which allows the player to perform a dash by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right key, or the Dash button once. The dash ability has a one-second cooldown between uses. The Tabi has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance to drop from Bone Lees in the post-Plantera Dungeon.
Tables: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement.
There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.
Tablet Fragment: The Tablet Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist pet-summoning item that spawns a Phantasmal Dragon that follows the player. The pet resembles the Phantasm Dragon spawned during the Lunatic Cultist's battle, and the only difference between the two is that the pet itself is smaller. The Tablet Fragment has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Lunatic Cultist in Master Mode.
Tackle Box: The Tackle Box is an accessory that decreases the chance of bait consumption while fishing. The Tackle Box can be acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details).

The Angler will not give the player a Tackle Box as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.
Tactical Shotgun: The Tactical Shotgun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance of being dropped by Tactical Skeletons in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires six bullets in a spread, consuming one piece of ammunition.
Tactical Skeleton: The Tactical Skeleton is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns in the Dungeon after Plantera is defeated. Once the player is within its line of sight, the Tactical Skeleton remains stationary before firing spreads of four bullets at them that deal immense damage.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Tactical Skeletons spawn most often in areas of the Dungeon backed by tiled walls. They can also spawn in other areas, but with a significantly reduced chance.
Tainted Ghoul: Ghouls are Hardmode Underground Desert enemies who follow the Fighter AI (behaving similarly to Zombies). Ordinary Ghouls spawn inside the normal Underground Desert, the Vile Ghoul inside Corrupt parts of the Underground Desert, the Tainted Ghoul inside Crimson parts of the Underground Desert, and the Dreamer Ghoul inside Hallowed parts of the Underground Desert.
Tall Gate: The Tall Gate is a furniture item which is essentially a tall, sliding door that can be opened and closed by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it. Tall Gate fulfills a house's door requirement.
Tall Gates differ from doors in the following ways:
The Tall Gate is 5 tiles in height, which is large enough to allow players on mounts to pass through without dismounting (unlike doors, which are only 3 tiles tall).
Unlike doors, Tall Gates do not occupy additional space when opened; hence blocks or furniture placed on either side will not prevent them from opening.
Tall Gates come in only one variety (unlike doors, which have a different version available for each furniture theme).
Tally Counter: The Tally Counter is a post-Skeletron informational accessory that displays the number of enemies of a specific type that have been killed. The Tally Counter will first display "Kill count unavailable" underneath the minimap. After an enemy has been attacked, the text will display how many times that enemy has ever been killed by all players combined in that world. Only the last attacked enemy's count is displayed.
The Tally Counter has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped from Angry Bones, Cursed Skulls, Librarian Skeletons and Dark Casters, all of which are found in the Dungeon.
Tam O' Shanter: The Tam O' Shanter is a Hardmode vanity item purchased from the Clothier for 2 Gold 50 Silver, during the third quarter moon phase.
Target Dummy: The Target Dummy is a furniture item that serves as a test target for player attacks. It can be attacked repeatedly by players, displaying damage numbers just as enemies would, in order to test the effective damage output of a weapon as affected by any modifiers, current buffs, or equipped boost items. The Target Dummy is indestructible, regardless of the amount of damage it takes. It can be freed using any pickaxe, drill, or explosive.

The Target Dummy will also display damage and visual effects caused by damage-producing debuffs, allowing players to test their damage output, frequency, and duration. Though it visually recoils when struck, the Target Dummy is unresponsive to knockback and will never move.
Tattered Bee Wing: The Tattered Bee Wing is a rare Hardmode crafting material dropped by Moss Hornets with a (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1/100 (1%) / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 1/150 (0.67%) chance. It is used solely to craft Bee Wings.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, at least one mechanical boss must be defeated before it will drop.
Tattered Cloth: The Tattered Cloth is a crafting material that is always dropped by Goblin Scouts.
Tattered Wood Sign: The Tattered Wood Sign is a placeable item that functions like the regular Sign. It can be crafted from wood when the player is near a Work Bench in the Graveyard mini-biome.
Tavernkeep: The Tavernkeep is a unique NPC vendor who only accepts Defender Medals as currency for most items instead of coins. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

Rescuing him as the Unconscious Man, who can be encountered in any layer once the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu has been defeated. Interacting with him in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will wake him. If the Unconscious Man is killed, he will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Tavernkeep NPC is killed, he will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.

The Tavernkeep sells sentry summon weapons which are associated with the Old One's Army event and can only be used within that event at first. They function elsewhere only after the event is completed once successfully. Each of the Tavernkeep's sentry summon weapons come in three tiers: rod, cane, and staff, with the staff being the most expensive and the most powerful. The armor he sells also associates each sentry type with a specific class: Ballista for melee or tank-style users, Flameburst for magic users, Explosive Trap for rangers, and Lightning Aura for "speedy melee" (or summoners).

When the player selects the “Eternia Crystal” option for the first time, the Tavernkeep will give the player 10 Defender Medals for free. All future Defender Medals must be earned by either defeating the Old One's Army outright or by clearing its later waves.

The Tavernkeep will defend himself against nearby enemies by throwing mugs of Ale. He deals 24 / 36 / 42 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses. The Tavernkeep also has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping the Ale Tosser upon death.
The Unconscious Man is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Tax Collector: The Tax Collector is a Hardmode NPC who taxes other housed NPCs to earn coins for players. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

Rescuing him by throwing Purification Powder onto a Tortured Soul, a rare enemy that only spawns in The Underworld after the Wall of Flesh has been defeated. After this is done, the Tortured Soul will transform into the Tax Collector. If the Tortured Soul is killed, he will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Tax Collector NPC is killed, he will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.

When the Tax Collector is present, 50 Copper will be earned per real-world minute (each in-game hour), for each NPC that has a house (including the Tax Collector himself but excluding the Old Man, Traveling Merchant, Skeleton Merchant, and town pets). The Tax Collector stores these funds, up to 25 Gold. These stats are doubled in Celebration Mk 10 and Zenith worlds (i.e. 1 Silver per NPC and 50 Gold maximum). Speaking to him will reveal the amount stored thus far, and offer the “Collect” option to collect the funds. His tax limit (as well as his current funds and how much he collects per minute) varies depending on his current happiness; thus, how much he earns per minute will be between 33 Copper and 66 Copper, while his limit will be between 16 Gold 66 Silver 66 Copper and 33 Gold 33 Silver 33 Copper.
Unlike other town NPCs, the Tax Collector is immune to lava, due to being spawned from a Tortured Soul.
The Tax Collector will attack nearby enemies with his Classy Cane, for which he has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of dropping upon death.
Tax Collector's set: The Tax Collector's set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Tax Collector's Hat, the Tax Collector's Suit and the Tax Collector's Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 9 Gold (set) when the Tax Collector is present in the world.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Teacup: The Teacup is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Teal Mushroom: The Teal Mushroom is a type of mushroom. It grows on Dirt, Stone, Mud, or regular Jungle grass in the Underground and Cavern layers. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Teal Dye.
Team Blocks: Team Blocks are decorative blocks purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Silver each. Team Blocks are available in six different colors, each representing one of the six team colors selectable in the player's inventory, including white for the neutral team. They can be transmuted into their respective "dull" variant via Shimmer.

Unlike Team Dye and Team Hair Dye, these blocks have no special function and are always the same color. The Traveling Merchant will only ever sell one color of Team Block at a time, along with the Team Platform of the same color, meaning that multiple visits will be required to collect all colors.
Team Dye: Team Dye is a dye that can be purchased from the Dye Trader while playing multiplayer. The color of this dye will correspond to the team the player is on; if the player is not on a team, it acts as though no dye was equipped.
Team Platforms: Team Platforms are decorative platforms purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Silver each. They are available in six different colors, each representing one of the six team colors selectable in the player's inventory, including white for the neutral team.

Unlike Team Dye and Team Hair Dye, these platforms have no special function and are always the same color. The Traveling Merchant will only ever sell one color of Team Platform at a time, along with the Team Block of the same color, meaning that multiple visits will be required to collect all colors.
Teapot: The Teapot is a crafting station used solely to make Teacups. It can be placed anywhere.
Teleportation Potion: The Teleportation Potion is a potion that teleports the user to a random location. In addition to being crafted, it can be found in Chests located in the Cavern layer and in Shadow Chests.
In choosing a destination, the following rules apply:Verify
The player will always be placed on top of a solid block and never inside blocks.
The player can never be placed in front of a natural, below-surface Dungeon wall before Skeletron has been defeated.
The player can never be placed in front of a natural, below-surface Lihzahrd Brick Wall (i.e., in the Jungle Temple) before Plantera has been defeated.
Teleporter: The Teleporter is a travel mechanism purchased from the (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Mechanic / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Steampunker for 2 Gold 50 Silver. When two Teleporters are wired together with a triggering mechanism, they can exchange players, NPCs, and most enemies between them. Teleporting is always instantaneous, has no load time or cooldown, no Mana or coin cost, and no limit on distance.
Unlike most furniture, Teleporters are foreground objects. They consist of three inseparable blocks which, like all block types, can individually be shaped with a hammer or actuated.
Tempest Staff: The Tempest Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Sharknado minion. It hovers near enemies, dealing contact damage and firing Mini Sharkron projectiles that visually splatter upon contact with enemies or blocks. The Tempest Staff has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron.
Templar's Sling: The Templar's Sling is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:
Allows the player to walk past a sentry to carry it
Temple Key: The Temple Key is dropped by Plantera and is used to unlock the Lihzahrd Door, the door to the Jungle Temple. It is consumed upon use, like Golden Keys.
Tendon Bow: The Tendon Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Demon Bow.
Tentacle Spike: The Tentacle Spike is a pre-Hardmode broadsword dropped by Eaters of Souls, Devourers, Crimeras, Face Monsters, and Blood Crawlers with a 1/525 (0.19%) chance. When swung, it sticks tentacle spikes into enemies on hit, which linger on the enemy and deal 3 damage per second for 9 seconds. The spikes can stack up to 5 times on each target.
On The Constant seed, the drop chance is increased to a 1/100 (1%) chance.
Terra Blade: The Terra Blade is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword. When swung, a green aura follows the swing, reaching farther than the sword itself. The aura can hit up to three enemies. The sword will also fire a green slash projectile that pierces infinitely, dealing the weapon's damage but reducing its damage by 25% of its current damage for each target it pierces. The projectile will dissipate after 1.5 seconds, upon contact with blocks, or when its damage falls to 0 after piercing.
Terraformer: The Terraformer is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord tool. It has the same effects as a Clentaminator but reaches 95 tiles and has a width of 7 tiles and has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance not to consume ammunition, compared to the Clentaminator which reaches 60 tiles and has a width of 5 tiles. The Terraformer can only be obtained by throwing a Clentaminator into Shimmer after the Moon Lord has been defeated.
The Terraformer cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Terragrim: The Terragrim is a pre-Hardmode melee weapon. When used, it rapidly releases slashes aimed towards the cursor. Anything within this area takes constant damage at a rate exceeding the weapon's stated use time.

It is obtainable from the unique background object found in an Enchanted Sword Shrine or very rarely in the Caverns layer. When the object is destroyed, it has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to drop a Terragrim rather than an Enchanted Sword.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. The Terragrim's unique means of attack is unaffected by any size and speed modifiers.
Terraprisma: The Terraprisma is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Terraprisma minion. It flies towards enemies, performing a quick stab before repeatedly attacking with a swinging or stabbing motion. Terraprisma arrange themselves in a wing-like pattern behind the player, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby.
The Terraprisma is always dropped from the Empress of Light when all damage dealt to the boss occurs during the day.
Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 158% (including whip bonuses) or 58% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.
Terrarian: The Terrarian is a Hardmode yoyo that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. It rapidly fires short-lived green orbs towards nearby enemies that bounce off blocks. It also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.

Its best modifier is Legendary. Although yoyos cannot normally obtain the Legendary modifier, the Terrarian is an exception and receives a unique set of boosts from the Legendary modifier: +17% damage, +8% critical strike chance, and +17% knockback.
Terrarium: The Terrarium is an item used to make Cages for critters caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net.
Terraspark Boots: The Terraspark Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory crafted from Frostspark Boots and Lava Waders, and combines their functionality. They grant the following effects while equipped:
The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of snow clouds as they sprint.
Increased maximum movement speed to 35 mph (25.67 tiles/second).
The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual trail of green sparks.
When paired with wings, this flight is disabled to give the wings an additional 0.7 seconds of flight time.
Increased acceleration and deceleration on all Ice Blocks, Thin Ice, Frozen Slime Blocks, and Aetherium Blocks. The player will no longer cause Thin Ice to break upon landing.
The ability to stand and walk on the surface of all liquids. Prevents fall damage when landing on the surface of any liquid.

Immunity to lava for 7 seconds. After this runs out, it decreases the damage taken from lava from 80 to 35, and reduces the duration of the On Fire! debuff inflicted by it from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds.
Equipping the Ash Wood armor at the same time provides immunity to lava damage and the debuff.
Tesla Turret: The Tesla Turret is a Hardmode enemy found only during the Martian Madness event. It is built by Martian Engineers and is completely immobile. Every three seconds, it will fire an Electric Bolt at the player, which has a 2/3 (66.67%) chance to inflict the Electrified debuff for 5 seconds. The Tesla Turret will continue to stay in place until it is destroyed by the player.
The Axe: The Axe is a Hardmode hamaxe that has a 1/50 (2%) / 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When swung, it produces an electric guitar sound that changes in tone depending on the distance from the cursor to the player.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
The Bee's Knees: The Bee's Knees is a pre-Hardmode bow that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee. When used, it converts Wooden Arrows into a line of Bee Arrows. Bee Arrows are unaffected by gravity and disperse upon contact with an enemy or solid block, spawning three small homing bee projectiles with three independent 1/3 (33.33%) chances to spawn an extra bee. The bee projectiles deal 1/3 (33.33%) of the weapon and ammo's damage (9 base damage) before dissipating after a 10-second duration or upon contact with water or lava, and have a 1/2 (50%) chance to deal 1 extra damage. Individual bees can either pierce one enemy or ricochet off of blocks once.
The Beheaded's set: The Beheaded's set is a vanity set consisting of The Beheaded's Head, The Beheaded's Cuirass, and The Beheaded's Trousers.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The Black Spot: The Black Spot is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that spawns a rideable Pirate Ship Mount which can fly infinitely. The Black Spot has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Flying Dutchman in Master Mode.

The Pirate Ship Mount has a maximum horizontal flight speed of 36 mph, a diagonal speed of 54 mph, and a vertical speed of 41 mph. It moves slightly slower (30 mph) while in water. Upon achieving a horizontal speed of 27 mph, a ring of gold particles appears around the player and trails behind the mount, indicating that the Pirate Ship Mount begins dealing 100 base summon damage and a knockback of 12 (Insane) upon ramming enemies, which also grants the player 0.1 seconds worth of invincibility frames.
The Breaker: The Breaker is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its Crimson counterpart is the Flesh Grinder.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
The Bride: The Bride is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns rarely during a Blood Moon or very rarely at any time in a Graveyard biome. She acts the same as regular Zombies.
The Groom is her themed counterpart.

She is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Bride requires 10 kills to be awarded completion of her Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
The Destroyer: The Destroyer is a Hardmode mechanical boss that is essentially a more difficult version of the Eater of Worlds. Its segments share a single health pool, meaning individual segments cannot die. Each of The Destroyer's segments fires lasers at the player, and as they take damage, they launch Probes, independent flying enemies that fire lasers and can be killed individually.
While The Destroyer is alive, its exclusive music The Destroyer will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.
The Dirtiest Block: The Dirtiest Block is a pet-summoning item that spawns The Dirtiest Block that follows the player. It can be found extremely rarely as a block that looks identical to Dirt Blocks. Upon world generation and depending on world size, up to 3 (in small worlds), 6 (medium), or 9 (large) random Dirt Blocks will be replaced with The Dirtiest Blocks.
The Doctor's set: The Doctor's set is a vanity set which consists of The Doctor's Shirt and The Doctor's Pants. They are purchased from the Clothier for 40 Gold (set) in total, during Waning Gibbous.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The Eye of Cthulhu: The Eye of Cthulhu is a Hardmode, post-Plantera yoyo that has a 1/3 (33.33%) / 5/9 (55.56%) chance of being dropped by Mothrons during a Solar Eclipse.

On every 7th yoyo hit, The Eye of Cthulhu deals 200% damage ((230 base damage) and also spawns an afterimage of the 2nd form of the Eye of Cthulhu boss, which dashes at the closest enemy with a 5-tile radius of the yoyo while passing through blocks, and disappears after a short distance. The afterimage pierces infinitely and deals 200% of The Eye of Cthulhu's damage ((230 base damage) and 100% of its knockback.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
The Grand Design: The Grand Design is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron tool for working with wiring and mechanisms. It combines and extends the abilities of its components: It allows a controlled view of wiring (Mechanical Lens) and measure distances and relative positions (Mechanical Ruler), and allows the player to place or remove any color of wire (Multicolor Wrench and Wire Cutter); unlike its components, it also shows and works with Actuators.
Creating the Grand Design costs 15 Gold in total. Its components are all bought from the Mechanic, and it is crafted at the Tinkerer's Workshop.
The Grand Design can be used at any part of the screen, regardless of block placement range.

When pressing ⚷ Open / Activate with the tool, a menu with six different buttons will be displayed, five for selecting Actuator and four colors of wires, one for toggling between placing or harvesting selected colors of wires and Actuator.
