The menu will pop up at the cursor's position, with buttons in a radial pattern.
The menu will pop up above the ⚷ Open / Activate button, with buttons listed in two rows.
When the menu is closed, five small colored square icons will appear near the cursor, showing the current mode (placing/harvesting) and selected wires/actuator.
In addition, as long as The Grand Design is anywhere in the inventory, it will provide seven toggles, controlling the functions of Mechanical Ruler and Mechanical Lens.
The Groom: The Groom is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns rarely during a Blood Moon or very rarely at any time in a Graveyard (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) biome. He acts the same as regular Zombies.
The Bride (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is his themed counterpart.

He is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. The Groom requires 10 kills to be awarded completion of his Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
The Horseman's Blade: The Horseman's Blade is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that can be dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When swung, an orange aura follows the swing, reaching farther than the sword itself. The aura can hit up to three enemies. Upon striking an enemy, The Horseman's Blade summons a Flaming Jack, a homing pumpkin head projectile that can pass through blocks.
The Hungry: The Wall of Flesh is the final pre-Hardmode boss. Once it is defeated, the world permanently converts to Hardmode, which brings new content and challenges.

To defeat the Wall of Flesh, the player must attack either its eyes or its mouth. They all share the same health counter, so attacking any of the three will deplete the total health of the boss. However, the eyes have less defense (thus take more damage) than the mouth. No other parts of the Wall of Flesh can be damaged.
See below for information on the two exclusive debuffs from the boss, Horrified and The Tongue.
While the Wall of Flesh is alive, its exclusive music Boss 2 will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Wall of Flesh (Otherworldly) will play instead.
The Imploder: The Imploder is an unimplemented item. Apart from a unique tooltip, no stats or behaviors exist for this item.
The Meatball: The Meatball is a pre-Hardmode flail.
Its Corruption counterpart is the Ball O' Hurt.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
The Plan: The Plan is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Slow and Confused debuffs.
The Possessed: The Possessed is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. Despite not resembling one, she acts similarly to spider-type enemies, climbing on background walls when able to and walking on the ground at all other times. While climbing on walls, The Possessed has increased movement speed and gains complete immunity to knockback.
The Rotted Fork: The Rotted Fork is a pre-Hardmode spear that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Crimson Hearts found in The Crimson or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Crimson Crates and Hematic Crates. When thrust, it creates a small shockwave at its tip.
Its Shadow Orb melee weapon counterpart is the Ball O' Hurt.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
The Torch God: The Torch God is an event that is initiated by clustering a large number of Torches underground. It consists of dodging projectiles, and survivors are rewarded with the Torch God's Favor, an item which grants the player the option for their Torches to automatically match the biome they are placed in. Torches placed in their matching type of biome positively influence the player's luck in most areas.

The event can begin in any biome when there are at least 101 Torches of any type are found in a 41×41-tile rectangular area centered on the player's center, while the player is below the surface layer. It is possible for the event to start with less than 101 Torches placed if the player is moving, due to the game's calculation incorrectly counting some Torches more than once. The Torch God event cannot take place for any character who has already consumed the Torch God's Favor or has one in their inventory.

As the Torch God begins, torch flames shoot off at the player as projectiles, one at a time. They are fired in a random order, at a rate of 3 projectiles per second, and deal 40 / 80 / 120 base damage. Projectiles can pass through blocks to reach the player, but they can collide with blocks again after passing the player. Each Torch shoots one projectile and extinguishes itself afterward, as if it was switched off via wire. For the entire duration of the event, the player is inflicted with the Blackout debuff, significantly reducing their field of vision.

The Torch God ends once all nearby Torches have been spent, to a maximum of 200 attacks. If at least 95 Torches were fired, the player is rewarded with the Torch God's Favor item. All Torches re-light when the event ends. If the player dies or leaves underground, the event ends early and nothing is awarded; if the player moves into an area without Torches, the event will also end early, however, the Torch God's Favor will still be awarded if at least 95 Torches were fired.
While The Torch God is alive, the music Torch God will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Wall of Flesh (Otherworldly) will play instead.
The Undertaker: The Undertaker is a pre-Hardmode gun. It will always drop from the first Crimson Heart destroyed in a Crimson world (along with 100 Musket Balls) and has a 1/5 (20%) chance of dropping from destroyed Crimson Hearts afterward. It also has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from Crimson and Hematic Crates fished in the Crimson.
Its Corruption counterpart is the Musket. The Undertaker has a lower damage per shot but fires much faster.
Thin Ice: Thin Ice is a type of block found in the Snow and Ice biomes. It is found naturally in two configurations: either as a single layer over a pool of water, or in large packed regions underground.

Similar to Ice Blocks, Thin Ice has reduced friction, and players will slide across it. Thin Ice will break if a player falls on it at a certain speed, usually achieved by falling normally onto it. Landing on Thin Ice will not cause fall damage itself, but it will not slow the player's fall on contact, and fall damage will continue to accumulate until the player lands on another block type (unlike Cobwebs, for instance, which reset fall damage). Ice Skates or their upgrades can be equipped to land on Thin Ice without breaking it, though this does not prevent fall damage.
Thin Ice is destroyed permanently when broken, dropping nothing. On the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, Thin Ice cannot be picked up, crafted, or moved in any way.
Thorn Chakram: The Thorn Chakram is a pre-Hardmode boomerang. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not necessarily return immediately upon contact with objects, but instead can bounce off blocks before returning. The Thorn Chakram has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Thorns Potion: The Thorns Potion is a buff potion which grants the Thorns buff when consumed. The buff inflicts a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on enemies that come into contact with the player, and deals 100% of their damage to them. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Thorns Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.
Threads: Threads are crafting materials used primarily in vanity items. Black Thread and Pink Thread can be purchased from the Clothier, while Green Thread can be crafted.
Throne: The Throne is a decorative furniture item. It fulfills a house's chair requirement.
As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on the Throne will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5.
Throwing Knife: The Throwing Knife is a consumable ranged weapon. It can hit up to 2 targets. It can be purchased from the Merchant during a Blood Moon for 50 Copper each and may also be found in Chests. The Throwing Knife is greatly affected by gravity and arcs similarly to Shurikens and Bones. It has the greatest range out of these consumable ranged weapons (with Bones having the least).
The Merchant will use Throwing Knives to defend himself against nearby enemies.
Thrown Powder: Thrown Powders are consumable items that can be used to convert blocks and walls between their pure, Crimson, or Corrupt forms. When thrown, they release a cloud of sparkling powder with a very short range, comparable to that of a broadsword, and produce a fair amount of light. Thrown Powder comes in three variants:

Purification Powder is able to revert any Corrupted, Crimson, or Hallowed blocks and walls back into their pure form, such as reverting Ebonstone into Stone, Crimsand into Sand, or Pink Ice into Ice. It is purchased solely from the Dryad for 75 Copper each, while a Blood Moon is not active.
Purification Powder can also be used on a Tortured Soul in order to transform him into the Tax Collector NPC, as well as on a Mystic Frog to transform it into the Mystic Slime town pet.

Vile Powder is able to convert blocks and walls, including the Crimson and the Hallowed ones, into their Corrupted form, such as converting Pearlstone into Ebonstone. If thrown at a Bunny, Penguin, or Goldfish, it will turn into its Corrupted variants: the Corrupt Bunny, Corrupt Penguin, and Corrupt Goldfish, respectively. It can be crafted from Vile Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a Corrupt world.
Vile Powder can be used to spread the Corruption onto convertible tiles.

Vicious Powder is functionally identical to its counterpart, Vile Powder, to where it can convert blocks and walls, including the Corrupted and the Hallowed ones, into their Crimson form. If thrown at a Bunny, Penguin, or Goldfish, it will turn into its Crimson variants: the Vicious Bunny, Vicious Penguin, and Vicious Goldfish, respectively. It can be crafted from Vicious Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a Crimson world.
Vicious Powder can be used to spread the Crimson onto convertible tiles.
Thrown Water: Thrown Water refers to a set of three consumable weapons that each convert a small area into a biome (Hallow, Corruption, or Crimson for Holy Water, Unholy Water, and Blood Water respectively) when thrown. This conversion affects a roughly circular area with a radius of four tiles from the center. Enemies within this radius are also damaged slightly; this damage is not classified as any of the four damage types and therefore cannot be modified by any buffs or equipment.

Holy Water is only available in Hardmode. In contrast, Unholy and Blood Water are available in pre-Hardmode, since the Ebonsand or Crimsand required for crafting them can be obtained by using Vile/Vicious Powder to convert pure sand.
Thunder Zapper: The Thunder Zapper is a pre-Hardmode wand that can be found in Sandstone Chests in the lower 3/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis. When used, it fires a lightning bolt that travels in a zigzag pattern horizontally (but traveling straight when shooting directly up or down). The bolt dissipates with a visual explosion after traveling for about one second or upon hitting an enemy or a block.
Tiger Climbing Gear: Tiger Climbing Gear is an accessory that allows for sliding down or completely stopping while touching walls. Holding the ▼ Down key while clinging to a wall allows the player to slide down walls a little faster than if they only had one of the ingredient accessories. While either clinging or sliding, the player can jump off of the wall, allowing them to scale vertical surfaces with ease. This accessory is useful if paired with wings, as the player's flight time is reset when latching onto a wall.
Tiki Torch: The Tiki Torch is a stationary light source that must be placed in order to provide light. Like Torches, it can be placed on platforms, and will be put out, broken and subsequently dropped when coming into contact with water. However, the Tiki Torch cannot be collected by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it.
Tiki Totem: The Tiki Totem is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Tiki Spirit that floats and spins above the player's head. Unlike most pets, it will not teleport to the player when the player moves too quickly for it to keep up; it will simply float straight towards the player. The Tiki Totem can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 2 Platinum when he is spoken to in the Jungle biome during Hardmode.
Tiki armor: Tiki armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summoner armor set consisting of the Tiki Mask, Tiki Shirt, and Tiki Pants. The set can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for a total of 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Tim: Tim is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the lower Cavern layer. With an appearance similar to Dark Casters, he can be distinguished by his Wizard Hat, which is guaranteed to drop when he is defeated. Like other casters, Tim will fire three destructible Chaos Balls that pass through solid blocks before teleporting to another visible location on the screen.

He is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades. Tim requires 10 kills to be awarded completion of his Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Timeless Traveler's set: The Timeless Traveler's set is a vanity set consisting of the Timeless Traveler's Hood, the Timeless Traveler's Cloak, and the Timeless Traveler's Footwear. It is one of the six sets that were added as part of the Journey's End Vanity Contest; the original concept was submitted by DisRicardo.
It can only be crafted in a Corruption world, unless the player creates an artificial Corruption biome or farms the chunks from a Corrupt Statue. Its Crimson counterpart is the Plaguebringer's set.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
When wearing the full set, the set displays an animation of soul-like apparitions that bear a striking visual resemblance to Mana Boosters.
Timers: Timers are triggering mechanisms that periodically send an activation signal to other mechanisms. There are five different types of timers, which differ in the interval at which the signal is sent: 5 Second Timer, 3 Second Timer, 1 Second Timer, 1/2 Second Timer, and 1/4 Second Timer.

Timers need to be placed in order to function; they can be placed freely in the air, allowing platforms and walls to be built off of them. They are toggled on and off by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Timers can also be activated and deactivated using other mechanism activation items. For example, a Switch on the same path of Wire will toggle a timer on and off. Multiple timers on the same circuit will also repeatedly toggle each other on and off.
All timers can be purchased from the Mechanic, while some can also be crafted.
Tin Axe: The Tin Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Axe.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Tin Bar: The Tin Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Bar.
Newly created characters outside of Journey Mode will always spawn with the Copper Shortsword, Copper Pickaxe, and Copper Axe, regardless of whether the world generated with Copper or Tin.
Tin Bow: The Tin Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Tin Brick: Tin Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material made from Tin Ore. In some worlds it can also be harvested from Jungle Shrines. Like the ore it is made of, placed Tin Bricks will sparkle. As tin becomes fairly useless early in the game, this is an inexpensive ore brick to build with. Despite being made of Tin, it has no sell value, as with most other blocks. Tin Plating is also available as a decorative block, with the same ingredients and color but a different texture.
Tin Brick Wall: The Tin Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.
Tin Broadsword: The Tin Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Tin Shortsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Broadsword.
Tin Hammer: The Tin Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Hammer.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, and Quick provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Tin Ore: Tin Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on the surface. Tin Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Copper Ore.
Tin Pickaxe: The Tin Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks weaker than Meteorite.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Pickaxe. The Tin Pickaxe has slightly more damage, mining speed, and range.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Tin Plating: Tin Plating is a pre-Hardmode brick. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Plating.
Tin Plating Wall: Tin Plating Wall is a background wall made of Tin Plating.
Tin Shortsword: The Tin Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Tin Broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Shortsword.
Tin armor: Tin armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Tin Helmet, Tin Chainmail, and Tin Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 48 Tin Bars (144 Tin Ore). The full set grants 7 defense while equipped.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Copper armor.
Tinkerer's Workshop: The Tinkerer's Workshop is a flat-surface item and crafting station that is used primarily to combine multiple accessories into single items that usually provide the abilities of their components. For instance, it can combine the Rocket Boots and Hermes Boots into a single item (the Spectre Boots) that provides the same rocket-jumping and accelerated movement as the individual items do, without occupying two accessory slots. The Tinkerer's Workshop can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 10 Gold.

(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) When combining items, the Tinkerer's Workshop will assign a new random modifier to the crafted item. The modifiers the individual items had beforehand do not influence the modifier of the new combined item.
(3DS version) Items crafted at the Tinkerer's Workshop will be assigned no modifier.

The Tinkerer's Workshop is also used to craft most of the unrecordable Music Boxes, the Shellphone (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Weighted Pressure Plates, The Grand Design (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Multicolor Wrench (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the Ultrabright Helmet (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Boulders on the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version.
Tissue Sample: The Tissue Sample is a pre-Hardmode crafting material dropped from Creepers (and the Brain of Cthulhu's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode).
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Shadow Scale.
Titan Glove: The Titan Glove is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by Mimics. While equipped, it grants the following effects:
Titan Potion: The Titan Potion is a buff potion which grants the Titan buff when consumed. The buff increases the amount of knockback the player inflicts on enemies by 50%. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Titan Potions can be found in Pots in the Underworld, as well as in Chests.
Titanium Bar: The Titanium Bar is a Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Bar.
Titanium Chainsaw: The Titanium Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Titanium Waraxe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Chainsaw.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Titanium Crate: The Titanium Crate is a Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any layer. It is the highest tier of standard crate, having the greatest value if sold directly. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Golden Crate.
Titanium Drill: The Titanium Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Titanium Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Drill. The Titanium Drill has slightly more pickaxe power and damage.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Titanium Ore: Titanium Ore belongs to the third tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the third altar broken, either it or Adamantite Ore can spawn in the cavern layer, roughly at lava depth. Mining Titanium Ore requires a Mythril/Orichalcum Pickaxe or better.

As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
It is one of the two ores able to create Hardmode Forges, which are used for smelting all ores obtained in future progression, as well as itself.
Titanium Pickaxe: The Titanium Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Titanium Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Pickaxe. The Titanium Pickaxe has slightly more pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Titanium Repeater: The Titanium Repeater is a Hardmode repeater.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Repeater.
Titanium Sword: The Titanium Sword is a Hardmode broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Sword.
Titanium Trident: The Titanium Trident is a Hardmode spear.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Glaive.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Titanium Waraxe: The Titanium Waraxe is a Hardmode axe and the alternative to the Titanium Chainsaw.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Waraxe.
Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Titanium armor: Titanium armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Titanium Breastplate and Titanium Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Titanium Mask, Titanium Helmet, and Titanium Headgear, providing bonuses for melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 59 Titanium Bars (236 Titanium Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 85 Titanium Bars (340 Titanium Ore).
Its alternate ore counterpart is Adamantite armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped, depending on the headpiece chosen:

Attacking grants the player the Titanium Barrier buff, which spawns Titanium Shards that spin around the player. The shards spin faster the more there are, and up to 7 shards can exist at once. Each Titanium Shard deals 50 damage with a knockback value of 15 (Insane), and cannot deal critical hits. Each shard dissipates on enemy hits or after 10 seconds has passed.
Titanstone Block: The Titanstone Block is a Hardmode brick. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite Beam.
Titanstone Block Wall: Titanstone Block Wall is a wall made from Titanstone Blocks.
Toilets: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo.
As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5.

Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds.
Tomb Crawler: The Tomb Crawler is a pre-Hardmode worm enemy found in the Underground Desert. Following the same AI pattern as Giant Worms, it moves through solid blocks to attack the player by charging. The sound of its burrowing grows louder and faster as it draws near. Like many other worm-type enemies, its head segment deals more damage on contact, but is also the part of its body most vulnerable to damage. It is the pre-Hardmode counterpart of the Dune Splicer.
Tombstones: A Tombstone is a furniture item that drops when a player dies. It can then be retrieved and used much like a sign or as a form of decoration. By default, it contains the death message generated based on how the player died along with the real-life date of the death.

Upon death, a Tombstone will bounce around until it lands on a suitable 2-tile wide surface, where it will place itself. If a Tombstone cannot find a place to land (due to lack of suitable space), it cannot be retrieved and will eventually despawn. Two Tombstones cannot land on each other.
Variants are chosen randomly upon death. Golden Tombstones drop when the player had more than 10 Gold in their inventory.

Having 4–8 Tombstones placed in close proximity will gradually darken and desaturate the environment. Five or more Tombstones placed in close proximity will generate a Graveyard mini-biome. Breaking a Tombstone has 12.5% / 25% / 50% chance to spawn a Ghost off-screen.

In Hardcore, Tombstones cannot be easily obtained because death is permanent. Instead, NPCs in worlds with Hardcore characters will drop Tombstones when they are killed. Variants are still chosen randomly; all NPCs drop a normal Tombstone except the Merchant and Tax Collector who drop a golden variant.

In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, the Tombstone projectiles dropped by players (but not those dropped by NPCs in Hardcore) deal 210 / 280 / 420 damage to players and 70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters.
Because Tombstones create Graveyards, and mark a place where a player had died, they are highlighted by Dangersense Potions.
Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. Its spawn chance is increased in a The Constant world.
Tome of Infinite Wisdom: The Tome of Infinite Wisdom is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss wand that possesses two different modes of attack. When used with ⚒ Use / Attack, it fires bursts of four high-velocity pages that dissipate upon contact with enemies or blocks. When used with ⚷ Open / Activate, it summons a large, high-velocity tornado that deals 175% of the weapon's damage (63 damage), pierces infinite enemies, travels along blocks and through one-block low roofs, and dissipates after a duration of four seconds or upon being stopped by a wall of solid blocks. The Tome of Infinite Wisdom is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3.
Toolbelt: The Toolbelt is a construction accessory that can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 10 Gold. While equipped, it grants +1 placement range, but not tool range.
Toolbox: The Toolbox is a construction accessory that is obtained when opening Presents dropped during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 0.309% in pre-Hardmode and 0.288% in Hardmode. While equipped, it grants +1 placement range and tool range.
Topaz: Topaz is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It is the second-least valuable gem available, being able to craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and it also has two exclusive recipes: the Sandgun and the Magiluminescence. They can be obtained in the following ways:
Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable yellow gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form.
Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator.
Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance.
Rarely, Topaz can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well.
Like all other gems, Topaz can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.
Topaz Bunny: Gem Bunnies are harmless critters that can only spawn in the Cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Bunnies, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa.
Gem Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Bunny Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Topaz Robe: The Topaz Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. The Topaz Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to burst in a large area of effect when the projectile expires, doing 35% of the original knockback and damage. The Topaz Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4.

Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Topaz Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.
Topaz Squirrel: Gem Squirrels are harmless critters that can only spawn in the cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. There are 7 variants of Gem Squirrels, with each corresponding to a gem type. The spawn chance of each variant depends on the rarity of its respective gem type, meaning the variants corresponding to a more common gem will spawn more often, and vice versa. Gem Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Gem Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Gem Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Squirrel Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Topaz Staff: The Topaz Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires a yellow bolt which does not pierce and explodes upon dissipating, dealing 35% of the weapon's damage (5 base damage) and knockback (base knockback of 1.225 (Extremely weak)) to other nearby enemies within an area, but not to the target hit directly by the bolt. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details).
Torch God's Favor: Torch God's Favor is a permanent booster item that permanently grants the player the ability to automatically convert regular Torches and Campfires in the player's hand to the current biome's torch or campfire variant, which increases the player's torch luck in most areas. The Torch God's Favor can only be obtained by surviving The Torch God event if at least 95 Torches were fired during the event.

Torch God's Favor is a one-time consumable whose effect cannot stack (similar to the Advanced Combat Techniques or the Demon Heart). When first used, the ability is switched on by default and can then be toggled off and on via a toggle appearing to the left of the inventory / in the tools menu below the inventory.
Torches and campfires placed with the ability toggled on will permanently remain converted to the biome variant they were placed as, even if freed and picked up.
Torch God's Flavor: The Torch God's Flavor is a buff potion which grants the Torch Blessing buff when consumed. The buff automatically converts placed Torches near the player to their biome variant, corresponding to the biome the player is in. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Torches: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each.

Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.
Tortured Soul: The Tortured Soul is an uncommon Hardmode enemy found in The Underworld. If the player throws Purification Powder on him, he will transform into the Tax Collector NPC. Afterwards, the Tortured Soul will no longer spawn. Using Clentaminator does not have any effect on him. If the Tax Collector is killed, he will respawn naturally without the need to purify another Tortured Soul. Only one Tortured Soul can be alive at a time.
He is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Toucan: The Toucan is a critter that spawns in the Jungle during the daytime. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. It may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. The Toucan has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Toucan can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Toucan Cage). Once crafted, the Toucan cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Toucan can be spawned by the Toucan Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Town Bunny: The Bunny is a town pet. It arrives at dawn (4:30 AM) the day after the player uses the Bunny License, which is purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold. The Bunny does not count towards the NPCs' "crowded" limit and hence will not affect NPC happiness, although it does count as a regular town NPC for the purpose of the Pylon network. There are six breeds of Bunny, with one randomly being chosen when it arrives. Only one Bunny can be present at a time.

Just like any other town NPC, the Bunny requires a valid house and can be manually assigned to one via its NPC flag. The Bunny can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). It may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for its home tile (standing point).

The Bunny can be talked to with the ⚷ Open / Activate button, like any other town NPC. It offers a “Pet” option, which places the player directly in front of the Bunny when selected, and displays an animation of them petting the Bunny, an effect that is purely visual. It only works if there are at least two flat tiles on the same level as the Bunny in front of it. Using any item, taking damage, or closing the dialogue window terminates the animation.

Like with the Angler and the Princess, the status message displayed when the Bunny is killed is “<Name of Bunny> has left!”. It will respawn within the next days, and may respawn as a different breed. Furthermore, using a Bunny License while a Bunny is already present causes the Bunny to be "exchanged", releasing a puff of smoke and rerolling its breed and name immediately.
Town Cat: The Cat is a town pet. It arrives at dawn (4:30 AM) the day after the player uses the Cat License, which is purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold. The Cat does not count towards the NPCs' "crowded" limit and hence will not affect NPC happiness, although it does count as a regular town NPC for the purpose of the Pylon network. There are six breeds of Cat, with one randomly being chosen when it arrives. Only one Cat can be present at a time.

Just like any other town NPC, the Cat requires a valid house and can be manually assigned to one via its NPC flag. The Cat can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). It may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for its home tile (standing point).

The Cat can be talked to with the ⚷ Open / Activate button, like any other town NPC. It offers a “Pet” option, which places the player directly in front of the Cat when selected, and displays an animation of them petting the Cat, an effect that is purely visual. It only works if there are at least two flat tiles on the same level as the Cat in front of it. Using any item, taking damage, or closing the dialogue window terminates the animation.

Like with the Angler, the status message displayed when the Cat is killed is “<Name of Cat> has left!”. It will respawn within the next days, and may respawn as a different breed. Furthermore, using a Cat License while a Cat is already present causes the Cat to disappear and be "exchanged", releasing a puff of smoke and rerolling its breed and name immediately.
Town Dog: The Dog is a town pet. It arrives at dawn (4:30 AM) the day after the player uses the Dog License, which is purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold. The Dog does not count towards the NPCs' "crowded" limit and hence will not affect NPC happiness, although it does count as a regular town NPC for the purpose of the Pylon network. There are six breeds of Dog, with one randomly being chosen when it arrives. Only one Dog can be present at a time.

Just like any other town NPC, the Dog requires a valid house and can be manually assigned to one via its NPC flag. The Dog can share a house already occupied by another NPC (although not with another town pet). It may not be able to share a house with another NPC if the house is too small, e.g. if there is no space for its home tile (standing point).

The Dog can be talked to with the ⚷ Open / Activate button, like any other town NPC. It offers a “Pet” option, which places the player directly in front of the Dog when selected, and displays an animation of them petting the Dog, an effect that is purely visual. It only works if there are at least two flat tiles on the same level as the Dog in front of it. Using any item, taking damage, or closing the dialogue window terminates the animation.

Like with the Angler, the status message displayed when the Dog is killed is “<Name of Dog> has left!”. It will respawn within the next days, and may respawn as a different breed. Furthermore, using a Dog License while a Dog is already present causes the Dog to disappear and be "exchanged", releasing a puff of smoke and rerolling its breed and name immediately.
Toxic Flask: The Toxic Flask is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic weapon that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance of being dropped by Dr. Man Flies during the Solar Eclipse event. When used, it throws a flask with low velocity and a heavy arc that explodes into a cluster of small, damaging toxic clouds upon colliding with an enemy or surface. The clouds last for one to two seconds and cannot pass through blocks.
Toxic Sludge: The Toxic Sludge is a Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Underground layer in place of ordinary slimes. It deals significantly increased damage and has a 1/2 (50%) chance of inflicting the Poisoned debuff for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds, which it is also immune to.
Like most other slimes, the Toxic Sludge will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
Toxikarp: The Toxikarp is a Hardmode ranged weapon that can be obtained extremely rarely by fishing in the Corruption biome in any layer.

When used, it fires greenish bubbles that travel in the direction aimed for a short distance before ascending rapidly and inflict the Poisoned debuff for 10–29 seconds. If the bubbles do not strike a creature or a block, they will eventually ascend into space. The bubbles can pass through platforms without breaking. If they come into contact with water, they will instantly start to ascend instead. The Toxikarp has infinite ammunition and will continue to launch bubbles as long as the player is firing it.
It is the Corruption counterpart to the Crimson's Bladetongue, the Hallow's Crystal Serpent, and the Jungle's Barnacle Staff.
Toy Sled: The Toy Sled is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Snowman that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Snowman rides in a toy sled to catch up to them. The Toy Sled has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Ice Mimics.
Toy Tank: The Toy Tank is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Santank Mount. The mount is notable for having a double jump as well as two auto-targeting weapons attached; a front-facing machine gun and a homing rocket launcher. The Toy Tank is dropped by Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event in Master Mode with a 6.25–25% chance depending on the current wave.

The maximum movement speed of the mount is 41 mph, and it takes about 1.5 seconds to reach top speed. The maximum jump height is 12 tiles without a double jump, or 26 tiles with the double jump when timed right. The double jump can be stacked with other double jump accessories. The Santank is 2 tiles wide and 3 tiles tall, meaning that it does not change the player's height and makes it easier to travel through narrower corridors than with larger mounts such as the Unicorn Mount and Pirate Ship Mount.

The Santank's two attached weapons only fire if there are enemies in front of the player. The machine gun's bullets deal 100 base damage and are fired in a spread of 22.9°, making the weapon somewhat inaccurate. The homing rockets are initially fired directly upwards, deal 120 base damage, and seek the closest target after being fired, including targets that are outside the mount's initial detection range (e.g. enemies behind the player). The damage of the projectiles does not scale with any damage bonuses the player has, but their critical strike chance is affected by the player's ranged critical strike chance. The machine gun fires a bullet every 0.17 seconds (i.e. 6 shots per second), while the rocket launcher fires a rocket every 0.67 seconds.
Toybreaker Brick: The Toybreaker Brick is a Hardmode, post-Plantera brick sold by the Cyborg for 2 Silver. It despawns "toy" projectiles upon contact, returning them to the player's inventory. It affects projectiles from the following items:
Glowstick, Sticky Glowstick, Bouncy Glowstick, Spelunker Glowstick, Rainbow Glowstick, Fairy Glowstick
Tragic Umbrella: The Tragic Umbrella is a pre-Hardmode melee weapon and held item that can be purchased from the Clothier for 10 Gold while in a Graveyard. It functions identical to the standard Umbrella, aside from dealing higher damage.
While held, the Tragic Umbrella appears above the character, allowing them to fall at a slower rate than normal and preventing fall damage. The player can hold ▼ Down to increase the fall speed.
Trap Door: Trap Doors are furniture items. They are essentially full-block horizontal Doors. Trap Doors can be opened using ⚷ Open / Activate, causing them to expand into a 2x2 block. They fulfill a house's door requirement.

Trap Doors open upward if the character opening it is below the Trap Door's level, and downward if above. The reference point for character altitude seems to be the character's center, not the feet: the character's feet can be about one half tile below the bottom of a closed Trap Door (standing on a stair), and the door will still open downward.

Trap Doors can be blocked by furniture and will then always open on the free side, regardless of character position. If a Trap Door is blocked on both sides, it will not open. An open Trap Door is too narrow to be used at the end of a ramp or stairway so that a character can climb through it without jumping, as it needs to be surrounded by solid blocks, not platforms or other Trap Doors.
Like normal doors, Trap Doors can be wired to be opened and closed remotely.
Unlike normal doors, Trap Doors cannot be opened by Zombies during a Blood Moon event and can be useful for early players in defending their base.
Trapped Chests: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire.
Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.
Trash Can: The Trash Can is a storage item with 40 storage slots. It is functionally identical to Chests; it does not delete items like the Trash Slot in the player's inventory.
Traveling Merchant: The Traveling Merchant is a unique NPC vendor who randomly visits the player's town for one in-game day. His inventory is randomized and different every visit, selling approximately 4–10 different items listed below.

In order for the Traveling Merchant to spawn, at least 2 other NPCs must already be present. The Guide counts as one of these, but the Old Man and Skeleton Merchant do not. He will not spawn during Solar Eclipses, the Goblin Army, Frost Legion, Pirate Invasion, or Martian Madness. He does not require his own house in order to spawn, and will instead spawn next to NPCs, including town pets, spending the day walking around them.

Once the criteria are met, the Traveling Merchant has a random chance of appearing between 4:30 AM and 12:00 PM. He leaves the same day at 6:00 PM, but can only do so once he is off-screen. He despawns if the world is exited.
If threatened by enemies, the Traveling Merchant will defend himself with a Revolver. Once Hardmode begins, he upgrades to a Pulse Bow.
Treasure Bag: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag-like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses. The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory, or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar. They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer, each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details.

Each Treasure Bag contains the boss's usual drops from Classic Mode, along with one Expert Mode-exclusive item (highlighted items below) – with the exception of the Lunatic Cultist, Dark Mage, Ogre, and Betsy, who do not provide an Expert Mode-exclusive item. Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses additionally have a 1/16 (6.25%) chance to contain one random set of developer items (with the exception of Queen Slime).
Expert Mode-exclusive items all have the rarity, with the exception of developer items, which have the rarity.
Treasure Hunter set: The Treasure Hunter set is a vanity set. It consists of a Treasure Hunter Shirt and Treasure Hunter Pants. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance of being obtained from opening Goodie Bags.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Treasure Magnet: The Treasure Magnet is a post-Skeletron accessory which increases the pickup range of items from 2.625 tiles to 12 tiles while equipped. When an item is within its range, before directly flying to the player, it will hover a few blocks off the ground. The Treasure Magnet has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.
Treasure Map: The Treasure Map is a decorative wall hanging randomly obtained as a reward for Angler fishing quests (1% chance).
Tree Globe: The Tree Globe is a thrown consumable item sold by the Zoologist for 3 Gold after 50% of the Bestiary (273 entries) has been filled out. When a Tree Globe is thrown and shatters on a surface, all of the trees in the current biome will switch to another random style.
Tree set: The Tree set is a vanity set consisting of the Tree Mask, Tree Shirt, and Tree Trunks. It is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode. Its male and female variants look identical.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Trident: The Trident is a pre-Hardmode spear that has a 9/40 (22.5%) chance of being found in Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates. When held while submerged in water or lava, the player is granted increased movement speed and jump height. The player can decrease fall speed by holding ▲ Up. These effects do not work in honey or Shimmer.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Trifold Map: The Trifold Map is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Confused debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Clowns, Giant Bats, and Light Mummies.
Trimarang: The Trimarang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang crafted using three different boomerangs. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not have to return to the player before being fired, with a maximum of three Trimarangs that can be thrown out at one time.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Trophies: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 35 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.
Tropical Smoothie: The Tropical Smoothie is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Trout: Trout are a type of fish which are found plentifully by fishing in the Ocean in the Sky or Surface layers.
True Copper Shortsword: The True Copper Shortsword is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord melee weapon obtained by throwing the Zenith into Shimmer. It functions completely identically to the Zenith, but every sword used in its attack animation is replaced with the Copper Shortsword. Throwing the True Copper Shortsword into Shimmer separates it into the component swords used to craft the Zenith.
True Excalibur: The True Excalibur is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses broadsword and the direct upgrade to the Excalibur. When swung, a large yellow aura with a pink edge follows the swing, reaching about twice the distance of the sword itself. The aura can hit up to six enemies.
True Night's Edge: The True Night's Edge is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses broadsword and the direct upgrade to the Night's Edge. When swung, a circular purple aura follows the swing, reaching farther than the sword itself. The aura can hit up to two enemies. The sword will also fire a spinning green blade that deals 50% of the weapon's damage (35 base damage) and can strike up to 3 times.
Truffle: The Truffle is a Hardmode NPC vendor who sells various mushroom-themed items. He can arrive homelessly as soon as Hardmode starts, and he can only move into vacant houses that are located in (or near) a surface Glowing Mushroom biome (i.e. one that is above 0 elevation).

Surface Glowing Mushroom biomes do not generate naturally and therefore must be manually created. 100 tiles of Mushroom grass and Glowing Mushroom plants are required to create a Glowing Mushroom biome.

If the Truffle spawns into a vacant house in a surface Glowing Mushroom biome, he is considered unlocked and can then be reassigned to a house at any elevation, as long as it is in a Glowing Mushroom biome. Moving a homeless Truffle into suitable house is not considered unlocking him; in this case, he can only be reassigned into houses in surface Glowing Mushroom biomes.

After the Truffle dies, if the Truffle is unlocked, he can respawn into vacant houses located in Glowing Mushroom biomes at any height; if he is not unlocked, he can only respawn into vacant houses located in surface Glowing Mushroom biomes. Otherwise, he can only respawn homelessly.
When threatened by enemies, the Truffle will release Mushroom Spores, which hover in midair and explode into spore clouds upon contact with enemies.
Truffle Worm: The Truffle Worm is a rare Hardmode critter and boss-summoning item that spawns in the underground Glowing Mushroom biome. It summons Duke Fishron when used as bait. It can only be used in the Ocean, at any time. It emits a small amount of light.

The Truffle Worm can be caught with a Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net and Golden Bug Net, however, it is more difficult to catch than other critters, as it burrows away when a player comes too close. It must be approached quickly in order to successfully catch it. After being caught, it can be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Truffle Worm Cage). Once crafted, the Truffle Worm cannot be released again unless decrafted via Shimmer.
Tsunami: The Tsunami is a Hardmode bow that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it fires a volley of five parallel arrows, consuming one arrow per use.
Tsunami in a Bottle: The Tsunami in a Bottle is an accessory which can be found in Wooden, Iron, Pearlwood (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Mythril Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Similar to the Cloud in a Bottle, it allows the player to double-jump. Instead of a cloud beneath the player's feet, it creates burst of water when jumping. The Tsunami jump goes 7 tiles into the air, totalling 13 tiles when put together with the first jump.
Tuna: Tuna are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in the Ocean in the Sky or Surface layers.
Tungsten Axe: The Tungsten Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Axe.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Tungsten Bar: The Tungsten Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Bar.
Tungsten Bow: The Tungsten Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Tungsten Brick: Tungsten Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Like the ore it is made of, placed Tungsten Bricks will sparkle. It is not recommended that it be used for building unless the player has tungsten to spare. Despite being made of Tungsten, it has no sell value. It can be crafted into Tungsten Brick Walls.
Tungsten Brick Wall: Tungsten Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Tungsten Bricks. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.
Tungsten Broadsword: The Tungsten Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Tungsten Shortsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Broadsword.
Tungsten Bullet: The Tungsten Bullet is a pre-Hardmode bullet. It deals 2 more damage and is slightly faster than Musket Balls. When either Musket Balls or Tungsten Bullets are fired with certain guns, they will be converted into a special projectile (e.g. the Uzi converting them into High Velocity Bullets). Some other guns, such as the Pew-matic Horn, can convert any type of bullet.

Tungsten Bullets can be bought from the Arms Dealer for 18 Copper each, or 1 Gold 80 Silver for 1000 rounds in worlds with Tungsten. During pre-Hardmode, they are only sold during Blood Moons. Once Hardmode begins, they are always available. Tungsten Bullets can also be found replacing Wooden Arrows in Pots during Hardmode, in Shadow Chests, or crafted using Tungsten Bars.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Bullet.
Tungsten Hammer: The Tungsten Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Hammer.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Tungsten Ore: Tungsten Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on Floating Islands. Tungsten Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Silver Ore.
Tungsten Pickaxe: The Tungsten Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Meteorite.

Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Pickaxe. The Tungsten Pickaxe has a significantly slower mining speed, but significantly more pickaxe power; it takes fewer hits to destroy blocks (e.g. 1 hit instead of 2 for Dirt Blocks, and 2 hits instead of 3 for Stone Blocks). Unlike the Silver Pickaxe, it can also mine Meteorite.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Tungsten Shortsword: The Tungsten Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Tungsten Broadsword.
Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Shortsword.
Tungsten armor: Tungsten armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Tungsten Helmet, Tungsten Chainmail, and Tungsten Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Tungsten Bars (240 Tungsten Ore). The full set grants 15 defense while equipped.
Its alternate ore counterpart is Silver armor.
Turtle: The Turtle is a critter which can spawn in bodies of water in the Forest during the day. They move slowly on land and swim at the surface of water. The Turtle has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Turtle can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Turtle Cage). Once crafted, the Turtle cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Turtle can be spawned by the Turtle Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Turtle Shell: The Turtle Shell is a Hardmode crafting material. It has a 1/12 (8.33%) chance of being dropped by Giant Tortoises, which spawn in the Jungle and Underground Jungle.
Turtle armor: Turtle armor is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses melee armor set consisting of the Turtle Helmet, Turtle Scale Mail, and Turtle Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore) and 3 Turtle Shells.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Stronger Thorns effect upon taking contact damage, which inflicts 200% of the enemy's contact damage back at them and applies a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong).
A visual turtle shell also appears on the player's back.
Tuxedo set: The Tuxedo set is a vanity set consisting of the Top Hat, Tuxedo Shirt and Tuxedo Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
While the other two pieces are crafted, the Top Hat is instead dropped by The Groom.
Twilight Dye: Twilight Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It can, like other dyes, be equipped in the dyes slot in the player's equipment or accessory tabs in their inventory. When the dye is used, the armor or vanity item associated with it will get a very night-sky-like effect which will move dynamically with the player.
Twilight Grasp: The Twilight Grasp is a Hardmode accessory that grants the following effects while equipped:
Twinkle Popper: The Twinkle Popper is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Stardust Pillar during the Lunar Events. It walks slowly until it is within the line-of-sight of the player, at which point it stops in place and attacks the player by vomiting up smaller enemies called Twinkles, which run around and can explode into an upwards spray of 3 damaging sparkles when close to the player or after 4 seconds have passed. Killing the Twinkles prevents them from exploding into sparkles.
Ugly Sweater: The Ugly Sweater is a vanity item dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode.
Ultrabright Helmet: The Ultrabright Helmet is an armor piece for the helmet slot that combines the functionalities of the Mining Helmet and the Night Vision Helmet.
Umbrella: The Umbrella is a pre-Hardmode melee weapon. It has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being obtained from wooden Chests on the Surface or in the Underground layer, and can also be purchased for 1 Gold from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waning Gibbous.
When held, the Umbrella appears above the character, allowing the player to fall at a slower rate and preventing fall damage. The player can hold ▼ Down to increase the fall speed.
If the player is in a world using the Vampirism secret world seed, the Umbrella can be held to prevent burning in the sunlight.
Umbrella Hat: The Umbrella Hat is a vanity item that has a 1/45 (2.22%) chance to drop from Umbrella Slimes during the Rain event.
Umbrella Slime: The Umbrella Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns during rainy days on the surface, holding an umbrella. It is larger than and statistically superior to Blue and Green Slimes.
Like most other slimes, the Umbrella Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel accessory equipped.
Undead Miner: The Undead Miner is a pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Cavern layer. Undead Miners wear a Mining Helmet, which provides a small amount of light around them. This light makes them much easier to find and can sometimes reveal sealed caves, much like blooming Blinkroot.
Killing them is the only way to obtain the Bone Pickaxe, Mining Shirt, and the Mining Pants. The Mining Helmet can be obtained from Undead Miners, but can also be bought from the Merchant for 4 Gold.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Undead Viking: The Undead Viking is a pre-Hardmode enemy found in the Ice biome. It behaves similarly to the Skeleton, but spawns more frequently and jumps higher.
Unholy Arrow: The Unholy Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It can pierce 4 enemies, and its damage decreases by 5% per enemy pierced.

In addition to being crafted, Unholy Arrows are dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu. Furthermore, they can be purchased from the Arms Dealer at night for 40 Copper each once the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu has been defeated. In Hardmode, these restrictions are lifted and Unholy Arrows are available at any time.
Unholy Trident: The Unholy Trident is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss wand that fires high-velocity purple tridents which lose speed as they travel and have 25 armor penetration, and inflict the Shadowflame debuff for 5–10 seconds on hit. Upon contact with blocks, the tridents briefly become stuck and will deal damage to enemies that touch them. The Unholy Trident has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Red Devils.
Unicorn: The Unicorn is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Hallow. It is a very fast enemy that has a rather large amount of health and can jump approximately 7 tiles high and 20 tiles wide. The Unicorn leaps around and charges, attempting to trample the player. Its unpredictable and speedy behavior, combined with a high damage output, can make fighting it difficult. It always drops one Unicorn Horn, a valued item. It also rarely drops the Blessed Apple, a strong Mount-summoning item for early Hardmode.
Unicorn Horn: The Unicorn Horn is a Hardmode crafting material that is always dropped by Unicorns in The Hallow.
Unicorn Wisp Dye: Unicorn Wisp Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye that can be acquired by bringing a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it turns the affected item into a deep shade of pink, and produces a glow effect similar to that of the Wisp in a Bottle.
Unicorn on a Stick: The Unicorn on a Stick is a Hardmode novelty item which, when selected, is held stationary in front of the player to provide the illusion that they are riding a unicorn. It has no real function, unlike the Unicorn Mount. The Unicorn on a Stick has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Unicorns.
Unicorn set: The Unicorn set is a vanity set consisting of the Unicorn Mask, Unicorn Shirt, and Unicorn Pants. It can be obtained from Goodie Bags, which are dropped by enemies with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance during the Halloween seasonal event.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Universal Pylon: The Universal Pylon is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pylon obtained by completing 100% of the Bestiary, at which point it will be sold by the Zoologist for 1 Platinum.
It can be placed anywhere, and used in any biome. Unlike other pylon variants, it does not require a nearby NPC to function. Only one Universal Pylon can be placed in a world.
Unlucky Yarn: The Unlucky Yarn is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Black Cat that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Black Cat flies on a broom to catch up with them. The Unlucky Yarn has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being obtained from Goodie Bags during the Halloween seasonal event.
Uzi: The Uzi is a Hardmode gun that has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Angry Trappers. When used, it rapidly fires bullets at a high velocity. It also converts Musket Balls and Tungsten Bullets (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) into High Velocity Bullets, giving them the special effects but not affecting their damage.
Valhalla Knight armor: Valhalla Knight armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Valhalla Knight's Helm, Valhalla Knight's Breastplate, and Valhalla Knight's Greaves. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 150 Defender Medals.
The Valhalla Knight armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Squire armor.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:
Ballista sentry summons have increased projectile velocity, greatly increased fire rate (from 3.1 seconds to 2.1 seconds), and increased pierce (3 to 6).
Upon taking damage, grants the Ballista Panic! buff for 5 seconds, increasing the fire rate of all Ballista sentries summoned by the player (from 2.1 seconds to 0.93 seconds).
Valkyrie Yoyo: The Valkyrie Yoyo is a Hardmode, Expert Mode-exclusive yoyo that can be obtained from any Hardmode boss's Treasure Bag (except Queen Slime's) as part of Lazure's set.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Valor: The Valor is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron yoyo that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Vampire: The Vampire is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Solar Eclipse event. It will transform into a bat if the player is far enough away from it, and attempts to fly near the player at high speed before turning back into a humanoid. It inflicts the Bleeding debuff upon contact with the player for 5–7 / 10–14 / 12.5–17.5 seconds.
Vampire Frog Staff: The Vampire Frog Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Vampire Frog minion. It hops towards enemies to deal contact damage. The Vampire Frog Staff has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen.
Vampire Knives: The Vampire Knives are a Hardmode, post-Plantera melee weapon. When used, it rapidly fires a spread of 4–8 red knife projectiles. Upon hitting an enemy, each knife causes a lifesteal effect that heals the player for 7.5% of the damage dealt (rounded down), signified by a red beam connecting to the player. The knives will eventually decrease in damage and fade after traveling a certain distance.
The Vampire Knives are always found in the Dungeon's Crimson Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Crimson Key after Plantera has been defeated.
Their best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Vampire set: The Vampire set is a vanity set obtained from Goodie Bags, which drop from all enemies with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance during the Halloween seasonal event. It consists of a Vampire Mask, Vampire Shirt and Vampire Pants.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The Vampire set can be found in naturally-generated chests in the Vampirism secret world seed.
Variegated Lardfish: Variegated Lardfish are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in the Underground Jungle. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Summoning Potions.
Vasculash: The Vasculash is a pre-Hardmode whip. It has a 40% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:
It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Soulscourge. Compared to Soulscourge, the Vasculash has 2 more base damage, slightly lower knockback, and 1 less tile of range.
Vases: Vases are non-craftable furniture items. They can be found either in the Dungeon or the Underworld and can be mined with any pickaxe or drill.
Venom Arrow: The Venom Arrow is a Hardmode, post-Plantera arrow. It has the highest base damage of all arrows and inflicts the Acid Venom debuff on hit for 10 seconds, as well as the Potent Acid debuff for 2 seconds.
Venom Bullet: The Venom Bullet is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bullet. It creates a conical splash of venom upon impact that afflicts the target it struck, as well as those within the area, with the Potent Acid debuff for two seconds and Acid Venom for 10.

Venom Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Venom Bullets is 17 Silver 50 Copper, which is 35 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Venom Bullets is 35 Gold.
Venom Dart Trap: The Venom Dart Trap is a Hardmode trap that fires a venomous dart when triggered via wire. It is a direct upgrade to the Dart Trap. It has a cooldown period of 3 1/3 seconds between firings. The darts deal 60 / 120 / 180 damage to players and 30 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters, as well as inflicting Acid Venom for 5 / 10 / 12.5 seconds to players (75/150/187.5 damage) and 5 seconds of Acid Venom to NPCs, enemies, and critters (150 damage).
Venom Dart Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer.
Venom Dart Traps do not generate naturally, and can only be obtained via crafting.
Venom Staff: The Venom Staff is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses wand and the direct upgrade to the Poison Staff. When used, it fires a burst of 4–7 Venom Fangs in a spread. Each projectile pierces four enemies and inflicts the Acid Venom debuff for 30 seconds.
Venus Magnum: The Venus Magnum is a Hardmode gun that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When used, it converts Musket Balls and Tungsten Bullets into High Velocity Bullets, giving them the special effects but not affecting their damage.
Vertebra: The Vertebra (Vertebrae (Old-gen console and 3DS versions)) is a crafting material that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Crimeras, Blood Crawlers, Face Monsters, Floaty Grosses.
Vial of Venom: The Vial of Venom is a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Witch Doctor for 15 Silver each, after Plantera has been defeated.
Vicious Bunny: The Vicious Bunny is a pre-Hardmode enemy that results from a Bunny that has been corrupted, either by the player using Vicious Powder on it or when a Bunny spawns during a Blood Moon in a Crimson world.
Vicious Goldfish: The Vicious Goldfish is a pre-Hardmode enemy that results from a Goldfish being corrupted, either by the player using Vicious Powder on it or when a Goldfish spawns during a Blood Moon in a Crimson world.
Vicious Mushroom: The Vicious Mushroom is a type of mushroom growing on Crimson grass or Crimson Jungle grass, where they can be cut and collected with a single swing of any weapon or tool. Vicious Mushroom can only grow when there are proper walls behind the soil block, or no walls at all.
Vicious Mushroom cannot be eaten or brewed into any potions; they are used solely to craft Vicious Powder.
Vicious Penguin: The Vicious Penguin is a pre-Hardmode enemy that results from a Penguin that has been corrupted, either by the player using Vicious Powder on it or when a Penguin spawns during a Blood Moon in a Crimson world.
Victorian Goth set: The Victorian Goth set is a vanity set consisting of the Victorian Goth Hat and Victorian Goth Dress.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) when he is spoken to in the Graveyard biome.
Viking Helmet: The Viking Helmet is an armor piece for the helmet slot. It has a 1/50 (2%) chance to be dropped by Undead Vikings in the Ice biome. It provides a sizeable amount of defense (as much as a Gold Helmet or Tungsten Helmet), but it does not have an associated set or set bonus, hindering its utility.
Vile Ghoul: Ghouls are Hardmode Underground Desert enemies who follow the Fighter AI (behaving similarly to Zombies). Ordinary Ghouls spawn inside the normal Underground Desert, the Vile Ghoul inside Corrupt parts of the Underground Desert, the Tainted Ghoul inside Crimson parts of the Underground Desert, and the Dreamer Ghoul inside Hallowed parts of the Underground Desert.
Vile Mushroom: The Vile Mushroom is a type of mushroom growing on Corrupt grass or Corrupt Jungle grass, where they can be cut and collected with a single swing from any weapon or tool. Vile Mushroom can only grow when there are proper walls behind the soil block, or no walls at all.
Vile Mushrooms cannot be eaten or brewed into any potions; they are used solely to craft Vile Powder.
Vilethorn: The Vilethorn is a pre-Hardmode wand. It has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Shadow Orbs found in The Corruption or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Corrupt Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Defiled Crates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). When used, it extends a thorn from the player's position, which passes through blocks, pierces infinite enemies, and deals 0.17 s global invincibility.
The thorn has 7 segments, and each has a length of 2 tiles. The thorn extends segmentally every 0.1 s, with each individual segment lasting 0.95 s.
Its Crimson counterpart is the Crimson Rod.

Its best modifier is Ruthless on Desktop and Mythical elsewhere. This is due to differences in how damage is rounded between versions, with Mythical Vilethorn dealing 11 damage on vanilla desktop versions and 12 elsewhere.
Vine: Vines are crafting materials dropped by Man Eaters in the Underground Jungle biome with a 1/2 (50%) / 100% drop chance.
Violet Husk: The Violet Husk is a dye material that is dropped by Lac Beetles, which only spawn in the Underground Jungle. Its sole purpose is to make Violet Dye.
Vital Crystal: The Vital Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's health regeneration. It can only be used once per player and is obtained by throwing a Life Crystal into Shimmer.
Vitamins: Vitamins are a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Weak debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Corruptors and Floaty Grosses.
Voice accessories: Voice accessories are a type of vanity accessory that change the sound the player makes when taking damage while they are equipped. Some also change the player's death sound. All voice accessories can be used with the ⚒ Use / Attack button to play the sound at any time.

All naturally generated Chests have a 1/12 (8.33%) chance to contain a random voice accessory as secondary loot, with the exception of the Whoopie Cushion. As there are 14 different options, the chance for a single given voice accessory to be found in a Chest is 1/168 (0.6%). The Whoopie Cushion is dropped by Giant Worms and Diggers with a 1/50 (2%) / 99/2500 (3.96%) chance, and can also be obtained by throwing a Zombie Arm into Shimmer. In Skyblock worlds, a random voice acccessory (except for the Whoopie Cushion) can be also dropped by the Voice accessory Slimes that very rarely spawn below surface.
Voice accessories cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Void Bag: The Void Bag is a portable storage item that grants the player access to the Void Vault anywhere. When used, it will summon a temporary portal which lasts for 3 minutes, and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the portal opens the player's Void Vault inventory. The Void Bag is never consumed and can be used limitlessly.
Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Void Bag item in the inventory turns it into the Closed Void Bag. Pressing the button again opens the Void Bag again.

When opened, the Void Vault storage will effectively act as the player's secondary inventory, which automatically stores items collected after the player's main inventory is full, indicated by a purple mask on the pickup text.
