Additionally, it also allows the player to interact with the items inside it as if they were in the main inventory without opening the Void Vault storage interface.

When closed, the Void Bag functions similarly to the Money Trough / Eye Bone, only acting as a regular portable storage item. This will prevent it from picking up items when the player has a full inventory, and it loses the function of the secondary inventory.
Void Dye: Void Dye is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord dye crafted using Luminite Bars. The dye causes a pulsating effect, much like the pulsating effect that the Moon Lord creates moments before he spawns.
Void Vault: The Void Vault is a placeable portable storage item that extends the player's inventory in a manner similar to the Piggy Bank, Safe, and Defender's Forge. Like all other storage items, the Void Vault provides 40 slots of storage.

The Void Vault can also be accessed via the Void Bag, similar to the way a player can access the Piggy Bank using a Money Trough. When the player's inventory is full and a Void Bag is present in the inventory, newly collected items are placed in the Void Vault (indicated by purple pickup text). If the Void Bag in the player's inventory is opened, it also allows the player to interact with the items inside the Void Vault as if they were in the main inventory without opening the storage interface. See Void Bag § Notes for details.
Volatile Gelatin: The Volatile Gelatin is a Hardmode accessory that periodically fires small, purple slimeballs similar to those of the Queen Slime's Regal Gel projectiles at nearby enemies. The Volatile Gelatin's projectiles are affected by gravity and can pierce up to two entities or ricochet up to two times, dissipating upon the third time. The projectiles deal 65 classless damage while inflicting a knockback value of 7 (Strong); these values are unaffected by any boosts. The Volatile Gelatin is always dropped from Queen Slime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

The Volatile Gelatin has a fixed cycle: once every 0.67 seconds (40 ticks), it attempts to release a projectile towards the nearest enemy within 40 tiles that has unobstructed line of sight to the player. If there are no valid targets, no projectile will be fired and the accessory will go on cooldown for the following 40 ticks.
Volcano: The Volcano is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it creates an explosion upon enemy hits, dealing 75% of the weapon's damage (30 base damage) to the enemy and 2 other targets in an area around the enemy. The Volcano has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3 seconds, while its explosion is guaranteed to inflict it for the same duration.
Voodoo Demon: The Voodoo Demon is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in The Underworld. It is identical to the Demon in behavior, but differs slightly in appearance: a small Guide Voodoo Doll hangs upside-down from one of its talons, and it lacks the blue bracelets and anklets that are worn by regular Demons.

Voodoo Demons will always drop a Guide Voodoo Doll when killed. Due to the terrain of the Underworld, defeating a Voodoo Demon may result in an unwanted summoning of the Wall of Flesh if the doll falls into one of the many large bodies of lava throughout the Underworld.
It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or its upgrades.
Vortex Beater: The Vortex Beater is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist gun. When used, it very rapidly fires bullets with inaccurate spread. It also fires a homing, explosive Vortex Rocket every 0.583 seconds without consuming additional ammo, which deals damage equal to the weapon's damage + 20 damage (50 + 7 + 20 = 77 base damage when using Musket Balls), and a knockback of 1.25× the weapon's knockback (base knockback of 5 (Average) when using Musket Balls). The Vortex Beater also has a 2/3 (66.67%) chance not to consume ammunition.
Its best modifier is Unreal, Godly or Demonic, as it does not benefit from attack speed and velocity modifiers.
Vortex Brick: The Vortex Brick is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist brick that is crafted from Vortex Fragments. It is one of the four Fragment Bricks, bricks which are crafted with Lunar Fragments. It glows when placed and can be used to craft Vortex furniture.
Vortex Brick Wall: Vortex Brick Wall is a background wall made from Vortex Bricks.
Vortex Dye: Vortex Dye is a Hardmode dye crafted from Vortex Fragments dropped by the Vortex Pillar in the Lunar Events and Bottled Water. The effect produced is reminiscent of a green warp drive effect on all clothing and accessories the dye is applied to.
Vortex Fragment: The Vortex Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist crafting material. It is one of the four Lunar Fragments, dropped from the Vortex Pillar during the Lunar Events in stacks of 12–60 / 24–100. Vortex Fragments can be used to craft Vortex armor, an end-game armor set that benefits all types of ranged weapons, as well as Vortex-themed tools, weapons, wings, etc.

Crafting all items requires 121 Vortex Fragments and 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite), which necessitates defeating the Vortex Pillar at least 3–11 / 2–8 times (note that the Vortex Fragment can also be crafted from the other fragments) and fighting the Moon Lord at least 4 / 3–4 times.
Vortex Fragment Block: Vortex Fragment Blocks are blocks made from Vortex Fragments which are dropped by the Vortex Pillar. The blocks have a crystal-like appearance with intense shades of green and blue. They can be crafted with the Ancient Manipulator. Walls cannot be crafted with them.
Vortex Pillar: The Celestial Pillars (also known as the Lunar Pillars, Lunar Towers, or Celestial Towers) are four late-Hardmode, stationary bosses that appear during the Lunar Events after the Lunatic Cultist has been defeated. To break their protective shields, 100 of the unique enemies that spawn in a large surrounding area must be defeated. Pillars drop Lunar Fragments when destroyed, and destroying all four of them results in the spawn of the Moon Lord.

The four Celestial Pillars are the Solar Pillar, the Vortex Pillar, the Nebula Pillar, and the Stardust Pillar. They represent the four damage types in Terraria: Solar for melee, Vortex for ranged, Nebula for magic, and Stardust for summon. After the defeat of the Lunatic Cultist, they appear at four locations equally spaced across the map (see pillar spawning mechanics below), and do not move apart from slowly bobbing up and down in place. Each pillar takes control of the world in a circular area around it with a radius of 250 tiles (500 feet). When the player is in that affected area, the background will change to a pillar-specific one, and only pillar-specific enemies will spawn in large numbers.

Initially, each Celestial Pillar has a large shield around it which prevents it from taking any damage. In order to remove the shield, the player must kill 100 enemies corresponding to that specific pillar, which are the major threat of the Lunar Events; they can deal high amounts of damage, inflict debuffs, and easily swarm the player if not dealt with quickly. The enemy kill count does not reset if the player dies, but leaving the world does reset it.

Defeating pillar-specific enemies releases small red energy particles that travel to the pillar shield to indicate the progress. Once the kill count of a pillar is reached, its shield is lowered and it becomes vulnerable to damage. The pillars themselves are fairly easy to defeat, being extremely large and immobile, and having only 20,000 health each and only fairly weak or no attacks. However, enemies continue to spawn even after the shield is lowered, until the pillar is defeated.
There is no set order in which the Celestial Pillars must be defeated. The following status messages will appear from whichever pillars are taken down first, second, third, and fourth:
First pillar defeated: "Your mind goes numb..."
Second pillar defeated: "You are overwhelmed with pain..."
Third pillar defeated: "Otherworldly voices linger around you..."
After defeating the fourth Celestial Pillar, the screen starts to vibrate and the music volume lowers before eventually going completely silent. After 60 seconds, the Moon Lord will spawn.
After defeating the Moon Lord, each pillar will only require 50 of their respective enemies killed to lower their shields instead of 100.
Vortex armor: Vortex armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord ranged armor set consisting of the Vortex Helmet, Vortex Breastplate, and Vortex Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Vortex Fragments.
The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

The ability to toggle stealth by double-tapping the ▼ Down key, which causes the player to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using any item. Stealth is engaged over the period of 0.42 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values:

Moving or grappling does not cancel stealth mode, but dashing or riding a mount does. Taking damage reveals the player and removes the stealth mode bonuses, and it takes another 0.42 seconds to fully engage stealth mode again.

As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details).
Vortexian: The Vortexian is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist enemy that spawns in the area of the Vortex Pillar during the Lunar Events. It walks towards the player, trying to deal contact damage. Upon death, a portal is summoned that shoots a lightning bolt aimed at the player, indicated by a glowing line, similar to one of the attacks of the Lunatic Cultist and the lightning portal of the Vortex Pillar. They are powerful in packs, and can potentially start an overwhelming lightning chain reaction if not dealt with properly.
Vulgar Display of Flower: The Vulgar Display of Flower is a Hardmode whip that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. It has a 15% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit:

Marks enemies with volatile energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by the Vulgar Display of Flower, 3 to 6 petals are released that home in on enemies after a short delay. All the petals together deal 2.25× of the minion/sentry's hit damage in total with the damage being evenly split between them, regardless of how many are released. The petals do not pierce, have 50 armor penetration, and do not inflict knockback. The volatile energy is only applied to the first enemy hit by each swing and expires after the petals are released from an enemy, meaning the enemy must be tagged again to reapply it, but the tag damage will still last for its usual duration.
Vulkelf Ears: Vulkelf Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.
Vulture: The Vulture is a pre-Hardmode flying enemy that commonly spawns in Deserts during the day; however, they can also spawn roosting on Sand Blocks in any biome. When the player comes close or attacks a Vulture, it will begin to fly at the player. Vultures will hover above the player for a second before swooping down to attack. They will continue to pursue the player until they die.
Waffle's Iron: Waffle's Iron is a Hardmode broadsword that is always dropped by Mechdusa, a boss exclusive to worlds with both Remix and For the Worthy enabled. When swung, it fires a waffle projectile once per swing, which is significantly affected by gravity. The weapon itself also has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Hellfire debuff upon contact for 5 seconds.
Wall Anchor: The Wall Anchor is a wall decoration acquired by completing Angler NPC quests.
Wall Creeper: The Wall Creeper is a pre-Hardmode enemy that can be found in and around Spider Nests in the Cavern layer, mostly during pre-Hardmode. Wall Creepers are spider-like enemies capable of climbing background walls as well as through platforms, but revert to acting like fighter enemies when there are no background walls for them to climb on.
Wall Racer Car: The Wall Racer Car is a Hardmode, post-Plantera novelty item purchased from the Cyborg for 10 Gold. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button while selected in the hotbar summons a harmless car that can be controlled by the ◀ Left, and ▶ Right buttons and the ↷ Jump to jump. Holding ▲ Up while the car is mid-air will cause it to do front flips. If jump is pressed while the car is mid-air, the car will switch modes to instead drive on any placed walls and be controlled by the left and right button to steer, up and down button to move forward or backwards, and the jump button to jump off the wall. Pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again or switching to another item instantly destroys the car. The player appears to wield a remote control when the car is in use.
The player is locked in place while the car is active. Equipping the FPV Goggles will center the camera on the car.
Wall Skeleton: The Wall Skeleton is a Decorative Furniture item that can be placed on walls, similar to Paintings. Wall Skeletons can only be obtained by looting them from the Dungeon, where they only appear in areas backed by Slab Walls.
Wall of Flesh: The Wall of Flesh is the final pre-Hardmode boss. Once it is defeated, the world permanently converts to Hardmode, which brings new content and challenges.

To defeat the Wall of Flesh, the player must attack either its eyes or its mouth. They all share the same health counter, so attacking any of the three will deplete the total health of the boss. However, the eyes have less defense (thus take more damage) than the mouth. No other parts of the Wall of Flesh can be damaged.
See below for information on the two exclusive debuffs from the boss, Horrified and The Tongue.
While the Wall of Flesh is alive, its exclusive music Boss 2 will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Wall of Flesh (Otherworldly) will play instead.
Wallpapers: Wallpapers are a group of walls purchased from the Painter. Despite the name, they work just like any other type of wall and do not have to be applied onto other walls. As such, they can be placed and used to prevent enemies from spawning, and can be used to fulfill the requirements of a house.
Christmas-themed wallpapers can only be purchased during the Christmas seasonal event.
Wand of Frosting: The Wand of Frosting is a pre-Hardmode wand and the direct upgrade to the Wand of Sparking. When used, it fires a blue spark that travels in a slight curve for about 23 tiles before dissipating. The spark can pierce one enemy and has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Frostburn debuff for 2 seconds (2/3 (66.67%) chance) or 3 seconds (1/3 (33.33%) chance). The Wand of Frosting also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
Its best modifier is Demonic or Deadly, with the former granting improved critical strike chance and the latter granting improved speed. It cannot get modifiers that affect knockback or mana cost.
Wand of Sparking: The Wand of Sparking is a pre-Hardmode wand. When used, it fires a spark that travels in a slight curve for about 23 tiles before dissipating. The spark can pierce one enemy and has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff. The Wand of Sparking also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. The Wand of Sparking has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being obtained from wooden Chests on the Surface or in the Underground layer, and can also be sold by the Skeleton Merchant during a third quarter moon for 1 Gold.
Its best modifier is Demonic or Deadly, with the former granting improved critical strike chance and the latter granting improved speed. It cannot get modifiers that affect knockback or mana cost.
Wandering Eye: The Wandering Eye is a Hardmode flying enemy that spawns on the surface at night. It behaves like a larger Demon Eye, as it pursues the player, bounces off blocks, and is highly susceptible to knockback. However, when its health is reduced to below 50% (150 / 300 / 450), the Wandering Eye's pupil will peel off and reveal a mouth with a row of sharp teeth, similar to the Eye of Cthulhu's second phase, and gains increased movement speed, but its behavior otherwise remains unchanged.
Similarly to Demon Eyes, Wandering Eyes will flee when the sun rises before despawning when off-screen.
Wandering Eye Fish: The Wandering Eye Fish is a pre-Hardmode enemy that can be spawned by fishing in water during a Blood Moon. When the bobber dips and the player attempts to reel in a fish, a Wandering Eye Fish or another enemy has a chance to spawn within a few tiles of the bobber in place of a fish.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Wandering Eye Fish requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Wandering set: The Wandering set or Wandering Ronin set is a vanity set consisting of the Wandering Jingasa, the Wandering Yukata, and the Wandering Geta. It is one of the six sets that were added as part of the Journey's End Vanity Contest; the original concept was submitted by crowflux.
When the full set is worn, fireflies can be seen flying around the player.
War Axe of the Night: The War Axe of the Night is a pre-Hardmode axe.
Its Crimson counterpart is the Blood Lust Cluster.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
War Table: The War Table is an animated furniture item which fulfills a house's table requirement that is dropped by the Dark Mage and the Ogre during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%) chance during Tier 1, and a 1/8 (12.5%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 3.

Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the War Table grants the Strategist buff, which increases the player's sentry capacity by 1. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.

Unlike equipment buff items, the War Table must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 5×4 tiles being available.
War Table Banner: The War Table Banner is a decorative banner obtained by defeating the Dark Mage in the Old One's Army event. During the last Tier 1 wave, it has a 50% / 100% chance to drop; during the fourth and sixth Tier 3 waves, it has a 12.5% / 25% chance to drop. The Dark Mage drops 4 banners at a time.
Warmth Potion: The Warmth Potion is a buff potion that grants the Warmth buff when consumed, which provides +30% damage reduction from cold-themed enemies (see below). It also reduces the duration of Chilled by 75% and Frozen by 50%. This lasts for 15 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Warrior Emblem: The Warrior Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that increases melee damage by 15%. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop from the Wall of Flesh.
Wasp Gun: The Wasp Gun is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When used, it fires 2–4 homing wasp projectiles that ricochet or hit enemies a maximum of three times before dissipating. The wasp projectiles also have 10 armor penetration.
Watches: Watches are informational accessories that show the current in-game time in the top-right corner of the screen.
The display of time can be toggled by clicking the watch icon underneath the minimap while the inventory is open or selecting the watch icon in the equipment menu.
Water Bolt: The Water Bolt is a pre-Hardmode spell book that can be found hidden within the shelves of the Dungeon, along with having a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to be dropped by Water Bolt Mimics. When used, it fires a slow-moving piercing water ball projectile that can bounce off blocks. The water ball dissipates after hitting blocks up to five times, after hitting ten enemies, or after lasting for 30 seconds.
Water Bolt Mimic: The Water Bolt Mimic is a rare pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns in front of placed Books in the Dungeon. It disguises itself as a placed Water Bolt until it takes damage, at which point it begins attacking the player. While attacking, it floats around the player and goes through blocks in a similar manner to Cursed Skulls. Additionally, it randomly alternates between firing destructible Water Spheres that go through blocks, dashing away from the player to keep distance, and dashing towards the player at high speed. The Water Bolt Mimic has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to drop the Water Bolt upon death.
Water Candle: The Water Candle is a furniture item that emits a low amount of light, and can be placed only on flat-surface items. While placed nearby or while held, it grants the Water Candle debuff to the player.

The Water Candle debuff increases all enemy and critter spawn rates by 33%, and increases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50%. The debuff is applied to any players holding or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Water Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice. Multiple candles will not stack with each other, even if one is placed and the other held.
Several Water Candles are found commonly on the shelves of the Dungeon. They can also be crafted at a Crystal Ball.

Placed Water Candles can be shut off by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them, and will toggle when activated via wiring. Water Candles that are turned off will not activate the Water Candle debuff.

The Water Candle's effect is the opposite of the Peace Candle, which decreases enemy spawn rates. If a Peace Candle and a Water Candle are active at the same time, neither have any effect on spawn rates. Conversely, the Water Candle's effect stacks with that of the Battle Potion.
Water Chest: Water Chests are a type of Chest that can be found in pools of water greater than 250 tiles, most notably in the Ocean, but more rarely in any body of water, including water lakes anywhere in the Underground and Caverns layers, Surface lakes and very occasionally Floating Lakes. In addition to containing common chest loot based on where they are found, there are special items that can only be found in these chests, listed below.
Water Gun: The Water Gun is a tool that sprays a stream of water which inflicts the Wet debuff on players, enemies, and NPCs for 25 seconds. Additionally, the stream turns off most light sources, as opposed to the slime of the Slime Gun, which turns them on. The Water Gun can be used limitlessly and does not consume any ammunition or mana.

The Water Gun can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Gold 50 Silver and also has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by Jungle Mimics, which spawn in worlds with the Celebration Mk 10 seed enabled.
The Water Gun cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Water Strider: The Water Strider is a harmless critter that spawns on bodies of water on the Surface during the day. It only spawns near Sand or Jungle grass blocks, but not in the Ocean biome. It will not spawn if the wind speed is greater than 22.5 mph, or if it is raining. The Water Strider moves by gliding on water and hopping around on land. The Water Strider has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Water Strider can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Water Strider Cage). Once crafted, the Water Strider cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Water Strider can be used as bait for fishing, with 17% bait power.
There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Water Strider to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Water Walking Boots: Water Walking Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that grants the ability to walk on water, honey, and Shimmer. They do not allow walking on lava. While on said liquids, pressing ▼ Down will cause the player to fall through the liquid, similarly to platforms. Water Walking Boots have a 1/10 (10%) chance of being obtained from Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates.
Water Walking Potion: The Water Walking Potion is a buff potion which grants the Water Walking buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to walk on the surface of all liquids (water, lava, honey, and Shimmer), and prevents fall damage when falling onto liquid surfaces. The player can sink into liquids by pressing ▼ Down. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
In addition to being crafted, Water Walking Potions can be found in pots and chests.
Water fountains: Water fountains are mechanisms and crafting stations that change the color of all nearby water. They can be activated via ⚷ Open / Activate or wire. Like Sinks, they can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The range of a fountain's effects is a radius 60 tiles horizontally and 53 tiles vertically, measured from the edges of its sprite.

There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 8 different obtainable fountains, all of which are purchased from the Witch Doctor for 4 Gold each at any time.
Additionally, some special world seeds contain naturally generated Water Fountains on their Floating Islands:
Drunk worlds have Icy and Desert Water Fountains.
Celebration Mk 10 worlds have Hallowed Water Fountains.
Remix worlds have Corrupt or Crimson Water Fountains depending on the world evil.
On the Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS versions, they can be purchased for free, but are only available after Plantera has been defeated.
Waterfall Block: The Waterfall Block is an animated block type which shows flowing water.
Waterfall Wall: Waterfall Wall is one of only a few animated background walls. It depicts flowing water.
Waterleaf: Waterleaf is a type of herb which appears as a small, turquoise-colored sprout. It grows naturally on Sand and Pearlsand Blocks, but will never spawn in the Ocean biome. Waterleaf can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Waterleaf Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles.

Waterleaf blooms when it is raining. Its blooming is indicated by turquoise leaves and little water particles emitted. Harvesting mature Waterleaf yields 1 Waterleaf item. Harvesting blooming Waterleaf yields 1 Waterleaf item and 1–3 Waterleaf Seeds. Harvesting blooming Waterleaf with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Waterleafs and 1–5 Waterleaf Seeds instead.
Both Waterleaf and Waterleaf Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.
Waterleaf Seeds: Waterleaf Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Waterleaves while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Waterleaves while they are fully grown. A Waterleaf plant only blooms during Rain. Each plant drops 1–3 Waterleaf Seeds when harvested while blooming.

Waterleaf Seeds can be placed on Sand and Pearlsand Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, even inside water or honey, and will grow into harvestable Waterleaves. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Desert, but will only yield seeds when blooming.
Weapon Rack: The Weapon Rack is a furniture item that can be placed on background walls. By pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, a player can mount any weapon-type item for display, including damage-dealing tools.

Displayed items are oriented the same way the rack was placed, and large item graphics may be resized to fit on it. A pickaxe or drill will remove the displayed item before freeing the Weapon Rack itself.
Weather Pain: The Weather Pain is a pre-Hardmode wand that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. When used, it fires a Hurtnado that dissipates after 9.5 seconds or after hitting 15 enemies. The Hurtnado has 10 armor penetration, bounces off blocks, and homes in on nearby enemies, attempting to hover in front of them to deal continuous damage. Only one Hurtnado can exist at a time. If the Weather Pain is used again while another Hurtnado is already active, the existing Hurtnado dissipates 0.25 seconds after the new one is summoned.
Weather Radio: The Weather Radio is an informational accessory that displays the current weather and wind speed on the Surface, even if the player is in the Underground, Cavern, or Underworld layers.

The Weather Radio can be received as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a Weather Radio as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.
Weather Vane: The Weather Vane is a decoration piece that will periodically sway in the wind if placed in the surface or space layer, and without a background wall behind it. If the wind speed hits 5 mph or more, it will start swaying in the direction of the wind.
Web Covered Chest: Web Covered Chests can be found in Spider Nests, though they are rare. They always contain a Web Slinger, in addition to common or uncommon items (also found in Gold Chests) depending on the height they were found: Underground or Caverns.
Wedding set: The Wedding set is a vanity set which consists of the Wedding Veil and the Wedding Dress. They are guaranteed to be dropped by The Bride, a rare enemy that spawns during a Blood Moon and in the Graveyard mini biome.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Welding Mask: The Welding Mask is a Hardmode vanity accessory.
The Welding Mask cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Werewolf: The Werewolf is a Hardmode enemy that commonly spawns at night only while a full moon is active. Werewolves can open doors and have a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to inflict the Bleeding debuff for 45 / 90 / 112.5 seconds. At close range, Werewolves attack the player by leaping or lunging, closing distances quickly to catch unwary players off-guard.
The Werewolf can drop the Moon Charm, which allows the player to transform into a Werewolf at night.
White Horseshoe Balloon: The White Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 33% and jump speed by 30%, grants a double-jump, and grants +0.05 luck (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks (~75% increase), while the double-jump's height is increased from 8 blocks to 14.5 blocks, reaching a total of 25 blocks with both jumps.
Jump height is oddly reduced when underwater, reducing total underwater jump height from 19 blocks (8 + 11 from Blizzard jump) to 16 blocks (7 + 9 from Blizzard jump).
White Tuxedo set: The White Tuxedo set is a vanity set consisting of the White Tuxedo Shirt and the White Tuxedo Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 50 Gold (set), on the night of a Full Moon. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
The set exists on Old-gen console and 3DS, but is unobtainable on these versions.
Whoopie Cushion: The Whoopie Cushion is a voice accessory that makes a farting sound when the player takes damage while it is equipped. It can also be used with the ⚒ Use / Attack key to play the sound at any time. The Whoopie Cushion has a 1/50 (2%) / 99/2500 (3.96%) chance of being dropped by Giant Worms and Diggers in the Underground and Cavern layers. It can also be obtained by throwing a Zombie Arm into Shimmer.
The Whoopie Cushion cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.
Wicked Armlet: The Wicked Armlet is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/25 (4%) chance to be dropped by Cursed Hammers and Crimson Axes. It grants the following effects while equipped:
Wicked Claws: The Wicked Claws are a Hardmode accessory that grant the following effects while equipped:
Enabled autoswing for melee weapons and whips
Will's set: Will's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Phlebas, an artist who formerly developed graphics for Terraria. Equipping the full set produces a glow effect similar to Spooky armor and grants an after-image movement effect similar to Ninja armor.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Will's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Wilted Clover: The Wilted Clover is an item obtained by throwing a Lucky Clover into Shimmer. It decreases the player's luck by 0.1 while it is in their inventory or opened Void Bag. Having more than one Wilted Clover does not decrease luck any further.
Windy Balloon: The Windy Balloon is a unique pre-Hardmode flying enemy that only spawns during the Windy Day event in daytime. It carries a slime which is bound to the string underneath. The balloon will pop if the player hits it or gets too close, or if it reaches the ground or comes in contact with a liquid, causing the slime to fall to the ground. The Windy Balloon itself does not deal damage, whereas the slime attached to it does, both while flying and after the balloon is popped.
The Windy Balloon does not drop any items when popped. Its loot can only be obtained by defeating the slime, which may drop one of the Windy Balloon's unique items along with its regular loot.
There are 7 differently colored variants of the Windy Balloon, all of which behave identically.
Wings: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range.

Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile.
Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.
Wire: Wire is a unique item generally used to connect mechanisms to triggers, like a Pressure Plate, Timer, Switch, or Lever. Wires are placed using Wrenches (or their upgrades), and are retrieved using the Wire Cutter (or its upgrades), both of which can only be obtained from the Mechanic. Wire placed by differently colored Wrenches will be of different colors, which allows independent wire paths to overlap without interfering with each other.

While Wire is available for purchase from the Mechanic for 5 Silver each, it can also be obtained from naturally-occurring mechanisms, which exist sparsely in the Caverns and more frequently in the Dungeon and Jungle Temple, such as in traps and Chain Lantern/Switch arrangements.

Wires occupy their own dedicated placement layer, and so can occupy the same tile space as blocks, walls, furniture, plants, and liquids. Wires can be placed in midair, without the need for support. Explosions have no effect on placed Wires.

By default, placed Wires are invisible unless the player holds a mechanism-related item as the tool in hand, (e.g., a Pressure Plate, Wrench, or even a stack of Wire itself). However, if the player is carrying a Mechanical Lens (or its upgrade, The Grand Design) they can not only see Wires at will, but can control the visibility of individual Wire colors.

With Wrenches and Wire Cutters, the player's Wire placing and cutting reach is roughly 25 tiles horizontally and vertically. With The Grand Design, the player can place or cut Wire anywhere on the screen.

Wires are considered "connected" to triggers and mechanisms when they are placed in the same tile space as those items. Usually, this is indicated by the Wire and the item visually "touching", though not all items fully occupy their tile space (e.g. certain statues).
Wire is considered "ammunition" for Wrenches, and can therefore be placed in the ammo slots of a player's inventory.
Wire Bulb: The Wire Bulb is a light source that has multiple colors. It is purchased from the Mechanic for 5 Gold. Each corner can be lit up by wires. Each color of wire lights up a different corner. As there are four wire colors, there are four corners with four separate colors. The Wire Bulb can be placed in midair, without the need for support.
Wire Cutter: The Wire Cutter is a tool that allows players to free and harvest Wires and Actuators. It is sold by the Mechanic NPC who is initially found in the Dungeon.
The Wire Cutter has a large range bonus, making it easier to remove wires at a distance.
Wisp Dye: Wisp Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye obtained from the Dye Trader when turning in a Strange Plant. It causes equipment it is applied to gain a solid bright cyan texture with no animation. It is based off the light pet summoned by the Wisp in a Bottle.
Wisp in a Bottle: The Wisp in a Bottle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera light pet-summoning item that spawns a light-providing Wisp that follows the player around. While active, it is similar to the Flickerwick. The Wisp emits cyan light and is brighter and keeps better pace with the player than other light pets, except the Suspicious Looking Tentacle and Jewel of Light (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) which have the same light radius. It moves in accordance with the direction keys the player is pressing, although it is oriented above the player's head by default. The Wisp's movement range appears to be about 7 tiles to the left, right, and below the player's hitbox and 7 tiles above the Wisp's normal starting position. The Wisp in a Bottle has a 1/400 (0.25%) / 799/160,000 (0.4994%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Rusty Armored Bones, and Hell Armored Bones.
Witch Doctor: The Witch Doctor is an NPC vendor who will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
The Queen Bee has been defeated.

The Witch Doctor will defend himself against nearby enemies by shooting Poison Darts from a Blowgun that damage and poison enemies for 30–60 seconds. He deals 20 / 30 / 35 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
Witch set: The Witch set is a vanity set. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to be obtained from a Goodie Bags during the Halloween seasonal event. It consists of a Witch Hat, Witch Dress and Witch Boots. It may also be found in chests in Vampirism worlds.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Witch's Broom: The Witch's Broom is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Witch's Broom, allowing the player to fly and hover indefinitely in any direction. It is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event in Expert Mode with a 5–20% chance depending on the current wave.
Wither Beast: The Wither Beast is a Hardmode enemy that spawns during the Old One's Army event. It spawns during Tier 2 during waves 6–7, and Tier 3 during waves 5–7.

When a Wither Beast is within 25 tiles of a player, it will briefly dig its way into the ground for approximately three seconds before burying itself, becoming stationary and emitting a 25-tile radius aura of purple crystals, visually similar to the Dryad's Blessing. This aura inflicts the Withered Armor debuff, which halves the player's defense for as long as the player is within the aura's radius, and disappears immediately when the player leaves the zone. When stationary, the Wither Beast will also regenerate its health when damaged, healing at a rate of 5% maximum health per second (25 / 50 / 63 health per second in Tier 2, or 70 / 140 / 178 health per second in Tier 3).
It is one of only two enemies from the Old One's Army that requires the usual 50 kills to obtain its corresponding banner, the other being the Etherian Lightning Bug.
Wizard: The Wizard is a Hardmode NPC vendor who sells magic-related items. He will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.

Rescuing him as the Bound Wizard, who can be rarely encountered in the Cavern layer once the Wall of Flesh has been defeated. Interacting with him in this state with ⚷ Open / Activate will free him. If the Bound Wizard is killed, he will still be able to respawn afterwards; if the Wizard NPC is killed, he will move in again after some time as long as there are vacant houses.

The Wizard will defend himself against nearby enemies by casting fireballs similar to those of the Flower of Fire, which damage and inflict the On Fire! debuff on enemies for 5 seconds. He deals 18 / 27 / 31 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
The Wizard occasionally replaces his regular quote with a comment about the player's luck, and this is the only way to estimate a player's luck value in the game.
The Bound Wizard is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.
Wizard Hat: The Wizard Hat is a pre-Hardmode armor piece that can be equipped in the helmet slot. While equipped, it grants +4 defense and increases the player's magic damage by 5%. It is always dropped by Tim.

The Wizard Hat is part of the Wizard set, which further consists of a Mystic Robe or any gem-augmented Robe. The Wizard set provides a Set Bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance with the Wizard Hat equipped. The Wizard Hat's alternative is the Magic Hat.
Wizard's Hat: The Wizard's Hat is a Hardmode vanity item purchased from the Wizard during Halloween for 3 Gold.
Wolf: The Wolf is a Hardmode enemy that spawns in the Snow biome at night. It has the same AI as the Unicorn, and attacks by leaping and charging into the player. Like Unicorns, Wolves move at very fast speeds and can jump fairly high, making them one of the hardest enemies to evade. Due to its relatively high defense and health, it is not recommended for early Hardmode players to fight these animals. If the player does happen to come across them, it is difficult to outrun them, even with sprinting accessories.
Wolf set: The Wolf set is a vanity set that has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to drop from Goodie Bags, which are obtained during the Halloween seasonal event. It consists of a Wolf Mask, Wolf Shirt and Wolf Pants.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Womannequin: The Womannequin is a furniture item that can be used to display armor and vanity items, as well as accessories and dyes.

Items can be placed on a Womannequin by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, which opens a small set of inventory-like slots beneath the player's main inventory. There are three slots for helmet, shirt, and pants, five slots for accessories, and one slot for weapons. In addition, each slot besides the weapons slot has an associated dye slot underneath it. Placing items in these slots immediately displays them on the Womannequin.
Womannequins can only be removed if no items are placed on them.
The Womannequin always displays armor and clothing in their female sprite forms. The Mannequin can be used to display them in their male counterparts.
Wood Wall: Wood Walls are a background wall made from Wood. Like other walls, it stops enemies from spawning when it is placed and can be used for houses.
Wood armor: Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Wood Helmet, Wood Breastplate, and Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Wood. The full set grants 3 defense while equipped.
Wooden Arrow: The Wooden Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It has no special properties and is used for crafting a variety of more advanced ammunition. When fired with certain bows, Wooden Arrows will be converted into a special projectile (e.g. the Molten Fury converting them into Flaming Arrows). Some other bows, such as the Pulse Bow, can convert any type of arrow.

Wooden Arrows can be crafted, found in Pots and Chests, dropped by Pincushion Zombies, and purchased from the Merchant for 5 Copper each. They can also be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant during moon phases 2, 3, 6, and 7.
Wooden Boomerang: The Wooden Boomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being obtained from wooden Chests on the Surface or in the Underground layer. It can also be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 1 Gold during a full moon.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Wooden Bow: The Wooden Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow.
Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Wooden Crate: The Wooden Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. It is the lowest tier of standard crate, having the least value if sold directly. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Pearlwood Crate.
Wooden Hammer: The Wooden Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer.
Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and either Agile or Forceful/Strong for combat purposes, due to its unusually low base damage.
Wooden Spike: The Wooden Spike is a type of trap block that damages players who come in contact with it. The Wooden Spike deals 80 damage on contact and inflicts the Bleeding debuff for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds. Wooden Spikes are exclusively obtainable in limited quantities from the Jungle Temple, and can be broken with any drill, pickaxe, or explosive, unlike the Lihzahrd Bricks found around them, which require a Picksaw or stronger mining tool to break.
Wooden Sword: The Wooden Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword.
Wooden Yoyo: The Wooden Yoyo is a pre-Hardmode yoyo.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Woods: Wood is a type of block that is generally obtained by cutting down trees using an axe or a chainsaw. Regular Wood can be harvested from Forest trees, vanity trees, Living Trees, and Underground Cabins in underground or cavern layers, as well as by using the Faecorn. Forest trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of regular grass or Mowed grass above surface, and vanity trees can be cultivated by placing Sakura Sapling or Yellow Willow Sapling on top of any grass (but yields Ebonwood or Shadewood instead if placed on Corrupt or Crimson grass variants).
Apart from regular Wood, there are 11 other types of wood. Crafting recipes that include Any Wood as an ingredient can use any type except Dynasty Wood, Feywood, and Pine Wood.
Work Benches: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement.

There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.
World Feeder: The World Feeder is a Hardmode worm-like enemy which spawns in The Corruption, and can be considered the Hardmode counterpart of the Devourer. Loot is dropped from its head segment, so it can get stuck and buried deep in blocks if one of the main body parts is killed first.
World Globe: The World Globe is a thrown consumable item sold by the Zoologist after the Bestiary is 50% complete (273 entries). Once a World Globe is thrown and shatters on a surface, the background for the current biome changes permanently for the current world, to a random one of the backgrounds available for that biome. This lasts until another World Globe is thrown. The World Globe can be used in any biome.
Worm: The Worm is a critter that spawns in the Underground layer at any time, or on the surface while it is raining. It also has a chance to spawn when grass plants or certain ambient dirt or stone piles are destroyed, jumping out of the destroyed object. Worms are always replaced by Maggots (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in Graveyard biomes.
The Worm has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

The Worm can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Worm Cage). Once crafted, the Worm cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
The Worm can be used as bait for fishing, with 25% bait power.
The Worm can be spawned by the Worm Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Worm to spawn in place of an ordinary one.
Worms can be obtained directly in item form by opening a Can Of Worms.
Worm Food: Worm Food is a boss-summoning item that summons the Eater of Worlds when used. It can only be used in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time.
Worm Scarf: The Worm Scarf is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from the Eater of Worlds' Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While equipped, it grants +17% damage reduction.
It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Brain of Confusion.
Worm Tooth: Worm Tooth is a crafting material dropped by Devourers in The Corruption. Unlike most Corruption items, it does not have a Crimson equivalent.
Wormhole Potion: The Wormhole Potion is a potion which allows a player to instantly teleport to another team member's location in multiplayer, done by selecting their player icon in the full-screen map (accessible by pressing the Toggle Full Map key) once consumed. It is only possible to teleport to players of the same team, and the teleport will be announced in a status message. It is not possible to use Wormhole Potions if the player has the minimap disabled.

In addition to being crafted, Wormhole Potions can be found in Pots and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes, but only in multiplayer. Other players do not have to be online for Wormhole Potions to drop, so just selecting multiplayer and hosting the game can allow them to drop. Wormhole Potions are still craftable in single-player worlds.
Wraith: The Wraith is a Hardmode enemy that spawns on the surface at night, can travel through blocks, and has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to inflict the Slow debuff upon contact with the player for 15 / 30 / 37.5 seconds. They have ghostly, pitch-black bodies which render them almost completely invisible in dark areas, but have two glowing red eyes that remain visible even in complete darkness. Although Wraiths appear to fly freely, they can only hover slightly above the ground. They need foreground blocks to "swim" through in order to fly any higher.
Wrath Potion: The Wrath Potion is a buff potion which grants the Wrath buff when consumed. The buff increases the damage dealt by melee, ranged, magic, and summon weapons by 10%. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon, by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff, or by double-tapping the buff icon.
Wrenches: Wrenches are tools for placing Wires, which are used to connect mechanisms together, such as a trap with a Pressure Plate. There are four different wrenches: the Red Wrench, Green Wrench, Blue Wrench, and Yellow Wrench (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), each placing its respective color of Wire. All wrenches are purchased from the Mechanic for 2 Gold each.

All Wrenches use the same ordinary Wire item as ammunition, but the color of wrench used will determine the color of Wire when placed. The colors all function identically but can be placed so as to overlap or intersect each other without interfering with each other. Junction Boxes (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can further be used to keep intersecting Wire paths of the same color from interfering with each other.
All four wrenches can be combined to make a Multicolor Wrench (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a single tool that can place Wire of any color.
Ordinary wrenches cannot be used to remove placed Wires. Instead, a Wire Cutter or one of its derivatives is required. All Wire colors become the same ordinary Wire item again when freed.
Writhing Remains: The Writhing Remains is a pet-summoning item that spawns an Eater of Worms that follows the player. The Writhing Remains has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Eater of Worlds in Master Mode.
Wyvern: The Wyvern is a large Hardmode enemy that spawns in Space. It resembles a long, white Chinese dragon and follows the Worm AI.
It will follow descending players down to ground level and can fly through blocks, but regular Wyverns tend not to fly below ground.
Wyverns will only spawn when the player is above a certain altitude (see Space altitudes) and is outside of the Dungeon biome. Furthermore, Wyverns have additional spawn conditions.
Xeno Staff: The Xeno Staff is a Hardmode, post-Golem summon weapon that summons a UFO minion. It hovers above enemies, firing blue lasers that hit the target instantaneously. If an enemy is 18.75 to 50 tiles away, it will instantly teleport above it. The Xeno Staff has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event.
Xenon Moss Brick: Xenon Moss Brick is a type of brick made from Xenon Moss that glows in the dark when placed.
Xenon Moss Brick Wall: Xenon Moss Brick Wall is a brick background wall that glows in the dark when placed, like Xenon Moss and the Xenon Moss Brick it is made from.
Xenopopper: The Xenopopper is a Hardmode, post-Golem gun that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. When used, it fires a burst of 4–5 purple bubbles, consuming one bullet. The bubbles deal no damage and will bounce off solid blocks, but pop after a 0.5-second delay, each firing a bullet directly towards the cursor.
Yelets: The Yelets is a Hardmode, post one-mechanical boss yoyo that has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance to drop from any enemy killed in the Jungle and Underground Jungle, including in the Jungle Temple. It inflicts the Acid Venom debuff for 2 seconds on hit.
Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Yellow Cockatiel: The Yellow Cockatiel and Gray Cockatiel are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. They may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details.
Cockatiels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.

Cockatiels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Yellow / Gray Cockatiel Cage). Once crafted, the Cockatiels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
Cockatiels can be spawned by the Cockatiel Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.
Yellow Horseshoe Balloon: The Yellow Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 75%, grants a double-jump, and grants +0.05 luck (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks, while the double-jump's height is increased from 15 blocks to 26.5 blocks, reaching a total of 37 blocks with both jumps.
Jump height is instead reduced by 15% when underwater, reducing total underwater jump height from 27 blocks (8 + 19 from Sandstorm jump) to 22 blocks (7 + 15 from Sandstorm jump).
Yellow Marigold: The Yellow Marigold is a type of plant. It grows on regular grass and Hallowed grass above surface. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Yellow Dye.
Yellow Slime: The Yellow Slime is a pre-Hardmode enemy and a slime variant that spawns in the Underground layer, alongside Red Slimes. They are slightly larger and stronger than Purple Slimes.
Like most other slimes, the Yellow Slime will be passive towards any player with the Royal Gel (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) accessory equipped.
On Desktop, Console, Mobile, and 3DS, they can rarely be found carrying bonus drops, which the player receives upon the slime's death.
Yellow Willow Sapling: The Yellow Willow Sapling is a type of seed that grows into a Yellow Willow tree, which is a tree that can also spawn naturally in Forest biomes, when planted. Its appearance is purely decorative and it functions identically to regular forest trees. Yellow Willow Saplings can be purchased from the Zoologist for 1 Gold once the Bestiary is 30% completed (164 entries).
Yeti: The Yeti is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that begins to spawn during wave 12 of the Frost Moon event. It behaves similarly to Krampus and the Nutcracker, although it is much stronger and is immune to knockback.
Defeating a Yeti during the Frost Moon event will add 18 / 36 / 45 points to the current score.
Yoraiz0r's Spell: Yoraiz0r's Spell is a developer wing. Like other developer items, it is dropped along with its respective developer's vanity set, which is Yoraiz0r's set.

Yoraiz0r's Spell is unique in that it functions as wings but displays no wing or other item graphic, instead displaying a rocket effect similar to the Rocket Boots. It also grants the ability to hover via the ▼ Down+↷ Jump keys.
Yoraiz0r's set: Yoraiz0r's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Yoraiz0r, one of the programmers who develops Terraria. The Scowl will add a shadow effect over the character's eyes.
These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
Yoraiz0r's equipment also includes this non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set:
Yoyo Bag: The Yoyo Bag is a Hardmode accessory which combines the functionalities of the Yoyo Glove, a counterweight, and string. It grants the following effects while equipped:
+25% yoyo range, with an additional +2 tiles
Creates a duplicate yoyo upon the first enemy hit with a yoyo
Creates a counterweight upon the second enemy hit with a yoyo, and a duplicate counterweight upon the third enemy hit
Like the Yoyo Glove, while the secondary yoyo is deployed, yoyos will run out of spin duration 2–4× as quickly (randomized). Having a secondary counterweight does not amplify this effect.
Yoyo Glove: The Yoyo Glove is a Hardmode accessory that is purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 50 Gold. While equipped, hitting an enemy with a yoyo will create a duplicate of that yoyo that rapidly orbits around the main one. If a counterweight is also equipped, the Yoyo Glove will additionally cause a duplicate counterweight to spawn upon hit, for a total of four projectiles.
Furthermore, while the secondary yoyo is deployed, yoyos will run out of spin duration 2–4× as quickly (randomized). Having a secondary counterweight does not amplify this effect.
Zenith: The Zenith is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord melee weapon. When used, it rapidly fires fast-moving swords towards the cursor in an arc returning to the player. The sword sprites can pass through blocks, pierce enemies infinitely, home in on nearby enemies, and create visual trails while traveling. The swords have varying appearances, which function identically and have the same hitbox size. The Zenith has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.
The Zenith will transform into the True Copper Shortsword when thrown into Shimmer.
Zephyr Fish: The Zephyr Fish is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Zephyr Fish pet that follows the player. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) The pet will not teleport to the player when it is far away, unlike most other pets. The Zephyr Fish is rarely caught from fishing in any body of water. The chance to catch it is 2/3125 (0.06%) with 50% Fishing Power and 4/3125 (0.13%) with 100% Fishing Power.
Zombie: The Zombie is a common pre-Hardmode enemy that spawns on the surface at night, and is a primary reason newer players will want to build a shelter before night arrives. Along with Demon Eyes, they are generally among the first nighttime enemies a player will encounter, as they appear in areas a player first spawns.

Zombies follow the Fighter AI and walk towards the player, dealing damage on contact. They can jump and navigate platforms. Zombies will seem to hit closed doors and Tall Gates (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in their path repeatedly, though most of them cannot open them unless it is a Blood Moon (any regular and Blood Zombies (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) that spawn during which are all able to open doors/Tall Gates); Spore Zombies and Maggot Zombies (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can open doors and Tall Gates at any time. See Fighter AI for more details.

In Expert Mode (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Armed Zombies that carry disembodied arms will spawn. When they are close to the player, they will stop to perform a special "claw attack" which extends their attack range and deals more damage to the player. These arm-wielding zombies are unable to open or interact with doors at any time. The Armed Zombie Statue can spawn regular Armed Zombies in any difficulty.
Zombie Arm: The Zombie Arm is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance of being dropped by Zombies, Frozen Zombies, and Raincoat Zombies. When held, it visually appears on the player. It will also randomly release visual Zombie gore when swung.
Zombie Elf: The Zombie Elf is a Hardmode, post-Plantera enemy that spawns during the Frost Moon event. They are the most basic fighter-type enemy that spawns during the event, and despite being relatively easy to hold off, they still deal heavy contact damage.
Defeating a Zombie Elf during the Frost Moon event will add 1 / 2 / 2.5 points to the final score.
All Zombie Elf varieties require 100 kills to be awarded completion of their Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Zombie Merman: The Zombie Merman is a pre-Hardmode enemy that can be spawned by fishing in water during a Blood Moon. When the bobber dips and the player attempts to reel in a fish, a Zombie Merman or another enemy has a chance to spawn within a few tiles of the bobber in place of a fish. While hindered by a somewhat slow initial walking speed, the Zombie Merman gains exceptional mobility and maneuverability when inside liquids, and can leap out of them with great speed if needed. The Zombie Merman also becomes faster as its health is further depleted.

It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. The Zombie Merman requires 25 kills to be awarded completion of its Bestiary entry and corresponding banner, as opposed to the usual 50 kills.
Zoologist: The Zoologist is an NPC vendor who sells animal-related items and vanity. She will move in once the following criteria have been met:
There is an available vacant house.
The Bestiary has been filled to at least 10% (55 entries).
She sells a large variety of vanity items, in addition to many mounts and pets, critter-themed accessories, and the Universal Pylon, depending on the Bestiary's completion percentage.

The Zoologist will transform into a werefox during a full moon or Blood Moon. Apart from having a different sprite and quotes, there is no difference between her normal and transformed state. When transformed, the Zoologist's minimap icon also does not change, and she will revert to normal at dawn (4:30 AM).

The Zoologist will defend herself against nearby enemies by attacking with her claws, with the color of the claw attack turning from green to red when she is transformed. She deals 15 / 22 / 26 damage at the start of the game, and gains various stat boosts as the player progresses.
